title: E04-030 udev database reader (read_udev_props)
description:
## Context
Disk model, bus, WWN, serial, filesystem labels, partition types and network adapter names live in the udev database, and ADR-001 allows no libudev binding. This bead adds a small reader for the udev database files under `/run/udev/data/` so the P1 disk persistent key (`disk:<ID_WWN or ID_SERIAL>`, PERF-005) and the P2 disk, network and GPU rows can use them (R-140 items 1 to 3). Sources: R-140, PERF-005, PERF-047, PERF-049, PERF-050, PERF-056, ADR-001, ADR-013, ADR-016.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/parse/udev.rs` (the `parse/mod.rs` line `pub mod udev;` is added by this bead if E04-001 did not write it):

```rust
pub const UDEV_FILE_LIMIT: usize = 64 * 1024;
/// Keys any caller may ask for (R-140 item 1, plus ID_PATH for the by-path key fallback).
pub const UDEV_KEYS: [&str; 15] = ["ID_MODEL", "ID_MODEL_FROM_DATABASE", "ID_VENDOR_FROM_DATABASE", "ID_BUS",
    "ID_WWN", "ID_SERIAL", "ID_SERIAL_SHORT", "ID_FS_TYPE", "ID_FS_LABEL", "ID_PART_TABLE_TYPE",
    "ID_PART_ENTRY_TYPE", "ID_PART_ENTRY_FLAGS", "ID_PART_ENTRY_OFFSET", "ID_PART_ENTRY_SIZE", "ID_PATH"];

#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct UdevProps(pub SmallVec<[(Arc<str>, Arc<str>); 8]>);
impl UdevProps {
    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&str>;
    pub fn clear(&mut self);
}

/// Reads one udev database file (at most UDEV_FILE_LIMIT bytes), keeps only `E:KEY=value` lines whose
/// key is in `keys`, and stores them in `out` (cleared first). A missing file is `Ok` with `out` empty.
pub fn read_udev_props(path: &Path, keys: &[&str], out: &mut UdevProps) -> Result<(), CollectError>;

/// Database entry names (udev layout, R-140 item 1).
pub fn block_entry(major: u32, minor: u32) -> String;   // "b<major>:<minor>"
pub fn net_entry(ifindex: u32) -> String;               // "n<ifindex>"
pub fn pci_entry(slot: &str) -> String;                 // "+pci:<slot>", for example "+pci:0000:2d:00.0"
```

Rules:
- The path is `SysRoot::run_path("udev/data/<entry>")` (E04-002 adds `run`).
- A line is used only when it starts with `E:` and has a `=`; the key is the text between `E:` and the first `=`, the value the rest of the line without the trailing newline. Other line types (`S:`, `I:`, `L:`, `G:`, `Q:`, `V:`) are skipped.
- Values are untrusted text: lossy UTF-8, then stored as given. Callers pass them through `sanitize` before display (ADR-015).
- A file over the limit is read up to the limit; a cut last line is dropped.
- The first occurrence of a key wins.

Fixture: `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/udev-basic/run/udev/data/` with `b8:0` (`E:ID_BUS=ata`, `E:ID_MODEL=WDC_WD10EZEX-08W`, `E:ID_WWN=SCRUBBED`, `E:ID_SERIAL_SHORT=SCRUBBED`, `E:ID_PART_TABLE_TYPE=gpt`, an `S:disk/by-id/x` line, an `I:123` line), `n2` (`E:ID_VENDOR_FROM_DATABASE=Intel Corporation`, `E:ID_MODEL_FROM_DATABASE=Ethernet Controller I225-V`) and `+pci:0000:2d:00.0` (`E:ID_MODEL_FROM_DATABASE=Navi 31 [Radeon RX 7900 XTX]`). Serial and WWN values are `SCRUBBED` (ADR-013 scrub list, R-140 item 2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the `b8:0` fixture and keys `["ID_BUS", "ID_MODEL"]` **When** `read_udev_props` runs **Then** `out.get("ID_BUS") == Some("ata")`, `out.get("ID_MODEL") == Some("WDC_WD10EZEX-08W")` and `out.get("ID_WWN") == None` (not asked for).
- **Given** a missing file **When** read **Then** the result is `Ok` and `out` is empty.
- **Given** a file with `E:ID_BUS=usb` twice with different values **When** read **Then** the first value is kept.
- **Given** a file of 70 KiB **When** read **Then** only the first 64 KiB are parsed and no error is returned.
- **Given** `block_entry(259, 0)`, `net_entry(2)`, `pci_entry("0000:2d:00.0")` **When** called **Then** `"b259:0"`, `"n2"`, `"+pci:0000:2d:00.0"`.
- **Given** arbitrary bytes **When** parsed (proptest) **Then** nothing panics (security regression: untrusted file content).

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/parse/udev.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-collect/src/parse/mod.rs`: `pub mod udev;` (only if E04-001 did not write it)
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/udev-basic/run/udev/data/`: the three files above

## Tests
- `parse/udev.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`: `reads_listed_keys_only`, `missing_file_is_empty`, `first_value_wins`, `limit_64k`, `entry_names`, `proptest no_panic_on_arbitrary_bytes`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: an I/O error other than "not found" is `CollectError` with its `Validity` (`Restricted` on `EACCES`).
- Validity: N/A here; callers map a missing key to `Unsupported` ("Not reported").
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: called on enumeration only (every 5 s while disks or interfaces are demanded); one read per entry; no per-tick cost.
- Privacy: `ID_SERIAL`, `ID_SERIAL_SHORT` and `ID_WWN` are hardware serials. Never log them; fixtures carry `SCRUBBED`.
- Security: the file content is untrusted; bounded read, no panics, values sanitized by callers.

## Notes
- No libudev and no `unsafe` (ADR-001). Plain file reads through E04-002's bounded read helper.
- E04-021 (kind and model), E12-002 (disk persistent key), E12-013, E12-014, E12-018 and E12-026 read through this reader (R-140 item 3).
- Read `/home/oystein/work/tasklens/CLAUDE.md` first.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-collect`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit once with a pathspec: `git add <your files> && git commit -m "E04-030: ..." -- <your files>`. Never a bare `git commit`, never change branch or history.
- Fixture allowlist (R-266): the capture tool keeps only the 15 `UDEV_KEYS` above in fixture udev files and scrubs `ID_WWN`, `ID_SERIAL`, `ID_SERIAL_SHORT` and `ID_FS_LABEL`. Do not read a key outside that list without adding it to `UDEV_KEYS`, to the capture allowlist in `xtask/src/capture_fixture.rs` (E04-033) and to the ADR-016 udev row in the same change.

title: E04-031 Partitions table rows (PERF-050)
description:
## Context
The disk page's Partitions table (PERF-050) needs one row per partition, ordered by start, with unallocated gaps, holders, mounts, labels, filesystem types, usage, GPT type names and attribute flags. This bead builds the whole table in tl-collect from the block enumeration (E04-021), the mount table (E04-024) and the udev database (E04-030). The E12 `Disk` worker (E12-013) calls it and puts the result into `DiskDetails.partitions` (R-140 item 4, R-139 item 6). Sources: R-140, PERF-050, PERF-049, E04-021, E04-024, ADR-016.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/parse/partitions.rs` (plus the `parse/mod.rs` line `pub mod partitions;` if E04-001 did not write it). The row and table types are the tl-model ones (E03-056, `tl_model::snapshot::{PartitionRow, PartitionTable}`):

```rust
// tl_model::snapshot (E03-056), repeated here for reference:
// pub struct PartitionRow { pub name, pub start_bytes: u64, pub size_bytes: u64, pub holder: Option<Arc<str>>,
//     pub mount: Option<Arc<str>>, pub extra_mounts: Arc<[Arc<str>]>, pub label: Option<Arc<str>>, pub fs_type: Option<Arc<str>>,
//     pub usage_pct: InvField<f32>, pub flags: Arc<[Arc<str>]>, pub type_name: Arc<str>, pub read_only: bool, pub unallocated: bool }

/// Builds the table of one disk. `udev_dir` is `SysRoot::run_path("udev/data")`.
pub fn partition_table(
    root: &SysRoot, disk: &BlockDevice, mounts: &[MountEntry],
    statvfs: &mut dyn FnMut(&str) -> Result<FsStat, CollectError>,
    udev: &mut UdevProps,
) -> PartitionTable;
/// GPT type GUID to name (case-insensitive), or "GPT partition {guid}"; "0x83" form to "MBR 0x83".
pub fn type_name(part_entry_type: &str) -> Arc<str>;
/// GPT attribute bits to names.
pub fn gpt_flags(hex: &str) -> SmallVec<[&'static str; 4]>;
```

Rules (PERF-050):
- `kind`: the disk's udev `ID_PART_TABLE_TYPE` upper-cased: `gpt` "GPT", `dos` "MBR"; missing "none".
- One row per `ChildKind::Partition` of `disk`, ordered by `start_sector`: `name` the kernel name; `start_bytes = start_sector × 512`; `size_bytes` from E04-021.
- `holder`: the first entry of `<sys>/block/<disk>/<part>/holders/` as `"<dm name> → <dm-N>"` using that holder's `dm/name`, else `None`.
- `mount`: the first `MountEntry` whose `(major, minor)` is the partition's or its holder's, in mountinfo order; `extra_mounts` the rest (the UI shows them in the tooltip "Additional mount points:").
- `label` = udev `ID_FS_LABEL`, `fs_type` = udev `ID_FS_TYPE` (the holder's entry when the partition is LUKS and the holder has one).
- `usage_pct`: `100 × (blocks − bfree) / blocks` from one `statvfs` of `mount`; no mount: `Unsupported`; a `statvfs` error: the error's validity.
- `type_name` from udev `ID_PART_ENTRY_TYPE`, case-insensitive: `c12a7328-f81f-11d2-ba4b-00a0c93ec93b` "EFI system", `0fc63daf-8483-4772-8e79-3d69d8477de4` "Linux filesystem", `4f68bce3-e8cd-4db1-96e7-fbcaf984b709` "Linux root (x86-64)", `933ac7e1-2eb4-4f13-b844-0e14e2aef915` "Linux home", `0657fd6d-a4ab-43c4-84e5-0933c84b4f4f` "Linux swap", `e6d6d379-f507-44c2-a23c-238f2a3df928` "Linux LVM", `a19d880f-05fc-4d3b-a006-743f0f84911e` "Linux RAID", `ca7d7ccb-63ed-4c53-861c-1742536059cc` "LUKS", `ebd0a0a2-b9e5-4433-87c0-68b6b72699c7` "Microsoft basic data", `e3c9e316-0b5c-4db8-817d-f92df00215ae` "Microsoft reserved", `de94bba4-06d1-4d40-a16a-bfd50179d6ac` "Windows recovery", `21686148-6449-6e6f-744e-656564454649` "BIOS boot"; any other GUID "GPT partition {guid}"; a value of the form `0x83` (MBR) "MBR 0x83" (two upper-case hex digits, `MBR 0x%02X`); missing "Unknown".
- `flags` from udev `ID_PART_ENTRY_FLAGS` (hex attribute bits): bit 0 "Required", bit 2 "Boot", bit 60 "Read-only", bit 62 "Hidden", bit 63 "No automount", in that order. `read_only` is true when bit 60 is set or `<part>/ro` reads `1`; "Read-only" appears in `flags` once only.
- Unallocated rows: a gap of more than 1 MiB between partitions, before the first partition (counted from sector 2048) or after the last up to the disk size gives a row with `name` "", `type_name` "Unallocated", `unallocated: true`, `size_bytes` the gap, `start_bytes` its start, other fields empty or `Unsupported`.
- Udev values are untrusted text; they are stored as read and sanitized by the UI before display.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the `disk-partitions-dm` fixture (E04-021, E04-024) plus udev files `run/udev/data/b8:1` (`E:ID_FS_TYPE=vfat`, `E:ID_FS_LABEL=EFI`, `E:ID_PART_ENTRY_TYPE=c12a7328-f81f-11d2-ba4b-00a0c93ec93b`, `E:ID_PART_ENTRY_FLAGS=0x1`) and `b8:0` (`E:ID_PART_TABLE_TYPE=gpt`) **When** `partition_table` runs for `sda` **Then** `kind == "GPT"` and the rows are `sda1` ("EFI system", flags `["Required"]`, label "EFI", `mount == Some("/boot")`, `extra_mounts == ["/mnt/boot copy"]`) and `sda2` (holder "cryptroot → dm-0", `mount == Some("/")` through the holder), ordered by `start_bytes`.
- **Given** a test copy with a 4 MiB gap between `sda1` and `sda2` **When** built **Then** an "Unallocated" row of 4 MiB sits between them.
- **Given** `type_name("0x83")` and `type_name("0X7")` **When** called **Then** `"MBR 0x83"` and `"MBR 0x07"`; an unknown GUID gives `"GPT partition <guid>"`.
- **Given** `ID_PART_ENTRY_FLAGS=0x1000000000000004` and `<part>/ro` = `1` **When** built **Then** `flags == ["Boot", "Read-only"]` and `read_only` is true.
- **Given** a disk with no udev entry **When** built **Then** `kind == "none"`, `type_name` "Unknown" on each row, `label` and `fs_type` `None`, and nothing panics.
- **Given** mutated udev and sysfs files (proptest) **When** built **Then** nothing panics (security regression: untrusted input).

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/parse/partitions.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-collect/src/parse/mod.rs`: `pub mod partitions;` (only if E04-001 did not write it)
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/disk-partitions-dm/run/udev/data/`: the `b8:0`, `b8:1`, `b8:2` and `b254:0` files

## Tests
- `parse/partitions.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`: `gpt_rows_ordered_with_holder_and_mounts`, `unallocated_gap_over_1mib`, `type_names_gpt_and_mbr`, `gpt_flag_bits_and_ro`, `no_udev_entry_defaults`, `proptest no_panic_on_mutated_inputs`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: missing files leave fields at their fallback; never a panic.
- Validity: `usage_pct` is `Valid`, `Unsupported` (no mount) or the `statvfs` error's validity.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: runs on enumeration only (every 5 s while the disk page is open); one `statvfs` per mounted partition.
- Privacy: partition labels and mount paths may hold user text; never log them above debug level.
- Security: udev files and sysfs attributes are untrusted input; bounded reads (E04-002, E04-030), no panics.

## Notes
- Depends on E04-021 (`BlockDevice`, `ChildKind::Partition`), E04-024 (`MountEntry`, `FsStat`) and E04-030 (`read_udev_props`, `UdevProps`). The types come from E03-056.
- E04-A4 closes this bead. E12-013 calls `partition_table` per disk (R-140 item 4).

It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E04-032 minimal-vm fixture capture
description:
## Context

title: E04-033 capture-fixture: substring user scrubbing and scrubbed udev data (R-260, R-261)
description:
## Context
Two privacy fixes to `cargo xtask capture-fixture` (E04-005, tasklens-2dl.8, commits 4976667 and 319dc22), decided by the leader after the implementer's report (R-260, R-261). First, user names were replaced only as whole words with `-` counted as a word character, so `oystein-firefox-...` in `proc/self/mountinfo` survived scrubbing. Second, the `run/udev/data` files that ADR-013 says the fixture may carry were not captured at all, and ADR-013's `ID_SERIAL`, `ID_SERIAL_SHORT` and `ID_WWN` scrub was never applied. No committed fixture may be captured before this bead (edge from E04-A1). Sources: ADR-013 (scrub list, `run/udev/data`), ADR-015, ADR-016 (udev row), R-140, R-162, R-260, R-261.

## Deliverable
Changes to `xtask/src/capture_fixture.rs` only:

1. User-name scrubbing (R-260): `scrub_text` replaces every occurrence of each user name as a case-insensitive substring (ASCII case folding), not a whole word. Names shorter than 3 characters are skipped (they would wreck unrelated text; the rule is listed in the module doc comment and in ADR-013). Longer names are replaced before shorter ones so `alice2` is handled before `alice` when both are users. The replacement keeps the mapping `user1`, `user2`, ... by uid order from E04-005. The hostname rule (every occurrence, at least 3 characters) is unchanged.
2. udev capture (R-261): copy every regular file directly under `<src_root>/run/udev/data/` whose name starts with `b` (block), `n` (net) or `+pci:` (PCI), each capped at 64 KiB (ADR-016 row), into `<out>/run/udev/data/` with the same name. Each file is rewritten from an allowlist (R-266): keep `I:`, `V:`, `G:` and `Q:` lines and the `E:` lines whose key is one of the 15 `UDEV_KEYS` of E04-030 (`ID_MODEL`, `ID_MODEL_FROM_DATABASE`, `ID_VENDOR_FROM_DATABASE`, `ID_BUS`, `ID_WWN`, `ID_SERIAL`, `ID_SERIAL_SHORT`, `ID_FS_TYPE`, `ID_FS_LABEL`, `ID_PART_TABLE_TYPE`, `ID_PART_ENTRY_TYPE`, `ID_PART_ENTRY_FLAGS`, `ID_PART_ENTRY_OFFSET`, `ID_PART_ENTRY_SIZE`, `ID_PATH`); drop every `S:` line (symlink names carry serials) and every other `E:` key (`ID_WWN_WITH_EXTENSION`, `ID_NET_NAME_MAC`, filesystem UUIDs and the like). The values of `ID_WWN`, `ID_SERIAL`, `ID_SERIAL_SHORT` and `ID_FS_LABEL` become `SCRUBBED` (the line keeps its key). The kept text then goes through the ordinary `scrub_text` pass like every other text file. Files that fail to read go to `skipped:` in `CAPTURE.txt`. A missing `run/udev/data/` directory is not an error (the fixture then has none).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** users `oystein` (uid 1000) and `al` (uid 1001) and the text `/home/oystein/x oystein-firefox-1.scope OYSTEIN al alfred` **When** `scrub_text` runs **Then** it reads `/home/user1/x user1-firefox-1.scope user1 al alfred` (R-260: substring, case-insensitive, `al` skipped as shorter than 3 characters).
- **Given** users `alice` (uid 1000) and `alice2` (uid 1001) and the text `alice2 alice` **When** scrubbed **Then** it reads `user2 user1` (longer name first).
- **Given** a source root with `run/udev/data/b259:0` containing `S:disk/by-id/nvme-Foo_S123\nI:12345\nE:ID_MODEL=Foo\nE:ID_SERIAL=S123_ABC\nE:ID_SERIAL_SHORT=ABC\nE:ID_WWN=0x5000c500\nE:ID_WWN_WITH_EXTENSION=0x5000c5000001\nE:ID_FS_LABEL=Data\nE:ID_FS_UUID=1234-ABCD\nE:ID_BUS=ata\nG:systemd\n` **When** captured **Then** the fixture file reads `I:12345\nE:ID_MODEL=Foo\nE:ID_SERIAL=SCRUBBED\nE:ID_SERIAL_SHORT=SCRUBBED\nE:ID_WWN=SCRUBBED\nE:ID_FS_LABEL=SCRUBBED\nE:ID_BUS=ata\nG:systemd\n` (R-261, R-266: the `S:` line, `ID_WWN_WITH_EXTENSION` and `ID_FS_UUID` are gone).
- **Given** `run/udev/data/` holding `b8:0`, `n2`, `+pci:0000:03:00.0` and `c1:3` **When** captured **Then** the first three are copied and `c1:3` is not.
- **Given** no `run/udev/data/` directory **When** captured **Then** the capture succeeds and `CAPTURE.txt` lists no udev files.
- **Given** a fixture captured on the owner machine (`#[ignore]`, run by hand) **When** `rg -i oystein crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/<name>` runs **Then** it prints nothing (regression for the mountinfo leak).

## Files
- `xtask/src/capture_fixture.rs`: change (`scrub_text`, the udev copy step, module doc comment).

## Tests
- `xtask/src/capture_fixture.rs::tests::users_scrubbed_as_substrings`: the first acceptance criterion (security regression).
- `xtask/src/capture_fixture.rs::tests::short_user_names_skipped`: `al` is left alone, `ali` (3 characters) is replaced.
- `xtask/src/capture_fixture.rs::tests::longer_user_name_first`: the `alice2` case.
- `xtask/src/capture_fixture.rs::tests::udev_values_scrubbed`: the `b259:0` case (security regression).
- `xtask/src/capture_fixture.rs::tests::udev_only_block_net_pci`: the `c1:3` case.
- `xtask/src/capture_fixture.rs::tests::udev_dir_optional`.
- Update `users_and_hostname_scrubbed` from E04-005: its old expectation `alicex` stays unchanged is replaced by `user1x` (substring rule, R-260).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: unreadable udev files are skipped and listed; nothing else changes.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: this bead is part of the privacy gate for every committed fixture (ADR-015). Do not commit any fixture captured before it; E04-A1 (2dl.1) depends on this bead for that reason. Never print scrubbed-out values in test names or logs.
- Security: label `security`; both fixes have regression tests.

## Notes
- Depends on E04-005 (2dl.8, closed). E04-A1 (2dl.1), which captures `owner-desktop`, depends on this bead; E04-032 (`minimal-vm`) depends on E04-A1 and is covered.
- xtask may use only `std`, `serde`, `serde_json` and `anyhow` (ADR-001); case folding is `eq_ignore_ascii_case` over byte windows, no regex crate.
- Read `/home/oystein/work/tasklens/CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` first.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p xtask`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git add xtask/src/capture_fixture.rs && git commit -m "xtask(<bead id>): scrub user names as substrings and capture scrubbed udev data" -- xtask/src/capture_fixture.rs`. Never a bare `git commit`, never change branch or history.
- Allowlist rule (R-266): the kept `E:` keys are exactly E04-030's `UDEV_KEYS`; the two lists change together.
close_reason: Substring user scrub (R-260), udev block/net/PCI capture with allowlisted keys and SCRUBBED serial, WWN and label values (R-261, R-263). Commits 772e23d, 632e1ef, 8f6b358.

title: E04-005 cargo xtask capture-fixture with scrubbing
description:
## Context
`cargo xtask capture-fixture <name>` copies the files tasklens reads from the running machine into `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/<name>/` as a fake root, scrubbing anything personal. Parser and sampler tests in E04, E05 and E06 run against these fixtures. This bead writes the subcommand module; E04-006 wires it into `xtask/src/main.rs`. Sources: ADR-013 (parser fixtures, scrub rules), ADR-016 (the files read), ADR-015 (what is never exported), PERF entries of E04 for the `/sys` file list.

## Deliverable
`xtask/src/capture_fixture.rs` (xtask may use only `serde`, `serde_json`, `anyhow` and std, ADR-001):
```rust
pub fn run(args: &[String]) -> anyhow::Result<()>;   // CLI entry: capture-fixture <name> [--force]
pub struct CaptureOpts { pub max_pids: usize /* 50 */, pub force: bool }
/// Testable core: copies from `src_root` (normally "/") into `out_dir`.
pub fn capture(src_root: &Path, out_dir: &Path, opts: &CaptureOpts) -> anyhow::Result<CaptureReport>;
pub struct CaptureReport { pub copied: Vec<PathBuf>, pub skipped: Vec<(PathBuf, String)> }
// scrub helpers, pub(crate) for tests:
fn user_map(passwd: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)>;      // [(real name, "userN")]
fn scrub_text(text: &str, users: &[(String, String)], hostname: Option<&str>) -> String;
fn scrubbed_cmdline(comm: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>;            // b"<comm>\0--arg\0"
fn is_serial_file(basename: &str) -> bool;
```
CLI rules:
- `<name>` must match `^[a-z0-9-]+$`, else exit with the error `fixture name must be lowercase letters, digits and dashes`.
- Output directory: `<workspace root>/crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/<name>/`, where the workspace root is the parent of `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` (the `xtask` directory). If it exists and `--force` is absent, exit with `fixture <name> exists; pass --force to replace it`. With `--force`, delete it first.
- At the end print, to stdout, `copied N files, skipped M` and then one line per skipped path with its reason (xtask may print; `clippy::print_stdout` is allowed locally in xtask with `#[allow(clippy::print_stdout)]` on `run`).
- Also write `<out>/CAPTURE.txt`: line 1 `kernel <contents of /proc/sys/kernel/osrelease>`, line 2 `captured-by cargo xtask capture-fixture`, then `copied:` and `skipped:` sections listing relative paths. No date, no hostname, no user name.

Files copied (paths relative to `src_root`; a path that does not exist is silently left out; a read error such as `EACCES` puts it in `skipped` with the reason `permission denied` or the error text):
- `proc/stat`, `proc/meminfo`, `proc/vmstat`, `proc/diskstats`, `proc/net/dev`, `proc/loadavg`, `proc/sys/fs/file-nr`, `proc/swaps`, `proc/cpuinfo`, `proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`, `proc/sys/kernel/osrelease`.
- `proc/self/mountinfo` written to `proc/self/mountinfo` with `proc/self` as a real directory; `proc/self/ns/net` recreated as a symlink with the same target text (for example `net:[4026531840]`).
- Per process: the first `max_pids` (50) numeric entries of `proc/`, in ascending numeric order, whose `stat` can be read. For each: `stat`, `statm`, `status`, `io`, `comm`, `cgroup`, and `cmdline` replaced by `scrubbed_cmdline(comm)` where `comm` is the file's content without the trailing newline. A file that fails to read (often `io` of another user) goes to `skipped`.
- `/sys`, expanding `*` as a directory glob and `N` as any decimal suffix:
  - `sys/devices/system/cpu/{online,possible,present}`; `cpuN/online`; `cpuN/cpu_capacity`; `cpuN/topology/{core_id,physical_package_id,die_id,thread_siblings_list,core_siblings_list}`; `cpuN/cache/indexN/{level,type,size,shared_cpu_list}`; `cpuN/acpi_cppc/nominal_freq`; `cpufreq/policyN/{related_cpus,affected_cpus,cpuinfo_avg_freq,scaling_cur_freq,base_frequency,bios_limit,cpuinfo_max_freq,cpuinfo_min_freq,scaling_driver,scaling_governor,energy_performance_preference,amd_pstate_prefcore_ranking}`
  - `sys/devices/cpu_core/cpus`, `sys/devices/cpu_atom/cpus`, `sys/firmware/acpi/platform_profile`
  - `sys/class/hwmon/hwmonN/{name,tempN_input,tempN_label,fanN_input,fanN_label,fanN_max,pwmN,pwmN_enable}` and the `device` symlink of each `hwmonN`
  - `sys/block/*/{dev,size,removable,ro,stat,queue/rotational,device/model,device/type,dm/name}`; `sys/block/*/*/{dev,size,partition,start}` (partitions); the symlinks in `sys/block/*/holders/` and `sys/block/*/slaves/`; `sys/block/zram*/{disksize,mm_stat,comp_algorithm}`; `sys/block/*/device/hwmonN/...` and `sys/block/*/device/hwmon/hwmonN/...` with the hwmon files above
  - `sys/class/net/*/{ifindex,type,operstate,carrier,speed,address,tun_flags}`; the symlinks `sys/class/net/*/phy80211`, `device` and `device/driver`; the directories `wireless/` and `bridge/` as markers (an empty directory with a `.keep` file)
  - `sys/class/powercap/intel-rapl:*/{name,energy_uj,max_energy_range_uj}`
  - `sys/module/zswap/parameters/{enabled,compressor,max_pool_percent}`
- Never copied, enforced by the allowlist above and checked again before every write: any path whose final component is `environ`, `maps`, `smaps`, `smaps_rollup`, `mem`, `fd`, `fdinfo` or `cwd`, and any path containing a `/fd/` component (ADR-013, ADR-015).

Symlinks (sysfs is mostly symlinks): for each wanted path, walk its components from `src_root`. Every component that is a symlink is recreated in the fixture as a symlink with its original target text (sysfs targets are relative, so they resolve inside the fixture). The file content is written at its canonical location, so `sys/block/nvme0n1/size` lands under `sys/devices/.../block/nvme0n1/size` and `sys/block/nvme0n1` is a symlink to it, exactly like the real tree. A symlink whose target is not copied (for example `device/driver` pointing into `sys/bus`) is still recreated; code only reads its target's basename.

Scrubbing (ADR-013), applied to every copied text file:
- Users: from `<src_root>/etc/passwd`, every entry with uid >= 1000 and uid != 65534, sorted by uid, maps to `user1`, `user2`, …. Every whole-word occurrence (the characters before and after are not `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`) is replaced.
- Hostname: the trimmed contents of `proc/sys/kernel/hostname`; every occurrence is replaced by `REDACTED` when the hostname is at least 3 characters long. `proc/sys/kernel/hostname` itself is not copied.
- Serials: a file whose basename is `serial`, `wwid`, `wwn`, `eui`, `nguid`, `uuid`, `product_serial`, `board_serial`, `chassis_serial` or `product_uuid` is written as `REDACTED\n`.
- MAC addresses: `sys/class/net/*/address` is written as `00:00:00:00:00:00\n` (confirmed, R-162; ADR-013's scrub list gains MAC addresses).
- `cmdline`: `<comm>\0--arg\0`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake source tree in a temp dir with `proc/1/{stat,statm,status,comm,cmdline,environ,maps}`, `proc/stat`, `etc/passwd` (uid 1000 `alice`, uid 1001 `bob`, uid 0 `root`) and `proc/sys/kernel/hostname` = `myhost` **When** `capture` runs **Then** the output has `proc/1/stat` and `proc/1/cmdline`, and has no `environ` or `maps` file.
- **Given** that tree with `proc/1/comm` = `bash\n` and a real cmdline `bash\0-c\0secret\0` **When** captured **Then** `proc/1/cmdline` is exactly `bash\0--arg\0`.
- **Given** a copied file containing `/home/alice/x bob alicex myhost` **When** scrubbed **Then** it reads `/home/user1/x user2 alicex REDACTED`.
- **Given** a file `sys/block/sda/device/serial` in the allowlist expansion **When** captured **Then** its content is `REDACTED\n`.
- **Given** 60 numeric pid dirs **When** captured with `max_pids = 50` **Then** exactly the 50 lowest pids are copied.
- **Given** `sys/block/sda` is a symlink to `../devices/x/block/sda` in the source **When** captured **Then** the fixture has the same symlink and `sys/devices/x/block/sda/size` holds the content.
- **Given** a file that returns `EACCES` **When** captured **Then** it is absent from the output and listed in `CAPTURE.txt` under `skipped:`.
- **Given** the name `Owner_Desktop` **When** `run` is called **Then** it fails with `fixture name must be lowercase letters, digits and dashes`.
- **Given** an existing fixture dir and no `--force` **When** `run` is called **Then** it fails with `fixture <name> exists; pass --force to replace it` and changes nothing.

## Files
- `xtask/src/capture_fixture.rs`: create (code and `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`)

## Tests
In `xtask/src/capture_fixture.rs::tests` (temp dirs via `std::env::temp_dir()` plus a unique subdirectory, since xtask has no `tempfile` dependency; remove it at the end):
- `never_copies_environ_or_maps`, `cmdline_is_scrubbed`, `users_and_hostname_scrubbed`, `serial_files_redacted`, `pid_limit_is_lowest_50`, `symlinks_recreated`, `unreadable_file_is_skipped` (skips itself when running as root), `bad_name_rejected`, `existing_fixture_needs_force`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the two CLI messages above, verbatim; other errors are `anyhow` context strings naming the relative path.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A (developer tool)
- Privacy: this bead is the privacy gate for every committed fixture. Never copy `environ`, `maps` or fd targets; scrub users, hostname, serials, MACs and command lines.

## Notes

- This bead does not touch `xtask/src/main.rs`; E04-006 adds the dispatch arm.

Run `cargo fmt --check` too. `heavy-build` waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs the build in a memory-capped scope, so run it in the background when your tool call has a timeout. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E30-A1 History crate
description:
## Context
Anchor E30-A1: the `tl-history` crate is complete and meets the ADR-012 verification. This bead finishes the public API in `lib.rs` and adds the accelerated 6-hour acceptance test. Other epics depend on this anchor (the engine recorder E30-A2 and anything that reads the history crate). Sources: ADR-012 (verification), ADR-001, U-11, U-22.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-history/src/lib.rs`: final module list `pub mod error; pub mod format; pub mod block; pub mod segment; pub mod store; pub mod retention; pub mod rolling; pub mod recorder; pub mod read;` and re-exports `pub use {error::HistoryError, format::*, block::{BlockBuilder, EncodedBlock, encode_block, decode_block}, store::{Store, StoreConfig, LoadProblem, LoadReport}, rolling::RollingWindow, recorder::{Recorder, ClosedBlock}, read::*, retention::*};`. Crate docs: one paragraph naming ADR-012.
- `crates/tl-history/tests/store_6h.rs`: a deterministic generator (seed 42, `std` only, a small xorshift) that produces 6 h of 1 s sweeps of 2,000 processes with 200 changing per second (values random-walk with steps above the thresholds), 120 system series at 1 Hz, written through `Recorder` into a `Store` in a temp directory, without real time passing (timestamps synthetic).
- Record the measured on-disk size and the compression ratio in the test output (`eprintln!`) so U-11 and U-22 can be settled; write both numbers into the bead's close comment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the 6 h synthetic run **When** it finishes **Then** the store's disk usage is under 64 MB (ADR-012 verification).
- **Given** 100 random seconds in the 6 h (seed 42) **When** the state at each is rebuilt from the store **Then** it equals the generator's recorded state at that second after threshold rounding (the generator keeps the last stored value per field by the same rule).
- **Given** the closed store **When** the last segment's footer is removed and its last block truncated by 3 bytes **Then** reopening recovers every block before the bad CRC.
- **Given** the 6 h store **When** `top_at` for 50 random seconds runs in a release build **Then** each answer takes at most 50 ms (PROC-090 budget); in debug builds the timing assertion is skipped with `cfg(not(debug_assertions))`.
- **Given** the 6 h store **When** decimating CPU over the whole span **Then** at most 1,024 points come back.

## Files
- `crates/tl-history/src/lib.rs`: final module list and re-exports
- `crates/tl-history/tests/store_6h.rs`: create

## Tests
- `tests/store_6h.rs::six_hours_under_64_mb`, `random_time_reconstruction_matches`, `truncated_last_block_recovered`, `top_at_within_50ms_release`, `whole_span_decimation_caps`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: the test must finish in under 60 s in release; mark it `#[ignore]` only if it exceeds 60 s in debug, and run it in CI with `--release -- --ignored` in that case.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- If the 64 MB target fails, do not lower it: report the measured numbers to the leader (U-11).
- Large-file rule: this bead creates a large file. Write it, commit it, then build and test. Fix-ups go in a follow-up commit, never an amend.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-history`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec of your files only: `git add <files> && git commit -m "..." -- <files>`. Never a bare `git commit`, never change branch or history.

## Reference

### History format reference (ADR-012; format details settled by R-169 OI-2 and OI-3)

- Store root: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens/history/` (ADR-011 paths table). One directory per boot: `history/<boot_id as 16 hex digits>/`, written with `format!("{:016x}", boot_id.0)` (lowercase, R-169 OI-3). Directories mode 0700, files mode 0600 (PROC-087), set with `std::os::unix::fs::DirBuilderExt::mode` and `OpenOptionsExt::mode` (no rustix: `tl-history` may depend only on tl-model, zstd, crc32fast, postcard, serde, thiserror; ADR-001).
- Segment file per 10 minutes: `seg-<start boottime seconds, 10 digits zero padded>.tlh`, for example `seg-0000012345.tlh`. `SEGMENT_SECS = 600`.
- Segment header, fixed 64 bytes, little endian, fields packed in this order with no padding (offsets R-169 OI-3): `0..4` magic `b"TLH\x01"`; `4..6` `format_version: u16 = 1`; `6..14` `boot_id: u64`; `14..22` `realtime_offset_ns: i64` (CLOCK_REALTIME minus CLOCK_BOOTTIME at segment start); `22..30` `start_t_ns: u64`; `30..64` zero bytes.
- Body: blocks of 60 s (`BLOCK_SECS = 60`). Each block on disk is `u32 LE compressed length | u32 LE crc32 (crc32fast) of the compressed bytes | zstd level 3 frame` of a postcard-encoded `Block`.
- Footer, written when a segment closes (layout R-169 OI-3): postcard `Vec<FooterEntry { start_t_ns: u64, offset: u64 }>` (offset = byte offset of the block's length field from file start), then `u32 LE footer length | u32 LE crc32 of the footer bytes | magic b"TLHF"`. A file whose last 4 bytes are not `TLHF`, or whose footer CRC fails, is read by scanning blocks from byte 64 until the first short read or bad CRC (crash recovery).
- Types (ADR-012 text; the additions marked `// OI-2` are settled by R-169 OI-2):

```rust
pub type MetaId = u32;
pub struct Block {
    pub start_t_ns: u64,
    pub gap_before: bool,                        // OI-2: first block after a suspend, resume or engine epoch change
    pub mem_total_kib: u64,                      // OI-2: MemTotal at block start, for "1.22 / 62.70 GiB"
    pub catalog: Option<Vec<HistDevice>>,        // OI-2: present in the first block of a segment and when the catalog changed
    pub new_meta: Vec<(MetaId, HistMeta)>,       // comm, display name, exe basename, app id; no cmdline
    pub keyframe: Vec<HistProcess>,              // every live process at block start
    pub deltas: Vec<SweepDelta>,                 // one per process sweep in the block
    pub system: Vec<(SeriesId, Vec<(u32 /*ms offset*/, f32)>)>,  // 1 Hz system series
}
pub struct HistMeta { pub comm: Arc<str>, pub name: Arc<str>, pub exe_basename: Option<Arc<str>>, pub app_id: Option<Arc<str>>,
                      pub exe_path: Option<Arc<str>>, pub user: Arc<str>, pub uid: u32, pub system: bool } // last four: OI-2
pub struct HistDevice { pub idx: DeviceIdx, pub kind: u8, pub parent: Option<DeviceIdx>, pub name: Arc<str> } // OI-2
// kind: 0 CpuPackage, 1 CpuLogical, 2 Memory, 3 Gpu, 4 Disk, 5 Net, 6 Sensor, 7 Fan, 8 Battery (DeviceIdentity order)
pub struct HistProcess { pub key: ProcessKey, pub meta: MetaId, pub ppid: u32,
                         pub cpu_permille: u16, pub mem_anon_kib: u32, pub io_r_kibps: u32, pub io_w_kibps: u32,
                         pub net_kibps: u32, pub gpu_pct: u8 }
pub struct SweepDelta { pub dt_ms: u32, pub changed: Vec<(u32 /*keyframe or new index*/, FieldPatch)>,
                        pub started: Vec<HistProcess>, pub exited: Vec<u32> }
pub struct FieldPatch { pub ppid: Option<u32>, pub cpu_permille: Option<u16>, pub mem_anon_kib: Option<u32>,
                        pub io_r_kibps: Option<u32>, pub io_w_kibps: Option<u32>, pub net_kibps: Option<u32>,
                        pub gpu_pct: Option<u8> }        // representation R-169 OI-3
```

- Indexes in `changed` and `exited`: index into the block's process list, where the keyframe occupies `0..keyframe.len()` and every `started` entry appends the next index in order (keyframe-then-started index space, R-169 OI-3). `dt_ms` is milliseconds from `Block.start_t_ns`.
- `FieldPatch` thresholds (binding): a field is written only when it changed against the last stored value by CPU ≥ 1 permille, memory ≥ 256 KiB, a rate (`io_r_kibps`, `io_w_kibps`, `net_kibps`) ≥ 1 KiB/s or to or from zero; `ppid` and `gpu_pct` on any change (R-169 OI-3). Stored values compare against the last stored value, not the last sampled one, so small drifts accumulate until they cross the threshold.
- Conversion from `ProcessRecord` (ADR-003): `cpu_permille = (cpu_pct * 10.0).round()` clamped to `0..=1000`; `mem_anon_kib = rss_anon_bytes / 1024` (RssAnon, D-004); `io_r_kibps = io_read_bps / 1024` rounded; `io_w_kibps = io_write_bps / 1024` rounded; `net_kibps = (net_rx_bps + net_tx_bps) / 1024` rounded; `gpu_pct = gpu_util_pct.round()` clamped to `0..=100`. A field whose `FieldValidity` is not `Valid` is stored as 0 (history never shows validity glyphs; R-169 OI-3).
- System series: stored at 1 Hz; a series sampled faster (CPU at 10 Hz) is reduced to the per-second maximum (bucket = whole boottime second). A point with value `f32::NAN` marks a gap (R-169 OI-3).
- `MetaId` scope (R-169 OI-3): ids are assigned from 0 per segment (store) or per window lifetime (rolling window); `new_meta` of block k holds every id first referenced in block k. A reader of block k loads `new_meta` of blocks `0..=k` of the same segment.
- Command lines are never stored (ADR-015).
close_reason: lib.rs module list and re-exports (318241e); 6 h store test (49ea96b, 794318d); FieldPatch presence-mask serde (d156e83). 6 h synthetic store: 60,044,245 bytes on disk (57.26 MiB, under 64 MiB), was 67,597,197 with Option tags. postcard 81,725,553 bytes, block frames 60,035,144 bytes, ratio 1.36:1 (zstd 3). Level 6 with mask: 62,512,624 bytes. top_at slowest 12.6 ms release. All tl-history tests, clippy -D warnings and fmt --check pass.

Breakdown (frames re-encoded per part): deltas about 40.7 MB (about 9.4 B per patch), keyframes 12.1 MB, metas 1.2 MB, system series 14.3 MB (about 5.5 B per point). title: E30-007 Segment writer and reader with footer and crash recovery
description:
## Context
Segment files: one file per 10 minutes holding a 64-byte header, 60 s blocks and, when the segment closes cleanly, a footer index. A segment without a footer (a crash) is read by scanning blocks until the first bad CRC (ADR-012, PROC-087). Sources: ADR-012, PROC-087, ADR-013 (recovery test).

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-history/src/segment.rs`:

```rust
pub struct SegmentWriter { /* file, offsets, index */ }
impl SegmentWriter {
    /// Creates `dir/seg-XXXXXXXXXX.tlh` with mode 0600 (O_CREAT | O_EXCL) and writes the header.
    pub fn create(dir: &Path, header: SegmentHeader) -> Result<SegmentWriter, HistoryError>;
    pub fn append(&mut self, b: &EncodedBlock) -> Result<(), HistoryError>;   // write_all, then fdatasync
    pub fn close(self) -> Result<(), HistoryError>;                            // footer, fsync
    pub fn bytes_written(&self) -> u64;
}
pub struct SegmentReader { pub header: SegmentHeader, pub index: Vec<FooterEntry>, pub recovered: bool, pub size: u64 }
impl SegmentReader {
    /// Reads the header and the footer; without a valid footer scans blocks from byte 64 and sets recovered = true.
    pub fn open(path: &Path) -> Result<SegmentReader, HistoryError>;
    pub fn read_block(&self, path: &Path, entry: &FooterEntry) -> Result<Block, HistoryError>;
}
```
- Footer layout and recovery rule as in the Reference. A scan stops at the first `Truncated` or `Crc` and keeps every block before it.
- `crates/tl-history/tests/recovery.rs`.
- `lib.rs`: add `pub mod segment;`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a segment with 10 blocks closed normally **When** opened **Then** `index.len() == 10`, `recovered == false` and every block decodes equal to what was written.
- **Given** the same segment with the footer removed and the last block truncated by 5 bytes **When** opened **Then** `recovered == true` and the first 9 blocks are listed (ADR-012 verification: truncated last block recovered up to the bad CRC).
- **Given** a block in the middle with a flipped byte and no footer **When** opened **Then** only the blocks before it are listed.
- **Given** a new segment **When** its file mode is read **Then** it is `0o600`.
- **Given** a path that already exists **When** `create` runs **Then** it returns `Io` and does not overwrite the file.

## Files
- `crates/tl-history/src/segment.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-history/tests/recovery.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-history/src/lib.rs`: module line

## Tests
- `tests/recovery.rs::footer_index_roundtrip`, `missing_footer_truncated_last_block`, `bad_crc_mid_segment_stops_scan`, `segment_file_mode_0600`, `create_refuses_existing`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `Io { path, source }`, `BadHeader`, `Version`, `Crc`, `Truncated`.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one `fdatasync` per block (once per 60 s); the reader keeps only the index in RAM.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes

It does blocking file I/O; the engine calls it only on the blocking pool. Sources: ADR-011 (paths), ADR-012, PROC-087, PROC-088, R-025, R-103.

## Deliverable

```rust
pub struct StoreConfig { pub root: PathBuf, pub boot: BootId, pub retention_ns: u64, pub max_disk_bytes: u64,

    /// stops when `deadline` (a std::time::Instant) passes.

    pub fn append(&mut self, b: Block, realtime_offset_ns: i64) -> Result<(), HistoryError>; // encodes, rotates at SEGMENT_SECS

    pub fn span(&self) -> Option<(TimeNs, TimeNs)>;

    pub fn deleted(&self) -> &DeletedKeys;
    pub fn disk_bytes(&self) -> u64;
    pub fn realtime_offset_ns(&self) -> i64;
}
```

- **Given** a store reopened after 25 minutes of blocks **When** `blocks(from, to)` covers minute 12 to 14 **Then** it returns exactly the 3 blocks overlapping that range in time order.
- **Given** a segment with header version 2 **When** `open` runs **Then** that segment is ignored and `problem` is `VersionMismatch`.
- **Given** a root path that is a regular file **When** `open` runs **Then** `problem` is `OpenFailed`.

- **Given** a deadline already in the past **When** `open` runs on a store with segments **Then** `problem` is `TimedOut` and `span` is `None`.

title: E30-009 History retention, disk cap and persist-off purge
description:
## Context
Retention keeps the store inside `history.retention_h` and `history.max_disk_mb`: segments older than retention are deleted, the oldest go first when over the disk cap, directories of other boots older than retention are deleted at start, and with `history.persist = false` every segment is deleted at shutdown (ADR-012, PROC-087, R-025). Sources: ADR-012, PROC-086, PROC-087, R-025, canonical table (a) `[history]`.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-history/src/retention.rs`:

```rust
pub struct RetentionReport { pub deleted_segments: u32, pub deleted_dirs: u32, pub freed_bytes: u64 }
/// Deletes closed segments whose last block ends before now - retention, then the oldest closed segments
/// until disk_bytes <= max_disk_bytes. Never deletes the open segment.
pub fn enforce(store: &mut Store, now_t_ns: TimeNs) -> Result<RetentionReport, HistoryError>;
/// At start: deletes boot directories other than the current one whose newest segment ends before now - retention,
/// using the segment header realtime_offset_ns to compare across boots in CLOCK_REALTIME.
pub fn prune_other_boots(root: &Path, current: BootId, now_realtime_ns: i64, retention_ns: u64) -> Result<RetentionReport, HistoryError>;
/// persist = false at shutdown: closes and deletes every segment and the deleted-keys file of the current boot.
pub fn purge_current_boot(store: Store) -> Result<RetentionReport, HistoryError>;
```
- `Store` gains `fn set_limits(&mut self, retention_ns: u64, max_disk_bytes: u64)` so a settings change applies at the next `enforce` (the engine calls `enforce` after every appended block).
- Settings values (table (a)): `retention_h` default 6, range 1..=12, so `retention_ns = retention_h * 3600 * 1e9`; `max_disk_mb` default 256, `max_disk_bytes = max_disk_mb * 1024 * 1024`. Clamping is done by the settings layer (E03, E33), not here.
- `lib.rs`: add `pub mod retention;`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** segments covering the last 8 h and retention 6 h **When** `enforce` runs **Then** every segment that ended more than 6 h ago is deleted and newer ones stay.
- **Given** a store of 300 MiB and `max_disk_mb = 256` **When** `enforce` runs **Then** the oldest closed segments are deleted until the total is at most 256 MiB, and the open segment is kept.
- **Given** a directory of another boot whose newest segment ended 7 h ago in realtime and retention 6 h **When** `prune_other_boots` runs **Then** that directory is deleted; another boot from 2 h ago stays.
- **Given** a non-directory file in the root **When** `prune_other_boots` runs **Then** the file is left alone.
- **Given** `persist = false` **When** `purge_current_boot` runs **Then** the current boot directory has no `seg-*.tlh` and no `deleted-keys.bin`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-history/src/retention.rs`: create, with unit tests

- `crates/tl-history/src/lib.rs`: module line

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `Io` for a failed delete; `enforce` continues with the next segment and returns the first error after trying all.

- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: `enforce` touches only the index in RAM plus `remove_file` calls.

description:
## Context
`RollingWindow` is the in-RAM history used while recording is off and the Processes tab is open: the open block plus the newest 10 closed blocks, each zstd-compressed when it closes, nothing written to disk (ADR-012 rolling window, D-010, R-103). It implements the tl-model `RecordSink` trait so the engine can feed it like the recorder. Sources: ADR-012, D-010, PROC-086, R-103.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-history/src/rolling.rs`:

```rust

pub struct RollingWindow { builder: BlockBuilder, closed: VecDeque<EncodedBlock>, metas: MetaTable, deleted: DeletedKeys, /* .. */ }
impl RollingWindow {
    pub fn new(boot: BootId) -> Self;
    pub fn mark_gap(&mut self, t_ns: TimeNs);
    pub fn set_mem_total_kib(&mut self, kib: u64);
    pub fn span(&self) -> Option<(TimeNs, TimeNs)>;
    /// Decoded closed blocks overlapping [from, to] plus a snapshot Block of the open block.
    pub fn blocks(&self, from: TimeNs, to: TimeNs) -> Result<(Vec<Arc<Block>>, &MetaTable), HistoryError>;
    pub fn delete_keys(&mut self, keys: &[ProcessKey]);
    pub fn deleted(&self) -> &DeletedKeys;
    pub fn ram_bytes(&self) -> usize;
}
impl RecordSink for RollingWindow { /* forwards to the builder; on a closed block: encode_block, push back,
```

- `lib.rs`: add `pub mod rolling;`.

title: E30-011 Recorder RecordSink for the store
description:
## Context
`Recorder` is the store-side `RecordSink`: it builds blocks from sweeps and samples and hands each closed block, with its segment rotation flag, to the engine, which writes it on the blocking pool (ADR-012, ADR-004 rule: no blocking I/O on the reducer). ## Deliverable

```rust
    pub fn flush(&mut self) -> Option<ClosedBlock>;
```

- Performance: queue bounded to 4 blocks (at most about 8 MB worst case).
- Privacy: N/A

title: E30-012 HistorySink and history worker messages in tl-engine
description:
## Context
The reducer calls a `RecordSink` on every process sweep, system sample and device catalog change (ADR-012). Disk and compression work must not run on the reducer, so the sink in tl-engine is a thin forwarder: it pushes each event into the `HistoryRecorder` worker's channel with `try_send` and never blocks. This bead adds the `tl-history` dependency to tl-engine and creates `workers/history.rs` with the message type, the per-generation sender slot and the sink. Sources: ADR-012, ADR-004 (worker list row `HistoryRecorder`, factory contract: never move an `mpsc::Receiver` into a restartable worker), ADR-001 (tl-engine row includes tl-history from P3), ADR-005.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-engine/Cargo.toml` (E08-owned, chain edit): one dependency line for `tl-history` in the same form as the other workspace path dependencies there. This is the only change to that file.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/mod.rs` (E08-owned, chain edit): one line `pub(crate) mod history;`.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/history.rs`:

```rust
pub(crate) enum HistoryMsg {
    SessionStart { epoch: u32, t_ns: TimeNs },
    System { t_ns: TimeNs, series: Box<[(SeriesId, Sample)]> },
    Sweep { t_ns: TimeNs, records: Arc<[ProcessRecord]> },
    Catalog(DeviceCatalog),                     // DeviceCatalog { version, entries: Arc<[..]> }: cheap clone
    Query { id: u64, range: HistoryRange, what: HistoryWhat },
    Delete { keys: Arc<[ProcessKey]> },
}
/// Each worker generation creates a fresh mpsc::channel(512) and stores its Sender here; the sink reads it.
pub(crate) type HistorySlot = Arc<arc_swap::ArcSwapOption<mpsc::Sender<HistoryMsg>>>;
pub(crate) struct HistorySink { slot: HistorySlot, dropped: u64 }
impl HistorySink {
    pub(crate) fn new(slot: HistorySlot) -> Self;
    /// For Command::HistoryQuery and Command::HistoryDelete routed by the reducer (E30-A2).
    pub(crate) fn command(&mut self, msg: HistoryMsg);
    pub(crate) fn dropped(&self) -> u64;
}
impl RecordSink for HistorySink { /* each callback builds one HistoryMsg and calls try_send on the slot's sender;
    no sender, Full or Closed: dropped += 1 and return */ }
```
- `on_system_sample` copies the slice into a `Box<[_]>` (one allocation per call); `on_process_sweep` clones the `Arc`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** an empty slot **When** `on_process_sweep` is called **Then** it returns immediately and `dropped() == 1`.
- **Given** a slot holding a sender of a channel with capacity 512 that nobody drains **When** 600 sweeps are sent **Then** 512 are queued, `dropped() == 88`, and no call blocks.
- **Given** a sweep of 2,000 records **When** sent **Then** the receiver gets the same `Arc` (pointer-equal), not a copy.
- **Given** the production build **When** `cargo xtask check-deps` runs **Then** tl-engine's closure still matches its row and `tl-history` is allowed.

- `crates/tl-engine/Cargo.toml`: one dependency line (chain edit, E08)

title: E30-013 HistoryRecorder worker loop and rolling-window mode
description:
## Context
The `HistoryRecorder` worker task (ADR-004 worker list) owns the history state and switches between three modes from demand and settings: recording to the store when `history.enabled` is true; the 10-minute `RollingWindow` when recording is off and the Processes tab is open (`Demand.process_table`); nothing otherwise (ADR-012, D-010, PROC-086). This bead writes the worker loop, the mode switching and the rolling-window path; E30-014 adds the store path. Sources: ADR-004 (supervision, factory contract, D-Bus-free worker loop rules), ADR-012 (rolling window rules), D-010, PROC-086, R-103.

## Deliverable
- In `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/history.rs`:

```rust
pub(crate) struct HistoryWorkerConfig { pub boot: BootId, pub history_dir: Option<PathBuf> }  // dir: EngineConfig.history_dir (R-150 item 3)
pub(crate) enum Mode { Off, Rolling(RollingWindow) /* E30-014: Recording(RecordingState) */ }   // E30-014 adds the Recording variant and RecordingState (R-262)
pub(crate) async fn run_history(cx: Cx, io: WorkerIo, slot: HistorySlot, cfg: HistoryWorkerConfig) -> Outcome<(), WorkerError>;
```
- Each generation: create `mpsc::channel::<HistoryMsg>(512)`, store the sender in `slot`, and clear the slot (`store(None)`) before returning on any path.
- Loop: `time::timeout(cx.now(), 500 ms, rx.recv(&cx))`, then `cx.checkpoint()`; on checkpoint error flush (E30-014 handles the store part) and return `Outcome::Ok(())`. Each turn re-reads `io.demand.borrow_and_clone()` and `io.settings.borrow_and_clone()` (never hold a `Ref`, bead c11v6v) and computes the wanted mode: `Recording` if `settings.history.enabled`, else `Rolling` if `demand.process_table`, else `Off`.
- Mode changes: Off to Rolling creates `RollingWindow::new(boot)`; Rolling to Off drops it (frees RAM at once); Rolling to Recording drops the window and starts the store (the store starts at that moment, ADR-012); Recording to anything flushes and closes the store (E30-014).
- Batching: after one `recv`, drain up to 63 more with `try_recv`, then apply the batch inside one `cx.spawn_blocking` job that takes the mode state by value and returns it (the same move-in, move-out pattern as `Source::sample`, ADR-004); never start a second job before the first is joined.
- Message handling in Rolling mode: `System`, `Sweep`, `Catalog` go to the window's `RecordSink` methods; `SessionStart` calls `mark_gap(t_ns)`; `Query` and `Delete` go to `history_query` (E30-015); in Off mode, `Query` answers with `HistorySource::None` and empty data. Messages that arrive while the mode is Off are dropped.
- `mem_total_kib` comes from `tl_collect`'s `/proc/meminfo` parser (E04-A3) on the blocking pool once per minute; `realtime_offset_ns` = `clock_gettime(REALTIME) - clock_gettime(BOOTTIME)` through rustix, read once per minute.
- Hidden window: hidden detection stops the sweep but keeps `process_table`, so the window survives a minimize with a gap in its data (ADR-012 [inferred], accepted).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `process_table = true`, recording off **When** 15 minutes of synthetic sweeps arrive in a LabRuntime test with virtual time **Then** a Live query returns `source = RollingWindow` and a span of at least 10 and at most 11 minutes.
- **Given** a running window **When** `process_table` becomes false **Then** within 500 ms of virtual time the window is dropped and the next query returns `source = None`.
- **Given** a worker generation that panics **When** the supervisor restarts it **Then** the slot holds the new generation's sender and the sink delivers to it.
- **Given** the worker is cancelled **When** it returns **Then** the slot is empty.
- **Given** `SessionStart` mid-window **When** the next block closes **Then** the following block has `gap_before = true`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/history.rs`: extend
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_history.rs`: create with the rolling-window cases

## Tests
- `tests/lab_history.rs::rolling_window_keeps_10_minutes`, `leaving_processes_tab_drops_window`, `restart_reinstalls_sender`, `cancel_clears_slot`, `session_start_marks_gap`. Each ends with `run_until_quiescent_with_report().lab_test_passed()` (ADR-013).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: a full channel is counted by the sink; the worker reports `dropped` in its `SourceHealth` message text "History dropped N events" (R-249) at most once per minute.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: no allocation per message beyond what the sink made; block compression (once per 60 s) runs inside the batch's `spawn_blocking` job.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Banned APIs (ADR-004): no `select!`, `race!`, `asupersync::fs`; use `Cx::spawn_blocking` and `time::timeout`.
- The worker is supervised like every other worker: its own one-child `ManagedSupervisor`, `Transient` restart (E08-A1 `supervise.rs`).
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-history`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E30-014 HistoryRecorder store mode: load, write, retention, shutdown
description:
## Context
The store path of the `HistoryRecorder` worker: when recording is on it loads the store within 2 s, writes every closed block on the blocking pool, enforces retention and the disk cap after each block, applies settings changes, and on shutdown closes the store or, with `history.persist = false`, deletes the segments (ADR-012, PROC-086, PROC-087, R-025). Sources: ADR-012, ADR-004, ADR-008 ("recording on" schedule column is the sources' job, not this worker's), PROC-087, canonical table (a) `[history]`.

## Deliverable
- In `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/history.rs`:

```rust
pub(crate) struct RecordingState { recorder: Recorder, store: Option<Store>, store_state: HistoryStoreState, persist: bool }   // this bead also adds `Recording(RecordingState)` to `Mode` and its arms in the worker loop (R-262)
```
- Entering Recording: `history_dir = None` gives `store_state = Problem(OpenFailed)` and recording runs RAM-only (queries see the open block only). Otherwise one `spawn_blocking` job runs `retention::prune_other_boots(root, boot, now_realtime, retention)` then `Store::open(cfg, now, Instant::now() + 2 s)` with `load_existing = settings.history.persist`; `store_state` is `Loading` until it returns, then `Ready` or `Problem(p)` mapped one-to-one from `LoadProblem`. The job is joined with `time::timeout(cx.now(), 2500 ms, ..)`; on timeout `store_state = Problem(TimedOut)`, the result is discarded when it arrives late, and a fresh `Store::open` with `load_existing = false` is used.
- Writing: after each batch, `while let Some(cb) = recorder.take_closed()`: if `store.will_rotate(cb.block.start_t_ns)` call `recorder.reset_meta_scope()`; then one `spawn_blocking` job does `store.append(cb.block, cb.realtime_offset_ns)` followed by `retention::enforce(&mut store, now)`. A write error sets `store_state = Problem(OpenFailed)` (R-249), keeps recording in RAM and retries opening the store after 60 s.
- Settings changes: `retention_h` and `max_disk_mb` call `store.set_limits` (applied at the next `enforce`); `persist` is read at shutdown.
- Leaving Recording or cancellation: `recorder.flush()`, append that block, `store.close()`; if `persist == false`, `retention::purge_current_boot(store)` instead. Cancellation work is bounded: the shutdown drain is 1000 ms (ADR-004 shutdown step 2), so use `cx.masked(..)` only around the final append and close, and skip the purge if more than 800 ms passed since the cancel was seen (log at warn).
- Retention values: `retention_ns = retention_h * 3_600_000_000_000`, `max_disk_bytes = max_disk_mb * 1_048_576`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** recording on with a temp `history_dir` **When** 3 minutes of synthetic sweeps run in LabRuntime **Then** `history/<boot hex>/seg-*.tlh` exists with 3 blocks after shutdown.
- **Given** a store directory whose segments have header version 2 **When** recording turns on **Then** `store_state = Problem(VersionMismatch)` and new blocks are still written.
- **Given** a load job that does not finish within 2.5 s of virtual time **When** the timeout fires **Then** `store_state = Problem(TimedOut)` and recording continues into a fresh store.
- **Given** `persist = false` **When** the engine shuts down **Then** the current boot directory has no `seg-*.tlh`.
- **Given** `max_disk_mb` lowered while recording **When** the next block is written **Then** `enforce` deletes oldest segments down to the new cap.
- **Given** `history_dir = None` **When** recording turns on **Then** no file is touched and `store_state = Problem(OpenFailed)`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/history.rs`: extend
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_history.rs`: add the store cases

## Tests
- `tests/lab_history.rs::recording_writes_segments`, `version_mismatch_reported_and_recording_continues`, `load_timeout_starts_fresh`, `persist_false_purges_at_shutdown`, `disk_cap_change_applies`, `no_dir_no_files`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `HistoryLoadProblem` values reach the UI through `HistoryView.store_state`; the UI shows the PROC-087 toast once each (E30-026).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one blocking job at a time; RAM within the 16 MB budget (recorder queue at most 4 blocks plus the store's 16-block cache).
- Privacy: files 0600, directories 0700 (PROC-087).

## Notes
- LabRuntime runs `spawn_blocking` inline (claude-asupersync-apis.md section 7), so the file I/O in these tests runs on the test thread against a temp directory.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-history`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec of your files only: `git add <files> && git commit -m "..." -- <files>`. Never a bare `git commit`, never change branch or history.

## Reference

### History format reference (ADR-012; format details settled by R-169 OI-2 and OI-3)

- Store root: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens/history/` (ADR-011 paths table). One directory per boot: `history/<boot_id as 16 hex digits>/`, written with `format!("{:016x}", boot_id.0)` (lowercase, R-169 OI-3). Directories mode 0700, files mode 0600 (PROC-087), set with `std::os::unix::fs::DirBuilderExt::mode` and `OpenOptionsExt::mode` (no rustix: `tl-history` may depend only on tl-model, zstd, crc32fast, postcard, serde, thiserror; ADR-001).
- Segment file per 10 minutes: `seg-<start boottime seconds, 10 digits zero padded>.tlh`, for example `seg-0000012345.tlh`. `SEGMENT_SECS = 600`.
- Segment header, fixed 64 bytes, little endian, fields packed in this order with no padding (offsets R-169 OI-3): `0..4` magic `b"TLH\x01"`; `4..6` `format_version: u16 = 1`; `6..14` `boot_id: u64`; `14..22` `realtime_offset_ns: i64` (CLOCK_REALTIME minus CLOCK_BOOTTIME at segment start); `22..30` `start_t_ns: u64`; `30..64` zero bytes.
- Body: blocks of 60 s (`BLOCK_SECS = 60`). Each block on disk is `u32 LE compressed length | u32 LE crc32 (crc32fast) of the compressed bytes | zstd level 3 frame` of a postcard-encoded `Block`.
- Footer, written when a segment closes (layout R-169 OI-3): postcard `Vec<FooterEntry { start_t_ns: u64, offset: u64 }>` (offset = byte offset of the block's length field from file start), then `u32 LE footer length | u32 LE crc32 of the footer bytes | magic b"TLHF"`. A file whose last 4 bytes are not `TLHF`, or whose footer CRC fails, is read by scanning blocks from byte 64 until the first short read or bad CRC (crash recovery).

```rust
    pub mem_total_kib: u64,                      // OI-2: MemTotal at block start, for "1.22 / 62.70 GiB"
    pub catalog: Option<Vec<HistDevice>>,        // OI-2: present in the first block of a segment and when the catalog changed
    pub new_meta: Vec<(MetaId, HistMeta)>,       // comm, display name, exe basename, app id; no cmdline
    pub keyframe: Vec<HistProcess>,              // every live process at block start
    pub deltas: Vec<SweepDelta>,                 // one per process sweep in the block
    pub system: Vec<(SeriesId, Vec<(u32 /*ms offset*/, f32)>)>,  // 1 Hz system series
}
pub struct HistMeta { pub comm: Arc<str>, pub name: Arc<str>, pub exe_basename: Option<Arc<str>>, pub app_id: Option<Arc<str>>,
                      pub exe_path: Option<Arc<str>>, pub user: Arc<str>, pub uid: u32, pub system: bool } // last four: OI-2
pub struct HistDevice { pub idx: DeviceIdx, pub kind: u8, pub parent: Option<DeviceIdx>, pub name: Arc<str> } // OI-2
// kind: 0 CpuPackage, 1 CpuLogical, 2 Memory, 3 Gpu, 4 Disk, 5 Net, 6 Sensor, 7 Fan, 8 Battery (DeviceIdentity order)

                         pub cpu_permille: u16, pub mem_anon_kib: u32, pub io_r_kibps: u32, pub io_w_kibps: u32,
                         pub net_kibps: u32, pub gpu_pct: u8 }
pub struct SweepDelta { pub dt_ms: u32, pub changed: Vec<(u32 /*keyframe or new index*/, FieldPatch)>,
                        pub started: Vec<HistProcess>, pub exited: Vec<u32> }
pub struct FieldPatch { pub ppid: Option<u32>, pub cpu_permille: Option<u16>, pub mem_anon_kib: Option<u32>,
                        pub io_r_kibps: Option<u32>, pub io_w_kibps: Option<u32>, pub net_kibps: Option<u32>,
                        pub gpu_pct: Option<u8> }        // representation R-169 OI-3
```

- Indexes in `changed` and `exited`: index into the block's process list, where the keyframe occupies `0..keyframe.len()` and every `started` entry appends the next index in order (keyframe-then-started index space, R-169 OI-3). `dt_ms` is milliseconds from `Block.start_t_ns`.
- `FieldPatch` thresholds (binding): a field is written only when it changed against the last stored value by CPU ≥ 1 permille, memory ≥ 256 KiB, a rate (`io_r_kibps`, `io_w_kibps`, `net_kibps`) ≥ 1 KiB/s or to or from zero; `ppid` and `gpu_pct` on any change (R-169 OI-3). Stored values compare against the last stored value, not the last sampled one, so small drifts accumulate until they cross the threshold.

title: E30-015 HistoryQuery and HistoryDelete answers in history_query.rs
description:
## Context
`history_query.rs` answers `Command::HistoryQuery` and `Command::HistoryDelete` from whichever history is active: the store when recording is on, the rolling window when it is off (ADR-012 "Reading", PROC-088 to PROC-090, R-103). It builds the `HistoryView` snapshot component (at most 1,024 points per series, min/max decimation) and sends it to the reducer. Sources: ADR-012, ADR-003 (`Snapshot.history`, bit `HISTORY`), ADR-005 (commands), PROC-088, PROC-089, PROC-090, PROC-091, UI-PRC-030 to UI-PRC-037, R-063, R-103.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-engine/src/history_query.rs` and its `mod history_query;` line in `crates/tl-engine/src/lib.rs` (E08-owned, chain edit, one line):

```rust
pub(crate) enum QuerySource<'a> { None, Rolling(&'a RollingWindow), Store { store: &'a Store, open: Option<Block> } }
pub(crate) struct QueryCtx { pub boot: BootId, pub now_t_ns: TimeNs, pub store_state: HistoryStoreState,
                             pub realtime_offset_ns: i64, pub version: u64 }
pub(crate) fn answer_frame(src: QuerySource, ctx: &QueryCtx, id: u64, range: &HistoryRange, what: &HistoryWhat /* Frame */) -> HistoryView;
pub(crate) fn answer_top(src: QuerySource, ctx: &QueryCtx, id: u64, t: TimeNs, metric: HistoryMetric, n: u8) -> HistoryTop;
```
- Range resolution: `Live` = the newest sweep second; `At(t)` = `t` snapped down to the whole second and clamped into `span`; `Span { from, to }` = averages and peaks over the range via `read::range_stats`.
- Rows: every process alive at `frame_t` (or seen in the span), minus deleted keys; `name`, `comm`, `user`, `exe` (full path), `app_id`, `system` from `HistMeta`; `present = true`; `previous_boot = key.boot_id != ctx.boot`. Then one row per key in `what.keys` that is not alive at `frame_t`: `present = false`, numeric fields 0 (the UI shows `-`). Rows are unsorted (the UI sorts).
- `process_count` = processes alive at `frame_t`.
- `totals` at `frame_t`: CPU from the CpuPackage `CPU_TOTAL`, memory used from `MEM_USED` and total from `Block.mem_total_kib`; for a Span, the averages over the span (R-169 OI-5, D-020).
- `series`: first the system total of `what.metric` over `what.view`, then one per key in `what.keys` (at most 8), each from `read::decimate` (≤ 1,024 points). `stack` from `read::stack` over the same view: per bucket the three largest per-process values plus "other" as the sum of the rest, drawn stacked in the metric colour (R-169 OI-5, confirmed by the owner in D-020). `overview` over the whole `span` only when `what.overview`. `gaps`: NaN buckets and blocks with `gap_before` inside the view, as `(start, end)` pairs.
- `HistoryTop`: `read::top_at` at `t` snapped to the second, `n` rows, with `cpu_total_pct` and `mem_total_bytes` at `t`.
- Delete: `Store::delete_keys` or `RollingWindow::delete_keys`, then re-answer the last Frame query so the rows disappear with the next `HistoryView` (UI-PRC-037).
- The worker (E30-013) runs both functions inside its `spawn_blocking` batch job, keeps the last Frame view and the last `HistoryTop`, merges them (`view.top = Some(top)`), bumps `header.version` on every answer, and sends `EngineMsg::Source(SourceUpdate::History(Arc<HistoryView>))` (variant `SourceUpdate::History`, R-150 item 1).
- No data yet (no sweep stored): `rows` empty, `span = None`, `frame_t = None`; the UI shows "Collecting first history snapshot..." (PROC-091).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a rolling window with 5 minutes of sweeps **When** a Live Frame query for CPU runs **Then** `source = RollingWindow`, `frame_t` is the newest second and `rows.len()` equals the processes alive then.
- **Given** a selected key that exited 2 minutes ago **When** `At(now - 30 s)` is queried with that key **Then** its row has `present = false` and is last.
- **Given** a key whose `boot_id` differs from the current boot **When** queried **Then** its row has `previous_boot = true`.
- **Given** a 6 h store **When** a Frame query with the whole span as view runs **Then** every series has at most 1,024 points.
- **Given** a Span of 2 min 42 s **When** queried **Then** each row's `peak` is `Some` and `frame_t` is `None`.
- **Given** `HistoryDelete { keys: [k] }` **When** the next view is published **Then** no row, series or top entry has key `k`.
- **Given** a TopAt query for Memory at t **When** answered **Then** `rows` holds at most 3 entries sorted by memory descending and `mem_total_bytes` is set.
- **Given** an empty window **When** queried **Then** `rows` is empty and `span` is `None`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/history_query.rs`: create, with unit tests on synthetic `RollingWindow` data
- `crates/tl-engine/src/lib.rs`: one `mod` line (chain edit, E08)

## Tests
- `history_query::tests::live_frame_from_window`, `absent_selected_key_listed_last`, `previous_boot_marked`, `series_capped_1024`, `span_has_peaks`, `deleted_keys_gone`, `top_at_memory_sorted`, `empty_window_no_rows`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: a store read error answers with the data that could be read and `store_state = Problem(EmptyOrTruncated)` (R-249).
- Validity: N/A (history rows carry no validity; absent rows use `present = false`).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: a TopAt answer within 50 ms (PROC-090); a Frame answer for a 10-minute view within 50 ms on 2,000 processes; measured in E30-A1 and here with a release-only assertion.
- Privacy: no command line exists in the history data.

## Notes
- The view type fields are the tl-model history types (R-156 item 3, Reference). E03-062 (tasklens-as2.28) carries them.

It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

```rust
    pub new_meta: Vec<(MetaId, HistMeta)>,       // comm, display name, exe basename, app id; no cmdline
    pub keyframe: Vec<HistProcess>,              // every live process at block start
    pub deltas: Vec<SweepDelta>,                 // one per process sweep in the block
    pub system: Vec<(SeriesId, Vec<(u32 /*ms offset*/, f32)>)>,  // 1 Hz system series
}
pub struct HistMeta { pub comm: Arc<str>, pub name: Arc<str>, pub exe_basename: Option<Arc<str>>, pub app_id: Option<Arc<str>>,
                      pub exe_path: Option<Arc<str>>, pub user: Arc<str>, pub uid: u32, pub system: bool } // last four: OI-2
pub struct HistDevice { pub idx: DeviceIdx, pub kind: u8, pub parent: Option<DeviceIdx>, pub name: Arc<str> } // OI-2
// kind: 0 CpuPackage, 1 CpuLogical, 2 Memory, 3 Gpu, 4 Disk, 5 Net, 6 Sensor, 7 Fan, 8 Battery (DeviceIdentity order)
pub struct HistProcess { pub key: ProcessKey, pub meta: MetaId, pub ppid: u32,
                         pub cpu_permille: u16, pub mem_anon_kib: u32, pub io_r_kibps: u32, pub io_w_kibps: u32,
                         pub net_kibps: u32, pub gpu_pct: u8 }
pub struct SweepDelta { pub dt_ms: u32, pub changed: Vec<(u32 /*keyframe or new index*/, FieldPatch)>,
                        pub started: Vec<HistProcess>, pub exited: Vec<u32> }
pub struct FieldPatch { pub ppid: Option<u32>, pub cpu_permille: Option<u16>, pub mem_anon_kib: Option<u32>,
                        pub io_r_kibps: Option<u32>, pub io_w_kibps: Option<u32>, pub net_kibps: Option<u32>,
                        pub gpu_pct: Option<u8> }        // representation R-169 OI-3
```

- Indexes in `changed` and `exited`: index into the block's process list, where the keyframe occupies `0..keyframe.len()` and every `started` entry appends the next index in order (keyframe-then-started index space, R-169 OI-3). `dt_ms` is milliseconds from `Block.start_t_ns`.
- `FieldPatch` thresholds (binding): a field is written only when it changed against the last stored value by CPU ≥ 1 permille, memory ≥ 256 KiB, a rate (`io_r_kibps`, `io_w_kibps`, `net_kibps`) ≥ 1 KiB/s or to or from zero; `ppid` and `gpu_pct` on any change (R-169 OI-3). Stored values compare against the last stored value, not the last sampled one, so small drifts accumulate until they cross the threshold.
- Conversion from `ProcessRecord` (ADR-003): `cpu_permille = (cpu_pct * 10.0).round()` clamped to `0..=1000`; `mem_anon_kib = rss_anon_bytes / 1024` (RssAnon, D-004); `io_r_kibps = io_read_bps / 1024` rounded; `io_w_kibps = io_write_bps / 1024` rounded; `net_kibps = (net_rx_bps + net_tx_bps) / 1024` rounded; `gpu_pct = gpu_util_pct.round()` clamped to `0..=100`. A field whose `FieldValidity` is not `Valid` is stored as 0 (history never shows validity glyphs; R-169 OI-3).
- System series: stored at 1 Hz; a series sampled faster (CPU at 10 Hz) is reduced to the per-second maximum (bucket = whole boottime second). A point with value `f32::NAN` marks a gap (R-169 OI-3).
- `MetaId` scope (R-169 OI-3): ids are assigned from 0 per segment (store) or per window lifetime (rolling window); `new_meta` of block k holds every id first referenced in block k. A reader of block k loads `new_meta` of blocks `0..=k` of the same segment.
- Command lines are never stored (ADR-015).

### tl-model history types this bead uses (R-156 item 3)

The tl-model history types (R-156 item 3). E03-062 (tasklens-as2.28) puts `HistoryMetric`, `HistoryRange` and the view types in `tl-model/src/history.rs`; E03-063 (tasklens-as2.29) puts `HistoryWhat` and the two history commands in `tl-model/src/command.rs`. `HistoryRange::Span` has the fields `from` and `to`. Use exactly these:

```rust
// history.rs (E03-062)
pub enum HistoryMetric { Cpu, Memory, Disk, Network, Gpu }          // chip order; keys 1..5
pub enum HistoryRange { Live, At(TimeNs), Span { from: TimeNs, to: TimeNs } }
// command.rs (E03-063)
pub enum HistoryWhat {
    Frame { metric: HistoryMetric, view: (TimeNs, TimeNs), keys: Arc<[ProcessKey]>, overview: bool },
    TopAt { t: TimeNs, metric: HistoryMetric, n: u8 },
}
// Command::HistoryQuery { id: u64, range: HistoryRange, what: HistoryWhat }, Command::HistoryDelete { keys: Arc<[ProcessKey]> } (ADR-005)

pub enum HistorySource { None, RollingWindow, Store }
pub enum HistoryStoreState { Off, Loading, Ready, Problem(HistoryLoadProblem) }
pub enum HistoryLoadProblem { OpenFailed, EmptyOrTruncated, VersionMismatch, NoInRange, Stale, TimedOut }
pub struct HistoryPoint { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub min: f32, pub max: f32 }
pub struct HistorySeries { pub key: Option<ProcessKey>, pub metric: HistoryMetric, pub points: Arc<[HistoryPoint]> } // None = system total
pub struct HistoryStackBucket { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub top: [f32; 3], pub other: f32 }
pub struct HistoryPeaks { pub cpu_pct: f32, pub mem_anon_bytes: u64, pub disk_bps: f32, pub net_bps: f32, pub gpu_pct: f32 }
pub struct HistoryProcessRow {
    pub key: ProcessKey, pub name: Arc<str>, pub comm: Arc<str>, pub user: Arc<str>, pub exe: Option<Arc<str>>,
    pub app_id: Option<Arc<str>>, pub system: bool, pub present: bool, pub previous_boot: bool,
    pub cpu_pct: f32, pub mem_anon_bytes: u64, pub disk_bps: f32, pub net_bps: f32, pub gpu_pct: f32,
    pub peak: Option<HistoryPeaks>,          // Some only for a Span range
}
pub struct HistoryTotals { pub cpu_pct: f32, pub mem_used_bytes: u64, pub mem_total_bytes: u64 } // averages over a Span (R-169 OI-5)
pub struct HistoryTopRow { pub key: ProcessKey, pub name: Arc<str>, pub app_id: Option<Arc<str>>, pub value: f32 }
pub struct HistoryTop { pub query_id: u64, pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub metric: HistoryMetric, pub cpu_total_pct: f32,
                        pub mem_total_bytes: u64, pub rows: Arc<[HistoryTopRow]> }
pub struct HistoryView {
    pub header: ComponentHeader,
    pub query_id: u64,                       // id of the Frame query this answers
    pub source: HistorySource,
    pub store_state: HistoryStoreState,
    pub span: Option<(TimeNs, TimeNs)>,      // oldest and newest retained frame
    pub gaps: Arc<[(TimeNs, TimeNs)]>,       // inside the requested view
    pub frame_t: Option<TimeNs>,             // the second the rows describe (None for a Span)
    pub range: HistoryRange,
    pub process_count: u32,                  // processes alive at frame_t
    pub rows: Arc<[HistoryProcessRow]>,
    pub totals: Option<HistoryTotals>,
    pub series: Arc<[HistorySeries]>,        // system total of the metric, then one per requested key
    pub stack: Arc<[HistoryStackBucket]>,    // top-3 plus other, same buckets as series (R-169 OI-5, D-020)
    pub overview: Arc<[HistoryPoint]>,       // whole span, system total of the metric; empty unless overview was asked
    pub top: Option<Arc<HistoryTop>>,        // latest TopAt answer
    pub realtime_offset_ns: i64,             // CLOCK_REALTIME minus CLOCK_BOOTTIME, for wall-clock labels
}
```

Values: rates in bytes per second, memory in bytes, CPU in percent of the whole machine (0..=100), GPU in percent. Every point list holds at most 1,024 points (ADR-012), decimated min/max per bucket as ADR-009 (absolute bucket boundaries: bucket `i` covers `[floor(t / w) * w, +w)` with `w = ceil((view.1 - view.0) / 1024)` rounded up to whole seconds).
