title: E30-A2 Recorder and query
description:
## Context
Anchor E30-A2: history is wired into the running engine. The reducer gets the `HistorySink` as its `RecordSink` (it is `None` in P1 and P2, ADR-012), forwards `Command::HistoryQuery` and `Command::HistoryDelete` to it, and stores the worker's `HistoryView` in `Snapshot.history` with the `HISTORY` component bit; the session spawns the `HistoryRecorder` worker like every other worker. These are chain edits to E09-owned files, allowed by R-150 item 4 as named insertion points: `session.rs` (install the `RecordSink`, start the history worker) and `reducer/apply.rs` (`HistoryQuery`, `HistoryDelete` forward to `SourceId::HistoryRecorder`). 00-epics.md section 2 records them. Sources: ADR-012 (hook), ADR-004 (session, worker list), ADR-005 (commands), ADR-003 (`Snapshot.history`).

## Deliverable
Chain edits, each the only change this bead makes to that file (exact placement follows what E09-A1 wrote; if a needed hook point does not exist, stop and report to the leader):
- `crates/tl-engine/src/session.rs` (E09): at session start, create `let slot: HistorySlot = Arc::new(ArcSwapOption::empty());`, build `HistorySink::new(slot.clone())`, send `HistoryMsg::SessionStart { epoch, t_ns: now_boot_ns() }` through it, install it with the reducer's record-sink setter (`Some(Box::new(sink))`), and spawn the `HistoryRecorder` worker through the same `SourceController` and one-child `ManagedSupervisor` path as the other workers with factory `move |cx, _gen| run_history(cx, io.clone(), slot.clone(), cfg.clone())` and `SourceId::HistoryRecorder`.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/apply.rs` (E09): the `Command::HistoryQuery { id, range, what }` arm calls `sink.command(HistoryMsg::Query { id, range, what })`; the `Command::HistoryDelete { keys }` arm calls `sink.command(HistoryMsg::Delete { keys })`; the `SourceUpdate::History(view)` arm replaces `snapshot.history` with `view` (a new `Arc`, so the UI's `ComponentMask::HISTORY` bit is set).
- `HistoryWorkerConfig.history_dir` comes from `EngineConfig` (R-150 item 3: field `history_dir: Option<PathBuf>`, set by tl-app to `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens/history`).
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_history.rs`: end-to-end cases through `Engine::start` with fake sources (E08 `tests/fake_sources.rs` style).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** an engine with a fake Processes source and `Demand.process_table = true` **When** the UI-side client sends `HistoryQuery { id: 7, range: Live, what: Frame { metric: Cpu, .. } }` **Then** a published snapshot carries `history.query_id == 7` with `source = RollingWindow`.
- **Given** that snapshot **When** the next snapshot after another query is installed **Then** its `history` `Arc` differs and its `header.version` increased.
- **Given** an engine session panic **When** the session restarts with epoch 2 **Then** the history worker receives `SessionStart { epoch: 2, .. }` and the next block has `gap_before = true`.
- **Given** P3 code with history settings at defaults (`enabled = false`) and the Processes tab not demanded **When** the engine runs 60 s **Then** the history worker holds no window and allocates nothing beyond its channel (checked with the sink's dropped counter staying 0 and a `ram_bytes` probe returning 0).
- **Given** `HistoryDelete` for a key **When** the next view arrives **Then** that key is absent.

- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/apply.rs`: chain edit (E09)
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_history.rs`: add the end-to-end cases

## Reference

### History format reference (ADR-012; format details settled by R-169 OI-2 and OI-3)

- Store root: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens/history/` (ADR-011 paths table). One directory per boot: `history/<boot_id as 16 hex digits>/`, written with `format!("{:016x}", boot_id.0)` (lowercase, R-169 OI-3). Directories mode 0700, files mode 0600 (PROC-087), set with `std::os::unix::fs::DirBuilderExt::mode` and `OpenOptionsExt::mode` (no rustix: `tl-history` may depend only on tl-model, zstd, crc32fast, postcard, serde, thiserror; ADR-001).
- Segment file per 10 minutes: `seg-<start boottime seconds, 10 digits zero padded>.tlh`, for example `seg-0000012345.tlh`. `SEGMENT_SECS = 600`.
- Segment header, fixed 64 bytes, little endian, fields packed in this order with no padding (offsets R-169 OI-3): `0..4` magic `b"TLH\x01"`; `4..6` `format_version: u16 = 1`; `6..14` `boot_id: u64`; `14..22` `realtime_offset_ns: i64` (CLOCK_REALTIME minus CLOCK_BOOTTIME at segment start); `22..30` `start_t_ns: u64`; `30..64` zero bytes.
- Body: blocks of 60 s (`BLOCK_SECS = 60`). Each block on disk is `u32 LE compressed length | u32 LE crc32 (crc32fast) of the compressed bytes | zstd level 3 frame` of a postcard-encoded `Block`.
- Footer, written when a segment closes (layout R-169 OI-3): postcard `Vec<FooterEntry { start_t_ns: u64, offset: u64 }>` (offset = byte offset of the block's length field from file start), then `u32 LE footer length | u32 LE crc32 of the footer bytes | magic b"TLHF"`. A file whose last 4 bytes are not `TLHF`, or whose footer CRC fails, is read by scanning blocks from byte 64 until the first short read or bad CRC (crash recovery).
- Types (ADR-012 text; the additions marked `// OI-2` are settled by R-169 OI-2):

```rust

pub struct Block {
    pub start_t_ns: u64,
    pub gap_before: bool,                        // OI-2: first block after a suspend, resume or engine epoch change
    pub mem_total_kib: u64,                      // OI-2: MemTotal at block start, for "1.22 / 62.70 GiB"
    pub catalog: Option<Vec<HistDevice>>,        // OI-2: present in the first block of a segment and when the catalog changed
    pub new_meta: Vec<(MetaId, HistMeta)>,       // comm, display name, exe basename, app id; no cmdline
    pub keyframe: Vec<HistProcess>,              // every live process at block start
    pub deltas: Vec<SweepDelta>,                 // one per process sweep in the block
    pub system: Vec<(SeriesId, Vec<(u32 /*ms offset*/, f32)>)>,  // 1 Hz system series
}
pub struct HistMeta { pub comm: Arc<str>, pub name: Arc<str>, pub exe_basename: Option<Arc<str>>, pub app_id: Option<Arc<str>>,
                      pub exe_path: Option<Arc<str>>, pub user: Arc<str>, pub uid: u32, pub system: bool } // last four: OI-2
pub struct HistDevice { pub idx: DeviceIdx, pub kind: u8, pub parent: Option<DeviceIdx>, pub name: Arc<str> } // OI-2
// kind: 0 CpuPackage, 1 CpuLogical, 2 Memory, 3 Gpu, 4 Disk, 5 Net, 6 Sensor, 7 Fan, 8 Battery (DeviceIdentity order)
pub struct HistProcess { pub key: ProcessKey, pub meta: MetaId, pub ppid: u32,
                         pub cpu_permille: u16, pub mem_anon_kib: u32, pub io_r_kibps: u32, pub io_w_kibps: u32,
                         pub net_kibps: u32, pub gpu_pct: u8 }
pub struct SweepDelta { pub dt_ms: u32, pub changed: Vec<(u32 /*keyframe or new index*/, FieldPatch)>,
                        pub started: Vec<HistProcess>, pub exited: Vec<u32> }
pub struct FieldPatch { pub ppid: Option<u32>, pub cpu_permille: Option<u16>, pub mem_anon_kib: Option<u32>,
                        pub io_r_kibps: Option<u32>, pub io_w_kibps: Option<u32>, pub net_kibps: Option<u32>,
                        pub gpu_pct: Option<u8> }        // representation R-169 OI-3
```

- Indexes in `changed` and `exited`: index into the block's process list, where the keyframe occupies `0..keyframe.len()` and every `started` entry appends the next index in order (keyframe-then-started index space, R-169 OI-3). `dt_ms` is milliseconds from `Block.start_t_ns`.
- `FieldPatch` thresholds (binding): a field is written only when it changed against the last stored value by CPU ≥ 1 permille, memory ≥ 256 KiB, a rate (`io_r_kibps`, `io_w_kibps`, `net_kibps`) ≥ 1 KiB/s or to or from zero; `ppid` and `gpu_pct` on any change (R-169 OI-3). Stored values compare against the last stored value, not the last sampled one, so small drifts accumulate until they cross the threshold.
- Conversion from `ProcessRecord` (ADR-003): `cpu_permille = (cpu_pct * 10.0).round()` clamped to `0..=1000`; `mem_anon_kib = rss_anon_bytes / 1024` (RssAnon, D-004); `io_r_kibps = io_read_bps / 1024` rounded; `io_w_kibps = io_write_bps / 1024` rounded; `net_kibps = (net_rx_bps + net_tx_bps) / 1024` rounded; `gpu_pct = gpu_util_pct.round()` clamped to `0..=100`. A field whose `FieldValidity` is not `Valid` is stored as 0 (history never shows validity glyphs; R-169 OI-3).
- System series: stored at 1 Hz; a series sampled faster (CPU at 10 Hz) is reduced to the per-second maximum (bucket = whole boottime second). A point with value `f32::NAN` marks a gap (R-169 OI-3).
- `MetaId` scope (R-169 OI-3): ids are assigned from 0 per segment (store) or per window lifetime (rolling window); `new_meta` of block k holds every id first referenced in block k. A reader of block k loads `new_meta` of blocks `0..=k` of the same segment.
- Command lines are never stored (ADR-015).

The tl-model history types (R-156 item 3). title: E30-017 History query controller with one query in flight
description:
## Context
History mode asks the engine for data with `Command::HistoryQuery { id, range, what }` on mode entry, on every scrub change, on range change and every second while live, with at most one Frame query in flight (UI-PRC-030). The minimap's overview is asked once per minute and on mode entry (UI-PRC-033). This bead adds that query controller to the page. Sources: UI-PRC-030, UI-PRC-033, ADR-005 (`EngineClient::send`, `CommandError::Busy`), ADR-012.

## Deliverable
- In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/mod.rs`:

```rust
pub(crate) struct QueryController {
    next_id: u64,                    // starts at 1
    in_flight: Option<u64>,          // id of the Frame query sent and not yet answered
    pending: Option<(HistoryRange, HistoryWhat)>,  // latest wanted query while one is in flight
    last_overview_ns: Option<TimeNs>,
}
impl QueryController {
    pub fn want(&mut self, range: HistoryRange, what: HistoryWhat, client: &dyn EngineClient);
    pub fn on_view(&mut self, view: &HistoryView, client: &dyn EngineClient);  // clears in_flight when view.query_id matches, sends pending
}
```
- Rules: `want` sends at once when nothing is in flight; otherwise it replaces `pending` (a new scrub while a query is pending replaces the pending request). `on_view` with `query_id == in_flight` sends `pending` if any. If no answer arrives within 1,000 ms, `in_flight` is cleared and the pending or latest query is resent (R-169 OI-6).
- `what` is `HistoryWhat::Frame { metric: state.metric, view: state.view_range, keys: state.selected[..min(8)], overview }` where `overview = true` on mode entry and when 60 s passed since the last overview.
- Range: `Live` while `scrub` and `range` are None; `At(scrub)`; `Span { from, to }` when a range is set.
- A 1 s GPUI timer (`cx.spawn` with `Timer::after(1 s)`) sends a Live query while live and History mode is on; it stops when the page is dropped or the mode turns off. No timer runs while scrubbed.
- `CommandError::Busy` from `send`: keep the query as pending and retry on the next timer tick.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a query in flight **When** three scrub changes arrive **Then** no new command is sent and `pending` holds the third.
- **Given** that state **When** the matching view arrives **Then** exactly one command is sent, carrying the third scrub time.
- **Given** a view with a different `query_id` **When** it arrives **Then** `in_flight` is unchanged.
- **Given** live mode **When** 5 s pass with answers arriving **Then** 5 Live queries were sent.
- **Given** mode entry **When** the first query is sent **Then** `overview = true`; the next one within 60 s has `overview = false`.
- **Given** a Busy error **When** the next tick comes **Then** the query is sent again.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/mod.rs`: add `QueryController` and its use
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_history.rs`: add tests

## Tests
- `tests/ui_history.rs::history_one_query_in_flight`, `pending_replaced_by_latest`, `foreign_answer_ignored`, `live_queries_each_second`, `overview_once_per_minute`, `busy_retried_next_tick` (fake engine records sent commands).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `CommandError::Busy` retried; no toast.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: at most one Frame query in flight; the hover card's TopAt queries have their own controller (E30-023).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- The 1,000 ms resend rule is settled by R-169 OI-6.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-history`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E30-018 History actions and History key context bindings
description:
## Context
Declares the History mode Actions and binds their keys in the `History` key context: Left/Right step 1 s, Shift+Left/Right step 1 min, Home oldest, End live, Esc live when a scrub point is set, 1..5 select a metric (table (b), UI-PRC-030, UI-PRC-032, UI-PRC-035). Actions live in the one `tasklens` namespace (R-128). Sources: RECONCILIATION table (b) rows "History scrubber", "History" and "History (scrub point set)", R-128, UI-PRC-030 to UI-PRC-037, APP-031.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/actions.rs`:

```rust
actions!(tasklens, [HistoryStepBack, HistoryStepForward, HistoryStepBackMinute, HistoryStepForwardMinute,
                    HistoryOldest, HistoryLive, HistoryMetricCpu, HistoryMetricMemory, HistoryMetricDisk,
                    HistoryMetricNetwork, HistoryMetricGpu, DeleteFromHistory, HistoryShowInLiveTable]);
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Action)] #[action(namespace = tasklens)] pub struct HistoryScrub { pub t: TimeNs }

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Action)] #[action(namespace = tasklens)] pub struct HistoryClearProcess { pub key: ProcessKey }
pub fn bind_keys_history(cx: &mut App);
```
- Bindings, all in context `"History"`: `left` HistoryStepBack, `right` HistoryStepForward, `shift-left` HistoryStepBackMinute, `shift-right` HistoryStepForwardMinute, `home` HistoryOldest, `end` HistoryLive, `1` HistoryMetricCpu, `2` HistoryMetricMemory, `3` HistoryMetricDisk, `4` HistoryMetricNetwork, `5` HistoryMetricGpu. `escape` HistoryLive in context `"History && scrubbed"` so it runs before the global Esc rule only when a scrub point is set (UI-PRC-030).
- Handlers on `HistoryPage` (registered with `on_action` on the page root): step sets `scrub` to `(scrub or newest) ± 1 s` or `± 60 s`, clamped to `span`; stepping forward past the newest second returns to live; `HistoryOldest` sets `scrub = span.0`; `HistoryLive` clears `scrub` and `range`; metric actions set `state.metric`; each change calls the query controller's `want` (E30-017). - `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/mod.rs`: `pub mod actions;`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the strip focused, live, newest second 1000 s **When** Left is pressed **Then** `scrub == Some(999 s)`.
- **Given** scrub 999 s **When** Shift+Right is pressed **Then** the page is live (newest is 1000 s).
- **Given** a scrub point **When** Esc is pressed **Then** the page returns to live and the global Esc action does not run.
- **Given** live **When** Esc is pressed **Then** the global Esc rule runs (the History binding is not active).
- **Given** focus in History **When** 3 is pressed **Then** `metric == Disk`.
- **Given** span (100 s, 1000 s) **When** Home is pressed **Then** `scrub == Some(100 s)`.

title: E30-019 History table delegate
description:
## Context
The History table: a flat `TlTreeTable` with 9 columns showing the processes at the scrub second, or averages over a selected range with the peak in cell tooltips (UI-PRC-031, PROC-088). It sorts by CPU descending by default and keeps its own sort and column state. Sources: UI-PRC-031, PROC-088, PROC-046 (Hide system in history), R-011, R-006 (widths), ADR-009 (tree table, cell painters), ADR-011 (`[sort.history]`, `[columns.history]`).

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/table.rs` with `HistoryTableDelegate: TreeTableDelegate`:
  - Rows: `RowKind::Plain`, depth 0, no chevrons, 16 px icons resolved from `app_id` the same way the live Name cell does.
  - Columns in default order and widths (logical px): Name 248 (`name`), PID 96 (`pid`), User 92 (`user`), Image path 200 (`image_path`), CPU 63 (`cpu`), Memory 92 (`memory`, RssAnon), Disk 82 (`disk`), Network 92 (`network`), GPU 72 (`gpu`). Ids are the `ColumnId` strings from tl-model (R-007); `image_path` is a `ColumnId` (R-156 item 3).
  - Values formatted with the same painters as the live table (UI-PRC-004): CPU one decimal percent, Memory IEC two decimals, Disk `MiB/s` one decimal, Network in `units.network` (bits default, `Mbps` one decimal), GPU percent one decimal.
  - Header line 2: system totals at the scrub time: CPU `totals.cpu_pct`, Memory `totals.mem_used_bytes / mem_total_bytes` as percent; other columns `-`.
  - Header tooltip on Name: "Values at the selected time", or with a range "Averages over the selected range (peak in cell tooltips)". With a range each metric cell's tooltip reads "peak <value>" (for example "peak 42.1%").
  - Absent identity (`present = false`): listed after every present row, every metric cell `-`, Name secondary text "Process not running" in `text_secondary`. Previous boot (`previous_boot = true`): Name secondary text "(previous boot)" plus a 12 px Lucide `rotate-ccw-clock` glyph.

- **Given** a range **When** hovering a CPU cell of a row with peak 42.1 **Then** the tooltip reads "peak 42.1%".

- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append keys (chain edit, E16)

```rust
// history.rs (E03-062)
pub enum HistoryMetric { Cpu, Memory, Disk, Network, Gpu }          // chip order; keys 1..5
pub enum HistoryRange { Live, At(TimeNs), Span { from: TimeNs, to: TimeNs } }
// command.rs (E03-063)
pub enum HistoryWhat {
    Frame { metric: HistoryMetric, view: (TimeNs, TimeNs), keys: Arc<[ProcessKey]>, overview: bool },
    TopAt { t: TimeNs, metric: HistoryMetric, n: u8 },
}
// Command::HistoryQuery { id: u64, range: HistoryRange, what: HistoryWhat }, Command::HistoryDelete { keys: Arc<[ProcessKey]> } (ADR-005)

pub enum HistorySource { None, RollingWindow, Store }
pub enum HistoryStoreState { Off, Loading, Ready, Problem(HistoryLoadProblem) }
pub enum HistoryLoadProblem { OpenFailed, EmptyOrTruncated, VersionMismatch, NoInRange, Stale, TimedOut }
pub struct HistoryPoint { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub min: f32, pub max: f32 }
pub struct HistorySeries { pub key: Option<ProcessKey>, pub metric: HistoryMetric, pub points: Arc<[HistoryPoint]> } // None = system total
pub struct HistoryStackBucket { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub top: [f32; 3], pub other: f32 }
pub struct HistoryPeaks { pub cpu_pct: f32, pub mem_anon_bytes: u64, pub disk_bps: f32, pub net_bps: f32, pub gpu_pct: f32 }
pub struct HistoryProcessRow {
    pub key: ProcessKey, pub name: Arc<str>, pub comm: Arc<str>, pub user: Arc<str>, pub exe: Option<Arc<str>>,
    pub app_id: Option<Arc<str>>, pub system: bool, pub present: bool, pub previous_boot: bool,
    pub cpu_pct: f32, pub mem_anon_bytes: u64, pub disk_bps: f32, pub net_bps: f32, pub gpu_pct: f32,
    pub peak: Option<HistoryPeaks>,          // Some only for a Span range
}
pub struct HistoryTotals { pub cpu_pct: f32, pub mem_used_bytes: u64, pub mem_total_bytes: u64 } // averages over a Span (R-169 OI-5)
pub struct HistoryTopRow { pub key: ProcessKey, pub name: Arc<str>, pub app_id: Option<Arc<str>>, pub value: f32 }
pub struct HistoryTop { pub query_id: u64, pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub metric: HistoryMetric, pub cpu_total_pct: f32,
                        pub mem_total_bytes: u64, pub rows: Arc<[HistoryTopRow]> }
pub struct HistoryView {
    pub header: ComponentHeader,
    pub query_id: u64,                       // id of the Frame query this answers
    pub source: HistorySource,
    pub store_state: HistoryStoreState,
    pub span: Option<(TimeNs, TimeNs)>,      // oldest and newest retained frame
    pub gaps: Arc<[(TimeNs, TimeNs)]>,       // inside the requested view
    pub frame_t: Option<TimeNs>,             // the second the rows describe (None for a Span)
    pub range: HistoryRange,
    pub process_count: u32,                  // processes alive at frame_t
    pub rows: Arc<[HistoryProcessRow]>,
    pub totals: Option<HistoryTotals>,
    pub series: Arc<[HistorySeries]>,        // system total of the metric, then one per requested key
    pub stack: Arc<[HistoryStackBucket]>,    // top-3 plus other, same buckets as series (R-169 OI-5, D-020)
    pub overview: Arc<[HistoryPoint]>,       // whole span, system total of the metric; empty unless overview was asked
    pub top: Option<Arc<HistoryTop>>,        // latest TopAt answer
    pub realtime_offset_ns: i64,             // CLOCK_REALTIME minus CLOCK_BOOTTIME, for wall-clock labels
}
```

description:
## Context
The History table's row menu, double-click and Enter behaviour, and "Delete from history" (UI-PRC-031, UI-PRC-037). Deleting sends `Command::HistoryDelete` with no confirmation; the engine adds the keys to the per-boot deleted list and the rows disappear with the next `HistoryView` (R-103). Show in live table jumps through `select_by_key` (UI-PRC-022), which leaves History mode. Sources: UI-PRC-031, UI-PRC-037, UI-PRC-022, PROC-070, PROC-088, R-103.

## Deliverable
- In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/table.rs`:
  - Right-click menu (`TlMenu`), in order: "Copy", "Copy details", "Copy all metrics", "Copy rows as table", separator, "Show in live table" (disabled when no selected row is live), separator, "Delete from history" (icon Lucide `trash-2` 14 px, text in `status.danger`).
  - Copy texts (PROC-070 formats, applied to the fields history has; the field set is R-169 OI-6): "Copy" copies the right-clicked cell's displayed text, one line per selected row in view order, toast "Selected process values copied." for several rows or "Copied to clipboard" for one. "Copy rows as table" copies TSV of the visible columns with a header line, toast "Copied to clipboard". "Copy details" prints Name, PID, Parent PID, CPU, Memory, Disk, Network and GPU. "Copy all metrics" prints every visible history column. Neither ever prints a command line (R-169 OI-6).

- **Given** one selected row **When** "Delete from history" is clicked **Then** `HistoryDelete { keys: [k] }` is sent, no dialog opens and the toast reads "History entry deleted".

- **Given** a deleted selected key **When** the command is sent **Then** its chip and series are gone before the next view arrives.
- **Given** a row whose key is live **When** double-clicked **Then** `select_by_key` is called and History mode turns off.
- **Given** a row whose key is not live **When** Enter is pressed **Then** the toast reads "Process not running" and the mode stays.
- **Given** the menu **When** opened on a non-live row **Then** "Show in live table" is disabled.

title: E30-021 Timeline scrubber element: paint and geometry cache
description:
## Context
The timeline strip is a custom GPUI `Element` (`HistoryScrubber`), 120 px high, drawing the stacked metric graph, selected process lines, gaps, the handle, a range fill and time labels (UI-PRC-032). This bead draws it and caches its geometry; E30-022 adds pointer and keyboard interaction. Sources: UI-PRC-032, UI-PRC-035 (colours), PROC-089, ADR-009 (chart element pattern, `ChartGeometryKey`, cached `ShapedLine`), ADR-014.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/scrubber.rs`: `pub struct HistoryScrubber` implementing `Element`:
  - `request_layout`: fixed height 120, full width. `prepaint`: one hitbox over the whole element. `paint`: as below.
  - Plot area y 0..100, background `list_bg`. Grid as the ADR-009 chart: hairline `graph.grid`, vertical lines every `visible_range / 10`, horizontal at 25, 50 and 75%.
  - Stacked area of `HistoryView.stack` (per bucket the three largest per-process values plus "other" as the sum of the rest, drawn stacked in the metric colour; R-169 OI-5, confirmed by the owner in D-020) and the system-total line from `series[0]`, in the active metric's `graph.*_fill` and `graph.*_line` colours (CPU `cpu_*`, Memory `mem_*`, Disk `disk_*`, Network `net_*`, GPU `gpu_*`).
  - One 1 px line, no fill, per selected-process series (`series[1..]`), colour k = the `accent` hue rotated by `k × 45°` with the same saturation and lightness, assigned in selection order (UI-PRC-035).
  - Gaps (`HistoryView.gaps`): a hatched band in `divider` at 30% alpha.
  - Axis: 1 px divider at y 100; labels `t_xs` (11) `text_secondary` with tabular numbers at y 104..118, aligned to the vertical grid lines. Label text: offsets from now under an hour "-M:SS" (for example "-8:20"), at or over an hour "-H:MM:SS" (for example "-1:02:03"), "now" at the right edge (R-169 OI-8). Labels that would overlap the previous label are dropped (keep every second label until none overlap).
  - Handle at `scrub`: 1 px `accent` vertical line over the plot height with a 10 × 10 `accent` diamond grip centred on the axis line. While live: a 1 px `text_secondary` line at the right edge, no grip.
  - Range: `row_selected` fill at 35% alpha between the bounds, 1 px `accent` edges, 6 × 10 bound grips at the axis.
  - Hover hairline: 1 px `text_secondary` at the pointer x when hovered (state set by E30-022).
  - Empty (no frames): grid only. Fewer than 2 points: a single 4 px marker.
  - Geometry (series fill and stroke paths via `PathBuilder`, built in local coordinates) is cached by a key over the series versions (`HistoryView.header.version`), the element size and the `view_range`; labels are `ShapedLine`s cached per text.
- Pure helpers with unit tests: `fn time_label(offset_ns: u64, out: &mut String)`, `fn span_label(d_ns: u64, out: &mut String)` giving "1h 02m", "2m 05s", "45s", and `fn drop_overlapping(labels: &[(f32 x, f32 width)]) -> SmallVec<[usize; 16]>`.
- `mod.rs`: `pub mod scrubber;` and place the element in the strip slot.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** offsets 45 s, 125 s, 3,723 s **When** `time_label` runs **Then** it writes "-0:45", "-2:05", "-1:02:03".
- **Given** durations 45 s, 125 s, 3,720 s **When** `span_label` runs **Then** it writes "45s", "2m 05s", "1h 02m".
- **Given** labels 40 px wide every 30 px **When** `drop_overlapping` runs **Then** every second label is kept.
- **Given** the same view, size and range twice **When** painted twice **Then** geometry is built once (geometry build counter, feature `test-hooks`).
- **Given** a new `HistoryView` version **When** painted **Then** geometry is rebuilt once.
- **Given** a gap in the view **When** painted **Then** a hatched band covers its x range (render test).

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/scrubber.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/mod.rs`: wire it
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_history.rs`: add tests

## Tests
- `scrubber::tests::scrubber_time_label_formats`, `span_label_formats`, `labels_drop_overlaps`; `tests/ui_history.rs::scrubber_geometry_cached_until_key_changes`, `scrubber_draws_gap_band` (painted quads or headless capture per ADR-013).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: NaN points split runs (gap), never drawn as zero.
- Accessibility: the header text states the time; the strip is decorative for screen readers.
- Performance: no path building when only the hover hairline moves; `ShapedLine`s are reused. The `history-scrub` scene (E30-028) measures this; target p99 ≤ 4 ms per scrub frame (UI-PRC-032).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Follow `ChartElement` (E19-A1) for the `Element` lifecycle and the `ChartGeometryKey` idea; do not copy code, reuse its helpers (`chart/geometry.rs`, `chart/grid.rs`) where they fit.
- Large-file rule applies (the element is large).

description:
## Context
Pointer and keyboard interaction for the timeline strip: click or drag to scrub, wheel zoom around the cursor, pan, Shift+drag range selection with resizable bounds, double-click to return to live, and a focus ring when the strip has focus (UI-PRC-032, PROC-089). Sources: UI-PRC-032, PROC-089, table (b), UI-PRC-030 (query coalescing while dragging).

## Deliverable
- In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/scrubber.rs` (pointer events registered with `window.on_mouse_event` in `paint`, as ADR-009 charts do):
  - Left click or drag in the plot: dispatch `HistoryScrub { t }` with `t` snapped to whole seconds. While dragging the handle the grip grows to 12 × 12 and the cursor is `ew-resize`.
  - Wheel (no modifier): zoom around the cursor time by a factor 1.25 per notch (in: span / 1.25, out: span × 1.25), the cursor's time stays under the cursor, span clamped to 60 s..retained span (whole span when shorter than 60 s).
  - Shift+wheel or middle-button drag: pan; cursor `grabbing` while dragging; the view range is clamped inside `span`.
  - Shift+left drag: range selection, dispatch `HistorySetRange { from, to }` (from < to, snapped to seconds). Dragging a bound grip resizes that bound. A click without Shift clears the range.
  - Double-click: dispatch `HistoryLive`.
  - Hover: sets the hover x for the hairline and the top-3 card (E30-023); hidden while dragging and after a wheel event until the pointer moves.
  - Focus: click gives focus; the strip is in the Tab order after the header controls; focused draws a 1 px `accent` inset ring.
- `HistoryPage` handles `HistoryScrub` (set `scrub`, clear nothing else), `HistorySetRange` (set `range`), and updates `view_range` from zoom and pan; each change calls the query controller (E30-017), which coalesces while dragging.
- Pure helpers with unit tests: `fn zoom(view: (TimeNs, TimeNs), cursor: TimeNs, notches: f32, span: (TimeNs, TimeNs)) -> (TimeNs, TimeNs)`, `fn pan(view, delta_ns: i64, span) -> (TimeNs, TimeNs)`, `fn x_to_t(x: f32, width: f32, view) -> TimeNs`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a 10-minute view and the cursor at its middle **When** zooming in one notch **Then** the span is 480 s and the cursor time is unchanged.
- **Given** a 70 s view **When** zooming in 3 notches **Then** the span is 60 s (clamped).
- **Given** a view at the newest edge **When** panning forward **Then** the view does not move past `span.1`.
- **Given** a click at x = 25% of the width **When** handled **Then** `HistoryScrub` carries the second at 25% of the view.
- **Given** Shift+drag from 20% to 40% **When** released **Then** `HistorySetRange` carries those seconds and the header shows the range text.
- **Given** a double-click **When** handled **Then** the page is live.
- **Given** the strip focused **When** rendered **Then** the focus ring is drawn.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/scrubber.rs`: interaction
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/mod.rs`: handlers
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_history.rs`: add tests

## Tests
- `scrubber::tests::scrubber_zoom_clamps_and_keeps_cursor_time`, `pan_clamped_to_span`, `x_to_t_maps`; `tests/ui_history.rs::click_scrubs_snapped`, `shift_drag_sets_range`, `double_click_returns_live`, `strip_focus_ring`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: every pointer gesture has a key path (E30-018); focus ring 1 px `accent`.
- Performance: pointer moves notify only the strip entity (UI-PRC-032); geometry is not rebuilt for hover.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-history`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec of your files only: `git add <files> && git commit -m "..." -- <files>`. Never a bare `git commit`, never change branch or history.

## Reference

### tl-model history types this bead uses (R-156 item 3)

The tl-model history types (R-156 item 3). E03-062 (tasklens-as2.28) puts `HistoryMetric`, `HistoryRange` and the view types in `tl-model/src/history.rs`; E03-063 (tasklens-as2.29) puts `HistoryWhat` and the two history commands in `tl-model/src/command.rs`. `HistoryRange::Span` has the fields `from` and `to`. Use exactly these:

```rust
// history.rs (E03-062)
pub enum HistoryMetric { Cpu, Memory, Disk, Network, Gpu }          // chip order; keys 1..5
pub enum HistoryRange { Live, At(TimeNs), Span { from: TimeNs, to: TimeNs } }
// command.rs (E03-063)
pub enum HistoryWhat {
    Frame { metric: HistoryMetric, view: (TimeNs, TimeNs), keys: Arc<[ProcessKey]>, overview: bool },
    TopAt { t: TimeNs, metric: HistoryMetric, n: u8 },
}
// Command::HistoryQuery { id: u64, range: HistoryRange, what: HistoryWhat }, Command::HistoryDelete { keys: Arc<[ProcessKey]> } (ADR-005)

pub enum HistorySource { None, RollingWindow, Store }
pub enum HistoryStoreState { Off, Loading, Ready, Problem(HistoryLoadProblem) }
pub enum HistoryLoadProblem { OpenFailed, EmptyOrTruncated, VersionMismatch, NoInRange, Stale, TimedOut }
pub struct HistoryPoint { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub min: f32, pub max: f32 }
pub struct HistorySeries { pub key: Option<ProcessKey>, pub metric: HistoryMetric, pub points: Arc<[HistoryPoint]> } // None = system total
pub struct HistoryStackBucket { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub top: [f32; 3], pub other: f32 }
pub struct HistoryPeaks { pub cpu_pct: f32, pub mem_anon_bytes: u64, pub disk_bps: f32, pub net_bps: f32, pub gpu_pct: f32 }
pub struct HistoryProcessRow {
    pub key: ProcessKey, pub name: Arc<str>, pub comm: Arc<str>, pub user: Arc<str>, pub exe: Option<Arc<str>>,
    pub app_id: Option<Arc<str>>, pub system: bool, pub present: bool, pub previous_boot: bool,
    pub cpu_pct: f32, pub mem_anon_bytes: u64, pub disk_bps: f32, pub net_bps: f32, pub gpu_pct: f32,
    pub peak: Option<HistoryPeaks>,          // Some only for a Span range
}
pub struct HistoryTotals { pub cpu_pct: f32, pub mem_used_bytes: u64, pub mem_total_bytes: u64 } // averages over a Span (R-169 OI-5)
pub struct HistoryTopRow { pub key: ProcessKey, pub name: Arc<str>, pub app_id: Option<Arc<str>>, pub value: f32 }
pub struct HistoryTop { pub query_id: u64, pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub metric: HistoryMetric, pub cpu_total_pct: f32,
                        pub mem_total_bytes: u64, pub rows: Arc<[HistoryTopRow]> }
pub struct HistoryView {
    pub header: ComponentHeader,
    pub query_id: u64,                       // id of the Frame query this answers
    pub source: HistorySource,
    pub store_state: HistoryStoreState,
    pub span: Option<(TimeNs, TimeNs)>,      // oldest and newest retained frame
    pub gaps: Arc<[(TimeNs, TimeNs)]>,       // inside the requested view
    pub frame_t: Option<TimeNs>,             // the second the rows describe (None for a Span)
    pub range: HistoryRange,
    pub process_count: u32,                  // processes alive at frame_t
    pub rows: Arc<[HistoryProcessRow]>,
    pub totals: Option<HistoryTotals>,
    pub series: Arc<[HistorySeries]>,        // system total of the metric, then one per requested key
    pub stack: Arc<[HistoryStackBucket]>,    // top-3 plus other, same buckets as series (R-169 OI-5, D-020)
    pub overview: Arc<[HistoryPoint]>,       // whole span, system total of the metric; empty unless overview was asked
    pub top: Option<Arc<HistoryTop>>,        // latest TopAt answer
    pub realtime_offset_ns: i64,             // CLOCK_REALTIME minus CLOCK_BOOTTIME, for wall-clock labels
}
```

Values: rates in bytes per second, memory in bytes, CPU in percent of the whole machine (0..=100), GPU in percent. Every point list holds at most 1,024 points (ADR-012), decimated min/max per bucket as ADR-009 (absolute bucket boundaries: bucket `i` covers `[floor(t / w) * w, +w)` with `w = ceil((view.1 - view.0) / 1024)` rounded up to whole seconds).

title: E30-023 History top-3 hover card
description:
## Context
Hovering the timeline shows a card with the time and the top 3 processes for the active metric at that second (PROC-090, UI-PRC-034, R-063). The engine rebuilds the sweep at that second and ranks it (50 ms budget); the UI debounces pointer moves by 32 ms and keeps one TopAt query in flight. Sources: UI-PRC-034, PROC-090, R-063, table (d) formats.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/hover.rs`:
  - `TopController`: on hover at second `t`, waits 32 ms without a new pointer move, then sends `Command::HistoryQuery { id, range: At(t), what: TopAt { t, metric, n: 3 } }`; at most one in flight, a newer request replaces the pending one (same rule as E30-017).
  - The card renders as a deferred overlay (`defer_draw`) from cached `ShapedLine`s, styled like `TlTooltip`: `menu_bg`, 1 px `divider`, `r_sm`, padding `sp4`, `t_sm`, width 260. Anchor: 12 px right of the hover hairline and 8 px below the strip top; flips to the left of the hairline when it would cross the right edge.
  - Lines: first "<HH:MM:SS>  (<offset>)" with the time in `t_sm` semibold `text_primary` and the offset in `text_secondary`, offset as a short age "-4m 12s" (table (d) short-age form with a leading minus); second "CPU total <value>" in `text_secondary` (CPU total at t, one decimal percent); a divider; then up to 3 rows 20 px high: rank, 16 px icon, "<name> (<pid>)", value right-aligned with tabular numbers.
  - Value formats per metric (R-063): "CPU: 12.3%", "Memory: 1.22 / 62.70 GiB" (process RssAnon over `mem_total_bytes`, IEC two decimals), "Disk: 4.2 MiB/s", "Network: 12.0 Mbps" (in the chosen `units.network` unit), "GPU: 41.0%". Fewer than 3 processes: fewer rows.
  - While waiting: the previous card stays; after 150 ms without an answer for the current second the rows read "…".
  - Shown while the pointer is over the plot and not dragging; hidden on leave, on drag start and on wheel. A click sets the scrub time (E30-022).
- `mod.rs`: `pub mod hover;`.
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl` (chain edit): `history-top-cpu-total` "CPU total { $value }", `history-top-cpu` "CPU: { $value }", `history-top-memory` "Memory: { $used } / { $total }", `history-top-disk` "Disk: { $value }", `history-top-network` "Network: { $value }", `history-top-gpu` "GPU: { $value }".

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a TopAt answer for CPU with values 12.3, 6.1, 2.0 **When** the card renders **Then** the rows read "CPU: 12.3%", "CPU: 6.1%", "CPU: 2.0%" in rank order.
- **Given** Memory with 1,310,000,000 bytes and total 67,320,000,000 **When** rendered **Then** the value reads "Memory: 1.22 / 62.70 GiB".
- **Given** `units.network = "bits"` and 1,500,000 B/s **When** rendered **Then** the value reads "Network: 12.0 Mbps".
- **Given** pointer moves every 10 ms for 100 ms **When** they stop **Then** exactly one TopAt query is sent 32 ms after the last move.
- **Given** the hairline 100 px from the right edge **When** the card would overflow **Then** it is placed left of the hairline.
- **Given** no answer for 150 ms **When** rendered **Then** the rows read "…".

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/hover.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/mod.rs`: wire it
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append keys (chain edit, E16)
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_history.rs`: add tests

## Tests
- `tests/ui_history.rs::top3_card_formats_per_metric`, `top3_query_debounced_and_coalesced`, `top3_card_flips_at_right_edge`, `top3_stale_rows_after_150ms`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: the same ranking is readable in the table sorted by the metric (UI-PRC-034).
- Performance: at most one query per 32 ms; the card re-shapes only when its text changes.
- Privacy: N/A

title: E30-024 History minimap
description:
## Context
The minimap under the strip shows the whole retained span of the active metric's system total with a viewport box marking the strip's visible range; dragging the box pans the strip and dragging an edge zooms (UI-PRC-033, PROC-089). Sources: UI-PRC-033, PROC-089, UI-PRC-036 (recording-off span).

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/minimap.rs`: custom `Element`, 24 high, full width, `list_bg`, 1 px `divider` top border.
  - One area path of `HistoryView.overview` (the active metric's `graph.*` fill at 50% alpha, no line), cached by the overview's identity and the size.
  - Viewport box over `view_range`: 1 px `accent` border, `accent` at 15% fill, 4 px edge grips; hover: border 2 px. The scrub time as a 1 px `accent` tick.
  - Interaction: drag the box to pan (cursor `grab`, `grabbing` while dragging); drag an edge to zoom (`ew-resize`), span clamped to 60 s..retained span; click outside the box centres it there; wheel zooms like the strip (factor 1.25 per notch, E30-022 `zoom`).
  - Recording off: the span is the 10-minute window, so the box fills the whole map when the strip shows everything.
- `mod.rs`: `pub mod minimap;` and place it in the 24 px slot.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a 6 h span and a 10-minute view at the end **When** rendered **Then** the box covers the last 1/36 of the width.
- **Given** a drag of the box by 10% of the width **When** released **Then** the strip's `view_range` moved by 10% of the span.
- **Given** dragging the left edge to the right **When** released **Then** the view span shrank and its right edge did not move.
- **Given** a click outside the box **When** handled **Then** the box is centred at the click.
- **Given** only `view_range` changes **When** repainted **Then** the overview path is not rebuilt.

- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_history.rs`: add tests

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: NaN points are gaps in the area.
- Accessibility: duplicates the strip's pan and zoom; keyboard users use the strip keys.

title: E30-025 History legend chips and process series
description:
## Context
Legend chips in the header line choose the active metric (exactly one: CPU, Memory, Disk, Network, GPU) and list the selected processes whose series are drawn, each with an × to clear it (UI-PRC-035, PROC-088 `history.process.clear`). Sources: UI-PRC-035, PROC-088, UI-FND-010 (`Segment { on }` look).

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/legend.rs`:
  - Five metric chips, `TlButton::Segment { on }`, 24 high, `t_sm`, padding `sp4`, `r_sm`, labels "CPU", "Memory", "Disk", "Network", "GPU". The active chip shows an 8 × 8 dot in the metric's `graph.*_line` colour before the label and the `Segment { on }` look (`accent` at alpha 0.25, 1 px `accent` border). Radio behaviour: clicking a chip dispatches the matching `HistoryMetric*` action (E30-018).
  - Process chips after the metric chips: "<name> (<pid>) ×" for each selected key in selection order, at most 8 visible, then "+N" for the rest; the dot colour is the series colour k (accent hue rotated by `k × 45°`, E30-021). Clicking × dispatches `HistoryClearProcess { key }`, which removes the key from `selected` and deselects the table row.
  - Hover: chip background `row_hover`.
- `HistoryPage` handles `HistoryClearProcess`.
- `mod.rs`: `pub mod legend;` and place it at the right of the header line, after the Live button (E30-026).
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl` (chain edit): `history-chip-cpu` "CPU", `history-chip-memory` "Memory", `history-chip-disk` "Disk", `history-chip-network` "Network", `history-chip-gpu` "GPU", `history-chip-more` "+{ $count }".

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** default state **When** rendered **Then** exactly one metric chip (CPU) is on.
- **Given** a click on Memory **When** handled **Then** Memory is on, CPU is off, and a query with `metric = Memory` is wanted.
- **Given** a selected row **When** rendered **Then** a chip "firefox (4321) ×" appears; clicking × removes the chip and deselects the row.
- **Given** 10 selected rows **When** rendered **Then** 8 process chips and "+2" show.
- **Given** 8 series **When** their colours are compared **Then** all 8 differ.

title: E30-A3 History mode UI
description:
## Context
Anchor E30-A3: History mode works inside the Processes tab. This bead mounts `HistoryPage` in place of the live table while `state.toml [processes] history_mode` is true, handles the toggle, and adds the end-to-end UI tests. The mount and toggle handling are the chain edit 00-epics.md section 2 gives E30 in `pages/processes/mod.rs`. Sources: UI-PRC-030, UI-SHL-023, PROC-088, D-010, R-023, UI-SHL-140 area of shell.md (Ctrl pause freezes the history table), ADR-009.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs` (E22-owned, chain edit; the only change this bead makes there):
  - When `UiState.processes.history_mode` is true, the tab content renders the `HistoryPage` entity (created on first entry, dropped when the mode turns off) instead of the live table; the live table entity is kept, not rebuilt.
  - A handler for `ToggleHistoryMode` (the Action E20 declares in `crates/tl-ui/src/actions.rs`; the window-level part that selects the Processes tab is E20's, UI-SHL-023): flips `history_mode` through `TlSettings::update` (persisted in `state.toml`), and on turning on with `history.enabled = false` triggers the once-per-session recording-off toast (E30-026).
  - While History mode is shown, the page's demand keeps `Demand.process_table = true`, so the engine keeps the rolling window (D-010).
  - While Ctrl is held (Ctrl pause), the history table renders from the paused snapshot like the live table (shell.md: pages that freeze include the history table).
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_history.rs`: end-to-end cases with the fake engine (E16 `testing/fake_engine.rs`), which records commands and returns scripted `HistoryView`s.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the Processes tab live **When** `ToggleHistoryMode` is dispatched **Then** the history layout (header, strip, minimap, table) replaces the live table, `history_mode` is true in the saved state, and a `HistoryQuery` with `range = Live` and `overview = true` is sent.
- **Given** History mode **When** toggled off **Then** the live table shows with its previous scroll position and selection, and the `HistoryPage` entity is dropped.
- **Given** recording off **When** History mode turns on **Then** the toast "History recording is off" appears once and `Demand.process_table` stays true.
- **Given** `history_mode = true` in `state.toml` at start **When** the window opens **Then** History mode shows at once.
- **Given** Ctrl held **When** a new `HistoryView` arrives **Then** the history table does not change until Ctrl is released.
- **Given** the full History mode **When** a scripted session scrubs, selects a range, picks Memory, selects two rows and deletes one **Then** the commands sent are, in order: Live Frame, At Frame, Span Frame, Span Frame with Memory, Span Frame with two keys, HistoryDelete with one key.

## Files

- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_history.rs`: end-to-end tests

## Tests

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: focus moves to the history table on entry and back to the live table on exit.
- Performance: the live table entity is not rebuilt on toggle; only `HistoryPage` is created or dropped.

title: Tests: history store test files under CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR, not /tmp
description:
Files: crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_history.rs (and any history unit test that uses std::env::temp_dir()).
Why: 8fx.17's store tests write under std::env::temp_dir(), which is /tmp (tmpfs on the owner machine; the house rule is no build or scratch output in /tmp).
Deliverable: integration tests use env!("CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR"); unit tests use a path under the target dir (for example from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/../../target/tmp). Each test still removes its folder.
AC: grep for temp_dir() under crates/tl-engine finds no test use. lab_history passes.
close_reason: tl-engine test files now go under the target dir (CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR in lab_history, target/tmp in gpu and actions unit tests), commit aa05e85

title: tl-history rolling window: keep the device catalog after the first block is dropped
description:
Files: crates/tl-history/src/rolling.rs and/or crates/tl-history/src/block.rs (and their tests).
Why: 8fx.18 found that BlockBuilder writes the device catalog only into the first block, or when the catalog changes. RollingWindow drops that block after 10 minutes. From then on system_series returns nothing: no system total series, no totals, no CPU total in the history hover. Store mode is fine because it loads one segment back.
Deliverable: the rolling window always holds a block with the current catalog. For example, mark the catalog due again when the window drops its oldest block, so the next sealed block carries it. Do not grow every block with the catalog.
AC: Given a RollingWindow fed sweeps for 11 minutes with an unchanged device catalog, when system_series is read for the last 5 minutes, then it returns the CPU total series with no empty result. Existing tl-history tests pass. clippy -p tl-history --all-targets -D warnings clean.
close_reason: RollingWindow keeps the catalog of the newest dropped block and puts the catalog in effect into the first block blocks() returns; stored blocks do not grow. Test catalog_survives_block_drop. Commit fe62a11

title: tl-history read::stack: rank single-sweep buckets without a HashMap
description:
Files: crates/tl-history/src/read.rs.
Why: 8fx.18's release test (10-minute Frame on 2,000 processes, budget 50 ms) took 75 ms at load 55 on 32 cores. About 56 ms was in read::stack, which does one HashMap insert per process per sweep. The test is #[ignore]d with that reason in crates/tl-engine (history_query.rs).
Deliverable: when a time bucket holds a single sweep, rank that sweep directly, with no HashMap. Keep results identical.
AC: A unit test shows single-sweep and multi-sweep buckets give the same ranking as before. Un-ignore the 8fx.18 release budget test and it passes under 50 ms when the machine load average is below 8 (say the measured time and load in the close comment; if the machine is busy, report the number and leave it ignored with the reason).
close_reason: read::stack keeps a bucket's first sweep in a plain Vec and only builds the HashMap on a second sweep, so 1 s buckets never hash (a3a0aa9). New test compares single-sweep (600 s) and two-sweep (1800 s) buckets, with and without deleted keys, against the old HashMap ranking. Un-ignored frame_answer_within_budget (bd7c9a3): 17 ms and 12 ms (top 3 ms, 1 ms) at load average 31 and 50 on 32 cores, down from 75 ms. Load never dropped below 8, so no quiet-machine number.

title: Tests: lab_processes fixture dir unique per run so parallel runs do not clash
description:
Files: crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_processes.rs (and its fixture helper if separate).
Why: two agents saw lab_processes fail with NotFound or "Directory not empty" when two cargo test runs of it overlapped; it uses one shared fixture directory. A rerun passed.
Deliverable: each test (and each process run) builds its fixture under a unique directory below CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR (for example with the pid and a counter), and removes it at the end.
AC: running `cargo test -p tl-engine --test lab_processes` twice at the same time passes both runs (show it with two background runs). No path under /tmp.
close_reason: lab_processes fixture dir is now lab-processes-<pid>-<n> under CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR and is removed on drop; 20 runs of 4 at a time all passed. Commit 5f3d4e9

title: Tests: probe_integration spawn_fd3_env_and_fds flakes (extra fd 5, empty env)
description:
Files: crates/tl-engine/tests/probe_integration.rs, and crates/tl-engine/src/gpu/spawn.rs if the cause is there.
Why: during parallel test runs on 2026-10-06, spawn_fd3_env_and_fds failed twice: once an extra open fd 5 in the child, once the child's environment came back empty. Both passed on rerun. ndy.16 added close_range CLOEXEC (R-290) in the probe; a test-process fd opened by another test thread between fork and exec may still leak if CLOEXEC is not set on it.
Deliverable: find the cause (an fd opened without O_CLOEXEC in the test binary, or a race in the env check), fix it in code, not by retrying.
AC: the test passes 200 times in a row under `cargo test -p tl-engine --test probe_integration -- --test-threads 8` (a loop script is fine). Explain the cause in the close comment.
close_reason: 600f7cc. Two test races, no spawn bug. (1) Extra fd 5: tl-gpu-probe's open_fd runs before the first read and keeps a pidfd_getfd copy of fd 3, so fd 5 is always there once the probe reaches main; the test only passed when it read /proc/<pid>/fd before that. (2) Empty env: std's spawn returns when exec closes the CLOEXEC error pipe (begin_new_exec), before the ELF loader sets mm->env_end, so /proc/<pid>/environ reads empty in that window (Python check: 1235 of 2000 immediate reads were empty). Fix: spawn_fd3_env_and_fds and spawn.rs child_env_is_minimal do the Hello round trip before reading /proc; the fd check accepts exactly one extra fd that is the fd 3 socket. 200 runs of probe_integration with --test-threads 8: spawn_fd3_env_and_fds passed 200/200; one run failed in client_segv_is_exited_signal_11 (Deadline 500ms), a separate flake from systemd-coredump holding the crashing fake probe.

title: tl-gpu-probe fake crash: disable core dumps so tests do not wait on systemd-coredump
description:
Files: crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/fake.rs.
Why: 8fx.36 found 438 tl-gpu-probe core dumps from 2026-10-06 tests. Every fake crash runs systemd-coredump, and the crashing probe keeps its socket open until the dump is read, so on a busy machine client_segv_is_exited_signal_11 hits its 500 ms deadline (Deadline instead of Exited("signal 11")). The dumps also fill the coredump store.
Deliverable: the fake crash script calls prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0) (or sets RLIMIT_CORE to 0) on itself just before it crashes. Production probe code unchanged.
AC: client_segv_is_exited_signal_11 passes 200 times in a row with --test-threads 8; coredumpctl list shows no new tl-gpu-probe entries after the run (count before and after). Report the count in the close comment. Do not delete existing core dumps; tell the leader the count instead.
close_reason: 8c44411: fake segv() calls prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0) via rustix set_dumpable_behavior (safe, no unsafe) before SIGSEGV. client_segv_is_exited_signal_11 passed 200/200 with --test-threads 8. coredumpctl tl-gpu-probe entries: 438 before, 438 after (also after the full probe_integration run). Existing 438 dumps left in place.

title: History page: send a query when the view range, metric or selection changes while scrubbed
description:
Files: crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/mod.rs, crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_history.rs.
Why: 8fx.20 (82cc143) sends queries on scrub, range, mode entry and the live 1 s tick. set_view_range, a metric change and a selection change send nothing on their own. While live the next tick covers it; while scrubbed or with a range set there is no tick, so the strip and table keep stale data until the user scrubs again.
Deliverable: setters for view_range, metric and selected that update HistoryUiState and call the controller's want() with the current scrub or range, only when the value actually changed. One query in flight still holds: a newer want replaces the pending one.
AC: with a scrub set and no tick running, changing each of the three sends exactly one query; setting the same value again sends none; while live nothing extra is sent beyond the tick. clippy clean for tl-ui with and without test-hooks.
close_reason: set_view_range, set_metric, set_selected send one query while scrubbed or ranged, none while live; commits ffa7653, 6bfb30f

title: History page: apply the filter text that was set before History mode started
description:
Files: crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/history/mod.rs, crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_history.rs.
Why: 8fx.22 (8afec71) makes the History table listen for FilterChanged on the Processes tab, but a filter typed before History mode starts is not applied until the next change. The user sees an unfiltered history table under a filled filter box.
Deliverable: when the page is created (or History mode turns on), read the current filter text from the filter global or the FilterBox and apply it once.
AC: a test types a filter, then turns on History mode, and sees only matching rows; clearing the filter shows all rows. clippy clean for tl-ui with and without test-hooks.

title: E30-001 tl-history crate skeleton, HistoryError and workspace members line

title: E30-002 History format types and segment header codec
description:
## Context
Defines the on-disk and in-RAM history types and the segment header codec in `tl-history/src/format.rs` (ADR-012 "Format"). Everything else in the crate builds on these types. The ADR fixes the field lists; R-169 OI-2 and OI-3 settle the added fields, the byte offsets, the footer layout and the `FieldPatch` shape (see Reference). Sources: ADR-012, ADR-003 (ids, `ProcessKey`, `SeriesId`, `DeviceIdx`, `ProcessRecord`), PROC-086, PROC-087, D-004, R-005, R-025.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-history/src/format.rs` with, all `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]`:
  - constants `MAGIC: [u8; 4] = *b"TLH\x01"`, `FOOTER_MAGIC: [u8; 4] = *b"TLHF"`, `FORMAT_VERSION: u16 = 1`, `HEADER_LEN: usize = 64`, `BLOCK_SECS: u64 = 60`, `SEGMENT_SECS: u64 = 600`, `ZSTD_LEVEL: i32 = 3`, `CPU_THRESHOLD_PERMILLE: u16 = 1`, `MEM_THRESHOLD_KIB: u32 = 256`, `RATE_THRESHOLD_KIBPS: u32 = 1`.
  - `MetaId`, `Block`, `HistMeta`, `HistDevice`, `HistProcess`, `SweepDelta`, `FieldPatch` exactly as in the Reference.
  - `FooterEntry { start_t_ns: u64, offset: u64 }`.
  - `SegmentHeader { boot_id: BootId, realtime_offset_ns: i64, start_t_ns: u64 }` with `fn encode(&self) -> [u8; 64]` and `fn decode(b: &[u8]) -> Result<SegmentHeader, HistoryError>` (wrong magic or length gives `BadHeader`, a version other than 1 gives `Version(v)`, non-zero reserved bytes are ignored).

## Context
The block frame codec: one 60 s `Block` becomes `u32 LE length | u32 LE crc32 | zstd level 3 frame` of postcard bytes, and back (ADR-012). Segments and the rolling window both use it. Decoding must never panic on bad input, because a crashed segment is read up to the first bad CRC. Sources: ADR-012, ADR-013 (proptest: arbitrary bytes never panic), PROC-087.

- `crates/tl-history/src/block.rs`:

title: E30-004 BlockBuilder: keyframes, deltas, 1 Hz system series
description:
## Context
`BlockBuilder` turns the stream of process sweeps and system samples that the reducer's `RecordSink` sees into 60 s `Block`s: a keyframe of every live process at block start, one `SweepDelta` per later sweep with only the changes beyond the thresholds, and 1 Hz system series (ADR-012). The store recorder and the rolling window share it. Sources: ADR-012 (format, thresholds, 1 Hz rule), ADR-003 (`ProcessRecord`, `Sample`, `SampleFlags::GAP_BEFORE`, `DeviceCatalog`), PROC-086 (gaps for suspend, resume and epoch changes).

## Deliverable
- In `crates/tl-history/src/block.rs`, after the codec:

```rust
pub struct BlockBuilder { /* private */ }
impl BlockBuilder {
    pub fn new(boot: BootId) -> Self;
    /// MetaId counter restarts at 0 (store: new segment).
    pub fn reset_meta_scope(&mut self);
    pub fn on_device_catalog(&mut self, catalog: &DeviceCatalog);
    pub fn set_mem_total_kib(&mut self, kib: u64);
    /// Returns a closed block when this call crossed the block boundary.
    pub fn on_process_sweep(&mut self, t_ns: TimeNs, records: &[ProcessRecord]) -> Option<Block>;
    pub fn on_system_sample(&mut self, t_ns: TimeNs, series: &[(SeriesId, Sample)]) -> Option<Block>;
    /// Gap: suspend, resume or engine epoch change. Closes the open block.
    pub fn mark_gap(&mut self, t_ns: TimeNs) -> Option<Block>;
    /// Closes the open block now (shutdown, mode switch).
    pub fn flush(&mut self) -> Option<Block>;
    pub fn open_bytes_estimate(&self) -> usize;
}
```

Rules:
- A block covers `[start, start + 60 s)` where `start` is the boottime of the first sweep or sample in it. The first event at or after `start + 60 s` closes the block and opens the next, whose first sweep becomes its keyframe.
- Keyframe: every record of the first sweep, converted with `format::hist_process`. Later sweeps: records whose `ProcessKey` is new go to `started` (appending indexes); keys that disappeared go to `exited` by index; others go to `changed` only when `FieldPatch::diff` against the last stored value returns `Some`. `dt_ms = (t_ns - start) / 1_000_000`.
- Records with `ProcFlags::EXITED` are treated as gone (not stored).
- Metadata: a `ProcessKey` gets a `MetaId` the first time it is seen in the current scope; `new_meta` of the block holds those first sightings. `HistMeta` fields: `comm`, `name`, `exe_basename` (last path component of `meta.exe`), `app_id`, `exe_path = meta.exe`, `user`, `uid`, `system = matches!(group kind, System)` taken from `ProcFlags::KERNEL_THREAD | OTHER_USER` or the System group (use the flag test `KERNEL_THREAD || OTHER_USER` if the group kind is not reachable from the record; R-169 OI-2). Never `cmdline`.
- System series: per `SeriesId`, one point per boottime second, value = max of the samples in that second; a sample without `SampleFlags::VALID` or with `GAP_BEFORE` writes a `f32::NAN` point for its second.
- `catalog` is `Some` in the first block after `reset_meta_scope` and in the first block after `on_device_catalog` saw a new `version`; `None` otherwise. `HistDevice.kind` follows the `DeviceIdentity` variant order (0 CpuPackage .. 8 Battery).
- `mark_gap` closes the open block (returns it) and sets `gap_before = true` on the next block.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 70 one-second sweeps of the same 10 processes with constant values **When** fed in order **Then** exactly one block is returned (at sweep 61) with 10 keyframe entries, 59 deltas and every delta's `changed`, `started` and `exited` empty.
- **Given** a sweep where one process's CPU goes from 10.0% to 10.05% **When** the next sweep is added **Then** no patch is written for it (0.5 permille is under the threshold).
- **Given** a new key in sweep 3 and a vanished key in sweep 4 **When** the block closes **Then** delta 2 has one `started` entry with index 10 and delta 3 has `exited = [index of the vanished key]`.
- **Given** 10 CPU samples in one second with values 1..=10 **When** the block closes **Then** the CPU series holds one point with value 10.0 for that second.
- **Given** a sample with `GAP_BEFORE` **When** the block closes **Then** that second's point is NaN.
- **Given** an open block **When** `mark_gap` is called **Then** it returns the block and the next returned block has `gap_before = true`.
- **Given** the first block after `reset_meta_scope` **When** it closes **Then** `catalog` is `Some` and later blocks with the same catalog version have `None`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-history/src/block.rs`: add `BlockBuilder` and its tests

## Tests
- `block::tests::steady_state_has_empty_deltas`, `sub_threshold_change_not_stored`, `started_and_exited_indexes`, `system_series_per_second_max`, `gap_sample_writes_nan`, `mark_gap_closes_and_flags_next`, `catalog_only_when_changed`, `meta_assigned_once_per_scope`, `no_cmdline_in_meta`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A (no I/O).
- Validity: invalid fields convert to 0 (format rules).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: the builder keeps a `HashMap<ProcessKey, (u32 index, HistProcess)>` of last stored values; per sweep it allocates only the delta vectors. 2,000 records per sweep must convert in under 1 ms in release (checked in E30-A1's bench-style test).
- Privacy: `cmdline` is never read.

## Context

This is the core of every history query, from the store and from the rolling window. Sources: ADR-012, PROC-088, PROC-090, UI-PRC-031.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-history/src/read.rs`:

```rust

impl MetaTable { pub fn absorb(&mut self, b: &Block); pub fn get(&self, id: MetaId) -> Option<&HistMeta>; }

pub fn state_at(b: &Block, t_ns: TimeNs) -> Option<Frame>;
/// Iterates every sweep state in the block in order (keyframe first).
pub fn for_each_state(b: &Block, f: impl FnMut(&Frame));
```

title: E30-006 History read side: decimation, top-K, system totals, deleted keys
description:
## Context
The rest of the read side: min/max decimation of system and process series to at most 1,024 points, the top-K processes at one second for the hover card, system totals at a second, and the deleted-keys filter (ADR-012 reading rules, PROC-089, PROC-090, R-103). Sources: ADR-012, ADR-009 (decimation with absolute buckets), PROC-088 to PROC-090, R-063, R-103.

## Deliverable
- In `crates/tl-history/src/read.rs`:

```rust
pub const MAX_POINTS: usize = 1024;
pub enum Metric { Cpu, Memory, Disk, Network, Gpu }   // mirrors tl_model::command::HistoryMetric
pub struct Point { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub min: f32, pub max: f32 }
/// Bucket width w = max(1 s, ceil((to - from) / MAX_POINTS)) rounded up to whole seconds; bucket i covers
/// [floor(t / w) * w, +w) in absolute boottime, so two calls 100 ms apart give the same boundaries.
pub fn bucket_width_ns(from: TimeNs, to: TimeNs) -> u64;
pub fn decimate(points: impl Iterator<Item = (TimeNs, f32)>, from: TimeNs, to: TimeNs) -> Vec<Point>;
/// Per-second value of one process for one metric, from blocks overlapping [from, to].
pub fn process_series<'a>(blocks: impl Iterator<Item = &'a Block>, key: ProcessKey, m: Metric, from: TimeNs, to: TimeNs) -> Vec<Point>;
/// System total of a metric per second from the stored 1 Hz series and the block catalog:
/// Cpu = CPU_TOTAL of the CpuPackage device; Memory = MEM_USED; Disk = sum of DISK_READ + DISK_WRITE over Disk devices
/// with parent None; Network = sum of NET_RX + NET_TX over Net devices; Gpu = max GPU_UTIL over Gpu devices.
pub fn system_series<'a>(blocks: impl Iterator<Item = &'a Block>, m: Metric, from: TimeNs, to: TimeNs) -> Vec<Point>;
/// Per bucket: the three largest per-process values of the metric and "other" as the sum of the rest,
/// drawn stacked in the metric colour (R-169 OI-5, confirmed by the owner in D-020).
pub fn stack<'a>(blocks: impl Iterator<Item = &'a Block>, m: Metric, from: TimeNs, to: TimeNs) -> Vec<(TimeNs, [f32; 3], f32)>;
/// Top n processes at second t, ranked by the metric descending, ties by ProcessKey ascending.
pub fn top_at(frame: &Frame, m: Metric, n: usize) -> Vec<(ProcessKey, MetaId, f32)>;
pub struct DeletedKeys(std::collections::HashSet<ProcessKey>);
impl DeletedKeys { pub fn contains(&self, k: &ProcessKey) -> bool; pub fn insert_all(&mut self, ks: &[ProcessKey]); }
```
- NaN points are gaps: `decimate` never folds a NaN into min or max; a bucket with only NaN is emitted as `min = max = NaN` so the UI draws a gap.
- Every function that returns rows skips keys in `DeletedKeys` (callers pass the set).
- Process metric values: Cpu in percent, Memory in bytes, Disk and Network in bytes per second, Gpu in percent (same conversions as E30-005).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 6 h of 1 Hz points **When** decimated over the whole span **Then** at most 1,024 points come back and each holds the min and max of its bucket.
- **Given** a single spike sample of 100 among zeros **When** decimated **Then** the bucket containing it has `max = 100` (ADR-009: the max spike survives).
- **Given** two calls with `from` 100 ms apart and the same width **When** bucket boundaries are compared **Then** they are identical.
- **Given** a bucket containing only NaN points **When** decimated **Then** that point is NaN.
- **Given** a frame with CPU values 5, 30, 12, 30 for keys k1..k4 (k2 < k4) **When** `top_at(.., Cpu, 3)` runs **Then** it returns k2, k4, k3 in that order.
- **Given** a deleted key **When** `top_at` or `range_stats` callers filter with `DeletedKeys` **Then** the key never appears.
- **Given** a catalog with one CpuPackage and 4 CpuLogical devices **When** `system_series(Cpu)` runs **Then** only the CpuPackage `CPU_TOTAL` points are used.

## Tests

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: NaN marks a gap; nothing else.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: decimation is one pass with no per-point allocation; output `Vec` reserved to `MAX_POINTS`.

- `MetaId` scope (R-169 OI-3): ids are assigned from 0 per segment (store) or per window lifetime (rolling window); `new_meta` of block k holds every id first referenced in block k. A reader of block k loads `new_meta` of blocks `0..=k` of the same segment.
- Command lines are never stored (ADR-015).

description:

title: E08: zbus connection helper with executor tick and timeouts (dbus/mod.rs)
description:
## Context
D-Bus workers (logind, systemd, KWin, udisks, UPower, NetworkManager, the openers) share one connection recipe: a `zbus::Connection` with `internal_executor(false)` driven by a child task that ticks its executor under a 500 ms timeout, every call wrapped in `time::timeout` (2 s for reads) and followed by a checkpoint, proxies that never outlive their generation. zbus futures do not see `Cx` cancellation, so the timeouts are the only cancellation point. Sources: ADR-004 (D-Bus workers), ADR-006 (action deadlines, used by E11), API notes section 9, ADR-001 (`zbus` allowed in `tl-engine`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/dbus/mod.rs`:

```rust
pub const READ_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);
pub const EXECUTOR_TICK: Duration = Duration::from_millis(500);
pub const CONNECT_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum DbusError { #[error("connect: {0}")] Connect(Arc<str>), #[error("timeout after {0:?}")] Timeout(Duration), #[error("{name}: {message}")] Call { name: Arc<str>, message: Arc<str> }, #[error("closed")] Closed }
impl From<DbusError> for WorkerError;   // → WorkerError::Dbus(text)

pub enum Bus { Session, System }
pub struct DbusConn { conn: zbus::Connection, _tick: TaskHandle<()> }   // dropping it ends the tick task
pub async fn connect(cx: &Cx, bus: Bus) -> Result<DbusConn, DbusError>;
impl DbusConn {
    pub fn raw(&self) -> &zbus::Connection;
    /// `time::timeout(cx.now(), d, fut)` then `cx.checkpoint()`; Elapsed → DbusError::Timeout(d)
    pub async fn call<T>(&self, cx: &Cx, d: Duration, fut: impl Future<Output = zbus::Result<T>>) -> Result<T, DbusError>;
    pub async fn read<T>(&self, cx: &Cx, fut: impl Future<Output = zbus::Result<T>>) -> Result<T, DbusError>;   // call with READ_TIMEOUT
    /// Next item of a signal stream with a timeout; Ok(None) on timeout so callers can loop and checkpoint.
    pub async fn next_signal<S: Stream + Unpin>(&self, cx: &Cx, s: &mut S, d: Duration) -> Result<Option<S::Item>, DbusError>;
}
pub fn error_name(e: &zbus::Error) -> Option<&str>;   // "org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.AccessDenied" and friends, for E11 mapping
```

`connect` builds `zbus::connection::Builder::session()` or `::system()` with `.internal_executor(false)`, awaits `.build()` under `CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, then spawns the tick task with `cx.spawn(|cx| async move { loop { let _ = time::timeout(cx.now(), EXECUTOR_TICK, conn.executor().tick()).await; if cx.checkpoint().is_err() { break; } } })`. The `zbus` dependency uses `default-features = false, features = ["async-io"]` (workspace pin, E02).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `call` with a future that never resolves and `d = 10 ms` **When** awaited in a LabRuntime task **Then** it returns `Err(DbusError::Timeout(10 ms))` after exactly 10 ms of virtual time.
- **Given** `call` after the `Cx` was cancelled **When** the inner future resolves **Then** `call` returns `Err(DbusError::Closed)` (checkpoint failed).
- **Given** a `zbus::Error::MethodError` with name `org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.AccessDenied` **When** `error_name` is called **Then** it returns that string.
- **Given** a real session bus (`#[ignore]` test) **When** `connect(Session)` is awaited **Then** `raw().unique_name()` is `Some` and dropping `DbusConn` ends the tick task within 500 ms.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/dbus/mod.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/src/source.rs`: chain edit at `// E08-009: shared`: add `pub shared: crate::dbus::SharedHandles` to `WorkerIo` and its constructor (R-262)
- `crates/tl-engine/Cargo.toml`: `zbus` is already listed by E08-A1

## Tests
- `dbus/mod.rs::tests::call_times_out_in_virtual_time`
- `dbus/mod.rs::tests::call_after_cancel_is_closed`
- `dbus/mod.rs::tests::error_name_extracts_dbus_name`
- `dbus/mod.rs::tests::real_session_connect` (`#[ignore]`, owner machine)

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: every D-Bus failure becomes `DbusError`; workers map it to `Validity::Failed` plus `last_error` unless the bus itself is gone (then `WorkerError::Dbus` restarts the generation).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one executor tick task per connection; at most 5 connections (session, system, plus the KWin and systemd pairs share these two).
- Privacy: log D-Bus error names, never message bodies that carry unit or window names above `debug`.

## Notes
zbus 5 with `async-io` starts its own reactor thread; its futures wake through the std `Waker` and run beside asupersync's reactor (API notes section 9, inferred and to be confirmed by the first real test here). `time::timeout` `time/timeout_future.rs:344`. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

## Shared handles (B3 open item 8, added after the B4 review)
`dbus/mod.rs` also owns the handle type the systemd workers fill and E11 reads:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct ManagerConnSlot(Arc<arc_swap::ArcSwapOption<zbus::Connection>>);
impl ManagerConnSlot { pub fn new() -> Self; pub fn set(&self, conn: Arc<zbus::Connection>); pub fn clear(&self); pub fn get(&self) -> Option<Arc<zbus::Connection>>; }
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct SharedHandles { pub systemd_system: ManagerConnSlot, pub systemd_user: ManagerConnSlot }
```

title: E08-A2 D-Bus helper and logind worker
description:
## Context
Anchor E08-A2 "D-Bus helper and logind worker". The `Logind` worker is the first event-driven worker and the pattern for every D-Bus worker: it subscribes to `PrepareForSleep` on `org.freedesktop.login1.Manager` and sends `SourceUpdate::Sleep { entering }` so the reducer can pause rates and mark gaps (ADR-008 suspend signal 1). It is always on, in `EngineMode::Full` only (the low-memory process has no graphs to gap). Sources: ADR-004 (`Logind` worker row, D-Bus workers), ADR-008 (suspend and resume), E08-009.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/workers/logind.rs`:

```rust
pub const BUS_NAME: &str = "org.freedesktop.login1";
pub const PATH: &str = "/org/freedesktop/login1";
pub const INTERFACE: &str = "org.freedesktop.login1.Manager";
pub const SIGNAL: &str = "PrepareForSleep";
pub fn spec() -> WorkerSpec;   // id: SourceId::Logind, name "logind", modes &[EngineMode::Full]
pub fn factory(_cfg: Arc<EngineConfig>, io: WorkerIo) -> WorkerFactory;
async fn run(cx: Cx, io: WorkerIo) -> Outcome<(), WorkerError>;
```

`run`: `connect(&cx, Bus::System)`, build a `zbus::Proxy` for the interface, `receive_signal(SIGNAL)` → stream; send `Health { Running }`; loop `{ match conn.next_signal(&cx, &mut stream, READ_TIMEOUT).await { Ok(Some(msg)) => { let entering: bool = msg.body().deserialize()?; io.updates.send(&cx, EngineMsg::Source(SourceUpdate::Sleep { entering, t_ns: now_boot_ns() })).await; } Ok(None) => { if cx.checkpoint().is_err() { return Outcome::Ok(()) } } Err(e) => return Outcome::Err(e.into()) } }`. A missing logind (connect error or `NameHasNoOwner`) sends `Health { state: Failed, last_error: "logind not available" }` and returns `Outcome::Err(WorkerError::Dbus(..))`, so the supervisor retries with backoff and the 60 s disable takes over. No tab lists `Logind` as a surface, so the Collector Health chip never shows it (UI-SHL collector health).

`workers/mod.rs::all_workers()` gets the logind entry (this bead, as the owner).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake stream that yields `true` then `false` **When** `run` consumes it under a LabRuntime `Cx` **Then** the channel receives `Sleep { entering: true }` then `Sleep { entering: false }` in that order with increasing `t_ns`.
- **Given** the stream yields nothing for 10 s **When** the `Cx` is cancelled **Then** `run` returns `Outcome::Ok(())` within one `READ_TIMEOUT` (2 s) of the cancel.
- **Given** a real system bus (`#[ignore]`) **When** the worker connects **Then** `Health { Running }` is sent within 5 s and the proxy's `PreparingForSleep` property reads `false`.
- **Given** `workers_for(EngineMode::LowMemory)` **When** called **Then** `Logind` is not in it; `workers_for(Full)` contains it once.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/logind.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/mod.rs`: add `pub mod logind;` and the `WorkerSpec` entry

## Tests
- `workers/logind.rs::tests::sleep_events_in_order` (stream abstraction injected through a `trait SleepSignals`, with a fake in tests)
- `workers/logind.rs::tests::cancel_ends_within_read_timeout`
- `workers/logind.rs::tests::real_logind_connect` (`#[ignore]`)

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: bus loss → `WorkerError::Dbus` → restart with backoff; health `Failed` text "logind not available".
- Validity: N/A (no values)
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one wake per 2 s while idle (the signal timeout loop).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
Depends on E08-A1 and E08-009. The signal body is a single boolean `b`. zbus: `Proxy::new(&conn, BUS_NAME, PATH, INTERFACE)`, `proxy.receive_signal("PrepareForSleep").await` gives a `SignalStream`. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
