title: E08: EngineConfig and EngineMode (config.rs)
description:
## Context
`tl-engine` needs a small configuration type that `tl-app` fills once at start and a mode enum that picks the worker set. ADR-004 fixes `EngineMode::{Full, LowMemory}` (fixed at start; `LowMemory` runs the `Processes` worker with the stripped sweep from `workers/lowmem.rs`, E32, and the `KWin` worker for `KWinCommand::KeepAbove` only, R-152 OI-9). ADR-013 says samplers take a `SysRoot { proc, sys }` so tests can point them at a fixture. ADR-012 puts history under the state directory. Sources: ADR-004 (engine modes), ADR-001 (public API is `EngineConfig`, `Engine::start`, `EngineHandle`, `ShutdownReport`), ADR-013, D-001.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/config.rs`:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum EngineMode { Full, LowMemory }

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct EngineConfig {
    pub mode: EngineMode,
    pub sys_root: tl_collect::SysRoot,      // `/proc` and `/sys` roots; tests pass a fixture
    pub state_dir: std::path::PathBuf,     // `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens`; dumps live under it
    pub history_dir: Option<PathBuf>,      // tl-app sets `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens/history` (ADR-012, R-150 item 3)
    pub helper_path: Option<PathBuf>,      // tl-app sets `/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper` when the file exists (ADR-006, R-150 item 3)
}
impl EngineConfig {
    pub fn new(mode: EngineMode, state_dir: PathBuf) -> Self; // sys_root = SysRoot::real(), history_dir None, helper_path None
    pub fn with_sys_root(self, root: SysRoot) -> Self;
    pub fn with_history_dir(self, dir: PathBuf) -> Self;
    pub fn with_helper_path(self, path: PathBuf) -> Self;
}
```

No asupersync type appears in this file. `Default` is not implemented (the state dir is mandatory).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `EngineConfig::new(EngineMode::Full, "/tmp/x".into())` **When** read **Then** `mode == Full`, `state_dir == "/tmp/x"` and `sys_root` equals `SysRoot::real()`.
- **Given** `with_sys_root(fixture)` **When** read **Then** `sys_root.proc` is the fixture path.
- **Given** `EngineConfig::new(..)` **When** read **Then** `history_dir` and `helper_path` are `None`; after `with_history_dir("/s/h")` and `with_helper_path("/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper")` they hold those paths (R-150 item 3).
- **Given** `cargo doc -p tl-engine` **When** the public items are listed **Then** `EngineConfig` and `EngineMode` are public and name no asupersync type.

## Files

- `config.rs::tests::with_sys_root_overrides`: fixture root is kept.
- `config.rs::tests::optional_paths_default_none`: the R-150 item 3 criterion.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: `state_dir` and `history_dir` are never logged above `debug`.

## Notes
`SysRoot` and its constructor name come from E04-A1 (`crates/tl-collect/src/sysroot.rs`); if the real-root constructor is not `real()`, use the name E04-A1 chose and keep the semantics. The field set is settled: `{ mode, sys_root, state_dir, history_dir, helper_path }` (R-150 item 3, R-166 B3-2). The E30 history worker reads `history_dir`; the E29 helper session reads `helper_path`.

title: E08: build_runtime with the ADR-004 RuntimeBuilder settings
description:
## Context
ADR-004 fixes how the asupersync runtime is built: 1 worker thread, a blocking pool of 1 to 4 threads, thread name prefix `tl-engine`, global queue limit 256. The blocking pool is off by default in asupersync 0.5.0 and must be set, or `Cx::spawn_blocking` runs inline on the async worker (API notes section 2). Sources: ADR-004 (runtime construction, banned APIs), `docs/research/claude-asupersync-apis.md` sections 1, 2, 4.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/runtime.rs`:

```rust
pub const WORKER_THREADS: usize = 1;
pub const BLOCKING_THREADS_MIN: usize = 1;
pub const BLOCKING_THREADS_MAX: usize = 4;
pub const GLOBAL_QUEUE_LIMIT: usize = 256;
pub const THREAD_NAME_PREFIX: &str = "tl-engine";

pub(crate) fn build_runtime() -> Result<asupersync::runtime::Runtime, asupersync::Error> {
    RuntimeBuilder::new()
        .worker_threads(WORKER_THREADS)
        .blocking_threads(BLOCKING_THREADS_MIN, BLOCKING_THREADS_MAX)
        .thread_name_prefix(THREAD_NAME_PREFIX)
        .global_queue_limit(GLOBAL_QUEUE_LIMIT)
        .build()
}
```

The function is `pub(crate)`; no asupersync type leaves the crate (ADR-001 rule 2). `current_thread()` is never called. A doc comment lists the banned asupersync APIs from ADR-004 so readers of this file see them.

`crates/tl-engine/Cargo.toml` gains `asupersync = { workspace = true }` (the workspace pin is `=0.5.0`, `default-features = false`, `features = ["proc-macros"]`) and under `[dev-dependencies]` `asupersync = { workspace = true, features = ["proc-macros", "test-internals"] }`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `build_runtime()` **When** called **Then** it returns `Ok` and `rt.handle()` can `spawn_checked` a task that completes.
- **Given** a task that calls `Cx::spawn_blocking(|_| std::thread::current().name().map(str::to_owned))` **When** joined **Then** the thread name starts with `tl-engine` and is not the async worker's thread.
- **Given** `cargo tree -p tl-engine -e features -i asupersync` **When** run without `--all-targets` **Then** neither `nightly-outcome-try` nor `test-internals` is listed.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/runtime.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/Cargo.toml`: add the asupersync dependency and dev-dependency lines

## Tests
- `runtime.rs::tests::builds_and_runs_a_task`: spawn and join one task.
- `runtime.rs::tests::blocking_pool_is_configured`: the blocking closure runs on a thread whose name starts with `tl-engine` and whose id differs from the async worker's.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `asupersync::Error` from `build()` is returned to `Engine::start` (E09), which maps it to `EngineError::Runtime`.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: 1 async thread; at most 4 blocking jobs at once (ADR-004 consequence).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
API lines (asupersync 0.5.0, `src/runtime/builder.rs`): `RuntimeBuilder::new` L803, `worker_threads` L2659, `blocking_threads` L2789, `thread_name_prefix` L2742, `global_queue_limit` L2749, `build` L3276. Idle blocking threads retire after 10 s. Stable toolchain works with `default-features = false, features = ["proc-macros"]` (API notes section 1).

title: E08: EngineMsg, SourceUpdate (every variant) and WorkerError (update.rs)
description:
## Context
Every worker talks to the reducer with one message type, and every later epic (E09 to E14, E29, E30, E32) compiles against it, so the full variant set is written now and never grows (`00-epics.md` section 2: "`SourceUpdate` carries every variant up front"). The payloads are built from `tl-model` types so the reducer can publish them without copying. Device-bound samples are keyed by `DeviceIdentity`, because `DeviceIdx` is assigned by the reducer's catalog (ADR-003). Sources: ADR-004 (`EngineMsg`, worker list), ADR-003 (component types), ADR-005 (`Command`), ADR-007 (GPU messages), ADR-008 (suspend signals), ADR-015 (`WorkerError`), R-119, R-137.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/update.rs`:

```rust
pub enum EngineMsg {
    Source(SourceUpdate),
    Command(Command),                      // tl_model::command::Command
    ActionFinished { id: ActionId },
    Tick,                                  // housekeeping, sent every 1 s by the session (stale marking, linger expiry)
}

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum WorkerError {
    #[error("collect: {0}")] Collect(#[from] tl_collect::CollectError),
    #[error("d-bus: {0}")] Dbus(Arc<str>),
    #[error("probe: {0}")] Probe(Arc<str>),
    #[error("timeout after {0:?}")] Timeout(Duration),
    #[error("channel closed")] Closed,
    #[error("{0}")] Other(Arc<str>),
}

pub enum SourceUpdate {
    Health { id: SourceId, state: SourceState, last_error: Option<Arc<str>>, t_ns: TimeNs },
    ResumeDetected { id: SourceId, t_ns: TimeNs },        // ADR-008 clock check: Δboot − Δmono > 250 ms
    Sleep { entering: bool, t_ns: TimeNs },               // Logind PrepareForSleep
    Cpu(CpuSample),                                       // E12 Cpu
    Memory(MemorySample),                                 // E12 Memory
    Disks(DiskSample),                                    // E12 Disk
    Nets(NetSample),                                      // E12 Net
    Sensors(SensorSample),                                // E12 Sensors
    Devices(DeviceList),                                  // E12 enumerate (every 5 s)
    Gpu(GpuSample),                                       // E13 GpuNvidia, E12 GpuDrm
    GpuInfo(GpuInfoUpdate),                               // static per-device info
    GpuApiVersions(tl_model::gpu_proto::ApiVersions),     // E13, once at start
    Processes(ProcessSweep),                              // E10 Processes, E32 lowmem
    Details(DetailsUpdate),                               // E10 ProcessDetail and handle search
    Connections(ConnectionsUpdate),                       // E14 Connections
    ConnectionsDestroySupport(bool),                      // E11 SockDestroy answer (sets destroy_supported)
    Services(ServicesUpdate),                             // E14 SystemdSystem / SystemdUser
    Startup(StartupUpdate),                               // E14 Startup
    Inventory(Box<InventorySnapshot>),                    // E12 Inventory (header rewritten by the reducer)
    Windows(Box<WindowsSnapshot>),                        // E14 KWin
    History(Arc<HistoryView>),                            // E30 answer to HistoryQuery
    DeviceDetails(DeviceDetailsUpdate),                   // E12 static and slow device rows (R-139 item 7)
    Helper(HelperUpdate),                                 // E29 helper session state (R-150 item 1)
    Setup(Arc<SetupState>),                               // E29 setup runner (R-150 item 1, R-149 item 4)
    ColorScheme(u8),                                      // E14 portal color-scheme 0, 1, 2 (R-170 item 4)
}

pub enum DeviceDetailsUpdate {                            // R-139 item 7; the reducer merges by field
    Cpu(Arc<CpuStaticInfo>),
    Memory(Arc<MemoryDetails>),
    Disks { from: SourceId, entries: Vec<(DeviceIdentity, DiskDetails)> },   // full list from that source
    Nets { from: SourceId, entries: Vec<(DeviceIdentity, NetDetails)> },
    Batteries(Vec<(DeviceIdentity, BatteryDetails)>),
}
pub struct HelperUpdate { pub state: HelperState, pub start: Option<(u64, HelperStartOutcome)> } // R-150 item 1

pub struct CpuSample { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub totals: CpuTotals, pub irq_pct: f32 /* Δ(irq+softirq)/Δtotal, for the Interrupts row */,
    pub per_cpu: Vec<CpuCoreSample>, pub freq_mhz: Option<u32>, pub temp_c: Option<f32>, pub temp_validity: Validity,
    pub topology: Option<Arc<CpuTopology>> /* Some on first sample and on hotplug */, pub validity: Validity }
pub struct CpuCoreSample { pub cpu: u16, pub pct: f32, pub kernel_pct: f32, pub freq_mhz: Option<u32>, pub validity: Validity }
pub struct MemorySample { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub totals: MemoryTotals, pub zram: Vec<ZramStat>, pub validity: Validity }
pub struct ZramStat { pub name: Arc<str>, pub disksize: u64, pub orig_bytes: u64, pub compr_bytes: u64, pub mem_used_total: u64, pub read_bps: f32, pub write_bps: f32 }
pub struct DiskSample { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub disks: Vec<(DeviceIdentity, DiskTotals)> }
pub struct NetSample { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub nets: Vec<(DeviceIdentity, NetTotals)> }
pub struct SensorSample { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub readings: Vec<(DeviceIdentity, SensorReading)> }
bitflags! { pub struct DeviceKinds: u8 { const CPUS=1; const DISKS=2; const NETS=4; const SENSORS=8; const FANS=16; const GPUS=32; const BATTERIES=64; } }
pub struct DeviceList { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub kinds: DeviceKinds, pub entries: Vec<DeviceDesc> }   // complete list for `kinds`; the reducer diffs
pub struct DeviceDesc { pub identity: DeviceIdentity, pub display_name: Arc<str>, pub parent: Option<DeviceIdentity>,
    pub persistent_key: Arc<str> /* PERF-005 key, computed by the worker (R-155 item 7) */, pub net_kind: Option<NetKind> /* Net only */ }
pub struct GpuSample { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub devices: Vec<(DeviceIdentity, GpuTotals)>, pub processes: Option<Vec<GpuProcessSample>> }
pub struct GpuInfoUpdate { pub devices: Vec<GpuStaticInfo> }
pub struct GpuStaticInfo { pub identity: DeviceIdentity, pub name: Arc<str>, pub mem_total: u64, pub power_limit_mw: Option<u32>, pub driver: Arc<str>, pub nvml: Arc<str>, pub supports_process_util: bool,
    pub persistent_key: Arc<str> /* "gpu:<uuid or PCI slot>" (R-155 items 7 and 8) */ }
pub struct ProcessSweep { pub observed_start: TimeNs, pub observed_end: TimeNs, pub records: Vec<ProcessRecord> /* sorted by key; NEW and EXITED are set by the reducer */,
    pub extras: Vec<ProcessExtras> /* index aligned with records (R-141 item 1) */,
    pub extras_p2: Vec<ProcessExtrasP2> /* index aligned; filled for detail_keys only (R-163 item 2) */,
    pub app_stats: Vec<AppCgroupSample> /* tl-model type (R-141 item 2) */, pub unit_stats: Vec<CgroupStats>, pub system_threads: u32,
    pub file_nr: Option<u64> /* /proc/sys/fs/file-nr; the reducer copies it into TableTotals.handles (R-166 B3-7) */, pub online_cpus: u16,
    pub low_memory: Option<Arc<LowMemoryInfo>> /* Some only from the E32 stripped sweep (R-150 item 2) */ }
pub struct CgroupStats { pub group: GroupKey, pub cgroup: CgroupRef, pub anon_bytes: u64, pub swap_bytes: u64, pub cpu_usage_usec: u64, pub io_rbytes: u64, pub io_wbytes: u64, pub pids_current: u32, pub validity: Validity }
pub enum DetailsUpdate {
    Pss { t_ns: TimeNs, entries: Vec<PssEntry> },
    Tab { target: DetailTarget, tab: DetailTab, payload: Arc<TabPayload>, validity: Validity },
    Affinity { t_ns: TimeNs, entries: Vec<(ProcessKey, AffinityInfo)> },
    HandleSearch(Arc<HandleSearchState>),
}
pub struct PssEntry { pub key: ProcessKey, pub pss_bytes: u64, pub uss_bytes: u64, pub swap_bytes: u64, pub validity: Validity }
pub struct ConnectionsUpdate { pub t_ns: TimeNs, pub records: Vec<ConnectionRecord>, pub validity: Validity }
pub struct ServicesUpdate { pub manager: Manager, pub state: ManagerState, pub units: Vec<UnitRecord>, pub details: Vec<(UnitRef, Arc<UnitDetails>)>, pub backend: ServiceBackend, pub validity: Validity }
pub struct StartupUpdate { pub entries: Vec<StartupEntry>, pub validity: Validity }
```

Every struct derives `Debug, Clone`. `ConnectionRecord`, `UnitRecord`, `UnitDetails`, `ServiceBackend`, `StartupEntry`, `TabPayload`, `AffinityInfo`, `HandleSearchState` are the element types of the matching `tl-model` snapshot components (ADR-003, `snapshot.rs` and `details.rs`); use the exact names E03-A2 chose. `pub fn source_of(&SourceUpdate) -> Option<SourceId>` returns the producing worker (None for `Sleep`, `ConnectionsDestroySupport`, `History`, `Helper`, `Setup`, `ColorScheme`; `DeviceDetails::Disks` and `Nets` return their `from`, `Cpu` gives `Cpu`, `Memory` gives `Memory`, `Batteries` gives `UPower`; `ColorScheme` comes from the portal reader in E14-020, which is not a supervised source). `ProcessExtras`, `ProcessExtrasP2`, `AppCgroupSample`, `LowMemoryInfo` are tl-model types (E03-072); `CpuStaticInfo`, `MemoryDetails`, `DiskDetails`, `NetDetails`, `BatteryDetails` are tl-model types (E03-056); `SetupState` is E03-063; `HelperState`, `HelperStartOutcome` are E03-011.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the crate **When** compiled **Then** every variant above exists with these payload names and no variant is `#[non_exhaustive]`.
- **Given** `size_of::<EngineMsg>()` **When** measured **Then** it is at most 256 bytes (large payloads are boxed or in `Vec`/`Arc`).
- **Given** `SourceUpdate::Cpu(..)` **When** `source_of` is called **Then** it returns `Some(SourceId::Cpu)`; for `Sleep`, `Helper(..)` and `Setup(..)` it returns `None` (R-150 item 1).
- **Given** `SourceUpdate::DeviceDetails(DeviceDetailsUpdate::Disks { from: SourceId::Udisks, .. })` **When** `source_of` is called **Then** it returns `Some(SourceId::Udisks)` (R-139 item 7).
- **Given** a later epic needs a new variant **When** it opens a bead **Then** it depends on E08-A1 and asks the leader; it does not edit this file (owner only).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/update.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/Cargo.toml`: add `bitflags`, `thiserror`, `tl-collect`, `tl-model` (workspace pins)

## Tests
- `update.rs::tests::engine_msg_size`: `size_of::<EngineMsg>() <= 256`.
- `update.rs::tests::source_of_covers_every_variant`: a match with no wildcard arm compiles and returns the table above.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `WorkerError` is the restart signal (`Outcome::Err`); expected conditions (EACCES, missing device, unsupported) are reported as `Validity` inside the payload, never as `WorkerError` (ADR-004).
- Validity: every payload carries `Validity` per device or field; missing is never zero.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: workers build `Vec`s once per sample; the reducer moves them into `Arc<[T]>` without a second copy (`Vec::into()`).
- Privacy: payloads carry `ProcessMeta` text that is already sanitized (E05); `Debug` output of `ProcessSweep` is never logged.

## Notes
This file is the E08-owned contract for B4 (E12, E14), E10, E11, E13, E29, E30 and E32. The payload field sets are the contract for B4 (R-166 B3-3). Every variant is written up front, so E29, E30 and E32 need no edits here (R-150). Large-file rule: commit this file before building.

title: E08: Source trait, WorkerIo, WorkerControl and the sampling loop (source.rs)
description:
## Context
Every periodic worker shares one loop: absolute deadlines from asupersync `interval` with `MissedTickBehavior::Skip`, a fresh `Sleep` each turn, a checkpoint, one `spawn_blocking` job per sample, `IDLE_RECHECK` when the source is off, and the `Late` rule. Workers receive demand and settings through `watch` receivers cloned per generation, and reducer-to-worker control (baseline resets after resume, `RefreshNow`, forwarded commands) through one more `watch` (B3 open item 1). Sources: ADR-004 (worker factory contract, sampling worker loop, `Source` trait), ADR-008 (tick semantics, schedule, hidden detection, suspend signal 1), API notes sections 3 to 5 (`watch` borrow rule, `Sleep` per turn, interval is synchronous).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/source.rs`:

```rust
pub const IDLE_RECHECK: Duration = Duration::from_millis(500);
pub const LATE_FRACTION: f64 = 0.8;      // job longer than 0.8 × period
pub const LATE_COUNT: u32 = 3;           // ... for 3 consecutive jobs → SourceState::Late

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct WorkerIo {
    pub updates: mpsc::Sender<EngineMsg>,            // asupersync mpsc, capacity 256, shared with the UI command path
    pub demand: watch::Receiver<Demand>,
    pub settings: watch::Receiver<EngineSettings>,
    pub control: watch::Receiver<WorkerControl>,
}
#[derive(Clone, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct WorkerControl {
    pub reset_generation: u64,                       // bumped on resume and on Command::ResetBaselines
    pub commands: Arc<[QueuedCommand]>,              // newest 64 forwarded commands, ascending seq
}
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
pub struct QueuedCommand { pub seq: u64, pub target: SourceId, pub command: WorkerCommand }
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub enum WorkerCommand {
    RefreshNow, Reprobe,
    KWin(KWinCommand),
    DetailRefresh { target: DetailTarget, tab: DetailTab }, ComputeHashes(ProcessKey), VerifyPackage(ProcessKey),
    StringScan { scan: ScanId, key: ProcessKey, opts: StringScanOpts }, CancelStringScan(ScanId),
    HandleSearch { search: SearchId, pattern: Arc<str>, include_maps: bool, privileged: bool }, CancelHandleSearch(SearchId),
    HistoryQuery { id: u64, range: HistoryRange, what: HistoryWhat }, HistoryDelete { keys: Arc<[ProcessKey]> },
    SetupStatus, RunSetup { step: SetupStep },
    Device(DeviceCommand),                           // R-139 item 3: Udisks, Inventory or UPower by variant
}

pub trait Source: Send + 'static {
    fn id(&self) -> SourceId;
    fn period(&self, demand: &Demand, settings: &EngineSettings) -> Option<Duration>;   // None = off
    fn sample(self) -> (Self, SourceUpdate) where Self: Sized;                           // blocking pool
    fn reset_baselines(&mut self) {}                                                     // reset_generation rose
    fn command(&mut self, cmd: &WorkerCommand) -> bool { false }                         // true = sample at once
    fn take_extra(&mut self) -> Option<SourceUpdate> { None }                            // device lists and details next to samples (R-139 item 8)
}

pub async fn run<S: Source>(cx: Cx, io: WorkerIo, src: S) -> Outcome<(), WorkerError>;
```

`run` behaviour, in order each turn:
1. `period = src.period(&io.demand.borrow_and_clone(), &io.settings.borrow_and_clone())`; if it changed, rebuild `iv = interval(cx.now(), period.unwrap_or(IDLE_RECHECK))` with `set_missed_tick_behavior(Skip)`; a change from one `Some` to another `Some` also calls `src.reset_baselines()` (ADR-008: first sample after a rate change is `WarmingUp`, `GAP_BEFORE` on the ring is the reducer's job).
2. `sleep_until(iv.deadline()).await` (a new `Sleep` each turn); `if cx.checkpoint().is_err() { return Outcome::Ok(()) }`; `iv.tick(cx.now())`.
3. Read `io.control.borrow_and_clone()`: if `reset_generation` rose, `src.reset_baselines()`; for each `QueuedCommand` with `target == src.id()` and `seq > last_seq`: `RefreshNow` forces a sample this turn, anything else goes to `src.command(..)` and forces a sample if it returns true.
4. If `period` is `None` and no forced sample: continue (no I/O).
5. `let job = cx.spawn_blocking(move |_| src.sample())?; let (s, update) = job.join(&cx).await?; src = s;` measure the job duration with `cx.now()`; after `LATE_COUNT` consecutive jobs longer than `LATE_FRACTION × period` send `SourceUpdate::Health { state: Late, .. }` once; when a job is on time again send `Health { state: Running }` once.
6. Drain extras: `while let Some(extra) = src.take_extra() { io.updates.send(&cx, EngineMsg::Source(extra)).await? }` so device lists and details reach the reducer before the sample that refers to them (R-139 item 8).
7. `io.updates.send(&cx, EngineMsg::Source(update)).await` mapped to `WorkerError::Closed` on error.

Never hold a `watch` `Ref` across another channel call (`borrow_and_clone()` only). A worker never starts a second job while one runs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a source with period 100 ms **When** the loop runs 1 s of virtual time **Then** `sample()` is called 10 times at 100 ms steps from the first deadline (absolute deadlines, no drift).
- **Given** a sample that takes 250 ms with period 100 ms **When** the loop runs **Then** no catch-up burst happens (next sample at the next future deadline) and after 3 such jobs one `Health { state: Late }` is sent.
- **Given** `period()` returns `None` **When** 60 s pass **Then** `sample()` is never called and the loop woke 120 times (`IDLE_RECHECK`).
- **Given** `reset_generation` rises **When** the next turn starts **Then** `reset_baselines()` is called exactly once before `sample()`.
- **Given** a `QueuedCommand { target: this, command: RefreshNow }` **When** the source is off **Then** exactly one `sample()` runs at once.
- **Given** the `Cx` is cancelled **When** the loop reaches its checkpoint **Then** it returns `Outcome::Ok(())` and never calls `sample()` again.
- **Given** a source whose `take_extra()` returns one `Devices` update and then `None` **When** one sample runs **Then** the channel receives the `Devices` update first and the sample second (R-139 item 8).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/source.rs`: create

## Tests
- Covered by `tests/lab_source_loop.rs` (E08-007) and `tests/lab_demand.rs` (E08-008); this bead adds `source.rs::tests::worker_control_default_is_empty` and `tests/lab_source_loop.rs::extras_sent_before_sample` (the `take_extra` order criterion).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `spawn_blocking` or `send` failure returns `Outcome::Err(WorkerError)` so the supervisor restarts the worker; a cancelled `Cx` returns `Ok`.
- Validity: N/A here (payload-level).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: an off source costs two wakeups per second and no I/O; the loop allocates only when the period changes.
- Privacy: `WorkerCommand::StringScan` and `HandleSearch` carry patterns; never log them.

## Notes
asupersync 0.5.0: `time::interval(now, period)` is synchronous (`time/interval.rs:430`); `sleep_until` `time/sleep.rs:1145` returns early on user or shutdown cancel; `Cx::checkpoint` `cx/cx.rs:2508`; `Cx::spawn_blocking` `cx.rs:4661`, joined with `TaskHandle::join(&mut self, &cx)`; `watch::Receiver::borrow_and_clone` (API notes section 5, bead `c11v6v`). The fourth `WorkerIo` field (`control: watch::Receiver<WorkerControl>` with `reset_generation` and the newest-64 `QueuedCommand` queue) is accepted (R-166 B3-1). `WorkerCommand::Device` carries `tl_model::command::DeviceCommand` (E03-063). Event-driven D-Bus workers do not use `run`; they take `WorkerIo` directly (E08-010 shows the pattern). Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

## Shared handles (accepted, R-166 B3-8)
`WorkerIo` gets a fifth field `pub shared: crate::dbus::SharedHandles` (cheap `Clone`), created once per session by E09-016 and handed to every worker factory, so the systemd workers can `set` their connection slot and E11 can read it. This bead does not declare it: leave the comment line `// E08-009: shared` in `WorkerIo` and in its constructor; E08-009 (8hz.11) adds the field as a chain edit (R-262). `WorkerControl` and the loop are unchanged.
close_reason: R-276 follow-up: WorkerControl.progress (CommandProgress, started/done per SourceId), restart resumes at started, crashed command reported as Health Failed with its kind (RefreshNow silent), WorkerCommand::kind. Lab tests: crashing_command_is_not_rerun, command_queued_during_restart_runs_once, sample_crash_blames_no_command. Commits 22e1a35, 4843dc4, b46bf00.

title: E08: per-worker ManagedSupervisor with backoff and budget (supervise.rs)
description:
## Context
Each worker gets its own one-child `ManagedSupervisor` so a crash-looping source cannot spend another source's restart budget (ADR-004, API notes section 3). The policy is fixed: one-for-one, `Transient`, exponential backoff 500 ms doubling to 30 s, 5 restarts per 60 s, escalation `Stop`. Sources: ADR-004 (per-worker supervisor), ADR-013 (LabRuntime cases), API notes section 3 and 7.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/supervise.rs`:

```rust
pub const MAX_RESTARTS: u32 = 5;
pub const RESTART_WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60);
pub const BACKOFF_INITIAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(500);
pub const BACKOFF_MAX: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);
pub const BACKOFF_MULTIPLIER: f64 = 2.0;

/// Any `Fn(Cx, ManagedGeneration) -> Fut` with `Fut: Future<Output = Outcome<(), WorkerError>> + Send`.
pub type WorkerFactory = Arc<dyn ManagedChildFactory<WorkerError>>;

pub fn build_supervisor(name: &str, factory: WorkerFactory) -> Result<ManagedSupervisor<WorkerError>, SuperviseError>;
pub async fn run_supervised(cx: &Cx, name: &str, factory: WorkerFactory) -> Result<ManagedSupervisorReport<WorkerError>, SuperviseError>;  // spawn + join
pub fn budget_exhausted(report: &ManagedSupervisorReport<WorkerError>) -> bool;  // true when the child is down because the 5-in-60 s budget was spent

fn legacy_unreachable(_: &Scope<'static, FailFast>, _: &mut RuntimeState, _: &Cx) -> Result<TaskId, SpawnError> { unreachable!("managed mode never calls the legacy start") }

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum SuperviseError { #[error("compile: {0}")] Compile(Arc<str>), #[error("bind: {0}")] Bind(Arc<str>), #[error("spawn: {0}")] Spawn(Arc<str>) }
```

- **Given** a factory that returns `Outcome::Ok(())` after a user cancel **When** the handle is aborted **Then** no generation starts after the abort and the report shows no restart batch after it.

title: E08: SourceController with the 60 s disable (controller.rs)
description:
## Context
A `SourceController` wraps one worker's supervisor for the life of a session. When the restart budget is spent it publishes `SourceState::Disabled { until }`, sleeps 60 s, binds a fresh supervisor and tries again: "five failures in a minute, then off for a minute" (ADR-004). It also publishes `Running` when a generation starts and `Failed` with the last error when one dies, so the Collector Health items ("<Source> paused after errors", "<Source> unavailable", UI-SHL collector health) have data. Sources: ADR-004 (task tree, per-worker supervisor), ADR-013, UI-SHL collector health texts, ADR-015 (log targets).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/controller.rs`:

```rust
pub const DISABLE_FOR: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60);

pub struct SourceController { id: SourceId, name: &'static str, factory: WorkerFactory, updates: mpsc::Sender<EngineMsg> }
impl SourceController {
    pub fn new(id: SourceId, factory: WorkerFactory, updates: mpsc::Sender<EngineMsg>) -> Self;
    /// Runs until `cx` is cancelled. Spawn with `cx.spawn(|cx| ctl.run(cx))` from the session.
    pub async fn run(self, cx: Cx);
}
```

`run` loop: send `Health { Running }`; `run_supervised(&cx, name, factory.clone()).await`; if `cx.is_cancel_requested()` return; if `budget_exhausted(&report)`: send `Health { state: Disabled { until: now_boot_ns() + 60 s }, last_error: <last Err text or "panic"> }`, `time::sleep(cx.now(), DISABLE_FOR).await`, checkpoint, loop; if the generation returned `Outcome::Ok(())` while `cx` is not cancelled, the worker has reported `Health { state: Unsupported }` before returning: the controller never restarts it and waits for `cx` cancellation (R-155 item 4; used for "GPU probe not installed", `LibraryNotFound`, `DriverNotLoaded` and "KWin bridge not available"); otherwise (supervisor ended for another reason) log at `warn` on target `tasklens::source::<name>` and loop at once. Sends use `updates.send(&cx, ..).await`; a `Closed` error ends the loop. The worker's own `Late` and `Running` health messages come from `source::run` (E08-004); the controller does not duplicate them.

`SourceState` values used: `Running`, `Late`, `Disabled { until: TimeNs }`, `Failed`, `Unsupported` (R-155 item 4) (defined in `tl-model/src/health.rs`, E03-A1; use its exact spelling).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a factory that always fails **When** the controller runs 130 s of virtual time **Then** the health messages are `Running`, then `Disabled { until = t0 + 60 s }` at about 7.5 s (after 5 backoffs: 0.5 + 1 + 2 + 4 = 7.5 s), then `Running` at about 67.5 s, then `Disabled` again at about 75 s.
- **Given** a factory that fails 3 times then runs **When** 60 s pass **Then** no `Disabled` message is sent.
- **Given** the controller's `Cx` is cancelled while a worker generation is running **When** the cancel propagates **Then** the generation returns `Ok` and `run` returns without sending `Disabled`.
- **Given** the `updates` receiver is dropped **When** the controller tries to send **Then** `run` returns.
- **Given** a factory whose worker sends `Health { Unsupported }` and returns `Ok` **When** the controller runs 300 s of virtual time **Then** the factory is called exactly once and no `Disabled` or second `Running` message follows (R-155 item 4).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/controller.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_supervise.rs`: add the controller cases

## Tests
- `lab_supervise.rs::controller_disables_for_60s_then_retries`: the message timeline above.
- `lab_supervise.rs::controller_no_disable_under_budget`: 3 failures, no `Disabled`.
- `lab_supervise.rs::controller_stops_on_cancel`: cancel ends the loop.
- `lab_supervise.rs::controller_never_retries_unsupported`: the R-155 item 4 criterion.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the last `WorkerError` text goes into `last_error` (shown in the health tooltip); a panic gives `"panic"`.
- Validity: while `Disabled`, the reducer marks the source's values `Failed` with `last_error` (E09-004).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: idle cost is one sleeping task per source.
- Privacy: `last_error` must not contain process text; `WorkerError::Collect` from `tl-collect` carries paths of `/proc` files only.

## Notes
`time::sleep(now, d)` `time/sleep.rs:1124` returns early on shutdown cancellation, so the 60 s sleep ends promptly at shutdown. `ManagedSupervisorReport` fields: child outcome, `started`, `restart_batches`, `escalations` (`supervision.rs` L1997). Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
close_reason: SourceController in controller.rs runs the supervisor inline so a cancel drains the worker; Running, Disabled for 60 s, Unsupported never retried; 5 lab tests in lab_supervise.rs. Commits 7b8ebf7, e768a12, 8e50d43

comments.text: Leader note from 8hz.7: cancelling the task that awaits run_supervised does NOT stop the supervisor (asupersync join ignores cancellation). To stop a source, cancel its region or call the handle's abort() (see tests/lab_supervise.rs abort tests, which use build_supervisor). Add a lab test that the 60 s disable and engine shutdown really stop the worker. Also: budget_exhausted is inferred from outcome Ok + restart_batches >= 5 + last generation errored.

title: E08: fake sources and Source-loop LabRuntime tests
description:
## Context

```rust
pub enum Step { Ok, Err(&'static str), Panic, Slow(Duration) }
pub struct FakeSource {
    pub id: SourceId,
    pub script: Vec<Step>,            // consumed in order; the last step repeats
    pub period_on: Option<Duration>,  // returned by period() when `on(demand, settings)` is true

}

pub fn channels() -> (mpsc::Sender<EngineMsg>, mpsc::Receiver<EngineMsg>, watch::Sender<Demand>, watch::Sender<EngineSettings>, watch::Sender<WorkerControl>);
```

title: E09: suspend and resume handling (reducer/suspend.rs, lab_suspend.rs)
description:
## Context
Suspend is detected two ways, whichever comes first: logind `PrepareForSleep(true)` pauses rate publication and `PrepareForSleep(false)` resets baselines, re-enumerates devices and marks `GAP_BEFORE` on every series; or a worker's clock check (`Δboot − Δmono > 250 ms`) reports `ResumeDetected`. After resume the GPU probe is not restarted. Sources: ADR-008 (suspend and resume), ADR-003 (`GAP_BEFORE`), PERF-022, R-051, ADR-013 (lab suspend case), E08-003 (`Sleep`, `ResumeDetected`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/suspend.rs`:

```rust
pub struct SuspendState { pub sleeping: bool, pub slept_at_ns: Option<TimeNs>, pub resumed_at_ns: Option<TimeNs>, pub resume_count: u32 }
impl SuspendState {
    pub fn on_sleep(&mut self, entering: bool, t_ns: TimeNs) -> Transition;      // Entering | Resumed | None
    pub fn on_clock_resume(&mut self, id: SourceId, t_ns: TimeNs) -> Transition; // Resumed once per 2 s window, then None (several workers report the same resume)
    pub fn drop_rates(&self) -> bool;   // true while sleeping: rate samples are appended as gaps
}
pub enum Transition { Entering, Resumed, None }
```

Reducer effects (wired in `apply.rs`): `Entering` → `sleeping = true` (rate samples become gaps until resume); `Resumed` → `series.mark_gap_all()`, `bump_reset_generation()`, `forward(Disk, RefreshNow)`, `forward(Net, RefreshNow)`, `forward(Sensors, RefreshNow)` (re-enumeration), `sleeping = false`. `GpuNvidia` gets no command.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `Sleep { entering: true }` then two CPU samples **When** applied **Then** both samples are gap samples (`VALID` clear).
- **Given** `Sleep { entering: false }` **When** applied **Then** `reset_generation` rose by 1, the next sample of every series has `GAP_BEFORE`, and `RefreshNow` was forwarded to `Disk`, `Net` and `Sensors` but not to `GpuNvidia`.
- **Given** `ResumeDetected` from `Cpu` and 50 ms later from `Memory` **When** applied **Then** the reset generation rose once, not twice.
- **Given** `ResumeDetected` with no earlier `Sleep` **When** applied **Then** the effects are the same as a logind resume.
- **Given** a sample pair with a 5 s boottime gap and a 10 ms monotonic gap (reported as `ResumeDetected` by the worker) **When** applied **Then** the series shows a gap and no rate spike (the first post-resume sample is `WarmingUp`, a gap).

title: E09: table builder flat mode, sort, tie-break, filter (reducer/table.rs)
description:
## Context
The engine builds the process table rows; the UI never sorts or filters (ADR-009). This bead builds the flat mode (`TableMode::Flat`): filter, sort with the `ProcessKey` tie-break, non-sortable columns, and the row list with `query_generation`. Tree and grouped modes extend it (E09-010, E09-011). Sources: ADR-009 (`TableQuery`, `TableRow`, `ProcessTableView`, filter rule), PROC-014 (modes), PROC-044 (filter matching), PROC-047 (sorting; non-sortable columns), R-007 (column ids), R-011 (default PID ascending), R-043, ADR-003 (`ProcessKey` ordering).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs` (part 1):

```rust
pub struct TableInput<'a> { pub records: &'a [ProcessRecord], pub extras: &'a [ProcessExtras] /* index aligned, R-141 item 1 */, pub app_stats: &'a [AppCgroupSample] /* R-141 item 2 */, pub unit_stats: &'a [CgroupStats], pub system: &'a SystemSnapshot, pub devices: &'a DeviceCatalog, pub settings: &'a EngineSettings, pub unit_names: &'a FxHashMap<UnitRef, Arc<str>> /* Description, E09-025; empty in P1 */ }
pub fn build(input: &TableInput<'_>, query: &TableQuery) -> ProcessTableView;
pub const NOT_SORTABLE: &[&str] = &["pss", "uss", "cycles", "cycles_delta", "ctx_switches", "ctx_switches_delta"];   // sorting on these falls back to PID ascending
pub enum SortKey { Int(i128), Float(f32), Text(Arc<str>), Absent }   // Absent sorts last in both directions
pub fn sort_key(r: &ProcessRecord, x: &ProcessExtras, col: ColumnId) -> SortKey;
pub struct Filter { terms: Vec<Term> }   // Term { lower: String, digits: bool }
impl Filter { pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Self; pub fn matches(&self, r: &ProcessRecord, extra: &[&str]) -> bool; pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool; }
```

Rules:
- `Filter::parse` splits on spaces, lowercases; every term must match: substring of `meta.search_lower`, or of any string in `extra` (group name, unit name), or, when the term is all digits, `key.pid.to_string().starts_with(term)`.
- `sort_key` maps each `ColumnId` to the field it displays: `pid` → `Int(pid)`, `name` → `Text(meta.name)`, `cpu` and `cpu_relative` → `Float(cpu_pct × factor)`, `memory` → `Int(rss_anon_bytes)`, `ws_total` → `Int(rss_bytes)`, `swap`, `disk_read`/`disk_write`/`disk` (rates), `network` (`net_rx + net_tx`), `gpu`, `gpu_mem_dedicated`, `threads`, `nice`/`priority`, `state`, `ppid`, `user` → `Text(meta.user)`, `description`, `cmdline`, `image`/`exe`, `cgroup`, `unit`, `app_id`, `start_time` → `Int(start_ticks)`. Columns whose value is in `ProcessExtras` read it from `x` (for example `cpu_kernel` → `Float(x.cpu_kernel_pct)`, `start_time` → `Int(x.start_ticks)`, `page_faults` → `Int(x.page_faults)`, `exe_path` → `Text(x.exe_path)`, `unit` → the unit name of `x.unit`). A `ColumnId` whose data is in neither `ProcessRecord` nor `ProcessExtras` returns `Absent`: the P2 and P4 package, file and security columns and the visible-row-only columns (`pss`, `uss`, `ctx_switches*`, `cycles*`, `windows`, `x11_resources`), matching R-007 and PROC-047 (R-141 item 6). List them in the function's doc comment. A field whose `FieldValidity` is not `Valid` or `Stale` is `Absent`.
- Order: `sort.ascending` on the key, ties by `ProcessKey` ascending; `Absent` last. Sorting on a `NOT_SORTABLE` id uses `pid` ascending.
- Flat rows: `TableRow { node: Process(key), depth: 0, expanded: false, has_children: false, record: Some(i), group: None, descendants: 0, subtree: None }` for every record that passes the filter; `groups` empty; `query_generation = query.generation`; `totals` from E09-013 (`TableTotals::default()` until then).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** records with PIDs 3, 1, 2 and `sort = pid asc` **When** built **Then** rows are 1, 2, 3; with `desc` 3, 2, 1.
- **Given** two records with equal `cpu_pct` **When** sorted by `cpu` **Then** they are ordered by `ProcessKey` ascending whatever the direction.
- **Given** filter `"fire 12"` and a record named "Firefox" with PID 1234 **When** built **Then** it matches; PID 2123 does not (prefix rule).
- **Given** filter `"root"` **When** built **Then** records whose `search_lower` contains "root" match (user field is part of it).
- **Given** `sort.column = pss` **When** built **Then** the order equals `pid` ascending.
- **Given** a record whose `cpu` validity is `WarmingUp` **When** sorted by `cpu desc` **Then** it is last.
- **Given** `generation = 42` **When** built **Then** `view.query_generation == 42`.

## Cross-cutting

- Accessibility: N/A

title: E09: table builder tree mode, forest, PID +N, include children
description:
## Context
Tree mode shows the ppid forest: a row is a root when its parent is not shown (filtered, hidden or exited); siblings sort under their parent; `expanded` comes from the query; a collapsed parent's PID cell shows "PID +N" with N = total descendants; reparenting moves a process at the next sweep. Include children (filter) shows every descendant of each match. Sources: PROC-014 (Tree View), PROC-018 (+N), PROC-045 (include children), ADR-009 (missing parent → root; UI owns expansion), E09-009.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs`:

```rust
pub struct Forest { pub children: Vec<SmallVec<[u32; 4]>>, pub parent: Vec<Option<u32>>, pub roots: Vec<u32> }   // indexes into the visible record list
pub fn forest(records: &[ProcessRecord], visible: &[bool]) -> Forest;   // parent = index of the record with key.pid == ppid among *visible* records, else None (root)
pub fn descendants_count(f: &Forest, i: u32) -> u32;
pub fn flatten_tree(f: &Forest, order: &dyn Fn(&[u32]) -> Vec<u32>, expanded: &FxHashSet<NodeId>, out: &mut Vec<TableRow>, depth: u8);
```

Rules:
- Visibility: a record is visible when it passes the filter, or (`query.include_children`) when any ancestor passes. With an empty filter every record is visible.
- The parent link uses `ppid` matched against visible records' `pid`; PID 0 and PID 2 handling: kernel threads have ppid 2 and show under `kthreadd` in tree mode (the "Kernel threads" fold is grouped mode only, E09-011).
- `has_children = !children.is_empty()`, `expanded = expanded.contains(&Process(key))`, `descendants = descendants_count`, `depth` increases by 1 per level and saturates at 255.
- Siblings at every level are ordered by the E09-009 sort.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** A(1) → B(2) → C(3) all visible and `expanded = {A, B}` **When** built in Tree mode **Then** rows are A d0, B d1, C d2 with `has_children` true, true, false.
- **Given** the same with `expanded = {A}` **When** built **Then** rows are A d0, B d1 and B has `descendants == 1`; A has `descendants == 2`.
- **Given** filter matches only C **When** built **Then** C is a root at depth 0.
- **Given** filter matches only A and `include_children = true` **When** built **Then** A, B, C all appear (B and C by inheritance).
- **Given** B exits (still lingering with `EXITED`) **When** built **Then** B stays in place and C stays under B; after B is dropped C becomes a root.
- **Given** two roots with `cpu` 10 and 20, sort `cpu desc` **When** built **Then** the 20 root comes first and each root's children are sorted the same way among themselves.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs`: extend

## Tests
- `lab_table.rs::tree_depths_and_has_children`
- `lab_table.rs::collapsed_parent_descendant_count`
- `lab_table.rs::filtered_child_becomes_root`
- `lab_table.rs::include_children_pulls_descendants`
- `lab_table.rs::exited_parent_keeps_place_then_child_reroots`
- `lab_table.rs::siblings_sorted_under_parent`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: a ppid cycle (impossible in Linux but possible in a fixture) must not loop: `descendants_count` uses an explicit stack with a visited bitset.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: O(n) forest build with one `FxHashMap<u32 /*pid*/, u32>`; no recursion deeper than the stack-based walk.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
Depends on E09-009 (same file). `query.include_children` is R-141 item 4. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E09: table builder grouped mode, app and unit rows, Kernel threads row
description:
## Context
Task Manager Grouping shows three fixed groups ("Apps (N)", "Background processes (N)", "System processes (N)") whatever the sort, app rows with their primary processes' subtrees, unit rows for systemd units with more than one process, the "Kernel threads (N)" row collapsed by default, and (from P2) the two pseudo rows. Group and app rows aggregate each process once. Sources: PROC-004 (classes and order), PROC-008 (app row contents and children), PROC-009 (unit rows, Kernel threads row), PROC-012 (pseudo rows, P2 in E09-023), ADR-009 (no double counting), R-137 (cgroup stats), D-011, E08-003 (`CgroupStats`).

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs`:

```rust
pub const GROUP_ORDER: [GroupKind; 3] = [GroupKind::App-class, GroupKind::Background, GroupKind::System];   // see classification below
pub fn group_class(r: &ProcessRecord) -> GroupClass;   // Apps | Background | System, from r.group (GroupKind::App → Apps; Background → Background; System and Ungrouped → System; KERNEL_THREAD → System)
pub fn aggregate(records: &[ProcessRecord], members: &[u32], stats: Option<&AppCgroupSample>, unit: Option<&CgroupStats>) -> GroupRow;   // Σ cpu, io, net, gpu, threads; memory = app or unit anon_bytes when Some, else Σ rss_anon; members = members.len(); pids from the cgroup sample; FieldValidity worst-of (GroupRow fields: R-141 item 3)
pub fn build_grouped(input: &TableInput<'_>, query: &TableQuery, filter: &Filter) -> (Vec<TableRow>, Vec<GroupRow>);
```

Rules:
- Group header rows: `NodeId::Group(GroupKey)` for the three fixed groups; `has_children = count > 0`; `expanded` from the query (default handling is the UI's; the engine treats a missing entry as collapsed); the count N is the number of processes in the group after filtering (pseudo rows excluded, PROC-012).
- Apps: one row per `GroupKind::App { app_id }` (key = that `GroupKey`), `record: None`, `group: Some(i)` into `groups`; children are the app's primary processes (members whose ppid is not a member) each with its subtree (E09-010 forest restricted to the members), sorted by the query; the app row sorts among app rows by the same column on the aggregated value; memory from `app_stats` (`anon_bytes`, R-137), Disk from members or from the cgroup `io.stat` rate when any member's Disk is `Restricted` (PROC-008, R-103).
- Background and System: processes of the class; those sharing a systemd unit with more than one process fold under a unit row (`node: NodeId::Unit(UnitRef)`, `kind: GroupRowKind::Unit`, name = `unit_names[unit]` else the unit name, aggregated like an app row with `unit_stats` when present; the unit comes from `ProcessExtras.unit`); a unit with one process shows the process directly.
- Kernel threads (`KERNEL_THREAD`) fold under one System row `node: NodeId::KernelThreads`, `kind: GroupRowKind::KernelThreads`, named "Kernel threads", count N, placed after the sorted System members; pseudo rows follow it (`NodeId::Pseudo(PseudoKind::{Interrupts, MemoryCompression})`, `GroupRowKind::Pseudo`, E09-023). App rows use `node: NodeId::Group(key)`, `kind: GroupRowKind::App`. `GroupKind` keeps its four classes (R-141 item 3). The row is expanded only when the query lists it.
- Filter: a term matching a group name ("apps", "background processes", "system processes") or an app or unit name matches every member of it; group headers always stay with their filtered counts.
- No double counting: a process contributes to exactly one app or unit row and to exactly one group header.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 2 app processes, 3 background, 4 system with sort `cpu desc` **When** built **Then** the rows start with "Apps" and the order of headers is Apps, Background, System whatever the sort.
- **Given** an app with primary P (cpu 10) and child C (cpu 5) **When** built with the app expanded **Then** the app `GroupRow.cpu_pct == 15`, rows are App, P d1, C d2, and the Apps header count is 2.
- **Given** `app_stats` with `anon_bytes = 1 GiB` for that app and members whose RssAnon sum is 1.5 GiB **When** built **Then** the app row memory is 1 GiB.
- **Given** 3 processes of unit `pipewire.service` **When** built **Then** one unit row "pipewire.service" with count 3 appears in Background and the processes are its children; a unit with 1 process shows no unit row.
- **Given** 50 kernel threads **When** built **Then** one "Kernel threads" row with count 50 sits after the other System rows and is collapsed unless in `expanded`.
- **Given** filter `"apps"` **When** built **Then** every app member matches and Background and System headers show count 0.
- **Given** the full fixture **When** the group counts are summed **Then** they equal the number of non-pseudo records that pass the filter (each counted once).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs`: extend

## Tests
- `lab_table.rs::group_order_fixed`
- `lab_table.rs::app_row_aggregates_once`
- `lab_table.rs::app_memory_from_cgroup_anon`
- `lab_table.rs::unit_rows_fold_multi_process_units`
- `lab_table.rs::kernel_threads_row_last_in_system`
- `lab_table.rs::group_name_filter_matches_members`
- `lab_table.rs::counts_sum_to_visible_records`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: `GroupRow` validity per field is the worst of its members (`Restricted` beats `Valid`); memory from the cgroup carries the `CgroupStats.validity`.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one pass to bucket by group, one forest per app or unit; 2,000 rows in under 2 ms.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
Depends on E09-010. Unit, Kernel threads and pseudo rows use `NodeId::{Unit, KernelThreads, Pseudo}` and `GroupRowKind` (R-141 item 3, R-155 item 2); the `GroupRow` field set is R-141 item 3. "Unit rows and app rows always aggregate" (PROC-019) holds here; per-process subtree totals are E09-024. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

Fix ede5723: depths per UI-PRC-002 (headers 0; app, unit, Kernel threads and loose rows 1; app or unit members 2 and deeper) and the Kernel threads row first in System with its threads flat at depth 2; test kernel_threads_row_last_in_system renamed kernel_threads_row_first_in_system

title: E09: hide system processes in the table builder
description:
## Context
"Hide system processes" is an `EngineSettings` flag that removes the System group, pseudo rows and desktop-infrastructure Background rows, with a fixed exception list; it applies in every mode. Sources: PROC-046 (scope, exception list), R-031, ADR-011 (`hide_system` in `EngineSettings`), PROC-012 (pseudo rows hidden too), E09-011.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs`:

```rust
pub const INFRA_SLICES: [&str; 2] = ["session.slice", "background.slice"];
pub const HIDE_SYSTEM_EXCEPTIONS: [&str; 3] = ["plasma-plasmashell.service", "plasma-kwin_wayland.service", "org.gnome.Shell@wayland.service"];
/// true when the record is hidden by `settings.hide_system`
pub fn hidden_by_hide_system(r: &ProcessRecord, class: GroupClass) -> bool;
```

Rules (PROC-046): hidden when `class == System` (kernel threads, the Kernel threads row, other users, system units), when the row is a pseudo row, or when `class == Background` and the cgroup path contains `/session.slice/` or `/background.slice/` or ends in `/init.scope` under `user@<uid>.service` (`systemd --user`), unless the unit name is in `HIDE_SYSTEM_EXCEPTIONS`; everything in `app.slice` stays. - **Given** `hide_system = true` and a record in `session.slice/plasma-plasmashell.service` **When** built **Then** it stays.
- **Given** `hide_system = true` in Grouped mode **When** built **Then** the System header is absent and the Background count excludes the hidden rows.
- **Given** `hide_system = false` **When** built **Then** nothing is removed.
- **Given** the user manager `init.scope` process (`user@1000.service/init.scope`) **When** `hide_system = true` **Then** it is hidden; PID 1's `init.scope` is System and hidden too.

title: E09: two-line header totals (TableTotals)
description:
## Context
The two-line header shows system totals under the column names: CPU and kernel from `/proc/stat`, Memory and Swap percent, Disk highest busy percent, Network as percent of summed link speed or a rate, GPU highest utilization and per-adapter GPU N, VRAM used over total, Threads, Handles from `/proc/sys/fs/file-nr`. The engine fills `ProcessTableView.totals` at every table build from the latest system snapshot. Sources: PROC-038, ADR-008 (CPU and memory math), ADR-003 (`TableTotals`), E08-003 (`ProcessSweep.system_threads`, `file_nr`).

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs`:

```rust
pub fn totals(system: &SystemSnapshot, devices: &DeviceCatalog, sweep: &SweepTotals) -> TableTotals;
pub struct SweepTotals { pub system_threads: u32, pub file_nr: Option<u64> }
```

Each total is a `Total<T>` (value plus `Validity`); the field names are the `TableTotals` of E03-051 (R-141 item 4):
- `cpu_pct`: from the CPU package totals (`Valid` after two samples, else `WarmingUp`).
- `memory_pct = (MemTotal − MemAvailable) / MemTotal × 100`; `swap_pct = SwapUsed / SwapTotal × 100` (`Unsupported` when `SwapTotal == 0`).
- `disk_pct`: max `DISK_ACTIVE` over present physical disks (parent == None; `loop`, `ram`, `zram`, `fd` excluded by E04's classification); `Missing` when no disk.
- `net_bps` = Σ(rx + tx) over physical interfaces in bytes per second; `net_link_bps: Option<u64>` = Σ link speed in bytes per second when every present physical interface reports a speed, else `None` (the UI then shows the rate).
- `gpu_pct`: max over present GPUs; `gpu_adapter_pct: [Total<f32>; 16]` by PCI bus address ascending (unused slots `Unsupported`); `vram_pct = Σ used / Σ total`; `Unsupported` with no GPU.
- `threads = system_threads`; `handles = file_nr` field 1 (`Unsupported` when `None`). The E05 sweep fills `ProcessSweep.file_nr` from `/proc/sys/fs/file-nr` (R-166 B3-7).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** MemTotal 32 GiB, MemAvailable 8 GiB **When** computed **Then** `memory_pct == 75.0`.
- **Given** SwapTotal 0 **When** computed **Then** `swap_pct` validity is `Unsupported`.
- **Given** disks `sda` busy 40, `nvme0n1` busy 70, `sda1` (child) busy 90 **When** computed **Then** `disk_pct == 70`.
- **Given** two interfaces with speeds 1 Gbit/s and 2.5 Gbit/s and rates summing to 350 Mbit/s **When** computed **Then** `net_bps == 43_750_000` and `net_link_bps == Some(437_500_000)` (10%); with one speed unknown **Then** `net_link_bps == None`.
- **Given** two GPUs at bus `0000:2d:00.0` (util 80) and `0000:01:00.0` (util 20) **When** computed **Then** `gpu_pct == 80`, `gpu_adapter_pct[0].value == 20`, `gpu_adapter_pct[1].value == 80`.
- **Given** `file_nr = None` **When** computed **Then** `handles` is `Unsupported`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs`: extend

## Tests

- `lab_table.rs::totals_disk_max_physical_only`
- `lab_table.rs::totals_net_pct_or_rate`
- `lab_table.rs::totals_gpu_order_by_pci`
- `lab_table.rs::totals_handles_unsupported_without_file_nr`

## Cross-cutting

- Validity: every total carries its own `Validity`; the UI renders `n/a` for `Unsupported`.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: O(devices) per build.
- Privacy: N/A

title: E09: sys_table.rs stub with full signatures and default sorts
description:
## Context
The three system tables (Services, Startup Apps, Connections) are sorted, filtered and flattened by the engine from one `SysTableQuery` (UI-SYS-002). title: E09: engine_root and engine_session with epochs and catch_unwind (session.rs)
description:
## Context
`engine_root` owns the UI-facing endpoints for the life of the process and runs sessions in a loop: each session builds its channels, spawns one `SourceController` per worker, runs the reducer inline under `catch_unwind`, and owns every handle so an unwind aborts every child. A reducer panic or `InvariantViolation` restarts with a new epoch after 1 s; more than 3 restarts in 60 s stops restarting and publishes an all-`Failed` health snapshot while the root stays alive. The session also runs the 1 s `Tick` task. Sources: ADR-004 (task tree, session restart rule), ADR-005 (channels), ADR-013 (session restart test), API notes section 2 and 3, E08-A1 (`workers_for`), E09-001.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/session.rs`:

```rust
pub const RESTART_DELAY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);
pub const MAX_RESTARTS: u32 = 3;
pub const RESTART_WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_secs(60);
pub const TICK: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);

pub struct RootEndpoints {
    pub msgs: mpsc::Receiver<EngineMsg>,                 // UI commands and worker updates share it (capacity 256)
    pub msgs_tx: mpsc::Sender<EngineMsg>,                // cloned into every worker's WorkerIo
    pub demand: watch::Receiver<Demand>, pub settings: watch::Receiver<EngineSettings>,
    pub control: watch::Sender<WorkerControl>,
    pub publisher: Publisher, pub events_tx: async_channel::Sender<ActionEvent>,
    pub config: Arc<EngineConfig>, pub boot_id: BootId, pub hooks: EngineHooks,
}
pub async fn engine_root(cx: Cx, mut ep: RootEndpoints);
async fn engine_session(cx: &Cx, ep: &mut RootEndpoints, epoch: u32) -> Result<(), SessionEnd>;   // Ok on cancel; Err on panic or invariant
enum SessionEnd { Panic, Invariant(&'static str) }
```

`engine_session`: `let mut reducer = Reducer::new(epoch, ep.boot_id, ep.control.clone(), ep.events_tx.clone())`; install `hooks.action_gate` and `hooks.record_sink` when present; for every `WorkerSpec` in `workers_for(config.mode)`: build `WorkerIo { updates: msgs_tx.clone(), demand: demand.clone(), settings: settings.clone(), control: control.subscribe() }`, `SourceController::new(id, (spec.factory)(config.clone(), io), msgs_tx.clone())`, `handles.push(cx.spawn(|cx| ctl.run(cx))?)`; spawn the tick task (`loop { sleep(cx.now(), TICK).await; checkpoint; msgs_tx.send(&cx, EngineMsg::Tick).await }`); then `reducer.run(cx, &mut ep.msgs, &mut ep.publisher).await` inline, wrapped in `futures_lite::FutureExt::catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(..))`. Dropping `handles` (a `Vec<TaskHandle>`) on return or unwind aborts every controller.

`engine_root`: `epoch = 1`; loop `{ match engine_session(..).await { Ok(()) => return, Err(end) => { tracing::error!(target: "tasklens::engine", ?end, epoch, "session ended"); restarts.push(now); if restarts in the last 60 s > 3 { publisher.publish(snapshot with health = HealthState::all_failed(epoch, "engine restarted too often")); park until cancel (loop sleep 60 s + checkpoint); return } sleep 1 s; epoch += 1 } } }`. The new session starts with empty rings so every series gets `GAP_BEFORE` on its first sample (rings are new, `pending_gap = true` in `SeriesStore::new`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake worker set and a reducer that panics on the 5th message **When** run in LabRuntime **Then** a new session starts after 1 s with `epoch == 2`, the same `msgs` receiver still delivers, and the first sample of every series in epoch 2 carries `GAP_BEFORE`.
- **Given** a reducer that panics at once in every session **When** run **Then** sessions 1 to 4 start (3 restarts), then the published snapshot has every `SourceHealth.state == Failed` with `last_error == "engine restarted too often"`, and the root task is still alive (not finished) 120 s later.
- **Given** a running session **When** the root `Cx` is cancelled **Then** every controller task ends, `engine_root` returns, and no `sample()` runs afterwards.
- **Given** 10 s of virtual time **When** nothing else happens **Then** exactly 10 `Tick` messages reached the reducer.
- **Given** the sequence from epoch 1 ended at 500 **When** epoch 2 publishes **Then** the sequence continues from 501 (strictly increasing per process: the sequence counter lives in `RootEndpoints`, not in the reducer).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/session.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_session.rs`: create (E09-017 adds the chaos run)

## Tests
- `lab_session.rs::reducer_panic_restarts_with_new_epoch`
- `lab_session.rs::four_restarts_publish_all_failed_and_stay_alive`
- `lab_session.rs::cancel_stops_everything`
- `lab_session.rs::tick_every_second`
- `lab_session.rs::sequence_continues_across_epochs`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: panic text is logged at `error` on `tasklens::engine` with the epoch; no payload content.
- Validity: after the final failure every source is `Failed`.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: a session restart costs one full re-warm of every source (visible gaps).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
Depends on E09-001, E09-007, E08-A1. `Reducer::sequence` is set from `ep.next_sequence` at session start and written back after each publish. `catch_unwind` needs `panic = "unwind"` (ADR-002). API notes: `cx.spawn` `cx.rs:4420`; `try_spawn_with_cx` is used by `Engine::start` (E09-019) to spawn `engine_root`. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

## Chain-edit points (R-150 item 4)
Two later beads edit this file at named insertion points, and only there. Leave a comment line at each point:
- `// E29-020: helper spawn` right after the reducer is built: E29-020 (qfx.23) spawns the helper session task there and sets `reducer.helper_tx` (R-148 item 1).
- `// E30-A2: history sink and worker` right after the action gate is installed: E30-A2 (tasklens-8fx.2) installs the `RecordSink` and starts the history worker there.
`ResumeDetected` stays with E08's logind worker only (R-150 item 5).

## Shared handles (accepted, R-166 B3-8)
`engine_session` creates `let shared = SharedHandles::default()` per session, puts it in every `WorkerIo { .., shared: shared.clone() }`, and installs the action gate as `hooks.action_gate.map(|f| f(HookCtx { events_tx: ep.events_tx.clone(), msgs_tx: ep.msgs_tx.clone(), boot_id: ep.boot_id, config: ep.config.clone(), shared: shared.clone() }))`. `HookCtx` is defined in `bridge.rs` (E09-018).

title: E09-A2 Shutdown
description:
## Context
Anchor E09-A2 "Shutdown". `EngineHandle::shutdown(self, total)` runs the five ADR-004 steps after GPUI has stopped: drop the UI-side senders, `drain_root_region(1000 ms)`, drop every `RuntimeHandle` clone, `shutdown_timeout(500 ms)`, and report; `tl-app` calls `std::process::exit(0)` when the report says a step timed out. Sources: ADR-004 (shutdown), ADR-010 (called on the main thread after GPUI stops), ADR-013 (real-system test: shutdown within 1.5 s under load; lab case: drain is `Quiescent`), API notes section 8, E33-A1 (caller).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/bridge.rs` (part 3):

```rust
pub const DRAIN_BUDGET: Duration = Duration::from_millis(1000);
pub const TEARDOWN_BUDGET: Duration = Duration::from_millis(500);
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ShutdownReport { pub drained: bool /* RootDrainOutcome::Quiescent */, pub torn_down: bool /* shutdown_timeout returned true */, pub elapsed: Duration }
impl ShutdownReport { pub fn clean(&self) -> bool { self.drained && self.torn_down } }
impl EngineHandle {
    /// Consumes the handle. `total` is advisory; the two budgets above are the real bounds (1.5 s together).
    pub fn shutdown(self, total: Duration) -> ShutdownReport;
}
```

Steps inside: set `stopped`; take `demand_tx`, `settings_tx`, `msgs_tx`, `events` out of `Inner` and drop them (step 1); `rt.drain_root_region(DRAIN_BUDGET)` (step 2); drop `rt_handle` and every clone (the `Inner` is the last owner; other `EngineHandle` clones must already be dropped by the caller, documented) (step 3); `rt.shutdown_timeout(TEARDOWN_BUDGET)` (step 4); on `!clean()` log `warn` on `tasklens::engine` with both flags (step 5). After `shutdown`, no `TaskHandle` is awaited from any thread (bead `bi2462.91`).

`crates/tl-engine/tests/real_shutdown.rs` (`#[ignore]`, owner machine): start the engine with the real worker set registered so far, `set_demand` with every surface visible, wait 3 s, `shutdown`; assert `clean()` and `elapsed < 1.5 s`; repeat 5 times in one process.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the fake worker set on the real runtime **When** `shutdown(2 s)` is called **Then** `drained && torn_down` and `elapsed < 1.5 s`.
- **Given** a fake worker whose `sample()` blocks for 3 s inside `spawn_blocking` **When** `shutdown` is called **Then** it returns within 1.6 s with `torn_down == false` and the report logged (the blocking job is not interrupted; the process exits anyway).
- **Given** the lab **When** the root `Cx` receives shutdown cancellation **Then** `drain` is `Quiescent` (ADR-013 "shutdown drain is Quiescent").
- **Given** another `EngineHandle` clone is still alive **When** `shutdown` runs **Then** `torn_down == false` (documented behaviour; the test proves the rule from API notes section 8).

title: E09: EngineHandle implementing EngineClient and EngineHooks (bridge.rs part 1)
description:
## Context
`EngineHandle` is the UI's only view of the engine: it implements `tl_model::client::EngineClient` with an `ArcSwap` load, the one-token wake, the action-event channel, the demand and settings `watch` senders and the command queue. No public item names an asupersync type (ADR-001 rule 2, D-001). Sources: ADR-005 (client trait, channels, `CommandError`), ADR-004 (shutdown steps belong to E09-A2), ADR-001, API notes section 5 (no-`Cx` sender operations), R-136.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/bridge.rs` (part 1):

```rust
pub struct EngineHandle { inner: Arc<Inner> }
struct Inner {
    latest: Arc<ArcSwap<Snapshot>>, wake_rx: async_channel::Receiver<()>, events_rx: async_channel::Receiver<ActionEvent>,
    demand_tx: watch::Sender<Demand>, settings_tx: watch::Sender<EngineSettings>, msgs_tx: mpsc::Sender<EngineMsg>,
    last_demand: Mutex<Demand>, journal: Option<JournalSpawner>,
    rt: Mutex<Option<asupersync::runtime::Runtime>>, rt_handle: Mutex<Option<RuntimeHandle>>, stopped: AtomicBool,
}
pub type JournalSpawner = Arc<dyn Fn(JournalQuery) -> JournalHandle + Send + Sync>;   // installed by E14-A4 through EngineHooks

impl EngineClient for EngineHandle {
    fn latest(&self) -> Arc<Snapshot> { self.inner.latest.load_full() }
    fn wake(&self) -> async_channel::Receiver<()> { self.inner.wake_rx.clone() }
    fn action_events(&self) -> async_channel::Receiver<ActionEvent> { self.inner.events_rx.clone() }
    fn set_demand(&self, d: Demand) { if *last != d { last = d.clone(); demand_tx.send(d) } }      // watch::Sender::send needs no Cx; never blocks
    fn set_settings(&self, s: EngineSettings) { settings_tx.send(s) }
    fn send(&self, cmd: Command) -> Result<(), CommandError> {
        if stopped { return Err(CommandError::EngineStopped) }
        msgs_tx.try_send(EngineMsg::Command(cmd)).map_err(|e| match e { SendError::Full(_) => CommandError::Busy, SendError::Closed(_) => CommandError::EngineStopped })
    }
    fn journal(&self, q: JournalQuery) -> JournalHandle { match &journal { Some(f) => f(q), None => JournalHandle::closed(JournalError::NotFound) } }
}
pub struct EngineHooks { pub action_gate: Option<Arc<dyn Fn() -> Box<dyn ActionGate> + Send + Sync>>, pub record_sink: Option<Arc<dyn Fn(&EngineConfig) -> Box<dyn RecordSink> + Send + Sync>>, pub journal: Option<JournalSpawner> }
impl Default for EngineHooks { fn default() -> Self { crate::default_hooks() } }   // lib.rs: filled by chain edits (E11-A1 action gate, E14-A4 journal, E30-A2 record sink)
```

`EngineHandle: Send + Sync + Clone`. `JournalHandle::closed(err)` is a `tl-model` constructor that yields one `JournalEvent::Error(err)` then ends; if E03-A2 did not add it, build the handle from its public parts here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a handle whose command queue holds 256 unread messages **When** `send` is called **Then** it returns `Err(CommandError::Busy)` and does not block.
- **Given** `set_demand(d)` twice with equal `d` **When** the worker side counts `changed()` wakes **Then** it saw one change.
- **Given** `stopped` is set **When** `send` is called **Then** `Err(EngineStopped)`.
- **Given** no journal spawner **When** `journal(q)` is called **Then** the first event on `events()` is `JournalEvent::Error(JournalError::NotFound)` and the channel then closes.
- **Given** `cargo doc --no-deps -p tl-engine` **When** the public signatures of `bridge.rs` are read **Then** none names an asupersync type (`EngineHooks` uses `tl-model` and `tl-engine` traits only).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/bridge.rs`: create (part 1)
- `crates/tl-engine/src/lib.rs`: add `pub mod bridge; pub mod session; pub mod reducer; pub use bridge::{EngineHandle, EngineHooks};   // E09-019 appends `Engine`, E09-A2 appends `ShutdownReport` (R-262)` and `pub fn default_hooks() -> EngineHooks { EngineHooks { action_gate: None, record_sink: None, journal: None } }` (later beads replace one field each)

## Tests
- `bridge.rs::tests::send_busy_when_full`
- `bridge.rs::tests::set_demand_dedups`
- `bridge.rs::tests::send_after_stop`
- `bridge.rs::tests::journal_without_spawner_errors_not_found`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `CommandError::{Busy, EngineStopped}` only.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: `latest()` is one atomic load; `send` is one lock-free `try_send`.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
Depends on E09-001 (`ActionGate`, `Publisher`) and E08-A1. asupersync: `watch::Sender::send` L488 works with zero receivers; `mpsc::Sender::try_send` L720 (`channel/mpsc.rs`). Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

## Shared handles (B3 open item 8, added after the B4 review)
`EngineHooks.action_gate` takes a context: `pub action_gate: Option<Arc<dyn Fn(HookCtx) -> Box<dyn ActionGate> + Send + Sync>>` with

```rust
pub struct HookCtx { pub events_tx: async_channel::Sender<ActionEvent>, pub msgs_tx: mpsc::Sender<EngineMsg>, pub boot_id: BootId, pub config: Arc<EngineConfig>, pub shared: crate::dbus::SharedHandles }
```

`HookCtx` is `pub` but used only inside the crate and by E11's `gate_factory`; it names asupersync's `mpsc::Sender`, so it is `#[doc(hidden)]` and excluded from the ADR-001 public-API check (the check lists `EngineConfig`, `EngineMode`, `Engine`, `EngineHandle`, `EngineHooks`, `ShutdownReport`, `EngineError`). `record_sink` and `journal` are unchanged.

title: E09: Engine::start (bridge.rs part 2)
description:
## Context
`Engine::start` builds the runtime, the channels and the UI-side endpoints, reads the boot id, and spawns `engine_root` with `try_spawn_with_cx` so shutdown cancellation reaches it. It is the only constructor `tl-app` calls (ADR-001 public API). Sources: ADR-004 (runtime construction, task tree), ADR-005 (channel capacities: wake 1, events 256, commands 256), ADR-003 (`BootId` from `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`), API notes section 2, E08-002, E09-016, E09-018.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/bridge.rs` (part 2):

```rust
pub struct Engine;
impl Engine {
    pub fn start(config: EngineConfig, hooks: EngineHooks) -> Result<EngineHandle, EngineError>;
}
```

Steps: `let rt = runtime::build_runtime().map_err(|e| EngineError::Runtime(e.to_string().into()))?`; `boot_id = tl_model::time::read_boot_id(&config.sys_root)` (or the E03 name); channels: `async_channel::bounded::<()>(1)`, `async_channel::bounded::<ActionEvent>(256)`, `mpsc::channel::<EngineMsg>(256)`, `watch::channel(Demand::default())`, `watch::channel(EngineSettings::default())`, `watch::channel(WorkerControl::default())`; `latest = Arc::new(ArcSwap::from_pointee(Snapshot::empty(boot_id)))` (sequence 0, every component empty with `WarmingUp`, `windows` `Unsupported`); build `RootEndpoints`; `rt.handle().try_spawn_with_cx(move |cx| session::engine_root(cx, ep)).map_err(..Spawn)?`; return the handle holding `rt`, one `RuntimeHandle` clone and the UI endpoints. `Snapshot::empty` lives in `tl-model` if E03-A2 provides it, else a private helper here.

## Acceptance Criteria

description:
## Context

title: E09: 1 Hz series tier with per-second max
description:
## Context
From P2 every series has a second, 1 Hz ring of 602 samples (10 min + 2) whose values are the per-second maximum of the fast tier, the same rule ADR-012 uses for history; it serves the 5 and 10 minute ranges. Sources: ADR-003 (two tiers), PERF-016, PERF-017, R-016, ADR-012 (per-second max), E09-002.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/series.rs`:

```rust
pub const SLOW_CAPACITY: u32 = 602;
pub const SLOW_PERIOD_NS: u64 = 1_000_000_000;
struct Entry { /* existing */ slow: SeriesRing, bucket_start_ns: TimeNs, bucket_max: Option<f32>, bucket_flags: SampleFlags }
```

`append` also folds into the slow tier: the bucket is `t_ns / 1e9`; within a bucket keep `max(value)` over `VALID` samples and OR the flags; when a sample falls in a later bucket, push `Sample { t_ns: bucket_start_ns, value: max, flags }` to `slow` (a bucket with no valid sample pushes a gap sample); a gap in the fast tier (`GAP_BEFORE`) sets `GAP_BEFORE` on the next slow sample. `publish` emits both tiers: the slow view is published in `SeriesSet.slow: Arc<[Arc<SeriesView>]>` (R-141 item 4), same ordering and `Arc` reuse rule, with `period_ns = 1e9`. Each slow view's id carries the tier bit: `SeriesId { device, metric: metric.with_tier_1hz() }` (`MetricId::TIER_1HZ = 0x8000`, R-170 item 2), so `SeriesSet::get` finds it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 10 Hz samples 1..=10 within one second **When** the next second's first sample arrives **Then** the slow tier holds one sample with value 10 and `t_ns` at the bucket start.
- **Given** 700 s of 1 Hz input **When** published **Then** the slow view holds 602 samples and the fast view 62.
- **Given** a second with no valid sample **When** folded **Then** the slow sample for it is a gap (`VALID` clear).
- **Given** `mark_gap_all` **When** the next bucket closes **Then** that slow sample has `GAP_BEFORE`.
- **Given** no new sample for a series **When** published twice **Then** the slow `Arc<SeriesView>` is pointer-equal across the two sets.
- **Given** a `CPU_TOTAL` series **When** published **Then** its slow view's id has `metric.is_tier_1hz()` true and `metric.base() == MetricId::CPU_TOTAL` (R-170 item 2).

title: E09: pseudo rows Interrupts and Memory compression (zram)
description:
## Context
Two pseudo-process rows stand for kernel work no process owns: "Interrupts" (CPU = irq + softirq share, every other column `n/a`, always present) and "Memory compression (zram)" (Memory = Σ `mem_used_total`, Disk = Σ zram read and write rates, CPU `n/a`, present only when a zram device has `disksize > 0`). They sit in System processes after "Kernel threads (N)", are top-level rows in Tree and List, are excluded from the "N Processes" count, and are hidden by Hide system processes. Sources: PROC-012, R-032, U-21 (`CONFIG_IRQ_TIME_ACCOUNTING`, E05 records), E08-003 (`CpuSample.irq_pct`, `MemorySample.zram`), E09-011.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs` and `apply.rs`:

```rust
pub struct PseudoInput { pub irq_pct: Option<f32> /* None when irq time is not accounted (U-21) */, pub zram: Vec<ZramStat> }
pub fn pseudo_rows(input: &PseudoInput) -> Vec<GroupRow>;   // GroupKind::Pseudo(PseudoRow::Interrupts) always; Pseudo(PseudoRow::Zram) when any zram.disksize > 0
```

Row values: Interrupts `cpu_pct = irq_pct` (`Unsupported` with the tooltip text carried in `GroupRow.note: Option<Arc<str>>` = "Interrupt time is included in task time on this kernel" when `None`), every other field `Unsupported`, name "Interrupts", user "root", count 0. Zram: `rss_anon_bytes = Σ mem_used_total`, `io_read_bps = Σ read_bps`, `io_write_bps = Σ write_bps`, `cpu_pct` `Unsupported`, `note` = "Original <orig> · Compressed <compr> · Ratio <orig/compr:.2>" formatted with `tl_model::units`, name "Memory compression (zram)". Placement: Grouped → after the Kernel threads row in System; Tree and Flat → top-level rows sorted like any other (sort key from the row's value, `Absent` for `Unsupported`). `hide_system` hides both. The group count N excludes them. The reducer keeps the latest `irq_pct` and `zram` from `Cpu` and `Memory` samples for the next table build.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `irq_pct = Some(1.5)` and one zram device with `disksize > 0` **When** built in Grouped mode **Then** the last two System rows are "Interrupts" then "Memory compression (zram)" and the System header count excludes them.
- **Given** no zram device or all `disksize == 0` **When** built **Then** only "Interrupts" appears.
- **Given** `irq_pct = None` **When** built **Then** the Interrupts row CPU is `Unsupported` with the kernel note.
- **Given** Flat mode sorted by `cpu desc` with Interrupts at 1.5 and processes at 1.0 and 2.0 **When** built **Then** the order is 2.0, Interrupts, 1.0.
- **Given** `hide_system = true` **When** built **Then** neither pseudo row appears.
- **Given** filter `"zram"` **When** built **Then** the zram row matches by name.

## Cross-cutting

- Validity: `Unsupported` for every field the row does not define.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: two rows per build.
- Privacy: N/A

Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`.
