title: E09: subtree totals on parent processes
description:
## Context
With `processes.subtree_totals = true` (Settings > Processes > "Show subtree totals on parent processes", default off, part of `EngineSettings`), process rows that have children show the sum over their subtree for CPU, Disk, Network, GPU, Threads, Handles and Memory (Σ RssAnon), with a "Σ" prefix drawn by the UI. Each process counts once. App and unit rows always aggregate (E09-011). Sources: PROC-019, R-005, ADR-011 (`EngineSettings`), E09-010.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/table.rs`:

```rust
pub fn subtree_totals(f: &Forest, records: &[ProcessRecord], visible: &[u32]) -> Vec<GroupRow>;   // one per row with children, computed bottom-up in one pass
```

When `settings.subtree_totals` is true, every `TableRow` whose `has_children` is true gets `subtree: Some(i)` into `ProcessTableView.subtree` (the `Vec<GroupRow>` above; field per B3 open item 5); when false, `subtree` is `None` everywhere and the vector is empty. A collapsed parent in Tree mode always gets its subtree sum (ADR-009: "the collapsed parent shows its subtree sum in secondary text"), independent of the setting.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** A → B → C with cpu 1, 2, 3 and the setting on **When** built with A and B expanded **Then** A's subtree row has `cpu_pct == 6`, B's `3`, C has `subtree == None`.
- **Given** the setting off and A expanded **When** built **Then** A has `subtree == None`; with A collapsed **Then** A has a subtree row (`cpu_pct == 6`).
- **Given** memory 100, 200, 300 MiB **When** built **Then** A's subtree `rss_anon_bytes == 600 MiB`.
- **Given** a filtered-out middle node B with `include_children = false` **When** built **Then** C is a root and A's subtree sum excludes B and C (sums are over visible descendants).

title: E09: DetailsSnapshot assembly with Arc reuse and demand retain
description:
## Context
`Snapshot.details` (bit `DETAILS`) holds the Properties payloads per target and tab, the affinity masks for `affinity_targets` and the handle-search state. Unchanged payloads reuse their `Arc`; a window re-renders only when its own tab's `Arc` changed. The `ProcessDetail` worker (E10) sends `DetailsUpdate`s; the reducer assembles the component. Sources: ADR-003 (`DetailsSnapshot`, `TargetDetail`), UI-PWN-002, ADR-008 (`details`, `affinity_targets`), E08-003 (`DetailsUpdate`), R-119.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/mod.rs` and `apply.rs`:

```rust
pub struct DetailsState { targets: FxHashMap<DetailTarget, TargetDetail>, affinity: FxHashMap<ProcessKey, AffinityInfo>, handle_search: Option<Arc<HandleSearchState>>, dirty: bool }
impl DetailsState {
    pub fn apply_tab(&mut self, target: DetailTarget, tab: DetailTab, payload: Arc<TabPayload>, validity: Validity);   // replaces that tab's Arc, bumps its version
    pub fn apply_affinity(&mut self, entries: Vec<(ProcessKey, AffinityInfo)>);
    pub fn apply_handle_search(&mut self, state: Arc<HandleSearchState>);
    pub fn retain(&mut self, demand: &Demand);   // drop targets not in demand.details and keys not in affinity_targets (called on every demand change seen by the reducer through a `Demand` snapshot in `Tick`)
    pub fn publish(&mut self) -> Option<Arc<DetailsSnapshot>>;
}
```

`Tick` reads `demand.borrow_and_clone()` (the reducer holds a `watch::Receiver<Demand>` too) and calls `retain` so closed windows free their payloads within 1 s.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `apply_tab(Process(A), General, p1)` then `apply_tab(Process(A), Threads, p2)` **When** published twice **Then** the General `Arc` is pointer-equal across both snapshots and `targets[A].threads.version == 1`.
- **Given** a demand without target A **When** `Tick` runs **Then** the next snapshot has no entry for A.
- **Given** `apply_affinity` for keys A and B **When** published **Then** `affinity` has both; after demand lists only A, `retain` drops B.
- **Given** `apply_handle_search` with progress 42 **When** published **Then** `handle_search.progress == 42`; a later `None`-clearing (search ended and cleared by E10) removes it.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/mod.rs`: add `DetailsState`
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/apply.rs`: replace the `Details` arm bodies
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_reducer.rs`: add the cases

## Tests

- `lab_reducer.rs::details_retain_on_tick`
- `lab_reducer.rs::details_affinity_retain`
- `lab_reducer.rs::details_handle_search_state`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: the tab validity (`Restricted` for other users without the helper) is stored per tab.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: at most 16 targets × 9 tabs; one pointer compare per unchanged tab.
- Privacy: payloads carry environment and command lines; never logged (ADR-015).

It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E09: P2 components (connections, services, startup, inventory, windows) and sys_table calls
description:
## Context
The P2 workers publish whole components: `Connections`, `Services`, `Startup`, `Inventory`, `Windows`, plus `GpuInfo` and `GpuApiVersions` into inventory and device names. For the three system tables the reducer calls `sys_table::build` whenever the component or its `SysTableQuery` changes and stores the rows and `query_generation` in the component. Sources: ADR-003 (component fields: `rows`, `query_generation`, `counts`, `managers`, `details`, `destroy_supported`), ADR-005 (`SetSysTableQuery`), UI-SYS-002, E08-003, E09-015, R-119.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/apply.rs` (arm bodies) and `mod.rs`:
- `Connections(u)` → new `ConnectionsSnapshot { header, records: u.records.into(), counts: computed (total, tcp, udp, established, listening), destroy_supported: kept, rows, query_generation }`, then `rebuild_sys(Connections)`.
- `ConnectionsDestroySupport(b)` → `destroy_supported = Some(b)`, component replaced.
- `Services(u)` → per-manager merge: the component keeps units of both managers; `managers[u.manager] = u.state`; `details` map replaced by `u.details`; `counts` recomputed; `backend`; then `rebuild_sys(Services)`; also feeds `unit_names` (E09-025).
- `Startup(u)` → `entries`, `counts { total, enabled, disabled }`, `rebuild_sys(Startup)`.
- `Inventory(b)` → header rewritten (version, observed, validity from the box), component replaced. `GpuApiVersions` → merged into the inventory's graphics section fields (`vulkan_version`, `opengl_version` per PCI bus id). `GpuInfo` → `devices.ensure` with the display name and the caps map used by E09-006.
- `Windows(b)` → component replaced with validity `Valid`.
- `Command::SetSysTableQuery(q)` → `sys_queries[q.table] = Some(q)`, `rebuild_sys(q.table)`.
- `rebuild_sys(table)`: `sys_table::build(&SysTableInput { .. }, query)` with `query = sys_queries[table].clone().unwrap_or(SysTableQuery { table, generation: 0, sort: default_sort(table), filter: "", expanded: [], services: None })`; stores `rows` and `query_generation`; marks the component bit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a `Connections` update with 3 TCP (2 established, 1 listening) and 1 UDP record **When** applied **Then** `counts == { total: 4, tcp: 3, udp: 1, established: 2, listening: 1 }`.
- **Given** `SetSysTableQuery { table: Services, generation: 5 }` **When** applied **Then** `services.query_generation == 5` and `SERVICES` was marked even with an empty stub result.
- **Given** `Services` updates from `User` then `System` **When** applied **Then** the component holds both managers' units and `managers` shows both states.
- **Given** `ConnectionsDestroySupport(false)` **When** applied **Then** `destroy_supported == Some(false)` and it survives the next `Connections` update.
- **Given** `GpuApiVersions` with one device **When** applied after `Inventory` **Then** the inventory graphics section shows the Vulkan and OpenGL versions; applied before `Inventory` **Then** they are kept and merged when `Inventory` arrives.

title: E09: Reducer state, loop, publish and the RecordSink hook (reducer/mod.rs)
description:
## Context
The reducer is the single owner of engine state and the only publisher (ADR-004). It receives one `EngineMsg`, drains up to 256 more with `try_recv`, applies all, then publishes once; it never awaits between `latest.store` and `wake_tx.try_send`. Every component is an `Arc` replaced only when its content changed, so a CPU-only publish reuses every other `Arc` (ADR-003). This bead builds the reducer shell: state struct, loop, publish, and the `RecordSink` hook held as `None` (ADR-012). Sources: ADR-004 (reducer), ADR-005 (publish), ADR-003 (`Snapshot`, `ComponentHeader`), ADR-012 (hook), ADR-013 (coalescing test), R-119.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/mod.rs`:

```rust
pub mod apply; pub mod series; pub mod devices; pub mod health; pub mod processes; pub mod suspend; pub mod table; pub mod sys_table;
pub const DRAIN_MAX: usize = 256;

pub struct Publisher { pub latest: Arc<ArcSwap<Snapshot>>, pub wake_tx: async_channel::Sender<()>, pub stop_publishing: bool }
impl Publisher {
    /// store, then try_send; Full is fine; Closed sets stop_publishing (ADR-005)
    pub fn publish(&mut self, next: Snapshot);
}

pub struct Reducer {
    pub epoch: u32, pub boot_id: BootId, pub sequence: u64,
    pub series: series::SeriesStore, pub devices: devices::Catalog, pub health: health::HealthState,
    pub processes: processes::ProcessState, // E09-008: pub suspend: suspend::SuspendState (added by 8q0.10 as a chain edit, R-262)
    pub query: TableQuery, pub sys_queries: [Option<SysTableQuery>; 3],
    pub components: Components,                    // current Arc of every component plus its header
    pub control: watch::Sender<WorkerControl>,     // reducer-to-worker control (E08-004)
    pub record_sink: Option<Box<dyn RecordSink>>,  // None in P1 and P2 (ADR-012)
    pub action_gate: Option<Box<dyn ActionGate>>,  // None until E11-A1 installs one
    pub events_tx: async_channel::Sender<ActionEvent>,
    pub helper_tx: Option<mpsc::Sender<HelperCommand>>, // None until E29-020 (qfx.23) sets it (R-148 item 1)
    dirty: ComponentMask,
}
/// Helper session commands routed by apply.rs (R-148 item 1). The helper is not a supervised source, so `forward()` does not fit.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum HelperCommand { Start, End, SetupStatus, RunSetup(SetupStep) }   // SetupStep is tl-model's (as2.29); SetupStatus and RunSetup added by R-247
pub struct Components { pub system: Arc<SystemSnapshot>, pub series: Arc<SeriesSet>, pub processes: Arc<ProcessSnapshot>, pub table: Arc<ProcessTableView>, pub connections: Arc<ConnectionsSnapshot>, pub services: Arc<ServicesSnapshot>, pub startup: Arc<StartupSnapshot>, pub inventory: Arc<InventorySnapshot>, pub devices: Arc<DeviceCatalog>, pub health: Arc<HealthSnapshot>, pub windows: Arc<WindowsSnapshot>, pub details: Arc<DetailsSnapshot>, pub history: Arc<HistoryView>,
    pub process_series: Arc<ProcessSeriesSet> /* R-154 */, pub device_details: Arc<DeviceDetailsSnapshot> /* R-139 */ }

pub trait ActionGate: Send + 'static {
    fn submit(&mut self, cx: &Cx, req: ActionRequest, view: &AdmissionView<'_>);
    fn finished(&mut self, id: ActionId) -> Option<SourceId>;   // which source to refresh (E11)
}
pub struct AdmissionView<'a> { pub boot_id: BootId, pub live: &'a FxHashMap<ProcessKey, ProcFlags>, pub exited_within_linger: &'a FxHashSet<ProcessKey> }

impl Reducer {
    pub fn new(epoch: u32, boot_id: BootId, control: watch::Sender<WorkerControl>, events_tx: async_channel::Sender<ActionEvent>) -> Self;   // empty rings, header versions 0, validity WarmingUp, helper_tx None
    /// The loop: recv one, drain up to DRAIN_MAX, apply, publish once. Returns Err on an invariant violation (session restarts).
    pub async fn run(&mut self, cx: &Cx, rx: &mut mpsc::Receiver<EngineMsg>, publisher: &mut Publisher) -> Result<(), InvariantViolation>;
    pub fn mark(&mut self, bit: ComponentMask);    // called by apply when a component changed
    fn build_snapshot(&mut self) -> Snapshot;      // sequence += 1; headers of dirty components get version += 1 and observed times; others reuse their Arc
}
pub use devices::InvariantViolation;   // `#[derive(Debug)] pub struct InvariantViolation(pub &'static str)` is defined in reducer/devices.rs by E09-003 (8q0.5), which this bead depends on (R-262)
```

`build_snapshot` bumps only dirty components; `published_ns = now_boot_ns()`; `epoch` and `boot_id` copied. The `Snapshot.history`, `windows`, `details` and other P2 and P3 components start as empty `Arc`s with validity `Unsupported` (`windows`, ADR-003) or `WarmingUp`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 100 queued `EngineMsg::Source` messages **When** `run` wakes once **Then** exactly one `publish` happens and `latest().sequence` rose by 1 (ADR-013 "coalesces 100 messages into one publish").
- **Given** 300 queued messages **When** `run` wakes **Then** two publishes happen (256 then 44) and the sequence rises by 2.
- **Given** a message that only changes CPU series **When** published **Then** `Arc::ptr_eq` holds for `processes`, `table`, `devices`, `health` and every other component against the previous snapshot, and `series.header.version` rose by 1.
- **Given** the wake receiver is never read **When** 10,000 publishes happen **Then** none blocks and `latest()` holds only the newest snapshot.
- **Given** the wake receiver is dropped **When** the next publish runs **Then** `stop_publishing` becomes true and `run` returns `Ok(())`.
- **Given** `record_sink` is `None` **When** a process sweep is applied **Then** no sink call happens (checked by a counting sink installed in a second test: with `Some`, `on_process_sweep` is called once per sweep).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/mod.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_reducer.rs`: create with the cases above (E09-021 adds more)

## Tests
- `lab_reducer.rs::coalesces_100_messages_into_one_publish`
- `lab_reducer.rs::drain_cap_256_splits_publishes`
- `lab_reducer.rs::cpu_only_change_reuses_other_arcs`
- `lab_reducer.rs::publish_never_blocks_without_reader`
- `lab_reducer.rs::closed_wake_stops_publishing`
- `lab_reducer.rs::record_sink_called_when_installed`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `InvariantViolation` (for example a `DeviceIdx` out of range) ends the session; the session loop restarts with a new epoch (E09-016).
- Validity: fresh components are `WarmingUp`; `windows` is `Unsupported` until the KWin worker publishes.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one `Arc::new(Snapshot)` per publish (14 pointer copies); no per-message allocation beyond the payload move.
- Privacy: the reducer never logs record contents; `tracing::debug!` on target `tasklens::engine` logs counts only.

## Notes
`ArcSwap::store` then `async_channel::Sender::try_send` (`TrySendError::{Full, Closed}`), ADR-005. `mpsc::Receiver::recv(&mut self, cx)` L1576 and `try_recv` L1807 (asupersync `channel/mpsc.rs`). Large-file rule: commit before building. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E09: HistoryView component and the remaining RecordSink calls
description:
## Context
In P3 the history recorder (or the 10-minute rolling window while recording is off) is a `RecordSink` installed through `EngineHooks.record_sink`, and `HistoryQuery` answers arrive as `SourceUpdate::History(Arc<HistoryView>)` for the `Snapshot.history` component (bit `HISTORY`). The reducer already calls the sink (E09-001, E09-005); this bead wires the remaining calls and the component. Sources: ADR-012 (hook, `HistoryView`, 1,024 points), D-003, D-010, E08-003, E30-A2 (producer).

- `on_system_sample(t_ns, &[(SeriesId, Sample)])` is called once per applied system sample batch (`Cpu`, `Memory`, `Disks`, `Nets`, `Sensors`, `Gpu`) with the samples appended in that batch.

title: E09-029 Per-process series from Demand.graph_targets
description:
## Context
Process, name and app graphs (the minigraph cards of E26 and the tray process graphs of E31) need a series that the engine samples even while the Processes table is hidden. R-154 item 2 settles the shape: the UI lists what it wants in `Demand.graph_targets: Arc<[(GraphTarget, ColumnId)]>` (at most 16, `GRAPH_TARGETS_MAX`), and the reducer appends one sample per sweep per target into rings published as `Snapshot.process_series: ProcessSeriesSet` (mask bit `PROCESS_SERIES = 1 << 13`). This bead writes that reducer part. Sources: R-154, PROC-093, PROC-094, PERF-080, PERF-085, ADR-003 `SeriesId`, ADR-008 `Demand`.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/process_series.rs` plus the `reducer/mod.rs` line `mod process_series;`:

```rust
/// Columns that may be graph sources (R-154 item 2); other columns are ignored.
pub(crate) const GRAPH_COLUMNS: [ColumnId; 6] = [ColumnId::CPU, ColumnId::MEMORY, ColumnId::DISK, ColumnId::NETWORK, ColumnId::GPU, ColumnId::GPU_MEM_DEDICATED];

pub(crate) struct ProcessSeries { /* entries: FxHashMap<ProcessSeriesId, Entry { fast: SeriesRing, slow tier as in series.rs }>, version: u64, last_published: Option<Arc<ProcessSeriesSet>> */ }
impl ProcessSeries {
    pub(crate) fn new() -> Self;
    /// Keeps entries for the ids in `targets` (after the GRAPH_COLUMNS filter), drops the rest at once.
    pub(crate) fn set_targets(&mut self, targets: &[(GraphTarget, ColumnId)]);
    /// One sample per entry from one process sweep.
    pub(crate) fn on_sweep(&mut self, t_ns: TimeNs, records: &[ProcessRecord], extras: &[ProcessExtras]);
    pub(crate) fn mark_gap_all(&mut self);
    /// Arc-reusing publish; `None` when nothing changed since the last call.
    pub(crate) fn publish(&mut self, header: ComponentHeader) -> Option<Arc<ProcessSeriesSet>>;
}
```

Rules:
- Value per target: `Process(key)` takes the record with that key; `Name(n)` sums over records whose `meta.name` equals `n` exactly; `App(id)` sums over records whose group is `App { app_id == id }` or whose unit name is `id` (R-161 item 5: tray `app:<id>` and unit rows). The column value is the one the table cell shows for that column, read through the same column getter the table builder uses (E09 table code), never re-derived here.
- No matching process, or a matching process whose value is not `Valid`, appends a gap sample (`VALID` clear), so the chart breaks the line.
- Rings: the same fast ring size as device series (60 s at the sweep period) plus the 1 Hz slow tier of E09-024 (8q0.24, per-second max, 602 samples). `ProcessSeriesId { target, column }` is the key; the slow view's id has no tier bit (process series ids are not `MetricId`s), and the slow views go in the same `ProcessSeriesSet.series` list after the fast ones, in the same order.
- `apply.rs` wiring (chain edit, three lines): the `Processes` arm calls `on_sweep` after the table update; the demand change path calls `set_targets(&demand.graph_targets)`; the publish path sets `Snapshot.process_series` and the `PROCESS_SERIES` bit when `publish` returns `Some`.
- The Processes worker runs while `graph_targets` is non-empty even when `process_table` is false (dwy.4, R-154 item 2); this bead only consumes the sweeps.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `graph_targets = [(Process(k), CPU)]` and three sweeps where `k` has CPU 10, 20, 30 % **When** published **Then** the series for `(Process(k), CPU)` holds the three values in order.
- **Given** `(Name("firefox"), MEMORY)` and two processes named `firefox` with memory 100 MB and 50 MB **When** one sweep runs **Then** the sample is 150 MB.
- **Given** `(App("org.kde.konsole"), CPU)` and a sweep without any konsole process **When** run **Then** the appended sample is a gap.
- **Given** a target with column `PID` **When** `set_targets` runs **Then** no entry is created.
- **Given** a target removed from `graph_targets` **When** `set_targets` runs **Then** its entry is gone from the next published set.
- **Given** no new sweep **When** `publish` is called twice **Then** the second call returns `None`; with a new sweep the unchanged series' `Arc<SeriesView>` values are pointer-equal to the previous set's.
- **Given** 17 targets in a demand **When** applied **Then** only the first 16 are kept (`clamp_lists`, GRAPH_TARGETS_MAX).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/process_series.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/mod.rs`: `mod process_series;` (chain edit, that line only)
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/apply.rs`: chain edit, the three call sites above

## Tests
- `process_series.rs::tests::process_target_values`, `::name_target_sums`, `::app_target_gap_when_absent`, `::non_graph_column_ignored`, `::removed_target_dropped`, `::publish_arc_reuse_and_none`, `::targets_clamped_16`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: gaps for missing or non-`Valid` values; never a zero in place of a missing value.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: at most 16 entries; `Name` and `App` targets scan the record slice once per sweep each (2,000 records: one compare per record per target).
- Privacy: process names are not logged.

## Notes
- Depends on E09-A1 (8q0.1) and E03-A2 (as2.2: `GraphTarget`, `ProcessSeriesId`, `ProcessSeriesSet`, `Demand.graph_targets`). Phase P2. wox.9 (E31 tray process graphs) and E26-011 (minigraph cards) depend on this bead (R-154).
- Read `/home/oystein/work/tasklens/CLAUDE.md` first.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

Commits 085786b, 9ab3a02. Open point: ProcessSeriesSet::get binary search does not fit the fast-then-slow layout with 2+ targets.

title: E09-030 Process power estimate (PROC-034)
description:
## Context
The "Power usage" and "Power usage trend" columns (PROC-034) show an estimate per process built from measured power: package power from RAPL (E12-008) shared by CPU time, plus each GPU's power shared by the process's GPU use. R-163 item 9 (E05 item 13) gives the computation to the reducer, which has the CPU totals, the GPU totals and the process records in one place, and writes `ProcessExtrasP2.power_w` and `power_trend_w` for every row. Sources: R-163, PROC-034, R-006, R-028, ADR-008.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/power.rs` plus the `reducer/mod.rs` line `mod power;`:

```rust
pub(crate) const POWER_TREND_WINDOW_NS: u64 = 120_000_000_000;   // 2 minutes

pub(crate) struct PowerEstimator { /* prev: FxHashMap<ProcessKey, u64 /* utime+stime ticks */>, trend: FxHashMap<ProcessKey, VecDeque<(TimeNs, f32)>> */ }
impl PowerEstimator {
    pub(crate) fn new() -> Self;
    /// One estimate per record. `p2` is index-aligned with `records` and is created with defaults when empty.
    pub(crate) fn on_sweep(&mut self, t_ns: TimeNs, records: &[ProcessRecord], extras: &[ProcessExtras],
                           cpu: &CpuTotals, gpus: &[GpuShare], p2: &mut Vec<ProcessExtrasP2>);
    pub(crate) fn reset(&mut self);   // on resume and on reset_baselines
}
/// Per GPU: measured power and each process's utilisation on it.
pub(crate) struct GpuShare<'a> { pub power_w: Option<f32>, pub util_by_key: &'a FxHashMap<ProcessKey, f32> }
```

Rules (PROC-034):
- CPU term: `P_pkg × Δcpu_p / Σ Δcpu`, where `P_pkg` is `cpu.package_power_w` when `Valid`, `Δcpu_p` is the change of `utime_ticks + stime_ticks` of the process since the previous sweep, and `Σ Δcpu` is the sum of that change over every record of this sweep. A process seen for the first time has no `Δcpu_p` and no estimate yet (`None`). `Σ Δcpu == 0` gives a CPU term of 0.
- GPU term: `Σ over GPUs of P_gpu × u_p / Σ_q u_q` with `P_gpu` the GPU's measured power (NVML through the probe, or hwmon `power1_average` for amdgpu, as the GPU workers already publish) and `u` the per-process utilisation on that GPU. A GPU without measured power, or with `Σ u == 0`, adds 0. If the reducer has only the per-process total over all GPUs and not the per-GPU values, stop and report to the leader.
- `power_w = Some(cpu_term + gpu_term)` when `P_pkg` is `Valid` or at least one GPU term exists; otherwise `None`. A guessed value is never written: when RAPL is `Restricted` and no GPU has power, every row is `None`, and the UI shows `n/a` with "Needs setup" from the RAPL validity (R-028), or "No power sensor available" when RAPL is `Unsupported` and no GPU reports power.
- `power_trend_w`: time-weighted mean of this key's `power_w` samples over the last `POWER_TREND_WINDOW_NS`; `None` until two samples exist. Entries of dead keys are dropped each sweep.
- Every row gets a value, not only `detail_keys` (one multiply per process per sweep). `p2` entries outside `detail_keys` keep `key == None` and default fields apart from the two power fields.
- `apply.rs` wiring (chain edit, two lines): the `Processes` arm calls `on_sweep` after E05-035's `extras_p2` is in place and before the snapshot is published; the resume path calls `reset`.
- App rows sum their members' values (PROC-034); the UI sums from the members, so this bead adds nothing to group rows.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `P_pkg = 20 W` and two processes whose ticks grow by 30 and 10 between two sweeps, no GPU power **When** the second sweep runs **Then** their `power_w` is `Some(15.0)` and `Some(5.0)`.
- **Given** one GPU at 100 W with utilisation 60 % for process A and 20 % for B **When** a sweep runs with `P_pkg` `Valid` and zero CPU deltas **Then** A gets 75 W and B 25 W.
- **Given** `package_power_w` `Restricted` and no GPU power **When** a sweep runs **Then** every `power_w` is `None`.
- **Given** a process first seen in this sweep **When** run **Then** its `power_w` is `None`.
- **Given** samples 10 W for 60 s then 20 W for 60 s **When** the trend is read at 120 s **Then** `power_trend_w` is `Some(15.0)` within 0.01.
- **Given** `reset` **When** the next sweep runs **Then** no process has a `power_w` (no previous ticks).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/power.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/mod.rs`: `mod power;` (chain edit, that line only)
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/apply.rs`: chain edit, the two call sites above

## Tests
- `power.rs::tests::cpu_share_by_ticks`, `::gpu_share_by_util`, `::restricted_rapl_no_estimate`, `::first_sight_none`, `::trend_two_minute_mean`, `::reset_clears_baselines`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: `None` whenever an input is missing; never a guessed class (PROC-034).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: O(records + GPU entries) per sweep; the trend keeps at most 120 s of samples per live key (at 1 Hz, 120 entries).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Depends on E09-A1 (8q0.1), E12-008 (hjn.11, `CpuTotals.package_power_w`) and E13-A1 (ndy.2, GPU power and per-process GPU use). Phase P2. Both columns are off by default (R-006).
- Read `/home/oystein/work/tasklens/CLAUDE.md` first.

It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: Reducer: normalise PCI bus ids for inventory GPU matching, rematch on catalog change, disk names
description:

The match also runs only when an Inventory arrives, so a GPU catalog entry that arrives later leaves device None until the next scan. DiskDrive has no name, so disks cannot be matched to the Disk catalog entry (R-166).

- Add DiskDrive.name: Option<Arc<str>> (kernel name like "nvme0n1"), fill it in the inventory worker, and map disks to the Disk catalog entry by name.

Lab test: Inventory first, then an NVIDIA GpuInfo with "00000000:01:00.0" and an adapter with "0000:01:00.0": the adapter gets device and api versions without a new Inventory. Lab test: a disk row gets its catalog device by name. clippy clean.

title: Reducer: merge GPU samples, device lists and caps per source so AMD and NVIDIA coexist
description:
Files: crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/apply.rs, crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_reducer.rs.
Why: hjn.29 (dce5917) added the AMD gpu_drm worker next to the NVIDIA worker. On a host with both: (1) a GpuDrm Devices(GPUS) full list leaves out NVIDIA cards and apply_list marks them absent; (2) a Gpu sample from either worker replaces system.gpus, dropping the other vendor's rows; (3) GpuInfo runs gpu_caps.clear(), dropping the other vendor's caps; (4) gpu_power is keyed by UUID, so AMD cards without a UUID share one entry.

GpuInfo from S clears only S's caps. Key gpu_power by the catalog device id (or pci bus id) rather than UUID when the UUID is missing. Keep the single-vendor paths unchanged.
AC: lab test with one NVIDIA and one AMD card: interleaved samples from both workers keep both rows, both catalog entries stay present, both caps stay, and two AMD cards get two gpu_power entries. Existing lab_reducer tests pass. clippy clean with and without test-hooks.

title: E09: SeriesStore fast tier with gaps and Arc reuse (reducer/series.rs)
description:
## Context
Every graph series is a `SeriesRing` owned by the reducer and published as an immutable `SeriesView`. The fast tier has capacity `ceil(60 s / period) + 2` (602 at 10 Hz, 62 at 1 Hz); a rate change keeps the ring and marks `GAP_BEFORE` on the first sample; unchanged series reuse their `Arc` in `SeriesSet`. Sources: ADR-003 (series, tiers, `SeriesSet`), ADR-008 (stale threshold, `GAP_BEFORE` on resume and rate change, counter rules), PERF-017, PERF-022, R-016, R-051.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/series.rs`:

```rust
pub struct SeriesStore { rings: FxHashMap<SeriesId, Entry>, pending_gap: bool /* set by suspend, applied to every series' next sample */ }
struct Entry { ring: SeriesRing, period_ns: u64, view: Option<Arc<SeriesView>> /* cached until the next append */, gap_next: bool }
impl SeriesStore {
    pub fn fast_capacity(period_ns: u64) -> u32;   // ceil(60e9 / period_ns) + 2
    /// Appends; creates the ring on first use; a period change sets gap_next; `valid == false` appends a gap sample (VALID clear).
    pub fn append(&mut self, id: SeriesId, t_ns: TimeNs, value: f32, period_ns: u64, flags: SampleFlags);
    pub fn append_gap(&mut self, id: SeriesId, t_ns: TimeNs);
    pub fn mark_gap_all(&mut self);                 // next sample of every series gets GAP_BEFORE
    pub fn mark_stale(&mut self, now_ns: TimeNs);   // STALE flag bookkeeping: a series whose last t is older than max(3 × period, 1.5 s)
    pub fn changed(&self) -> SmallVec<[SeriesId; 64]>;
    pub fn publish(&mut self) -> Arc<SeriesSet>;    // sorted by SeriesId; unchanged entries reuse `view`
}
```

Value conversion: callers pass `f32` graph values; counters stay `u64` upstream (ADR-003). `Sample { t_ns, value, flags }` is 16 bytes. The 1 Hz tier is E09-022 (P2) and must not change these signatures.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** period 100 ms **When** `fast_capacity` is called **Then** it returns 602; for 1 s it returns 62.
- **Given** 700 appends at 100 ms **When** `publish` runs **Then** the view holds the newest 602 in chronological order.
- **Given** a series at 100 ms **When** the next append passes period 1 s **Then** that sample carries `GAP_BEFORE` and the ring keeps its older samples.
- **Given** two series and an append to one **When** `publish` runs twice **Then** the untouched series' `Arc<SeriesView>` is pointer-equal across the two sets and the touched one is not.
- **Given** `mark_gap_all` then one append per series **When** published **Then** every series' newest sample has `GAP_BEFORE`.
- **Given** a 1 s series whose last sample is 4 s old **When** `mark_stale(now)` runs **Then** `changed()` names it and its view is rebuilt with `STALE` on the newest sample; a 10 Hz series 1.4 s old is not stale (threshold `max(0.3 s, 1.5 s)`).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/series.rs`: create

## Tests
- `series.rs::tests::capacity_rule`
- `series.rs::tests::ring_keeps_newest_602`
- `series.rs::tests::rate_change_marks_gap_before`
- `series.rs::tests::unchanged_series_reuse_arc`
- `series.rs::tests::gap_all_then_append`
- `series.rs::tests::stale_threshold`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: a gap sample has `VALID` clear; stale samples carry `STALE` (the chart draws at 50% alpha then a gap).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: about 1.5 MB for 80 series; `publish` allocates one `Arc<[Sample]>` per changed series only.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
`SeriesRing` and `SeriesView` live in `tl-model/src/series.rs` (E03-A1); if `SeriesRing` lacks a `to_view` method, add the copy here, not in `tl-model`. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E09: device catalog with generations (reducer/devices.rs)
description:
## Context
The reducer owns the device catalog: every `DeviceIdentity` gets a stable `DeviceIdx` for the session; a device that disappears keeps its index with `present = false`; one that returns with the same identity keeps the index and gets `generation + 1`; counters are never subtracted across generations. The CPU package and each logical CPU are devices too. Sources: ADR-003 (device identity, catalog), ADR-008 (CPU hotplug, enumeration every 5 s), PERF-005 (hotplug and stable keys), E08-003 `DeviceList`.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/devices.rs`:

```rust
pub struct Catalog { entries: Vec<DeviceEntry>, by_identity: FxHashMap<DeviceIdentity, DeviceIdx>, version: u64, dirty: bool }
impl Catalog {
    pub fn new() -> Self;   // entry 0 = CpuPackage, present = true, display "CPU", persistent_key "cpu"; then Aggregate(Disks), Aggregate(Nets),
                            // Aggregate(Gpus), present = true, keys "aggregate:disk", "aggregate:net", "aggregate:gpu" (R-154 item 1)
    pub fn idx(&self, id: &DeviceIdentity) -> Option<DeviceIdx>;
    pub fn ensure(&mut self, id: &DeviceIdentity, display_name: &str, parent: Option<&DeviceIdentity>, persistent_key: &str, net_kind: Option<NetKind>) -> (DeviceIdx, bool /* new or regenerated */);
    // persistent_key and net_kind come from DeviceDesc (E08-003) and GpuStaticInfo; stored in DeviceEntry (R-155 item 7).
    // The Gpu and GpuInfo arms call ensure per identity; there is no GPUS list in P1 (R-155 item 8).
    /// Apply a full list for `kinds`: new identities are added, missing ones become present=false, returning ones bump generation.
    pub fn apply_list(&mut self, list: &DeviceList) -> Vec<(DeviceIdx, DeviceChange)>;   // Added | Removed | Returned
    pub fn set_cpus(&mut self, online: &CpuSet) -> bool;   // CpuLogical devices; offline → present=false; returns changed
    pub fn generation(&self, idx: DeviceIdx) -> u32;
    pub fn publish(&mut self) -> Option<Arc<DeviceCatalog>>;   // Some when changed since the last publish
}
pub enum DeviceChange { Added, Removed, Returned }
```

`DeviceIdx` is `u16`; more than 65,535 devices is an `InvariantViolation`. Kinds in `DeviceList.kinds` decide which identity variants a list is complete for (`DISKS` → `Disk`, `NETS` → `Net`, `SENSORS` → `Sensor`, `FANS` → `Fan`, `GPUS` → `Gpu`, `BATTERIES` → `Battery`, `CPUS` → `CpuLogical`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a list with disk `sda` **When** applied, then a list without it, then with it again **Then** `sda` keeps its `DeviceIdx`, `present` goes true, false, true and `generation` goes 0, 0, 1.
- **Given** a `DISKS` list **When** applied **Then** `Net` entries are untouched.
- **Given** `set_cpus` with CPUs 0 to 31 then 0 to 30 **When** applied **Then** CPU 31 is `present = false` and the catalog version rose.
- **Given** no change **When** `publish` is called **Then** it returns `None` and the previous `Arc<DeviceCatalog>` stays valid.
- **Given** a partition `sda1` with parent `sda` **When** applied **Then** `entries[sda1].parent == Some(idx(sda))`.
- **Given** a `DeviceDesc` with `persistent_key "disk:0x5002538e40a1b2c3"` **When** applied **Then** the published entry carries that key (R-155 item 7); a `Net` entry with `net_kind: Some(Wired)` stores it.
- **Given** `Catalog::new()` **When** published **Then** it holds `CpuPackage` at idx 0 and the three `Aggregate` devices, all `present = true` (R-154 item 1).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/devices.rs`: create; it also defines `#[derive(Debug)] pub struct InvariantViolation(pub &'static str);`, which `reducer/mod.rs` (E09-001) re-exports (R-262)

## Tests
- `devices.rs::tests::returning_device_keeps_idx_and_bumps_generation`
- `devices.rs::tests::list_scoped_by_kinds`
- `devices.rs::tests::cpu_hotplug_marks_missing`
- `devices.rs::tests::publish_none_when_unchanged`
- `devices.rs::tests::partition_parent_link`
- `devices.rs::tests::persistent_key_stored`, `new_catalog_has_aggregates`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: index overflow → `InvariantViolation("device index overflow")`.
- Validity: a `present = false` device's series get `Missing` at the next sample (E09-007 uses `generation` and `present`).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: `apply_list` is O(n) with one hash lookup per entry; runs every 5 s.
- Privacy: display names are device model strings; no serials beyond `wwn_or_serial` in the identity (never logged above `debug`).

## Notes
`DeviceIdentity`, `DeviceEntry`, `DeviceCatalog` are in `tl-model/src/devices.rs` (E03-A1). Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
close_reason: Catalog in crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/devices.rs with generations, kind-scoped apply_list, set_cpus, publish and InvariantViolation; ensure/apply_list/set_cpus return Result for index overflow. Commits c85eee9, e8fa85a, f697228

title: E09: health state and stale marking (reducer/health.rs)
description:
## Context
`Snapshot.health` carries one `SourceHealth` per `SourceId` so the Collector Health chip can show "<Source> data stale", "<Source> unavailable" and "<Source> paused after errors" with the `last_error` tooltip. Workers send `Health` updates (`Running`, `Late`, `Failed`, `Disabled { until }`); the reducer adds `Stale` from timestamps on `Tick`. Sources: ADR-004 (controller health), ADR-008 (stale threshold), ADR-015 (errors appear as `Validity::Failed` plus `last_error`), UI-SHL collector health, E08-003, E08-006.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/health.rs`:

```rust
pub struct HealthState { by_id: FxHashMap<SourceId, Entry>, dirty: bool }
struct Entry { state: SourceState, last_error: Option<Arc<str>>, last_ok_ns: Option<TimeNs>, period_ns: Option<u64>, stale: bool }
impl HealthState {
    pub fn apply(&mut self, id: SourceId, state: SourceState, last_error: Option<Arc<str>>, t_ns: TimeNs);
    pub fn sample_ok(&mut self, id: SourceId, t_ns: TimeNs, period_ns: u64);   // called by apply.rs for every data update
    pub fn tick(&mut self, now_ns: TimeNs) -> bool;   // stale = now - last_ok > max(3 × period, 1.5 s) for Running sources; returns changed
    pub fn is_down(&self, id: SourceId) -> bool;      // Failed or Disabled
    pub fn publish(&mut self) -> Option<Arc<HealthSnapshot>>;
    pub fn all_failed(epoch: u32, reason: &str) -> Arc<HealthSnapshot>;   // used by the session after 3 restarts in 60 s
}
```

`SourceHealth` (tl-model `health.rs`) is filled as: `state`, `last_error`, `last_ok_ns`, `stale`. The display names table ("CPU", "Memory", "Disks", "Network", "GPU", "Sensors", "Processes", "Services", "Startup", "Connections", "Inventory", "KWin") is UI-side; the engine sends only `SourceId`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `apply(Cpu, Running)` and `sample_ok(Cpu, t, 100 ms)` **When** `tick(t + 1.4 s)` **Then** not stale; **When** `tick(t + 1.6 s)` **Then** stale and `tick` returned true.
- **Given** a 1 s source **When** `tick(t + 2.9 s)` **Then** not stale; at `t + 3.1 s` stale.
- **Given** `apply(Cpu, Disabled { until })` **When** `is_down(Cpu)` **Then** true; `apply(Cpu, Running)` clears it and `stale` resets.
- **Given** `all_failed(3, "engine restarted too often")` **When** read **Then** every `SourceId` is `Failed` with that `last_error`.
- **Given** two consecutive `tick`s with no change **When** `publish` is called **Then** the second returns `None`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/health.rs`: create

## Tests
- `health.rs::tests::stale_after_threshold_10hz`
- `health.rs::tests::stale_after_threshold_1hz`

title: E09: process cache with linger, NEW and EXITED (reducer/processes.rs)
description:
## Context
The reducer keeps the process metadata cache: live records plus at most 256 exited ones kept for the linger time (`2 × processes.interval_ms` clamped to 1..=3 s), sets `NEW` and `EXITED`, keeps records sorted by `ProcessKey`, and builds `ProcessSnapshot` with `coverage`. It also feeds `RecordSink::on_process_sweep`. Sources: ADR-004 (bounded reducer state, linger), ADR-003 (`ProcFlags`, `ProcessSnapshot`, `Coverage`), ADR-008 (coverage of PSS), PROC-043, R-041, ADR-012 (hook), E08-003 `ProcessSweep`.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/processes.rs`:

```rust
pub const MAX_EXITED: usize = 256;
pub fn linger_ns(interval_ms: u32) -> u64;   // clamp(2 × interval_ms, 1000, 3000) × 1e6

pub struct ProcessState {
    live: FxHashMap<ProcessKey, Live>,           // Live { record: ProcessRecord, first_seen_ns }
    exited: VecDeque<(ProcessKey, TimeNs /* exit seen */, ProcessRecord)>,
    extras: FxHashMap<ProcessKey, ProcessExtras>,      // from ProcessSweep.extras (R-141 item 1)
    extras_p2: FxHashMap<ProcessKey, ProcessExtrasP2>, // from ProcessSweep.extras_p2, detail_keys only (R-163 item 2)
    app_stats: Vec<AppCgroupSample>, unit_stats: Vec<CgroupStats>,   // AppCgroupSample is the tl-model type (R-141 item 2)
    low_memory: Option<Arc<LowMemoryInfo>>,            // from ProcessSweep.low_memory (R-150 item 2)
    system_threads: u32, file_nr: Option<u64>, online_cpus: u16,
    last_sweep_ns: TimeNs, dirty: bool,
}
impl ProcessState {
    /// Diff the sweep against `live`: new keys get NEW (first_seen = observed_end); missing keys move to `exited` with EXITED; cap 256 (drop oldest).
    pub fn apply_sweep(&mut self, sweep: ProcessSweep, now_ns: TimeNs, interval_ms: u32, sink: Option<&mut dyn RecordSink>);
    /// Called on Tick: clears NEW after linger, drops exited after linger; returns changed.
    pub fn expire(&mut self, now_ns: TimeNs, interval_ms: u32) -> bool;
    pub fn flags(&self, key: &ProcessKey) -> Option<ProcFlags>;
    pub fn live_keys(&self) -> &FxHashMap<ProcessKey, ProcFlags>;          // for admission (E11)
    pub fn exited_within_linger(&self) -> FxHashSet<ProcessKey>;
    pub fn records_sorted(&self) -> Vec<ProcessRecord>;                    // live plus exited, by ProcessKey
    pub fn publish(&mut self, coverage: Coverage, observed: (TimeNs, TimeNs)) -> Option<Arc<ProcessSnapshot>>;
}
```

`apply_sweep` keeps the sweep's record for a key seen before (counters already rate-converted by `tl-collect`), copies the flags `KERNEL_THREAD`, `OTHER_USER`, `IS_SELF`, `PROTECTED` from the sweep, and owns `NEW` and `EXITED` itself. An exited record keeps its last values; the table shows it greyed (UI). `on_process_sweep(t_ns = observed_end, &Arc<[ProcessRecord]>)` is called once per sweep when a sink is installed. `publish` builds `ProcessSnapshot.extras` and `.extras_p2` index aligned with `records` (an exited record keeps its last extras; a record without P2 values gets `ProcessExtrasP2::default()`), `.apps` sorted by `GroupKey`, and copies `.low_memory` (R-141, R-150, R-163).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a sweep of three records with three extras **When** published **Then** `extras.len() == records.len()` and `extras[i].start_ticks == records[i].key.start_ticks` for every `i` (R-141 item 1).
- **Given** sweep 1 with keys A, B **When** applied at t0 **Then** both have `NEW`; **When** `expire(t0 + linger + 1 ms)` **Then** neither has `NEW`.
- **Given** sweep 2 without B at t1 **When** applied **Then** B is in `exited` with `EXITED`, `records_sorted` still contains B, and `exited_within_linger` contains B; after `expire(t1 + linger + 1 ms)` B is gone.
- **Given** 300 processes exit in one sweep **When** applied **Then** `exited.len() == 256` and the 44 oldest by exit time were dropped.
- **Given** `interval_ms = 250` **When** `linger_ns` is called **Then** 1,000,000,000; for 1000 → 2,000,000,000; for 5000 → 3,000,000,000.
- **Given** a key that exited and a new process reuses its PID with a different `start_ticks` **When** the next sweep arrives **Then** both records exist (different keys) and only the new one has `NEW`.
- **Given** a sweep identical to the previous one **When** `publish` is called **Then** it still returns `Some` (values are the same but the observation window moved; `header.version` rises).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/processes.rs`: create

## Tests
- `processes.rs::tests::new_flag_lifecycle`
- `processes.rs::tests::exited_lingers_then_drops`
- `processes.rs::tests::exited_cap_256`
- `processes.rs::tests::linger_clamp`
- `processes.rs::tests::pid_reuse_is_a_new_key`
- `processes.rs::tests::sink_called_once_per_sweep`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: records carry `FieldValidity` from the sweep unchanged; the reducer never turns a missing value into zero.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: the diff is O(n) with hash lookups; `records_sorted` allocates one `Vec` per sweep (about 2,000 × 160 B).
- Privacy: never log `ProcessMeta` text; debug logs carry counts only.

## Notes
`Coverage` and `ProcFlags` are in `tl-model/src/process.rs` (E03-A1). The GPU and PSS enrichment of records is E09-006. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E09: GPU pid mapping and PSS coverage in process records
description:
## Context
Two workers enrich process records after the sweep: the GPU probe reports per-pid samples that the reducer maps to `ProcessKey` through the current table (a pid not in the table is dropped; utilization is never divided among processes), and the `ProcessDetail` worker reports PSS and USS for `detail_keys` only. `ProcessSnapshot.coverage` tells the UI which keys have PSS so others show `WarmingUp`. Sources: ADR-007 (pid mapping), ADR-008 (PSS coverage, "Only measured for visible rows"), PROC-033, PROC-030 (`pss`, `uss` columns), E08-003 (`GpuSample.processes`, `DetailsUpdate::Pss`).

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/processes.rs`:

```rust
impl ProcessState {
    /// pid → key through `live`; sums over devices per pid; sets gpu_util_pct = max over devices of max(sm, enc, dec), gpu_mem_bytes = Σ mem_used; validity Valid, or Unsupported when the device has `supports_process_util == false`.
    pub fn apply_gpu_processes(&mut self, samples: &[GpuProcessSample], device_caps: &FxHashMap<[u8; 16], bool>) -> u32 /* matched */;
    /// For each entry: set pss_bytes, uss_bytes, swap_bytes and the Pss/Uss validity; keys not in `live` are ignored; records the key in `coverage.pss`.
    pub fn apply_pss(&mut self, entries: &[PssEntry]);
    pub fn coverage(&self) -> Coverage;   // pss keys (sorted), gpu_process: bool (any GPU sample this interval)
    pub fn clear_pss_outside(&mut self, keep: &[ProcessKey]);   // when detail_keys shrink, PSS of dropped keys becomes WarmingUp
}
```

A process with GPU support but no sample this interval keeps `gpu_util_pct = 0` with validity `Valid` only when some device reported `supports_process_util == true` (PROC-033: "0%" only then; otherwise `Unsupported`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** two GPU samples for pid 100 on two devices (sm 30 and 60, mem 1 GiB and 2 GiB) and pid 100 live **When** applied **Then** `gpu_util_pct == 60`, `gpu_mem_bytes == 3 GiB`, validity `Valid`, return value 1.
- **Given** a sample for pid 999 not live **When** applied **Then** it is dropped and no record changes.
- **Given** `device_caps` all false **When** applied with no samples **Then** every live record's GPU validity is `Unsupported`.
- **Given** `apply_pss` for key A only **When** `coverage()` is read **Then** `pss` contains A and not B, and B's Pss validity is `WarmingUp`.
- **Given** `clear_pss_outside(&[B])` after A had PSS **When** read **Then** A's Pss validity is back to `WarmingUp` and `coverage.pss` is empty.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/processes.rs`: extend

## Tests
- `processes.rs::tests::gpu_pid_mapping_max_and_sum`
- `processes.rs::tests::gpu_unknown_pid_dropped`
- `processes.rs::tests::gpu_unsupported_without_capability`
- `processes.rs::tests::pss_coverage_tracks_keys`
- `processes.rs::tests::pss_cleared_when_key_leaves_demand`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: `ProcessField::GpuUtil`, `GpuMem`, `Pss`, `Uss` in `FieldValidity` are the only fields this bead writes.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one hash lookup per GPU sample; PSS entries are at most 512 (`detail_keys` cap).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
Depends on E09-005 (same file) and E09-A1 for the apply.rs arms that call these. `GpuProcessSample` is `tl-model::gpu_proto`. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E09: apply.rs dispatch for every EngineMsg and Command
description:
## Context
`apply.rs` is the one `match` over `EngineMsg`: every `SourceUpdate` variant and every `Command` variant has an arm from the start (owner only, up front). At this anchor the P0 arms do the work (health, CPU and system samples into series and devices, process sweeps, table query, reset baselines, control forwarding); later E09 beads replace the bodies of the P1 to P3 arms, which until then only log at `debug`. Sources: ADR-004 (reducer owns everything; `EngineMsg`), ADR-005 (`Command` list, demand and settings paths), ADR-008 (suspend, reset baselines, series period), E08-003, E08-004 (`WorkerControl`), R-119, R-134.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/apply.rs`:

```rust
impl Reducer {
    pub fn apply(&mut self, cx: &Cx, msg: EngineMsg, settings: &EngineSettings);
    fn apply_source(&mut self, cx: &Cx, up: SourceUpdate, settings: &EngineSettings);
    fn apply_command(&mut self, cx: &Cx, cmd: Command);
    fn forward(&mut self, target: SourceId, command: WorkerCommand);   // appends a QueuedCommand (seq += 1, keep newest 64) and sends the watch
    fn bump_reset_generation(&mut self);
}
```

Arm table (P0 bodies):
- `Health { id, state, last_error, t_ns }` → `health.apply`; `Disabled`/`Failed` also sets the component header validity of that source's component to `Failed`; `Unsupported` sets it to `Unsupported` (R-155 item 4).
- `Cpu(s)` → series `CPU_TOTAL`, `CPU_KERNEL`, `CPU_FREQ`, `CPU_TEMP` on the `CpuPackage` device and `CPU_TOTAL`, `CPU_KERNEL`, `CPU_FREQ` per `CpuLogical` (period from the sample spacing or `settings`; a `WarmingUp` sample appends a gap); `topology: Some` → `devices.set_cpus` and `system.cpu_topology`; `irq_pct` stored for the Interrupts row (E09-023); `system` component replaced; `health.sample_ok`.
- `Memory(s)` → `MEM_USED`, `MEM_COMMIT`, `SWAP_USED`, `MEM_CACHED` on the `Memory` device; zram stats stored (E09-023); `system` replaced; the running maximum of `committed` (`Committed_AS`) since engine start is kept and written to `inventory.memory.peak_committed_bytes` (R-166, E12-OI-8).
- `Disks(s)`, `Nets(s)`, `Sensors(s)` → `devices.ensure` per identity, then `DISK_ACTIVE`, `DISK_READ`, `DISK_WRITE`, `DISK_LATENCY`; `NET_RX`, `NET_TX`; `FAN_RPM`, `SENSOR_TEMP` per device; a device with `present == false` gets `Missing` (gap). `system` totals replaced. `BATTERY_PCT` is appended in the `DeviceDetails::Batteries` arm instead (R-139 item 7).
- Aggregate devices (R-154 item 1): the three `DeviceIdentity::Aggregate` devices are created at session start with `present = true`. In the `Disks` arm, `Aggregate(Disks)` gets `DISK_ACTIVE` = max over present physical disks (no partitions, no device-mapper children) and `DISK_READ`, `DISK_WRITE` = sums. In the `Nets` arm, `Aggregate(Nets)` gets `NET_RX`, `NET_TX` = sums over interfaces whose `NetKind` is shown under `settings.show_network_{wired,wireless,vpn,virtual,other}`. In the `Gpu` arm, `Aggregate(Gpus)` gets `GPU_UTIL` = max and `GPU_MEM` = sum.
- `Devices(list)` → `devices.apply_list`; `Returned` devices get `mark_gap` on their series.
- `Gpu(s)` → `GPU_UTIL`, `GPU_MEM`, `GPU_ENC`, `GPU_DEC`, `GPU_TEMP`, `GPU_POWER`, `GPU_CLOCK` per GPU device; `processes: Some` → `processes.apply_gpu_processes` (E09-006, P1 arm). `GpuInfo` → display names and caps; `GpuApiVersions` → inventory fields (E09-027).
- `Processes(sweep)` → `processes.apply_sweep` with the sink (it also moves `sweep.extras`, `extras_p2`, `app_stats` into `ProcessSnapshot.extras`, `.extras_p2`, `.apps` and `sweep.low_memory` into `.low_memory`, R-141, R-150, R-163), then `table::rebuild` (E09-009..) with `self.query` and `settings`; marks `PROCESSES` and `TABLE`.
- `DeviceDetails(d)` (R-139 item 7) → keeps one record per device and merges by field: `Cpu` and `Memory` replace `device_details.cpu` and `.memory`; `Disks { from, entries }` and `Nets { from, entries }`: a sysfs source (`Disk`, `Net`) fills every field it knows, a D-Bus source (`Udisks`, `NetworkManager`) overwrites `model`, `wwn`, `serial`, `rotation_rpm`, `smart`, `smart_data`, `smart_temp_c`, `ejectable`, `can_power_off`, `eject` (disks) and `kind`, `type_label`, `connection`, `wifi` (interfaces; a NetworkManager record with `wifi: None` keeps nothing from it); a full list replaces that source's contribution for every device, and a device missing from the list loses that source's fields; `Batteries(list)` replaces the battery records and appends `BATTERY_PCT` from `percentage` per battery. Identities map to `DeviceIdx` with `devices.ensure`; `Blocker.app` is filled from the process grouping. Marks `DEVICE_DETAILS`.
- `Helper(u)` and `Setup(s)` (R-150 items 1 and 4) → arms written up front that log at `debug` and return; E29-020 (qfx.23) fills them as its named chain edit (set `health.helper`, `health.helper_start`, `health.setup`, mark `HEALTH`).
- `ColorScheme(v)` → `system.color_scheme = v`; marks `SYSTEM` (R-170 item 4).
- `Details(..)` → E09-006 (`Pss`) and E09-026 (`Tab`, `Affinity`, `HandleSearch`).
- `Connections`, `ConnectionsDestroySupport`, `Services`, `Startup`, `Inventory`, `Windows` → E09-027. `History` → E09-028.
- `Sleep { entering }`, `ResumeDetected` → `suspend` (E09-008; at P0 the arm records the flag and calls `series.mark_gap_all()` on resume plus `bump_reset_generation()`).
- `Command::SetTableQuery(q)` → store, rebuild the table, mark `TABLE` (even when rows are equal, `query_generation` must echo). `SetSysTableQuery(q)` → store in `sys_queries[table]` and rebuild that table (E09-027).
- `Command::Action(req)` → `action_gate.submit(..)` with `AdmissionView`; no gate → one `ActionEvent { id, target: None, state: Rejected(Unsupported) }` through `events_tx.try_send`.
- `RefreshNow(id)` → `forward(id, RefreshNow)`; `ResetBaselines` → `bump_reset_generation` and `series.mark_gap_all`; `ReprobeSource(id)` → `forward(id, Reprobe)`; `KWin(c)` → `forward(KWin, KWin(c))`; `DetailRefresh`, `ComputeHashes`, `VerifyPackage`, `StringScan`, `CancelStringScan`, `HandleSearch`, `CancelHandleSearch` → `forward(ProcessDetail, ..)`; `HistoryQuery`, `HistoryDelete` → `forward(HistoryRecorder, ..)`; `SetupStatus` → `self.helper_tx` with `HelperCommand::SetupStatus`, `RunSetup { step }` → `HelperCommand::RunSetup(step)`, both via `try_send` like `Start` and `End` (R-247; `None` or a full queue logs at `debug` and drops the command); `Device(DeviceCommand::SmartRead | SmartReadAdmin | Eject)` → `forward(Udisks, WorkerCommand::Device(cmd))`, `Device(FetchPublicIp)` → `forward(Inventory, ..)`, `Device(BatteryHistory)` → `forward(UPower, ..)` (R-139 item 3); `StartHelperSession` and `EndHelperSession` → `self.helper_tx` with `HelperCommand::Start` or `End` via `try_send`; `None` logs at `debug` and drops the command (R-148 item 1).
- `ActionFinished { id }` → `action_gate.finished(id)` → `forward(source, RefreshNow)` when `Some`.
- `Tick` → `health.tick`, `series.mark_stale`, `processes.expire`; marks `HEALTH`, `SERIES`, `PROCESSES` and `TABLE` when anything changed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `Cpu` samples at 100 ms with `totals.cpu_pct = 50` **When** applied **Then** `CPU_TOTAL` on `CpuPackage` has one new sample per update with value 50 and the `SeriesSet` version rose once per update.
- **Given** a `Disks` sample for an identity not in the catalog **When** applied **Then** the device is added and its `DISK_READ` series exists.
- **Given** `Command::SetTableQuery` with `generation = 7` and unchanged rows **When** applied **Then** the published `table.query_generation == 7` and `TABLE` was marked.
- **Given** `Command::RefreshNow(SourceId::Startup)` **When** applied **Then** the control watch holds a `QueuedCommand { target: Startup, command: RefreshNow }` with `seq` one higher than before.
- **Given** 70 forwarded commands **When** read **Then** the queue holds the newest 64 in ascending `seq`.
- **Given** `Command::Action` with no gate **When** applied **Then** one `Rejected(Unsupported)` event with `target: None` is on `events_tx`.
- **Given** `ResumeDetected` **When** applied **Then** `reset_generation` rose by 1 and the next sample of every series carries `GAP_BEFORE`.
- **Given** a message of every `SourceUpdate` variant and every `Command` variant **When** applied at this anchor **Then** nothing panics (P1 to P3 arms log and return).
- **Given** `Disks` samples for two present disks with `active_pct` 30 and 70 and read rates 1 MB/s and 2 MB/s **When** applied **Then** `Aggregate(Disks)` has `DISK_ACTIVE` 70 and `DISK_READ` 3,000,000 (R-154 item 1).
- **Given** `Nets` samples for `eno1` (Wired) and `docker0` (Virtual) with `show_network_virtual = false` **When** applied **Then** `Aggregate(Nets)` `NET_RX` equals `eno1`'s value only.
- **Given** `DeviceDetails(Batteries([bat0 with percentage 81]))` **When** applied **Then** the `BATTERY_PCT` series of `bat0` gets 81 and `DEVICE_DETAILS` is marked (R-139 item 7).
- **Given** a `Disks { from: Udisks }` record with `model "X"` and then a `Disks { from: Disk }` record with `model "Y"` for the same disk **When** both are applied **Then** `model` is "X" (the D-Bus source owns it) and the sysfs-only fields come from the `Disk` record.
- **Given** `Command::Device(DeviceCommand::FetchPublicIp)` **When** applied **Then** the control watch holds a `QueuedCommand { target: Inventory, command: Device(FetchPublicIp) }` (R-139 item 3).
- **Given** `Command::StartHelperSession` with `helper_tx == None` **When** applied **Then** nothing is sent and nothing panics (R-148 item 1).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/apply.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_reducer.rs`: add the cases

## Tests
- `lab_reducer.rs::cpu_update_appends_series`
- `lab_reducer.rs::unknown_disk_identity_is_added`
- `lab_reducer.rs::set_table_query_echoes_generation`
- `lab_reducer.rs::refresh_now_is_forwarded`
- `lab_reducer.rs::forward_queue_keeps_newest_64`
- `lab_reducer.rs::action_without_gate_is_rejected_unsupported`
- `lab_reducer.rs::resume_bumps_reset_and_gaps`
- `lab_reducer.rs::every_variant_applies_without_panic`
- `lab_reducer.rs::aggregate_disk_max_and_sum`, `aggregate_net_respects_visibility`
- `lab_reducer.rs::battery_details_append_battery_pct`, `disk_details_merge_by_source`
- `lab_reducer.rs::device_commands_forward_to_owner`, `helper_session_without_tx_is_dropped`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: an unknown `DeviceIdx` or a series append on a missing device is an `InvariantViolation`.
- Validity: a sample whose validity is not `Valid` becomes a gap sample; `Stale` is added on `Tick`.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: no allocation per sample beyond the ring append; the table rebuild is the expensive step and runs only on sweep or query change.
- Privacy: forwarded `StringScan` and `HandleSearch` patterns are never logged.

## Notes
Depends on E09-001 to E09-005. The period passed to `series.append` is `settings.interval_ms` for process-derived series and the spacing of the last two samples for system series (first sample uses the worker's nominal period: 100 ms when `cpu_fast`, else 1 s). Large-file rule: commit before building. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E28-A1 Startup Apps page
description:
## Context
Anchor E28-A1 (tasklens-9o0.1): the Startup Apps tab is complete and mounted. This bead adds the Startup Apps page to `MainWindow` (chain edit of E20's `window/main.rs`) and the end-to-end tests that drive the whole tab, its menu, flows, delete dialog and Properties window through the fake engine. Other epics that need "the Startup Apps page" depend on this bead. Sources: UI-SYS-040 to UI-SYS-050, SYS-019 to SYS-027, R-023 (tab 4), ADR-009 (page match, pages created on first visit and kept), table (b).

## Deliverable

title: Startup Apps: delete confirmation window and delete flow
description:
## Context
"Delete entry…" on the Startup Apps tab opens a modal confirmation window and, on "Delete", sends `ActionKind::StartupDelete`. Only entries the user owns can be deleted (user XDG entries, user systemd units not owned by a package, Plasma scripts). Sources: UI-SYS-047, UI-SYS-044, UI-SYS-007, SYS-024, APP-045, UI-FND-021 (`TlDialog::confirm`, focus on Cancel for destructive actions), ADR-005, R-119.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/windows/confirm_startup_delete.rs`:
- `pub fn open_startup_delete(parent: WindowHandle<..>, entries: SmallVec<[StartupEntryView; 4]>, skipped: usize, on_delete: impl Fn(&mut Window, &mut App) + 'static, cx: &mut App) -> WindowHandle<..>` where `StartupEntryView { name: SharedString, source_path: SharedString, kind: StartupKind }` holds only the deletable entries.
- `TlDialog::confirm` window, modal to the main window, title "tasklens Delete Startup Entry", width 440, height fits content. Icon `triangle-alert` 20 px in `status.warning`.
- One entry: heading "Delete startup entry" (`t_md` semibold); text "Permanently remove this startup entry?" (`t_base`); type line (`t_base` `text_secondary`): user XDG entry "The autostart file will be deleted. The app stays installed."; user systemd unit "The unit will be disabled and its unit file deleted."; Plasma pre-startup or logout script "The script file will be deleted."; then the entry name (`t_base` medium); then the source path (`t_sm` `text_secondary`, selectable).
- Several entries: heading "Delete startup entries"; text "Permanently remove these <n> startup entries?"; then up to 5 names (`t_base` medium), then "and <m> more" when there are more than 5; when `skipped > 0` a line "<skipped> entries cannot be deleted and are skipped." (`t_base` `text_secondary`). No type line and no paths in this form.
- Footer: "Cancel" (`TlButton::Secondary`) then "Delete" (`TlButton::Danger`). Focus starts on "Cancel". Enter triggers the focused button; Esc cancels.
- While deleting: both buttons disabled, "Delete" shows a 14 px `TlSpinner` (static under reduced motion). The window closes when the request's final event arrives.

`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/startup/flows.rs`: `StartupDelete` handler:
- Targets from `menu_targets` or the selection; keep those with `can_delete`; `skipped` = the rest. No deletable target: Warning toast "This startup entry cannot be deleted" (E28-012 (tasklens-9o0.8) rule), no window.
- Opens the dialog; on "Delete" submits `SysActions::submit(ActionKind::StartupDelete, ActionKindTag::StartupDelete, targets, texts)` with: pending none (open item B8-E28-10), done_one "Startup entry deleted.", done_many "{ $n } startup entries deleted", partial_many "{ $ok } of { $n } startup entries deleted. { $failed } failed.", failed_prefix "Failed to delete startup entry", unknown "Outcome unknown", busy "A startup action is already in progress.", no failed button, progress_cap true. The app stays installed.", "Discord" and the path, and focus is on "Cancel".

- **Given** the dialog **When** Tab then Enter **Then** a `StartupDelete` request is sent, both buttons are disabled and "Delete" shows the spinner; on `Succeeded` the window closes and "Startup entry deleted." shows in the main window.
- **Given** a user systemd unit **When** the dialog opens **Then** the type line is "The unit will be disabled and its unit file deleted.".
- **Given** 7 entries selected, 2 of them system entries **When** Delete entry… is chosen **Then** the heading is "Delete startup entries", the text "Permanently remove these 5 startup entries?", five names, no "and … more" line, and "2 entries cannot be deleted and are skipped.".

title: Startup Apps: copy commands and Open file location
description:
## Context
Copy commands and "Open file location" for the Startup Apps tab: the "Copy row" text block, "Copy rows as table", "Copy" (cell), "Copy command", and showing the entry's source file in the file manager. The shared mechanics are E27's `sys_copy.rs`; this bead supplies the startup source and the two startup-only commands. Sources: UI-SYS-048, UI-SYS-006, UI-SYS-044, SYS-025, R-012, R-134 (`ActionKind::ShowInFileManager`), APP-044, ADR-015 (exports).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/startup/copy.rs` (new; `mod copy;` in `mod.rs`):
- `impl SysCopySource for StartupPage` with `RowId = StartupRef`:
  - `copy_rows`: selected refs in view order.
  - `write_block`, exactly these eight lines (no trailing newline):
    ```
    Name: <name>
    Publisher: <publisher>
    Status: <status label>
    Startup impact: <impact word>
    Type: <type words>
    Location: <full directory path>
    Command: <command>
    Resolved path: <absolute binary path, or "Not found">
    ```
    Location prints the full path (no `~`), so the copy works in a shell. Empty publisher prints "Publisher: " with nothing after the space.
  - `visible_columns` and `write_cell`: the cell text as shown (Location with `~`), validity glyph cells empty.
  - `copy_texts`: `row_ok` "Copied to clipboard", `row_failed` "Failed to copy to clipboard", `nothing_selected` "Select a startup row first.".
- Handlers on `StartupPage`: `CopyCell { col }` → `copy_cell` with the cell captured at menu open; `CopyDetails` (Ctrl+C) → `copy_row`; `CopyRowsAsTable` (Ctrl+Shift+C) → `copy_rows_as_table`.
- `StartupCopyCommand` (one target): writes the Command value to the clipboard; Success toast "Startup command copied.".
- `StartupOpenFileLocation` (one target): when the entry's source file no longer exists (entry `file_exists == false`), Warning toast "Startup file location unavailable." and nothing is sent. Otherwise submit `ActionRequest { kind: ActionKind::ShowInFileManager { path: source_path, properties: false }, targets: [] }` through `ActionTracker` (E16-A3); Info toast "Opening file location" with `ToastKey(id.0)`; on `Failed` or `OutcomeUnknown` the same key becomes the Error toast "Failed to open file location".

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the entry fixture "Discord" **When** `CopyDetails` runs **Then** the clipboard equals the golden `tests/golden/startup_copy_block.txt` and the toast is "Copied to clipboard".
- **Given** two selected entries **When** `CopyDetails` runs **Then** the two blocks are joined by one blank line in view order.
- **Given** nothing selected **When** Ctrl+C is pressed **Then** the toast "Select a startup row first." shows and the clipboard is unchanged.
- **Given** a location under $HOME **When** copied as a block **Then** the Location line has the full path; **When** copied as a table **Then** the Location cell has `~`.
- **Given** one entry **When** "Copy command" runs **Then** the clipboard holds its command and the toast is "Startup command copied.".
- **Given** an entry whose source file is gone **When** "Open file location" runs **Then** the toast "Startup file location unavailable." shows and no request is sent.
- **Given** an existing file **When** "Open file location" runs and the engine answers `Failed` **Then** the toast changes in place from "Opening file location" to "Failed to open file location".

- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/startup/mod.rs`: change (`mod copy;`, handler registration)
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_startup.rs`: add tests; `crates/tl-ui/tests/golden/startup_copy_block.txt`: create

title: Startup Apps: Startup Properties window
description:
## Context
The read-only Startup Properties window, opened by Properties (Enter, Alt+Enter, Ctrl+I, double-click) on a startup row. One window per entry, at most 10, each line with its own copy button. Sources: UI-SYS-050, SYS-026, APP-045, UI-FND-021 (`TlSecondaryWindow`, `WindowRegistry`, `WindowKey::StartupProperties(StartupRef)`), UI-FND-025, docs/ui/INDEX.md window keys.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/windows/startup_properties.rs`:
- `pub fn open_startup_properties(r: StartupRef, hub: &Entity<SnapshotHub>, cx: &mut App)`: if `WindowRegistry` holds `WindowKey::StartupProperties(r)`, activate that window; else if 10 startup properties windows are open, push the Warning toast "Too many startup properties windows are already open" in the main window and open nothing; else open a `TlSecondaryWindow` (Properties kind, not modal) titled "Startup properties: <Name>", default size 620 × 520, minimum 480 × 360.
- `StartupPropertiesView` (Entity): subscribes to `SnapshotHub`; on STARTUP changes it looks up its entry by `StartupRef` and notifies only when the entry `Arc` differs by pointer. Content: `TlKeyValueGrid` inline layout in a vertical scroll region, padding `sp6`, `.label_width(220)`; each line ends with a copy button (`TlButton::Icon`, icon `copy` 14 px in a 20 × 20 hit area at the line's right end, `text_secondary` at 60% alpha, full alpha on row hover or focus; accessible name "Copy <label>"). Footer 48 px high with one `TlButton::Secondary` "Close".
- Lines, in order (labels exact):

  | Label | Value |
  |---|---|
  | "Name" | name |
  | "Publisher" | publisher, or "Not reported" (Unsupported-no-value word) |
  | "Status / Enabled / State code" | "<status label> / <Yes or No> / <ActiveState (SubState)>", for example "Enabled / Yes / active (running)"; State code "-" when there is no generated unit |
  | "Startup impact" | "<High, Medium or Low> (<activation_ms> ms)", for example "Low (212 ms)"; "None" and "Not measured" without ms |
  | "Type / Source / Scope" | "<type words> / <source word> / <user or system>", for example "Autostart (user) / XDG autostart / user"; source words "XDG autostart", "systemd user unit", "Plasma pre-startup script", "Plasma logout script" |
  | "Location" | directory (full path) |
  | "Source path" | file path |
  | "Resolved path" | binary found on PATH, or "Not found" |
  | "Command" | command; wraps to several lines |
  | "Can run / Can toggle / Can delete / File exists" | four "Yes"/"No" words joined with " / ", for example "Yes / Yes / No / Yes" |
  | "OnlyShowIn" | list joined with ", "; line shown only when set |
  | "NotShowIn" | list; only when set |
  | "TryExec" | value; only when set |
  | "Autostart phase" | `X-KDE-autostart-phase` value; only when set |
  | "Generated unit" | unit name; only for desktop entries |
  | "Overrides" | the system path; only when a user file shadows one |

- Entry removed from the snapshot: the title becomes "Startup properties: <Name> (removed)" and every value is drawn in `text_secondary`; values keep their last text.
- Interaction: a copy button copies that line's value with the toast "Copied to clipboard" (in this window's own toast stack); Ctrl+C with a line focused copies its value; Esc and "Close" close the window; Ctrl+W closes.
- `StartupPage` handles `OpenProperties` for its selection: opens one window per selected entry (focused entry first), each through `open_startup_properties`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the fixture entry "Discord" **When** Properties opens **Then** the window title is "Startup properties: Discord" and the lines equal the golden `tests/golden/startup_props_lines.txt` (label, tab, value per line).
- **Given** an entry without OnlyShowIn, NotShowIn, TryExec, phase and override **When** opened **Then** those five lines are absent.
- **Given** an open window **When** a snapshot without the entry arrives **Then** the title ends with " (removed)" and the values are `text_secondary`.
- **Given** 10 open startup properties windows **When** an 11th is requested **Then** the toast "Too many startup properties windows are already open" shows and no window opens.
- **Given** a window open for entry A **When** Properties is chosen for A again **Then** the existing window is activated and the window count does not change.
- **Given** the Command line's copy button **When** clicked **Then** the clipboard holds the command and the toast is "Copied to clipboard".
- **Given** a snapshot that changes another entry only **When** installed **Then** the window's render count does not change.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/startup_properties.rs`: change (fill the stub)
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/startup/mod.rs`: change (`OpenProperties` handler)
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_startup.rs`: add tests; `crates/tl-ui/tests/golden/startup_props_lines.txt`: create
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append `startup-props-*` keys

## Tests
- `ui_startup::startup_props_lines_golden`.
- `ui_startup::startup_props_optional_lines_only_when_set`.
- `ui_startup::startup_props_removed_title`.
- `ui_startup::startup_props_cap`.
- `ui_startup::startup_props_same_entry_focuses`.
- `ui_startup::startup_props_copy_line`.
- `ui_startup::startup_props_rerender_only_on_own_entry`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: "Too many startup properties windows are already open".
- Validity: "Not reported" for a missing publisher; other missing values use the PERF-013 words.
- Accessibility: copy buttons are Tab stops named "Copy <label>"; Esc closes; Ctrl+C copies the focused line.
- Performance: re-renders only when its own entry changes (pointer compare); static otherwise.
