title: E03-068 wire.rs: length-prefixed postcard framing with limits
description:
## Context
Fills `tl-model/src/wire.rs`: the length-prefixed postcard framing shared by the GPU probe channel (ADR-007) and the P3 helper's stdin and stdout (ADR-006), with its frame limits and the multi-frame reply reader. A wrong length, a short read or a postcard error is a protocol failure, and the reader must never allocate more than the limit. Sources: ADR-007 "Framing", ADR-006 "Privileged helper boundary" (64 KiB frames, 4 MiB per request), R-003.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-model/src/wire.rs` (placeholder from E03-001):

```rust
/// frame = u32 little-endian payload length | payload (postcard)
pub const MAX_PROBE_FRAME: usize = 1_048_576;        // 1 MiB
pub const MAX_HELPER_FRAME: usize = 65_536;          // 64 KiB
pub const MAX_HELPER_REPLY_TOTAL: usize = 4_194_304; // 4 MiB per request, summed over frames

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum WireError {
    #[error("frame of {len} bytes exceeds the limit of {max}")] TooLarge { len: usize, max: usize },
    #[error("reply of {total} bytes exceeds the limit of {max}")] ReplyTooLarge { total: usize, max: usize },
    #[error("truncated frame")] Truncated,           // EOF inside the length prefix or the payload
    #[error("end of stream")] Eof,                   // clean EOF before the first byte of a frame
    #[error("decode error: {0}")] Decode(postcard::Error),
    #[error("encode error: {0}")] Encode(postcard::Error),
    #[error("i/o error: {0}")] Io(std::io::Error),
}

pub fn encode_frame<T: Serialize>(msg: &T, max: usize, out: &mut Vec<u8>) -> Result<(), WireError>; // appends prefix + payload
pub fn write_frame<W: std::io::Write, T: Serialize>(w: &mut W, msg: &T, max: usize) -> Result<(), WireError>;
pub fn read_frame<R: std::io::Read, T: DeserializeOwned>(r: &mut R, max: usize) -> Result<T, WireError>;
/// Reads frames until `is_last(&msg)` is true. Fails with ReplyTooLarge when the summed payload
/// bytes pass `max_total`, checked before reading each payload.
pub fn read_reply<R: std::io::Read, T: DeserializeOwned>(
    r: &mut R, max_frame: usize, max_total: usize, is_last: impl Fn(&T) -> bool,
) -> Result<Vec<T>, WireError>;
```

Rules: the length is checked against `max` before any payload allocation; a length of 0 is a valid empty payload only if postcard accepts it for `T`; `write_frame` refuses to send a payload over `max` (`TooLarge`) without writing anything; `EINTR` is retried by `read_exact` semantics; `Eof` is returned only when the stream ends before the first prefix byte. Blocking `std::io` only; callers run it on a blocking thread.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a message whose postcard payload is exactly `MAX_HELPER_FRAME` bytes **When** written then read with `max = MAX_HELPER_FRAME` **Then** it round-trips.
- **Given** a stream whose prefix says `MAX_HELPER_FRAME + 1` **When** `read_frame` runs with the helper max **Then** it returns `TooLarge` and reads no payload bytes (the reader's position is 4).
- **Given** a prefix of 10 followed by 6 bytes then EOF **When** `read_frame` runs **Then** it returns `Truncated`.
- **Given** 2 bytes of prefix then EOF **When** `read_frame` runs **Then** it returns `Truncated`; an empty stream returns `Eof`.
- **Given** a valid prefix with bytes that are not a valid postcard `T` **When** `read_frame` runs **Then** it returns `Decode`.
- **Given** a message larger than `max` **When** `write_frame` runs **Then** it returns `TooLarge` and the writer is empty.
- **Given** five frames of 1 MiB each where only the fifth is last **When** `read_reply` runs with `max_frame = MAX_PROBE_FRAME` and `max_total = MAX_HELPER_REPLY_TOTAL` **Then** it returns `ReplyTooLarge` on the fifth frame.
- **Given** three frames with the third marked last **When** `read_reply` runs **Then** it returns the three messages in order.

## Files
- `crates/tl-model/src/wire.rs`: constants, `WireError`, the four functions.
- `crates/tl-model/tests/wire_framing.rs`: integration tests below, plus a proptest.

## Tests
- `tests/wire_framing.rs::max_size_roundtrip`, `oversize_prefix_rejected_without_alloc`, `truncated_payload`, `truncated_prefix_and_clean_eof`, `bad_postcard_is_decode_error`, `write_refuses_oversize`, `reply_total_cap`, `reply_reads_until_last`.
- `tests/wire_framing.rs::prop_roundtrip_bytes` (proptest, dev-dependency `proptest` from the workspace pins): any `Vec<u8>` up to 4096 bytes wrapped in a test struct round-trips; any random byte stream fed to `read_frame::<TestMsg>` with max 4096 returns `Ok` or an error and never panics.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the `WireError` variants above; the engine maps any of them to a protocol failure (probe killed and restarted, helper session ended).
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one allocation per frame of exactly the payload size; no allocation before the length check.
- Privacy: payloads are never logged; `WireError` messages carry sizes only.
- Security: this parser reads input from a separate process (probe) and from a root process (helper); the length check before allocation is the regression guard. The `oversize_prefix_rejected_without_alloc` test is the security regression test.

## Notes
- `thiserror` and `postcard` are in tl-model's allowed row (ADR-001). Add `proptest = { workspace = true }` under `[dev-dependencies]` in `crates/tl-model/Cargo.toml` (this crate's own manifest, owned by E03).
- Depends on E03-A1 (crate skeleton and lib.rs module list).
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-model`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
close_reason: wire.rs framing, limits, WireError, read_reply; tests/wire_framing.rs with 8 named tests and 2 proptests. Commits c4820b9, df43a4e

title: E03-069 gpu_proto.rs: GPU probe messages
description:
## Context
Fills `tl-model/src/gpu_proto.rs`: the messages between the engine and the `tl-gpu-probe` child (ADR-007), including the one-shot `--api-versions` output. NVML runs only in the probe, so a crash there cannot take down the app; these types are the whole contract. Sources: ADR-007 "Messages", "API versions mode", R-026, R-087.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-model/src/gpu_proto.rs` (placeholder from E03-001). Every type derives `Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize` (owned `String` and `Vec`, no `Arc`):

```rust
pub const GPU_PROTO_VERSION: u16 = 1;

pub enum ProbeRequest { Hello { proto: u16 }, Sample { seq: u32, processes: bool }, Shutdown }

pub enum ProbeResponse {
    Hello { proto: u16, driver: String, nvml: String, devices: Vec<GpuDeviceInfo> },
    InitFailed { kind: InitFailure, message: String },
    Sample { seq: u32, t_ns: u64, devices: Vec<GpuDeviceSample>, processes: Option<Vec<GpuProcessSample>> },
}

pub enum InitFailure { LibraryNotFound, DriverNotLoaded, NoPermission, Other }   // also Copy, Eq

pub struct GpuDeviceInfo { pub uuid: [u8; 16], pub name: String, pub pci_bus_id: String,
                           pub mem_total: u64, pub power_limit_mw: Option<u32>,
                           pub cuda_version: Option<String>, pub vbios: Option<String>,
                           pub architecture: Option<String> }   // last three: R-156 item 1

pub enum Reading<T> { Ok(T), Unsupported, Failed }   // never encode missing as zero; Copy when T: Copy

pub struct GpuDeviceSample {
    pub uuid: [u8; 16],
    pub util_pct: Reading<u32>, pub mem_util_pct: Reading<u32>,
    pub mem_used: Reading<u64>,
    pub enc_pct: Reading<u32>, pub dec_pct: Reading<u32>,
    pub temp_c: Reading<u32>, pub power_mw: Reading<u32>,
    pub clock_gfx_mhz: Reading<u32>, pub clock_mem_mhz: Reading<u32>,
    pub fan_pct: Reading<u32>,
    pub pcie_rx_kbps: Reading<u32>, pub pcie_tx_kbps: Reading<u32>,
}

pub struct GpuProcessSample {
    pub uuid: [u8; 16], pub pid: u32,
    pub sm_pct: Reading<u32>, pub mem_pct: Reading<u32>,
    pub enc_pct: Reading<u32>, pub dec_pct: Reading<u32>,
    pub mem_used: Reading<u64>,
}

// --api-versions one-shot mode: one frame on stdout, then exit 0
pub struct ApiVersions { pub devices: Vec<GpuApiVersions> }
pub struct GpuApiVersions {
    pub pci_bus_id: String,              // key, matched by VK_EXT_pci_bus_info / EGL device
    pub vulkan_api: Option<String>,      // "1.4.312"
    pub vulkan_driver: Option<String>,   // driver properties driverInfo
    pub opengl: Option<String>,          // GL_VERSION string
}

impl<T> Reading<T> { pub fn ok(self) -> Option<T>; pub fn validity(&self) -> Validity; } // Ok -> Valid, Unsupported -> Unsupported, Failed -> Failed
```

Frames use `wire.rs` with `MAX_PROBE_FRAME` (1 MiB). Deadlines (Hello 3000 ms, Sample 500 ms) belong to the engine client (E13), not here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `Reading::<u32>::Unsupported` **When** `validity()` is called **Then** it returns `Validity::Unsupported`; `Ok(5).ok()` is `Some(5)`; `Failed.validity()` is `Validity::Failed`.
- **Given** a `ProbeResponse::Sample` with two devices and `processes: Some` of three entries **When** encoded with `wire::encode_frame` and read back with `wire::read_frame` **Then** it equals the original.
- **Given** `GPU_PROTO_VERSION` **When** read **Then** it is 1.
- **Given** a `Sample` with 16 devices and 4,096 processes **When** encoded **Then** the payload is under `MAX_PROBE_FRAME` (proves the limit fits a large machine).

## Files
- `crates/tl-model/src/gpu_proto.rs`: the types above.

## Tests
- `gpu_proto.rs` unit tests: `reading_validity_and_ok`, `proto_version_one`, `large_sample_fits_probe_frame`.
- Round trips of every message are in `tests/proto_roundtrip.rs` (E03-070).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `InitFailed` kinds map to the ADR-007 failure table in the engine.
- Validity: `Reading<T>` maps to `Validity` as above; missing is never zero.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: about 2 KB per second at 1 Hz.
- Privacy: N/A.
- Security: the engine treats every probe message as untrusted input; sizes are bounded by the frame limit.

## Notes
- All message types are copied from ADR-007. `GpuApiVersions { pci_bus_id, vulkan_api, vulkan_driver, opengl }` is accepted (R-156 item 1). `GpuDeviceInfo` gains `cuda_version`, `vbios` and `architecture: Option<String>` (R-156 item 1, B3 item 12); the probe fills them from NVML when the call succeeds, else `None`.
- Depends on E03-068 (`wire.rs` for the tests) and E03-A1 (`Validity`).
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-model`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E03-070 helper_proto.rs: helper allowlist, replies and protocol round trips
description:
## Context
Fills `tl-model/src/helper_proto.rs`: the request allowlist of the P3 privileged helper `tl-helper` and its replies, framed with `wire.rs` over the helper's stdin and stdout (64 KiB frames, at most 4 MiB per request). The request set is the security boundary: no path, command or free-form file argument may appear in it. Also adds `tests/proto_roundtrip.rs`, which round-trips every serializable message of the crate (probe, helper, action types). Sources: ADR-006 "Privileged helper boundary", R-002, R-003, R-004, R-097, R-098, SYS-013, SYS-031, SYS-037, PROC-076, PROC-084, PROC-096.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-model/src/helper_proto.rs` (placeholder from E03-001). Every type derives `Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize`; owned `String`/`Vec` only.

```rust
pub const HELPER_PROTO_VERSION: u16 = 1;

pub enum HelperTarget { Process(ProcessKey), Thread { process: ProcessKey, tid: u32 } }

bitflags! { #[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct ProcFiles: u16 {   // the ReadProcessFiles set (R-004, R-098)
    const IO = 1 << 0; const FD_LIST = 1 << 1; const FDINFO = 1 << 2; const ENVIRON = 1 << 3;
    const MAPS = 1 << 4; const SMAPS = 1 << 5; const SMAPS_ROLLUP = 1 << 6; const NS = 1 << 7;
    const CWD = 1 << 8; const EXE = 1 << 9; const STATUS = 1 << 10;
    const ROOT = 1 << 11;   // /proc/<pid>/root for PROC-078 and PROC-096 (R-157)
}}

pub enum DropInKey {   // keys limited to Restart*, StartLimit*, FailureAction, OnFailure
    Restart, RestartSec, RestartSteps, RestartMaxDelaySec,
    StartLimitBurst, StartLimitIntervalSec, StartLimitAction, FailureAction, OnFailure,
}

pub struct HelperCgroup { pub rel_path: String, pub cgroup_id: u64 } // any uid's cgroup under /sys/fs/cgroup

pub enum HelperRequest {
    Hello { proto: u16 },
    Signal { target: HelperTarget, signal: Signal },
    SetNice { target: HelperTarget, nice: i8 },
    SetSched { target: HelperTarget, policy: SchedPolicy, rt_prio: u8 },
    SetAffinity { target: HelperTarget, set: CpuSet },
    SetIoPriority { key: ProcessKey, prio: IoPriority },
    FreezeGroup(HelperCgroup), ThawGroup(HelperCgroup), KillGroup(HelperCgroup),
    ReadProcessFiles { key: ProcessKey, files: ProcFiles },
    ScanStrings { key: ProcessKey, opts: StringScanOpts },        // streams batches
    Dump { key: ProcessKey, mode: DumpMode },                     // output fd travels as SCM_RIGHTS with this frame (R-145)
    ResolveSocketInodes { inodes: Vec<u64> },
    SockDestroy { family: Family, proto: Proto, four_tuple: FourTuple, cookie: u64 },
    WriteServiceDropIn { unit: String, keys: Vec<(DropInKey, String)> }, // manager is always System; empty keys deletes the file
    NetnsSockDiagDump { netns_ino: u64 },
    CancelScan { seq: u32 },   // stops the ScanStrings stream with that frame seq (R-157)
}

pub struct HelperFrame { pub seq: u32, pub request: HelperRequest }   // engine -> helper

pub enum HelperError { IdentityChanged, PermissionDenied, NoSuchProcess, NotAllowed, Partial { done: u16, total: u16 }, Os(i32),
                       TooLarge }   // reply over the 4 MiB cap (R-157)

pub enum HelperReplyBody {
    Hello { proto: u16 },
    Ok,
    Err(HelperError),
    File { file: ProcFiles /* exactly one bit */, data: Vec<u8> },   // raw file content, chunked
    Strings(Vec<(u64 /*address*/, StringEncoding, String)>),
    SocketOwners(Vec<(u64 /*inode*/, ProcessKey)>),
    NetlinkDump(Vec<u8>),                                             // raw sock_diag messages
}

pub struct HelperReply { pub seq: u32, pub last: bool, pub body: HelperReplyBody } // helper -> engine

/// WriteServiceDropIn validation: unit name is non-empty, at most 255 bytes, contains no '/',
/// no NUL and no "..", and ends in a known unit suffix; values contain no '\n' or NUL.
pub fn validate_drop_in(unit: &str, keys: &[(DropInKey, String)]) -> Result<(), HelperError>; // NotAllowed on failure
impl DropInKey { pub const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; } // "Restart", "RestartSec", ...
```

In `crates/tl-model/src/details.rs`: add `Serialize, Deserialize` to the derives of `StringScanOpts` and `StringEncoding` (no other change). Frames use `wire::MAX_HELPER_FRAME` and replies are read with `wire::read_reply(.., MAX_HELPER_FRAME, MAX_HELPER_REPLY_TOTAL, |r: &HelperReply| r.last)`.

`tests/proto_roundtrip.rs`: postcard round trip through `wire::encode_frame` / `read_frame` of every variant of `ProbeRequest`, `ProbeResponse` (with every `InitFailure` and every `Reading` arm), `ApiVersions`, `HelperFrame` (every `HelperRequest` variant), `HelperReply` (every body), and the serde types of `actions.rs` (`ActionId`, `Signal` including `Other(34)`, `SchedPolicy`, `IoPriority`, `DumpMode`, `Family`, `Proto`, `FourTuple` with an IPv6 scope id).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** every `HelperRequest` variant **When** framed and read back **Then** each equals the original.
- **Given** `validate_drop_in("sshd.service", [(Restart, "on-failure")])` **When** run **Then** it is `Ok`.
- **Given** the unit names `"../etc/passwd"`, `"a/b.service"`, `""`, `"x\0.service"`, `"sshd"` (no suffix) **When** `validate_drop_in` runs **Then** each returns `Err(NotAllowed)`.
- **Given** a value containing `"\n"` (for example `"on-failure\nExecStart=/bin/sh"`) **When** `validate_drop_in` runs **Then** it returns `Err(NotAllowed)` (the injection regression test).
- **Given** a `HelperReply` sequence of three frames with `last` only on the third **When** read with `read_reply` **Then** three replies are returned.
- **Given** the `HelperRequest` enum **When** a test matches it exhaustively **Then** there are exactly the 17 variants above, `CancelScan` included (R-157; a new variant breaks the test and forces a security review).
- **Given** `ProcFiles::ROOT` **When** its bits are read **Then** it is `1 << 11` and no other constant shares the bit (R-157).

## Files
- `crates/tl-model/src/helper_proto.rs`: the types and `validate_drop_in`.
- `crates/tl-model/src/details.rs`: the two derive additions.
- `crates/tl-model/tests/proto_roundtrip.rs`: the round-trip tests.

## Tests
- `tests/proto_roundtrip.rs::probe_messages_roundtrip`, `api_versions_roundtrip`, `helper_requests_roundtrip`, `helper_replies_roundtrip`, `action_serde_types_roundtrip`, `helper_reply_sequence_read_reply`.
- `helper_proto.rs` unit tests: `drop_in_valid`, `drop_in_rejects_bad_unit_names`, `drop_in_rejects_newline_value` (security regression), `helper_request_variant_count` (17), `proc_files_bits_distinct`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `HelperError` variants; the engine maps them to `ActionError` (`PermissionDenied`, `NoSuchProcess`, `Partial`, `Os`) or `Rejected(IdentityChanged)`.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: 64 KiB frames; file contents larger than one frame are sent as several `File` replies. The 4 MiB cap is per reply message for the streamed requests (`ScanStrings`, `NetnsSockDiagDump`) and total for the rest (R-157); over it the helper answers `Err(TooLarge)`.
- Privacy: environment and memory contents travel in `File` and `Strings` replies; never log reply bodies.
- Security: the request set is exactly R-004's allowlist; no path or command field. `validate_drop_in` is shared by the engine (before sending) and the helper (on receipt; the helper never trusts the engine). The helper re-runs `open_verified` on every process target (ADR-006); that is E29's code.

## Notes
- This bead's shape holds and is the type owner (R-157): `HelperFrame { seq, request }`, `HelperReply { seq, last, body }`, `Hello { proto }` both ways, `HELPER_PROTO_VERSION = 1`, `HelperError` plus `TooLarge`, `validate_drop_in`, the 64 KiB frame. E29 beads use these names (`seq`, `Ok`, `Err`, `File`, `SocketOwners`, `NetlinkDump`). `ReadProcessDetail` is dropped from ADR-006.
- `Dump` has no fd field: the engine opens the output file and passes the fd as `SCM_RIGHTS` ancillary data on the `Dump` frame over the helper's socketpair stdin and stdout (R-145 item 3).
- `CpuSet` derives `Serialize, Deserialize` in E03-009 (R-156 item 1).
- Depends on E03-053, E03-059, E03-068, E03-069, E03-A1.
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-model`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
close_reason: helper_proto.rs types, validate_drop_in, proto_roundtrip tests, FourTuple serde keeps IPv6 flowinfo and scope id (R-270). Commits 3209512, 0a20862, 6873854, 8b849b8

FourTuple with an IPv6 scope id cannot round-trip without a custom serde on FourTuple in actions.rs (E03-053). Test four_tuple_keeps_ipv6_scope_id is #[ignore]d until decided. title: E03-072 process.rs, ids.rs, snapshot.rs: ProcessExtras, AppCgroupSample, ProcessExtrasP2, LowMemoryInfo, NodeId::Unit
description:
## Context
The settled open items add per-process extra values, app cgroup samples, P2 column values and the low-memory sweep data to tl-model (R-141 items 1 and 2, R-163 item 2, R-150 item 2), and a `Unit` variant to `NodeId` (R-141 item 3). These types use `SchedPolicy` and `CgroupRef` (E03-053, `actions.rs`), `UnitRef` (E03-052, `table.rs`) and `CpuSet` (E03-009), so they cannot be written by E03-008 or E03-050, which come earlier. This bead appends them once those types exist. Sources: R-141, R-150, R-163, ADR-003 "Process record and metadata", ADR-008 (visible-rows rule), ADR-009 (`NodeId`), PROC-027 to PROC-038, PROC-097.

## Deliverable
Append to `crates/tl-model/src/process.rs` (uses `ids::{ProcessKey, GroupKey}`, `system::CpuSet`, `actions::{SchedPolicy, CgroupRef}`, `table::UnitRef`, `time::TimeNs`, `validity::FieldValidity`):

```rust
/// P1 extra-column values, index aligned with ProcessSnapshot.records (same length, same order) (R-141 item 1).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct ProcessExtras {
    pub cpu_kernel_pct: f32, pub cpu_user_pct: f32, pub cpu_relative_pct: f32,
    pub utime_ticks: u64, pub stime_ticks: u64, pub start_boot_ns: u64, // start_ticks × 1e9 / ticks_per_sec, filled by E05-A1
    pub rss_peak_bytes: u64, pub rss_shared_bytes: u64, pub commit_bytes: u64,
    pub vsize_bytes: u64, pub vsize_peak_bytes: u64,
    pub page_faults: u64, pub page_faults_delta: u64, pub major_faults: u64,
    pub policy: SchedPolicy, pub rt_prio: u8, pub affinity: CpuSet,
    pub handles: Option<u32>,
    pub exe_name: Arc<str>, pub exe_path: Arc<str>, pub exe_deleted: bool,
    pub unit: Option<UnitRef>,
    pub state_letter: u8, pub frozen: bool,
    pub disk_read_bps: f32, pub disk_write_raw_bps: f32,
    pub flag_since_ns: TimeNs,
}

/// One app cgroup sample (R-141 item 2). Filled by the tl-collect sweep (E05-A1).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct AppCgroupSample {
    pub group: GroupKey, pub anon_bytes: u64, pub swap_bytes: u64,
    pub io_read_bps: f32, pub io_write_bps: f32, pub rios: u64, pub wios: u64,
    pub pids: u32, pub cgroup: CgroupRef, pub validity: FieldValidity,
}

/// P2 per-process column values, filled only for Demand.detail_keys (ADR-008 visible-rows rule) by
/// E05-035; `power_w` and `power_trend_w` by the reducer (E09-030) for every row (R-163 items 2 and 9).
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Default)]
pub struct ProcessExtrasP2 {
    pub key: Option<ProcessKey>,         // Some for a filled entry; None for a row outside detail_keys
    pub exe_mtime_s: Option<i64>,        // statx mtime of the exe
    pub exe_size_bytes: Option<u64>,     // statx size of the exe
    pub elf_class: Option<u8>,           // 32 or 64
    pub elf_machine: Option<u16>,        // e_machine
    pub session_id: Option<u32>,         // /proc/<pid>/sessionid
    pub security_label: Option<Arc<str>>,// /proc/<pid>/attr/current
    pub elevated: Option<bool>,          // PROC-028 elevation rule
    pub sandbox: Option<Arc<str>>,       // PROC-028 sandbox rule
    pub sched_policy_text: Option<Arc<str>>,
    pub oom_score: Option<i32>, pub oom_score_adj: Option<i16>,
    pub tty: Option<Arc<str>>,           // decoded tty_nr
    pub cwd: Option<Arc<str>>,
    pub ctx_switches_voluntary: Option<u64>, pub ctx_switches_involuntary: Option<u64>, // sum over task/*/status
    pub power_w: Option<f32>,            // PROC-034 estimate (E09-030)
    pub power_trend_w: Option<f32>,      // 2-minute average of power_w (E09-030)
    pub ctx_switches_delta: Option<u64>, // change since the previous fill of this key
    pub package: Option<Arc<PackageInfo>>,       // owning package (E05-034 index), PROC-027
    pub package_status: Option<PackageStatus>,   // PROC-027 Package status column
}

/// Owning package of an executable (R-163 item 1, PROC-027), from the E05-034 index.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct PackageInfo { pub name: Arc<str>, pub version: Arc<str>, pub description: Option<Arc<str>>, pub packager: Option<Arc<str>>, pub build_date_s: Option<i64>, pub url: Option<Arc<str>> }

/// PROC-027 Package status. `PackagedModified` only after a `pacman -Qkk` check (PROC-078).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum PackageStatus { Packaged, PackagedModified, NotPackaged, DeletedUpgraded, Flatpak, Snap, AppImage, Wine }

/// Low-memory sweep data (R-150 item 2), moved from E32's types.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct LowMemGroup { pub group: GroupKey, pub name: Arc<str>, pub process_count: u32, pub uid: u32, pub cgroup: CgroupRef, pub memory_current: u64 }
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct LowMemoryInfo { pub groups: Arc<[LowMemGroup]>, pub mem_total: u64, pub mem_available: u64, pub psi_full_pct: Option<f32>, pub critical: bool }
```

In `crates/tl-model/src/ids.rs`, append the variant to `NodeId` (R-141 item 3, ADR-009):

```rust
pub enum NodeId { Group(GroupKey), Process(ProcessKey), KernelThreads, Pseudo(PseudoKind), Unit(UnitRef) }
```

title: E03-002 time.rs: CLOCK_BOOTTIME timestamps and BootId
description:
## Context
Every sample and snapshot timestamp in tasklens uses CLOCK_BOOTTIME, so suspend shows as a real gap and history timestamps stay comparable across suspend (ADR-003 deviation from Astra). CLOCK_MONOTONIC is read beside it only to detect suspend (ADR-008: a resume is detected when `Δboot_ns - Δmono_ns > 250 ms`). `BootId` scopes process identity to one boot. Sources: ADR-003 "Time", ADR-008 "Suspend and resume", PROC-001.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-model/src/time.rs`:

```rust
/// Nanoseconds of CLOCK_BOOTTIME. Every sample and snapshot timestamp uses this clock.
pub type TimeNs = u64;

/// CLOCK_BOOTTIME now, via rustix::time::clock_gettime(ClockId::Boottime).
pub fn now_boot_ns() -> TimeNs;

/// CLOCK_MONOTONIC now, via rustix::time::clock_gettime(ClockId::Monotonic). Used only for suspend detection.
pub fn now_mono_ns() -> u64;

/// Folded from /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id: first 8 bytes XOR last 8 bytes of the UUID.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct BootId(pub u64);

impl BootId {
    /// Parses the text of /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id (36-char UUID, optional trailing
    /// newline, hex digits upper or lower case, hyphens at positions 8, 13, 18, 23) and folds it.
    /// Returns None for any other input. Pure: tl-model does no file I/O; tl-collect reads the file.
    pub fn from_uuid_text(text: &str) -> Option<BootId>;
}
```

- Conversion: `secs as u64 * 1_000_000_000 + nanos as u64` from the rustix `Timespec`.
- Fold: decode the 32 hex digits into 16 bytes `b[0..16]` in text order; `hi = u64::from_be_bytes(b[0..8])`, `lo = u64::from_be_bytes(b[8..16])`; result `BootId(hi ^ lo)`.
- `PartialOrd, Ord` are needed because `ProcessKey` (ids.rs) derives `Ord` and contains `BootId`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the text `"00112233-4455-6677-8899-aabbccddeeff\n"` **When** `BootId::from_uuid_text` runs **Then** it returns `Some(BootId(0x0011223344556677 ^ 0x8899aabbccddeeff))`.
- **Given** the same UUID in upper case **When** parsed **Then** the result equals the lower-case result.
- **Given** a 35-character string, a string with a non-hex digit, or hyphens in the wrong places **When** parsed **Then** it returns `None`.
- **Given** two calls to `now_boot_ns()` **When** compared **Then** the second is greater than or equal to the first.
- **Given** a running system **When** `now_boot_ns()` and `now_mono_ns()` are read together **Then** `now_boot_ns() >= now_mono_ns()` (boottime includes suspend time).

## Files
- `crates/tl-model/src/time.rs`: fill the placeholder from E03-001

## Tests
- `time.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`:
  - `boot_id_fold_known_value`: the known-value case above.
  - `boot_id_case_insensitive`: upper and lower case give the same id.
  - `boot_id_rejects_bad_input`: wrong length, non-hex, wrong hyphen positions, empty string all give `None`.
  - `boot_id_trailing_newline_optional`: with and without `\n` give the same id.
  - `clocks_monotonic`: two reads of each clock never go backwards; boottime is at least monotonic.
  - `proptest boot_id_never_panics`: arbitrary `String` input never panics.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: parse failure is `None`, never a panic.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: `now_boot_ns` is one syscall (vDSO), no allocation. `from_uuid_text` does not allocate.
- Privacy: the boot id is not secret, but do not log it at info level; it is a stable machine-per-boot identifier.

## Notes
- `rustix::time::clock_gettime` and `ClockId::{Boottime, Monotonic}` need the rustix `time` feature, which E03-001 enables.
- `unsafe_code = "deny"` is a workspace lint; this file needs no `unsafe`.
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `cargo test -p tl-model`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E03-007 series.rs: TieredRing with the 1 Hz per-second-max tier
description:
## Context
From P2 every series also keeps a 1 Hz tier of 602 samples (10 min + 2) that serves the 5 min and 10 min graph ranges. Each 1 Hz value is the per-second maximum of the fast tier, the same rule ADR-012 uses for history; there is no per-sample min/max pair and `Sample` stays 16 bytes (ADR-003, PERF-017, R-016). This bead adds the two-tier wrapper the reducer (E09) owns per series. tl-model writes it now because every tl-model file is written up front (00-epics section 2). Sources: ADR-003 "Series", ADR-012 (per-second max), PERF-016, PERF-017, R-016.

## Deliverable
Add to `crates/tl-model/src/series.rs`:

```rust
/// Capacity of the 1 Hz tier: 10 min + 2.
pub const SLOW_TIER_CAPACITY: u32 = 602;

/// Fast ring plus the 1 Hz tier built from it.
pub struct TieredRing {
    pub fast: SeriesRing,
    pub slow: SeriesRing,           // capacity SLOW_TIER_CAPACITY
    bucket_sec: Option<u64>,        // t_ns / 1_000_000_000 of the open bucket
    bucket: Option<Sample>,         // running maximum of the open second
}

impl TieredRing {
    /// fast capacity = SeriesRing::fast_capacity(period_ns); slow capacity = 602.
    pub fn new(period_ns: u64) -> TieredRing;
    /// Pushes into the fast ring and folds the sample into the open 1 Hz bucket.
    pub fn push(&mut self, s: Sample);
    /// mark_gap on both tiers.
    pub fn mark_gap(&mut self);
}
```

Bucket rule, applied in `push(s)`:
1. `sec = s.t_ns / 1_000_000_000`.
2. If a bucket is open and `sec > bucket_sec`, close it: push the bucket sample into `slow`, then open a new bucket for `sec`.
3. Fold `s` into the bucket: the bucket's flags are the OR of the folded samples' `GAP_BEFORE`, `RESET` and `STALE` flags; `VALID` is set if any folded sample is valid; the value is the maximum value over the valid folded samples (0.0 when none is valid).
4. The closed bucket's `t_ns` is `sec × 1_000_000_000` (the start of that second), so 1 Hz samples are exactly 1 s apart.
5. A sample whose `sec` is lower than the open bucket's (clock went back, should not happen with CLOCK_BOOTTIME) is pushed to `fast` only and not folded.
6. A 1 Hz source (period 1 s) still goes through the same rule; its slow tier then equals its fast tier shifted to second boundaries.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a 100 ms ring **When** ten valid samples in second 5 with values 1..=10 and then one sample in second 6 are pushed **Then** `slow` holds one sample with `t_ns == 5_000_000_000`, value 10.0 and `VALID`.
- **Given** a bucket whose samples are all gaps **When** it closes **Then** the slow sample has no `VALID` flag.
- **Given** one sample with `GAP_BEFORE` among ten in a second **When** the bucket closes **Then** the slow sample has `GAP_BEFORE`.
- **Given** a bucket with valid values 3.0 and an invalid sample with value 99.0 **When** it closes **Then** the slow value is 3.0.
- **Given** `TieredRing::new(100_000_000)` **When** created **Then** `fast.capacity() == 602` and `slow.capacity() == 602`.
- **Given** samples that skip from second 5 to second 9 **When** the second-9 sample arrives **Then** exactly one slow sample (second 5) is pushed; missing seconds produce no samples (the chart's gap rule handles the hole).
- **Given** `mark_gap()` **When** the next samples arrive **Then** the first fast sample and the first closed slow sample both carry `GAP_BEFORE`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-model/src/series.rs`: add `TieredRing` and `SLOW_TIER_CAPACITY`

## Tests
- `series.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tier_tests`:
  - `slow_tier_per_second_max`
  - `slow_tier_all_gap_bucket_invalid`
  - `slow_tier_flags_ored`
  - `slow_tier_ignores_invalid_values_in_max`
  - `slow_tier_capacities`
  - `slow_tier_no_fill_for_skipped_seconds`
  - `slow_tier_mark_gap_both`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: the slow sample is a gap only when no folded sample was valid.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: `push` is O(1), no allocation. Memory per series: (fast capacity + 602) × 16 bytes.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- The docs fix "per-second maximum" but not the 1 Hz sample's timestamp or how flags combine. Rules 3 and 4 are the B1 writer's proposal (open item in docs/plan/b1-infra.md); the leader confirms before this bead starts.
- The reducer (E09) decides when to call `mark_gap` (suspend, rate change, epoch). This type only applies it.
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...` On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E21-A1 Menu bar entity and File menu
description:
## Context
Builds the main window's menu bar: the `MenuBar` entity that opens, closes and switches menu popups, handles the menu keys, and returns focus, plus the File menu with its one P1 item "Exit tasklens". Every later menu (View, Settings, Help, Debug) plugs into the registry this bead creates. tasklens uses its own `MenuBar` instead of the kit `AppMenuBar`, because the kit one reads static `OwnedMenu`s and cannot show live checks, sliders or painted theme rows. Sources: UI-SHL-030, UI-SHL-031, UI-SHL-032, UI-SHL-003 part 4, APP-012, APP-002, table (b) F10 and Alt+F/V/S/H, UI-FND-022, R-128.

Anchor E21-A1. Other beads depend on this one for `MenuBar`, `MenuId` handling and the per-menu builder registry. The full P1 menu set is this bead plus E21-001 (View, Columns), E21-002 (Process View), E21-003 (Graphs) and E21-004 (Settings menu).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/window/menubar.rs`:
- `pub struct MenuBar { open: Option<MenuId>, popup: Option<Entity<PopupMenu>>, return_focus: Option<FocusHandle>, opened_by_key: bool }` (Entity, one per main window). `MenuId` is the enum E20-A1 declares with `OpenMenu(MenuId)` in `actions.rs` (variants `File`, `View`, `Settings`, `Help`, `Debug`).
- `pub fn init(cx: &mut App)`: registers the global `on_action` handlers this file owns and installs the menu bar into the title bar slot (see Notes, slot item). Called once from `TasklensUi::init` in `app.rs` (one added line).
- `pub fn new(window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App) -> Entity<MenuBar>`.
- A builder registry: `fn build_menu(id: MenuId, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App) -> Option<Entity<PopupMenu>>` with one `match` arm per menu. This bead writes the `MenuId::File` arm (calls `menus_file::build`); every other arm returns `None`. A menu whose builder returns `None` or an empty menu has no button (the "no dead items" rule: in P1 Help and Debug have no button).
- Render: one button per present menu in the order File, View, Settings, Help, Debug. Each button: `TlButton` ghost, height 26, padding-x 16, label `t_md` weight 400, colour `text_primary` (window active) or `text_secondary` (window inactive). Between two buttons and after the last: a vertical separator 1 physical px wide, 16 px tall, colour `divider`, vertically centred. Open state fill `menu_hover` (also on hover). Button labels: "File", "View", "Settings", "Help", "Debug".
- Mouse-down on a menu button calls `cx.stop_propagation()` and `window.prevent_default()` so it never starts a title bar drag. Right-click and middle-click on a menu button do nothing.
- Behaviour:
  - Click a closed menu button: build its popup fresh (from `TlSettings` and app state at that moment) and show it below the button with left edges aligned and 0 px gap, using `deferred(anchored().anchor(Anchor::TopLeft).snap_to_window_with_margin(px(8.)))`.
  - Click the open menu's button: close it.
  - While a menu is open, hovering another menu button opens that menu and closes the first.
  - `OpenMenu(id)` (bound by E20 to F10 = File, Alt+F, Alt+V, Alt+S, Alt+H, Alt+D): opens that menu if present; when opened by a key, the first enabled item is highlighted.

  - Activating an item closes the whole menu chain and dispatches the item's Action to `return_focus`: every popup is built with `PopupMenu::action_context(previous_focus)`.

title: E21-009 Menu slider rows and View > Appearance submenu
description:
## Context
Adds the `slider_row` menu helper and View > Appearance: UI Scale, Row Height, Rounded Corners, Value Color Coding, its intensity and Drop Shadow Intensity. Sliders preview live while dragged and save once on release. The keys Ctrl+Plus, Ctrl+Minus and Ctrl+0 (P1) and the re-layout steps belong to E20 (UI-SHL-130). Sources: UI-SHL-037, UI-SHL-130, APP-040, R-020, R-077, ADR-009 (metrics and scale), UI-FND-014.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/window/menubar.rs`:
- `pub(crate) struct MenuSliders { ui_scale: Entity<SliderState>, row_height: Entity<SliderState>, heat_intensity: Entity<SliderState>, shadow_intensity: Entity<SliderState>, tab_switch: Entity<SliderState> }` created once in `MenuBar::new` and reused across menu opens (entities are never created in render). Each slider subscribes to `SliderEvent` once in `MenuBar::new`.
- `pub(crate) fn slider_row(label: SharedString, state: &Entity<SliderState>, value_text: SharedString) -> impl IntoElement` rendered as a `PopupMenu::menu_element` row, height 28:
  `| [check col 20] Label (min w 140, t_base, ellipsis "…") [track 120 × 4] value (w 40, right, t_sm, tabular figures, text_secondary) |`.
- Slider events: `SliderEvent::Change(v)` applies the value in memory (no persist) and runs the scale re-layout through the `TlSettings` observer; `SliderEvent::Release(v)` persists once. Use the in-memory write and the persisting write E20-A2 provides (see Notes).

`crates/tl-ui/src/window/menus_view.rs`: `fn appearance_submenu(..)` and its root item "Appearance" (fourth in the View root order). Items in order:

| # | Label | Kind | Key | Range, step, value text |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | UI Scale | slider row | `appearance.ui_scale_pct` | 75..=200, step 5, "%d%%" ("120%") |
| 2 | Row Height | slider row | `appearance.row_height_pct` | 80..=150, step 5, "%d%%" |
| 3 | Rounded Corners | check | `appearance.rounded_corners` | `ToggleSetting(AppearanceRoundedCorners)` |
| 4 | Value Color Coding | check | `appearance.heat_coloring` | `ToggleSetting(AppearanceHeatColoring)` |
| 5 | Value Color Coding Intensity | slider row | `appearance.heat_intensity_pct` | 0..=100, step 5, "%d%%" |
| 6 | Drop Shadow Intensity | slider row | `appearance.shadow_intensity_pct` | 0..=100, step 5, "%d%%" |

Behaviour:
- UI Scale release pushes the Info toast "UI scale changed to 120%" (the released value) with toast id `ui-scale`, so repeated changes replace one toast.
- Keyboard on a highlighted slider row: Left and Right step by the row's step, Home and End jump to min and max; each key press counts as a release (persist, and the UI Scale toast).
- The popup stays open while dragging, after release, and after clicking a check row (the check toggles and the popup stays).
- A UI Scale change re-lays out the menu; the popup stays anchored to its row.
- String keys appended (`shell-menu-appearance-*`): "UI Scale", "Row Height", "Rounded Corners", "Value Color Coding", "Value Color Coding Intensity", "Drop Shadow Intensity", and `shell-toast-ui-scale` "UI scale changed to { $pct }%" if E20 has not added it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** View > Appearance open **When** the UI Scale slider sends Change 105, Change 110, Change 115, then Release 115 **Then** the persist callback runs once, `ui_scale_pct == 115`, and the toast "UI scale changed to 115%" shows.
- **Given** a Change event **When** it is applied **Then** the in-memory value changes and the persist callback is not called.

- **Given** "Rounded Corners" is clicked **When** the click is handled **Then** the key flips and the popup stays open.
- **Given** the menu is closed and opened again **When** it renders **Then** the same four `SliderState` entities are reused (no new entity).

- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: chain edit.

## Tests

- `appearance_slider_keys`: Left, Right, Home, End on a slider row; each press persists once.
- `appearance_popup_stays_open`: after a check click and after a release the popup is still open.
- `slider_entities_reused`: entity ids equal across two menu opens.

title: E21-011 Settings menu: Start at login and Start minimized
description:
## Context
Adds "Start at login" and the indented "Start minimized" to the Settings menu, and the `ToggleStartAtLogin` Action that writes or deletes the XDG autostart entry. The Settings window rows (E21-026) dispatch the same Action. Sources: UI-SHL-040, UI-SHL-069, APP-048, table (c) autostart path.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/window/menus_settings.rs`:
- `actions!(tasklens, [ToggleStartAtLogin]);` and its global handler registered from a `pub fn init(cx: &mut App)` in this file (one `app.rs` line: `window::menus_settings::init(cx);`).
- Group "Window & startup", in the order given in E21-010: "Start at login" (check bound to `startup.start_at_login`, dispatches `ToggleStartAtLogin`), then "Start minimized" (check bound to `startup.start_minimized`, `ToggleSetting(StartupStartMinimized)`, label indented by 16, disabled unless `startup.start_at_login` is true).
- `ToggleStartAtLogin` handler:
  - tl-app writes the entry; tl-ui calls `(cx.global::<AppEnv>().set_autostart)(enabled, minimized)` (`AppEnv.set_autostart: Arc<dyn Fn(bool /*enabled*/, bool /*minimized*/) -> Result<(), String>>`, E16-A1, R-171, R-236). tl-app writes `~/.config/autostart/io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.desktop` with `Exec=tasklens` (or `Exec=tasklens --start-minimized` when `minimized` is true) and `X-KDE-autostart-phase=2` atomically, and deletes it when `enabled` is false.
  - Turning on: call `set_autostart(true, settings.startup.start_minimized)`; on `Ok(())` set `startup.start_at_login = true`.
  - Turning off: call `set_autostart(false, settings.startup.start_minimized)`; on `Ok(())` set the key false.
  - Toggling "Start minimized" while Start at login is on: call `set_autostart(true, <new value>)` again (R-236); on `Ok(())` write the new `startup.start_minimized`. While Start at login is off, only the key changes.
  - Failure: Error toast "Could not change the autostart entry" and the setting keeps its old value.
- String keys appended: `shell-menu-settings-start-at-login` "Start at login", `shell-menu-settings-start-minimized` "Start minimized", `shell-toast-autostart-failed` "Could not change the autostart entry".

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `startup.start_at_login = false` **When** the Settings menu opens **Then** "Start minimized" is disabled and indented by 16.
- **Given** Start at login off **When** "Start at login" is activated and the write succeeds **Then** the autostart writer was called with `enabled = true, minimized = false` and the key is true.
- **Given** the writer fails **When** "Start at login" is activated **Then** the toast "Could not change the autostart entry" shows and the key stays false.
- **Given** Start at login on **When** "Start minimized" is activated **Then** the key is true and the entry is rewritten with `minimized = true`.
- **Given** Start at login on **When** it is activated again **Then** the writer is called with `enabled = false` and the key becomes false.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/menus_settings.rs`: rows, Action, handler.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/app.rs`, `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: chain edits.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_menus.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_menus.rs` (with a fake autostart writer):
- `start_minimized_disabled`: disabled while `startup.start_at_login = false`.
- `start_at_login_success`: writer called once with enabled true; key true.
- `start_at_login_failure_reverts`: writer returns an error; toast text; key unchanged.
- `start_minimized_rewrites_entry`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: "Could not change the autostart entry" (Error toast, 8 s); the setting reverts.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: the disabled row is skipped by arrow keys.
- Performance: the closure runs on the main thread (it is not `Send`); tl-app keeps the write short (one small file).
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- Settled (R-171, R-236): tl-ui does no file I/O (ADR-011); the autostart entry is written by tl-app (`tl-app/src/autostart.rs`, E33) behind `AppEnv.set_autostart(enabled, minimized)`. Tests use `AppEnv::test()` with a recording fake.

An explicit theme choice turns sync off so the next portal change does not overwrite it. Create copy and Delete are E21-013; Edit, Share and Import are P3 (E21-031). Sources: UI-SHL-038, UI-SHL-080, APP-035, APP-036, R-068, R-069, UI-FND-022 (`painted_item`), UI-FND-040, UI-FND-043.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/window/menus_view.rs`:
- `actions!(tasklens, [ ... ])` with `#[derive(Action, Clone, PartialEq, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[action(namespace = tasklens)] pub struct ActivateTheme { pub name: SharedString }`.
- `pub fn init(cx: &mut App)` registering the global theme handlers (one `app.rs` line: `window::menus_view::init(cx);`).
- `fn theme_submenu(..)` and its root item "Theme" (fifth in the View root order). Items in order:
  1. One theme row per built-in theme in `ThemeStore.builtin` order (P2: Default Dark, Vivid Nightfall, Catppuccin Frappé, Catppuccin Macchiato, Catppuccin Mocha, Dracula, OLED Black, Default Light, Windows 7 Aero, Golden Summer Fields, Soft Pink Delight, Catppuccin Latte; P1 builds only have Default Dark and Default Light), then one per user theme in `themes.json` order. Each row: `TlMenu::painted_item(label, bg, fg, suffix_icon, action)` 26 tall, bg = that theme's `menu_bg`, fg = that theme's `text_primary`, radio mark on the active theme, dispatches `ActivateTheme { name }`. A user theme whose name equals a built-in name shows " (custom)" after it. While the Theme Editor previews a theme, that row shows " (editing)" and carries the mark.
  2. The suffix copy icon (Lucide `copy`, `i_sm`, tooltip "Create copy") is added by E21-013.
  3. separator; the per-theme items (Create copy, Edit colors, Share theme, Delete theme) are added by E21-013 and E21-031; separator; "Import theme" (E21-031).
  4. "Sync theme with system": check bound to `theme.follow_system`, `ToggleSetting(ThemeFollowSystem)`.
  5. "Preferred Light Theme": submenu, every theme name as a radio bound to `theme.light`, `SetSetting { ThemeLight, Str(name) }`.
  6. "Preferred Dark Theme": submenu, every theme name as a radio bound to `theme.dark`, `SetSetting { ThemeDark, Str(name) }`.
- `ActivateTheme { name }` handler:
  - If a Theme Editor preview is live (`ThemeStore.preview.is_some()`): refuse with the Info toast "Finish or cancel the theme editor first".
  - Else write `theme.active = name`, call `ThemeStore::activate(name, cx)` (E17), and if `theme.follow_system` was true set it false and push the Info toast "Theme sync turned off".
- Turning sync on (observe the `theme` section version): apply the preferred theme for the current portal scheme at once (`theme.dark` for scheme 0 and 1, `theme.light` for 2) through `ThemeStore` (E17-A2 follow-system).
- `ThemeEvent::Activated` from the store produces no toast.
- String keys appended: `shell-menu-theme-sync` "Sync theme with system", `shell-menu-theme-light` "Preferred Light Theme", `shell-menu-theme-dark` "Preferred Dark Theme", `shell-menu-theme-custom` " (custom)", `shell-menu-theme-editing` " (editing)", `shell-toast-theme-sync-off` "Theme sync turned off", `shell-toast-theme-editor-busy` "Finish or cancel the theme editor first". Theme names are data, not translated.

- **Given** `theme.follow_system = true` **When** `ActivateTheme { name: "Dracula" }` runs **Then** `theme.follow_system == false`, `theme.active == "Dracula"`, and the toast "Theme sync turned off" shows.

- **Given** a live editor preview **When** `ActivateTheme` runs **Then** the active theme is unchanged and the toast "Finish or cancel the theme editor first" shows.
- **Given** sync off and portal scheme 2 **When** "Sync theme with system" is activated **Then** `theme.light`'s theme becomes active at once.
- **Given** the Preferred Dark submenu **When** "OLED Black" is chosen **Then** `theme.dark == "OLED Black"`.

title: E21-013 View > Theme: Create copy and Delete theme with confirmation
description:
## Context
Adds "Create copy" (menu item and the copy icon on every theme row) and "Delete theme" with its confirmation window to View > Theme. Both act on the active theme from the menu item; the row icon copies that row's theme. Sources: UI-SHL-038, UI-SHL-084, UI-SHL-091, APP-036, UI-FND-042.

## Deliverable

- Theme rows get the suffix icon: Lucide `copy`, `i_sm`, tooltip "Create copy"; clicking it dispatches `CopyTheme { name: <that row's theme> }` and does not apply the theme or close the menu.
- After the theme rows: separator, then "Create copy" (`CopyTheme { name: <active> }`) and "Delete theme" (`DeleteTheme { name: <active> }`). (E21-031 inserts "Edit colors" between them and "Share theme" after "Edit colors" in P3.)

`crates/tl-ui/src/window/confirm.rs`:

If it was active, activate `theme.dark` or `theme.light` matching the deleted theme's mode, falling back to "Default Dark" or "Default Light" when that preferred theme is the deleted one. A `theme.light` or `theme.dark` that named it resets to its default ("Default Light" / "Default Dark"). Success toast "Theme deleted" (from `ThemeEvent::Deleted`).

description:
## Context

title: E21-016 Keyboard Shortcuts window
description:
## Context
Builds the "tasklens Keyboard Shortcuts" window: a searchable list of every key binding, grouped by context, with key caps read from the live keymap so it always matches what is bound. Actions not built in the current phase have no binding and so no row. Sources: UI-SHL-095, APP-030, APP-031, canonical table (b), R-083, R-120.

- `pub struct ShortcutsWindow { search: Entity<InputState>, rows: Vec<ShortcutRow>, filtered: Vec<usize> }` opened with `TlSecondaryWindow::open`: title "tasklens Keyboard Shortcuts", Tool window, 560 × 640, minimum 420 × 360.
- `struct ShortcutRow { heading: Heading, description: SharedString, keys: SmallVec<[Kbd; 2]>, search_text: String }`.
- Row source: a static table `SHORTCUT_DOCS: &[(&'static str /* action name, e.g. "tasklens::SelectTab" */, Heading, &'static str /* Fluent key of the description */)]` holding one entry per row of canonical table (b), with the description text equal to that row's "Action" column (for example "Select tab 1 to 6 (Processes, Performance, Services, Startup Apps, Connections, Information)", "Next / previous tab", "Run…", "Exit tasklens", "Close window (follows close behaviour)", "All settings…", "Keyboard Shortcuts", "Open File menu", "Open File / View / Settings / Help menu", "Focus filter", "Refresh current tab now", "UI scale +5 / −5 / 100", "Performance mini window", "Move row selection", "Select all visible rows", "Toggle expand", "Properties", "Copy row", "Copy rows as table (TSV with header)", "Collapse all", "Open context menu for the selection", "End Task (SIGTERM)", "End Process (SIGKILL)", "Copy device info", "Graph Summary View", "Toggle device sidebar", "Select visible device 1 to 8", "Cancel window picking", and the remaining table (b) rows).

Several bindings are joined with " or ".
- Rows without a key in table (b) as a GPUI binding (Hold Ctrl, Shift held at launch, printable character, Shift+click, Ctrl+click) are static rows with literal key text: "Hold Ctrl" (Global, "Pause display"), "Printable character" (Tables, "Start filtering"), "Shift+click, Ctrl+click" (Tables, "Extend or toggle selection"). "Shift held at launch" is listed under Startup only from P3.
- Layout: search input at top (placeholder "Search shortcuts"), then a scrollable list with heading rows in the fixed order Global, Tables, Processes, Services, Performance, Dialogs, Startup (plus the headings settled by open item 4). Row height 28: description `t_base` left, key caps right (kit `Kbd`).

- Esc and Ctrl+W close.

title: E21-017 Public IP Notice window and fetch entry point
description:
## Context
Builds the "tasklens Public IP Notice" modal window shown before the first public IP fetch, and the entry point that callers use to fetch: it runs the fetch at once when the notice was accepted, otherwise asks first. The fetch itself belongs to the Network page and Information tab owners (PERF-060). Sources: UI-SHL-096, APP-056, PERF-060, R-058, UI-FND-021.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/window/public_ip.rs` (create):
- `pub fn request_public_ip_fetch(window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App, fetch: impl FnOnce(&mut Window, &mut App) + 'static)`:
  - If `network.public_ip_notice_accepted` is true: call `fetch` at once.
  - Else open the notice (modal to `window`). Continue: if the checkbox is checked, write `network.public_ip_notice_accepted = true`; then call `fetch`. Cancel or Esc: close, do not fetch.
  - While the notice is open, a second call focuses it (`WindowKey::PublicIpNotice`) and drops the second `fetch`.
- Notice window: `TlSecondaryWindow::open` kind Dialog (modal), title "tasklens Public IP Notice", width 460, content-sized height. Text lines, `t_base`, each its own paragraph:
  1. "tasklens will fetch your public IP address from an online service."
  2. "Service: https://api.ipify.org"
  3. "Continue only if you want this computer to contact that service."
  Then `TlCheckbox` "Do not ask again for public IP fetches" (unchecked on open). Footer: "Cancel" (Secondary), "Continue" (Primary, default; focus starts on it: not destructive).
- String keys appended (`shell-public-ip-*`): title, the three lines, the checkbox label, "Continue"; "Cancel" reuses `shell-confirm-cancel`.
- Chain edit `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`: `pub mod public_ip;`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `public_ip_notice_accepted = false` **When** `request_public_ip_fetch` is called **Then** the notice opens with focus on "Continue" and `fetch` has not run.
- **Given** the notice with the box unchecked **When** Continue is clicked **Then** `fetch` runs once and the key stays false.
- **Given** the notice with the box checked **When** Continue is clicked **Then** the key becomes true and `fetch` runs once.
- **Given** the notice **When** Esc is pressed **Then** it closes and `fetch` never runs.
- **Given** `public_ip_notice_accepted = true` **When** `request_public_ip_fetch` is called **Then** `fetch` runs at once and no window opens.

## Files

- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`, `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: chain edits.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell_windows.rs`: add tests.

## Tests

- `public_ip_continue_unchecked`.
- `public_ip_continue_checked_writes_key`.

- `public_ip_accepted_skips_notice`.

## Cross-cutting

title: E21-018 Settings window frame, page list and PageBuilder
description:
## Context
Builds the frame of the "tasklens Settings" window: the window itself, the kit `Settings` widget with a 220 px sidebar, search and the eleven-page list, the refocus rule, and a page-builder helper that binds controls to `TlSettings` and records which keys each page binds (used by the "every key once" test). Page beads E21-019 to E21-026 and E21-A2 fill the pages. Sources: UI-SHL-060, APP-023, APP-045, R-028, UI-FND-021.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/window/settings/mod.rs` (create; a large file: commit it before building):
- `pub fn init(cx: &mut App)`: registers the handler for `OpenSettings` (declared and bound to `ctrl-,` by E20-A1): if `WindowKey::Settings` is open, focus it; else open. One `app.rs` line.
- `pub struct SettingsWindow { sliders: SettingsSliders, inputs: SettingsInputs, _settings_sub: Subscription, _hub_sub: Subscription }`, opened with `TlSecondaryWindow::open`: title "tasklens Settings", Tool window (`WindowKind::Floating`, parent = main window, not modal), default size 900 × 640, minimum 720 × 480, no position requested.
- Body: gpui-kit `Settings::new("settings").sidebar_width(px(220.))` with pages in this order and these Lucide icons (16 px): General `settings`, Appearance `palette`, Motion `activity`, Units `scaling`, Processes `list-tree`, Performance `gauge`, Graphs `chart-area`, Services `server`, Startup and window `app-window`, Privileges `shield`, Advanced `sliders-horizontal`. A page with no item in the current build is not listed (its bead adds it).
- `pub(crate) struct PageBuilder { page: SettingPage, keys: Vec<SettingKey> }` with methods that build a `SettingItem` and push the key:
  - `switch(&mut self, group, key: SettingKey, label, description: Option<SharedString>)`
  - `checkbox(..)` (same shape)
  - `dropdown(&mut self, group, key, label, options: &[(SharedString /*label*/, SettingValue /*stored*/)])`
  - `slider(&mut self, group, key, label, range: RangeInclusive<i64>, step: i64, fmt: fn(i64) -> SharedString)`: Change writes in memory, Release persists (same as the menu sliders).
  - `number(&mut self, group, key, label, range, step, suffix: SharedString)`
  - `custom(&mut self, group, keys: &[SettingKey], label, render: impl Fn(..) -> AnyElement)` for custom controls (device list, fans).
  - `button(&mut self, group, label, action: Box<dyn Action>, style)` (binds no key).
  Group rendering: `SettingGroup` title `t_sm` semibold `text_secondary`; item title `t_base` `text_primary`; description `t_sm` `text_secondary`; control at the right.
  Every setter goes through the kit `SettingField` get and set closures that call `TlSettings::update` (E20-A2).
- `pub(crate) fn all_pages(cx: &mut App) -> Vec<PageBuilder>`: calls each page module's `pub fn page(cx: &mut App) -> PageBuilder` in page order; page beads add one `mod` line and one call here.
- Item labels equal the menu labels where a menu item exists.
- Restart items: `appearance.decorations` and `rendering.gpu` show the description "Takes effect after restart" and push their restart toast on change (page beads use `PageBuilder::restart_note`).
- Search: the kit search matches item titles, descriptions and per-item keywords (`SettingItem::keywords`).
- Esc closes the window (tool window rule); Ctrl+W closes.
- The window re-renders only on input and on `TlSettings` changes; it subscribes to no snapshot data except the device catalog and the GPU engine list (`ComponentMask::DEVICES`).
- Slider and input state entities are created in `SettingsWindow::new`, never in render.
- String keys appended: title, the eleven page names, "Takes effect after restart".
- Chain edit `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`: `pub mod settings;`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** no Settings window **When** Ctrl+, is pressed (or `OpenSettings` dispatched) **Then** a window "tasklens Settings" opens at 900 × 640 with the sidebar 220 px wide.
- **Given** the window is open **When** `OpenSettings` is dispatched again **Then** the existing window is focused and no second one opens.
- **Given** the window is focused **When** Esc is pressed **Then** it closes.
- **Given** a test page built with `PageBuilder::switch(.., SettingKey::MotionAnimations, ..)` **When** the switch is toggled **Then** `motion.animations` flips through `TlSettings::update` and the builder's `keys` holds `MotionAnimations`.
- **Given** a slider item **When** it sends Change then Release **Then** the persist callback runs once.
- **Given** no snapshot change except PROCESSES **When** snapshots arrive **Then** the Settings window does not re-render.

- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`, `crates/tl-ui/src/app.rs`, `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: chain edits.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_settings_window.rs`: create.

## Tests

- `settings_window_size_and_sidebar`.
- `settings_esc_closes`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: Tab moves through the search field, the page list, then the page's controls in reading order; Up and Down move in the page list.
- Performance: renders only on input and `TlSettings` changes (plus DEVICES for the Performance page lists).

title: E21-005 Reset settings confirmation and ResetSettings action
description:
## Context
Creates the shell's confirmation module and its first use, "Reset Settings to Defaults": a destructive confirm window, then a reset of `settings.toml` to defaults that keeps `state.toml`, `themes.json` and history. The Settings menu item (E21-004) and the Advanced page button (E21-A2) both dispatch the `ResetSettings` Action declared here. Sources: UI-SHL-072, UI-SHL-091, APP-022, UI-FND-021, R-104.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/window/confirm.rs` (create):
- `actions!(tasklens, [ResetSettings]);`
- `pub fn init(cx: &mut App)`: registers `cx.on_action(|_: &ResetSettings, cx| ..)`. Called from `TasklensUi::init` (one added line in `app.rs`).
- `pub fn confirm_reset_settings(window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App)`: opens `TlDialog::confirm` (E16-A2) with window title "tasklens", text "Reset all settings to their defaults? Themes and history are kept.", buttons "Cancel" (Secondary, left) and "Reset" (Danger, right), destructive = true, so focus starts on Cancel (Enter there cancels; Reset needs Tab then Enter, or a click). Esc cancels. Modal to the window it was opened from.
- On Reset:
  1. Write first: `(cx.global::<AppEnv>().write_settings_now)(&Settings::default())`, the synchronous settings write tl-app provides (`AppEnv` (E16-A1, `crates/tl-ui/src/app.rs`, installed as a Global; R-171)). On `Err(_)`: Error toast "Failed to reset settings" and stop; nothing changes. On `Ok(())`: `TlSettings::update(cx, |s| s.settings = Settings::default())` (E20-A2): every settings section version bumps once, the persist callback runs (500 ms debounce), and changed `EngineSettings` go to `EngineClient::set_settings`.
  2. Re-apply the theme: `ThemeStore::activate(&Settings::default().theme.active, cx)` (E17-A1; "Default Dark").
  3. Scale and row height re-apply through the existing `TlSettings` observer for the `appearance` section (E20, UI-SHL-130); nothing extra here.
  4. Success toast "Settings reset to defaults".
- `UiState` (`state.toml`), `themes.json` and history are not touched.
- Shell confirmation texts owned by this file (later beads add their functions here): reset settings (this bead), delete theme (E21-013), skip password prompts (E21-042).
- String keys appended: `shell-confirm-title` "tasklens", `shell-confirm-reset-text` "Reset all settings to their defaults? Themes and history are kept.", `shell-confirm-reset-button` "Reset", `shell-confirm-cancel` "Cancel", `shell-toast-settings-reset` "Settings reset to defaults", `shell-toast-settings-reset-failed` "Failed to reset settings".
- Chain edit `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`: `pub mod confirm;`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** any tab **When** `ResetSettings` is dispatched **Then** a modal window titled "tasklens" opens with the text above and focus on "Cancel".
- **Given** the confirm is open **When** Esc is pressed **Then** it closes and no setting changes.
- **Given** the confirm is open with focus on Cancel **When** Enter is pressed **Then** it closes and no setting changes.
- **Given** `appearance.ui_scale_pct = 150` and saved column widths in `UiState` **When** the user clicks "Reset" **Then** `ui_scale_pct == 100`, the `UiState` columns and window size are unchanged, and the toast "Settings reset to defaults" shows.
- **Given** `theme.active = "Default Light"` **When** Reset runs **Then** `ThemeStore` activates "Default Dark".
- **Given** `processes.interval_ms = 2000` **When** Reset runs **Then** the fake engine receives `EngineSettings` with `interval_ms = 1000`.

- `reset_enter_on_cancel_does_nothing`.

Tests use `AppEnv::test()` with a closure that returns `Err` to cover it.

description:
## Context
Builds the frame of the "tasklens Theme Editor" window: name input, the 23-row slot list, footer buttons, the live-preview session with `ThemeStore`, Cancel and Done with name validation. The colour picker (E21-028) and the preview pane plus Random, Share and Import (E21-029) fill the middle and right columns. Sources: UI-SHL-081, APP-037, APP-035, APP-045, R-083, UI-FND-043.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/window/theme_editor.rs` (create; commit before building):
- Action `EditTheme { name: SharedString }` (namespace `tasklens`), handler registered in `pub fn init(cx)` (one `app.rs` line):
  - Built-in theme (`ThemeError::BuiltinCannotBeEdited`): Warning toast "Built-in themes cannot be edited. Copy it first." (R-209), no window.
  - Custom theme, editor open for the same theme: focus it.
  - Custom theme, editor open for another theme: cancel that preview, close that editor, open a new one.
  - Otherwise open a new editor.
- `pub struct ThemeEditor { token: Option<PreviewToken>, base_name: Arc<str>, selected_slot: ThemeSlot, name: Entity<InputState>, name_error: Option<SharedString>, /* E21-028: plane, hue, hex */ }` (E21-028 adds `plane: Option<Entity<ColorPlane>>`, `hue: Option<Entity<HueStrip>>`, `hex: Option<Entity<InputState>>` and their init as a chain edit to this file, R-262).
- Window: `TlSecondaryWindow::open`, title "tasklens Theme Editor", Tool window (Floating, not modal), default 820 × 560, minimum 720 × 480, `WindowKey::ThemeEditor`.
- On open: `ThemeStore::begin_preview(&def, cx)` (E17-A2 `preview.rs`), keep the token.
- Layout:
  - Top row (height 32, padding 16): label "Name:" and `TlTextInput` filling the width, max 64 characters, initial value the theme name. Each edit calls `ThemeStore::set_preview_name`.
  - Middle: slot list column (width 240) | picker column (flex, min 280; E21-028) | preview column (width 260; E21-029).
  - Slot list: 23 rows, 26 tall: the 22 slots in APP-035 order with their labels, then "Accent". Each row: swatch 14 × 14, radius `r_sm`, 1 px `divider` border; label `t_base`; hex value `t_xs` tabular `text_secondary` right-aligned ("#27292B"). Selected row fill `row_selected`, text `text_selected_primary`. Up and Down move the selection when the list has focus. Colours read from `ThemeStore::current()` (the preview).
  - Footer (height 48): left "Random", "Share", "Import" (E21-029 wires them; disabled until then), right "Cancel" (Secondary) and "Done" (Primary, Enter).
- Cancel, the close button, Esc and Ctrl+W: `ThemeStore::cancel_preview(token)`, then close.
- Done: validate the name (not empty after trim; not equal, case-insensitive, to another theme's name other than the one being edited). Valid: `ThemeStore::commit_preview(token)` (saves `themes.json` and activates), close, Success toast "Theme saved". Invalid: the name input gets a `status.danger` border, the text "Choose a name that no other theme uses" shows under it, and Done is disabled until the name is valid.
- Tab order: Name, slot list, plane, hue strip, hex input, Random, Share, Import, Cancel, Done.
- String keys appended (`shell-theme-editor-*`): title, "Name:", the 22 slot labels and "Accent" (APP-035 labels), "Random", "Share", "Import", "Cancel", "Done", "Choose a name that no other theme uses", `shell-toast-theme-saved` "Theme saved", `shell-toast-theme-copy-first` "Built-in themes cannot be edited. Copy it first.".
- Chain edit `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`: `pub mod theme_editor;`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** active built-in theme **When** `EditTheme` runs **Then** the Warning toast "Built-in themes cannot be edited. Copy it first." shows and no window opens.
- **Given** custom theme "Mine" **When** `EditTheme { name: "Mine" }` runs **Then** the editor opens and `ThemeStore.preview` is `Some`.
- **Given** the editor with a changed slot **When** Cancel is clicked **Then** `ThemeStore::current()` equals the theme active before opening and the window closes.
- **Given** a name equal to "dracula" (built-in "Dracula" exists) **When** typed **Then** Done is disabled and the error text shows.
- **Given** a valid new name "Mine 2" **When** Done is clicked **Then** the theme is saved under "Mine 2", activated, the window closes and the toast "Theme saved" shows.
- **Given** the editor open for "Mine" **When** `EditTheme { name: "Other" }` runs **Then** the first preview is cancelled, the first editor closes and a new editor for "Other" opens.
- **Given** the slot list focused on row 1 **When** Down is pressed **Then** row 2 is selected.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/theme_editor.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`, `crates/tl-ui/src/app.rs`, `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: chain edits.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell_windows.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell_windows.rs`:
- `editor_builtin_refused`.
- `editor_cancel_restores`: edit a slot, Cancel: `ThemeStore::current()` equals the theme active before opening.
- `editor_done_duplicate_name`: duplicate name disables Done.
- `editor_done_saves`.
- `editor_second_theme_replaces_first`.
- `editor_slot_list_keys`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: name validation text above; a failed `themes.json` save is reported by E17's store.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: Tab order as listed; Enter = Done when valid; Esc cancels.
- Performance: one preview application per frame (E17 coalesces); the slot list is 23 static rows.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- `PreviewToken`, `ThemeSlot`, `begin_preview`, `set_preview_slot`, `set_preview_name`, `commit_preview`, `cancel_preview`, `current()`: E17-A2 (`theme/preview.rs`, UI-FND-043).
- Large-file rule: commit `theme_editor.rs` before building.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E21-028 Theme Editor colour plane, hue strip, readouts and hex input
description:
## Context
Adds the colour picker to the Theme Editor: a saturation/value plane, a hue strip, RGB and HSV readouts and a hex input, all editing the selected slot of the live preview. tasklens draws its own plane because the kit `ColorPicker` is a popover with featured colours, not this layout. Sources: UI-SHL-081, APP-037, UI-FND-043.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/window/theme_editor.rs`:
- `pub struct ColorPlane { hue: f32, s: f32, v: f32, focus: FocusHandle }` (custom element, 200 × 200): painted with two `paint_quad` linear gradients (horizontal white to the pure hue, vertical transparent to black); cursor a 10 px ring at (s, 1 − v). Mouse down or drag sets s and v from the pointer position (clamped to 0..=1).
- `pub struct HueStrip { hue: f32, focus: FocusHandle }` (custom element, 16 × 200, right of the plane): vertical hue gradient 0 to 360; cursor a 2 px bar. Mouse down or drag sets hue.
- Readouts under the plane in `t_sm` tabular: "R %d G %d B %d" (0..=255) and "H %03d S %03d V %03d" (H 0..=360, S and V 0..=100).
- Hex input `TlTextInput` with placeholder "Enter a 6-digit hex color": accepts 6 hex digits with or without "#", applies on Enter or blur. Invalid text: `status.danger` border and the text "Enter a 6-digit hex color" below; the value is not applied.
- Selecting a slot in the list loads its colour into plane, strip, readouts and hex.
- Every change (drag, key, valid hex) calls `ThemeStore::set_preview_slot(token, selected_slot, hsla, cx)`; the store applies at most one change per frame.
- Keyboard: on the plane, arrows move S (Left/Right) or V (Up/Down) by 1 unit (Shift: 10); on the hue strip, Up and Down move hue by 1 degree (Shift: 10).
- String keys appended: `shell-theme-editor-hex-hint` "Enter a 6-digit hex color", readout patterns.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** slot "Title bar" = #27292B selected **When** the picker renders **Then** readouts show "R 39 G 41 B 43" and the hex input shows "#27292B".
- **Given** the hex input **When** "12345" is entered and Enter pressed **Then** nothing is applied and the error text shows.
- **Given** the hex input **When** "1E1F22" (no "#") is entered and Enter pressed **Then** the selected slot's preview colour becomes #1E1F22.
- **Given** the plane focused **When** Right is pressed **Then** S rises by 1 and one preview update is sent.
- **Given** the hue strip focused **When** Shift+Up is pressed **Then** hue changes by 10 degrees.
- **Given** a drag across the plane producing 30 pointer moves in one frame **When** the frame renders **Then** `ThemeStore` applied one preview change.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/theme_editor.rs`: add `ColorPlane`, `HueStrip`, readouts, hex input, and the `ThemeEditor` fields `plane: Option<Entity<ColorPlane>>`, `hue: Option<Entity<HueStrip>>`, `hex: Option<Entity<InputState>>` with their init at the `// E21-028` comment (R-262).
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: chain edit.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell_windows.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell_windows.rs`:
- `editor_readouts_for_slot`.
- `editor_hex_invalid`: "12345" does not apply.
- `editor_hex_without_hash_applies`.
- `editor_plane_keys`.
- `editor_hue_shift_step`.
- `editor_drag_coalesced`.
- Unit tests in `theme_editor.rs`: `hsv_rgb_roundtrip` (for all 8-bit RGB triples on a 17-step grid, RGB → HSV → RGB is exact).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: invalid hex text as above.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: plane and strip are focusable with the keyboard steps above; readouts are text.
- Performance: the plane paints 2 quads; drags cost one preview application per frame.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- gpui: `Window::paint_quad` (`gpui-pre-0.3.7/src/window.rs:4502`), `linear_gradient` (`src/color.rs:865`), under the B7 scratchpad `crates/`.

title: E21-030 Share Theme window
description:
## Context
Builds the "tasklens Share Theme" window: a read-only box with the theme's `TL1.` code and a Copy button. Opened from View > Theme > Share theme (E21-031) and from the Theme Editor (E21-029). Sources: UI-SHL-082, APP-038, APP-045, UI-FND-043 rule 8.
