title: E33-017 kglobalaccel.rs: Open with Ctrl+Esc through KDE kglobalaccel (verify U-16)
description:
## Context
Settings > Startup and window > "Open with Ctrl+Esc" makes KDE's Ctrl+Esc open tasklens instead of Plasma System Monitor; off restores the KDE default. There is no settings key: the check state is read from kglobalaccel. Whether `setForeignShortcutKeys` sticks for a `.desktop` launch component that is not running is unverified (U-16); the fallback edits `kglobalshortcutsrc`. Sources: APP-051, R-080, U-16.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/kglobalaccel.rs` (blocking zbus on the session bus, service `org.kde.kglobalaccel`, object `/kglobalaccel`):
```rust
pub fn is_enabled() -> Result<bool, KgaError>;     // tasklens _launch currently bound to Ctrl+Esc
pub fn set_enabled(on: bool) -> Result<Applied, KgaError>;
pub enum Applied { Live, NeedsRelogin }
```
- On: register component `io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.desktop` action `_launch` with key Ctrl+Esc and set `org.kde.plasma-systemmonitor.desktop` `_launch` to no key, using `setForeignShortcutKeys`.
- Off: set tasklens `_launch` to no key and restore `org.kde.plasma-systemmonitor.desktop` `_launch` to Ctrl+Esc.
- U-16 check inside `set_enabled`: after the call, read the shortcut back; if it did not stick, write `~/.config/kglobalshortcutsrc` group `[services][io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.desktop]` key `_launch=Ctrl+Esc` (or remove the key when off) and return `NeedsRelogin`; the UI then asks the user to log out and back in (R-080; the UI text is E21's).
- Errors: no bus or no kglobalaccel gives `KgaError::Unavailable`; the UI hides or disables the item.
- The Settings window reaches this module through `AppEnv.global_shortcut: Option<GlobalShortcutApi { get, set }>`, built by tl-app from this module; `None` outside KDE, and the settings row then shows "Not available" (R-153 item 3 as ADR-009 records it, R-171).
- The exact kglobalaccel method signatures (`setForeignShortcutKeys(as actionId, a(ai) keys)` in Plasma 6, key encoding of Ctrl+Esc as a Qt key code) must be read from the KDE `kglobalaccel` sources before coding; record the file and line in the commit message.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** Plasma 6 and the option turned on **When** Ctrl+Esc is pressed **Then** tasklens opens.
- **Given** the option turned off **When** Ctrl+Esc is pressed **Then** Plasma System Monitor opens.
- **Given** `setForeignShortcutKeys` did not stick **When** `set_enabled(true)` returns **Then** it is `NeedsRelogin` and `kglobalshortcutsrc` has the `_launch=Ctrl+Esc` line under `[services][io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.desktop]`.
- **Given** no kglobalaccel service **When** `is_enabled` runs **Then** it returns `Unavailable`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/kglobalaccel.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: `mod kglobalaccel;`.

## Tests
- `kglobalaccel.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`: `rc_fallback_writes_line` and `rc_fallback_removes_line` (pure function over the INI text; keeps every other line and group unchanged).
- Manual on Plasma 6, recorded for U-16 in the commit message: on, press Ctrl+Esc, off, press again; also with tasklens not running.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `Unavailable`; logged at `warn!`.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: Ctrl+Esc is a global shortcut; no in-app focus impact.
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Write `kglobalshortcutsrc` with `write_atomic` and keep the user's other shortcuts byte for byte.
Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...`. One commit for this bead, with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`. Read CLAUDE.md first. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E33-018 import_ts.rs: import TaskSlinger UserSettings.ini into settings
description:
## Context
Settings > Advanced > "Import from TaskSlinger…" lets the owner bring over TaskSlinger settings from `UserSettings.ini` (TaskSlinger runs under Wine). This bead is the settings half: parse the INI and map its keys onto `Settings` and `UiState` with the APP-032 origin table. The themes half (`themes.json`) is E17's. The INI comes from a file the user picks, so it is untrusted input. Sources: APP-034, APP-032 (origin table), ADR-011.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/import_ts.rs`:
```rust
pub struct ImportResult { pub settings: Settings, pub state: UiState, pub imported: usize, pub skipped: Vec<String> }
pub fn parse_ini(text: &str) -> Vec<(String /*section*/, String /*key*/, String /*value*/)>;
pub fn import(text: &str, base: (&Settings, &UiState)) -> ImportResult;
```
- `parse_ini`: `[Section]` headers, `key=value` lines, `;` and `#` comments, trims whitespace, accepts CRLF, ignores lines without `=`. Input above 1 MiB is rejected before parsing ("File is too large to be a TaskSlinger settings file"). Invalid UTF-8 is decoded with `from_utf8_lossy`.
- Mapping: one row per APP-032 origin with a TaskSlinger source, for example `DefaultTab` to `general.start_tab`, `UIScale` to `appearance.ui_scale_pct`, `RowHeightPct` to `appearance.row_height_pct`, `AnimationsEnabled` to `motion.animations`, `SmoothGraphs` to `motion.smooth_graphs`, `RefreshIntervalMs` to `processes.interval_ms`, `HighlightNewExitedProcesses` to `processes.highlight_new_exited`, `HideMicrosoftProcesses` to `processes.hide_system`, `CloseToTray`, `MinimizeToTray`, `AlwaysShowTrayIcon` to `tray.*`, `StartWithWindows` and `StartMinimized` to `startup.*`, `Window.Width`, `Window.Height`, `Window.Maximized` to state `[window]`, and every other TS row of the APP-032 table. The INI section names and value encodings (for example whether `DefaultTab` is a number or a name, and the `UIScale` format) are not in the docs. Owner decision D-018 (R-159 OI-13): import only keys whose value is a plain `true`/`false` or a decimal integer inside the target range; everything else goes to `skipped` until the owner supplies `UserSettings.ini`.
- An integer outside the target range is skipped, not clamped (D-018). A key that is unknown, unparseable or out of the mapping goes to `skipped` with its `section.key` name.
- `imported` counts mapped keys. The UI toast "Imported N settings and M themes" (APP-034) is built by the caller with N = `imported` and M from the theme half.
- The Settings window calls `AppEnv.import_taskslinger` (no path argument; tl-app finds the TaskSlinger files and returns `ImportSummary`), R-153 item 3 as ADR-009 records it, R-171. Where tl-app looks for `UserSettings.ini` is not settled; this bead exposes `import(text, base)` and the `AppEnv` builder supplies the text.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** an INI with `AnimationsEnabled=false` **When** imported **Then** `motion.animations == false` and `imported == 1`.
- **Given** `RefreshIntervalMs=50` (below the 250 minimum) **When** imported **Then** it is in `skipped` and `processes.interval_ms` keeps its value; `RefreshIntervalMs=1000` gives `processes.interval_ms == 1000`.
- **Given** `Window.X=100` **When** imported **Then** it is in `skipped` (position is not restored, APP-032).
- **Given** a 2 MiB file **When** imported **Then** it is rejected with "File is too large to be a TaskSlinger settings file".
- **Given** binary garbage **When** imported **Then** the result has `imported == 0` and no panic.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/import_ts.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: `mod import_ts;`.

## Tests
- `import_ts.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`: `parse_sections_and_comments`, `crlf_accepted`, `bool_key_mapped`, `int_key_in_range`, `int_key_out_of_range_skipped`, `position_skipped`, `too_large_rejected`, plus a proptest `never_panics_on_arbitrary_bytes` (proptest is a workspace dev-dependency; add it to tl-app `[dev-dependencies]`).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the size error text above.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: do not log INI values; log only skipped key names at `debug!`.

## Notes
- Security: untrusted input; the size cap and the fuzz-style proptest are the regression tests.
Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...`. One commit for this bead, with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`. Read CLAUDE.md first. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
close_reason: import_ts.rs: parse_ini, import, read_ini/decode_ini with 1 MiB cap, D-018 bool and in-range int rows only; 12 tests pass. Commits 8361a3c da42146 66f0f74

title: E33-019 --app-id: separate instance with its own directories, app_id and bus name
description:
## Context
`--app-id <reverse-dns id>` runs a separate instance with its own config, state, cache and runtime directories, Wayland `app_id` and bus name, for development builds next to an installed tasklens (APP-052, taken from Mission Center). It replaces TaskSlinger's `--internal-skip-single-instance` (APP-050). Sources: APP-052, APP-050, ADR-010 (Single instance), ADR-011 (Paths).

## Deliverable
Changes to `crates/tl-app/src/paths.rs`, `single_instance.rs` and `main.rs`:
- Validation: the id must match `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*)+$` and be at most 255 bytes (D-Bus well-known name rules); otherwise print "Invalid --app-id: <id>" to stderr and exit 2.
- Single instance: the bus name is the given id instead of `io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens`, and the object path is the id with `.` replaced by `/` and a leading `/`.
- Paths (owner decision D-016, R-159 OI-6): the id replaces the `tasklens` directory component in all four XDG roots: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/<id>/`, `$XDG_STATE_HOME/<id>/`, `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/<id>/`, `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/<id>/`. History, logs, crash reports, run history and the icon cache follow, because they live under those roots. The Wayland `app_id` of every window is the id.
- Without `--app-id`, nothing changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `--app-id io.github.oysteinkrog.TasklensDev` **When** the installed tasklens is running **Then** the dev build starts its own window instead of forwarding.
- **Given** `--app-id bad id` **When** parsed **Then** stderr has "Invalid --app-id: bad id" and the exit code is 2.
- **Given** `--app-id io.example.Dev` **When** the object path is built **Then** it is `/io/example/Dev`.
- **Given** `--app-id io.example.Dev` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/c`, `XDG_STATE_HOME=/s`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME=/k`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/r` **When** `Paths` is built **Then** the four roots are `/c/io.example.Dev`, `/s/io.example.Dev`, `/k/io.example.Dev`, `/r/io.example.Dev`, and the history directory is `/s/io.example.Dev/history`.
- **Given** `--app-id io.example.Dev` **When** the main window opens **Then** its Wayland `app_id` is `io.example.Dev`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/paths.rs`, `crates/tl-app/src/single_instance.rs`, `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`.

## Tests
- `single_instance.rs` tests: `app_id_valid`, `app_id_invalid`, `object_path_from_id`.
- `tests/paths.rs::app_id_dirs`; the Wayland `app_id` check is a manual step in the commit body.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the invalid id text above.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- E33-OI-6 is settled by the owner (D-016). The window `app_id` is set where E33-A1 passes it to tl-ui; if tl-ui has no field for it, stop and report.
Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...`. One commit for this bead, with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`. Read CLAUDE.md first. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
close_reason: App id option: validated (exit 2 with 'Invalid --app-id: <id>'), replaces tasklens under config/state/cache/runtime roots, is the bus name; object path derived from it. Commits cfb9e79, 92eadf3. Wayland app_id criterion not done: tl-ui has no field, lead is filing a tl-ui bead.

title: Startup: cut first_frame_ms from 900 ms toward the 200 ms warm gate
description:
Files: crates/tl-app/src/main.rs, crates/tl-ui/src/app.rs, crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs, docs/spike/phase0-results.md.
Why: cr0.1 (cb51c7b, d25c86a) measured first_frame_ms=900 on the first release start on the owner desktop (KDE Wayland). ADR-014 gates: warm <= 200 ms median, cold <= 500 ms. About 450 ms was the wgpu GPU adapter probe. The log also shows lookups for gpui's default fonts IBM Plex Sans and Lilex, which we do not bundle, and no monospace match.
Deliverable: (1) Add tracing spans with timings for each startup step (process start, engine start, settings, font load, adapter, window open, first frame) under target tasklens::perf. (2) Measure 5 warm starts and record the step breakdown in docs/spike/phase0-results.md. (3) Cut what tasklens controls: start the engine and load settings in parallel with window creation where that is safe; register the bundled Noto faces as the default and monospace fonts so gpui does not search for IBM Plex Sans or Lilex; do no blocking I/O before the window opens. (4) If the wgpu adapter probe alone is over budget, record that as a finding with numbers and do not patch gpui.
AC: the per-step timing log exists; warm median and per-step numbers are recorded; the font warnings are gone; first_frame_ms is lower than before, with numbers. Start the binary only as your own background process and stop it only by its own PID. clippy clean for tl-app and tl-ui.
close_reason: tasklens::perf step timing (41b0299); logo SVG text as outlines, font warnings gone (9515dab); results in docs/spike/phase0-results.md (f3007b8). Warm median first_frame_ms 385 -> 365, cold 2660 -> 1060, load 25-30. gpui adapter probe about 265 ms alone, over the 200 ms gate; recorded as a finding.

title: rendering.gpu = software: verify that the GL backend also uses software rendering
description:
Files: crates/tl-app/src/rendering_env.rs, crates/tl-app/src/main.rs (only if a new env var must be set), docs/spike/phase0-results.md.
Why: cr0.19 (acf9d32, 9193258) found from the gpui-pre-wgpu 0.3.7 source that gpui never reads WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME and always enables the GL backend. VK_ICD_FILENAMES limits Vulkan to lavapipe, but a GL/EGL adapter for the real GPU may still be listed and picked, so "software" may not force software rendering. Not tested on hardware.
Deliverable: run the release binary once with rendering.gpu = "software" (scratch XDG_CONFIG_HOME with that setting) and read which adapter gpui picked from its log. If the real GPU is still used, also set LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1 (and, if needed, MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE=llvmpipe) in env_for for "software", and run again. Record both runs in docs/spike/phase0-results.md. Do not patch gpui.

title: Wire the TaskSlinger settings import: file path from the portal chooser, apply and persist
description:
Files: crates/tl-app/src/main.rs, crates/tl-app/src/import_ts.rs, crates/tl-ui/src/app.rs (only the import_taskslinger callback type), crates/tl-app/tests/settings_store.rs.
Why: cr0.21 (8361a3c, da42146, 66f0f74) built import_ts.rs, but main.rs still passes a stub `import_taskslinger: Arc::new(|| Ok(ImportSummary::default()))`. APP-034 says Settings > Advanced > "Import from TaskSlinger…" opens a portal file chooser for UserSettings.ini, maps keys with the APP-032 table and shows "Imported N settings and M themes".
Leader decisions: the callback takes the path the user picked (Fn(&Path) -> Result<ImportSummary, String>); tl-ui owns the portal chooser (its own bead), tl-app does read_ini, import onto the current Settings, applies the result through the same path as a settings change (so the UI and the store both update), and persists. Add UTF-16 detection by BOM (FF FE or FE FF) in decode_ini, because TaskSlinger is a Windows program; without a BOM keep the lossy UTF-8 read. Themes import stays with the themes.json bead (lgw).
AC: a test feeds a fixture INI path through the callback and checks the store saved the imported values; a UTF-16LE fixture with BOM imports the same keys as the UTF-8 one; a missing or oversize file returns the error text and changes nothing. clippy clean for tl-app and tl-ui.

title: Exit with an error when the main window cannot open
description:
Files: crates/tl-app/src/main.rs, crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs (only the open-failure path), crates/tl-app/tests/ (new test if a seam exists).
Why: cr0.25 (5bde23c) found that when no GPU adapter passes the surface test, tasklens logs "main window did not open" and keeps running with no window and no tray entry the user can use. The process then lingers until killed.

Do not retry with other adapters (that is gpui's job). A later failure to reopen the window after it was closed to the tray keeps today's behaviour plus the log line.

title: E33-A3 Packaging
description:
## Context
Anchor bead E33-A3. An Arch `PKGBUILD` builds the workspace in release mode and installs the binaries, the desktop file and the app icon to the paths in table (c). Later phases add their own install lines through E33 beads (E33-015 for P3). `tasklens --version` proves the installed binary runs. Sources: table (c) (Binaries and scripts, Identity), ADR-002 (Build and run packages, profiles, release without `bench`), APP-050 (pacman installs binary, desktop file, icon, policy), APP-052 (`--version`).

## Deliverable
`packaging/PKGBUILD`:
- `pkgname=tasklens`, `arch=('x86_64')`.
- `makedepends=('base-devel' 'clang' 'pkgconf' 'rustup')`, with the toolchain from `rust-toolchain.toml` (E02).
- `depends=('wayland' 'libxkbcommon' 'libxkbcommon-x11' 'libxcb' 'fontconfig' 'vulkan-icd-loader')` (ADR-002). `nvidia-utils` goes in `optdepends=('nvidia-utils: NVIDIA GPU monitoring')` because tl-gpu-probe loads NVML at run time and handles its absence (ADR-007; R-159 OI-10).
- `build()`: `cargo build --release --locked --workspace` from the repo root; no `--features bench` (ADR-002).
- `check()`: `cargo test --release --locked --workspace` (no `--ignored`).
- `package()` installs:
  - `target/release/tasklens` to `$pkgdir/usr/bin/tasklens`, mode 0755.
  - `target/release/tl-gpu-probe` to `$pkgdir/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-gpu-probe`, mode 0755.
  - `packaging/io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.desktop` to `$pkgdir/usr/share/applications/io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.desktop`, mode 0644.
  - `assets/icons/tasklens.svg` (E15) to `$pkgdir/usr/share/icons/hicolor/scalable/apps/io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.svg`, mode 0644 (icon path settled, R-159 OI-9).
- `pkgver=0.1.0`, `pkgrel=1`, a local source (`source=()`, build from `$startdir/..`, the local checkout) (R-159 OI-10), `license=('MIT')` (owner decision D-017), `pkgdesc='Task manager for Linux'` (the clap `about` line, R-159 OI-7). `url` is left out.
  - `package()` also installs the repo's `LICENSE` file to `$pkgdir/usr/share/licenses/tasklens/LICENSE`, mode 0644 (Arch rule for MIT). The `LICENSE` file is written by E02-011 (tasklens-v9m.13, R-258), which this bead depends on; if it is still missing, stop and report.
- Release builds use the workspace `release` profile unchanged (`panic = "unwind"`, `lto = "fat"`, `debug = "line-tables-only"`, `strip = "none"`); set `options=('!strip')` so makepkg does not strip the line tables needed for crash backtraces.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a clean checkout **When** `makepkg -f` runs in `packaging/` **Then** a package builds and `namcap` reports no errors.
- **Given** the installed package **When** `tasklens --version` runs **Then** it prints `tasklens 0.1.0` and exits 0.
- **Given** the installed package **When** the file list is checked **Then** it contains exactly `/usr/bin/tasklens`, `/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-gpu-probe`, the desktop file, the icon and `/usr/share/licenses/tasklens/LICENSE`.

title: E33-002 paths.rs: XDG path resolution with fallbacks and 0700/0600 modes
description:
## Context
Every tasklens file lives under one of three XDG roots (ADR-011, table (c)). `paths.rs` resolves them by hand (no `directories` crate, ADR-002) and creates directories with mode 0700. Logging, crash reports, the settings store and the autostart writer all take their paths from here. Sources: ADR-011 (paths table), table (c) XDG paths, R-018, APP-033.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/paths.rs`:
```rust
pub struct Paths {
    pub config_dir: PathBuf,   // $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tasklens
    pub state_dir: PathBuf,    // $XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens
    pub cache_dir: PathBuf,    // $XDG_CACHE_HOME/tasklens
    pub home: PathBuf,
}
impl Paths {
    pub fn from_env() -> anyhow::Result<Paths>;          // reads the process environment
    pub fn from_vars(get: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<OsString>) -> anyhow::Result<Paths>; // testable core
    pub fn settings_file(&self) -> PathBuf;   // config_dir/settings.toml
    pub fn themes_file(&self) -> PathBuf;     // config_dir/themes.json
    pub fn state_file(&self) -> PathBuf;      // state_dir/state.toml
    pub fn logs_dir(&self) -> PathBuf;        // state_dir/logs
    pub fn crash_dir(&self) -> PathBuf;       // state_dir/crash
    pub fn history_dir(&self) -> PathBuf;     // state_dir/history
    pub fn dumps_dir(&self) -> PathBuf;       // state_dir/dumps
    pub fn run_history_file(&self) -> PathBuf;// state_dir/run-history.json
    pub fn icon_cache_file(&self) -> PathBuf; // cache_dir/icons.toml
    pub fn autostart_file(&self) -> PathBuf;  // $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/autostart/io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.desktop
}
pub fn ensure_dir(path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<()>; // create_dir_all, then chmod 0700 on each directory it created
pub const FILE_MODE: u32 = 0o600;
pub const DIR_MODE: u32 = 0o700;
```
Rules (ADR-011): for each of `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, a value that is unset, empty or not absolute falls back to `$HOME/.config`, `$HOME/.local/state`, `$HOME/.cache`. `HOME` unset, empty or not absolute is an error: "HOME is not set to an absolute path". `autostart_file` uses the same resolved `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` root (not the `tasklens` subdirectory). `ensure_dir` does not change the mode of a directory that already existed.
Add `mod paths;` to `main.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/x/cfg` **When** `from_vars` runs **Then** `settings_file()` is `/x/cfg/tasklens/settings.toml`.
- **Given** `XDG_STATE_HOME` unset and `HOME=/home/u` **When** `from_vars` runs **Then** `state_file()` is `/home/u/.local/state/tasklens/state.toml`.
- **Given** `XDG_CACHE_HOME=""` **When** `from_vars` runs **Then** `icon_cache_file()` is `$HOME/.cache/tasklens/icons.toml`.
- **Given** `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=relative/dir` **When** `from_vars` runs **Then** the default `$HOME/.config` is used.
- **Given** `HOME` unset **When** `from_vars` runs **Then** it returns the error "HOME is not set to an absolute path".
- **Given** a missing nested directory **When** `ensure_dir` runs **Then** every created directory has mode 0700.
- **Given** an existing directory with mode 0755 **When** `ensure_dir` runs **Then** its mode stays 0755.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/paths.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: add `mod paths;`.
- `crates/tl-app/tests/paths.rs`: create. Because tl-app is a binary crate, the test file includes the module with `#[path = "../src/paths.rs"] mod paths;`.

## Tests
- `tests/paths.rs::config_home_set`, `state_home_default`, `cache_home_empty_falls_back`, `relative_xdg_ignored`, `home_missing_is_error`, `autostart_path`, `ensure_dir_creates_0700` (in a `tempfile::TempDir`), `ensure_dir_keeps_existing_mode`, `all_file_names` (asserts every getter's file name: `settings.toml`, `themes.json`, `state.toml`, `logs`, `crash`, `history`, `dumps`, `run-history.json`, `icons.toml`, `io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.desktop`).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: only the HOME error above; I/O errors from `ensure_dir` are returned as is.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: called once at start; no caching needed.
- Privacy: paths are not logged above `debug`.

## Notes
- `--app-id` (P4) may later change the `tasklens` subdirectory name; that is E33-019 and open item E33-OI-6. Do not add it here.
- Use `std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt` for modes (no `unsafe`).
Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...`. One commit for this bead, with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`. Read CLAUDE.md first. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

description:
## Context
All command-line arguments are declared once, up front, in `args.rs` (00-epics section 2). Later beads add only the `main.rs` arms that act on them (E01 for `--bench` and `--gallery`, E32 for `--low-memory` and `--watch-memory`). Sources: APP-052, table (c) argument list, R-138 item 15 (`--gallery`), UI-SHL-110 step 2, APP-011 (forwarded arguments).

`crates/tl-app/src/args.rs` with clap derive (see open item E33-OI-2 for the crate):
```rust
#[derive(clap::Parser, Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
#[command(name = "tasklens", version, about = "Task manager for Linux")]
pub struct Args {
    #[arg(long)] pub start_minimized: bool,
    #[arg(long)] pub low_memory: bool,
    #[arg(long)] pub watch_memory: bool,
    #[arg(long, value_enum)] pub tab: Option<TabArg>,
    #[arg(long, value_name = "PID")] pub select_pid: Option<u32>,

    #[arg(long)] pub force_full_memory_mode: bool,

    #[cfg(feature = "bench")] #[arg(long, requires = "bench", value_name = "SECONDS")] pub duration: Option<u32>,
    #[cfg(feature = "bench")] #[arg(long, requires = "bench", value_name = "SECONDS")] pub warmup: Option<u32>,

    #[cfg(feature = "bench")] #[arg(long, conflicts_with = "bench")] pub gallery: bool,
}
#[derive(clap::ValueEnum, Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum TabArg { Processes, Performance, Services, Startup, Connections, Information }
#[cfg(feature = "bench")]
#[derive(clap::ValueEnum, Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BenchScene { PerfCpu, Table2000, Bridge, Static, HistoryScrub }  // CLI names perf-cpu, table-2000, bridge, static, history-scrub
impl TabArg { pub fn to_model(self) -> tl_model::command::Tab; }   // Tab is the enum used by AppRequest::SelectTab (R-136)

```

- `--tab` values are exactly `processes`, `performance`, `services`, `startup`, `connections`, `information`.
- Defaults for `--duration`, `--warmup` and the `--json` form belong to the E01 bead that handles `--bench` (ADR-014); this bead only declares them as optional.
- Without the `bench` feature, `--bench` and `--gallery` are unknown arguments (exit 2).
- Help text per argument (clap `help`): `--start-minimized` "Start hidden to the tray, or minimized when the tray is off"; `--low-memory` "Open the low-memory rescue window"; `--watch-memory` "Run the low-memory watcher (no window)"; `--tab` "Open on this tab"; `--select-pid` "Open Processes and select this process"; `--debug` "Show the Debug menu"; `--force-full-memory-mode` "Test option: with --low-memory, run the full engine" (R-152 OI-13, D-015); `--app-id` "Run a separate instance with its own settings, state, cache and bus name (development builds)" (R-159 OI-6, D-016); `--bench` "Run a benchmark scene"; `--gallery` "Open the component gallery". title: E33-004 logging.rs: tracing subscriber, daily log file, 200-line ring
description:
## Context
Logging is set up in `main` right after the panic hook (UI-SHL-110 step 1). It follows ADR-015 exactly: `tracing-subscriber` with `EnvFilter` from `TASKLENS_LOG`, a daily rotating file kept 7 days, stderr only when it is a terminal. The crash report needs the last 200 log lines, so the subscriber also keeps them in memory. Sources: ADR-015 (Logging), APP-054, R-048, R-049.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/logging.rs`:
```rust
pub const DEFAULT_FILTER: &str = "info,wgpu=warn,wgpu_core=warn,wgpu_hal=warn,naga=warn,zbus=warn";
pub const RING_LINES: usize = 200;
pub struct LogGuard { _file: tracing_appender::non_blocking::WorkerGuard }  // held in main, dropped last
#[derive(Clone)] pub struct RecentLines(Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<String>>>);
impl RecentLines { pub fn snapshot(&self) -> Vec<String>; }   // oldest first, at most 200
pub fn init(logs_dir: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<(LogGuard, RecentLines)>;
pub fn build_filter(var: Option<&str>) -> EnvFilter;  // TASKLENS_LOG value or DEFAULT_FILTER
```
- Filter: `TASKLENS_LOG` if set and parseable, else `DEFAULT_FILTER`. An unparseable `TASKLENS_LOG` falls back to the default and logs one `warn!` "TASKLENS_LOG is invalid; using the default filter". `RUST_LOG` is never read (do not call `EnvFilter::from_default_env`).
- File output: `tracing_appender::rolling::RollingFileAppender::builder().rotation(Rotation::DAILY).filename_prefix("tasklens").filename_suffix("log").max_log_files(7).build(logs_dir)`, wrapped in `tracing_appender::non_blocking`. `logs_dir` is created with `paths::ensure_dir` (0700). Files are created by the appender; after `init`, chmod the current file to 0600 if it exists.
- stderr output: a second `fmt` layer, added only when `std::io::IsTerminal::is_terminal(&std::io::stderr())` is true, with ANSI colours.
- Ring layer: a `tracing_subscriber::Layer` that formats each event the same way as the file layer (one line, no ANSI) and pushes it into `RecentLines`, dropping the oldest beyond 200. It sees only events that passed the filter.
- If `logs_dir` cannot be created, logging continues to stderr and the ring only, and `init` logs `warn!` "Log folder is not writable; logging to stderr only". `init` fails only if a global subscriber was already set.
- Targets used across tasklens (documented in a module comment, not enforced here): `tasklens::engine`, `tasklens::source::<name>`, `tasklens::action`, `tasklens::ui`, `tasklens::frame`, `tasklens::probe`, `tasklens::perf`.
Add `mod logging;` to `main.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `TASKLENS_LOG` unset **When** `build_filter(None)` runs **Then** the filter string equals `DEFAULT_FILTER`.
- **Given** `TASKLENS_LOG=debug` **When** `build_filter(Some("debug"))` runs **Then** debug events pass.
- **Given** `RUST_LOG=trace` and `TASKLENS_LOG` unset **When** `init` runs **Then** trace events are filtered out.
- **Given** 250 events logged **When** `snapshot()` is read **Then** it holds 200 lines, the oldest being event 51.
- **Given** a temp logs dir **When** one event is logged and the guard dropped **Then** a file named `tasklens.<yyyy-mm-dd>.log` exists in it and contains the event.
- **Given** a logs dir path that cannot be created **When** `init` runs **Then** it returns `Ok` and later events still reach the ring.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/logging.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: add `mod logging;`.

## Tests
- `logging.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`: `default_filter_string`, `tasklens_log_used`, `invalid_tasklens_log_falls_back`, `ring_keeps_last_200` (uses the ring layer with a local subscriber via `tracing::subscriber::with_default`), `ring_skips_filtered_events`, `file_written_with_prefix_and_suffix` (tempfile dir, local subscriber, drop guard, assert one file whose name starts with `tasklens.` and ends with `.log`).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: as above; never panics.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: the ring layer formats into a reused `String` per event and allocates one `String` per kept line; no logging in per-frame or per-process loops above `trace` (ADR-015) is a rule for callers.
- Privacy: ADR-015 never-logged list applies to every caller: command lines, environment, working directories, open file paths, executable paths of other users' processes, window titles, user names other than the current user. This module adds no fields of its own.

## Notes
- Tests that install a global subscriber must not run in the same process as others; use `with_default` for unit tests.
Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...`. One commit for this bead, with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`. Read CLAUDE.md first. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
close_reason: logging.rs: EnvFilter from TASKLENS_LOG, daily file kept 7 days (0600), stderr when a terminal, 200-line ring; mod line in main.rs. Commits cace9dc, 8ca8732

title: E33-005 crash.rs: panic hook writes crash-<unix seconds>.txt, keeps newest 20
description:
## Context
The panic hook is the first thing `main` installs (UI-SHL-110 step 1). It writes one report file per panic with version, thread, message, location, backtrace and the last 200 log lines, then calls the default hook (ADR-015, R-049). The report never contains process metadata or settings. Sources: ADR-015 (Crash handling), APP-055, R-049, UI-SHL-093 (report files read later by the Crash Report window).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/crash.rs`:
```rust
pub const KEEP_REPORTS: usize = 20;
pub fn install_hook(crash_dir: PathBuf, recent: Arc<OnceLock<RecentLines>>, on_main_thread_panic: fn());
pub fn write_report(crash_dir: &Path, info: &PanicHookInfo<'_>, recent: &[String], now_unix: u64) -> io::Result<PathBuf>;
pub fn format_report(info_text: &ReportFields, recent: &[String]) -> String;
pub struct ReportFields<'a> { pub version: &'a str, pub git_sha: &'a str, pub thread: &'a str, pub message: &'a str, pub location: &'a str, pub backtrace: &'a str }
pub fn prune(crash_dir: &Path) -> io::Result<()>;   // keep the newest 20 crash-*.txt by the number in the name; remove older ones and their crash-<t>.seen markers
```
- File: `<crash_dir>/crash-<unix seconds>.txt`, mode 0600, directory created 0700 with `paths::ensure_dir`. If that name exists (two panics in one second), append `-1`, `-2` before `.txt`.
- Content, in this order, one field per line, then sections:
  ```
  tasklens <CARGO_PKG_VERSION> (<TASKLENS_GIT_SHA>)
  thread: <name or "unnamed">
  message: <panic payload as &str or String, else "Box<dyn Any>">
  location: <file>:<line>:<column>

  backtrace:
  <std::backtrace::Backtrace::force_capture()>

  last log lines:
  <up to 200 lines, oldest first>
  ```
- No process metadata, no settings contents, no command lines or environment (ADR-015).
- `install_hook` takes the previous hook with `std::panic::take_hook()`, installs a new one that writes the report (errors are ignored), calls `prune`, then, if the panicking thread is the main thread (`std::thread::current().name() == Some("main")`), calls `on_main_thread_panic`, and finally calls the previous hook. The hook must not panic; wrap the body in `std::panic::catch_unwind` with `AssertUnwindSafe`.
- `recent` is a `OnceLock` because the hook is installed before logging; it is filled right after `logging::init`. Before that, the "last log lines" section is empty.
- `on_main_thread_panic` is the desktop notification hook added by E33-012; in this bead `main.rs` passes a no-op `fn noop() {}`.
Add `mod crash;` to `main.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a panic with message "boom" on a thread named "worker" **When** the hook runs **Then** a file `crash-<t>.txt` exists with lines `thread: worker` and `message: boom` and a `backtrace:` section.
- **Given** 3 recent log lines **When** a report is written **Then** the `last log lines:` section holds those 3 lines in order.
- **Given** 25 report files with different times and 25 `.seen` markers **When** `prune` runs **Then** the 20 newest reports remain and the 5 oldest reports and their `.seen` markers are gone.
- **Given** two reports in the same second **When** both are written **Then** the second is named `crash-<t>-1.txt`.
- **Given** an unwritable crash dir **When** the hook runs **Then** the default hook still runs and the process behaves as without the hook.

title: E33-006 settings_store.rs: load settings.toml and state.toml (corrupt, newer, clamp)
description:
## Context
UI-SHL-110 step 5 loads `settings.toml` and `state.toml` before the engine starts. ADR-011 fixes the load steps for each file: missing file gives defaults, a parse error renames the file and warns, a missing `schema_version` counts as 1, a lower one migrates, a higher one is read-only, out-of-range values clamp, unknown keys are dropped. The toasts are queued and shown after the first frame (UI-SHL-110 step 11). Sources: ADR-011 (Load), APP-033, R-018, canonical table (a), UI-SHL-110 steps 5 and 11.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/settings_store.rs` (load half; E33-008 adds the save half):
```rust
pub enum FileKind { Settings, State }
pub struct Loaded<T> { pub value: T, pub read_only: bool, pub notices: Vec<LoadNotice> }
pub enum LoadNotice {
    Corrupt { kept_as: String },  // file name only, e.g. "settings.toml.corrupt-1759500000"
    Newer,
}
impl LoadNotice { pub fn toast_text(&self) -> String; }
pub fn load_settings(path: &Path, now_unix: u64) -> Loaded<tl_model::settings::Settings>;
pub fn load_state(path: &Path, now_unix: u64) -> Loaded<tl_model::settings::UiState>;
fn load_table(path: &Path, now_unix: u64) -> LoadStep;  // shared core
```
Steps, the same for each file (ADR-011):
1. File missing (`ErrorKind::NotFound`): defaults, `read_only = false`, no notice, nothing written.
2. Read and parse to `toml::Table`. Read or parse error: rename the file to `<name>.corrupt-<unix seconds>` in the same directory (for example `settings.toml.corrupt-1759500000`), use defaults, push `LoadNotice::Corrupt { kept_as }`. Toast text: `Settings file was unreadable and has been reset. The old file was kept as {name}` with `{name}` replaced by `kept_as`. If the rename fails, log `warn!` and still use defaults; the notice is still pushed with the intended name.
3. `schema_version` missing: treat as 1. Lower than `tl_model::settings::SCHEMA_VERSION`: call `migrations::migrate(&mut table, from)` (E33-007), then deserialize. Higher: deserialize what is understood, `read_only = true`, push `LoadNotice::Newer` with toast text `Settings were written by a newer tasklens; changes will not be saved`.
4. Deserialize with `toml::Table::try_into::<T>()`; all structs are `#[serde(default)]` (E03), so missing keys take defaults. A type error in one value must not reset the whole file: deserialize section by section (each top-level table into its section struct), and a section that fails takes its default with a `warn!` naming the section.
5. Clamp out-of-range values with the clamp function E03-A2 provides on `Settings` and `UiState` (ranges from canonical table (a)); each clamped key is logged at `info!` with key name, old and new value.
6. Unknown keys are ignored (serde default behaviour, no `deny_unknown_fields`); they are not preserved on save. Unknown column ids are dropped with a log line by the `ColumnId::from_str` path in E03; this module only keeps the order of the known ones.
- The two files have independent `read_only` flags.
- Logs never include file contents.
Add `mod settings_store;` to `main.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** no settings file **When** `load_settings` runs **Then** the value equals `Settings::default()`, there are no notices and no file is created.
- **Given** a file with `[general` (broken TOML) **When** `load_settings` runs at unix time 1759500000 **Then** the file is renamed to `settings.toml.corrupt-1759500000`, defaults load and the notice text is "Settings file was unreadable and has been reset. The old file was kept as settings.toml.corrupt-1759500000".
- **Given** a file without `schema_version` and `[processes] interval_ms = 2000` **When** loaded **Then** `interval_ms == 2000`.
- **Given** `schema_version = 2` (newer) **When** loaded **Then** `read_only == true`, known keys are read and the notice text is "Settings were written by a newer tasklens; changes will not be saved".
- **Given** `[appearance] ui_scale_pct = 500` **When** loaded **Then** the value is 200 and an info line names `appearance.ui_scale_pct`.
- **Given** `[processes] interval_ms = "fast"` **When** loaded **Then** the `processes` section takes its defaults and the other sections keep their file values.
- **Given** an unknown key `[general] colour = 3` **When** loaded **Then** loading succeeds.
- **Given** `state.toml` with `[columns.processes] visible = ["name", "bogus", "pid"]` **When** loaded **Then** visible is `["name", "pid"]`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/settings_store.rs`: create (load half).
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: add `mod settings_store;`.
- `crates/tl-app/tests/settings_store.rs`: create; includes the modules with `#[path]` as in `tests/paths.rs`.

## Tests
`tests/settings_store.rs` (each with `tempfile::TempDir`, for both `settings.toml` and `state.toml` where the case applies):
- `missing_file_defaults_no_write`
- `corrupt_file_renamed` (checks the new name, defaults, notice text)
- `v0_without_version_loaded_as_v1`
- `newer_version_read_only`
- `out_of_range_clamped`
- `bad_section_keeps_others`
- `unknown_keys_ignored`
- `unknown_column_id_dropped_order_kept`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the two toast texts above, exact. They are queued and shown after the first frame by tl-ui (UI-SHL-110 step 11), not by this module.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: part of the 200 ms warm first-frame budget; parse each file once.
- Privacy: never log file contents.

## Notes
- If E03 does not expose a clamp function, stop and ask the leader; do not write ranges here.

description:
## Context

This bead assembles `PerformancePage::render`: the sidebar, the splitter, the page column, the hidden-sidebar state, `nav_width` persistence, the `MainWindow` page arm, and the P0 tests. The resize handle: the kit's 1 px `divider` line with 4 px hit padding each side and the `col-resize` cursor while dragging (kit default appearance).
- Actions on the page root: `PerfToggleSidebar` (flips `sidebar_visible`; animates the panel width 252 → 0 over `m_base` `ease_out_cubic` with `with_animation`, instant under reduced motion or `motion.animations = false`; not persisted), `PerfJumpToType` (selects the first visible card of that kind; E24-017 adds the menu), `PerfSelectDevice` forwarded to the sidebar.

A build without `bench` has no such field. Also put `#[cfg(feature = "bench")]` on the test `ui_cpu_page.rs::bench_show_both_layout`.

title: E24: CPU Details grid, P1 rows 1 to 9 and 11 to 14 (pages/performance/cpu_details.rs)
description:
## Context
The CPU page's Details grid shows 12 live values at 1 Hz and the static core counts and caches. This bead writes the P1 rows with their exact labels, formats and tooltips; the P2 rows are E24-020. Sources: PERF-033 to PERF-036, PERF-039, PERF-040, UI-PRF-024 (row table), table (d), ADR-014 fixture ("a stats block with 12 values updated at 1 Hz").

```rust
pub fn update_static(model: &mut KeyValueModel, sys: &SystemSnapshot, catalog: &DeviceCatalog) -> bool;  // rows 13, 14, 19 to 21
```

P1 rows, labels, formats, tooltips (grid order; values are examples):

| # | Label | Value | Tooltip and rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Utilization` | `18.6%` | |
| 2 | `Kernel time` | `2.3%` | |
| 3 | `Speed` | `4631 MHz` | tooltip `Fastest core: 5050 MHz`; BogoMIPS-only source: value `4200 MHz (?)`, tooltip `Reported by the kernel at boot; the current clock is not available` |
| 4 | `Processes` | `295` | count format |
| 5 | `Threads` | `5 596` | thin-space grouping |
| 6 | `Handles` | `253 248` | tooltip `Open file descriptors, system-wide` |

| 8 | `Base speed` | `4200 MHz` | |
| 9 | `Sockets` | `1` | |
| 11 | `Temperature` | `52 °C` | tooltip lists the chip's sensors `Tctl 52 °C · Tccd1 48 °C · Tccd2 50 °C`; the row is hidden when the machine has no CPU hwmon chip (`model.hide`) |
| 12 | `Load average` | `1.24 0.98 0.87` | two decimals each, single spaces; tooltip `1, 5 and 15 minutes` |
| 13 | `Cores` | `8` | static |
| 14 | `Logical processors` | `16` | static |
| 19 | `L1 cache` | `512 KiB` | cache format; tooltip `16 × 32 KiB data + 16 × 32 KiB instruction` |

| 21 | `L3 cache` | `96 MiB` | tooltip `98 304 KiB · 1 × 96 MiB`; `L4 {size}` appended to the tooltip when present |

title: E24: CpuPage entity: header toggles, Overall and Per core modes, kernel toggle, demand, bench layout (pages/performance/cpu.rs)
description:
## Context
The CPU page is the phase-0 scene: the overall chart or the per-core grid, the kernel toggle, the Details grid, and the demand that switches the engine to 10 Hz per-core sampling. This bead writes the P1 page (Overall and Per core); overlaid, stacked, marks and the secondary graph are P2 beads. Sources: PERF-027, PERF-028, PERF-029, PERF-033, UI-PRF-023 (anatomy, buttons, data binding, build), UI-PRF-053 (`bench_show_both`), ADR-008 (`cpu: PerCore`, `cpu_fast`), ADR-014, table (a) `cpu_graph_mode`, `cpu_kernel`, R-126 (`cpu_fast` stays on with smooth off).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/cpu.rs`:

```rust
pub struct CpuPage {
    key: DeviceKey, row: DeviceRow,
    overall: Entity<ChartView>, grid: CpuGrid,
    overlaid: Option<Entity<ChartView>>, stacked: Option<Entity<ChartView>>,   // E24-018
    secondary: Option<Entity<ChartView>>,                                      // E24-021
    details: KeyValueModel, mode: CpuGraphMode, kernel: bool,
    pub bench_show_both: bool,            // bench-only (UI-PRF-053): overall chart above the grid

    hub, demand, #[cfg(..)] pub render_count: Cell<u32>,
}
impl CpuPage { pub fn new(key, row, hub, demand, cx) -> Self; }
impl DevicePage for CpuPage { .. }
impl Render for CpuPage { .. }   // renders DevicePageFrame { page: self, .. }
```

Behaviour:

title: E24: sidebar hotplug: insert and remove animations, re-plug gap, saved slot
description:
## Context
Disks and network interfaces appear and disappear while tasklens runs. A new card slides in at its saved place, a removed card collapses, the selection moves to the next card, and a re-plugged device is a new card whose graph starts with a gap. Sources: PERF-005, UI-PRF-012 (hotplug add, remove, re-plug), UI-FND-003 (motion tokens), ADR-009 (page entities dropped).

## Deliverable
In `pages/performance/sidebar.rs`:
- `CardState.anim: CardAnim { Steady, Inserting { started: Instant }, Removing { started: Instant } }`.
- On `DEVICES`: a row that is new (key not in `cards`) gets `Inserting`; a card whose row is gone or became hidden gets `Removing` and keeps rendering until the animation ends (`m_base` 200 ms, `ease_out_cubic`), then is dropped together with its page entity (the sidebar emits `SidebarEvent::Removed(key)`; `PerformancePage` removes `pages[key]`).
- Insert: the card wrapper animates height 0 → 80 and opacity 0 → 1 through `with_animation(ElementId, Animation::new(m_base).with_easing(ease_out_cubic), |div, t| div.h(px(80 × t)).opacity(t))`; cards below move with the flex layout. Remove: opacity 1 → 0 and height 80 → 0. Reduced motion (`cx.reduce_motion()`) or `motion.animations == false`: no animation, the state changes at once.
- Selection: when the selected card starts `Removing`, `selection_after_removal` picks the next visible card and `select` runs at once (not after the animation).
- Re-plug: a device returning with a new `generation` is a new `CardState` (new `ChartView`); the engine marks `GAP_BEFORE`, so the chart shows the gap by itself (no sidebar logic).
- F-keys and Up/Down skip cards in `Removing`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a snapshot adding `disk:Z` with `device_order = [cpu, disk:Z, memory]` **When** installed **Then** the new card is at index 1 and in `Inserting` state (`device_appears_in_saved_slot`).
- **Given** the selected `disk:X` removed **When** the snapshot installs **Then** the selection moves to the next visible card at once and after 200 ms `cards` no longer contains `disk:X` and `pages` no longer contains its page (`selected_device_removed_selects_next`).
- **Given** reduce motion on **When** a card is added **Then** it is `Steady` immediately with full height.
- **Given** a card in `Removing` **When** `PerfSelectVisibleDevice { index }` counts cards **Then** it is skipped.
- **Given** `disk:X` removed then re-added with `generation + 1` **When** installed **Then** a new `ChartView` entity exists (`Entity` id differs).

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/sidebar.rs`: change
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/mod.rs`: change (handle `Removed`)
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_sidebar.rs`: change

## Tests
- `ui_sidebar.rs::device_appears_in_saved_slot`
- `ui_sidebar.rs::selected_device_removed_selects_next`
- `ui_sidebar.rs::reduced_motion_skips_animation`
- `ui_sidebar.rs::removing_card_skipped_by_keys`
- `ui_sidebar.rs::replug_creates_new_chart`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: the re-plug gap comes from `GAP_BEFORE` (PERF-005).
- Accessibility: the selection never lands on a vanishing card.
- Performance: animations run only during the 200 ms window and use GPUI `Animation` (not the chart driver); the sidebar is a `v_flex`, no `uniform_list`.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
`Animation` and `with_animation` are gpui-pre 0.3.7 `src/elements/animation.rs:15`; they respect `reduce_motion` only if the code checks it, so check `cx.reduce_motion() || !settings.motion.animations` before wrapping. title: E24: card context menu (Select Pages, Hide This Page, Show This Page, tray item slot) (pages/performance/menu.rs)
description:
## Context
Right-clicking a sidebar card opens a short menu to enter edit mode or hide the page. Hiding the selected page selects the next card; hiding the last visible page is refused. Sources: PERF-002, UI-PRF-014 (items, states, interaction), UI-FND-022 (`TlMenu`), R-019 (`device_overrides`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/menu.rs`, part 1:

```rust
pub fn card_menu(menu: TlMenu, key: &DeviceKey, visible_count: usize, hidden: bool, edit_mode: bool, tray_available: Option<bool>) -> TlMenu;
```
Items in order:
1. `Select Pages` → `PerfEnterEditMode`
2. `Hide This Page` → `PerfSetPageVisible { key, visible: false }`; disabled when `visible_count == 1` with tooltip `At least one performance page must stay visible`
3. `Show This Page` → `PerfSetPageVisible { key, visible: true }`; present only when `edit_mode && hidden`
4. separator
5. `Add tray icon graph` → `PerfAddTrayGraph { source: key }`; present only when `tray_available.is_some()` (P3, E24-024 passes `Some`); disabled with tooltip `No system tray available` when `Some(false)`

Wiring in `sidebar.rs`: each card row gets `.context_menu(move |menu, w, cx| card_menu(..))`; Shift+F10 on the focused sidebar opens the menu for the selected card (bound in the `Performance` context by E24-002: add `shift-f10` and `menu` → `PerfOpenCardMenu` to that file's binding list in this bead, declared as a unit action here). Right-click does not change the selection.

`PerfSetPageVisible` handler (in `sidebar.rs`): `visible: false` on the only visible page → refused with the toast `At least one performance page must stay visible` (`ToastQueue::push(Info, text, Some(ToastKey::PerfLastPage), None)`); otherwise writes `performance.device_overrides[key] = "hide"`; `visible: true` writes `"show"` when the type default is off and removes the entry when the default is on (PERF-002). Hiding the selected page selects the next visible card (E24-010's rule).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a visible, selected card among 9 and not in edit mode **When** the menu builds **Then** items are `Select Pages`, `Hide This Page`, separator (and nothing else before P3) (`card_menu_items_default`).
- **Given** edit mode and a hidden card **When** the menu builds **Then** `Show This Page` is present; outside edit mode it is absent (`card_menu_show_only_in_edit_mode_hidden`).
- **Given** one visible card **When** the menu builds **Then** `Hide This Page` is disabled with the tooltip.
- **Given** `PerfSetPageVisible { key: disk:X, visible: false }` with `show_disks = true` **When** handled **Then** `device_overrides["disk:X"] == "hide"`; `visible: true` afterwards removes the entry; with `show_disks = false`, `visible: true` writes `"show"` (`show_override_written_only_when_default_off`).
- **Given** the last visible page **When** `PerfSetPageVisible { visible: false }` is dispatched from a switch **Then** the toast text appears and the override is unchanged.
- **Given** a right-click on an unselected card **When** the menu opens **Then** the selection is unchanged.

- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/sidebar.rs`: change (context menu, handler)
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/actions.rs`: change (`PerfOpenCardMenu`, `shift-f10` and `menu` bindings)

- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_sidebar.rs`: change

## Tests

- `ui_sidebar.rs::card_menu_show_only_in_edit_mode_hidden`
- `ui_sidebar.rs::card_menu_hide_disabled_for_last`

- `ui_sidebar.rs::last_visible_refused_with_toast`
- `ui_sidebar.rs::right_click_keeps_selection`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the refusal is an Info toast with the exact text; nothing is logged.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: Shift+F10 and Menu open the menu for the selected card.
- Performance: the menu is built on open.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
`PerfEnterEditMode` has no handler until E24-013 (P2); the item exists from P1 as UI-PRF-014 says. `TlMenu` (E16-A3): `menu`, `menu_with_disabled`, `separator`, item tooltips per UI-FND-022; the kit `PopupMenu` methods are `crates/component/src/menu/popup_menu.rs:465` (`menu`), `:481` (`menu_with_disabled`), `:680` (`separator`). `ToastQueue::push(kind, text, key, action)` and `ToastKey` are E16-A2 (UI-FND-020); add the variant `ToastKey::PerfLastPage` there only if `ToastKey` is an open enum owned by E16 with a documented extension rule; otherwise use `ToastKey::Text(SharedString)` or whatever E16 provides for de-duplication and say so. description:
## Context
In edit mode a card can be dragged by its handle to another slot inside its group; a 3 px accent line marks the drop position; Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the focused row by one slot. The result is `performance.device_order`. Sources: PERF-003, UI-PRF-013 (drag, drop indicator, keyboard reorder, data binding), PERF-005 (saved place).

## Deliverable
In `sidebar.rs`:
- `drag: Option<DragState { key: DeviceKey, group: DeviceKind, over: Option<usize> /* drop index inside the group */ }>`.
- Handle `on_drag(DraggedCard { key }, |drag, _, w, cx| ghost view)`: the ghost is the card at opacity 0.8 following the pointer; the original row renders at opacity 0.3.
- Card rows `on_drag_move::<DraggedCard>`: compute the drop index from the pointer y against each row's midpoint, only among rows of the same group (a drop into another group is ignored and shows no indicator); the indicator is a 3 px `accent` line across the sidebar width at the drop position between two cards.
- `on_drop::<DraggedCard>` → `PerfMoveDevice { key, before: Option<DeviceKey> }` (`before = None` = end of the group).
- `PerfMoveDevice` handler: builds the new `device_order` as the full current sidebar order with the moved key placed before `before` (or last in its group) and writes `performance.device_order` (every present device key, so later re-plugs keep their slot; PERF-005).
- `PerfMoveFocusedDevice { delta }` (Alt+Up −1, Alt+Down +1): moves `edit_focus_row` one slot within its group; no-op at the group's ends.
- Numbering (`Disk N`, `GPU N`, `Fan N`) re-computes from the new order (`type_number`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** disks `[X, Y, Z]` **When** `PerfMoveDevice { key: Z, before: Some(X) }` is handled **Then** `device_order` lists `Z, X, Y` in the disk positions and the cards read `Disk 0` = Z, `Disk 1` = X (`drag_shifts_cards` for the sidebar).
- **Given** a drag of a disk over the Fans group **When** `on_drag_move` runs **Then** no indicator is shown and a drop does nothing (`reorder_within_group_only`).
- **Given** `edit_focus_row = Y` **When** Alt+Up is pressed **Then** the order is `Y, X, Z`; Alt+Up again is a no-op.
- **Given** the drop indicator between X and Y **When** rendered **Then** a 3 px accent quad spans the sidebar width at that boundary.
- **Given** a re-plugged device whose key is in `device_order` **When** it returns **Then** it takes its saved slot (E24-010 covers the insert; this test asserts the order after a move then remove then re-add).

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/sidebar.rs`: change
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_sidebar.rs`: change

## Tests
- `ui_sidebar.rs::move_device_rewrites_order_and_numbering`
- `ui_sidebar.rs::reorder_within_group_only`
- `ui_sidebar.rs::alt_up_down_moves_focused_row`
- `ui_sidebar.rs::drop_indicator_geometry`
- `ui_sidebar.rs::saved_order_survives_replug`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: Alt+Up and Alt+Down keep reordering keyboard-reachable; the handle has tooltip `Drag to reorder`.
- Performance: the ghost is one card render per drag frame.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
`on_drag` is gpui-pre 0.3.7 `src/elements/div.rs:615`, `on_drag_move` `div.rs:360`, `on_drop` `div.rs:568`. Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E24: Graph summary mode: SummaryView tiles, key context, Esc and Ctrl+M, title suffix (pages/performance/summary.rs)
description:
## Context
Ctrl+M replaces the whole window content with a tiled grid of every visible device's main graph. Esc or Ctrl+M returns; tab switching is blocked while it is on. Sources: PERF-010, UI-PRF-016 (anatomy, states, interaction, build), UI-SHL-001 (`MainWindow::render` hook `summary_view()`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/summary.rs`:

```rust
pub struct SummaryView { tiles: Vec<Tile { key: DeviceKey, heading: SharedString, line1: SharedString, chart: Entity<ChartView> }>, selected_on_entry: Option<DeviceKey>, focus: FocusHandle /* key_context "PerformanceSummary" */, .. }
pub fn tile_grid(n: usize, w: Pixels, h: Pixels) -> TileLayout { cols, rows, tile_w, tile_h, scrolls: bool }
    // cols = ceil(sqrt(n)), rows = ceil(n / cols); tile_w = (W − 2 sp6 − (cols − 1) sp4) / cols, tile_h likewise over H; minimum tile 200 × 120: while tile_w < 200 and cols > 1, cols −= 1; if tile_h < 120 the grid scrolls vertically with tile_h = 120
```

Behaviour:
- `PerfToggleSummaryMode` on `PerformancePage`: on → create `SummaryView` with one tile per visible device in sidebar order (a fresh `ChartView` per tile with the card's series and scale, `background: Window`); off → drop it. `PerformancePage::summary_view(&self) -> Option<AnyView>`; `MainWindow::render` (E20-A1) asks the Performance page for it before rendering the tab strip and renders it instead of tab strip plus page when `Some` (chain edit in `window/main.rs`: one `if let Some(v) = perf.summary_view()` branch; the title bar stays with its caption buttons and its menus hidden).
- Tile: bg `window_bg` padding `sp6`, gap `sp4`; label row: heading `t_md` 500 left (plus ` · {line1}` in `text_secondary` when the tile is ≥ 280 px wide), value `t_md` 400 `tnum` right; the chart fills the rest; legend shown when tile width ≥ 200; range label when tile height ≥ 160; a 2 px `accent` line under the label row on the tile of `selected_on_entry`.
- Entering: sidebar and page fade out over `m_fast`, tiles fade in over `m_base`; reduced motion instant. Window title gets the suffix ` · Graph Summary` (`window.set_window_title("tasklens · Graph Summary")`), restored on exit.
- Keys in `PerformanceSummary` (bound by E24-002): Esc and Ctrl+M → off; tab keys swallowed. Click on a tile → off, then `PerfSelectDevice { key }`. Right-click on a tile → `page_menu` for that device's page (created on demand through `build_page` if not visited). Double-click → `PerfShowMiniWindow`. Window resize re-tiles (layout computed in render from the bounds).
- Demand unchanged (the sidebar still contributes while hidden under the summary; the sidebar entity is kept).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 9 visible devices in a 1600 × 1000 window **When** summary mode opens **Then** 9 tiles in 3 × 3 (`summary_tile_grid_for_9`) and `tiles` follow the sidebar order (`summary_tiles_all_visible_devices`).
- **Given** summary mode on **When** `ctrl-2` is pressed **Then** the active tab is still Performance (`summary_blocks_tab_switch`).
- **Given** memory selected on entry **When** Esc is pressed **Then** summary is off and memory is still selected (`summary_esc_returns_to_selected_device`); the window title is `tasklens` again.
- **Given** a click on the GPU tile **When** handled **Then** summary is off and `gpu` is selected.
- **Given** a 500 × 300 window and 9 devices **When** `tile_grid` runs **Then** `cols == 2` (200 px minimum) and `scrolls == true`.
- **Given** reduce motion on **When** entering **Then** no animation frames are requested by the fade.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/summary.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/mod.rs`: change (add the field `pub(crate) summary: Option<Entity<summary::SummaryView>>` at the `// E24-015` comment with `None` init, R-262; handler, `summary_view()`)
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`: add the `summary_view()` branch (chain edit, E20-A1)
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append `perf-summary-title-suffix =  · Graph Summary` (chain edit)
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_performance.rs`: change

## Tests
- `ui_performance.rs::summary_tiles_all_visible_devices`
- `ui_performance.rs::summary_tile_grid_for_9`
- `ui_performance.rs::summary_blocks_tab_switch`
- `ui_performance.rs::summary_esc_returns_to_selected_device`
- `ui_performance.rs::summary_click_selects_and_exits`
- `ui_performance.rs::summary_small_window_shrinks_cols_and_scrolls`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: tiles show the same glyphs as cards.
- Accessibility: Esc always exits; the title suffix announces the mode.
- Performance: n tiles at 1 Hz plus CPU at 10 Hz; tile charts are created on entry and dropped on exit.
- Privacy: N/A

`set_window_title` is gpui-pre 0.3.7 `src/window.rs:2876`. The `MainWindow` hook is a one-branch chain edit; if E20-A1 already renders `summary_view()`, this bead only implements it. Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E24: Copy device info (Ctrl+C, menu Copy): text format, CPU page copy_text, toast
description:
## Context

When a Details value selection is active (E24-022), Ctrl+C copies that value instead and shows no toast.

title: E24: CPU "All cores overlaid" and "All cores stacked" modes with cross-fade and the kernel button rule
description:
## Context
The two Mission Center modes draw every core in one 300 px chart: overlaid lines at `max(1/n, 0.08)` alpha, or stacked filled bands with a `Stacked(n)` axis ("1600%"). The kernel toggle is disabled in these modes and a mode change cross-fades. Sources: PERF-027, PERF-029, PERF-030, UI-PRF-023 (modes, animation, button states), UI-PRF-006 `Stacked`.

## Deliverable
In `cpu.rs`:
- `overlaid: Option<Entity<ChartView>>` created on first use: `ChartSpec { series: one per logical CPU with fill None, line cpu_line.alpha(max(1/n, 0.08)), y: Fixed 0..100, stack: false }`, labels heading `Utilization`, no legend, `show_axis_max: false`.
- `stacked`: `series` one per CPU with `fill = Some(cpu_fill.alpha(0.85 … stepped: band k uses lightness offset k/n × 0.15 of cpu_fill)` and `line = cpu_line`, `y: Stacked(n)`, `stack: true`, `show_axis_max: true` (axis text `1600%` from E19-004).
- `CPU_EXTRA_MODES_ENABLED = true`; the mode menu items are enabled.
- Kernel button: disabled (opacity 0.5, tooltip kept) in `AllCoresOverlaid` and `AllCoresStacked`; its label is unchanged.
- Demand: `cpu: PerCore` in both modes.
- Mode change: cross-fade `m_base` between the old and new graph area (both rendered during the fade, old opacity 1 → 0, new 0 → 1 with `with_animation`); the graph area height animates between 300 and the grid height over the same duration; reduced motion or `motion.animations == false`: instant.
- CPU hotplug (`DEVICES` with a changed topology) rebuilds both specs.

title: E24: CPU Details P2 rows: Power draw, Virtualization, Running in VM, Security features, Hypervisor, cpufreq rows, Microcode
description:
## Context
The P2 rows of the CPU Details grid: RAPL power with the `Needs setup` link, the virtualisation and security rows, the cpufreq driver rows and the microcode. Sources: PERF-035, PERF-037, PERF-038, PERF-013 (hidden rows, `Needs setup`), R-056, UI-PRF-024 rows 10, 15 to 18, 22 to 26.

## Deliverable
In `cpu_details.rs`: the model gains rows at their grid positions (10 after Sockets; 15 to 18 after Logical processors; 22 to 26 after L3 cache):

| # | Label | Value | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | `Power draw` | `31.9 W` | tooltip `Package 31.9 W · Core 18.2 W`; RAPL present but unreadable → `set_fallback(Unsupported, NeedsSetup)` (link to Additional Setup); no RAPL zone at all → `hide` |
| 15 | `Virtualization` | `Enabled (KVM available)` / `Supported, KVM module not loaded` / `Not supported` | static |
| 16 | `Running in VM` | `No` or the hypervisor name | static |
| 17 | `Security features` | `Secure Boot, IOMMU` (the active ones of Secure Boot, Kernel lockdown, Memory encryption, User shadow stack, IOMMU, in that order; `None` when none) | tooltip `12 mitigated, 0 vulnerable, 3 not affected`, plus ` · Could not read: {source}` for each unreadable source |
| 18 | `Hypervisor` | `None` or the vendor | static |
| 22 | `Cpufreq driver` | `amd-pstate-epp` | static |
| 23 | `Governor` | `powersave` | static |
| 24 | `Power preference` | `balance_performance` | static |
| 25 | `Platform profile` | `balanced` | static; `Not supported` when neither sysfs nor power-profiles-daemon has it |
| 26 | `Microcode` | `0xa601206` | static |

title: E24: CPU secondary graph: Power draw, Clock speed, Temperature, fallback rule and the menu
description:
## Context
Under the CPU graph area sits one 120 px chart chosen from the page menu: power (default), clock, temperature or none. When power is not available the chart falls back to temperature, then clock, without changing the saved choice. Sources: PERF-032, PERF-038 to PERF-040, UI-PRF-025 (table, states, interaction), table (a) `cpu_secondary_graph`.

## Deliverable
In `cpu.rs`:
- `secondary: Option<Entity<ChartView>>` under the graph area with `sp4` gap, height `SECONDARY_GRAPH_H` 120, `show_axis_max: true`:

| Choice | Heading, range word | Series | Scale | Value format |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Power | `Power draw` | package W filled (`cpu_fill`/`cpu_line`), core W dashed `cpu_line` | `StickyUp { hw_max: None }` | Watts |
| Clock | `Clock speed` | average MHz filled, maximum-core MHz dashed | `StickyUp { hw_max: cpuinfo_max_freq }` | Mhz |
| Temperature | `Temperature` | main sensor °C | `StickyTemp` | Celsius |
| None | absent | | | |

- Series: `cpu.power_pkg`, `cpu.power_core`, `cpu.clock_avg` (`CPU_FREQ`), `cpu.clock_max`, `cpu.temp` (`CPU_TEMP`) at 1 Hz; the constants without an ADR-003 id are plan open item 1.

title: E24: Details value selection fallback: click selects, Ctrl+C copies the value, Esc clears, "Copy value" context item (U-46)
description:
## Context
PERF-012 wants selectable Details values, but gpui-pre 0.3.7 has no text selection on arbitrary elements. tasklens ships a fallback: clicking a value selects it visually, Ctrl+C copies that value, Esc clears, and a right-click offers "Copy value". The bead also records U-46. Sources: PERF-012, UI-PRF-020 (interaction), R-126, U-46.

## Deliverable
- `details.rs`: `KeyValueModel.selected: Option<&'static str>` (label of the selected row); `render_details` draws the selected value with bg `row_selected` and text `text_selected_primary`; click on a value sets `selected` and notifies; click elsewhere on the page or Esc clears it.
- `mod.rs`: `PerfCopyDeviceInfo` copies the selected value only when `selected.is_some()` (no toast); `PerfCopyValue` (from the context item) copies the clicked value. Esc in the `Performance` context clears the selection before the global Esc chain (bind `escape` → `PerfClearValueSelection`, a unit action added to `actions.rs`, on the page root only while a selection exists, so the global chain runs otherwise).
- Context menu on a value: `Copy value` → `PerfCopyValue` (the item is added at the top of the page menu when the right-click landed on a value, through `PageMenuCtx.clicked_value: Option<&'static str>`).
- U-46 check: before coding, the implementer greps gpui-pre 0.3.7 for a text-selection API on `div` or `Label` (`selectable`, `text_selection`, `InteractiveText` selection); if one exists and works in a `TestAppContext`, use it instead of the fallback and record the finding in the closing comment and in `docs/RECONCILIATION.md`'s unverified list entry U-46 (one line, the only doc edit this bead makes).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a click on the `Speed` value **When** handled **Then** that value renders with `row_selected` bg and `PerfCopyDeviceInfo` copies `4631 MHz` without a toast.
- **Given** a selection **When** Esc is pressed **Then** the selection is cleared and the filter box (none on Performance) is untouched; a second Esc runs the global chain.
- **Given** a right-click on a value **When** the menu builds **Then** the first item is `Copy value` and it copies the value.
- **Given** no selection **When** `PerfCopyDeviceInfo` dispatches **Then** the whole page text is copied (E24-016 behaviour unchanged).

title: E24: DeviceKey, DeviceKind, sidebar order and visibility rules, PerformancePage skeleton (pages/performance/mod.rs)
description:
## Context
The Performance tab identifies devices by persistent string keys (`cpu`, `gpu:<uuid>`, `disk:<wwn>` …) in settings and state, orders them by `performance.device_order` then by type, and shows or hides them by per-device overrides and per-type defaults. This bead writes those pure rules and the `PerformancePage` entity skeleton every later E24 bead fills. Sources: PERF-002, PERF-004, PERF-005 (key forms), PERF-008 (type order), UI-PRF-010 (entity fields), UI-PRF-012 (order, visibility, selection rules), canonical table (a) `[performance]` keys, ADR-003 `DeviceIdentity`.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/mod.rs` and the line `pub mod performance;` in `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/mod.rs` (chain edit, E16-A1).

```rust
pub mod page; pub mod sidebar; pub mod card; pub mod summary; pub mod menu; pub mod actions; pub mod details; pub mod cpu; pub mod cpu_grid; pub mod cpu_details;  // empty modules with a `//! filled by <plan key>` line until their beads run

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema)]
pub struct DeviceKey(pub Arc<str>);
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
pub enum DeviceKind { Cpu, Memory, Gpu, Disk, Net, Fan, Battery, AggregateDisk, AggregateGpu }
impl DeviceKey {
    pub fn from_identity(id: &DeviceIdentity) -> Option<DeviceKey>;  // None for CpuLogical and Sensor (not cards)
    pub fn kind(&self) -> DeviceKind;      // from the prefix
    pub const CPU: &'static str = "cpu"; pub const MEMORY: &'static str = "memory";
    pub const AGGREGATE_DISK: &'static str = "aggregate:disk"; pub const AGGREGATE_GPU: &'static str = "aggregate:gpu";
}
```

Key forms (PERF-005): `CpuPackage` → `cpu`; `Memory` → `memory`; `Gpu { uuid, pci_bus_id }` → `gpu:GPU-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx` (lower-case hex of the 16 bytes in 8-4-4-4-12 groups) when `uuid != [0; 16]`, else `gpu:pci:<pci_bus_id>`; `Disk { wwn_or_serial: Some(s), .. }` → `disk:<s>`; `Disk { wwn_or_serial: None, name, .. }` → `disk:<name>` (plan open item 6 records that the by-path fallback is not available from `DeviceIdentity`); `Net { name, .. }` → `net:<name>`; `Fan { chip, index }` → `fan:<chip>:<index>` (open item 6: the device path is not in the identity); `Battery { native_path }` → `bat:<native_path>`.

```rust
pub struct PerformanceSettingsView<'a> { pub order: &'a [DeviceKey], pub overrides: &'a HashMap<DeviceKey, Override /* Show | Hide */>, pub show_disks: bool, pub show_gpus: bool, pub show_fans: bool, pub show_batteries: bool, pub show_network_wired: bool, pub show_network_wireless: bool, pub show_network_vpn: bool, pub show_network_virtual: bool, pub show_network_other: bool }
pub struct DeviceRow { pub key: DeviceKey, pub kind: DeviceKind, pub idx: DeviceIdx, pub generation: u32, pub net_class: Option<NetClass> }
pub fn sidebar_order(catalog: &DeviceCatalog, settings: &PerformanceSettingsView, out: &mut Vec<DeviceRow>);
    // present devices only; keys in `order` first, in that order; the rest by kind order Cpu, Memory, Gpu, Disk, Net, Fan, Battery, AggregateDisk, AggregateGpu; within a kind by DeviceCatalog order; `lo` never included
pub fn is_visible(row: &DeviceRow, settings: &PerformanceSettingsView) -> bool;
    // override Show → true, Hide → false; else Cpu and Memory → true; Disk → show_disks; Gpu → show_gpus; Fan → show_fans; Battery → show_batteries; Net → by NetClass (Wired → show_network_wired, Wireless → show_network_wireless, VpnOrTunnel → show_network_vpn, Virtual → show_network_virtual, Other → show_network_other); aggregates → false
pub fn visible_rows<'a>(rows: &'a [DeviceRow], settings: &PerformanceSettingsView) -> impl Iterator<Item = &'a DeviceRow>;
pub fn selection_after_removal(visible: &[DeviceRow], removed_at: usize) -> Option<DeviceKey>;  // next below, else the one above, else None
pub fn initial_selection(visible: &[DeviceRow], saved: Option<&DeviceKey>) -> Option<DeviceKey>; // saved if visible, else the first visible
pub fn type_number(rows: &[DeviceRow], key: &DeviceKey) -> u16;   // index among visible rows of the same kind, counting from 0 ("Disk 0", "GPU 0")

pub struct PerformancePage {
    // E24-004: sidebar: Entity<sidebar::DeviceSidebar> (added by crw.6 as a chain edit, R-262)
    pub(crate) pages: FxHashMap<DeviceKey, AnyView>,         // created on first visit, kept (ADR-009)
    pub(crate) selected: Option<DeviceKey>,
    // E24-015: summary: Option<Entity<summary::SummaryView>> (added by crw.17 as a chain edit, R-262)
    pub(crate) sidebar_visible: bool,                        // not persisted (R-090)
    pub(crate) focus: FocusHandle,                           // key_context "Performance"
    #[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-hooks"))] pub render_count: Cell<u32>,
}
```

`NetClass` is the PERF-054 type class of an interface as the engine reports it in the device catalog (`DeviceEntry` carries `NetKind` from `tl_model::devices`, E03-A1; map `NetKind::{Ethernet, Usb} → Wired`, `WiFi → Wireless`, `Tunnel | Vpn → VpnOrTunnel`, `Virtual | Bridge → Virtual`, `Cellular | Other → Other`).

## Acceptance Criteria

title: E24: every Perf* action, bind_keys_performance and the app.rs registration (pages/performance/actions.rs)
description:
## Context
Every menu item, button and key on the Performance tab dispatches one GPUI Action in the `tasklens` namespace with a `Perf` prefix. This bead declares all of them up front, for E24 and for the E25 device pages, so no later bead edits this file, and binds the table (b) keys in the `Performance` context. Sources: UI-PRF-010 (interaction), UI-PRF-012 (keys), UI-PRF-013 to UI-PRF-016, UI-PRF-020 to UI-PRF-035 (page actions), PERF-007, canonical table (b), R-128 (one namespace), UI-SHL-120 (binding mechanism).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/actions.rs`:

Unit actions (`actions!(tasklens, [..])`): `PerfSelectPrevDevice`, `PerfSelectNextDevice`, `PerfSelectFirstDevice`, `PerfSelectLastDevice`, `PerfToggleSidebar`, `PerfToggleSummaryMode`, `PerfCopyDeviceInfo`, `PerfCopyValue`, `PerfEnterEditMode`, `PerfExitEditMode`, `PerfEnableAllPages`, `PerfDisableAllPages`, `PerfResetPagesToDefault`, `PerfShowMiniWindow`, `PerfToggleCpuKernel`, `PerfToggleMemoryComposition`, `PerfToggleMemorySwapGraph`, `PerfOpenNetworkSettings`.

Data actions (`#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Deserialize, JsonSchema, Action)] #[action(namespace = tasklens)]`): `PerfSelectDevice { key: DeviceKey }`, `PerfSelectVisibleDevice { index: u8 }`, `PerfSetGraphRange { secs: u16 }`, `PerfJumpToType { kind: DeviceKind }`, `PerfSetPageVisible { key: DeviceKey, visible: bool }`, `PerfMoveDevice { key: DeviceKey, before: Option<DeviceKey> }`, `PerfMoveFocusedDevice { delta: i8 }` (Alt+Up −1, Alt+Down +1), `PerfAddTrayGraph { source: DeviceKey }`, `PerfSetCpuGraphMode { mode: CpuGraphMode }`, `PerfSetCpuSecondaryGraph { choice: CpuSecondaryGraph }`, `PerfShowSmart { key: DeviceKey }`, `PerfSmartRefresh { key: DeviceKey }`, `PerfSmartReadSmartctl { key: DeviceKey }`, `PerfEject { key: DeviceKey }`, `PerfToggleGpuEngine { key: DeviceKey, engine: Arc<str> }`, `PerfToggleGpuOptionalGraph { key: DeviceKey, which: GpuOptionalGraph }`, `PerfRenameFan { key: DeviceKey }`, `PerfSetFanTempSensor { key: DeviceKey, sensor: Option<Arc<str>> }`, `PerfFetchPublicIp { key: DeviceKey }`. `CpuGraphMode { Overall, PerCore, AllCoresOverlaid, AllCoresStacked }`, `CpuSecondaryGraph { None, Power, Clock, Temperature }` and `GpuOptionalGraph { Power, Clocks }` are the `tl_model::settings` enums (E03-A2) re-exported here.

```rust
pub fn bind_keys_performance(cx: &mut App);
```
Bindings (GPUI keystroke syntax, context `Performance`): `f1`..`f8` → `PerfSelectVisibleDevice { index: 0..7 }`; `up` → `PerfSelectPrevDevice`; `down` → `PerfSelectNextDevice`; `home` → `PerfSelectFirstDevice`; `end` → `PerfSelectLastDevice`; `f9` and `ctrl-t` → `PerfToggleSidebar`; `ctrl-m` → `PerfToggleSummaryMode`; `ctrl-c` → `PerfCopyDeviceInfo`; `alt-up` → `PerfMoveFocusedDevice { delta: -1 }`; `alt-down` → `PerfMoveFocusedDevice { delta: 1 }`. Context `PerformanceSummary`: `escape` and `ctrl-m` → `PerfToggleSummaryMode`; `ctrl-1`..`ctrl-6`, `alt-1`..`alt-6`, `ctrl-tab`, `ctrl-shift-tab` → `NoOp` (swallowed, PERF-010; `NoOp` is a unit action declared here).

Chain edit in `crates/tl-ui/src/app.rs` (E16-A1): one line `pages::performance::actions::bind_keys_performance(cx);` next to the other `bind_keys_*` calls in `TasklensUi::init`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `bind_keys_performance` ran **When** `cx.bindings_for_action(&PerfSelectVisibleDevice { index: 2 })` is queried **Then** it contains `f3` in context `Performance`.
- **Given** the `Performance` context **When** `ctrl-c` is resolved **Then** the action is `PerfCopyDeviceInfo` (not the Table copy).
- **Given** the `PerformanceSummary` context **When** `ctrl-2` is resolved **Then** the action is `NoOp` and in `Global` it is `SelectTab(1)`.
- **Given** `PerfSetGraphRange { secs: 300 }` **When** serialised and deserialised through the Action machinery **Then** it round-trips.
- **Given** every action above **When** `cx.all_action_names()` is read **Then** each name starts with `tasklens::Perf` (or `tasklens::NoOp`).

## Cross-cutting
