title: E24: DeviceCard: layout, per-kind heading and lines, states (pages/performance/card.rs)
description:
## Context
Each sidebar entry is a card: a 116 × 56 mini graph with the value at its top-left, a heading and two detail lines. The same card is reused by the mini window (E26) and the summary mode reads its heading. This bead writes the card's rendering and the pure text builders for every device kind. Sources: PERF-001, PERF-005, PERF-008, PERF-013, PERF-053, PERF-054, R-050, R-055, UI-PRF-011 (anatomy, lines table, states), UI-FND-003 (tokens), UI-FND-026 (glyphs), table (d).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/card.rs`:

```rust
pub struct CardLines { pub heading: SharedString, pub line1: SharedString, pub line2: SharedString, pub line2_accent: bool, pub tooltip: Option<SharedString>, pub disconnected: bool }
pub struct CardTextInput<'a> { pub kind: DeviceKind, pub number: u16, pub entry: &'a DeviceEntry, pub system: &'a SystemSnapshot, pub network_unit: NetworkUnit, pub auto_scale: bool }
pub fn card_lines(input: &CardTextInput, scratch: &mut String) -> CardLines;   // re-formats into reused buffers; the caller compares with the previous lines and keeps the old SharedStrings when equal
pub struct DeviceCard { pub key: DeviceKey, pub chart: Entity<ChartView>, pub lines: CardLines, pub selected: bool, pub focused: bool, pub edit_mode: bool, pub hidden_in_edit: bool, pub width: Pixels }
impl RenderOnce for DeviceCard { .. }
pub const CARD_H: f32 = 80.0; pub const CARD_GRAPH_W: f32 = 116.0; pub const CARD_GRAPH_H: f32 = 56.0;
```

Lines per kind (exact; glyph words per UI-FND-026 replace a value whose `Validity` is not `Valid`; `…` while `WarmingUp`):

| Kind | heading | line1 | line2 | line2_accent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cpu | `CPU` | CPU model, else `Unknown processor` | `4631 MHz · 52 °C`; temperature part omitted when no CPU hwmon exists | false |
| Memory | `Memory` | `34.68 GiB / 63.16 GiB` | `Commit 69.0%` | false |
| Gpu | `GPU {n}` | GPU name, else `Unknown GPU` | `52 °C` | false |
| Disk | `Disk {n}` | `NVMe - /` (kind, ` - `, primary mount; no mount: kind only) | model; from P2 `{model} · 41 °C` when the temperature is Valid | false |
| Net | the interface name | type word (`Ethernet`, `Wi-Fi`, `Virtual`, `USB network`, `Bridge`, `Cellular`, `Tunnel`, `VPN`, `Other`) | connected: `↓ 1.2 Mbps ↑ 0.3 Mbps` when both rates are non-zero, else the total rate `0.01 Mbps` (table (d) network format, `network_unit`, `auto_scale`); not connected: the state word (`Disconnected`, `Testing`, `Dormant`, `Not present`, `Lower layer down`, `Unknown`) | true when connected |
| Fan | `Fan {n}` or the fan label when set | label, else chip name | `1200 RPM · 45 °C` (`45 °C` part omitted without a paired sensor) | false |
| Battery | kind word (`Battery`, `Mouse`, `UPS`, …) | vendor and model | `85.0% · Discharging` | false |
| AggregateDisk | `Aggregate storage` | `{k} disks` | `Multiple` when kinds differ, else the kind | false |
| AggregateGpu | `Aggregate graphics` | `{k} adapters` | `Multiple` when vendors differ, else the vendor | false |

`tooltip`: the full model when `line1` would truncate (the owner decides truncation from width; the card always sets the tooltip to the full line1 and `TlTooltip` shows it on hover of the text column); network cards append the NetworkManager connection name on a second line when known. `disconnected = true` for a Net card whose state is not Connected.

Card rendering (sizes × `ui_scale`): `h_flex` width × 80, bg `list_bg`, 1 px `divider` border, radius `r_md`; left inset `sp5` (12); the chart box 116 × 56 (`ChartSpec.background = List`, `ChartLabels { heading: None, value_align: Left, legend: empty, show_axis_max: false }`, grid on, outline on); `sp4` gap; text column `v_flex` vertically centred, lines 18 / 16 / 16 px high: heading `t_md` 500 `text_primary`, line1 and line2 `t_sm` 400 `text_secondary` (line2 in `accent` when `line2_accent`), each `overflow_hidden` + `text_ellipsis` + `whitespace_nowrap`. States: hover bg `row_hover`; pressed bg `row_selected` at alpha 0.6; selected: a 2 px `accent` outline quad drawn inside the card bounds (`div().absolute().inset_0().border_2().border_color(accent).rounded(r_md)`); focused and selected: a second outline 1 px `accent` at alpha 0.5, 2 px outside; `disconnected`: whole card `opacity(0.6)`; edit mode: no selected border, `hidden_in_edit` → opacity 0.6. Click → `PerfSelectDevice { key }` (not in edit mode when the click lands on the switch; E24-013). Double-click: nothing. `cursor` default.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a CPU entry with model "AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D 8-Core Processor", clock 4631 MHz and temperature 52 °C **When** `card_lines` runs **Then** heading `CPU`, line1 the model, line2 `4631 MHz · 52 °C` (`card_lines_cpu`).
- **Given** a Net entry with rx 1.2 Mbps and tx 0.3 Mbps, bits, auto-scale off **When** `card_lines` runs **Then** line2 `↓ 1.2 Mbps ↑ 0.3 Mbps` and `line2_accent == true` (`card_lines_network_both_directions`).
- **Given** rx 1.2 Mbps and tx 0 **When** `card_lines` runs **Then** line2 `1.2 Mbps` (`card_lines_network_one_direction`).
- **Given** a Net entry with operstate down **When** rendered **Then** the card has opacity 0.6 and line2 is `Disconnected` in `text_secondary` (`card_disconnected_opacity`).
- **Given** a Disk entry with temperature `Validity::Restricted` **When** `card_lines` runs **Then** line2 is `{model} · ` followed by the lock glyph text placeholder handled by the renderer: the line is split into `model` text and a `TlValidityGlyph` for the temperature (`card_value_glyph_for_restricted`).
- **Given** `selected == true, focused == false` **When** rendered **Then** one 2 px accent outline and no 1 px outer ring; with `focused == true` both.
- **Given** the same inputs twice **When** `card_lines` runs **Then** the returned `SharedString`s compare equal and the caller's cache keeps the first allocation (test asserts `Arc::ptr_eq` after the caller's compare-and-keep step).

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/card.rs`: create
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append keys `perf-card-heading-cpu = CPU`, `perf-card-heading-memory = Memory`, `perf-card-heading-gpu = GPU {$n}`, `perf-card-heading-disk = Disk {$n}`, `perf-card-heading-fan = Fan {$n}`, `perf-card-aggregate-storage = Aggregate storage`, `perf-card-aggregate-graphics = Aggregate graphics`, `perf-card-multiple = Multiple`, `perf-card-commit = Commit {$pct}`, `perf-unknown-processor = Unknown processor`, `perf-unknown-gpu = Unknown GPU`, `perf-unknown-adapter = Unknown adapter`, and the state words `perf-net-state-connected = Connected`, `-disconnected = Disconnected`, `-testing = Testing`, `-dormant = Dormant`, `-not-present = Not present`, `-lower-layer-down = Lower layer down`, `-unknown = Unknown` (chain edit, R-132)

## Tests

- `card::tests::card_lines_memory`
- `card::tests::card_lines_network_both_directions`
- `card::tests::card_lines_network_one_direction`
- `card::tests::card_lines_disk_with_and_without_mount`
- `card::tests::card_lines_fan_battery_aggregate`

## Cross-cutting

title: E24: DeviceSidebar entity: cards, charts, selection, keys, scroll, demand (pages/performance/sidebar.rs)
description:
## Context
The sidebar lists one card per visible device, keeps one `ChartView` per card, owns the roving selection and its keys, scrolls the selected card into view, and tells the demand aggregator which sources it needs. Hotplug animations and edit mode are later beads. Sources: UI-PRF-010 (sidebar part, focus), UI-PRF-011 (data binding, build), UI-PRF-012 (selection, keys, demand), PERF-001, PERF-007, ADR-008 `Demand`, ADR-009 (cached entities, notify rules).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/sidebar.rs`:

```rust
pub struct CardState { pub row: DeviceRow, pub chart: Entity<ChartView>, pub lines: CardLines, pub line_bits: [u64; 3] /* value bits of the last format per line */ }
pub struct DeviceSidebar {
    pub(crate) cards: IndexMap<DeviceKey, CardState>,   // in sidebar order
    pub(crate) rows: Vec<DeviceRow>,                     // from sidebar_order (all present devices, hidden included)
    pub(crate) selected: Option<DeviceKey>,
    pub(crate) focus: FocusHandle,                      // key_context "Performance", tab_stop true (the one Tab stop of the list)
    pub(crate) scroll: ScrollHandle,
    pub(crate) edit_mode: bool,                         // E24-013
    pub(crate) hub: Entity<SnapshotHub>, pub(crate) demand: Entity<DemandAggregator>,
    #[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-hooks"))] pub render_count: Cell<u32>,
}
pub enum SidebarEvent { Selected(DeviceKey), Removed(DeviceKey) }   // EventEmitter; PerformancePage listens
impl DeviceSidebar {
    pub fn new(hub, demand, cx) -> Self;    // subscribes to the hub (DEVICES, SYSTEM, SERIES) and observes TlSettings (performance section)
    pub fn select(&mut self, key: DeviceKey, cx);         // sets selected, scrolls into view (ScrollHandle::scroll_to_item Nearest), emits Selected, notifies
    pub fn visible_keys(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &DeviceKey>;
    pub fn heading_for(&self, key: &DeviceKey) -> Option<&CardLines>;
}
```

Behaviour:
- On `DEVICES` or a `performance` settings change: recompute `rows = sidebar_order(..)`; for a new visible row create `CardState` with a `ChartView` (`ChartSpec` per kind: Cpu `[total filled cpu_fill/cpu_line, kernel line kernel_line when cpu_kernel]` `Fixed 0..100`; Memory `[used filled mem, committed dashed mem_line]` `FixedTotal(MemTotal)`; Gpu `[3D/Compute engine]` `Fixed`; Disk `[active time]` `Fixed`; Net `[rx filled net, tx dashed tinted]` `AutoRate { iec: unit == Bytes }` or `LinkSpeed` when `network_dynamic_scale == false` and the speed is known; Fan `[rpm]` `StickyUp { hw_max: fan_max }`; Battery `[percent]` `Fixed` for peripherals, `[power]` `Symmetric` for system batteries; `range_ns = performance.graph_range_s`, `smooth = motion.smooth_graphs`, `background = List`, `grid.lines = true`); drop the state of a row that is gone (E24-010 adds the animation); keep the order of `cards` equal to `rows`. Series ids: `SeriesId { device: row.idx, metric }` with the `MetricId` constants from E03-A1 (`CPU_TOTAL`, `CPU_KERNEL`, `MEM_USED`, `MEM_COMMIT`, `GPU_UTIL`, `DISK_ACTIVE`, `NET_RX`, `NET_TX`, `FAN_RPM`, `BATTERY_PCT`; battery power per plan open item 1).
- On `SYSTEM` and on `SERIES` for a card's ids: re-run `card_lines` for that card, compare each line's value bits (`line_bits`) and keep the old `SharedString` when unchanged; `cx.notify()` only when some line changed.
- Selection: `initial_selection(visible, state.performance.selected_device)` at construction; `select` writes `state.performance.selected_device` through `TlSettings::update` (debounced persist, ADR-011); when the selected card disappears or becomes hidden, `selection_after_removal` picks the next and `select` runs.
- Actions on the focus element: `PerfSelectDevice`, `PerfSelectVisibleDevice { index }` (the Nth visible, hidden cards not counted), `PerfSelectPrevDevice`, `PerfSelectNextDevice`, `PerfSelectFirstDevice`, `PerfSelectLastDevice`. Up at the first card and Down at the last do nothing.
- Demand: after each `rows` change, give the aggregator this surface's part: `cpu: Total` always (the CPU card), `memory` always, `disks` when any Disk card is visible, `nets` when any Net card, `gpus` when any Gpu card, `sensors` when any Fan or Battery card; `cpu_fast` is not set by the sidebar.
- Render: `v_flex` with `sp4` padding, `sp4` gaps, `overflow_y_scroll` with the kit scrollbar in `ScrollbarMode::Scrolling`, one `DeviceCard` per visible row (`selected`, `focused = focus.is_focused(window)`), `.track_focus(&focus)`, `.key_context("Performance")`, `.cached(StyleRefinement::default().size_full())` applied by the parent. Right-click on a card is wired by E24-011.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a `FakeEngine` catalog with 9 devices (CPU, Memory, GPU, 4 disks, 2 nets) **When** the sidebar renders **Then** 9 cards exist in type order and `cards.len() == 9`.
- **Given** `selected_device = "disk:X"` saved and visible **When** constructed **Then** `selected == disk:X`; when it is hidden by `show_disks = false`, the first visible key is selected.
- **Given** `show_disks = false` and 4 disks **When** `PerfSelectVisibleDevice { index: 2 }` dispatches **Then** the third visible card (GPU → the third of CPU, Memory, GPU, nets) is selected (`f3_selects_third_visible_card_skipping_hidden`).
- **Given** the first card selected **When** `PerfSelectPrevDevice` dispatches **Then** the selection is unchanged.
- **Given** a snapshot that changes only memory series **When** installed **Then** the Memory card's lines re-format and the CPU card's `lines` are pointer-equal to before; `render_count` increased by 1.
- **Given** a snapshot that changes nothing the sidebar draws (a process sweep) **When** installed **Then** `render_count` is unchanged.
- **Given** visible card kinds CPU, Memory, Disk **When** demand is read from the aggregator **Then** `disks == true`, `nets == false`, `gpus == false`, `cpu == Total`.
- **Given** `select(key)` **When** called **Then** `UiState.performance.selected_device == key` after the debounce and `SidebarEvent::Selected(key)` was emitted once.

title: E24: Details grid model: KvRow, fallback words, tooltips, change-only formatting (pages/performance/details.rs)
description:
## Context
Every device page ends with a three-column "Details" grid of label-over-value pairs. The page keeps a `KeyValueModel` and re-formats a value only when its bits change; validity maps to the PERF-013 words with their tooltips; some rows hide when missing. Sources: PERF-012, PERF-013, R-050, UI-PRF-021, UI-FND-025 (`TlKeyValueGrid`, `TlValue`), table (d).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/details.rs`:

```rust
pub struct KvRow { pub label: &'static str /* Fluent key */, pub value: SharedString, pub validity: Validity, pub tooltip: Option<SharedString>, pub action: Option<Box<dyn Action>>, pub link: bool, pub bits: u64 }
pub struct KeyValueModel { pub rows: Vec<KvRow>, scratch: String }
pub enum Fallback { NeedsSetup, NotSupported, NotReported, Unavailable, Unknown }
impl KeyValueModel {
    pub fn set_valid(&mut self, label: &'static str, bits: u64, write: impl FnOnce(&mut String)) -> bool;  // formats only when bits differ from the row's; returns true when the text changed
    pub fn set_text(&mut self, label: &'static str, text: &str) -> bool;
    pub fn set_fallback(&mut self, label: &'static str, validity: Validity, fallback: Fallback, reason: Option<&str>) -> bool;
    pub fn set_stale(&mut self, label: &'static str, age_ns: u64) -> bool;     // keeps the last value, validity Stale, tooltip "Last updated {age} ago"
    pub fn set_tooltip(&mut self, label: &'static str, text: Option<SharedString>);
    pub fn hide(&mut self, label: &'static str); pub fn show(&mut self, label: &'static str);   // hidden rows are skipped by the grid (PERF-013 hidden-when-missing list)
    pub fn to_kv_rows(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = TlKvRow<'_>>;   // for TlKeyValueGrid
    pub fn copy_into(&self, out: &mut String);   // "    Label: value" per visible row, PERF-011 (E24-016 uses it)
}
pub fn fallback_word(v: Validity, f: Fallback) -> (&'static str, Option<&'static str> /* tooltip */);
```

Word and tooltip table (`text_secondary` for every non-valid word):

| Validity | Word | Tooltip |
|---|---|---|
| WarmingUp | `Collecting…` | none |
| Stale | the last value | `Last updated {age} ago` (short age, table (d)) |
| Restricted | `Restricted` | `Needs administrator access.` (from P3 `Needs administrator access. Click the shield to grant it.`; the string is one Fluent key `validity-restricted-tooltip` owned by E15-A2, read here) |
| Unsupported + NeedsSetup | `Needs setup` | `Needs setup. Open Additional Setup…`; `link = true`, `action = OpenAdditionalSetup { focus_row }` (shell action) |
| Unsupported + NotSupported | `Not supported` | `Not available on this device` |
| Unsupported + NotReported | `Not reported` | none |
| Failed | `Unavailable` | `Could not read: {reason}` |
| Unknown (enum or status unknown) | `Unknown` | none |

Grid rendering helper: `pub fn render_details(model: &KeyValueModel, m: &UiMetrics, theme: &TlTheme, cx) -> impl IntoElement` builds `TlKeyValueGrid` in stacked layout with `.columns(3)`, `.row_height(46 × ui_scale)` (`kv_row_h`), `.column_gap(sp6)` (`kv_col_gap`), label `t_sm` `text_secondary`, value `t_base` `text_primary` `tnum`; link values in `accent`; a value with a tooltip or action gets a dotted underline on hover; rows fill left to right, top to bottom in model order.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a row with `bits = 0x1` **When** `set_valid(label, 0x1, ..)` is called **Then** the closure does not run and it returns false; with `0x2` it runs and returns true.
- **Given** `set_fallback(label, Unsupported, NeedsSetup, None)` **When** read **Then** `value == "Needs setup"`, `link == true`, the action is `OpenAdditionalSetup` and the tooltip is `Needs setup. Open Additional Setup…` (`kv_grid_fallback_words_per_validity` covers every row of the table).
- **Given** `set_stale(label, 125_000_000_000)` **When** read **Then** the value text is unchanged and the tooltip is `Last updated 2m 5s ago`.
- **Given** `hide("Serial")` **When** `to_kv_rows` iterates **Then** the row is absent and `copy_into` omits it (`kv_grid_hidden_rows_rule`).
- **Given** 14 rows **When** rendered at 1000 px width **Then** the grid has 5 rows of 3 columns, pitch 46 px (`render_details` test through element bounds).

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/details.rs`: create
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append `perf-fallback-collecting = Collecting…`, `perf-fallback-restricted = Restricted`, `perf-fallback-needs-setup = Needs setup`, `perf-fallback-needs-setup-tooltip = Needs setup. Open Additional Setup…`, `perf-fallback-not-supported = Not supported`, `perf-fallback-not-supported-tooltip = Not available on this device`, `perf-fallback-not-reported = Not reported`, `perf-fallback-unavailable = Unavailable`, `perf-fallback-could-not-read = Could not read: {$reason}`, `perf-fallback-unknown = Unknown`, `perf-last-updated = Last updated {$age} ago`, `perf-details-heading = Details` (chain edit)
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_performance.rs`: change

## Tests
- `details::tests::set_valid_formats_only_on_bits_change`
- `ui_performance.rs::kv_grid_fallback_words_per_validity`
- `ui_performance.rs::kv_grid_stale_keeps_value`
- `ui_performance.rs::kv_grid_hidden_rows_rule`
- `ui_performance.rs::details_grid_three_columns_46px`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `Failed` rows carry `Could not read: {reason}` from `SourceHealth.last_error` passed by the page.
- Validity: the full PERF-013 table.
- Accessibility: label and value are adjacent text; link rows are reachable through the page's focus order (E24-022 adds the selection fallback and context menu).
- Performance: 12 to 30 rows; a value re-formats only on bits change; the grid lives inside the page's `.cached()` Details block.
- Privacy: `copy_into` is the only path to the clipboard and prints exactly the visible rows (D-007 is enforced by never reading serials, E25).

## Notes
`TlKeyValueGrid`, `TlKvRow`, `TlValue` are E15-A2 (UI-FND-025); pass `.row_height(px(46.) × ui_scale)` because the Performance file owns `kv_row_h = 46` (UI-FND-025's 56 is its default). `OpenAdditionalSetup { focus_row: Option<SetupRow> }` is the shell's action (UI-PRF-052); `SetupRow` is `tl_model::command::SetupStep`'s UI twin declared by E29 (`window/setup.rs`), so until E29 lands pass `focus_row: None` through the unit form `OpenAdditionalSetup` declared by E20-A1. Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

Grid column gap stays sp7 and no dotted hover underline: TlKeyValueGrid has no setters for them.

title: E24: DevicePage trait and DevicePageFrame: header, toggles, graph area, Details, blocks, page builder (pages/performance/page.rs)
description:
## Context
Every device page has the same frame: a header row with the type word, the model and the page toggles, the graph area, the "Details" heading, the grid and page blocks, inside a scrolling area with `page_pad`. This bead writes the trait pages implement and the frame that renders them, plus the builder that maps a device kind to its page entity (CPU here, the other arms are E25 chain edits).     fn focus_order(&self) -> SmallVec<[FocusHandle; 4]>;        // header toggles then block controls (UI-SHL-121)

```rust
}
pub struct DevicePageFrame<'a> { pub page: &'a dyn DevicePage, pub m: &'a UiMetrics, pub theme: &'a TlTheme }
impl RenderOnce for DevicePageFrame<'_> { .. }
pub fn header_text(kind: DeviceKind, number: u16, entry: &DeviceEntry, system: &SystemSnapshot) -> (SharedString, SharedString);
pub fn build_page(key: &DeviceKey, row: &DeviceRow, hub, demand, cx) -> AnyView;   // match row.kind { /* E24-009: Cpu arm */ _ => placeholder }  (E24-009 adds `Cpu => cx.new(|cx| CpuPage::new(key, row, hub, demand, cx)).into()` and E25 one arm per other kind, each as a chain edit, R-262; the placeholder renders the frame with an empty graph area and an empty model, and never panics)
pub const PAGE_PAD: f32 = 16.; pub const PAGE_HEADER_H: f32 = 36.; pub const DETAILS_GAP: f32 = 24.; pub const PAGE_MIN_W: f32 = 400.;
pub const GRAPH_H_SINGLE: f32 = 240.; pub const GRAPH_H_STACKED: f32 = 150.; pub const GRAPH_H_OVERALL: f32 = 300.; pub const SECONDARY_GRAPH_H: f32 = 120.;
```

title: E24: CPU per-core grid wrapper: cell specs from topology, headings, tooltips, offline cells (pages/performance/cpu_grid.rs)
description:
## Context
The per-core grid is a `ChartGridView` whose cells come from the CPU topology: one cell per logical CPU titled "CPU N", a kernel overlay per cell when the toggle is on, the "Total"/"Kernel" legend in cell 0, a tooltip "Core C, thread T, 4200 MHz" on each heading, and "Offline" for CPUs that are off. Sources: PERF-028, PERF-029, PERF-031 (marks are E24-019), UI-PRF-002, UI-PRF-023 (per-core cell), ADR-003 `CpuTopology`, ADR-014 fixture.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/cpu_grid.rs`:

```rust
pub struct CpuGrid { pub view: Entity<ChartGridView>, cores: Arc<CpuTopology>, kernel: bool, scratch: String }
impl CpuGrid {
    pub fn new(hub, topology: Arc<CpuTopology>, logical_devices: &[DeviceIdx] /* DeviceIdx per logical CPU id, from the catalog's CpuLogical entries */, kernel: bool, range_ns: u64, smooth: bool, theme: &TlTheme, cx) -> Self;
    pub fn set_kernel(&mut self, on: bool, cx);          // rebuilds the ChartGridSpec with or without overlay series
    pub fn set_topology(&mut self, topology, logical_devices, cx);   // CPU hotplug: offline cells, new cells
    pub fn update_clocks(&mut self, per_cpu_mhz: &[(u16, f32, Validity)], cx);  // refreshes heading tooltips at 1 Hz, re-formatting only changed values
    pub fn set_range(&mut self, range_ns, cx); pub fn set_smooth(&mut self, smooth, cx);
}
pub fn cell_specs(topology: &CpuTopology, logical_devices: &[DeviceIdx], kernel: bool, out: &mut Vec<GridCellSpec>);
pub fn heading_tooltip(core: u16, thread: u16, mhz: Option<u32>, out: &mut String);   // "Core 3, thread 1, 4200 MHz"; without a clock "Core 3, thread 1"
```

Rules:
- One cell per logical CPU id in ascending id order; `heading = "CPU {id}"`; `fill_series = SeriesId { device: logical_devices[id], metric: CPU_TOTAL }`; `overlay_series = Some(SeriesId { .., CPU_KERNEL })` when `kernel`; `offline = !topology.online.contains(id)`; `tooltip` from `heading_tooltip(core_id, thread index within the core's `logical` list, mhz)`.
- `ChartGridSpec { fill: theme.graph.cpu_fill, line: theme.graph.cpu_line, overlay_line: theme.graph.kernel_line, y: Fixed 0..100, cell_min_w: 120, cell_h: 112, gap: sp4 (8), legend: [("Total", Solid), ("Kernel", Dashed)] when kernel else [("Total", Solid)], value_fmt: Percent, hover: false (E19-015 turns it on in P2) }`.
- The value label per cell is the newest total percent (`6.1%`), formatted by the grid element (E19-010).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a topology with 16 logical CPUs, all online **When** `cell_specs` runs with `kernel = true` **Then** 16 specs, headings `CPU 0`..`CPU 15`, every `overlay_series.is_some()`, cell 0's legend has two entries (`cpu_grid_16_cores_6_cols` also asserts `grid_layout(16, 1000, 120, 8).cols == 6`).
- **Given** `kernel = false` **When** `set_kernel(false)` runs **Then** every `overlay_series` is `None` and the legend has one entry.
- **Given** CPU 5 offline **When** `cell_specs` runs **Then** spec 5 has `offline == true`.
- **Given** core 3 with logical CPUs `[3, 11]` and 4200 MHz on CPU 11 **When** `heading_tooltip` runs for CPU 11 **Then** `Core 3, thread 1, 4200 MHz`.
- **Given** `update_clocks` twice with the same values **When** run **Then** no tooltip `SharedString` is re-allocated the second time (bits compare).

- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append `perf-cpu-cell = CPU {$n}`, `perf-cpu-cell-tooltip = Core {$core}, thread {$thread}, {$mhz} MHz`, `perf-cpu-cell-tooltip-noclock = Core {$core}, thread {$thread}`, `perf-cpu-offline = Offline`, `perf-legend-total = Total`, `perf-legend-kernel = Kernel` (chain edit)

## Tests
- `ui_cpu_page.rs::cpu_grid_16_cores_6_cols`
- `ui_cpu_page.rs::cpu_grid_kernel_toggle_changes_overlays`

title: E10: handle search walk with globs, progress and cancel (workers/handle_search.rs)
description:
## Context
Search File Handles walks `/proc/*/fd` readlinks, `/proc/*/maps` paths, `cwd`, `exe` and `root` on the blocking pool, cancellable between PIDs, matching a case-insensitive substring with `*` and `?` globs, with progress "Retrieving file handles... 42% (18 234 total handles)" and a footer "Searched 412 of 530 processes. 118 need administrator rights." when other users' processes were skipped. Sources: PROC-096, UI-PWN-030, ADR-003 (`HandleSearchState { search, phase, progress, chunks, searched, total, skipped }`, `HandleHit`), E05-A3 (`proc/handles.rs` walk), ADR-006 (helper `ReadProcessFiles { fd_list, maps, cwd, exe }`), E08-003.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/workers/handle_search.rs`:

```rust
pub struct HandleSearch { pub id: SearchId, pattern: Matcher /* lowercase; glob when it contains * or ? */, include_maps: bool, privileged: bool, cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>, pids: Vec<u32>, next: usize, hits: Vec<HandleHit>, total_handles: u64, searched: u32, skipped: u32 }
pub enum Phase { Init, Retrieving, Searching, Done, Failed }
impl HandleSearch {
    pub fn new(id: SearchId, pattern: &str, include_maps: bool, privileged: bool, sys_root: &SysRoot) -> Self;   // lists pids (Init)
    /// Walks up to `budget` pids, returns the state to publish; `done()` when finished or cancelled.
    pub fn step(&mut self, sys_root: &SysRoot, helper: Option<&dyn RestrictedReader>, budget: usize) -> Arc<HandleSearchState>;
    pub fn cancel(&self);
}
pub struct Matcher { .. }   // `*` any run, `?` one char, else substring; case-insensitive on lowercase
```

Per pid: `fd/*` readlinks (type `fd`), `maps` paths when `include_maps` (type `mmap`, de-duplicated per pid), `cwd`, `exe`, `root` (types `cwd`, `exe`, `root`); each hit is `HandleHit { key: ProcessKey, name, user, kind, fd: Option<u32>, path }`. EACCES on `fd` or `maps` of another user's process: with `helper` Some and `privileged`, `read_files(key, [FdList, Maps, Cwd, Exe])`; else count the pid in `skipped`. Progress is `searched / pids.len()`; `phase` moves Init → Retrieving → Searching (after the first budget) → Done; a walk error that is not EACCES sets `Failed` ("Handle search failed").

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** pattern `"*.log"` and a fixture where pid 100 has `fd/3 → /var/log/x.log` and pid 101 has `cwd → /var/log` **When** stepped to completion **Then** hits are `(100, fd, 3, "/var/log/x.log")` and `(101, cwd, None, "/var/log")`, `searched == pids.len()`, `phase == Done`.
- **Given** `include_maps = false` **When** a match exists only in `maps` **Then** no hit.
- **Given** the other-user fixture pid **When** stepped without a helper **Then** `skipped == 1` and no hit from it; with a fake helper returning its files **Then** the hit appears and `skipped == 0`.
- **Given** `cancel()` after the first step **When** stepped again **Then** `done()` is true and `searched` did not grow.
- **Given** `Matcher::new("FIRE")` **When** matched against "/opt/firefox/firefox" **Then** true; `"fi?e"` matches "fire"; `"fi*x"` matches "firefox".
- **Given** a budget of 10 pids and 530 pids **When** stepped once **Then** `progress == 10 / 530` and `phase == Searching`.

- `handle_search.rs::tests::fixture_walk_hits`

title: E10: ProcessesSource wrapping the tl-collect sweep (workers/processes.rs)
description:
## Context
The `Processes` worker runs one whole `/proc` sweep per `spawn_blocking` job at `processes.interval_ms` (default 1000, range 250..=10000) while the table or any process consumer is visible, or recording is on, and stops otherwise. It wraps E05's synchronous sweep and app grouping in the `Source` trait and publishes `SourceUpdate::Processes(ProcessSweep)`. `EngineMode::LowMemory` selects the stripped sweep from `workers/lowmem.rs` (E32 adds that arm). Sources: ADR-004 (worker row, one job per sweep), ADR-008 (schedule row, hidden policy), ADR-016 (sources, FD policy, metadata refresh), PROC-002, PROC-004, R-137, R-138, E08-003, E08-004, E05-A1, E05-A2.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/workers/processes.rs`:

```rust
pub struct ProcessesSource { sweeper: tl_collect::proc::Sweeper /* E05-A1's stateful sweep: keeps per-key counter baselines and the metadata cache */, apps: tl_collect::apps::AppIndex /* E05-A2 */, cfg: Arc<EngineConfig>, last: Option<(TimeNs, TimeNs)> }
impl ProcessesSource { pub fn new(cfg: Arc<EngineConfig>) -> Self; }
impl Source for ProcessesSource {
    fn id(&self) -> SourceId { SourceId::Processes }
    fn period(&self, d: &Demand, s: &EngineSettings) -> Option<Duration> {
        let wanted = d.process_table || !d.detail_keys.is_empty() || d.gpu_process || d.recording || !d.details.is_empty() || !d.affinity_targets.is_empty() || !d.graph_targets.is_empty();   // graph_targets: R-154 item 2, PROC-093
        wanted.then(|| Duration::from_millis(s.interval_ms.clamp(250, 10_000) as u64))
    }
    fn sample(mut self) -> (Self, SourceUpdate) {
        let observed_start = now_boot_ns();
        let out = self.sweeper.sweep(&self.cfg.sys_root, &mut self.apps);   // records with FieldValidity, app and unit cgroup stats, system_threads, file_nr (from /proc/sys/fs/file-nr, R-166 B3-7), online_cpus; EACCES → Restricted, never an error
        let observed_end = now_boot_ns();
        (self, SourceUpdate::Processes(ProcessSweep { observed_start, observed_end, records: out.records, app_stats: out.app_stats, unit_stats: out.unit_stats, system_threads: out.system_threads, file_nr: out.file_nr, online_cpus: out.online_cpus }))
    }
    fn reset_baselines(&mut self) { self.sweeper.reset_baselines() }   // rates become WarmingUp at the next sweep
}
pub fn spec() -> WorkerSpec;   // id Processes, name "processes", modes &[Full, LowMemory]
pub fn factory(cfg: Arc<EngineConfig>, io: WorkerIo) -> WorkerFactory {
    match cfg.mode { EngineMode::Full => /* source::run(cx, io.clone(), ProcessesSource::new(cfg.clone())) per generation */, EngineMode::LowMemory => /* E32 chain-edits this arm to `workers::lowmem::source(cfg)`; until then it runs the full sweep */ }
}
```

A sweep error that is not per-field (for example `/proc` unreadable) returns `SourceUpdate::Health { Failed, last_error }` from `sample`, not a panic. The per-key `Restricted` rule (other users' `io`, `exe`, `cmdline` where applicable) is E05's; the worker passes the result through.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `Demand::default()` (nothing visible) **When** `period` is read **Then** `None`.
- **Given** `process_table = true` and `interval_ms = 2000` **When** `period` is read **Then** `Some(2 s)`; with `interval_ms = 100` **Then** `Some(250 ms)` (clamped).
- **Given** `process_table = false` but `detail_keys` non-empty **When** `period` is read **Then** `Some(interval)`.
- **Given** `process_table = false`, `graph_targets = [(GraphTarget::Name("firefox"), cpu)]` and `interval_ms = 1000` **When** `period` is read **Then** `Some(1 s)`: a non-empty `graph_targets` runs the worker at `processes.interval_ms` even when the table is hidden (R-154 item 2, PROC-093).
- **Given** the `owner-desktop` fixture root (E04-A1) **When** `sample()` runs **Then** `records.len()` equals the fixture's pid count, every record has `key.boot_id` equal to the fixture's boot id, `observed_end >= observed_start`, and no record has `NEW` or `EXITED` set (the reducer owns them).
- **Given** two samples 1 s apart on a fixture with changing `utime` **When** compared **Then** the first has `Cpu` validity `WarmingUp` and the second `Valid`; after `reset_baselines()` the next is `WarmingUp` again.
- **Given** `EngineMode::LowMemory` **When** `factory` is called at this bead **Then** it compiles and runs the full sweep (the E32 arm replaces it).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/processes.rs`: create

## Tests
- `tests/lab_processes.rs` (E10-002) holds the cases; this bead adds `processes.rs::tests::period_table` for the first three criteria and `processes.rs::tests::period_graph_targets_without_table` for the fourth.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `/proc` unreadable → `Health { Failed }` once per sweep; the supervisor is not involved (expected condition).
- Validity: passes E05's `FieldValidity` through unchanged.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one blocking job per sweep; the 2,000-process sweep gate (15 ms) is E05's bench; this worker adds one `Vec` move.
- Privacy: never logs records; `tracing::debug!(count = records.len())` only.

## Notes
Depends on E05-A1, E05-A2, E08-A1. Use the entry-point names E05-A1 and E05-A2 chose if they differ from `Sweeper::sweep` and `AppIndex`; the behaviour contract above is what matters. Tray process graphs (P3) use `Demand.graph_targets` like every other process graph; `TrayDemand` has no process list (R-154 item 3, R-156 item 2). The reducer appends the per-target samples (E09-029); this worker only keeps the sweep running. `ProcessSweep.file_nr` is filled by the E05 sweep; the reducer copies it into `TableTotals.handles` (R-166 B3-7). Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E10: Processes worker LabRuntime tests on fixtures (lab_processes.rs)
description:
## Context
LabRuntime tests for the `Processes` worker against fixture roots: rate follows demand and settings, hidden gives zero sweeps, recording keeps sweeps, a fixture change shows up as a new record with the right metadata refresh rule, and `Restricted` fields stay `Restricted`. Sources: ADR-013 (fixtures, lab tests), ADR-008, PROC-002, ADR-016 (metadata refresh every 10 sweeps and on `comm` change), E10-001.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_processes.rs` with a `FixtureRoot` helper that copies `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/<name>` into a temp dir so tests can mutate it (add a pid directory, change `comm`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `process_table = true`, `interval_ms = 1000` **When** 5 s run **Then** 5 `Processes` updates arrived at 1 s spacing.
- **Given** `any_surface_visible = false`, `process_table = false`, `recording = false` **When** 60 s run **Then** zero updates.
- **Given** `process_table = false`, `recording = true` **When** 10 s run **Then** 10 updates.
- **Given** a new pid directory is added to the fixture between sweeps **When** the next update arrives **Then** it contains the new key and the previous keys unchanged.
- **Given** a pid's `comm` file changes **When** the next sweep runs **Then** that record's `meta.comm` and `meta.name` changed in that very sweep (immediate refresh on `comm` change), while a changed `cmdline` without a `comm` change is picked up only by the 10th sweep after the last refresh.

title: E10: ProcessDetail PSS and USS for detail_keys through the FD cache
E10: ProcessDetail Properties tab payloads at the ADR-008 rates
description:
## Context
Properties windows register `DetailDemand { target, tab }` (max 16); the `ProcessDetail` worker reads the demanded tab of each demanded target at `processes.interval_ms`, except Memory maps (`smaps` at most once per second), Environment (once on open and again only on `DetailRefresh`), and Strings (never from demand). The General tab always loads too (title and exited state). Payloads are published as `Arc<TabPayload>` per tab and reused when unchanged. Sources: UI-PWN-002, ADR-008 (`details` row), PROC-078 to PROC-083, PROC-085 (`AppGeneral`, `AppProcesses`), ADR-003 (`TabPayload`, `DetailTab`), ADR-015 (environment never logged), E05-A3 (`proc/detail.rs` readers), E08-003, E10-A2.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/process_detail.rs`:

```rust
pub const SMAPS_MIN_PERIOD: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);
struct TabState { last_hash: u64, last_read_ns: TimeNs, env_loaded: bool }
impl ProcessDetailSource {
    fn period(..) -> Option<Duration> { /* PSS rule OR (!d.details.is_empty() && Some(interval_ms)) OR affinity rule (E10-005); when both PSS and details apply use min(1 s, interval) */ }
    fn read_tab(&mut self, target: DetailTarget, tab: DetailTab, now: TimeNs, interval: Duration) -> Option<DetailsUpdate>;
}
```

Per tab, using E05-A3's readers (`tl_collect::proc::detail`): `General` → PROC-078 fields except hashes and package status (E10-005): started, ppid, user with uid/euid/suid, priority text "Nice 0, SCHED_OTHER, kernel prio 120" plus autogroup, affinity text and "(threads differ)", hardening (PIE, NX stack, RELRO, shadow stack, ASLR, NoNewPrivs, Seccomp), architecture, exe, location category, cmdline, cwd, root, cgroup, unit, app id, memory and I/O and disk counters; `Threads` → PROC-079 columns from `task/<tid>/{stat,status,wchan,comm}`; `Fds` → PROC-080 (`readlinkat` on `fd/*`, `fdinfo` fields, type classification, socket inode left for the connections map); `Maps` → PROC-081 (`maps` plus `smaps` RSS, not more often than `SMAPS_MIN_PERIOD`); `Security` → PROC-082 (`status` caps, `loginuid`, `sessionid`, `attr/current`, `ns/*` with the "Same as tasklens" fallback when PID 1's namespaces are unreadable); `Environment` → PROC-083 (`environ` capped at 1 MiB; read only when `env_loaded == false` or a `DetailRefresh` for that target and tab is pending); `AppGeneral` → PROC-085 (cgroup files, desktop index fields); `AppProcesses` → member keys. Each read yields `(TabPayload, Validity)`; `EACCES` → `Restricted` payload with no data and, when `helper` is `Some`, a `read_files` attempt first. The payload is published only when its hash changed (`FxHasher` over the payload's `Debug`-free serialized form, or a `PartialEq` compare with the previous `Arc`); the `Arc` is reused otherwise. Targets not in demand are forgotten.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `details = [{ Process(A), Threads }]` and `interval_ms = 500` **When** 2 s run **Then** 4 `Tab { Threads }` reads and 4 `Tab { General }` reads happened for A, and none for other tabs.
- **Given** `details = [{ Process(A), Maps }]` and `interval_ms = 250` **When** 2 s run **Then** `smaps` was read at most 2 times (1 Hz cap) while `maps` was read 8 times.
- **Given** `details = [{ Process(A), Environment }]` **When** 5 s run **Then** `environ` was read once; **When** `DetailRefresh { Process(A), Environment }` arrives **Then** it is read once more.
- **Given** an unchanged Threads tab **When** two samples run **Then** only the first produced a `DetailsUpdate::Tab` for it (the second reuses the `Arc`; no message).
- **Given** a target whose `environ` is EACCES and `helper == None` **When** read **Then** the `Environment` payload has validity `Restricted` and is empty.
- **Given** `details = [{ App(G), AppGeneral }]` **When** read **Then** the payload has the cgroup `anon`, `memory.swap.current`, process count and the primary's cmdline.
- **Given** 17 `DetailDemand`s **When** applied **Then** only the first 16 are served (cap) and a `warn` is logged once.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/process_detail.rs`: extend

## Tests
- `lab_details.rs` (E10-007): `tabs_read_at_interval_plus_general`, `smaps_capped_1hz`, `environment_once_then_on_refresh`, `unchanged_tab_reuses_arc`, `restricted_without_helper`, `app_general_payload`, `details_cap_16`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: per-tab read errors are `Validity::Failed` with the payload's `error: Option<Arc<str>>`; the worker never restarts for them.
- Validity: `Valid`, `Restricted`, `Failed`, `Missing` (process gone: the General payload sets `exited = true` and the window title gets " (not running)").
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: at most 16 targets; `smaps` is the expensive read and is capped.
- Privacy: environment values and command lines live only in payloads; never logged; the env mask is UI-side (R-099).

## Notes

It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E10: ProcessDetail hashes, VerifyPackage and affinity masks
description:
## Context
Three more `ProcessDetail` duties: `ComputeHashes(key)` once per window open (SHA-256 and MD5 of `/proc/<pid>/exe`, cached by (dev, inode, mtime), shared with Open in VirusTotal), `VerifyPackage(key)` (compare the file's sha256 with the package mtree), and affinity masks for `affinity_targets` at 1 Hz while a Set Affinity dialog is open (`mask` from `Cpus_allowed_list`, `cpuset_limit` from the cgroup's `cpuset.cpus.effective`). Sources: PROC-074, PROC-078 (column 2), UI-PWN-002, UI-PWN-021 (affinity), ADR-008 (`affinity_targets` row), E05-A3 (`hash.rs`, `proc/detail.rs`), E08-003 (`DetailsUpdate::Affinity`), E10-004.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/process_detail.rs`:
- `ComputeHashes(key)` handler: `tl_collect::hash::exe_hashes(&sys_root, key)` on the blocking pool (it already is: inside `sample`), result written into the General payload fields `sha256: Option<Arc<str>>`, `md5`, `hash_error: Option<Arc<str>>` ("Failed to compute one or more hashes", "Executable path unavailable"); cached per (dev, inode, mtime) in `self.hash_cache: FxHashMap<(u64, u64, i64), (Arc<str>, Arc<str>)>` capped at 64 entries.
- `VerifyPackage(key)` handler: `tl_collect::apps::verify_package(exe_path, sha256)` → General payload `package_status: Arc<str>` (E05 defines the strings: matches, differs, not packaged, unavailable) and `packager`.
- Affinity: `period` also returns `Some(1 s)` when `!d.affinity_targets.is_empty()`; `sample` emits `DetailsUpdate::Affinity { entries }` for every target (max 256) with `AffinityInfo { mask, cpuset_limit }`; a gone process is skipped.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `ComputeHashes(A)` for a fixture exe **When** processed **Then** the next General payload for A has the expected sha256 and md5 hex strings (lowercase) and a second `ComputeHashes(A)` does not re-read the file (cache hit counter).
- **Given** an exe that is unreadable **When** processed **Then** `hash_error == "Executable path unavailable"` and `sha256 == None`.
- **Given** `affinity_targets = [A, B]` **When** 3 s run **Then** 3 `Affinity` updates with 2 entries each, `mask` matching the fixture's `Cpus_allowed_list` and `cpuset_limit` matching `cpuset.cpus.effective`.
- **Given** `affinity_targets` empty and no details **When** read **Then** `period` is `None`.
- **Given** `VerifyPackage(A)` **When** processed **Then** the General payload `package_status` is one of E05's strings and `packager` is filled when the package index has it.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/process_detail.rs`: extend

## Tests
- `lab_details.rs` (E10-007): `hashes_once_and_cached`, `hashes_unreadable_exe`, `affinity_targets_1hz`, `affinity_off_when_empty`, `verify_package_status`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: hash and package failures are payload strings, not `WorkerError`.
- Validity: N/A beyond the payload.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: hashing a 100 MiB binary takes about 300 ms on the blocking pool; the sample that does it is `Late` once (accepted).
- Privacy: exe paths of other users' processes are never logged (ADR-015).

## Notes
Depends on E10-004. Phase P2. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E10: ProcessDetail StringScan with cancel and limits
description:
## Context
The Strings tab scans process memory only on the user's "Scan" click: `Command::StringScan { scan, key, opts }` streams progress and results into the Strings tab payload; `CancelStringScan(scan)` stops it between chunks. With `ptrace_scope = 1` (this machine) a non-descendant needs CAP_SYS_PTRACE, so the in-process scan runs only when `ptrace_scope == 0` or the target is a child of tasklens; otherwise the payload is `Restricted` and the helper path (E29) takes over. Limits: 1,000,000 strings or 256 MiB of text. Sources: PROC-084, UI-PWN-017, ADR-006 (helper `ScanStrings`), E05-A3 (`proc/strings.rs`), ADR-003 (`ScanId`, `StringScanOpts`), E10-A2.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/process_detail.rs`:

```rust
pub const SCAN_MAX_STRINGS: u32 = 1_000_000;
pub const SCAN_MAX_BYTES: u64 = 256 << 20;
pub const SCAN_CHUNK: usize = 1 << 20;   // process_vm_readv chunk
struct ScanState { id: ScanId, key: ProcessKey, opts: StringScanOpts, cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>, progress_pct: u8, found: u32, bytes: u64, regions_done: usize }
```

`StringScan` handler: check access (`/proc/sys/kernel/yama/ptrace_scope` and whether `key.pid`'s ancestor chain contains `getpid()`); if not allowed → publish `Tab { Strings, validity: Restricted }` with `payload.message = "Strings unavailable: needs administrator rights"` (the UI shows the Enable button); else run `tl_collect::proc::strings::scan(&sys_root, key, &opts, &cancel, |batch, progress| ..)` across several `sample()` calls (one region set per call so the worker loop keeps checkpointing: the scan state persists in `self`, and `period` returns `Some(0 ms → clamp 50 ms)` while a scan is active) publishing a Strings payload with `progress: "Scanning process memory... 42%  18234 strings found"`-ready numbers (`progress_pct`, `found`), the rows so far (address hex, encoding, length, value), and `done`. Stop at the limits with `message = "String scan stopped: not enough memory."`; read failures `"Failed to read process memory."`; kernel threads `"Strings unavailable for this process."`. `CancelStringScan(scan)` sets `cancel` and publishes the final payload with `cancelled = true`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `ptrace_scope = 0` (fixture flag) and a fixture process with a readable memory image (test double for `process_vm_readv` behind a trait in `tl-collect`) **When** `StringScan` runs **Then** payloads arrive with rising `progress_pct` and the final one has `done == true` and the expected strings.
- **Given** `ptrace_scope = 1` and a non-child target **When** `StringScan` runs **Then** one `Restricted` payload with the "needs administrator rights" message and no memory read.
- **Given** `CancelStringScan` after the first chunk **When** processed **Then** no further chunks are read and the final payload has `cancelled == true`.
- **Given** a double that yields 1,000,001 strings **When** scanned **Then** the scan stops at 1,000,000 with the "not enough memory" message.
- **Given** a kernel thread key **When** `StringScan` runs **Then** the message is "Strings unavailable for this process.".

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/process_detail.rs`: extend
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_details.rs`: add the cases

## Tests
- `lab_details.rs::string_scan_streams_progress`
- `lab_details.rs::string_scan_restricted_under_yama`
- `lab_details.rs::string_scan_cancel`
- `lab_details.rs::string_scan_limit`
- `lab_details.rs::string_scan_kernel_thread`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: payload messages as above; never `WorkerError`.
- Validity: `Restricted` without access.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: 1 MiB chunks; the worker yields between region sets so other detail reads keep running.
- Privacy: scanned strings are user-requested process memory; never logged; the pattern of the scan options is never logged.

## Notes
Depends on E10-A2, E10-004, E05-A3. Phase P3. The helper path (E29) plugs into `RestrictedReader` with a streaming variant E29 defines. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E16-007 TlDialog confirmation windows
description:
## Context
Builds `TlDialog`, the confirmation window body and footer every "are you sure" prompt uses, opened as a modal `TlSecondaryWindow` of kind Confirmation. It fixes the one focus and Enter rule for every confirmation (R-104). Spec phase P1; priority 0 because it sits in the E16-A2 group that E18-A2 (P0) needs. Sources: UI-FND-021 (confirmation body), R-104, UI-SHL-091, APP-045 (title "tasklens", modal to parent), R-083.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/components/dialog.rs` (add `pub mod dialog;` to `components/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub enum DialogIcon { Warning, Info, None }
pub struct TlDialog { text: SharedString, heading: Option<SharedString>, icon: DialogIcon,
                      action_label: SharedString, destructive: bool, extra: Option<AnyElement>,
                      checkbox: Option<(SharedString, bool)>, title: SharedString }
impl TlDialog {
    pub fn confirm(text: impl Into<SharedString>, action_label: impl Into<SharedString>) -> Self; // title "tasklens", icon Info, not destructive
    pub fn destructive(self) -> Self;            // Danger action button, icon Warning, focus on Cancel
    pub fn heading(self, text: impl Into<SharedString>) -> Self;
    pub fn title(self, title: impl Into<SharedString>) -> Self;   // default "tasklens" (APP-045, R-083)
    pub fn extra(self, el: impl IntoElement) -> Self;             // owner lines under the text (entry name, path, target list)
    pub fn checkbox(self, label: impl Into<SharedString>, initial: bool) -> Self; // "Do not ask again" where a spec allows; none in P1
    pub fn open(self, parent: &mut Window, cx: &mut App,
                on_result: impl FnOnce(DialogResult, &mut Window, &mut App) + 'static) -> gpui::Result<()>;
}
pub enum DialogResult { Confirmed { checkbox: bool }, Cancelled }
```
Layout (width 420, height content-sized 140 to 320, min 360 × 120, not resizable): padding `sp6` (16). Left a leading icon `i_lg` 20: Warning = Lucide `triangle-alert` in `status.warning` (destructive actions), Info = `info` in `status.info`. Right of it, gap `sp5`: optional heading `t_md` 500 `text_primary`, one line; then the text `t_base` `text_primary`, wrapping, at most 6 lines; then the owner's extra element (`t_base` or `t_sm`); then the optional `TlCheckbox`. Footer right-aligned, gap `sp4`, buttons md (28 high, min width 72): Cancel (`TlButton::Secondary`, label "Cancel") left of the action button (`Primary`, or `Danger` when destructive). Button labels name the result ("End tree", "Delete", "Reset"), never "Yes".
Behaviour (R-104, one rule for every confirmation):
- Focus on open: Cancel when destructive; the action button otherwise.
- Enter activates the focused button (bound on the dialog window root; not while a multi-line input has focus). So a stray Enter in a destructive confirmation cancels; the destructive button needs Tab then Enter, or a click.
- Esc always cancels. Closing the window by its X cancels.
- Tab order: content (checkbox if any), Cancel, action, then the pin.
- The window is modal to `parent` (GPUI `WindowKind::Dialog`, xdg_dialog_v1); the parent's content gets `derived.overlay` and ignores input until the dialog closes.
- `on_result` is called exactly once.
In-window kit `Dialog` is used only for sub-prompts inside a secondary window; it reuses this body and footer through `TlDialog::render_body` (pub fn returning the body element).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a destructive confirmation **When** it opens **Then** Cancel has focus.
- **Given** a destructive confirmation just opened **When** Enter is pressed **Then** `on_result` receives `Cancelled`.
- **Given** a destructive confirmation **When** Tab then Enter is pressed **Then** `on_result` receives `Confirmed`.
- **Given** a non-destructive confirmation just opened **When** Enter is pressed **Then** `on_result` receives `Confirmed`.
- **Given** any confirmation **When** Esc is pressed **Then** `on_result` receives `Cancelled` and the window closes.
- **Given** a heading set **When** it renders **Then** the heading line uses `t_md` 500 above the text.
- **Given** a long text **When** it renders **Then** it wraps to at most 6 lines and the window height stays between 140 and 320.
- **Given** the dialog is open **When** the parent window receives a click **Then** the parent ignores it.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/components/dialog.rs`: create, with tests.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/components/mod.rs`: add `pub mod dialog;`.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_dialogs.rs`: add the tests below.

## Tests
- `tests/ui_dialogs.rs::destructive_focuses_cancel`
- `tests/ui_dialogs.rs::confirm_enter_runs_focused_button_escape_cancels` (both kinds)
- `tests/ui_dialogs.rs::tab_then_enter_confirms_destructive`
- `tests/ui_dialogs.rs::result_called_once_on_window_close`
- `tests/ui_dialogs.rs::parent_blocked_while_open`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: if the window cannot open, `open` returns `Err` and `on_result` is not called; the owner treats that as Cancelled and logs.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: the warning icon is always paired with text; buttons are keyboard reachable; focus rule above.
- Performance: one small view per confirmation.
- Privacy: owner texts may name a process; nothing is logged.

## Notes
- Owners' exact texts live in their specs (UI-PRC-014, UI-SHL-091, UI-SYS-047, UI-SYS-064); this bead fixes only shape and behaviour.
- Build rule: run cargo only through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <files>` (run `git add` on new files first). Never a bare `git commit`.
- Read `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` in the repo first. Sources: `docs/ui/foundation.md` UI-FND-021, `docs/RECONCILIATION.md` R-104, `docs/ui/shell.md` UI-SHL-091.

title: E16-008 TlSecondaryWindow frame and pin
description:
## Context
Builds `TlSecondaryWindow`, the frame every tasklens dialog, tool window and Properties window opens through: a client-drawn 34 px title bar with icon, title, the pin and the kit caption buttons, its own kit Root (so it has its own toasts and menus), the window kinds, Esc and Ctrl+W rules. Spec phase P1 (frame and pin drawn), P2 (pin working); priority 0 because the column picker (E18-A2, P0) opens through it. Sources: UI-FND-021, UI-SHL-090, APP-045, APP-009, R-073, PROC-056, ADR-010 decorations, D-006, R-083 (titles).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/components/window_frame.rs` (add `pub mod window_frame;` to `components/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub enum TlWindowKind { Confirmation, Tool { resizable: bool }, Run, Properties }
pub struct TlWindowSpec { pub kind: TlWindowKind, pub title: SharedString, pub size: Size<Pixels>,
                          pub min_size: Size<Pixels>, pub parent: Option<AnyWindowHandle>, pub key: Option<WindowKey> }
pub struct TlSecondaryWindow<V> { content: Entity<V>, pinned: bool, toasts: Entity<ToastQueue>, key: Option<WindowKey> }
impl TlSecondaryWindow<V: Render> {
    pub fn open(cx: &mut App, spec: TlWindowSpec, build: impl FnOnce(&mut Window, &mut App) -> Entity<V>) -> gpui::Result<WindowHandle<Root>>;
}
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, gpui::Action)] #[action(namespace = tasklens, no_json)]
pub struct ToggleAlwaysOnTop { pub window: WindowKey, pub caption: SharedString }  // R-176; the shell handles it: main window E20-022, secondary windows E20-029, KWin bridge only (R-177)
pub struct CloseSecondaryWindow;                              // unit Action, namespace tasklens, bound to ctrl-w in context "TlWindow"
```
Window kinds (UI-FND-021 table):
| Kind | GPUI `WindowKind` | Modal | Default size | Min size | Resizable | Esc |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Confirmation | `Dialog` | yes, to its parent | width 420, height content-sized 140 to 320 | 360 × 120 | no | Cancel |
| Tool (Settings, Theme Editor, Shortcuts, Handle Search, About, Additional Setup, Crash Report) | `Floating` | no | per owner | 480 × 320 | yes (About, Crash Report: no) | closes |
| Run ("tasklens Run") | `Floating` | no | 480 × 248 fixed | 480 × 248 | no | cancels (the owner's Cancel) |
| Properties (process, service, startup, connection) | `Floating` | no | 900 × 640 (PROC-077); others per owner | 640 × 400 | yes | closes |
`open` calls `gpui_kit::open_window` (kit `crates/kit/src/lib.rs:149`) with `WindowOptions { window_decorations: Some(WindowDecorations::Client), window_background: WindowBackgroundAppearance::Opaque, kind, window_min_size: Some(min), app_id: Some("io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens".into()), window_bounds: centred on the parent, ..TitleBar::window_options() }` (kit `crates/component/src/title_bar.rs:81`), then wraps the view in the kit Root. Each window creates its own `ToastQueue::new(window, cx, top)`. In P1 `top` is the main-window value, 72 × `ui_scale` (66 with server decorations), because the kit `Theme::notification` is app-global (R-195); secondary windows get 42 (34 × `ui_scale` + `sp4`) in P2, when the queue takes a per-window top.
Title bar (34 px, background `titlebar`, 1 px `divider` below; Linux left padding 12): icon 16 (`TlAssets` app icon, or none until E15-022 lands), title `t_base` 500 `text_primary`, end ellipsis when narrow (never middle). Right side, right to left: kit close (34 wide; hover `status.danger` fill, white icon), maximize and minimize (34 wide, hover `tab_hover`) only when `window.window_controls()` reports them, then the pin: `TlButton::Toggle` 34 × 34, icon Lucide `pin` `i_md`; on: `accent` fill at alpha 0.25, icon tinted `accent`, tooltip "Always on top (on)"; off tooltip "Always on top". The pin is disabled with tooltip "Not supported by this desktop" when `GlobalHub` snapshot `windows.header.validity == Validity::Unsupported` (no KWin bridge, R-073). Pin click dispatches `ToggleAlwaysOnTop { window: key, caption }`, where `caption` is the exact window title at dispatch time, and flips the drawn state; secondary windows keep the pin state in memory only (R-176).
Double-click on the title: maximize for Tool and Properties, nothing for Confirmation and Run. Right-click on the title: compositor window menu (`window.show_window_menu`).
Server decorations (`appearance.decorations = "server"`): no title bar is drawn, `window_decorations: Some(Server)`, and the pin becomes a 24 px `TlButton::Toggle` at the top-right corner of the content (inset `sp4`).
Keys inside every secondary window (bound on its root with `key_context("TlWindow")`): Esc per the kind table; Ctrl+W closes Tool and Properties windows (and cancels Run and Confirmation); Tab order is content, then footer buttons left to right, then the pin. Focus on open goes to the first focusable content element (the owner's `build` decides; confirmations are E16-007).
Modal parent: while a Confirmation is open, its parent's content is covered by `derived.overlay` and ignores input.
Inactive window: the kit dims the shadow and border.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a Tool spec 600 × 400 **When** `open` runs **Then** a Floating window with min size 480 × 320, client decorations, a 34 px title bar and the given title exists.
- **Given** a Run spec **When** it opens **Then** it is 480 × 248 and not resizable.
- **Given** the windows snapshot validity `Unsupported` **When** a secondary window renders **Then** the pin is disabled with tooltip "Not supported by this desktop".
- **Given** a supported desktop and a window titled "Settings" **When** the pin is clicked **Then** `ToggleAlwaysOnTop { window: key, caption: "Settings" }` is dispatched and the pin draws its on look with tooltip "Always on top (on)".
- **Given** a Tool window **When** Esc or Ctrl+W is pressed **Then** it closes.
- **Given** `appearance.decorations = "server"` **When** a window opens **Then** no title bar is drawn and a 24 px pin sits at the content's top-right.
- **Given** an open secondary window **When** a toast is pushed to its queue **Then** it appears in that window only.
- **Given** a narrow window **When** the title does not fit **Then** it ends with "…".

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/components/window_frame.rs`: create, with tests.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/components/mod.rs`: add `pub mod window_frame;`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/registry.rs`: create with the `WindowKey` enum only (see Notes); add `pub mod registry;` to `window/mod.rs`.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_dialogs.rs`: create with the frame tests (E16-007 and E16-A2 append).

## Tests
- `tests/ui_dialogs.rs::tool_window_options`: kind, min size, decorations.
- `tests/ui_dialogs.rs::run_window_fixed_size`
- `tests/ui_dialogs.rs::pin_disabled_without_bridge` (UI-FND-021 `window_frame::tests::pin_disabled_without_bridge`)
- `tests/ui_dialogs.rs::pin_dispatches_toggle`
- `tests/ui_dialogs.rs::escape_and_ctrl_w_close_tool_window`
- `tests/ui_dialogs.rs::server_decorations_pin_fallback`
- `tests/ui_dialogs.rs::secondary_window_has_own_toasts`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: if `open_window` fails, `open` returns the error and the owner shows the Error toast "Could not open properties." (Properties) or logs (others); no window.
- Validity: pin availability follows `windows.header.validity`.
- Accessibility: the window title is the accessible name (compositor reads it); every caption control is keyboard reachable; the pin tooltip states the state in text.
- Performance: one frame loop per window; content follows ADR-009 caching rules; a confirmation costs one small view.
- Privacy: titles come from owners; nothing logged beyond the window kind.

## Notes
- `WindowKey` is defined in `window/registry.rs` (E16-A2). This bead lands first, so define `WindowKey` in `window/registry.rs` here with the full INDEX.md variant list (see E16-A2) plus `Main` (R-176: the main window; never stored in `WindowRegistry`, `cap_class()` returns `None`), and leave `WindowRegistry` itself to E16-A2; E16-A2 adds the registry type to the same file.
- `CloseWindow` is the shell's action (UI-SHL-120, `actions.rs`, E20). Ctrl+W inside secondary windows uses `CloseSecondaryWindow` declared here, so this bead does not depend on E20.
- The `ToggleAlwaysOnTop` handler is the shell's: E20-022 for `WindowKey::Main`, E20-029 for secondary windows, both through the KWin bridge only. There is no X11 keep-above in v1 (R-177). Until a handler exists the pin flips only its drawn state.
- `ToggleAlwaysOnTop` carries `WindowKey`, which holds tl-model types without `JsonSchema`, so it uses `#[action(no_json)]` (gpui-pre-macros `src/derive_action.rs:43`); it is dispatched from code, never from a JSON keymap.
- Large-file rule: commit the file before building or testing; fix-ups go in a follow-up commit, never an amend.
- Build rule: run cargo only through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <files>` (run `git add` on new files first). Never a bare `git commit`.
- Read `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` in the repo first. Sources: `docs/ui/foundation.md` UI-FND-021, `docs/ui/shell.md` UI-SHL-090, `docs/spec/merged/sys-app.md` APP-045, APP-009.

title: E16-009 TlMenu builder
description:
## Context
Builds `TlMenu`, the thin builder over the kit `PopupMenu` that every context menu, dropdown and menu bar menu in tasklens uses, so no view repeats the menu look or keyboard rules. Spec phase P1; priority 0 because the tree table (E18-005, E18-A1, P0) takes a `TlMenu` in its delegate trait and opens row and header menus. Sources: UI-FND-022, R-112 (min width override), table (b) Shift+F10 and Menu, ADR-009 (right-click selects, actions capture targets), APP-036 (painted theme items).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/components/menu.rs` (add `pub mod menu;` to `components/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub struct TlMenu { inner: PopupMenu, has_mark_column: bool }
impl TlMenu {
    pub fn build(window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App, action_context: FocusHandle,
                 f: impl FnOnce(TlMenu, &mut Window, &mut App) -> TlMenu) -> Entity<PopupMenu>;
    pub fn min_w(self, w: Pixels) -> Self;                  // default 180; process row and header menus 240, system table menus 220 (R-112)
    pub fn item(self, label: impl Into<SharedString>, action: Box<dyn Action>) -> Self;
    pub fn item_disabled(self, label: impl Into<SharedString>, tooltip: Option<SharedString>) -> Self;
    pub fn check_item(self, label: impl Into<SharedString>, checked: bool, action: Box<dyn Action>) -> Self;
    pub fn radio_item(self, label: impl Into<SharedString>, selected: bool, action: Box<dyn Action>) -> Self;
    pub fn submenu(self, label: impl Into<SharedString>, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App,
                   f: impl Fn(TlMenu, &mut Window, &mut App) -> TlMenu + 'static) -> Self;
    pub fn separator(self) -> Self;
    pub fn header(self, label: impl Into<SharedString>) -> Self;
    pub fn painted_item(self, label: impl Into<SharedString>, bg: Hsla, fg: Hsla, suffix_icon: Option<TlIcon>, action: Box<dyn Action>) -> Self;
}
pub const MENU_ITEM_H: f32 = 26.0;
pub const MENU_MIN_W: f32 = 180.0;
pub const MENU_MAX_W: f32 = 360.0;
```
Every menu sets `.min_w(px(180))` (unless raised), `.max_w(px(360))`, `.scrollable(true)` with max height window height minus `sp6`, `.check_side(Side::Left)` (kit `crates/component/src/menu/popup_menu.rs:453`), and `.action_context(handle)` (line 371) so shortcut hints come from the bindings: the row menu passes the table's focus handle, a menu bar menu the window's.
Look (UI-FND-022; colours come from the kit tokens mapped in `theme/map.rs`: `popover` = `menu_bg`, `accent` = `menu_hover`, `border` = `divider`): background `menu_bg`, 1 px `divider` border, radius `r_sm` (4), menu shadow offset (0, 2) blur 8 with `derived.shadow`, padding y `sp2` (4). Item height 26, padding x `sp4` (8), label `t_base`, end ellipsis at max width minus the shortcut column. Mark column 20 wide, reserved only when any item in that menu has a check, radio or icon, else 0 (the process row menu has none). Check mark Lucide `check` `i_xs` 12; radio mark a 6 px filled circle; both `text_primary`. Shortcut column `t_xs` 11 `text_secondary`, right-aligned, min gap `sp6` (16) from the label. Separator: hairline `divider`, margin y `sp2`, x `sp4`. Header rows: `t_xs` `text_secondary`, 22 high, not selectable, not uppercased. Submenu chevron Lucide `chevron-right` `i_xs` `text_secondary`; submenus open to the right with a 4 px overlap, flip left when no room, first item aligned with the parent item. Painted items: 26 high, the theme's own `menu_bg` and `text_primary`, `copy` `i_sm` icon at the right, full text in a tooltip when truncated (user theme names can be long).
States: hover or keyboard highlight: background `menu_hover`, label and shortcut `text_primary`. Disabled: opacity 0.5, not highlightable, skipped by arrows, tooltip shown if given. Open submenu parent stays highlighted. Open: kit fade 120 ms; reduced motion instant. Empty menu: one disabled row "No items".
Keyboard and mouse (kit behaviour plus these checks): Up/Down move with wrap, skipping separators, headers and disabled items; Right opens a submenu and focuses its first item; Left closes back to the parent; Enter and Space run; Esc closes the topmost level and returns focus to the opener; typing a letter jumps to the next item starting with it; Home and End jump. Clicking outside closes and the click is consumed. Opening a menu closes any tooltip. A click on a submenu parent opens it without closing.
Helper for tables: `pub fn open_context_menu_at(position: Point<Pixels>, window, cx, menu: Entity<PopupMenu>)` used by right-click (pointer position) and Shift+F10 / Menu (focused row's left edge plus `sp4`, y = row bottom; the caller computes the point).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a menu with items A, separator, disabled B, C **When** Down is pressed from A **Then** C is highlighted.
- **Given** C highlighted **When** Down is pressed **Then** A is highlighted (wrap).
- **Given** a submenu parent highlighted **When** Right is pressed **Then** the submenu opens with its first item focused, and Left closes it with the parent highlighted.
- **Given** a menu at 100% scale **When** it renders **Then** each item is 26 px high.
- **Given** an open menu over a table **When** the user clicks outside it **Then** the menu closes and the table row under the pointer is not selected.
- **Given** a menu whose items have no check, radio or icon **When** it renders **Then** the label starts at padding 8 with no mark column.
- **Given** `TlMenu::min_w(px(240))` **When** it renders **Then** the menu is at least 240 wide.
- **Given** every item filtered out **When** the menu renders **Then** it shows one disabled row "No items".
- **Given** an item whose action has a binding in the action context **When** it renders **Then** the shortcut text appears right-aligned in `t_xs` `text_secondary`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/components/menu.rs`: create, with tests.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/components/mod.rs`: add `pub mod menu;`.

## Tests
- `components::menu::tests::arrow_keys_skip_separators_and_disabled`
- `components::menu::tests::right_opens_submenu_left_closes`
- `components::menu::tests::shift_f10_opens_at_row` (helper places the menu at the given row point)
- `components::menu::tests::item_height_is_26_at_100pct` (render test under `render-tests`, or a layout-bounds assertion when E16-005 is not yet available)
- `components::menu::tests::outside_click_consumed`
- `components::menu::tests::mark_column_collapses`
- `components::menu::tests::empty_menu_shows_no_items`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: every command also has a non-menu path (table b or the menu bar); shortcut hints shown; full keyboard navigation.
- Performance: built on open only from the owner's closure; nothing per frame while closed. One menu handler per table, not per row.
- Privacy: menu labels may contain process names; not logged.

## Notes
- The item height 26 is the kit's `text_sm` row at rem 13 plus padding; if the measured height differs, adjust the item padding, not `MENU_ITEM_H`.
- `"No items"` text comes from `i18n::tr(cx, "fnd-menu-no-items")` (E16-002).
- Large-file rule: commit the file before building or testing; fix-ups go in a follow-up commit, never an amend.
- Build rule: run cargo only through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <files>` (run `git add` on new files first). Never a bare `git commit`.
- Read `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` in the repo first. Sources: `docs/ui/foundation.md` UI-FND-022, `docs/RECONCILIATION.md` R-112.

title: E16-010 TlShield
description:
## Context
Builds `TlShield`, the toolbar button that shows and toggles the privileged-helper state. The spec phase is P3 (hidden until then), but the component sits in anchor E16-A3 (P1) because E29 (helper, batch B4) depends on that anchor; it is written now and stays hidden while the helper is missing. Sources: UI-FND-028, APP-003, APP-002, PROC-058 ("Retry as administrator" dispatches the same `StartHelperSession`), ADR-006 (120 s polkit deadline, 300 s idle exit), ADR-003 Restricted tooltip.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/components/shield.rs` (add `pub mod shield;` to `components/mod.rs`):
```rust
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Default, gpui::Action)] #[action(namespace = tasklens)] pub struct StartHelperSession;
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Default, gpui::Action)] #[action(namespace = tasklens)] pub struct EndHelperSession;
#[derive(IntoElement)] pub struct TlShield { state: HelperState }
impl TlShield { pub fn new(state: HelperState) -> Self; }
```
`HelperState { Missing, Locked, Starting, Unlocked }` is read from `snapshot.health.helper` (UI-FND-028). The owner re-renders on the `HEALTH` bit.
Look: a `TlButton::Toggle` 24 × 24 (E15-008), `.tab_stop(false)` like every main toolbar button (UI-FND-010).
| State | Rendered | Icon | Toggle look | Tooltip | Click, Space, Enter |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Missing (before P3, or `/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper` absent) | nothing (no element) | | | | |
| Locked | yes | Lucide `shield` `i_md` 16, `text_primary` | off | "Unlock privileged actions" | dispatch `StartHelperSession` |
| Starting (polkit prompt open or helper starting) | yes, inert | `TlSpinner` `i_md` in place of the icon | off | "Waiting for authentication…" | nothing |
| Unlocked | yes | app SVG `shield-unlocked.svg` (`AppIcon::ShieldUnlocked`, E15-005) tinted `status.success` | on: `accent` fill at alpha 0.25, 1 px `accent` border | "Privileged actions unlocked (click to lock)" | dispatch `EndHelperSession` |
Hover, pressed and focus as `TlButton::Toggle`.
Toast texts the shell pushes when the state leaves Starting (owned by the engine-facing flow in E29; listed here as the foundation's accepted strings): "Authentication cancelled" when the prompt was dismissed, "Could not start the privileged helper" on any other failure. The 300 s idle exit returns to Locked with no toast (APP-003).
The status bar text "Restricted: N processes" (APP-029) is the shell's, not this component's.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `HelperState::Missing` **When** the toolbar renders the shield **Then** no element is produced.
- **Given** `Locked` **When** it renders **Then** the Lucide shield shows with tooltip "Unlock privileged actions".
- **Given** `Locked` **When** it is clicked **Then** `StartHelperSession` is dispatched.
- **Given** `Starting` **When** it is clicked **Then** nothing is dispatched and a spinner shows.
- **Given** `Unlocked` **When** it renders **Then** the unlocked SVG in `status.success` shows with the on look and tooltip "Privileged actions unlocked (click to lock)".
- **Given** `Unlocked` **When** Space is pressed with focus on it **Then** `EndHelperSession` is dispatched.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/components/shield.rs`: create, with tests.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/components/mod.rs`: add `pub mod shield;`.
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append `fnd-shield-unlock = Unlock privileged actions`, `fnd-shield-waiting = Waiting for authentication…`, `fnd-shield-unlocked = Privileged actions unlocked (click to lock)`.

## Tests
- `components::shield::tests::hidden_without_helper`
- `components::shield::tests::states_and_tooltips` (one case per state: icon, look, tooltip)
- `components::shield::tests::click_dispatches_per_state`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: failure toasts are pushed by the shell flow (E29), not here.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: tooltip text is the accessible name and states the state in words, not colour alone.
- Performance: one button; the spinner runs only in Starting.
- Privacy: N/A
- Security: the shield only dispatches actions; it never starts processes itself (the engine runs pkexec, ADR-006).

## Notes
- Blocked on open item 7 in docs/plan/b5-ui-foundation.md: `HealthSnapshot.helper: HelperState` is not in ADR-003; E03 must add it. If E03-A2 lands without it, stop and report.
- UI-FND-028 gives no tooltip for Starting; this bead reuses the accepted shell string "Waiting for authentication…" (new B5 open item, confirm).
- INDEX.md lists `StartHelperSession` and `EndHelperSession` among the window-level actions. They are declared here because E15/E16 cannot depend on E20; E20's `actions.rs` re-exports them instead of declaring them again (GPUI action names must be unique per namespace, R-128).
- Build rule: run cargo only through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <files>` (run `git add` on new files first). Never a bare `git commit`.
- Read `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` in the repo first. Sources: `docs/ui/foundation.md` UI-FND-028, `docs/spec/merged/sys-app.md` APP-003.
