title: Services: Start, Stop, Restart, Reload and Reset failed flows
description:
## Context
Start, Stop, Restart, Reload and Reset failed state run without confirmation, show a toast replaced in place, and overlay the row's Status cell while pending; failures carry a "View logs" button that opens Service Properties on the Logs tab. This bead writes those flows in `pages/services/flows.rs` on top of `SysActions` (E27-A1). Sources: UI-SYS-018, UI-SYS-007, SYS-005, SYS-006, ADR-005 (`UnitStart`, `UnitStop`, `UnitRestart`, `UnitReload`, `UnitResetFailed`), R-114, R-117.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/flows.rs` and `pub mod flows;` in `pages/services/mod.rs`.

```rust
pub enum UnitVerb { Start, Stop, Restart, Reload, ResetFailed }
pub fn unit_action_kind(v: UnitVerb) -> ActionKind;   // UnitStart, UnitStop, UnitRestart, UnitReload, UnitResetFailed
pub fn unit_action_tag(v: UnitVerb) -> ActionKindTag; // Start, Stop, Restart, Reload, ResetFailed
pub fn unit_action_texts(v: UnitVerb) -> ActionTexts;
/// Submits one request for the captured unit targets (group rows and child rows already removed).
pub fn run_unit_verb(v: UnitVerb, units: &[UnitRef], actions: &Entity<SysActions>,
                     window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App);
```

Texts (exact; `failed_suffix = true` for all five; service jobs have no client-side timeout, and their Progress toast stays until the final event, R-197):

| Verb | pending_one | done_one | failed_prefix | Button on failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Start | "Starting service..." | "Service started" | "Failed to start service" | "View logs" |
| Stop | "Stopping service..." | "Service stopped" | "Failed to stop service" | "View logs" |
| Restart | "Restarting service..." | "Service restarted" | "Failed to restart service" | "View logs" |
| Reload | "Reloading service..." | "Service reloaded" | "Failed to reload service" | "View logs" |
| ResetFailed | "Clearing failed state..." | "Failed state cleared" | "Failed to clear failed state" | none |

Shared for all five: `unknown` "Service action finished." (Warning; the engine resyncs), `busy` "A service action is already in progress.". Summary texts for 4 or more targets (R-114): Start `pending_many` "Starting { $n } services...", `done_many` "{ $n } services started", `partial_many` "{ $ok } of { $n } services started. { $failed } failed."; Stop "Stopping { $n } services...", "{ $n } services stopped", "{ $ok } of { $n } services stopped. { $failed } failed."; Restart "Restarting { $n } services...", "{ $n } services restarted", "{ $ok } of { $n } services restarted. { $failed } failed."; Reload "Reloading { $n } services...", "{ $n } services reloaded", "{ $ok } of { $n } services reloaded. { $failed } failed."; ResetFailed "Clearing failed state of { $n } services...", "Failed state cleared for { $n } services", "Failed state cleared for { $ok } of { $n } services. { $failed } failed.".

- The failure text is `failure_text(prefix, err)` (E27-A1): "<prefix>: <result>" where result is the systemd job word, the D-Bus error text, or "not authorized".
- "View logs" dispatches `ServicePropertiesWindow::open(unit, ServicePropsTab::Logs)` for the failed target (E27-A3 API); the toast lasts 15 s.
- The request is `ActionRequest { kind: unit_action_kind(v), targets: units.map(ActionTarget::Unit), privileged: false }` through `SysActions::submit`. No confirmation dialog for any verb.
- While pending, the Status cell overlay ("Starting…", "Stopping…", "Restarting…", "Reloading…") comes from the delegate (E27 cells bead) via `SysActions::pending_tag`. Reset failed has no overlay.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a stopped unit **When** Start runs and the fake engine emits `Started` then `Succeeded` **Then** the toast goes "Starting service..." (Progress) then "Service started" (Success) under one key.
- **Given** a Start that fails with job result `failed` **When** the final event arrives **Then** the toast reads "Failed to start service: failed" with a "View logs" button, lasting 15 s, and pressing it opens Service Properties on Logs for that unit.
- **Given** a Reset failed **When** it succeeds **Then** the toast reads "Failed state cleared" and no overlay was drawn.
- **Given** a Start already pending on the unit **When** Start runs again **Then** the toast "A service action is already in progress." shows and no request is sent.
- **Given** `OutcomeUnknown` **When** it arrives **Then** a Warning toast "Service action finished." shows.
- **Given** 5 units **When** Stop runs and all succeed **Then** one toast "Stopping 5 services..." becomes "5 services stopped".

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/flows.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/mod.rs`: add `pub mod flows;`
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_services.rs`: add the tests below
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append every string above (keys `services-sys018-<slug>`)

- `ui_services::failed_start_shows_view_logs`.
- `ui_services::busy_rejection_toast`.
- `ui_services::reset_failed_no_overlay`.
- `ui_services::stop_five_units_summary_toast`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: per the table; polkit dismissal and denial both read "not authorized" on systemd calls until U-39 is verified (R-117).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: toast text states the outcome; the overlay label is text.
- Performance: none per frame.

- R-114 names the summary pattern for start, stop, restart, enable and disable only. The Reload and Reset failed summary strings above extend that pattern and are open item B8-E27-6 (recommended as written).
- Build rule: run every cargo build, check, clippy or test through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_services`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: Services: startup type flow, file openers and Jump to process
description:
## Context
The rest of the Services row commands: change the startup type (Enabled, Disabled, Masked), File properties, Open file location, Open unit file, and Jump to process. Startup changes go through systemd unit-file calls; the three openers go through the engine's opener actions (R-134); Jump to process uses the Processes tab's jump entry point. This bead adds them to `pages/services/flows.rs`. Sources: UI-SYS-019, UI-SYS-017 (interaction rows), UI-SYS-021 (outbound jump), SYS-007, SYS-008, SYS-010, PROC-071, R-134, R-114, ADR-005 (`UnitEnable`, `UnitDisable`, `UnitMask`, `UnitUnmask`, `ShowInFileManager`, `OpenUri`).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/flows.rs`, add:

```rust
/// Request kind for a startup change, or None when the choice equals the current value.
pub fn startup_change_kind(current: StartupType, choice: StartupChoice) -> Option<ActionKind>;
pub fn run_set_startup(choice: StartupChoice, units: &[(UnitRef, StartupType)], actions: &Entity<SysActions>,
                       window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App);
pub fn run_file_properties(unit: &UnitRecord, actions: &Entity<SysActions>, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App);
pub fn run_open_file_location(unit: &UnitRecord, actions: &Entity<SysActions>, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App);
pub fn run_open_unit_file(unit: &UnitRecord, actions: &Entity<SysActions>, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App);
pub fn run_jump_to_process(unit: &UnitRecord, snap: &Snapshot, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App);
pub fn file_uri(path: &str) -> String;   // "file://" + RFC 3986 percent-encoding of every byte outside unreserved and '/'
```

Startup type (UI-SYS-019):
- `startup_change_kind`: current Enabled or "Enabled (runtime)" counts as Enabled. Same value -> None (nothing sent). Choice Enabled -> `UnitEnable`; Disabled -> `UnitDisable`; Masked -> `UnitMask`. Leaving Masked for Enabled or Disabled sends `UnitEnable` or `UnitDisable`; the engine unmasks first as part of that request (open item B8-E27-7 confirms this split with E11).
- Multi-select: one request per distinct resulting kind, each with all its units as targets (units whose value already equals the choice are left out).
- Texts: `pending_one` "Changing startup type...", `done_one` "Startup type changed", `failed_prefix` "Failed to change startup type", `failed_suffix = true` (so ": <error>" is appended), `unknown` "Service action finished.", `busy` "A service action is already in progress.", `progress_cap = false`, no button. Summary for 4 or more targets: "Changing startup type of { $n } services...", "Startup type changed for { $n } services", "Startup type changed for { $ok } of { $n } services. { $failed } failed." (open item B8-E27-6). Tag `ActionKindTag::SetStartup`. Polkit may prompt twice for system units; the toast stays pending through both.

File properties: `ShowInFileManager { path: exec_start_path, properties: true }`, else the unit file path when there is no ExecStart. Texts: `pending_one` empty (no pending toast), `done_one` "Opened service file properties.", `failed_prefix` "Could not open service file properties.", `failed_suffix = false`. Neither path known -> Warning toast "Service image unavailable", nothing sent.

Open file location: `ShowInFileManager { path: exec_start_path, properties: false }`. Texts: `pending_one` empty, `done_one` "Opening service file location.", `failed_prefix` "Could not open service file location.", `failed_suffix = false`. No ExecStart -> Warning toast "Service image unavailable", nothing sent.

Open unit file: `OpenUri(file_uri(fragment_path))`. Texts: `pending_one` empty, `done_one` empty (no success toast: when `done_one` is empty `SysActions` removes the toast silently on success), `failed_prefix` "Could not open the unit file", `failed_suffix = false`. Empty `FragmentPath` -> nothing (the menu item is disabled).

Jump to process (outbound, UI-SYS-021): one unit. `main_pid == 0` -> Info toast "Service not running", nothing else. Otherwise find the `ProcessKey` whose pid equals `main_pid` in `snap.processes.records`, and call the Processes jump entry point (E22-A3, `select_by_key(key, source)`) with caller texts: success "Switched to service process."; hidden by filter or Hide system processes: "Service process not visible in the current process view." with the "Show" button (E22 shows it); key missing: E22's "Process not found in current view".

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a Masked unit **When** the user chooses Enabled **Then** one request with kind `UnitEnable` and that unit is sent.
- **Given** an Enabled (runtime) unit **When** the user chooses Enabled **Then** nothing is sent.
- **Given** a failure "Access denied" on enable **When** the final event arrives **Then** the toast reads "Failed to change startup type: not authorized".
- **Given** a unit with ExecStart `/usr/bin/sshd` **When** File properties runs **Then** the request is `ShowInFileManager { path: "/usr/bin/sshd", properties: true }` and no toast shows before the result.
- **Given** a unit with no ExecStart **When** Open file location runs **Then** the Warning toast "Service image unavailable" shows and nothing is sent.
- **Given** `FragmentPath = /usr/lib/systemd/system/a b.service` **When** Open unit file runs **Then** the request is `OpenUri("file:///usr/lib/systemd/system/a%20b.service")` and success shows no toast.
- **Given** MainPID 0 **When** Jump to process runs **Then** the toast reads "Service not running" and the tab does not change.
- **Given** MainPID 812 present in the process snapshot **When** Jump to process runs **Then** the jump entry point is called with that key and the toast reads "Switched to service process.".

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/flows.rs`: change, add the functions above
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_services.rs`: add the tests below
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append every string above (keys `services-sys019-<slug>`, `services-sys017-<slug>`, `services-sys021-<slug>`)

## Tests

- `ui_services::startup_same_value_sends_nothing`.
- `ui_services::open_unit_file_uri_encoding`.
- `ui_services::file_properties_falls_back_to_unit_file`.
- `ui_services::jump_to_process_main_pid_zero_toast`.
- `ui_services::jump_to_process_calls_entry_point`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: per the texts above.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: every command is reachable from the context menu with the keyboard (Shift+F10).
- Performance: one request per command.
- Privacy: paths are passed to the engine only; never logged (ADR-015).

## Notes
- `SysActions` (E27-A1) shows no toast before the result when `pending_one` is empty and none on success when `done_one` is empty.
- `StartupChoice` is in `pages/services/actions.rs`; `StartupType`, `UnitRecord` from `tl-model` (E03-A2).
- Build rule: run every cargo build, check, clippy or test through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_services`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: Services: unit row context menu and Startup type submenu
description:
## Context
Right-click, Shift+F10 or the Menu key on a unit row opens the Services context menu: 15 items in a fixed order with show and enable rules, a "Startup type" submenu, and disabled-item tooltips. Child process rows get the process row menu instead. Targets are captured when the menu opens. This bead writes `pages/services/menu.rs`. Sources: UI-SYS-017, UI-SYS-019 (submenu states), UI-SYS-016 (child rows), SYS-006 to SYS-010, R-012, R-091, PROC-057, ADR-009 (targets captured at menu open), UI-FND-022 (`TlMenu`, system table menus `min_w` 220).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/menu.rs` and `pub mod menu;` in `pages/services/mod.rs`.

```rust
/// Captured at menu open; every item acts on these, never on the live selection.
pub struct ServiceMenuTargets {
    pub units: SmallVec<[UnitRef; 1]>,     // unit rows of the selection (max 256)
    pub records: SmallVec<[UnitRecord; 1]>,// their records at open time
    pub clicked_col: ColumnId,
}
pub fn service_menu(t: &ServiceMenuTargets, pending: &SysActions, backend: ServiceBackend,
                    menu: PopupMenu, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<PopupMenu>) -> PopupMenu;
/// Which menu a right-click gets.
pub enum MenuChoice { Unit, Process, None }
pub fn menu_choice(selection: &[SysNodeId]) -> MenuChoice;
```

Items in order (labels exact; key hints right-aligned by the kit through `.action_context(table focus)`):

| # | Label | Key hint | Action | Shown when | Enabled when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "Start" | Ctrl+S | `ServiceStart` | always | any target not active and not pending |
| 2 | "Stop" | Ctrl+E | `ServiceStop` | always | any target active and not pending |
| 3 | "Restart" | Ctrl+R | `ServiceRestart` | always | any target active and not pending |
| 4 | "Reload" | | `ServiceReload` | any target has `CanReload` | that target active |
| 5 | "Reset failed state" | | `ServiceResetFailed` | any target Failed | always |
| 6 | "Startup type" › | | submenu | always | see below |
| | separator | | | | |
| 7 | "View logs" | | `ServiceViewLogs` | always | exactly one target; disabled on OpenRC |
| 8 | "Properties" | Enter | `OpenProperties` | always | always |
| 9 | "File properties" | | `ServiceFileProperties` | always | binary or unit file known |
| 10 | "Open file location" | | `ServiceOpenFileLocation` | always | binary known |
| 11 | "Open unit file" | | `ServiceOpenUnitFile` | always | `FragmentPath` not empty |
| | separator | | | | |
| 12 | "Copy" | | `CopyCell { col: clicked_col }` | always | always |
| 13 | "Copy row" | Ctrl+C | `CopyDetails` | always | always |
| 14 | "Copy rows as table" | Ctrl+Shift+C | `CopyRowsAsTable` | always | always |
| 15 | "Jump to process" | | `ServiceJumpToProcess` | always | exactly one target with MainPID not 0 |

- "Active" means ActiveState `active` or `reloading` (the same set UI-SYS-022 counts as Running); "pending" is `SysActions::is_pending(target, tag)`.
- Items have no icons. The kit hides a separator next to a hidden item.
- Disabled items draw `text_secondary` at 50% alpha and show a tooltip with the reason: "A service action is already in progress." (pending), "Service not running" (Jump with MainPID 0), "Service image unavailable" (File properties or Open file location with no ExecStart).
- "Startup type" submenu: three check items "Enabled", "Disabled", "Masked" dispatching `ServiceSetStartupType { startup }`. The current value is checked ("Enabled (runtime)" counts as Enabled); with several targets of different values none is checked. The parent item is disabled with tooltip "This unit has no install section" when any target is Static, Indirect, Generated or Transient, and with tooltip "This unit has no unit file" when any target's startup type is "-".
- Menu `min_w(220)`, `max_w(360)`.
- `menu_choice`: only group rows -> `None` (group rows have no unit menu; Enter or the chevron toggles them); only `UnitProcess` rows -> `Process` (the page opens the process row menu from E22-A2 with the process keys); any `Unit` row present -> `Unit`, and the menu acts on the unit rows only (a mixed selection ignores child rows).
- Right-click on an unselected row selects it first (E18). Shift+F10 or Menu opens the menu for the selection at the focused row's left edge.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** one running unit with `CanReload` **When** the menu opens **Then** the labels in order are Start, Stop, Restart, Reload, Startup type, View logs, Properties, File properties, Open file location, Open unit file, Copy, Copy row, Copy rows as table, Jump to process, with Start disabled.
- **Given** a unit without `CanReload` and not Failed **When** the menu opens **Then** "Reload" and "Reset failed state" are not built.
- **Given** a Stop pending on the target **When** the menu opens **Then** Start, Stop and Restart are disabled with tooltip "A service action is already in progress.".
- **Given** a Static unit **When** the menu opens **Then** "Startup type" is disabled with tooltip "This unit has no install section".
- **Given** two units, one Enabled and one Disabled **When** the submenu opens **Then** no item is checked.
- **Given** the menu opened on unit A **When** rows re-sort before the user picks Start **Then** Start acts on unit A.
- **Given** a selection of one unit row and one child row **When** the menu opens **Then** the unit menu shows and its actions target only the unit.
- **Given** only a child row selected **When** the menu is requested **Then** `menu_choice` returns `Process`.

## Files

- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/mod.rs`: add `pub mod menu;`
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_services.rs`: add the tests below
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append every label and tooltip above (keys `services-sys017-<slug>`, `services-sys019-<slug>`)

## Tests

- `ui_services::startup_submenu_no_check_on_mixed`.
- `ui_services::menu_target_captured_at_open`.

- Accessibility: full keyboard path through Shift+F10 and Menu; every item reachable with Up/Down; check items announce their state.

title: Services: inbound Go to service (ServicesPage::select_unit)
description:
## Context
"Go to service" from the Processes tab, the Connections tab or a Service Properties link lands on the Services tab: it removes strip filters only when they hide the unit, expands the manager group, selects the unit, centres it and focuses the table. This bead writes that inbound jump, `ServicesPage::select_unit`. Sources: UI-SYS-021, SYS-010, PROC-071, SYS-032 (Go to service from Connections), UI-PRC-022 (same shape on the Processes side).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/mod.rs`:

```rust
impl ServicesPage {
    /// Called after the main window has made Services the active tab.
    pub fn select_unit(&mut self, unit: UnitRef, origin: JumpOrigin, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>);
}
```

Steps (exact):
1. If `origin` is not already the Services tab (all current origins come from other tabs), push Info toast "Switched to Services tab".
2. Find the unit in `ServicesSnapshot.units` (unfiltered records). Not present: Warning toast "Service not found in current view"; stop.
3. If the strip hides it (its state class not in the on-states while some are on, its unit type unchecked, or its manager toggle off), change only the strip parts that hide it: turn on its state toggle, check its unit type, turn its manager on. Never change the text filter here.
4. If the text filter hides it (the unit's id, description and path do not contain the lowercased filter): Warning toast "Service not found in current view" with a "Show" button; "Show" dispatches `ClearFilter` and then continues at step 5.
5. Add the manager group to `expanded` and send one query (`set_expanded`, plus `set_services_filter` if step 3 changed the strip).
6. When the first view with `query_generation == last_sent` arrives, select `SysNodeId::Unit(unit)` only, scroll it with `scroll_to_item_strict(ix, ScrollStrategy::Center)` (`gpui-pre-0.3.7/src/elements/uniform_list.rs:163`), focus the table, and push Info toast "Switched to service.".

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** Processes is active and sshd.service exists in a collapsed System group **When** `select_unit(sshd, Processes)` runs **Then** the System group expands, sshd.service is the only selected row, centred, the table has focus, and the toasts "Switched to Services tab" and "Switched to service." show.
- **Given** the strip shows only Failed and sshd is running **When** `select_unit` runs **Then** the Running toggle turns on, Failed stays on, and sshd is selected.
- **Given** the text filter "nginx" **When** `select_unit(sshd, ..)` runs **Then** the Warning toast "Service not found in current view" with a "Show" button shows and the filter stays "nginx" until Show is pressed.
- **Given** an unknown unit **When** `select_unit` runs **Then** only "Service not found in current view" shows.
- **Given** the jump sent a query **When** a view with an older generation arrives **Then** no selection or scroll happens until the matching view arrives.

title: E27-A2 Services page
description:
## Context
Anchor E27-A2. This bead writes the `ServicesPage` entity that puts the Services tab together: the shared system-table frame with the Services delegate, the filter strip, the status text, F5 refresh, the first-visit loading toast, and the action handlers that route every Services command to the flows, menus, copy and Properties beads. Sources: UI-SYS-010, UI-SYS-022, UI-SYS-023, UI-SYS-001, UI-SYS-004 (loading toast), UI-SYS-005 (Clear filters), UI-SYS-014 (Ctrl+L), UI-SYS-016 (child rows), UI-SYS-017, SYS-001, SYS-004, SYS-006, SYS-016, APP-029, R-023, R-060, D-008.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/mod.rs`:

```rust
pub struct ServicesPage {
    frame: SysTableFrame<ServicesDelegate>,
    strip: ServiceFilterState,
    unit_types_menu_open: bool,
    loading_toast_shown: bool,
    refresh_pending: Option<(u64 /*services version at F5*/, Task<()>)>,
    status_cache: (u32, u32, u32, usize), // total, running, stopped, selected count
    _subs: Vec<Subscription>,
}
impl ServicesPage {
    pub fn new(window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> Self;
    pub fn status_text(&self, out: &mut String);
}
impl Render for ServicesPage { ... }   // frame.render(Some(strip), Box::new(ServicesClearAllFilters), ..)
```

Construction: `SysTableFrame::new(Tab::Services, "ServiceTable", &[SourceId::SystemdSystem, SourceId::SystemdUser], ServicesDelegate::new(..), sort from UiState [sort.services] (default name ascending), Some(strip.to_filter()), ..)`; strip from settings `services.unit_types` and `services.filter_states`; group expansion from `UiState [services] group_expanded`. Subscribes to `SnapshotHub` (`SnapshotChanged`), to the `SysActions` entity (`PendingChanged` -> notify), to the shell's `FilterChanged { tab: Services, .. }`, and to tab activation. All created in `new`. The page root is embedded by the main window with `.cached(size_full)`.

Status text (UI-SYS-022, exact): "<total> Total | <running> Running | <stopped> Stopped", plus " | <n> selected" when n > 0. Counts come from `ServicesSnapshot.counts { total, running, stopped }` (engine-computed over unit rows after all filters; Running = ActiveState active or reloading; Stopped = inactive or failed; Starting and Stopping count in Total only), numbers thin-space (U+2009) grouped. While the body is `Skeleton`: "Loading…". Emit `StatusChanged` only when the four cached numbers change.

Loading toast (UI-SYS-004, SYS-016): on the first activation of the session push Progress toast "Loading service data..." with the fixed key `SERVICES_LOADING_TOAST` (open item B8-E27-8; recommended value `ToastKey(0x8000_0000_0000_0101)`); remove it in the same update where the body leaves `Skeleton` or turns into an error state.

F5 (`RefreshCurrentTab` while Services is active): call `frame.refresh` (sends `RefreshNow(SystemdSystem)` and `RefreshNow(SystemdUser)`), remember the current services `header.version`, start a 2 s timer; on the first services version greater than the remembered one, or when the timer fires, whichever is first, push Success toast "Services refreshed." once.

Action handlers on the page root (each reads the selection or the captured menu targets, never the live selection for menu items):
- `ServiceStart`, `ServiceStop`, `ServiceRestart`, `ServiceReload`, `ServiceResetFailed` -> `flows::run_unit_verb` with the unit rows of the targets. Special keyboard rule (UI-SYS-023): `ServiceStop` (Ctrl+E) with only child process rows selected runs End Task on those processes through the E22-A2 End Task entry point (same confirmation and toasts as the Processes tab); Ctrl+S and Ctrl+R on child rows and on group rows do nothing.
- `ServiceSetStartupType` -> `flows::run_set_startup`; `ServiceFileProperties`, `ServiceOpenFileLocation`, `ServiceOpenUnitFile`, `ServiceJumpToProcess` -> the matching `flows` function; `ServiceViewLogs` -> `ServicePropertiesWindow::open(unit, ServicePropsTab::Logs)`.
- `OpenProperties` (Enter, Alt+Enter, Ctrl+I, double-click): unit rows -> one `ServicePropertiesWindow::open(unit, General)` per selected unit up to the cap of 10; group row -> toggle expand; child rows -> handled by the Process Properties bead (E27 chain bead that depends on E23-A1).
- `OpenContextMenu` and right-click: `menu::menu_choice` decides; `Unit` -> `menu::service_menu` with targets captured at open; `Process` -> E22-A2's process `row_menu` with the child process keys; `None` -> no menu.
- `CopyCell`, `CopyDetails`, `CopyRowsAsTable` -> `sys_copy` with the `ServicesDelegate` source and `services_copy_texts()`.
- `CollapseAll` (Ctrl+L): collapse every unit row and keep both group rows expanded (implement through the E18 collapse-all hook on the delegate if E18 provides one; otherwise `capture_action` on the page root and send one `set_expanded` with only the group ids).
- Strip actions (`ServicesToggleStateFilter`, `ServicesToggleManagerFilter`, `ServicesToggleUnitType`, `ServicesResetUnitTypes`, `ServicesRemoveFilters`) -> `filter_strip` methods, then `set_services_filter`.
- `ServicesClearAllFilters` -> dispatch `ClearFilter` (shell clears the text and sends `FilterChanged`) and `strip.remove_filters()`.
- Expanding or collapsing units updates the process demand from `delegate::child_demand`.

Layout (1280 x 800, 100% scale): filter strip 28, header 28, rows `row_h`, status chip floating bottom-left (shell). Tab order: strip toggles left to right, Unit types, System, User, Remove filters, then the table.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the fake engine's 20-unit services fixture **When** the page renders at 1280 x 800 **Then** the element tree has the strip (4 state toggles, Unit types, System, User, Remove filters) above a 28 px header with Name, Display name, Status, Startup type, PID, User, Path.
- **Given** counts total 255, running 198, stopped 57 and 3 selected rows **When** `status_text` runs **Then** it writes "255 Total | 198 Running | 57 Stopped | 3 selected".
- **Given** the first visit **When** the page activates **Then** the toast "Loading service data..." shows, and it is gone in the update where the first services data arrives.
- **Given** F5 **When** a newer services version arrives after 300 ms **Then** "Services refreshed." shows once at that moment; with no new version it shows after 2 s.
- **Given** a child process row selected **When** Ctrl+E is pressed **Then** End Task runs on that process and no unit action is sent.
- **Given** a group row focused **When** Enter is pressed **Then** the group toggles and no window opens.
- **Given** three unit rows selected **When** Enter is pressed **Then** three Service Properties windows open.
- **Given** expanded unit rows **When** Ctrl+L is pressed **Then** every unit collapses and both group rows stay expanded.
- **Given** "No matches" with text "zzz" and Failed on **When** "Clear filters" is pressed **Then** the text filter is empty and the strip is at its defaults.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/mod.rs`: change, `ServicesPage`
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_services.rs`: add the tests below
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append the status text pattern, "Loading service data...", "Services refreshed." (keys `services-sys022-<slug>`, `services-sys004-<slug>`)

## Tests

- `ui_services::services_status_text_counts`.
- `ui_services::services_loading_toast_removed_on_data`.
- `ui_services::f5_refresh_toast_after_update` (both the version and the 2 s paths).
- `ui_services::ctrl_e_on_child_ends_process`.
- `ui_services::enter_on_group_row_toggles`.
- `ui_services::properties_one_window_per_selected_unit`.
- `ui_services::collapse_all_keeps_groups_open`.
- `ui_services::child_rows_use_process_menu`.
- `ui_services::empty_state_filter_clear_resets_strip`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: through the frame's empty and error states and the flows' toasts.
- Validity: skeleton until first data; stale rows while a manager reconnects.
- Accessibility: full keyboard path per UI-SYS-023; status text repeats counts as text.

title: Service Properties: General tab
description:
## Context
The General tab of Service Properties shows the unit's identity, documentation links, command, unit file and drop-ins, a Startup type combo that applies through the footer, the status line with Start, Stop and Restart buttons, the Main PID link and resource values. Sources: UI-SYS-031, SYS-011 (General), SYS-007 (combo), SYS-006 (buttons), R-050, UI-FND-025 (`TlKeyValueGrid`), UI-FND-032 (`TlLink`), table (d).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/windows/service_properties/general.rs` (`GeneralTab` view implementing `ServicePropsTabView`) and `mod general;` plus its wiring as the General tab in `windows/service_properties/mod.rs`.

Grid: `TlKeyValueGrid` inline layout, label column 120, row height 28, label `text_secondary` `t_base` with a trailing ":", value `text_primary` `t_base`, values selectable. Rows in order with the exact labels:

| Label | Value |
|---|---|
| "Name" | unit id |
| "Display" | `description` |
| "Desc" | one `TlLink` per `documentation` entry, separated by two spaces; none -> "Not reported" |
| "Path" | `exec_start_argv` joined by spaces; wraps, max 3 lines |
| "Unit file" | `fragment_path` as a `TlLink` |
| "Drop-ins" | one `TlLink` per `drop_in_paths` entry, one per line; none -> "None" |
| "Startup" | `TlSelect` width 200, values "Enabled", "Disabled", "Masked" |
| "Status" | dot (UI-SYS-003 look) and "<Status> (<SubState>) since <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS>" from `active_enter_timestamp` local time; inactive units: "Stopped (dead)" with no "since" part; under it `TlButton::Secondary` sm "Start", "Stop", "Restart" with gap `sp4` |
| "Main PID" | `main_pid` as a `TlLink`; 0 -> "None" |
| "Memory" | `memory_current` IEC two decimals; `u64::MAX` -> "Not reported" |
| "Tasks" | `tasks_current`; `u64::MAX` -> "Not reported" |
| "CPU time" | `cpu_usage_nsec` as `h:mm:ss` |
| "Manager" | "System" or "User" |

Behaviour:
- Startup combo: shows the current word ("Enabled (runtime)" shows "Enabled"). Static, Indirect, Generated, Transient: the combo is disabled, shows the current word, tooltip "This unit has no install section". A different choice marks the tab dirty (enables Apply). `apply` runs `flows::run_set_startup` for this unit through the window's `SysActions` with the window texts: `done_one` "Changes applied" (replaces "Startup type changed" in this window), failure "Failed to change startup type: <error>". `reset` restores the shown value.
- Start, Stop, Restart: enablement as the Services menu (Start when not active, Stop and Restart when active, all disabled while an action is pending on the unit); they call `flows::run_unit_verb` through the window's `SysActions`; while pending the Status line shows the overlay label ("Starting…" etc.) and all three are disabled. - Links: `man:` documentation -> `OpenUri("man:<page>")`; `http:` and `https:` -> `OpenUri(url)`; failure toast "Could not open the link". Unit file and drop-in links -> `OpenUri(file_uri(path))`; failure toast "Could not open the unit file". No success toasts.
- Main PID link: activates the main window and runs the Processes jump (E22-A3) with the UI-SYS-021 texts ("Switched to service process.", "Service process not visible in the current process view." with "Show").
- Right-click on any value: `TlMenu` with one item "Copy value"; copies the value text; toast "Copied to clipboard".

- **Given** `memory_current = u64::MAX` **When** the tab renders **Then** Memory reads "Not reported".

- **Given** the combo changed from Enabled to Disabled **When** Apply is pressed and the action succeeds **Then** the window toast reads "Changes applied" and the tab is clean.

title: Service Properties: Logs tab list, toolbar, filter, copy, Open in terminal
description:
## Context
The Logs tab of Service Properties shows the unit's journal for the current boot: a toolbar (filter, Follow, Load older, Copy, Open in terminal) over a monospace list with time, priority and message columns, coloured by priority. Lines are streamed from the engine's journal handle. This bead writes the `LogsView` entity, the toolbar, the list, the filter, copy and Open in terminal. Follow mode, paging and the states come in the next two beads. Sources: UI-SYS-036, SYS-015, R-074, R-118, ADR-005 (`EngineClient::journal`, `JournalHandle`, `JournalEvent`, `JournalEntry`), R-134 (`Launch`), table (d), U-40.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/windows/service_properties/logs.rs` and `mod logs;` plus its wiring as the Logs tab in `windows/service_properties/mod.rs`.

```rust
pub struct LogLine { pub time: SharedString, pub prio_word: SharedString, pub priority: u8,
                     pub first_line: SharedString, pub extra_lines: u32, pub full: Arc<str>,
                     pub pid: Option<u32>, pub cursor: Arc<str> }
pub struct LogsView {
    unit: UnitRef,
    lines: VecDeque<LogLine>,        // formatted once on arrival
    filtered: Vec<u32>,              // indices into lines shown after the filter
    filter: SharedString,
    handle: Option<JournalHandle>,
    follow: bool,                    // default true
    stick_to_bottom: bool,
    new_since_unstick: u32,
    selection: Selection<u32>,       // line index selection
    scroll: UniformListScrollHandle,
    focus: FocusHandle,
}
pub fn priority_word(p: u8) -> &'static str; // 0 emerg, 1 alert, 2 crit, 3 err, 4 warning, 5 notice, 6 info, 7 debug
pub fn priority_tone(p: u8) -> LabelTone;    // 0..=3 Danger, 4 Warning, 5..=6 Primary, 7 Secondary
pub fn format_copy_line(l: &LogLine, out: &mut String); // "<time> <priority> <message>" with the full multi-line message
```

Opening: when the Logs tab is first shown, `handle = Some(client.journal(JournalQuery { unit, follow: true }))` (the engine sends the last 200 entries of this boot first). A task reads `handle.events()`; each `Batch { entries, older, .. }` is formatted once (`time` local `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` from `realtime_us`; `prio_word`; `first_line` = message up to the first `\n`; `extra_lines` = number of further lines) and appended (or, for `older`, prepended), then `filtered` is updated for the new lines only.

Toolbar (`h_flex`, gap `sp4`, padding y `sp2`, height 32, `toolbar` background, bottom border):

| Part | Widget | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Filter | `TlTextInput` small with `search` prefix, cleanable, placeholder "Filter logs", width 220 | case-insensitive substring over message and priority word, 100 ms debounce, applied to loaded lines only |
| Follow | `TlButton::Segment` with icon `arrow-down-to-line` 14, label "Follow", 24 high | on by default (behaviour in the follow bead) |
| Load older | `TlButton::Secondary` sm "Load older", 24 high | behaviour in the follow bead |
| Copy | `TlButton::Icon` `copy` 14, 24 x 24, tooltip "Copy logs to clipboard" | right side |
| Open in terminal | `TlButton::Icon` `terminal` 14, 24 x 24, tooltip "Open in terminal" | right side |

List: `uniform_list`, font family "Noto Sans Mono" (bundled, R-118) at `t_sm` (12), line height 18, `list_bg`, no alternate rows. Columns: time 19 characters wide in `text_secondary`; priority word 7 characters wide with `sp4` on both sides; message the rest, one line with ellipsis; multi-line messages show the first line plus " (+N lines)" in `text_secondary`. Colours: `priority_tone` for both the priority word and the message; the time column is always `text_secondary`. Selected lines: `row_selected` with `text_selected_primary`; danger and warning colours stay.

Interaction:
- Click selects one line, Shift+click a range, Ctrl+click toggles; `ServiceLogsSelectAll` (Ctrl+A) selects all shown lines; `ServiceLogsCopySelected` (Ctrl+C) copies the selected lines with `format_copy_line` joined by `\n`, toast "Copied to clipboard". The list has key context `JournalList` and a focus handle.
- Hover over a message 600 ms: tooltip with the full message (first 2000 characters) and "PID <n>" when `pid` is known.
- Copy button: copies all shown lines (after the filter) with `format_copy_line`, toast "Copied to clipboard".
- Open in terminal: sends `ActionKind::Launch(LaunchSpec { what: LaunchWhat::Command("xdg-terminal-exec journalctl -u \"<id>\" -b"), as_admin: false, cwd: None })` (user units: `--user-unit` instead of `-u`); if that action fails, sends the same with `konsole -e journalctl …`; if that fails too, Error toast "Could not open a terminal". The unit id is quoted with Desktop Entry `Exec` rules: wrapped in double quotes, with `"`, `` ` ``, `$` and `\` escaped by a backslash.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** entries with priorities 3, 4, 6 and 7 **When** the list renders **Then** their priority words are "err", "warning", "info", "debug" in `status.danger`, `status.warning`, `text_primary`, `text_secondary`.
- **Given** a three-line message **When** its row renders **Then** it shows the first line plus " (+2 lines)" in `text_secondary`.
- **Given** the filter "timeout" **When** 100 ms pass after the last keystroke **Then** only lines whose message or priority word contains "timeout" (any case) are shown; the input of a second key within 100 ms restarts the wait.
- **Given** two selected lines **When** Ctrl+C is pressed in the list **Then** the clipboard holds both lines as "<time> <priority> <message>" with full messages, joined by a newline.
- **Given** the unit `sshd.service` (system) **When** Open in terminal is pressed **Then** a `Launch` action with command `xdg-terminal-exec journalctl -u "sshd.service" -b` is sent.
- **Given** both terminal launches fail **When** the second failure arrives **Then** the Error toast "Could not open a terminal" shows.

- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_service_props.rs`: add the tests below

- `ui_service_props::logs_copy_format`.
- `ui_service_props::logs_multiline_suffix`.

## Cross-cutting

title: Service Properties: Logs follow mode, new-lines pill, Load older, 10,000-line cap
description:
## Context
The Logs tab follows new journal lines by default and sticks to the bottom; scrolling up unsticks and counts new lines into a pill; Follow off stops the stream and on resumes from the last cursor; Load older pages 200 entries back; at most 10,000 lines are kept. This bead adds that behaviour to `LogsView`. Sources: UI-SYS-037, SYS-015, R-074, R-118, U-49, ADR-005 (`JournalHandle::load_older`, `set_follow`).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/service_properties/logs.rs`:

- Stick to bottom: when the list is scrolled to within one line (18 px times scale) of the bottom, `stick_to_bottom = true` and each appended batch scrolls so the newest line stays visible (`scroll_to_item(last, ScrollStrategy::Bottom)`, `gpui-pre-0.3.7/src/elements/uniform_list.rs:150`). Scrolling up by more than one line sets it false; new lines then add to `new_since_unstick`.
- Pill: while `!stick_to_bottom && new_since_unstick > 0`, a `TlButton::Primary` sm, fully rounded, `accent` fill, 24 high, centred horizontally, 16 px above the list bottom, text "↓ N new lines" (N thin-space grouped). Clicking it, or `ServiceLogsBottom` (End), scrolls to the bottom, sets `stick_to_bottom = true`, resets the count, hides the pill. `ServiceLogsTop` (Home) scrolls to the top. Reduced motion: the pill appears without fade; scrolling to the bottom is instant either way. The pill is focusable with the same accessible name as its text.
- Follow toggle: off -> `handle.set_follow(false)` (the engine kills the `-f` child at once), the pill hides; on -> `handle.set_follow(true)` (the engine resumes with `--after-cursor` at the last cursor, so no line is lost or doubled).
- Leaving the Logs tab or closing the window drops the handle (child killed). Returning to the tab keeps the loaded lines and opens a new handle that resumes from the last loaded cursor.
- Load older: `handle.load_older()`; the button shows "Loading…" and is disabled until the `Batch { older: true, .. }` arrives; lines are inserted at the top and the scroll position is kept on the line that was first before (adjust the scroll offset by the inserted count times the line height). When the batch had fewer than 200 entries (`exhausted = true`), the button reads "No older entries" and stays disabled.
- Cap: at most 10,000 lines. In follow mode, beyond the cap the oldest lines are dropped (and removed from `filtered` and the selection) and Load older is enabled again.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the list at the bottom **When** a batch of 5 lines arrives **Then** the newest line is visible and no pill shows.
- **Given** the user scrolled up 10 lines **When** 12 lines arrive **Then** the scroll position is unchanged and the pill reads "↓ 12 new lines".
- **Given** the pill shows **When** End is pressed **Then** the list is at the bottom and the pill is gone.
- **Given** Follow on **When** the user turns it off **Then** the fake engine records `set_follow(false)` and later batches stop.
- **Given** 300 loaded lines with the first visible line L **When** Load older returns 200 lines **Then** L is still the first visible line and the button is enabled again.
- **Given** Load older returns 37 lines with `exhausted = true` **When** the batch arrives **Then** the button reads "No older entries" and is disabled.
- **Given** 10,000 lines loaded in follow mode **When** 50 more arrive **Then** the 50 oldest are dropped and Load older is enabled.
- **Given** the user leaves the Logs tab and comes back **When** the tab shows again **Then** the earlier lines are still there and a new handle resumes after the last cursor.

## Files

title: E27-A3 Service Properties
description:
## Context
Anchor E27-A3. The Service Properties window is a floating secondary window per unit with five tabs (General, Log On, Recovery, Dependencies, Logs), an OK / Cancel / Apply footer, its own toast stack, a cap of 10 windows, and focus-existing on a second open. This bead writes the window frame and its open API in `windows/service_properties/mod.rs`; the tab contents come in later beads. Sources: UI-SYS-030, SYS-011 (frame), SYS-015 ("View logs" entry), SYS-018 (OpenRC: General only), APP-045, R-073 (pin), UI-FND-021, ADR-008 (`Demand.unit_details`, max 10), R-119, canonical table (b) `ServiceProps` rows, R-120.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/service_properties/mod.rs`:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum ServicePropsTab { General, LogOn, Recovery, Dependencies, Logs }

/// What each tab view implements so the footer can apply it.
pub trait ServicePropsTabView {
    fn is_dirty(&self, cx: &App) -> bool;
    fn is_valid(&self, cx: &App) -> bool { true }
    /// Starts the apply; returns the action ids it submitted (empty when nothing to do).
    fn apply(&mut self, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App) -> SmallVec<[ActionId; 2]>;
    fn reset(&mut self, cx: &mut App);
}

pub struct ServicePropertiesWindow {
    unit: UnitRef,
    details: Option<Arc<UnitDetails>>,   // pointer-compared on every SERVICES change
    not_loaded: bool,
    active: ServicePropsTab,
    tabs: TabViews,                      // one Option<AnyView + ServicePropsTabView handle> per tab, created on first show
    actions: Entity<SysActions>,         // this window's own action layer (toasts in this window)
    applying: SmallVec<[(ActionId, ServicePropsTab); 4]>,
    close_after_apply: bool,
    focus: FocusHandle,
}

impl ServicePropertiesWindow {
    /// Opens or focuses the window for `unit`, on `tab`.
    pub fn open(unit: UnitRef, tab: ServicePropsTab, cx: &mut App);
}
```

Frame (exact):
- `TlSecondaryWindow::open` with kind Properties (`WindowKind::Floating`, own gpui-kit Root), default size 720 x 560, minimum 560 x 440, resizable, title "<id> Properties" (for example "sshd.service Properties"), pin in the title bar (R-073), key context `ServiceProps` on the root (nested `PropsWindow` rows of table b do not apply; this window uses `ServiceProps`).
- Tab strip `TlTabs`, 32 high, tabs "General", "Log On", "Recovery", "Dependencies", "Logs", `tab_bg`, active tab with the `accent` underline. OpenRC backend (`ServicesSnapshot.backend == OpenRc`): only "General".
- Content area padding `sp6` (16), `window_bg`.
- Footer: `h_flex` right-aligned, gap `sp4`, padding `sp5`, height 48, `toolbar` background, 1 px `divider` top border. Buttons: "OK" `TlButton::Primary` md min width 80; "Cancel" `TlButton::Secondary` md min width 80; "Apply" `TlButton::Secondary` md min width 80, disabled unless some tab `is_dirty` and every dirty tab `is_valid`. OK is disabled while any dirty tab is invalid.
- Registry: `WindowRegistry` key `WindowKey::Service(unit)`. A second `open` for the same unit activates the existing window and switches to `tab`. When 10 Service Properties windows are open, an 11th `open` opens nothing and pushes the Warning toast "Too many service properties windows are already open" on the main window.
- Demand: while open, the window's `UnitRef` is in `Demand.unit_details` (through `DemandAggregator`; max 10); removed on close.
- Data: on `SnapshotChanged` with `ComponentMask::SERVICES`, read `ServicesSnapshot.details.get(&unit)`; notify only when the `Arc<UnitDetails>` pointer changed (`Arc::ptr_eq`) or the unit's presence in `units` changed. Unit gone or no longer loaded: title becomes "<id> Properties (not loaded)", values stay as last seen in `text_secondary`, Apply and the General tab's Start, Stop, Restart buttons are disabled. A tab whose data has not arrived shows "Collecting…" in its value fields.
- Apply: calls `apply` on every dirty tab and records the returned ids in `applying`. When every recorded action reaches a final state: all succeeded -> the tabs reset their dirty state; if `close_after_apply` (OK), the window closes. Any failure -> the window stays open and switches to the first failing tab. OK = Apply with `close_after_apply = true`; OK with nothing dirty closes at once.
- Cancel, Esc and Ctrl+W close without applying and without a question.
- Keys (`ServiceProps` context, bound in `pages/services/actions.rs`): `ServicePropsNextTab` (Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+PgDn), `ServicePropsPrevTab` (Ctrl+Shift+Tab, Ctrl+PgUp), `ServicePropsSelectTab { index }` (Ctrl+1..Ctrl+5), `ServicePropsOk` (Enter outside text inputs). Hidden tabs are skipped by next and previous; selecting a hidden tab does nothing.
- Focus starts on the tab strip. Tab order: tab strip, tab content, footer buttons left to right, then the pin.
- Toasts for actions started from this window appear in this window's own stack (UI-FND-020 rule 9) through its own `SysActions`.
- Tab views are placeholders in this bead: each tab shows an empty `div` until its bead lands; `TabViews` stores them as `Option` and creates a tab's view the first time it is shown.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** no window for sshd.service **When** `open(sshd, General)` runs **Then** a 720 x 560 window titled "sshd.service Properties" opens with five tabs and General active, and `Demand.unit_details` contains sshd.service.
- **Given** that window is open **When** `open(sshd, Logs)` runs **Then** no second window opens; the existing one is activated with Logs active.
- **Given** 10 Service Properties windows **When** an 11th `open` runs **Then** nothing opens and the main window shows "Too many service properties windows are already open".
- **Given** a SERVICES change that leaves sshd's `Arc<UnitDetails>` unchanged **When** it is installed **Then** the window does not re-render.
- **Given** sshd.service disappears from the snapshot **When** the next snapshot is installed **Then** the title reads "sshd.service Properties (not loaded)" and Apply is disabled.
- **Given** a dirty tab whose apply fails **When** OK is pressed **Then** the window stays open on that tab.
- **Given** a dirty tab whose apply succeeds **When** OK is pressed **Then** the window closes after the success event.
- **Given** the OpenRC backend **When** the window opens **Then** only the "General" tab is shown.
- **Given** the window is focused **When** Ctrl+3 is pressed **Then** the Recovery tab becomes active.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/service_properties/mod.rs`: change, the window frame above
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_service_props.rs`: create (E27 owns it); add the tests below
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append the title pattern, tab names, button labels, the cap toast and " (not loaded)" (keys `services-sys030-<slug>`)

## Tests
- `ui_service_props::service_props_cap_10`.
- `ui_service_props::service_props_focus_existing`.
- `ui_service_props::service_props_ok_applies_then_closes` (test tab view that is dirty and submits one action; fake engine succeeds).
- `ui_service_props::service_props_failed_apply_stays_on_tab`.
- `ui_service_props::service_props_not_loaded_title`.
- `ui_service_props::service_props_rerender_only_on_own_details`.
- `ui_service_props::service_props_tab_keys`.
- `ui_service_props::service_props_demand_unit_details`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the cap toast; apply failures keep the window open (texts from the tab beads).
- Validity: "Collecting…" in fields whose data has not arrived (R-050 words).
- Accessibility: focus starts on the tab strip; Esc closes; Enter outside text fields is OK; every control reachable with Tab.
- Performance: one window renders only when its unit's details Arc changes; tabs are created on first show.
- Privacy: N/A

- `TlSecondaryWindow`, `WindowRegistry`, `WindowKey::Service`, `ToastQueue` are E16-A2; `TlTabs` and `TlButton` E15-A1; `SysActions` E27-A1.

title: Service Properties: Logs loading, empty, error and access states
description:
## Context
The Logs tab shows text states while the first fetch runs, when there are no entries, when the filter hides everything, and when `journalctl` is missing, times out or fails; when the user may only read their own entries it shows a banner with a "Copy command" button. Sources: UI-SYS-038, SYS-015 (privilege banner), APP-042, PERF-105, ADR-005 (`JournalEvent::Access`, `JournalError`), UI-FND-029, UI-FND-031.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/service_properties/logs.rs`, add the state logic and rendering. Text states are centred in the list area, `t_base` `text_secondary`:

| State | Display |
|---|---|
| First fetch running (handle open, no batch yet) | "Loading logs…" (no skeleton) |
| First batch empty | "No log entries for this unit in the current boot." |
| Lines loaded, filter hides all | "No log entries match the filter." |
| `JournalError::NotFound` | `TlEmptyState` icon `circle-alert`, heading "journalctl not found", no button |
| `JournalError::Timeout` | `TlEmptyState` heading "Reading the journal took too long.", button "Retry" |
| `JournalError::Exit { stderr_first_line, .. }` | `TlEmptyState` heading "Could not read the journal", text = `stderr_first_line`, button "Retry" |

- Retry drops the handle and opens a new one (`client.journal(JournalQuery { unit, follow })`), which requests the last 200 entries again.
- `JournalEvent::Access(JournalAccess::OwnOnly)`: a `TlBanner` (Info, `t_sm`, 32 high) above the list: "Only your own log messages are visible. Add your user to the systemd-journal group to see all." with a button "Copy command" that copies `sudo usermod -aG systemd-journal $USER` (literal text, `$USER` not expanded) and shows the toast "Copied to clipboard". The banner cannot be dismissed. `JournalAccess::All` hides it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the tab just opened **When** no batch has arrived **Then** "Loading logs…" shows.
- **Given** an empty first batch **When** it arrives **Then** "No log entries for this unit in the current boot." shows.
- **Given** loaded lines and a filter that matches none **When** the filter applies **Then** "No log entries match the filter." shows.
- **Given** `JournalError::Timeout` **When** it arrives **Then** "Reading the journal took too long." shows with "Retry", and Retry opens a new handle.
- **Given** `Exit { code: 1, stderr_first_line: "Failed to open journal" }` **When** it arrives **Then** the heading "Could not read the journal" and the text "Failed to open journal" show.
- **Given** `Access(OwnOnly)` **When** it arrives **Then** the banner shows above the list and "Copy command" puts `sudo usermod -aG systemd-journal $USER` on the clipboard.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/service_properties/logs.rs`: change, states and banner
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_service_props.rs`: add the tests below
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append every string above (keys `services-sys038-<slug>`)

title: Service Properties: Recovery drop-in editor (P3)
description:
## Context
From P3 the Recovery tab becomes an editor: the user changes restart and failure settings, and Apply writes a tasklens drop-in with only the changed keys (system units through the privileged helper, user units directly), then the engine reloads systemd. A button removes the tasklens drop-in after a confirmation. Input is validated before it can reach the helper. Sources: UI-SYS-034, SYS-013 (P3 edit), R-004 (`WriteServiceDropIn` allowlist and fixed path), R-002, R-119 (`UnitWriteRecovery`, `UnitRemoveRecovery`, empty key set deletes), ADR-006, ADR-011 (`write_atomic`), canonical table (c) drop-in paths, UI-FND-021 (confirmation).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/service_properties/recovery.rs`, replace the P2 view with edit mode (`RecoveryTab` now dirty-capable):

```rust
pub struct RecoveryForm {
    pub restart: RestartPolicy,          // no, on-success, on-failure, on-abnormal, on-watchdog, on-abort, always
    pub restart_ms: u32,                 // 0..=3_600_000, step 100
    pub burst: u32,                      // 0..=1000
    pub interval_s: u32,                 // 0..=86_400
    pub start_limit_action: LimitAction, // none, reboot, reboot-force, reboot-immediate, poweroff, poweroff-force, poweroff-immediate, exit, exit-force
    pub failure_action: LimitAction,
    pub on_failure: SharedString,        // unit names separated by spaces
}
pub fn validate_on_failure(text: &str) -> bool;
pub fn changed_keys(form: &RecoveryForm, current: &RecoverySettings, in_dropin: &RecoveryKeySet) -> RecoveryEdit;
```

Layout (labels with trailing ":"):

| Field | Widget | Range or values |
|---|---|---|
| "On failure" | `TlSelect` width 200 | no, on-success, on-failure, on-abnormal, on-watchdog, on-abort, always |
| "Restart service after" | `TlStepper` width 100, suffix "ms" | 0..=3 600 000, step 100 |
| "Give up after" | two `TlStepper` width 80: "<starts> starts within <s> s" | starts 0..=1000; within 0..=86 400 s |
| "When giving up", "Failure action" | `TlSelect` width 200 | none, reboot, reboot-force, reboot-immediate, poweroff, poweroff-force, poweroff-immediate, exit, exit-force |
| "Run on failure" | `TlTextInput`, full width | unit names separated by spaces |
| "Restarts so far" | text, read-only | `NRestarts` |
| "Saved as" | `t_sm` `text_secondary`, selectable | `/etc/systemd/system/<unit>.d/50-tasklens-recovery.conf` (system) or `~/.config/systemd/user/<unit>.d/50-tasklens-recovery.conf` (user) |
| "Remove tasklens settings" | `TlButton::Secondary` sm | shown only when `UnitDetails.recovery_dropin_exists` |

States and rules:
- Form created on tab open from `UnitDetails.recovery`; `reset` (Cancel) recreates it.
- Dirty: Apply enabled only when a value differs from the unit's current value.
- Validation: each space-separated token of "Run on failure" must match `^[A-Za-z0-9:_.\\@%-]{1,255}\.(service|socket|target|timer|mount|path|slice|scope)$`. Invalid input: 1 px `status.danger` border and the line "Enter unit names separated by spaces, for example failure-notify@%n.service" (`t_sm` `status.danger`) under the field; `is_valid` false, so Apply and OK are disabled.
- A reboot or poweroff value (reboot, reboot-force, reboot-immediate, poweroff, poweroff-force, poweroff-immediate) in "When giving up" or "Failure action": a `t_sm` `status.warning` line under that field: "The computer will restart or power off when this happens.".
- System unit, helper not installed (the helper state in `HealthSnapshot` says not installed; E29-A2 fills it): every control disabled with tooltip "Needs the tasklens helper", and above the grid a `TlLink` "Additional setup…" dispatching `OpenAdditionalSetup`.
- System unit, helper installed but locked: controls enabled; Apply starts a helper session (the engine's polkit prompt for `io.github.oysteinkrog.tasklens.helper`).
- `apply`: `ActionKind::UnitWriteRecovery(changed_keys(..))` with target `ActionTarget::Unit(unit)`: the edit carries the changed keys plus the keys already in the tasklens drop-in (keys limited to `Restart*`, `StartLimit*`, `FailureAction`, `OnFailure`, R-004); the engine then calls `Manager.Reload()`. Texts: `pending_one` "Saving recovery settings...", `done_one` "Recovery settings saved", `failed_prefix` "Failed to save recovery settings", `failed_suffix = true`; a dismissed pkexec prompt gives "Authentication cancelled" (pkexec exit 126, R-117).
- Remove: a `TlDialog::confirm` window titled "tasklens", heading "Remove tasklens recovery settings?", text "The unit goes back to the settings in its unit file.", buttons "Cancel" (Secondary, focused first) and "Remove" (Danger). Remove sends `ActionKind::UnitRemoveRecovery` for the unit (for system units the engine sends `WriteServiceDropIn` with an empty key set, R-119).
- The P2 note "Editing recovery settings comes in a later version." is removed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** "Run on failure" = "notify@%n.service" **When** validated **Then** it is valid; "rm -rf /" is invalid and Apply is disabled.
- **Given** "Run on failure" = "a.service b;c.service" **When** validated **Then** it is invalid and the danger line shows.
- **Given** "When giving up" set to "reboot" **When** the tab renders **Then** the warning line shows under that field.
- **Given** a system unit and no helper installed **When** the tab renders **Then** every control is disabled with tooltip "Needs the tasklens helper" and the "Additional setup…" link shows.
- **Given** only "Restart service after" changed from 100 to 500 **When** Apply runs **Then** the request is `UnitWriteRecovery` whose edit holds `RestartSec` (500 ms) plus any keys already in the tasklens drop-in, and nothing else.
- **Given** the tasklens drop-in exists **When** "Remove tasklens settings" is pressed **Then** the confirmation opens with focus on "Cancel"; "Remove" sends `UnitRemoveRecovery`.
- **Given** the save succeeds **When** the final event arrives **Then** the toast reads "Recovery settings saved".

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/service_properties/recovery.rs`: change, edit mode
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_service_props.rs`: add the tests below
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append every string above (keys `services-sys034-<slug>`)

## Tests
- `ui_service_props::recovery_invalid_unit_blocks_apply` (regression for the validation pattern; includes shell metacharacters, `/`, newline, 256-char names).
- `ui_service_props::recovery_helper_missing_disables`.
- `ui_service_props::recovery_remove_confirm`.
- `ui_service_props::recovery_changed_keys_only`.
- `ui_service_props::recovery_reboot_warning`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the saving toasts above; "Authentication cancelled" for a dismissed pkexec prompt.
- Validity: "Collecting…" before details arrive.
- Accessibility: each control's accessible name is its row label; the validation text is linked as its description; Tab order follows the rows.
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Security: the UI never sends a path; the engine and helper derive the fixed drop-in path. The validation pattern is the first gate; the helper's allowlist (E29) is the second.
- Labels: `security`. `RecoveryEdit`, `RecoverySettings` are `tl-model` types (E03-A2); `RecoveryKeySet` stands for whatever E03 uses to list the keys present in the tasklens drop-in.
- Helper state and `OpenAdditionalSetup` come from the health snapshot and the shell (E20-A1); the helper itself is E29.

title: Services: actions and bind_keys_services (ServiceTable, ServiceProps, JournalList)
description:
## Context
Every Services command is one GPUI `Action` in the single `tasklens` namespace, carrying the page word in its name; menu items and keys dispatch the same Action. This bead declares all Services, Service Properties and Logs-list actions and their key bindings in `pages/services/actions.rs`. Sources: UI-SYS-011, UI-SYS-012, UI-SYS-017 to UI-SYS-023, UI-SYS-030, UI-SYS-036, UI-SYS-037, R-128, R-129, R-120, canonical table (b) rows for `ServiceTable`, `ServiceProps`, `JournalList`, D-008.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/services/actions.rs` and one `pub mod actions;` line in `pages/services/mod.rs`.

Actions without data (`gpui::actions!(tasklens, [...])`):

title: System tables: status cell looks and painter (sys_status.rs)
description:
## Context
The Services, Startup Apps and Connections tables draw a status cell: a small dot plus a text label, or (Connections) coloured text only. This bead writes the shared look tables and the one cell painter in `pages/sys_status.rs`, so all three tables colour states the same way and never by colour alone. Sources: UI-SYS-003, SYS-003, SYS-020, SYS-029, R-050, APP-058, 00-epics section 2 (`pages/sys_status.rs` owned by E27).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/sys_status.rs`:

```rust
/// One label colour role; resolved against TlTheme at paint time.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum LabelTone { Primary, Secondary, Danger, Warning, Info, Success }

/// Dot shape and colour role. `None` draws no dot (Connections).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum DotStyle { Filled(LabelTone), Ring(LabelTone), None }

/// The UI-side status words of the three tables. Pages map their model enums onto these.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub enum SysStatus {
    // Services (SYS-003 labels)
    Running, Active, Starting, Stopping, Reloading, Stopped, Failed, Maintenance,
    // Startup Apps (SYS-020)
    Enabled, Disabled, Masked, NotInThisDesktop, MissingProgram,
}

/// Connections State column classes (SYS-029). Labels are the page's (E28); only colour lives here.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum ConnStateClass { Listening, Established, Transitional, TimeWaitOrClosed, Unknown, Udp }

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub struct StatusLook { pub dot: DotStyle, pub label: LabelTone }

pub fn status_look(s: SysStatus) -> StatusLook;
pub fn status_label(s: SysStatus) -> SharedString;          // interned once per language, see Strings
pub fn conn_state_tone(c: ConnStateClass) -> LabelTone;
pub fn tone_color(t: LabelTone, theme: &TlTheme, selected: bool) -> Hsla;

/// The status cell: dot 8 x 8, gap sp3 (6 px), label t_base with ellipsis.
pub fn status_cell(look: StatusLook, label: SharedString, selected: bool, stale: bool,
                   theme: &TlTheme, metrics: &UiMetrics) -> impl IntoElement;
```

`status_look` table (exact):

| SysStatus | dot | label |
|---|---|---|
| Running | Filled(Success) | Primary |
| Active | Ring(Success) | Primary |
| Starting, Stopping, Reloading | Filled(Info) | Primary |
| Stopped | Ring(Secondary) | Secondary |
| Failed | Filled(Danger) | Danger |
| Maintenance | Filled(Warning) | Primary |
| Enabled | Filled(Success) | Primary |
| Disabled | Ring(Secondary) | Secondary |
| Masked | Filled(Warning) | Primary |
| NotInThisDesktop | Ring(Secondary) | Secondary |
| MissingProgram | Filled(Warning) | Primary |

The dot tone `Success` means `status.success`; `Success` is never used as a label tone.

`status_label` strings (exact): "Running", "Active", "Starting", "Stopping", "Reloading", "Stopped", "Failed", "Maintenance", "Enabled", "Disabled", "Masked", "Not in this desktop", "Missing program".

`conn_state_tone`: Listening -> Info; Established -> Primary; Transitional (SYN-SENT, SYN-RECEIVED, FIN-WAIT-1, FIN-WAIT-2, CLOSE-WAIT, CLOSING, LAST-ACK) -> Primary; TimeWaitOrClosed -> Secondary; Unknown -> Warning; Udp (UNCONNECTED and CONNECTED) -> Secondary.

`tone_color(t, theme, selected)`: Primary -> `text_primary` (selected: `text_selected_primary`); Secondary -> `text_secondary` (selected: `text_selected_secondary`); Danger -> `status.danger` in both cases (a failure stays visible on a selected row); Warning -> `status.warning`; Info -> `status.info`; Success -> `status.success`. Dots keep their colour on a selected row.

`status_cell` geometry: an `h_flex` with `items_center`, `gap(sp3)`; dot is a `div().size(px(8) * scale).rounded_full()` with `bg(color)` for `Filled` or `border(px(1.5) * scale).border_color(color)` for `Ring`; label `t_base`, `text_ellipsis`, `whitespace_nowrap`, `overflow_hidden`. `DotStyle::None` draws no dot and no gap. Stale (`stale = true`): label colour is `text_secondary` whatever the tone, and the dot colour is drawn at 50% alpha.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** each `SysStatus` value **When** `status_look` is called **Then** it returns the dot and label tones of the table above.
- **Given** `SysStatus::Failed` and `selected = true` **When** `tone_color(look.label, ..)` is called **Then** it returns `status.danger`, not `text_selected_primary`.
- **Given** `SysStatus::Running` and `selected = true` **When** the label colour is resolved **Then** it is `text_selected_primary` and the dot is still `status.success`.
- **Given** `stale = true` **When** `status_cell` renders `Running` **Then** the label uses `text_secondary` and the dot alpha is half the theme colour's alpha.
- **Given** `DotStyle::None` **When** `status_cell` renders **Then** the element has no dot child and the label starts at the cell's left padding.
- **Given** each `ConnStateClass` **When** `conn_state_tone` is called **Then** it returns the tone listed above.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/sys_status.rs`: create the types and functions above
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_sys_table.rs`: create (E27 owns it); add the tests below
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append the 13 status labels (chain edit allowed by 00-epics, see Notes)

## Tests
- `ui_sys_table::status_cell_colors_per_state`: for every `SysStatus`, `status_look` matches the table, and `tone_color` with the Default Dark theme maps each tone to the named token.
- `ui_sys_table::status_cell_selected_keeps_danger`: `Failed` selected resolves to `status.danger`; `Running` selected resolves to `text_selected_primary`.
- `ui_sys_table::status_cell_stale_dims`: `TestAppContext` render of `status_cell(.., stale: true, ..)`; the label colour is `text_secondary` and the dot alpha is halved.
- `ui_sys_table::conn_state_tones`: one assertion per `ConnStateClass`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: stale only (dimmed). Other validity glyphs are drawn by `table/cells.rs` (E18), not here.
- Accessibility: the label always shows; colour is a second cue only (APP-058).
- Performance: no allocation per frame; `status_label` returns cached `SharedString`s interned once per language (keep them in a `OnceCell` keyed by the `strings_version` from `i18n.rs`).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Strings: append each label to `assets/locales/en-US.ftl` with keys `sys-sys003-<slug>` where the slug is the label lowercased with spaces replaced by `-` (for example `sys-sys003-not-in-this-desktop = Not in this desktop`). Read them with `tr(key)` from `i18n.rs` (E16-A1). The `.ftl` append is the chain edit 00-epics section 2 allows "in the bead that uses them".
- UI-SYS-003 names `table/cells.rs` for the painter; 00-epics section 2 moves system-table status cells to `pages/sys_status.rs` (E27). Follow 00-epics; never edit `table/cells.rs`.
- Colour tokens are `TlTheme` fields (E17-A1); `UiMetrics` gives `sp3` and the scale.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, check, clippy or test through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_sys_table`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: System tables: SysQuery and SysPageState (query generation, demand, first visit)
System tables: skeleton and empty or error body states
description:
## Context
Before the first data of a session a system table shows skeleton rows under a live header; afterwards an empty or failed table shows a centred empty state. This bead writes the body-state decision and its rendering in `pages/sys_table.rs`, shared by Services, Startup Apps and Connections. Sources: UI-SYS-004, UI-SYS-005, UI-FND-024, UI-FND-029, UI-SHL-111, R-060, APP-059, SYS-001, SYS-016, SYS-027, SYS-028, SYS-036, U-48.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/sys_table.rs`, add:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum SysBody {
    Skeleton,                        // first data not seen yet in this session
    Rows,                            // draw the TlTreeTable body
    NoMatches,                       // rows empty and a filter is active
    NoEntries,                       // rows empty, no filter, source fine
    FailedFirst { error: SharedString }, // source Failed before first data
    ManagerMissing,                  // Services only: both systemd managers Unavailable
}

pub struct SysBodyInput<'a> {
    pub tab: Tab,
    pub first_data_seen: bool,
    pub rows_len: usize,
    pub filter_active: bool,              // text filter non-empty, or (Services) strip not at defaults
    pub source: Option<&'a SourceHealth>, // health of the page's source; Services passes the worse of the two
    pub managers_unavailable: bool,       // Services only
}

pub fn sys_body(input: &SysBodyInput) -> SysBody;
pub fn render_skeleton(columns: &[Pixels], viewport_h: Pixels, metrics: &UiMetrics) -> AnyElement;
pub fn render_empty(body: &SysBody, tab: Tab, clear_action: Box<dyn Action>, cx: &App) -> AnyElement;
```

`sys_body` order of rules (first match wins):
1. `source` state `Failed` and `!first_data_seen` -> `FailedFirst { error: last_error }` (one line).
2. `!first_data_seen` -> `Skeleton`.
3. `tab == Services && managers_unavailable` -> `ManagerMissing`.
4. `rows_len == 0 && filter_active` -> `NoMatches`.
5. `rows_len == 0` -> `NoEntries` (Services never returns this: with no filter and managers reachable it returns `Rows`).
6. otherwise `Rows`.
A `Failed` source after first data keeps `Rows` (the status chip shows the health item; no empty state).

`render_skeleton`: `TlSkeletonRows { rows: min(floor(viewport_h / row_h), 12), columns }` (UI-FND-024: bar height 10, `r_sm`, widths `[0.6, 0.45, 0.8, 0.5, 0.7]` of each column width, inset `sp4`, alternating `list_bg` / `row_alt`). It is drawn in place of the `uniform_list`, never inside it.

`render_empty` uses `TlEmptyState` (icon `i_lg`, heading `t_md` semibold, text `t_base` `text_secondary` max width 420, optional `TlButton::Secondary` sm), with these exact values:

| SysBody, tab | Icon | Heading | Text | Button |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ManagerMissing (Services) | `server` | "systemd not found" | "tasklens lists services from systemd. Neither the system manager nor the user manager answered." | "Retry" -> `RefreshCurrentTab` |
| NoMatches, Services | `funnel-x` | "No matches" | "No services match the current filters." | "Clear filters" -> `clear_action` |
| NoMatches, Startup | `funnel-x` | "No matches" | "No startup entries match the filter." | "Clear filter" -> `clear_action` |
| NoMatches, Connections | `funnel-x` | "No matches" | "No connections match the filter." | "Clear filter" -> `clear_action` |
| NoEntries, Startup | `app-window` | "No startup entries" | "Nothing starts automatically when you log in." | none |
| NoEntries, Connections | `network` | "No connections" | none | none |
| FailedFirst, Services | `circle-alert` in `status.warning` | "Could not load services" | the error | "Retry" -> `RefreshCurrentTab` |
| FailedFirst, Startup | same | "Could not load startup entries" | the error | "Retry" -> `RefreshCurrentTab` |
| FailedFirst, Connections | same | "Could not load connections" | the error | "Retry" -> `RefreshCurrentTab` |

The "Clear filters" / "Clear filter" button action is passed in, so this file does not depend on the Services actions: Services passes `ServicesClearAllFilters`, Startup Apps and Connections pass `ClearFilter`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `first_data_seen = false` and a healthy source **When** `sys_body` runs **Then** it returns `Skeleton`.
- **Given** `first_data_seen = false` and the source `Failed` with `last_error = "bus timeout"` **When** `sys_body` runs **Then** it returns `FailedFirst { error: "bus timeout" }`.
- **Given** `first_data_seen = true`, `rows_len = 0`, a non-empty text filter on Startup **When** the body renders **Then** it shows "No matches", "No startup entries match the filter." and a "Clear filter" button that dispatches `ClearFilter`.
- **Given** Services with both managers `Unavailable` **When** the body renders **Then** it shows "systemd not found" with a "Retry" button that dispatches `RefreshCurrentTab`.
- **Given** `first_data_seen = true` and the source turns `Failed` **When** `sys_body` runs **Then** it returns `Rows`.
- **Given** a viewport of 1000 px and `row_h = 28` **When** `render_skeleton` runs **Then** it draws 12 rows.
- **Given** the skeleton showed, data arrived, the tab was left and re-entered **When** the body is computed **Then** it is never `Skeleton` again in the session.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/sys_table.rs`: add `SysBody`, `SysBodyInput`, `sys_body`, `render_skeleton`, `render_empty`
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_sys_table.rs`: add the tests below
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append the strings of the table (keys `sys-sys005-<slug>`, see Notes)

## Tests
- `ui_sys_table::sys_body_rules_order`: one case per rule above, including Failed-after-data -> `Rows`.
- `ui_sys_table::skeleton_shows_once_per_session`: fake engine with an empty `WarmingUp` component, then rows, then empty again; the page body is `Skeleton` only in the first state.
- `ui_sys_table::skeleton_row_count_capped_at_12`.
- `ui_sys_table::empty_state_strings_per_tab`: render each table row of `render_empty` and compare heading, text and button label.
- `ui_sys_table::services_systemd_missing_state`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `SourceHealth.last_error` shown as one line with ellipsis; never a toast (ADR-015).
- Validity: `WarmingUp` before first data drives the skeleton; `Failed` drives `FailedFirst`.
- Accessibility: the heading is the region's accessible name; Tab reaches the button; Enter or Space presses it. While the skeleton shows, keys and clicks on the body do nothing; the header stays live.
- Performance: the kit `Skeleton` requests frames while visible (2 s pulse; U-48 says it stops once removed). Twelve rows by up to 7 bars is at most 84 quads. Reduced motion: static at opacity 0.7 (UI-FND-024).
- Privacy: N/A
