title: E06-003 sock_diag netlink dump requests
description:
## Context
Sends the `SOCK_DIAG_BY_FAMILY` dump requests to the kernel and feeds the replies to `parse_dump` (E06-002). The Connections worker (E14) calls it every 2 s while demanded; the per-process TCP column uses the TCP part. Unprivileged dumps work; the `inet_diag` and `udp_diag` modules load on demand. Sources: SYS-028, PROC-032, ADR-016, ADR-008 (connections every 2 s).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-collect/src/net/sock_diag.rs`:

```rust
pub struct SockDiag { sock: netlink_sys::Socket, buf: Vec<u8>, seq: u32 }
impl SockDiag {
    /// Opens a NETLINK_SOCK_DIAG (protocol 4) socket with SOCK_CLOEXEC, bound with port id 0.
    pub fn open() -> Result<Self, CollectError>;
    /// One dump for one family and protocol. Appends to `out`.
    pub fn dump(&mut self, family: Family, proto: Proto, out: &mut Vec<SockRecord>) -> Result<(), CollectError>;
    /// The four dumps TCPv4, TCPv6, UDPv4, UDPv6 in that order. Clears `out` first.
    pub fn dump_all(&mut self, out: &mut Vec<SockRecord>) -> Result<(), CollectError>;
    /// TCP v4 and v6 only, for per-process attribution when the Connections tab is not shown.
    pub fn dump_tcp(&mut self, out: &mut Vec<SockRecord>) -> Result<(), CollectError>;
}
```

Request (`inet_diag_req_v2`): `sdiag_family` = 2 or 10, `sdiag_protocol` = 6 or 17, `idiag_states = 0xFFF` (all states), `idiag_ext = 1 << (INET_DIAG_INFO - 1)` for TCP (INET_DIAG_INFO = 2) and 0 for UDP, zeroed `id` with `idiag_cookie = [!0, !0]` (INET_DIAG_NOCOOKIE). Netlink flags `NLM_F_REQUEST | NLM_F_DUMP` (0x1 | 0x300), type 20, sequence number incremented per request.

Receive loop: `recv` into `buf` (capacity 64 KiB, kept between calls) until `parse_dump` returns `Ok(true)`. A reply whose sequence number differs from the request is skipped. `EINTR` is retried; any other `recv` error is returned. A protocol whose diag module is missing (`ENOENT` or `EINVAL` in `NLMSG_ERROR`) returns `Ok(())` with nothing appended, so UDP missing never hides TCP.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a test process that listens on TCP 127.0.0.1 port P **When** `dump_all` runs **Then** `out` holds a TCP V4 record with `sport == P`, `state == 10` and `inode != 0`.
- **Given** a bound UDP v6 socket on [::1] port Q **When** `dump_all` runs **Then** `out` holds a UDP V6 record with `sport == Q`.
- **Given** an established TCP pair over loopback that has sent 1000 bytes **When** `dump_tcp` runs **Then** the sender's record has `tcp_info.bytes_acked >= 1000`.
- **Given** two calls to `dump_all` **When** the second runs **Then** `out` holds only the second dump (cleared first) and the `buf` capacity is unchanged.

title: E06-004 Socket inode to process map
description:
## Context
Maps socket inodes to the processes that hold them, by walking `/proc/<pid>/fd` symlinks of the form `socket:[<inode>]`. The Connections tab shows the owner from it, and the per-process TCP Network column attributes traffic with it. Other users' fd directories give EACCES; those pids are recorded as restricted so the UI can show the lock glyph, never 0 and never blank. Sources: SYS-030, PROC-032, ADR-016 ("Socket to pid map", "Restricted, not zero"), U-23.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/net/socket_map.rs` (add `pub mod socket_map;` to `net/mod.rs`):

```rust
pub struct SocketMap {
    /// inode -> every process holding an fd to it, sorted by ProcessKey, no duplicates.
    pub owners: rustc_hash::FxHashMap<u64, smallvec::SmallVec<[tl_model::ProcessKey; 1]>>,
    /// pids whose /proc/<pid>/fd could not be read (EACCES or EPERM), with their uid from fstat of /proc/<pid>.
    pub restricted: rustc_hash::FxHashMap<u32, u32>, // pid -> uid
    pub built_ns: tl_model::TimeNs,                   // now_boot_ns() at the start of the walk
    pub elapsed_ns: u64,                              // walk duration, for the U-23 budget
}
impl SocketMap {
    pub fn new() -> Self;
    /// Rebuilds in place, reusing the maps' capacity.
    pub fn rebuild(&mut self, root: &SysRoot, boot: tl_model::BootId) -> Result<(), CollectError>;
    pub fn owners_of(&self, inode: u64) -> &[tl_model::ProcessKey]; // empty slice when unknown
}
```

Walk rules:
- Open `<root.proc>` with `O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC`, read entries, keep names that are all digits.
- For each pid: `openat(proc_dirfd, "<pid>", O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC)`; then `openat(pid_dirfd, "fd", O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC)`. `ENOENT` or `ESRCH` (process gone) skips the pid silently. `EACCES` or `EPERM` adds `pid -> st_uid of the pid dir` to `restricted`.
- For each fd entry: `readlinkat(fd_dirfd, name)` into a reused 64-byte buffer. A target that starts with `socket:[` and ends with `]` with digits in between gives the inode. Anything else is ignored.
- Before inserting a pid's inodes, read its `start_ticks` (field 22 of `/proc/<pid>/stat`, parsed from the last `)`) with the reader that E05-A1 delivers in `crate::proc::pid_stat`, using the same `pid_dirfd`. Build `ProcessKey { start_ticks, boot_id: boot, pid }`. If the stat read fails the pid is skipped.
- Every fd is closed in the same walk. Nothing is cached between rebuilds.
- Kernel threads have empty fd dirs and cost one `getdents` each.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the fixture `tests/fixtures/sockets-basic/proc` where pid 100 has fds `3 -> socket:[5001]` and `4 -> /dev/null`, and pid 200 has `5 -> socket:[5001]` **When** `rebuild` runs **Then** `owners_of(5001)` holds the keys for 100 and 200 in `ProcessKey` order and `owners_of(4)` is empty.
- **Given** a pid directory that vanishes between `readdir` and `openat` **When** `rebuild` runs **Then** it returns `Ok` and that pid appears nowhere.
- **Given** a link target `socket:[12x]` or `socket:[]` **When** parsed **Then** it is ignored.
- **Given** the real system as uid 1000 **When** `rebuild` runs **Then** pid 1 is in `restricted` with uid 0 and the test's own TCP listener inode maps to the test's own pid.
- **Given** the real system **When** `rebuild` runs **Then** `elapsed_ns` is recorded; the test prints it, and the bead's close note records the value against the 20 ms target (U-23).

- `crates/tl-collect/src/net/socket_map.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-collect/src/net/mod.rs`: add `pub mod socket_map;`
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/sockets-basic/proc/{100,200}/{stat,fd/*}`: create (fd entries are committed symlinks with the targets above; stat lines are hand-written with field 22 = 5000 and 6000)

## Tests
- `net::socket_map::tests::fixture_shared_inode`: first criterion against the fixture.
- `net::socket_map::tests::parse_socket_link`: `socket:[5001]` gives 5001; `socket:[12x]`, `socket:[]`, `pipe:[1]`, `/dev/null` give none.
- `net::socket_map::tests::vanished_pid_is_skipped`: a fixture pid dir without `fd` behaves as gone.
- `tests/fixture_sockets.rs::real_socket_map_pid1_restricted` (`#[ignore]`): fourth criterion.
- `tests/fixture_sockets.rs::real_socket_map_timing` (`#[ignore]`): fifth criterion; asserts only that `elapsed_ns > 0`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: only a failure to open `<root.proc>` is returned; per-pid errors are absorbed as above.
- Validity: pids in `restricted` give `Restricted` downstream (E06-005, E06-006); never zero.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: target under 20 ms per rebuild on the owner machine (U-23, unverified). Reuse the maps and the link buffer; no `String` per fd.
- Privacy: never log fd targets or paths. Socket inodes only at `trace`.

## Notes
- `rustix::fs::{openat, readlinkat, Dir, fstat}`; `SysRoot` from E04-A1 (`root.proc`).
- Git stores the fixture symlinks as links; dangling targets such as `socket:[5001]` are fine.
- U-23 is settled by recording the measured time in the bead's close comment.

title: E06-005 Per-process TCP attribution
description:
## Context
Turns two TCP dumps plus the socket map into per-process send and receive rates for the process table's Network columns (`network`, `net_send_rate`, `net_recv_rate`). The column is labelled "Network (TCP, attributed)": UDP is not attributed, a socket shared by several processes counts fully for each of them, and the header total includes unattributed traffic. Sources: PROC-032, ADR-016 ("Per-process network"), ADR-008 (counter rules, rates from elapsed time, first sample is WarmingUp).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/net/attribution.rs` (add `pub mod attribution;` to `net/mod.rs`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct NetRate { pub rx_bps: f32, pub tx_bps: f32, pub shared: bool, pub validity: tl_model::Validity }

pub struct TcpAttribution {
    prev: rustc_hash::FxHashMap<u64, (u64, u64)>, // cookie -> (bytes_acked, bytes_received) at prev_ns
    prev_ns: Option<tl_model::TimeNs>,
    pub per_process: rustc_hash::FxHashMap<tl_model::ProcessKey, NetRate>,
    pub restricted_pids: rustc_hash::FxHashMap<u32, u32>, // copied from SocketMap::restricted
    pub total_rx_bps: f32, pub total_tx_bps: f32,             // every TCP socket in the dump
    pub unattributed_rx_bps: f32, pub unattributed_tx_bps: f32, // sockets with inode 0 or no owner
    pub validity: tl_model::Validity,                          // WarmingUp on the first update, else Valid
}
impl TcpAttribution {
    pub fn new() -> Self;
    /// `records` from SockDiag::dump_tcp taken at `t_ns` (CLOCK_BOOTTIME read just before the dump).
    pub fn update(&mut self, records: &[SockRecord], map: &SocketMap, t_ns: tl_model::TimeNs);
    /// Drops all baselines (suspend, epoch change, ResetBaselines). The next update is WarmingUp.
    pub fn reset(&mut self);
}
```

Rules for `update`:
- Only `Proto::Tcp` records with `tcp_info: Some(..)` count. Records are matched to the previous update by `cookie`.
- `dt_s = (t_ns - prev_ns) as f64 / 1e9`. Per socket: `tx = (acked - prev_acked) / dt_s`, `rx = (received - prev_received) / dt_s`, in bytes per second, using the rate and reset helpers in `crate::counters` (E04-A1). A counter that went backwards is a reset: that socket adds nothing this interval and gets a new baseline. A cookie with no previous entry adds nothing this interval.
- The first `update` after `new` or `reset` sets `validity = WarmingUp`, fills baselines and leaves `per_process` empty.
- A socket's rate is added in full to every key in `map.owners_of(inode)`; when there are 2 or more owners each gets `shared = true`. Sockets with `inode == 0` or no owners go to `unattributed_*`. All sockets go to `total_*`.
- Every key that owns at least one TCP socket gets an entry (0.0 rates when idle) with `Validity::Valid`. Keys without TCP sockets get no entry; the engine shows 0 for them when their fd dir was readable. `restricted_pids` lets the engine show `Restricted` for those pids instead (never zero).
- Baselines for cookies not seen in this dump are removed, so `prev` never grows past the live socket count.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** two updates 2 s apart where cookie 7 owned by key A goes from acked 1000 to 3000 and received 0 to 4000 **When** the second update runs **Then** A has `tx_bps == 1000.0`, `rx_bps == 2000.0`, `shared == false`, `Valid`.
- **Given** cookie 7 owned by A and B **When** rates are computed **Then** both have the full rate and `shared == true`, and `total_tx_bps` counts it once.
- **Given** the first update after `new` **When** it runs **Then** `validity == WarmingUp` and `per_process` is empty.
- **Given** cookie 7 whose `bytes_acked` drops from 3000 to 100 **When** updated **Then** it adds 0 for this interval, and the next update computes from 100.
- **Given** a TIME-WAIT socket with inode 0 and traffic **When** updated **Then** its rate is in `unattributed_*` and `total_*` and in no process entry.
- **Given** `reset()` **When** the next update runs **Then** it is `WarmingUp` again.
- **Given** a UDP record **When** updated **Then** it is ignored.

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/net/attribution.rs`: create with unit tests
- `crates/tl-collect/src/net/mod.rs`: add `pub mod attribution;`

## Tests
- `net::attribution::tests::rate_from_elapsed_time`: first criterion.
- `net::attribution::tests::shared_socket_counts_for_each`: second criterion.
- `net::attribution::tests::first_update_warming_up`: third criterion.
- `net::attribution::tests::counter_reset_no_spike`: fourth criterion.
- `net::attribution::tests::inode_zero_unattributed`: fifth criterion.
- `net::attribution::tests::reset_restarts_warmup`: sixth criterion.
- `net::attribution::tests::udp_ignored`: seventh criterion.
Build `SocketMap` values directly in the tests (its fields are public).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A (pure computation).
- Validity: `WarmingUp` (first update), `Valid`; `Restricted` is the engine's mapping of `restricted_pids`.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: no allocation after warm-up beyond map growth; clear and reuse `per_process`.
- Privacy: N/A

- Rates are f32 bytes per second; formatting into bits or bytes is `tl-model::units` in the UI.
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-collect`. title: E06-006 Connection records, owners and address formats
description:
## Context
Builds one connection record per socket for the Connections tab, with the address strings formatted once (ADR-003: "engine-formatted address strings, formatted once per cookie") and the owner resolved from the socket map. Rows keep identity by socket cookie. Sources: SYS-028, SYS-029, SYS-030, ADR-003 (`ConnectionsSnapshot`), canonical table (d) "Addresses".

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/net/connections.rs` (add `pub mod connections;` to `net/mod.rs`):

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum Owner {
    Kernel,                                                      // inode 0 or state TIME-WAIT (6): PID "-", Process "No owner (kernel)"
    Processes(smallvec::SmallVec<[tl_model::ProcessKey; 1]>),    // one or more owners
    Restricted { uid: u32 },                                     // no owner found and the socket uid's processes were unreadable: PID "?"
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct ConnRecord {
    pub cookie: u64,                // row identity
    pub sock: SockRecord,
    pub local: std::sync::Arc<str>,   // formatted local address with port
    pub foreign: std::sync::Arc<str>, // formatted foreign address with port
    pub interface: Option<std::sync::Arc<str>>, // name for sock.ifindex, None when 0 or unknown
    pub owner: Owner,
}

pub struct ConnectionTable {
    pub records: Vec<ConnRecord>,   // sorted by cookie
    pub counts: ConnCounts,
}
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ConnCounts { pub total: u32, pub tcp: u32, pub udp: u32, pub established: u32, pub listening: u32 }

impl ConnectionTable {
    pub fn new() -> Self;
    /// Rebuilds from one `dump_all`. Address strings of cookies seen last time with the same
    /// (src, sport, dst, dport, ifindex) are reused (Arc clone), not re-formatted.
    pub fn update(&mut self, socks: &[SockRecord], map: &SocketMap, ifnames: &IfNames);
}

/// ifindex -> interface name, read from /sys/class/net/<name>/ifindex.
pub struct IfNames(pub rustc_hash::FxHashMap<u32, std::sync::Arc<str>>);
impl IfNames { pub fn read(root: &SysRoot) -> Result<Self, CollectError>; }

pub fn format_endpoint(addr: std::net::IpAddr, port: u16, scope: Option<&str>, foreign_unbound: bool, out: &mut String);
```

Formatting rules (`format_endpoint`, table d, SYS-029):
- IPv4: `a.b.c.d:port`.
- IPv6: `[addr]:port`, with `addr` in the `std::net::Ipv6Addr` `Display` form (RFC 5952). An IPv4-mapped address (`::ffff:a.b.c.d`) is written in IPv4 form `a.b.c.d:port`.
- Link-local IPv6 (`fe80::/10`) gets `%scope` inside the brackets, where `scope` is the interface name for `ifindex` (`[fe80::1%enp5s0]:22`); when the name is unknown the decimal ifindex is used.
- Port 0 is written `*`: wildcard listeners give `0.0.0.0:*` and `[::]:*`.
- `foreign_unbound = true` (a TCP LISTEN socket, or a UDP socket with state 7 and an all-zero destination) writes `*:*` for the foreign side.

Owner rules:
- `inode == 0` or (`Tcp` and `state == 6`): `Owner::Kernel`.
- `map.owners_of(inode)` not empty: `Owner::Processes`.
- Otherwise, if any pid in `map.restricted` has uid `sock.uid`: `Owner::Restricted { uid }`.
- Otherwise (the owner exited between the dump and the walk): `Owner::Processes` with an empty list, which the UI shows as `-` (Missing).

Counts: `established` and `listening` count TCP rows only (state 1 and 10).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a TCP v4 listener on 0.0.0.0 port 22 **When** formatted **Then** local is `0.0.0.0:22` and foreign is `*:*`.
- **Given** a UDP v6 socket bound to [::] port 0 **When** formatted **Then** local is `[::]:*` and foreign is `*:*`.
- **Given** the v6 address `::ffff:192.168.1.5` port 443 **When** formatted **Then** the result is `192.168.1.5:443`.
- **Given** `fe80::1` port 22 on ifindex 3 named `enp5s0` **When** formatted **Then** the result is `[fe80::1%enp5s0]:22`; with an unknown ifindex 9 it is `[fe80::1%9]:22`.
- **Given** a TIME-WAIT record with inode 4242 **When** the owner is resolved **Then** it is `Owner::Kernel`.
- **Given** a socket with uid 0 and no owners while pid 1 (uid 0) is in `restricted` **When** resolved **Then** it is `Owner::Restricted { uid: 0 }`.
- **Given** two updates where cookie 9 keeps the same endpoints **When** the second runs **Then** `local` is the same `Arc` (pointer-equal) as before.
- **Given** 3 TCP ESTABLISHED, 1 TCP LISTEN and 2 UDP records **When** counted **Then** counts are total 6, tcp 4, udp 2, established 3, listening 1.

- `net::connections::tests::time_wait_owner_kernel`: criterion 5.

title: E11 tl-engine: action admission, tasks, deadlines, events
description: Epic E11 (engine-actions). Phases: P1 to P3. Estimated beads: 25. Scope, sources and file ownership: docs/plan/00-epics.md sections 1 and 2, key E11.

title: E11-A1 Action pipeline for processes
description:
## Context
Anchor E11-A1 "Action pipeline for processes": the `ActionGate` the reducer calls is implemented, installed through `EngineHooks::default()` (chain edit in `lib.rs::default_hooks`), spawns `run_action` tasks in the session's region, tracks in-flight actions and busy units, and answers `ActionFinished` with the source to refresh (`Processes` for process kinds). E29 (privileged routing) and E32 (rescue window End Task) depend on it. Sources: ADR-004 (actions region), ADR-005 (`ActionFinished` triggers a targeted refresh), ADR-006, E09-001 (`ActionGate`), E09-018 (`EngineHooks`, `HookCtx`), E11-001 to E11-008, B3 open item 8.

## Deliverable
1. `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/mod.rs` (part 3):

```rust
pub struct Gate { ctx: Arc<ActionCtx>, in_flight: FxHashMap<ActionId, InFlight>, busy_units: FxHashSet<UnitRef> }
struct InFlight { handle: TaskHandle<()>, kind: ActionKind /* cloned from the request; tl-model, R-265 */, units: SmallVec<[UnitRef; 1]>, manager: Option<Manager> }
impl ActionGate for Gate {
    fn submit(&mut self, cx: &Cx, req: ActionRequest, view: &AdmissionView<'_>) {
        match admit(&req, view, self.in_flight.len(), &self.busy_units) {
            Admission::Reject(r) => emit one { id, target: None, Rejected(r) } via events.try_send (dropped when full),
            Admission::Run { per_target } => { record the Unit targets in busy_units; let h = cx.spawn(|cx| run_action(cx, self.ctx.clone(), req, per_target)).expect("spawn"); self.in_flight.insert(id, ..) }
        }
    }
    fn finished(&mut self, id: ActionId) -> Option<SourceId> {
        remove; free its units; match kind { Signal | KillTree | Suspend | Resume | SetNice | SetSched | SetAffinity | SetIoPriority | FreezeGroup | ThawGroup | KillGroup | Dump => Some(Processes) (Unit-target freeze/thaw/kill also Processes), Unit* | UnitWriteRecovery | UnitRemoveRecovery => Some(SystemdSystem) or Some(SystemdUser) by the target's manager, Startup* => Some(Startup), SockDestroy => Some(Connections), OpenUri | ShowInFileManager | Launch => None }
    }
}
pub fn gate_factory(hook: HookCtx) -> Box<dyn ActionGate>;   // builds ActionCtx { events: hook.events_tx, msgs: hook.msgs_tx, ops: Arc::new(RealOps), boot_id: hook.boot_id, uid: rustix::process::getuid().as_raw(), config: hook.config, systemd_system: hook.shared.systemd_system, systemd_user: hook.shared.systemd_user, openers: None /* E11-016 */, helper: None /* E29-014 */ }
```

`HookCtx` and `SharedHandles` are E09-018's and E08-009's types (B3 open item 8): `HookCtx { events_tx, msgs_tx, boot_id, config: Arc<EngineConfig>, shared: SharedHandles }`, `SharedHandles { systemd_system: ManagerConnSlot, systemd_user: ManagerConnSlot }`.

2. `crates/tl-engine/src/lib.rs`: `pub mod actions;` (if E11-001 did not add it) and `default_hooks()` sets `action_gate: Some(Arc::new(actions::gate_factory))`.

3. `tests/lab_actions.rs`: `Engine`-level lab runs with `FakeOps` injected through a test-only `EngineHooks` whose `action_gate` closure builds the gate with the fake ops (add `pub fn gate_with_ops(hook: HookCtx, ops: Arc<dyn ActionOps>) -> Box<dyn ActionGate>` for this):

title: E11: cgroup freeze, thaw and kill on app.slice cgroups (actions/cgroup.rs)
description:
## Context
Freeze App, Thaw App and Kill App on app rows act on the app's cgroup under `app.slice` through `tl-ops::cgroup`: `open_validated(cg, uid)` checks the path prefix `user.slice/user-{uid}.slice/user@{uid}.service/app.slice/`, the `.scope` or `.service` suffix, the inode against `cgroup_id`, the owner uid, and that tasklens's own cgroup is not inside it; then writes `"1"` to `cgroup.freeze`, `"0"` to thaw, `"1"` to `cgroup.kill`; freeze completion polls `cgroup.events` for `frozen 1` every 50 ms for up to 2 s, else `OutcomeUnknown("freeze still in progress")`. `uid` comes from `getuid()`. Sources: ADR-006 (cgroup operations), PROC-064, R-092 (dispatch: `Cgroup` target for `app.slice`, `Unit` target otherwise is E11-012), E07-A2, E11-002.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/actions/cgroup.rs`:

```rust
pub async fn run_target(cx: &Cx, actx: &ActionCtx, kind: &ActionKind, cg: &CgroupRef) -> ActionState;
```

`spawn_blocking { dir = ops.cgroup_open_validated(cg, actx.uid)?; match kind { FreezeGroup => { ops.cgroup_write(&dir, "cgroup.freeze", "1")?; ops.cgroup_wait_frozen(&dir, 2 s) }, ThawGroup => ops.cgroup_write(&dir, "cgroup.freeze", "0"), KillGroup => ops.cgroup_write(&dir, "cgroup.kill", "1") } }` under `with_deadline(2 s)` for the write (the frozen wait has its own 2 s inside tl-ops and returns `NotFrozen` → `OutcomeUnknown("freeze still in progress")`). Mapping: `OpsError::CgroupInvalid(reason)` → `Rejected(Unsupported)` (bad path, suffix, inode or uid), `OpsError::OwnCgroup` → `Rejected(Protected)`, EACCES → `Failed(PermissionDenied)`, other errno → `Failed(Os)`. Any other `ActionKind` on a `Cgroup` target → `Rejected(Unsupported)`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake where `open_validated` succeeds and `wait_frozen` reports frozen **When** `FreezeGroup` runs **Then** `Succeeded` and the fake log is `[open, write(cgroup.freeze, "1"), wait_frozen]`.
- **Given** `wait_frozen` reports `NotFrozen` **When** run **Then** `OutcomeUnknown("freeze still in progress")`.
- **Given** `open_validated` returns `CgroupInvalid` **When** run **Then** `Rejected(Unsupported)` and no write happened.
- **Given** `open_validated` returns `OwnCgroup` **When** run **Then** `Rejected(Protected)`.
- **Given** `KillGroup` **When** run **Then** the fake saw `write(cgroup.kill, "1")`.
- **Given** `Signal(Term)` on a `Cgroup` target **When** run **Then** `Rejected(Unsupported)`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/cgroup.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/mod.rs`: `pub mod cgroup;`

## Tests
- `lab_actions.rs` (E11-017 adds; or here if E11-017 is later): `cgroup_freeze_waits_frozen`, `cgroup_freeze_not_frozen_unknown`, `cgroup_invalid_rejected`, `cgroup_own_protected`, `cgroup_kill_write`, `cgroup_wrong_kind_unsupported`.
- `real_cgroup.rs` (E11-010).

- Validity: N/A

- Privacy: logs the cgroup's last path component only.

It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E11: unit start, stop, restart, reload, reset-failed with the JobRemoved wait (actions/unit.rs part 1)
description:
## Context
Service actions Start, Stop, Restart, Reload and Reset failed run on the systemd manager that owns the unit, over the connection the `SystemdSystem` or `SystemdUser` worker holds (`ManagerConnSlot`), with the `ALLOW_INTERACTIVE_AUTHORIZATION` flag so polkit can prompt for system units. The `JobRemoved` match is added before the method call so a fast job cannot be missed; the returned job path is matched; result `done` is success, any other result word is `Failed(UnitJob(result))`. Jobs have no client-side timeout (ADR-005, SYS-005); the method call itself has one. A bus loss before `JobRemoved` is `OutcomeUnknown`. The same arm serves "Restart Plasma Shell" and "Restart unit <name>" from the process table (PROC-072). Sources: ADR-006 (systemd units, deadlines), ADR-005 (no client timeout for jobs), SYS-005, SYS-006, PROC-072, R-117, U-39, E08-009 (`DbusConn`, `error_name`, `ManagerConnSlot`), E14-001, E11-002.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/actions/unit.rs` (part 1):

```rust
pub const MANAGER_BUS: &str = "org.freedesktop.systemd1";
pub const MANAGER_PATH: &str = "/org/freedesktop/systemd1";
pub const MANAGER_IFACE: &str = "org.freedesktop.systemd1.Manager";
pub const JOB_MODE: &str = "replace";
pub const CALL_TIMEOUT_USER: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);
pub const CALL_TIMEOUT_SYSTEM: Duration = Duration::from_secs(120);   // may show a polkit prompt

/// The manager calls this module makes, behind a trait so tests fake the bus. `ZbusUnitBus` wraps an `Arc<zbus::Connection>` from the slot.
pub trait UnitBus: Send + Sync {
    fn call<'a>(&'a self, cx: &'a Cx, method: &'a str, args: &'a [zvariant::Value<'static>], timeout: Duration) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<zvariant::OwnedValue, UnitBusError>> + Send + 'a>>;   // sets ALLOW_INTERACTIVE_AUTHORIZATION on every call
    fn job_removed<'a>(&'a self, cx: &'a Cx) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<JobStream, UnitBusError>> + Send + 'a>>;   // adds the match rule and returns the stream; call BEFORE the method
    fn get_property<'a>(&'a self, cx: &'a Cx, unit_path: &'a str, iface: &'a str, name: &'a str) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<zvariant::OwnedValue, UnitBusError>> + Send + 'a>>;   // 2 s
}
pub struct JobStream { /* zbus SignalStream of JobRemoved(u id, o job, s unit, s result) */ }
impl JobStream { pub async fn next_result(&mut self, cx: &Cx, job: &str) -> Result<Option<Arc<str>>, UnitBusError>; }   // Ok(None) after each 500 ms wake with no match (callers checkpoint and loop); Ok(Some(result)) when `job` matches
pub enum UnitBusError { NoConnection, Timeout, Closed, Call { name: Arc<str>, message: Arc<str> } }

pub fn bus_for(actx: &ActionCtx, manager: Manager) -> Option<Arc<dyn UnitBus>>;   // ZbusUnitBus over systemd_system.get() / systemd_user.get(); tests swap it through ActionCtx.unit_bus_override: Option<Arc<dyn Fn(Manager) -> Option<Arc<dyn UnitBus>>>> (add that field)
pub async fn run_target(cx: &Cx, actx: &ActionCtx, kind: &ActionKind, unit: &UnitRef) -> ActionState;   // dispatch by kind; this bead: the five job kinds; E11-012 and E11-013 add theirs
async fn job_call(cx: &Cx, bus: &dyn UnitBus, method: &str, unit: &UnitRef, manager: Manager) -> ActionState;
pub fn map_bus_error(e: &UnitBusError, context: &str) -> ActionState;
```

`run_target`: `UnitStart` → `job_call("StartUnit")`; `UnitStop` → `"StopUnit"`; `UnitRestart` → `"RestartUnit"`; `UnitReload` → `"ReloadUnit"`; `UnitResetFailed` → `bus.call("ResetFailedUnit", [name], timeout)` → `Succeeded` (no job). No bus (`bus_for` is `None`) → `Failed(Internal("manager not connected"))`.

`job_call`: `let mut jobs = bus.job_removed(cx).await?;` then `bus.call(method, [name, JOB_MODE], timeout)` where `timeout` is `CALL_TIMEOUT_USER` or `CALL_TIMEOUT_SYSTEM` by manager; the reply is the job object path; then loop `jobs.next_result(cx, &job)` with `cx.checkpoint()` between wakes until `Some(result)`: `"done"` → `Succeeded`; `"failed" | "timeout" | "canceled" | "dependency" | "skipped" | "invalid"` or any other word → `Failed(UnitJob { result, error_name: None })` (R-170 item 9). `Closed` or a `Timeout` while waiting for the signal → `OutcomeUnknown("connection lost before the job ended")`.

`map_bus_error` by D-Bus error name (`dbus::error_name`): `org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.AccessDenied` → `Failed(NotAuthorized)` (UI text "<failure text>: not authorized"; R-148 item 3); `org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.InteractiveAuthorizationRequired` → `Failed(Internal("no authentication agent is running"))`; `org.freedesktop.systemd1.NoSuchUnit` → `Rejected(Unsupported)`; `org.freedesktop.systemd1.UnitMasked` → `Failed(UnitJob { result: "masked", error_name: Some("org.freedesktop.systemd1.UnitMasked") })`; `org.freedesktop.systemd1.JobTypeNotApplicable` → `Rejected(Unsupported)`; `Timeout` on the method call → `OutcomeUnknown("timed out")`; `NoConnection` → `Failed(Internal("manager not connected"))`; any other name → `Failed(UnitJob { result: "failed", error_name: Some(name) })`, so the UI can show the D-Bus error name (R-170 item 9). A dismissed prompt and a denial cannot be told apart on this path (R-117, U-39): both are `AccessDenied` until phase 0 records otherwise.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake bus whose `StartUnit` returns `/org/freedesktop/systemd1/job/7` and whose stream yields `JobRemoved(.., "/org/freedesktop/systemd1/job/7", .., "done")` **When** `UnitStart` runs **Then** the fake log is `[job_removed, call(StartUnit, [name, "replace"])]` in that order and the state is `Succeeded`.
- **Given** the stream first yields a `JobRemoved` for another job path, then `"failed"` for ours **When** run **Then** `Failed(UnitJob { result: "failed", error_name: None })` and the foreign job was ignored.
- **Given** `JobRemoved` for our job arrives before the method reply is processed (the fake queues the signal first) **When** run **Then** still `Succeeded` (the match was added before the call).
- **Given** the stream closes before any match **When** run **Then** `OutcomeUnknown("connection lost before the job ended")`.
- **Given** `UnitResetFailed` **When** run **Then** `call(ResetFailedUnit, [name])` and `Succeeded` with no `job_removed` call.
- **Given** the call returns `AccessDenied` **When** run **Then** `Failed(NotAuthorized)`; `NoSuchUnit` → `Rejected(Unsupported)`; `UnitMasked` → `Failed(UnitJob { result: "masked", error_name: Some("org.freedesktop.systemd1.UnitMasked") })`; an unknown name `org.example.Odd` → `Failed(UnitJob { result: "failed", error_name: Some("org.example.Odd") })`.
- **Given** `bus_for` returns `None` **When** run **Then** `Failed(Internal("manager not connected"))` and no call.
- **Given** a `System` unit **When** `StartUnit` is called **Then** the call timeout passed is 120 s; for a `User` unit 10 s.
- **Given** 300 s of virtual time with no `JobRemoved` **When** `UnitStart` waits **Then** it is still waiting (no client timeout) and a `Cx` cancel ends it within 500 ms with no event after.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/unit.rs`: create (part 1)
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/mod.rs`: `pub mod unit;`, the `Unit` dispatch arm, the `unit_bus_override` test field

## Tests
- `lab_actions.rs` (E11-017): `unit_start_match_before_call`, `unit_job_failed_word`, `unit_job_removed_before_reply`, `unit_bus_closed_is_outcome_unknown`, `unit_reset_failed_no_job`, `unit_error_name_mapping`, `unit_no_connection`, `unit_call_timeout_by_manager`, `unit_job_wait_has_no_client_timeout`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: as mapped above; the UI toasts ("Service started", "Failed to start service: <result>", "Service action finished.") come from `ActionTracker` by state and kind.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one match rule plus one method call per action; the stream is dropped when the action ends.
- Privacy: log the unit name at debug only; never log method arguments beyond the unit name.
- Security: `ALLOW_INTERACTIVE_AUTHORIZATION` lets polkit prompt; tasklens never escalates by itself (ADR-006).

## Notes
Depends on E11-002, E08-009, E14-A1 (`ManagerConnSlot` filled by the systemd workers). zbus: `Proxy::call_method` with `MessageFlags::ALLOW_INTERACTIVE_AUTHORIZATION` through `zbus::message::Builder` (or `Proxy::builder().call_with_flags`), `MatchRule::builder().msg_type(Signal).interface(MANAGER_IFACE).member("JobRemoved")`, `MessageStream::for_match_rule`. Every bus future goes through `DbusConn::call` (timeout then checkpoint); the job wait uses `next_signal` with 500 ms wakes. Phase P2. Label `security`. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

Commits 451e246, 1d93945, b057733. 13 in-file tests incl. two p2p fake-manager tests.

title: E11: unit freeze, thaw and kill through the manager
description:
## Context
Freeze App, Thaw App and Kill App on a unit row whose cgroup is not under `app.slice` (user units in `session.slice` or `background.slice`, and system units) go through the owning manager instead of the cgroup files: `FreezeUnit(name)`, `ThawUnit(name)` and `KillUnit(name, "all", SIGKILL)` with `ALLOW_INTERACTIVE_AUTHORIZATION`. Freeze completion is the unit's `FreezerState` property reading `frozen` within 2 s. The UI picks the target type (R-092): `ActionTarget::Cgroup` for `app.slice`, `ActionTarget::Unit` otherwise. Sources: ADR-006 ("Units outside `app.slice`"), R-092, PROC-064, E11-009, E11-011.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/unit.rs`:

```rust
pub const FREEZE_POLL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(50);
pub const FREEZE_WAIT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);
pub const UNIT_IFACE: &str = "org.freedesktop.systemd1.Unit";
async fn freeze_thaw_kill(cx: &Cx, bus: &dyn UnitBus, kind: &ActionKind, unit: &UnitRef) -> ActionState;
fn unit_object_path(name: &str) -> String;   // "/org/freedesktop/systemd1/unit/" + systemd D-Bus label escaping (bytes outside [A-Za-z0-9] become _XX lowercase hex; a leading digit is also escaped)
```

`run_target` arms: `FreezeGroup` → `bus.call("FreezeUnit", [name], t)`, then poll `get_property(unit_object_path(name), UNIT_IFACE, "FreezerState")` every 50 ms for up to 2 s: `"frozen"` → `Succeeded`; still `"freezing"` or `"running"` at 2 s → `OutcomeUnknown("freeze still in progress")`. `ThawGroup` → `"ThawUnit"` → `Succeeded`. `KillGroup` → `bus.call("KillUnit", [name, "all", 9i32], t)` → `Succeeded`. `t` is `CALL_TIMEOUT_USER` (2 s is the action deadline from `deadline()`, so the call timeout is the smaller of the two) or `CALL_TIMEOUT_SYSTEM`. Errors through `map_bus_error`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake bus whose `FreezerState` reads `freezing`, `freezing`, `frozen` **When** `FreezeGroup` on a `Unit` target runs **Then** the fake log is `[call(FreezeUnit, [name]), get_property ×3]` and the state is `Succeeded` after about 100 ms of virtual time.
- **Given** `FreezerState` stays `freezing` **When** 2 s pass **Then** `OutcomeUnknown("freeze still in progress")` and about 40 property reads happened.
- **Given** `KillGroup` **When** run **Then** `call(KillUnit, [name, "all", 9])` and `Succeeded`.
- **Given** `FreezeUnit` returns `AccessDenied` on a `System` unit **When** run **Then** `Failed(PermissionDenied)` and no property read.
- **Given** `unit_object_path("plasma-plasmashell.service")` **When** computed **Then** `/org/freedesktop/systemd1/unit/plasma_2dplasmashell_2eservice`; `"1foo.service"` → `/org/freedesktop/systemd1/unit/_31foo_2eservice`.
- **Given** `Signal(Term)` on a `Unit` target **When** run **Then** `Rejected(Unsupported)`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/unit.rs`: extend

title: E11: unit enable, disable, mask, unmask and Reload
description:
## Context
Startup type changes for services (the "Startup type >" submenu and the Properties General combo): Enabled, Disabled and Masked, plus Unmask when leaving Masked. The calls are `EnableUnitFiles([name], false, true)`, `DisableUnitFiles([name], false)`, `MaskUnitFiles([name], false, true)` and `UnmaskUnitFiles([name], false)`, each followed by `Manager.Reload()` as systemctl does. Enable or Disable on a masked unit unmasks first. System units may prompt twice (unit-files and reload-daemon polkit actions); that is accepted (SYS-007). The same functions serve startup entries that are user units (E11-014, E11-015). Sources: ADR-006 (systemd units: enable/disable + Reload, 10 s, 120 s with prompt), SYS-007, SYS-011, SYS-022, E11-011.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/unit.rs`:

```rust
pub async fn set_unit_file_state(cx: &Cx, bus: &dyn UnitBus, unit: &UnitRef, kind: &ActionKind) -> ActionState;   // UnitEnable | UnitDisable | UnitMask | UnitUnmask
pub async fn reload(cx: &Cx, bus: &dyn UnitBus, manager: Manager) -> Result<(), UnitBusError>;   // Manager.Reload(), same timeout rule
async fn unit_file_state(cx: &Cx, bus: &dyn UnitBus, name: &str) -> Result<Arc<str>, UnitBusError>;   // Manager.GetUnitFileState(name)
```

`set_unit_file_state`: for `UnitEnable` and `UnitDisable`, read `unit_file_state`; `"masked"` or `"masked-runtime"` → `UnmaskUnitFiles([name], false)` first, inside the same action with one summary event (R-170 item 10). Then: `UnitEnable` → `EnableUnitFiles([name], false /*runtime*/, true /*force*/)` (reply `(b carries_install_info, a(sss) changes)`; `false` is logged at debug and still `Succeeded`, systemctl does the same); `UnitDisable` → `DisableUnitFiles([name], false)`; `UnitMask` → `MaskUnitFiles([name], false, true)`; `UnitUnmask` → `UnmaskUnitFiles([name], false)`. Then `reload`. A `reload` error after a successful change → `OutcomeUnknown("changed, but the manager reload failed")`. Call timeouts by manager (10 s user, 120 s system); errors through `map_bus_error`. `run_target` gets the four arms.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `GetUnitFileState` returns `disabled` **When** `UnitEnable` runs **Then** the fake log is `[GetUnitFileState, EnableUnitFiles([name], false, true), Reload]` and `Succeeded`.
- **Given** `GetUnitFileState` returns `masked` **When** `UnitEnable` runs **Then** `UnmaskUnitFiles([name], false)` is called before `EnableUnitFiles`.
- **Given** `UnitMask` **When** run **Then** `[MaskUnitFiles([name], false, true), Reload]` with no state read.
- **Given** `UnitUnmask` **When** run **Then** `[UnmaskUnitFiles([name], false), Reload]`.
- **Given** `Reload` returns `AccessDenied` after a successful `DisableUnitFiles` **When** run **Then** `OutcomeUnknown("changed, but the manager reload failed")`.
- **Given** `EnableUnitFiles` returns `AccessDenied` **When** run **Then** `Failed(NotAuthorized)` (E11-011's `map_bus_error`, R-148 item 3) and no `Reload`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/unit.rs`: extend

## Tests
- `lab_actions.rs` (E11-017): `unit_enable_then_reload`, `unit_enable_unmasks_first`, `unit_mask_calls`, `unit_unmask_calls`, `unit_reload_failure_is_unknown`, `unit_enable_denied_no_reload`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: as E11-011; the UI toasts are "Startup type changed" and "Failed to change startup type" (SYS-007), "Changes applied" (SYS-011).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: at most four calls per action.
- Privacy: unit name at debug only.

## Notes
Depends on E11-011. The method signatures: `EnableUnitFiles(as files, b runtime, b force) → (b, a(sss))`, `DisableUnitFiles(as, b) → a(sss)`, `MaskUnitFiles(as, b runtime, b force) → a(sss)`, `UnmaskUnitFiles(as, b) → a(sss)`, `GetUnitFileState(s) → s`, `Reload()`. ADR-006 names these forms; SYS-007's `*WithFlags` variants are not used (ADR precedence). Phase P2. Label `security`. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E11: startup enable and disable (actions/startup.rs part 1)
description:
## Context
Startup Apps "Enable" and "Disable" (`StartupEnable`, `StartupDisable`) on an `ActionTarget::Startup(StartupRef { source, id })`. The file operations live in `tl-ops::fs` (E07-011) and run on the blocking pool under the 2 s deadline; systemd user units go over D-Bus through E11-013's functions. A system XDG entry is disabled by writing a user override and enabled by removing it; a user XDG entry toggles `Hidden` in place; a Plasma script toggles its executable bit. Sources: SYS-022, SYS-019 (lookup precedence), ADR-006 (2 s startup write deadline), ADR-016 (startup row), E07-011 (`StartupRoots`, functions), E03-052 (`StartupRef`, `StartupSource`), E11-002, E11-013.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/actions/startup.rs` (part 1):

```rust
pub struct StartupPaths { pub roots: tl_ops::fs::StartupRoots, pub system_autostart_dirs: Vec<PathBuf> }   // roots from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME (default $HOME/.config); system dirs = each $XDG_CONFIG_DIRS entry (default /etc/xdg) + "/autostart", in precedence order
impl StartupPaths { pub fn from_env() -> Self; }
pub fn user_file(paths: &StartupPaths, r: &StartupRef) -> Option<PathBuf>;   // AutostartUser → roots.autostart/<id>; UserUnit → roots.systemd_user/<id>; PlasmaEnv → roots.plasma_env/<id>; PlasmaShutdown → roots.plasma_shutdown/<id>; AutostartSystem → None
pub fn system_file(paths: &StartupPaths, id: &str) -> Option<PathBuf>;        // first existing <dir>/<id> over system_autostart_dirs
pub fn valid_id(id: &str) -> bool;   // non-empty, no '/', not "." or "..", no NUL; autostart ids end in ".desktop", unit ids in a known unit suffix
pub async fn run_target(cx: &Cx, actx: &ActionCtx, kind: &ActionKind, r: &StartupRef) -> ActionState;   // this bead: StartupEnable, StartupDisable; E11-015 adds StartupRunNow and StartupDelete
```

`ActionOps` gains `startup_disable_system(system_file, roots) -> OpsResult<PathBuf>`, `startup_enable_override(user_file, roots) -> OpsResult<EnableOutcome>`, `startup_set_hidden(user_file, hidden, roots) -> OpsResult`, `startup_script_set_enabled(script, enabled, roots) -> OpsResult` (RealOps → `tl_ops::fs::*`). `ActionCtx` gets `startup_paths: StartupPaths` (built once by `gate_factory`; tests point it at a temp directory).

`run_target`, `!valid_id(&r.id)` → `Rejected(Unsupported)` before any I/O. Then by `r.source`:
- `AutostartUser`: `spawn_blocking { ops.startup_set_hidden(user_file, hidden = (kind == StartupDisable), roots) }` under 2 s.
- `AutostartSystem`, `StartupDisable`: `system_file(id)` → `None` → `Failed(Internal("system entry not found"))`; else `ops.startup_disable_system(path, roots)`; `InvalidInput("user entry already exists")` → fall through to `startup_set_hidden(roots.autostart/<id>, true)`.
- `AutostartSystem`, `StartupEnable`: the override `roots.autostart/<id>` exists → `ops.startup_enable_override(it, roots)` → `Succeeded` for both outcomes; it does not exist → `Succeeded` (already enabled, nothing to do).
- `UserUnit`: `unit::set_unit_file_state(cx, bus_for(User), UnitRef { manager: User, name: id }, UnitEnable | UnitDisable)` (E11-013), deadline 10 s; no user bus → `Failed(Internal("manager not connected"))`.
- `PlasmaEnv`, `PlasmaShutdown`: `ops.startup_script_set_enabled(path, enabled = (kind == StartupEnable), roots)`.
Results: `Ok` → `Succeeded`; `OpsError` → `map_ops_error` (so `NotOwner` → `Rejected(NotOwner)`, which the UI shows as "Failed to update startup entry"); `Elapsed` → `OutcomeUnknown("timed out")`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `AutostartUser` id `foo.desktop` **When** `StartupDisable` runs **Then** the fake saw `set_hidden(<autostart>/foo.desktop, true)` and the state is `Succeeded`.
- **Given** `AutostartSystem` id `bar.desktop` with `/etc/xdg/autostart/bar.desktop` present (temp dir) **When** `StartupDisable` runs **Then** `disable_system(<that path>, roots)` was called.
- **Given** the fake returns `InvalidInput("user entry already exists")` **When** `StartupDisable` on a system entry runs **Then** a second call `set_hidden(<autostart>/bar.desktop, true)` follows and the state is `Succeeded`.
- **Given** `AutostartSystem` and an existing override **When** `StartupEnable` runs **Then** `enable_override(<autostart>/bar.desktop)`; without an override → `Succeeded` and no call.
- **Given** `UserUnit` id `foo.service` **When** `StartupEnable` runs **Then** the unit fake saw `EnableUnitFiles(["foo.service"], false, true)` then `Reload`.
- **Given** `PlasmaEnv` id `x.sh` **When** `StartupDisable` runs **Then** `script_set_enabled(<plasma_env>/x.sh, false)`.
- **Given** id `../evil.desktop` or `a/b.desktop` **When** any kind runs **Then** `Rejected(Unsupported)` and no call (security regression).
- **Given** the fake returns `NotOwner` **When** run **Then** `Rejected(NotOwner)`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/startup.rs`: create (part 1)
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/mod.rs`: `pub mod startup;`, the `Startup` dispatch arm, `ActionOps` methods, `ActionCtx.startup_paths`

## Tests
- `lab_actions.rs` (E11-017): `startup_user_entry_toggle`, `startup_system_disable_writes_override`, `startup_system_disable_falls_back_to_existing_user_entry`, `startup_system_enable_override`, `startup_user_unit_enable`, `startup_script_toggle`, `startup_bad_id_rejected`, `startup_not_owner`.
- `startup.rs::tests::paths_from_env_defaults` (XDG defaults), `startup.rs::tests::valid_id_table`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: as above; UI toasts "Startup entry enabled." / "Startup entry disabled." / "Failed to update startup entry" (SYS-022).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one or two blocking calls per entry.
- Privacy: log the entry id at debug only; never file contents (ADR-015).
- Security: ids are validated before any path is built; `tl-ops` confines paths to the roots a second time.

## Notes
Depends on E11-002, E11-013, E07-A3. Takes effect at next login; running programs are not stopped (SYS-022). Phase P2. Label `security`. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E11: startup Run now and Delete entry
description:
## Context
Startup Apps "Run now" and "Delete entry". Run now starts the entry whatever its status through the shared launcher (E14-A3): a desktop entry goes as `LaunchWhat::DesktopEntry(id)` (the launcher prefers the generated `app-<id>@autostart.service` and reports `AlreadyRunning` when it is active), a user unit as `LaunchWhat::Unit`, a Plasma script as `LaunchWhat::Command` with the shell-quoted path, built from `tl_ops::launch::script_argv` (R-148 item 5). Delete unlinks a user file; a user unit is disabled first, then its file is unlinked, then the manager reloads. System XDG entries and package-owned units cannot be deleted (the UI disables the item; the engine refuses too). Sources: SYS-023, SYS-024, R-134, E14-A3 (`launch`, `LaunchOutcome`), E07-011 (`delete_startup_file`), E07-014 (`script_argv`), E11-013, E11-014, B3 open item 10.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/startup.rs`:

```rust
pub fn launch_spec(paths: &StartupPaths, r: &StartupRef) -> Result<LaunchSpec, ActionState>;
// AutostartUser | AutostartSystem → LaunchWhat::DesktopEntry(id without the ".desktop" suffix), cwd None
// UserUnit → LaunchWhat::Unit(UnitRef { manager: User, name: id })
// PlasmaEnv | PlasmaShutdown → LaunchWhat::Command(shell-quoted "/bin/sh '<abs path>'") with cwd = $HOME; the path is user_file(); single quotes in the path are escaped as '\''
async fn run_now(cx: &Cx, actx: &ActionCtx, r: &StartupRef) -> ActionState;
async fn delete(cx: &Cx, actx: &ActionCtx, r: &StartupRef) -> ActionState;
```

`run_now`: `actx.openers` is `None` → `Rejected(Unsupported)`; else `openers.launch(cx, &spec)` with no action deadline (`deadline()` gives `None`; the launcher bounds its own calls): `Ok(Launched)` → `Succeeded`; `Ok(AlreadyRunning)` → `Rejected(AlreadyRunning)` (R-148 item 4; the UI shows the Info toast "Already running"; `Busy` means the queue is full); `Err(e)` → `Failed(e)`.

`delete`: `AutostartSystem` → `Rejected(Unsupported)`; `AutostartUser` → `spawn_blocking { ops.startup_delete_file(roots.autostart/<id>, roots) }` under 2 s; `PlasmaEnv | PlasmaShutdown` → same on that root; `UserUnit` → `unit::set_unit_file_state(.., UnitDisable)` without its `Reload` (add a `reload: bool` parameter to E11-013's function), then `ops.startup_delete_file(roots.systemd_user/<id>, roots)`, then `unit::reload(User)`; a delete `ENOENT` → `Succeeded` (already gone); other `OpsError` → `map_ops_error`. `ActionOps` gains `startup_delete_file(path, roots) -> OpsResult`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `AutostartUser` id `foo.desktop` **When** `StartupRunNow` runs **Then** the fake openers saw `launch(DesktopEntry("foo"))` and the state is `Succeeded`.
- **Given** the fake launcher returns `AlreadyRunning` **When** run **Then** `Rejected(AlreadyRunning)`.
- **Given** `UserUnit` id `bar.service` **When** `StartupRunNow` runs **Then** `launch(Unit(User, "bar.service"))`.
- **Given** `PlasmaEnv` id `it's.sh` **When** `launch_spec` runs **Then** `Command("/bin/sh '<plasma_env>/it'\''s.sh'")` with `cwd = $HOME`.
- **Given** `openers` is `None` **When** `StartupRunNow` runs **Then** `Rejected(Unsupported)`.
- **Given** `AutostartUser` **When** `StartupDelete` runs **Then** `delete_file(<autostart>/foo.desktop)` and `Succeeded`; `ENOENT` → `Succeeded`.
- **Given** `UserUnit` **When** `StartupDelete` runs **Then** the order is `DisableUnitFiles`, `delete_file(<systemd_user>/bar.service)`, `Reload`.
- **Given** `AutostartSystem` **When** `StartupDelete` runs **Then** `Rejected(Unsupported)` and no call.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/startup.rs`: extend
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/unit.rs`: `reload: bool` parameter on `set_unit_file_state`

## Tests
- `lab_actions.rs` (E11-017): `startup_run_now_desktop_entry`, `startup_run_now_already_running`, `startup_run_now_unit`, `startup_run_now_without_openers`, `startup_delete_user_file`, `startup_delete_unit_order`, `startup_delete_system_unsupported`.
- `startup.rs::tests::launch_spec_table` (including the quoting case).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: UI toasts "Startup entry launched." / "Failed to launch startup entry" / "Already running" / "Startup entry deleted." / "Failed to delete startup entry" (SYS-023, SYS-024).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one launch or at most three calls per delete.
- Privacy: never log the command text or script path above debug.
- Security: Plasma scripts run only through `/bin/sh <path>` with a confined path; deletes go through `tl-ops` path confinement.

## Notes
Depends on E11-014, E11-013, E14-A3 (through the `Openers` trait; the `RealOpeners` impl is E11-016). Phase P2. Label `security`. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E11: targetless kinds OpenUri, ShowInFileManager, Launch and RealOpeners
description:
## Context
The three targetless kinds `OpenUri`, `ShowInFileManager` and `Launch` run one job each in the action task and report only the summary event (there are no targets). They call E14's `opener.rs` and `launcher.rs` on the user manager's session connection through the `Openers` trait, so the toasts for "Open file location", "Open in VirusTotal", links, the Run dialog and "Run as administrator" all come through the normal action path. Sources: R-134, ADR-005 (targetless kinds, 2 s, 120 s when `as_admin`), PROC-073, PROC-074, PROC-095, R-117, E14-020, E14-A3, E11-002.

## Deliverable
1. `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/targetless.rs`:

```rust
pub async fn run(cx: &Cx, actx: &ActionCtx, kind: &ActionKind, privileged: bool) -> ActionState;
```

`actx.openers` is `None` → `Rejected(Unsupported)`. Else under `with_deadline(deadline(kind, None, privileged))`: `OpenUri(u)` → `openers.open_uri(cx, &u)`; `ShowInFileManager { path, properties }` → `openers.show_in_file_manager(cx, &path, properties)`; `Launch(spec)` → `openers.launch(cx, &spec)` → `Launched` → `Succeeded`, `AlreadyRunning` → `Rejected(AlreadyRunning)` (R-148 item 4). `Ok(())` → `Succeeded`; `Err(e)` → `Failed(e)`; `Elapsed` → `OutcomeUnknown("timed out")`. `run_action` (E11-002) calls this for `targetless(kind)` and emits `Started` then the one summary event.

2. `pub struct RealOpeners { pub session: ManagerConnSlot }` implementing `Openers` by calling `crate::opener::open_uri(cx, self.session.get(), target)`, `crate::opener::show_in_file_manager(cx, self.session.get(), path, properties)` and `crate::launcher::launch(cx, self.session.get(), spec)`; `gate_factory` sets `openers: Some(Arc::new(RealOpeners { session: hook.shared.systemd_user.clone() }))`. `LaunchOutcome` becomes `pub use crate::launcher::LaunchOutcome` (E11-002's local enum is removed).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `OpenUri("https://example.org")` with fake openers **When** run **Then** the fake saw `open_uri("https://example.org")`, the events are `Started` then summary `Succeeded`, and no per-target event exists.
- **Given** `ShowInFileManager { path: "/usr/bin/foo", properties: true }` **When** run **Then** `show_in_file_manager("/usr/bin/foo", true)`.
- **Given** `Launch(Command("kate"), as_admin = false)` and a fake that blocks 3 s **When** run **Then** `OutcomeUnknown("timed out")` after 2 s; with `as_admin = true` the same fake blocking 3 s → `Succeeded` (the deadline is 120 s).
- **Given** the fake returns `Err(Internal("not an absolute path"))` **When** run **Then** `Failed(Internal(..))`.
- **Given** the fake launcher returns `AlreadyRunning` **When** run **Then** `Rejected(AlreadyRunning)`.
- **Given** `openers` is `None` **When** any of the three runs **Then** `Rejected(Unsupported)`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/targetless.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/mod.rs`: `pub mod targetless;`, `RealOpeners`, the `gate_factory` change, the `LaunchOutcome` re-export

## Tests
- `lab_actions.rs` (E11-017): `targetless_open_uri`, `targetless_show_in_file_manager`, `targetless_launch_deadline_and_admin`, `targetless_error_passthrough`, `targetless_already_running`, `targetless_without_openers`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the openers' `ActionError`s pass through, including `NotAuthorized` (pkexec 127), `AuthCancelled` (pkexec 126) and `Unsupported` (no `FileManager1` owner, invalid command text) (R-148 item 3). Their UI texts are R-240: "Administrator access was refused.", "Authentication was cancelled.", "Not supported on this system.". A `pkexec` launch counts as `Succeeded` when the child still runs 2 s after the prompt closed (R-148 item 5); UI texts come from the specs ("Opening file location", "Command launched", "Failed to run command", "Authentication cancelled", "Command contains invalid text.").
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one job per action.
- Privacy: never log URIs, paths or command text above debug (ADR-015).
- Security: the administrator path is the launcher's `pkexec env … /bin/sh -c` form only; `privileged` on these kinds is ignored (no helper route).

## Notes
Depends on E11-002, E14-A3 (`launcher.rs`, `opener.rs`, which are `pub(crate)` in the same crate). Phase P2. Label `security`. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
close_reason: Done in 5c39fc6 and 0ec63a5. The gate_factory openers line moves to i3o.1 (leader told the i3o.1 implementer to set openers: Some(RealOpeners { session: hook.shared.systemd_user.clone() })).

title: E11: lab_actions.rs part 2: unit, startup, opener and cgroup cases
description:
## Context
Second part of `tests/lab_actions.rs`: the fakes and cases for the P2 modules (unit, startup, targetless, cgroup, the P2 process kinds), so every bead from E11-006 and E11-009 to E11-016 has its named tests in one file with one harness. Sources: ADR-013, E11-006, E11-009, E11-011 to E11-016.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_actions.rs`:

```rust
struct FakeUnitBus { calls: Mutex<Vec<FakeBusCall>>, replies: Mutex<VecDeque<Result<OwnedValue, UnitBusError>>>, signals: Mutex<VecDeque<JobRemovedSignal>>, properties: Mutex<VecDeque<Arc<str>>>, close_stream: bool }
struct FakeOpeners { calls: Mutex<Vec<OpenerCall>>, script: Mutex<VecDeque<OpenerStep>> }   // OpenerStep { Ok, AlreadyRunning, Err(ActionError), Block(Duration) }
fn harness_p2(tmp: &TempDir) -> (LabRuntime, Arc<ActionCtx>, Arc<FakeOps>, Arc<FakeUnitBus>, Arc<FakeUnitBus>, Arc<FakeOpeners>, Receiver<ActionEvent>, Receiver<EngineMsg>);   // system bus, user bus, startup_paths under tmp
fn startup_tree(tmp: &TempDir) -> StartupPaths;   // creates autostart, systemd/user, plasma-workspace/{env,shutdown} and an "/etc/xdg/autostart" under tmp
```

The `FakeOps` from E11-007 gains the cgroup, startup and PID-op steps the P2 beads name. Tests: every case named in E11-006 (`sched_validation_and_call`, `ioprio_classes_and_realtime_guard`, `signal_other_number`, `thread_target_tgkill_and_missing_tid`, `thread_target_unsupported_kinds`), E11-009 (`cgroup_*`), E11-011 (`unit_start_match_before_call` … `unit_job_wait_has_no_client_timeout`), E11-012 (`unit_freeze_*`, `unit_kill_all_sigkill`, `unit_wrong_kind_unsupported`), E11-013 (`unit_enable_*`, `unit_mask_calls`, `unit_unmask_calls`, `unit_reload_failure_is_unknown`), E11-014 (`startup_*`), E11-015 (`startup_run_now_*`, `startup_delete_*`), E11-016 (`targetless_*`), plus `busy_unit_second_action_rejected` (two `UnitStart` on the same unit: the second gets `Rejected(Busy)` while the first waits for `JobRemoved`; after `done` the unit is free and a third succeeds) and `#[explore_seeds(seeds = 0..16, workers = 2, chaos)] explore_unit_jobs` (two units, interleaved signals, every action ends with exactly one summary).

title: E11: Dump direct or through the helper (actions/dump.rs)
description:
## Context
"Create dump file" (`ActionKind::Dump { mode, path }` on one `Process` target, P3). With `ptrace_scope = 0` and the same uid the engine runs `tl_ops::dump::dump_to_path` itself on the blocking pool; otherwise (`PermissionDenied` from the ptrace check, or `req.privileged`) it opens the output file itself with `O_CREAT | O_EXCL`, mode `0600`, and asks the helper to write into that descriptor (`HelperRequest::Dump { key, mode }` with the fd passed beside the frame, E29-OI-6 hook). The action has no deadline; the UI reads the file size every 500 ms for progress. Sources: PROC-075, ADR-006 (helper `Dump`), ADR-005 (`Dump` kind, R-119), UI-PWN-034 (path under `$XDG_STATE_HOME/tasklens/dumps/`), E07-012 (`dump_to_path`, `dump_available`, `ptrace_allowed`), E11-002 (`PrivilegedOps`), B3 open item 15.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/actions/dump.rs`:

```rust
pub fn dumps_dir(config: &EngineConfig) -> PathBuf;   // config.state_dir.join("dumps")
pub fn valid_dump_path(path: &str, dir: &Path) -> bool;   // absolute, parent == dir (component compare, no canonicalisation), file name matches ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.core$ and is not "." or ".."
pub async fn run_target(cx: &Cx, actx: &ActionCtx, mode: DumpMode, path: &str, key: ProcessKey, privileged: bool) -> ActionState;
```

`run_target`: `!valid_dump_path` → `Rejected(Unsupported)`; `!ops.dump_available()` → `Rejected(Unsupported)` (UI tooltip "Install gdb to create dumps"). Create `dir` with mode `0700` if missing. Then:
- `privileged == false`: `spawn_blocking { ops.dump_to_path(key, boot_id, mode, path) }` with no deadline. `Ok` → `Succeeded`; `OpsError::PermissionDenied` → `Failed(PermissionDenied)` (UI toast "Creating a dump needs administrator rights" with the retry button); other → `map_ops_error`.
- `privileged == true`: `helper` is `None` or `helper.state() == Missing` → `Rejected(Unsupported)`; else open `path` with `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_CLOEXEC`, mode `0600` (`EEXIST` → `Failed(Os(EEXIST))`), and `helper.call(cx, HelperRequest::Dump { key, mode }, Some(fd), PROMPT_DEADLINE)`; `Ok` with body `Ok` → `Succeeded`; `Err(HelperError)` → the E29-014 mapping (`IdentityChanged` → `Rejected(IdentityChanged)`, `PermissionDenied` → `Failed(PermissionDenied)`, `Os(n)` → `Failed(Os(n))`); `HelperCallError::Timeout` → `OutcomeUnknown("no answer from the administrator helper")`; `Cancelled` → `Failed(AuthCancelled)`; `NotAuthorized` → `Failed(NotAuthorized)` (R-148 item 3); `Exited | Protocol` → `Failed(Internal("administrator helper stopped"))`; `Missing` → `Rejected(Unsupported)`. On any failure the engine unlinks the file it created.
`ActionOps` gains `dump_available() -> bool` and `dump_to_path(key, boot, mode, &Path) -> OpsResult`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `path = "<dumps>/firefox_1234_20261003_120000.core"` **When** `valid_dump_path` runs **Then** true; `"<dumps>/../x.core"`, `"/tmp/x.core"`, `"<dumps>/x.txt"`, `"<dumps>/sub/x.core"` → false (security regression).
- **Given** `privileged = false` and the fake `dump_to_path` returns `Ok` **When** run **Then** `Succeeded` and the fake saw `(key, mode, path)`.
- **Given** the fake returns `PermissionDenied` **When** run **Then** `Failed(PermissionDenied)`.
- **Given** `privileged = true` and a fake helper that answers `Ok` **When** run **Then** the helper saw `Dump { key, mode }` with `Some(fd)` and the file exists with mode `0600`; the state is `Succeeded`.
- **Given** `privileged = true` and the file already exists **When** run **Then** `Failed(Os(EEXIST))` and the existing file is unchanged.
- **Given** the helper answers `Err(IdentityChanged)` **When** run **Then** `Rejected(IdentityChanged)` and the created file was removed.
- **Given** `dump_available()` false **When** run **Then** `Rejected(Unsupported)` and no call.
- **Given** a 3 s fake dump **When** run **Then** `Succeeded` (no deadline).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/dump.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/mod.rs`: `pub mod dump;`, the `Dump` arm in `dispatch` (Process target only; other targets → `Rejected(Unsupported)`), `ActionOps` methods

## Tests
- `lab_actions.rs` (E11-021): `dump_path_validation`, `dump_direct_ok`, `dump_direct_permission_denied`, `dump_privileged_passes_fd`, `dump_privileged_eexist`, `dump_privileged_identity_changed_cleans_up`, `dump_without_gdb_unsupported`, `dump_has_no_deadline`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: as above; UI toasts "Dump created: <path>", "Creating a dump needs administrator rights" (PROC-075).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: the direct path blocks one pool thread for the whole dump (minutes for a large process); it is one action, so at most 16 such jobs.
- Privacy: core files hold process memory: mode `0600`, never read or logged by tasklens; the path is logged at debug only.
- Security: the engine writes only inside its own dumps directory; the helper never receives a path, only a descriptor.

## Notes
Depends on E11-002, E07-A3 (`dump.rs`), E03-A2 (`HelperRequest::Dump`). The fd travels as `SCM_RIGHTS` ancillary data on the `Dump` frame over the socketpair that is the helper's stdin and stdout (R-145 item 3); `HelperRequest::Dump { key, mode }` has no fd field; the `PrivilegedOps::call` signature already carries `Option<OwnedFd>`. Phase P3. Label `security`. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
close_reason: actions/dump.rs (dumps_dir, valid_dump_path, run_target direct and through the helper), ActionOps dump methods, RealOps forwarding, Dump arm in dispatch; commit 20b0621

title: E11: SockDestroy through the helper and destroy_supported (actions/socket.rs)
description:
## Context
"Close TCP connection" (`ActionKind::SockDestroy` on `ActionTarget::Socket { cookie, family, proto, four_tuple }`, P3) always goes through the helper, which sends the `SOCK_DESTROY` netlink message matched by the exact 4-tuple and cookie, so a reused 4-tuple cannot be hit. The first answer also tells the engine whether the kernel supports it (`CONFIG_INET_DIAG_DESTROY`); the reducer stores it as `ConnectionsSnapshot.destroy_supported` so the menu item can be disabled with the tooltip "Kernel lacks CONFIG_INET_DIAG_DESTROY". Sources: SYS-031, ADR-006 (helper `SockDestroy`), R-004, E08-003 (`SourceUpdate::ConnectionsDestroySupport`), E03-070 (`HelperRequest::SockDestroy`), E11-002 (`PrivilegedOps`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/actions/socket.rs`:

```rust
pub const DESTROY_DEADLINE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);
pub async fn run_target(cx: &Cx, actx: &ActionCtx, kind: &ActionKind, cookie: u64, family: Family, proto: Proto, four_tuple: FourTuple) -> ActionState;
```

`run_target`: any kind other than `SockDestroy` → `Rejected(Unsupported)`; `proto != Tcp` → `Rejected(Unsupported)`; `helper` is `None` or `state() == Missing` → `Rejected(Unsupported)` (UI tooltip "Needs the tasklens helper"); `state() == Locked` → the call still goes (the helper start prompts; use `PROMPT_DEADLINE` for this call instead of 2 s); else `helper.call(cx, HelperRequest::SockDestroy { family, proto, four_tuple, cookie }, None, DESTROY_DEADLINE)`. Reply `Ok` → send `SourceUpdate::ConnectionsDestroySupport(true)` (only the first time per session; keep an `AtomicBool` in `ActionCtx`) and `Succeeded`. `Err(Os(95))` (EOPNOTSUPP) → send `ConnectionsDestroySupport(false)` and `Rejected(Unsupported)`. `Err(Os(2))` (ENOENT, socket already gone) → `Failed(NoSuchProcess)` (UI text "Failed to close TCP connection: no such connection"). `Err(PermissionDenied)` → `Failed(PermissionDenied)`; other `Os(n)` → `Failed(Os(n))`; `HelperCallError` mapped as in E11-018.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake helper answering `Ok` **When** run **Then** the helper saw `SockDestroy` with the exact 4-tuple and cookie, `Succeeded`, and one `ConnectionsDestroySupport(true)` message on `msgs`.
- **Given** two successful destroys **When** run **Then** `ConnectionsDestroySupport(true)` is sent once.
- **Given** the helper answers `Err(Os(95))` **When** run **Then** `Rejected(Unsupported)` and `ConnectionsDestroySupport(false)` is sent.
- **Given** `Err(Os(2))` **When** run **Then** `Failed(NoSuchProcess)`.
- **Given** `proto = Udp` **When** run **Then** `Rejected(Unsupported)` and no call.
- **Given** no helper **When** run **Then** `Rejected(Unsupported)` and no call.
- **Given** a helper that does not answer **When** 2 s pass **Then** `OutcomeUnknown("no answer from the administrator helper")`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/socket.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/mod.rs`: `pub mod socket;`, the `Socket` dispatch arm, the `destroy_support_sent: AtomicBool` field

## Tests
- `lab_actions.rs` (E11-021): `sock_destroy_ok_reports_support`, `sock_destroy_support_sent_once`, `sock_destroy_eopnotsupp`, `sock_destroy_enoent`, `sock_destroy_udp_unsupported`, `sock_destroy_without_helper`, `sock_destroy_timeout`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: UI toasts "TCP connection close requested", "TCP connection closed", "Failed to close TCP connection: <errno text>" (SYS-031).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one helper call per action.
- Privacy: addresses are logged at debug only.
- Security: the engine never opens a netlink socket for destroy itself (needs `CAP_NET_ADMIN`); the cookie match is the helper's and the kernel's.

## Notes
Depends on E11-002, E03-A2. The 4-tuple and cookie come from the connection record the UI captured at menu-open time (E03-055 `ConnRecord.four_tuple`, `cookie`). Phase P3. Label `security`. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E11: recovery drop-in write and remove (actions/recovery.rs)
description:
## Context
Recovery tab edits (P3): `UnitWriteRecovery(RecoveryEdit)` writes a drop-in with only the changed keys and `UnitRemoveRecovery` deletes it, then the owning manager reloads. User units: the engine writes `~/.config/systemd/user/<unit>.d/50-tasklens-recovery.conf` with `write_atomic`. System units: the helper writes `/etc/systemd/system/<unit>.d/50-tasklens-recovery.conf` (`HelperRequest::WriteServiceDropIn { unit, keys }`, empty keys deletes). Both paths render the same text. Sources: SYS-013, ADR-006 (helper `WriteServiceDropIn`, key limits), ADR-011 (`write_atomic`), E03-053 (`RecoveryEdit`), E03-070 (`DropInKey`, `validate_drop_in`), E07-A3 (`write_atomic`), E11-013 (`reload`), E29-OI-10 (one renderer).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/actions/recovery.rs`:

```rust
pub const DROP_IN_NAME: &str = "50-tasklens-recovery.conf";
pub use tl_ops::dropin::HEADER;   // "# Written by tasklens. Edit it in the Service Properties Recovery tab or delete this file.\n" (defined by E29-009, R-248)
pub fn keys_of(edit: &RecoveryEdit) -> Vec<(DropInKey, String)>;
// restart → (Restart, word); restart_usec → (RestartSec, "<n>us"); restart_steps → (RestartSteps, n); restart_max_delay_usec → (RestartMaxDelaySec, "<n>us");
// start_limit_burst → (StartLimitBurst, n); start_limit_interval_usec → (StartLimitIntervalSec, "<n>us"); start_limit_action → (StartLimitAction, word); failure_action → (FailureAction, word); on_failure → (OnFailure, names joined by one space)
pub use tl_ops::dropin::render;   // render(keys: &[(DropInKey, String)]) -> String, the one renderer (E29-009, R-248)
// HEADER, then "[Unit]\n" with StartLimitIntervalSec, StartLimitBurst, StartLimitAction, FailureAction, OnFailure (only those present, in that order), then "[Service]\n" with Restart, RestartSec, RestartSteps, RestartMaxDelaySec (same rule); a section with no keys is omitted; every line "Key=value\n"; no blank lines
pub fn user_drop_in_path(config_home: &Path, unit: &str) -> PathBuf;   // <config_home>/systemd/user/<unit>.d/50-tasklens-recovery.conf
pub async fn run_target(cx: &Cx, actx: &ActionCtx, kind: &ActionKind, unit: &UnitRef) -> ActionState;
```

`run_target`: build `keys` (`UnitRemoveRecovery` → empty); `tl_model::helper_proto::validate_drop_in(&unit.name, &keys)` fails → `Rejected(Unsupported)` (also rejects a `.d` path escape through the unit name). Then by manager:
- `User`: `spawn_blocking` under 2 s: non-empty keys → create `<unit>.d` with mode `0755` if missing, `write_atomic(path, render(&keys), 0o644)`; empty keys → unlink the file (`ENOENT` is fine) and remove the `.d` directory if it is now empty. Then `unit::reload(cx, bus_for(User), User)`; reload failure → `OutcomeUnknown("written, but the manager reload failed")`.
- `System`: `helper` is `None` or `Missing` → `Rejected(Unsupported)` (tooltip "Needs the tasklens helper"); else `helper.call(cx, HelperRequest::WriteServiceDropIn { unit: name, keys }, None, PROMPT_DEADLINE)`; `Ok` → `unit::reload(cx, bus_for(System), System)` (120 s, may prompt); errors mapped as in E11-018.
`ActionOps` gains `write_atomic(path, text, mode) -> OpsResult`, `remove_file(path) -> OpsResult`, `remove_dir_if_empty(path) -> OpsResult`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `RecoveryEdit { restart: Some("on-failure"), restart_usec: Some(5_000_000), start_limit_burst: Some(3), start_limit_interval_usec: Some(60_000_000), ..Default }` **When** rendered **Then** the text is exactly `HEADER + "[Unit]\nStartLimitIntervalSec=60000000us\nStartLimitBurst=3\n[Service]\nRestart=on-failure\nRestartSec=5000000us\n"` (R-248).
- **Given** only `on_failure: Some(["a.service", "b.service"])` **When** rendered **Then** `HEADER + "[Unit]\nOnFailure=a.service b.service\n"` (no `[Service]` section; `OnFailure` is a `[Unit]` key, R-248).
- **Given** a `User` unit **When** `UnitWriteRecovery` runs **Then** the fake saw `write_atomic(<config>/systemd/user/foo.service.d/50-tasklens-recovery.conf, <text>, 0o644)` then `Reload` on the user bus, and the state is `Succeeded`.
- **Given** a `User` unit **When** `UnitRemoveRecovery` runs **Then** `remove_file(<path>)`, `remove_dir_if_empty(<dir>)`, `Reload`.
- **Given** a `System` unit and a fake helper **When** `UnitWriteRecovery` runs **Then** the helper saw `WriteServiceDropIn { unit: "foo.service", keys }` and then `Reload` ran on the system bus.
- **Given** unit name `../evil.service` or a value with `\n` **When** run **Then** `Rejected(Unsupported)` and no write or call (security regression).
- **Given** a `System` unit without the helper **When** run **Then** `Rejected(Unsupported)`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/recovery.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/mod.rs`: `pub mod recovery;`, the two arms in the `Unit` dispatch, `ActionOps` methods

## Tests
- `recovery.rs::tests::render_full`, `render_unit_only`, `keys_of_table`, `user_drop_in_path_shape` (the render tests exercise the re-exported `tl_ops::dropin::render`).
- `lab_actions.rs` (E11-021): `recovery_user_write_and_reload`, `recovery_user_remove`, `recovery_system_via_helper`, `recovery_rejects_bad_unit_or_value`, `recovery_system_without_helper`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: as above; UI toast "Changes applied" on success (SYS-011).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one write and one reload.
- Privacy: N/A (unit names and systemd words only).
- Security: keys are limited to the `DropInKey` set; values are validated against newlines; the unit name is validated before any path is built. The system path is the helper's fixed path; the engine never writes under `/etc`.

## Notes
Depends on E11-013 (`reload`), E07-A3, E03-A2. One renderer (R-248): `render` and `HEADER` live in `tl-ops/src/dropin.rs` (E29-009, qfx.12); this file re-exports them and keeps its tests. Depends on E29-009 for the renderer. Phase P3. Label `security`. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E11: lab_actions.rs part 3: FakePrivilegedOps, dump, socket, recovery cases
description:
## Context

title: E11: action admission rules (actions/mod.rs part 1)
description:
## Context
Admission runs in the reducer on `Command::Action`: more than 16 actions in flight is `Rejected(Busy)`; more than 256 targets is `Rejected(TooManyTargets)`; a process target whose `boot_id` differs or whose key is neither live nor exited within the linger is `Rejected(IdentityChanged)` per target; `KERNEL_THREAD` is `Rejected(KernelThread)`; tasklens itself (`IS_SELF`) and PID 1 are `Rejected(Protected)` (the UI shows the refusal toasts; other `PROTECTED` targets were confirmed by the UI and pass). `OpenUri`, `ShowInFileManager` and `Launch` carry no targets and skip the target checks. A unit with an action already running is `Rejected(Busy)` (SYS-005 "A service action is already in progress."). Sources: ADR-006 (admission), ADR-005 (`RejectReason`, event order), PROC-059, R-036, R-134, SYS-005, E09-001 (`ActionGate`, `AdmissionView`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/actions/mod.rs` (part 1):

```rust
pub mod process; pub mod cgroup; pub mod unit; pub mod startup; pub mod dump; pub mod socket; pub mod recovery;   // module lines are added by their beads; E11-001 adds `process` only
pub const MAX_IN_FLIGHT: usize = 16;
pub const MAX_TARGETS: usize = 256;

pub enum Admission { Reject(RejectReason), Run { per_target: Vec<Option<RejectReason>> /* Some = this target is rejected before start */ } }
pub fn admit(req: &ActionRequest, view: &AdmissionView<'_>, in_flight: usize, busy_units: &FxHashSet<UnitRef>) -> Admission;
pub fn targetless(kind: &ActionKind) -> bool;   // OpenUri | ShowInFileManager | Launch
```

Rules in order: `in_flight >= 16` → `Reject(Busy)`; `targets.len() > 256` → `Reject(TooManyTargets)`; `targetless(kind)` → `Run { per_target: [] }` (an empty `targets` is required; non-empty is `Reject(Unsupported)`); otherwise per target: `Process(key)` or `Thread { process: key, .. }`: `key.boot_id != view.boot_id` → `IdentityChanged`; not in `view.live` and not in `view.exited_within_linger` → `IdentityChanged`; flags has `KERNEL_THREAD` → `KernelThread`; flags has `IS_SELF` or `key.pid == 1` → `Protected`; `Unit(u)` in `busy_units` → `Busy`; `Cgroup`, `Startup`, `Socket` → `None` (validated by their modules). If every target is rejected the request is still `Run` (so the UI gets `Started` then per-target `Rejected` events and a `Rejected` summary), except when `targets.is_empty()` for a kind that needs targets → `Reject(Unsupported)`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `in_flight = 16` **When** admitted **Then** `Reject(Busy)`; with 15 → `Run`.
- **Given** 257 targets **When** admitted **Then** `Reject(TooManyTargets)`; 256 → `Run`.
- **Given** a process key with another `boot_id` **When** admitted **Then** `per_target[i] == Some(IdentityChanged)`.
- **Given** a key in `exited_within_linger` **When** admitted **Then** `per_target[i] == None` (the pidfd open will report it).
- **Given** a key with `KERNEL_THREAD` **When** admitted **Then** `Some(KernelThread)`; with `IS_SELF` or pid 1 → `Some(Protected)`; with `PROTECTED` only (kwin) → `None`.
- **Given** `Signal(Term)` with empty targets **When** admitted **Then** `Reject(Unsupported)`; `OpenUri` with empty targets → `Run`; `OpenUri` with one target → `Reject(Unsupported)`.
- **Given** a `Unit` target already in `busy_units` **When** admitted **Then** `Some(Busy)`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/mod.rs`: create (part 1)
- `crates/tl-engine/src/lib.rs`: add `pub mod actions;`

## Tests
