title: E20-021 Tab switch animation
description:
## Context
Animates tab switches: the accent outline slides from the old tab to the new one and the new page fades in, over `motion.tab_switch_ms` (default 250 ms) with `ease_out_cubic`. With animations off, reduced motion on, or a duration of 0, the switch stays instant as in P1. Only the active page renders (ADR-009), so the crossfade is a fade-in over the window background. Phase P2. Sources: UI-SHL-021, UI-SHL-132, APP-027, R-017, ADR-009 (only the active page renders; one-shot animations only), canonical table (a) `motion.tab_switch_ms` 0..=500 step 10.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/window/tabstrip.rs`:
- `TabStrip` gets `anim: Option<TabAnim>` with `struct TabAnim { from: Bounds<Pixels>, generation: u64, start: Instant, duration: Duration }` and `pub fn begin_switch(&mut self, from_bounds: Bounds<Pixels>, duration: Duration, cx: &mut Context<Self>)`.
- When `anim` is set, the `AccentRule` is wrapped in `with_animation(ElementId::from(("tab-switch", generation)), Animation::new(duration).with_easing(ease_out_cubic), |rule, t| ..)` that interpolates the outline's x and width from `from` to the active tab's bounds (`x = from.x + (to.x − from.x) × t`, same for width) and rebuilds the path each frame only during the animation. When the animation ends, clear `anim` and cache the final path as before.
- A new switch during an animation starts from the current interpolated bounds (pass them as `from`).
In `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`:
- `select_tab`: if `settings_global::animations_on(cx)` and `motion.tab_switch_ms > 0`, call `tabstrip.begin_switch(old_outline_bounds, Duration::from_millis(ms))` and wrap the page container in `with_animation(ElementId::from(("page-fade", generation)), Animation::new(same).with_easing(ease_out_cubic), |el, t| el.opacity(t))`. Otherwise no animation (P1 behaviour).
- `ease_out_cubic(t) = 1 − (1 − t)³`. Use the GPUI or kit function of that name if one exists; else define it in `tabstrip.rs`.
- Both animations are one-shot: frames stop when they end.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `motion.animations = true`, no reduced motion and `tab_switch_ms = 250` **When** `SelectTab(1)` runs **Then** after 125 ms the outline's x lies strictly between the old and new tab's x and the page opacity is between 0 and 1, and after 250 ms the outline is on the new tab and opacity is 1.
- **Given** reduced motion **When** `SelectTab(1)` runs and one frame passes **Then** the page opacity is 1.0, the outline is on the new tab and no animation runs.
- **Given** `tab_switch_ms = 0` **When** a tab switch happens **Then** it is instant.
- **Given** an animation half done **When** another `SelectTab` runs **Then** the new animation starts from the current interpolated outline position.
- **Given** the animation ended **When** 1 s passes with no changes **Then** no frame is requested.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/tabstrip.rs`: `TabAnim`, `begin_switch`, animated rule.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`: start the animations in `select_tab`.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`: tests.

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`:
- `tab_switch_animates`: criterion 1 (advance the test clock).
- `tab_switch_instant_when_reduced_motion`: criterion 2 (`cx.set_reduce_motion(true)`).
- `tab_switch_zero_ms_instant`: criterion 3.
- `tab_switch_restarts_from_current`: criterion 4.
- `tab_switch_no_frames_after_end`: criterion 5.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: reduced motion and the Animations setting turn it off (R-017).
- Performance: during the 250 ms, each frame rebuilds a 12-segment path and sets an opacity (well under 0.1 ms); charts in the new page start their own driver requests after the first render.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- `with_animation`, `Animation` are gpui-pre 0.3.7 (`src/elements/animation.rs`). This is one of the permitted shell uses of `Animation` (UI-SHL-021); it is never a continuous redraw.
- `animations_on` is E20-001.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_shell`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

- Read `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` in the repo first.

title: E20-022 Always-on-top pin caption button and ToggleAlwaysOnTop handler
description:
## Context
Adds the pin caption button ("Always on top") to the main window title bar and the shell's handler for `ToggleAlwaysOnTop` on the main window. On KDE the KWin bridge keeps the window above others; where the bridge is not available the pin is disabled with "Not supported by this desktop". The setting `window.always_on_top` is saved at once and re-applied at the next start. Phase P2. Sources: UI-SHL-005 (pin row and states), UI-SHL-006 (pin in the server-decorations row), APP-008, APP-009, R-073, UI-FND-021 (pin look and tooltips), PROC-056.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/window/titlebar.rs`:
- Pin cell left of minimize: 36 × 34 (client bar), 36 × 28 (server row of E20-014, at its pin position). `TlButton::Toggle { on: settings.window.always_on_top }` filling the whole cell; icon Lucide `pin` (on, tinted `accent`, Toggle on look: `accent` at alpha 0.25 with a 1 px `accent` border) or `pin-off` (off). Tooltip "Always on top" (off) or "Always on top (on)" (on). Not a Tab stop. Mouse-down stops propagation.
- Disabled when `keep_above_supported(cx)` is false: icon at the foundation's disabled opacity (0.5), no hover, tooltip "Not supported by this desktop", click does nothing.
- Click dispatches `ToggleAlwaysOnTop { window: WindowKey::Main, caption: "tasklens".into() }` (R-176: the caption is the window title at dispatch time).
In `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`:
- Handler for `ToggleAlwaysOnTop` registered in `window::main::init` with `cx.on_action`: when `window == WindowKey::Main` and `keep_above_supported(cx)`: `on = !settings.window.always_on_top`; `TlSettings::update` writes it (persisted, no toast); send `Command::KWin(KWinCommand::KeepAbove { pid: std::process::id(), caption: None, on })` through `EngineGlobal`. Any other `WindowKey`: return without doing anything; E20-029 adds the secondary-window arm (R-176).
- At start: when `window.always_on_top` is true, send the same `KeepAbove { on: true }` once, the first time `keep_above_supported` becomes true after the main window opened (watch `ComponentMask::WINDOWS` changes; stop watching after sending).
- `Command::KWin` returning `Err(CommandError::Busy)`: retry once on the next `WINDOWS` change; log `warn!` if it fails again.

Strings: reuse E16-002's `fnd-pin-off = Always on top`, `fnd-pin-on = Always on top (on)`, `fnd-pin-unsupported = Not supported by this desktop`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the KWin bridge is up (windows validity `Valid`) and the pin is off **When** the pin is clicked **Then** `window.always_on_top` is true, the fake engine received `KWin(KeepAbove { on: true, caption: None, pid: <own pid> })`, and the pin shows the on look with tooltip "Always on top (on)".
- **Given** the pin is on **When** clicked **Then** the setting is false and `KeepAbove { on: false, .. }` is sent.
- **Given** windows validity `Unsupported` **When** the title bar renders **Then** the pin is disabled with tooltip "Not supported by this desktop" and a click sends nothing.
- **Given** `window.always_on_top = true` at start and the windows validity changes from `WarmingUp` to `Valid` **When** observed **Then** exactly one `KeepAbove { on: true }` is sent.
- **Given** server decorations **When** the menu row renders **Then** the pin is its last item, 36 × 28.
- **Given** a click on the pin followed by a mouse move **When** handled **Then** no window drag starts.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/titlebar.rs`: pin cell in both bars.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`: the handler and the start-up apply.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`: tests.

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`:
- `pin_toggles_setting`: criteria 1 and 2.
- `pin_disabled_without_bridge`: criterion 3.
- `pin_applied_at_start_once`: criterion 4.
- `server_mode_has_pin`: criterion 5.
- `pin_no_drag`: criterion 6.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: a failed KWin command is logged; no toast (UI-SHL-005 says no toast).
- Validity: availability from `Snapshot.windows.header.validity` (E20-004 `keep_above_supported`).
- Accessibility: View > Window > Always On Top (E21-008) dispatches the same Action; the tooltip carries the state.
- Performance: no per-frame work.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- `ToggleAlwaysOnTop { window: WindowKey, caption: SharedString }` is declared by E16-008 (`components/window_frame.rs`) with `#[action(no_json)]`. E16-008 adds `WindowKey::Main` (never stored in the registry map, `cap_class()` returns `None`) (R-176).
- There is no X11 keep-above in v1 (R-177, ADR-004, ADR-010). On X11 and every desktop without the KWin bridge the pin is disabled with tooltip "Not supported by this desktop".
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_shell`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- crates/tl-ui/src/window/titlebar.rs crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`. Never a bare `git commit`.
- Read `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` in the repo first.

title: E20-023 Information tab copy-all icon

title: E20-024 Startup public IP auto-fetch
description:
## Context
Starts the public IP fetch after the first frame when "Auto-fetch Public IP on launch" is on and the user already accepted the Public IP notice. Without the notice accepted, nothing is fetched at launch (no network contact before consent). Phase P2. Sources: UI-SHL-110 step 11 (last item), APP-056, PERF-060, UI-SHL-096, canonical table (a) `[network] auto_fetch_public_ip`, `public_ip_notice_accepted`.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`, at the `// step 11: public IP auto-fetch (E20-024)` line of `after_first_frame`:
- Once per process (a `PublicIpAutoFetched` Global guards it): if `settings.network.auto_fetch_public_ip && settings.network.public_ip_notice_accepted`, send `Command::Device(DeviceCommand::FetchPublicIp)` through `EngineGlobal` (R-139 item 5; there is no `SourceId::PublicIp`, the Inventory worker runs the fetch on request). On `Err(CommandError::Busy)` retry once after 1 s; on a second failure log `warn!(target: "tasklens::ui", "public IP auto-fetch not queued")`. No toast in any case.
- If `auto_fetch_public_ip` is true but the notice was never accepted, do nothing (the notice only opens from a user Fetch, E21-017).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** both keys true **When** the first frame runs **Then** the fake engine receives one `RefreshNow(SourceId::PublicIp)`.
- **Given** `auto_fetch_public_ip = true` and `public_ip_notice_accepted = false` **When** the first frame runs **Then** nothing is sent and no window opens.
- **Given** `auto_fetch_public_ip = false` **When** the first frame runs **Then** nothing is sent.
- **Given** both true and the main window is reopened later **When** its first frame runs **Then** nothing more is sent.
- **Given** the engine answers `Busy` once **When** the first frame runs **Then** the command is sent again 1 s later and succeeds.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`: the step-11 item.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`: tests.

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`:
- `public_ip_auto_fetch_when_accepted`: criterion 1.
- `public_ip_no_fetch_without_consent`: criterion 2.
- `public_ip_no_fetch_when_off`: criterion 3.
- `public_ip_auto_fetch_once_per_process`: criterion 4.
- `public_ip_auto_fetch_retries_busy`: criterion 5 (the FakeEngine returns `Busy` for the first `send`).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: no user text; a failed fetch shows on the Network page and Information tab (their owners).
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one command at start.
- Privacy: no network contact unless the user accepted the notice (PERF-060, APP-056). The address is never logged.

## Notes
- The fetch command is `Command::Device(DeviceCommand::FetchPublicIp)` (E03-063, R-139 items 1 and 5). The engine has no startup auto-fetch of its own: this bead is the only startup trigger, because only the UI knows `public_ip_notice_accepted`. The result appears in `snapshot.inventory.public_ip` (R-139 item 4).
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_shell`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E20-025 History toggle icon on the Processes tab and ToggleHistoryMode handler
description:
## Context
Adds the History toggle icon inside the Processes tab and the shell's handler for `ToggleHistoryMode`: it selects the Processes tab when needed and flips `UiState.processes.history_mode`, which relabels the tab "History" and switches the Processes page to its history table (E30). The shell owns the Action so the icon, View menu items and keys all work even when the Processes page is not active. Phase P3. Sources: UI-SHL-023 (history icon), UI-SHL-020 (History label), PROC-088, PROC-086, D-010, R-023.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/window/tabstrip.rs`:
- The Processes tab draws after its label, with gap 6: Lucide `rotate-ccw-clock` at `i_sm` 14 × 14 in a 22 × 22 hit area, colour `text_secondary`, or `accent` while History mode is on. Hover or pressed: icon `text_primary` on a `tab_hover` rounded square (`r_sm`). Tooltip and accessible name "Show history" when off, "Show live processes" when on.
- Click dispatches `ToggleHistoryMode` and stops propagation (the tab click does not also fire); mouse-down stops propagation. The icon counts in the tab's width (E20-015).
In `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`:
- Handler for `ToggleHistoryMode` on the `MainWindow` root (at the `// window-level on_action handlers (chain edits)` line): if the active tab is not Processes, `select_tab(Tab::Processes)`; then `TlSettings::update(cx, |d| d.state.processes.history_mode = !d.state.processes.history_mode)`. Nothing else: the tab label follows from the state (E20-005), and the Processes page reacts to the state change (E30 shows the RAM window and the "History recording is off" toast when `history.enabled` is false, D-010, PROC-086).
- This is the only handler of `ToggleHistoryMode`. E30 must observe `UiState.processes.history_mode` instead of registering a handler (told to the leader in `docs/plan/b7-ui-shell.md`).

Strings (`assets/locales/en-US.ftl`, chain edit): `shell-tab-show-history = Show history`, `shell-tab-show-live = Show live processes`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** Performance active and History mode off **When** `ToggleHistoryMode` is dispatched **Then** Processes is active, `history_mode` is true (persisted in state.toml) and the first tab label reads "History".
- **Given** Processes active in History mode **When** the icon is clicked **Then** `history_mode` is false, the label reads "Processes" and no `SelectTab` was dispatched.
- **Given** History mode on **When** the strip renders **Then** the icon colour is `accent` and its tooltip "Show live processes".
- **Given** History mode off **When** the icon is hovered **Then** it is `text_primary` on a `tab_hover` square with tooltip "Show history".

- `history_icon_click_toggles_off`: criterion 2.

- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: the View menu and keys reach the same Action; the tooltip text is the accessible name and carries the state.
- Performance: one state write per toggle.
- Privacy: N/A.

title: E20-026 Shield toolbar slot and unlock at launch
description:
## Context
Places the shield (unlock privileged actions) in toolbar slot 1 on every tab when the privileged helper is installed, and starts the helper session once after the first frame when "Unlock privileged actions at launch" is on or Shift was held at launch. The shield's look, states, Actions and failure toasts are the foundation's `TlShield` (E16-010); the helper flow is E29's. Phase P3. Sources: UI-SHL-011, UI-SHL-010 (slot 1), UI-SHL-110 steps 6 and 11, APP-003, APP-049, R-002, R-003, R-124, U-43, canonical table (b) "Shift held at launch".

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`:
- In `window::main::init`: `cx.set_global(HelperInstalled(std::path::Path::new("/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper").exists()))` (checked once per process). `pub struct HelperInstalled(pub bool); impl Global`.
- `ToolbarModel.helper_installed` (E20-003) is filled from it, and `ToolbarModel.helper` from `snapshot.health.helper`; `MainWindow` updates the model when the hub's `SnapshotChanged` has `ComponentMask::HEALTH` and the helper state changed.
- At the `// step 11: helper unlock at launch (E20-026)` line of `after_first_frame`: if `settings.privilege.unlock_at_launch || StartOptions.shift_held`, call `self.request_launch_unlock(window, cx)`.
- `pub fn request_launch_unlock(&mut self, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>)`: once per process (a `LaunchUnlockRequested` Global guards it) and only when `HelperInstalled(true)`: `window.dispatch_action(Box::new(StartHelperSession), cx)`. E29-030 calls this function when it detects Shift on Wayland within 500 ms of first focus (U-43).
In `crates/tl-ui/src/window/titlebar.rs`:
- `Toolbar::shield(..)` gets `Some(TlShield::new(model.helper).into_any_element())` when `model.helper_installed`, on every tab; else `None` (no space). `TlShield` renders nothing for `HelperState::Missing`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `HelperInstalled(true)` and helper state Locked **When** each of the six tabs is active (fake pages) **Then** toolbar slot 1 holds the shield on every tab.
- **Given** `HelperInstalled(false)` **When** the toolbar renders **Then** there is no shield and no space for it.
- **Given** `privilege.unlock_at_launch = true` and the helper installed **When** the first frame runs **Then** `StartHelperSession` is dispatched once; on a reopened window it is not dispatched again.
- **Given** `StartOptions.shift_held = true` and `unlock_at_launch = false` **When** the first frame runs **Then** `StartHelperSession` is dispatched once.
- **Given** the helper is not installed and `unlock_at_launch = true` **When** the first frame runs **Then** nothing is dispatched.
- **Given** `request_launch_unlock` was already used **When** E29 calls it again **Then** nothing is dispatched.
- **Given** the helper state changes from Locked to Unlocked **When** the HEALTH snapshot arrives **Then** the shield shows its Unlocked look.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`: `HelperInstalled`, model updates, step-11 item, `request_launch_unlock`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/titlebar.rs`: slot 1.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`: tests.

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`:
- `shield_slot_every_tab`: criteria 1 and 2 (override `HelperInstalled` in the test).
- `unlock_at_launch_once`: criterion 3.
- `shift_at_launch_unlocks`: criterion 4.
- `unlock_needs_helper`: criterion 5.
- `request_launch_unlock_once`: criterion 6.
- `shield_follows_helper_state`: criterion 7.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the failure toasts "Authentication cancelled" and "Could not start the privileged helper" belong to the shield flow (E16-010, E29).
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: the shield is not a Tab stop (R-108); the Settings menu and the restricted chip link (E22) reach the same Action.
- Performance: one path check per process; model updates only on helper state changes.
- Privacy: N/A.
- Security: the launch unlock only dispatches `StartHelperSession`; polkit authenticates (E29). It never runs when the helper is not installed.

## Notes
- `TlShield`, `StartHelperSession` are E16-010 (`components/shield.rs`, anchor E16-A3). `HelperState` is tl-model `health.rs`. `StartOptions.shift_held` is E16-012 (filled by tl-app on X11).
- The clickable " | 42 restricted" status segment is E22's `StatusAction` (E22 bead `tasklens-pdu.44`), not this bead.

title: E20-027 Window picker toolbar slot and picking mode
description:
## Context
Adds the window picker "+" in toolbar slot 4 on every tab when the KWin bridge is available: a click starts picking, the next click on any window selects its process (or ends it with Ctrl held, after a confirmation). The shell starts and cancels picking and shows the start toast; the result handling (selecting the row, Ctrl+click confirmation, result toasts) is the Processes page's (PROC-055). Phase P3. Sources: UI-SHL-014, UI-SHL-010 (slot 4), UI-SHL-122 step 3, APP-006, PROC-055, R-046, R-076, canonical table (b) Picker context.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/window/titlebar.rs`:
- `Toolbar::picker(..)` gets, when `model.picker_available` (windows validity is `Valid` or `Stale`, same test as `keep_above_supported`): `toolbar_toggle("picker", Lucide plus, on: model.picking, tooltip "Select process by window", action)` where the action is `StartWindowPick` when not picking and `CancelWindowPick` while picking. Hidden (no space) when not available.
In `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs` (listeners at the `// window-level on_action handlers (chain edits)` line):
- `StartWindowPick`: send `Command::KWin(KWinCommand::Pick)`; on `Ok`, set `self.picking = true` (the field E20-011 added), set `ToolbarModel.picking = true`, push the Info toast "Click a window to select its process. Hold CTRL while clicking to terminate process. Esc cancels." with key `PICK_TOAST`, and add the key context "Picker" to the root element while picking (`.when(self.picking, |el| el.key_context("Picker"))` on an inner element that holds focus, so "Picker" sits above "Global" and `escape` maps to `CancelWindowPick`). On `Err(Busy)`: Warning toast "Could not start window picking".
- `CancelWindowPick`: if picking, send `Command::KWin(KWinCommand::CancelPick)`, end picking (below) and push the Info toast "No window selected" with key `PICK_TOAST`.
- `pub fn end_window_pick(&mut self, cx: &mut Context<Self>)`: `picking = false`, model update, remove the "Picker" context, remove the `PICK_TOAST` toast. The Processes page calls it (through `MainWindow`) when the pick result arrives (PROC-055); the shell also calls it when the windows validity becomes `Unsupported` while picking.
- `pub const PICK_TOAST: ToastKey = ToastKey(0x7069_636b_0000_0001);`

Strings (`assets/locales/en-US.ftl`, chain edit): `shell-toolbar-picker = Select process by window`, `shell-toast-pick-start = Click a window to select its process. Hold CTRL while clicking to terminate process. Esc cancels.`, `shell-toast-pick-none = No window selected`, `shell-toast-pick-failed = Could not start window picking`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** windows validity `Unsupported` **When** the toolbar renders **Then** there is no picker button and no space for it.
- **Given** the bridge is up **When** each tab is active **Then** slot 4 holds the picker on every tab.
- **Given** the bridge is up **When** the picker is clicked **Then** the fake engine receives `KWin(Pick)`, the button shows the Toggle on look and the start toast shows.
- **Given** picking **When** Esc is pressed **Then** the fake engine receives `KWin(CancelPick)`, the toast "No window selected" replaces the start toast, and picking ends.
- **Given** picking **When** the picker is clicked again **Then** picking is cancelled the same way.
- **Given** picking **When** `end_window_pick` is called **Then** the button is off, the start toast is gone and Esc maps to `EscapeChain` again.
- **Given** the engine answers `Busy` to `Pick` **When** the picker is clicked **Then** the Warning toast "Could not start window picking" shows and picking does not start.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/titlebar.rs`: slot 4.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`: handlers, Picker context, `end_window_pick`.
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: four keys (chain edit).
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`: tests.

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`:
- `picker_hidden_without_bridge`: criterion 1.
- `picker_every_tab`: criterion 2.
- `picker_click_starts_pick`: criterion 3.
- `picker_esc_cancels`: criterion 4.
- `picker_second_click_cancels`: criterion 5.
- `picker_end_clears_state`: criterion 6.
- `picker_busy_warns`: criterion 7.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: "Could not start window picking" (Warning) when the command queue is full.
- Validity: availability from `Snapshot.windows.header.validity`.
- Accessibility: Esc cancels; the button is not a Tab stop; the toast explains the mode.
- Performance: N/A.
- Privacy: N/A.
- Security: ending a process by Ctrl+click goes through PROC-055's confirmation (E22), never directly from here.

## Notes
- `KWinCommand::{Pick, CancelPick}` are tl-model `command.rs` (E03-063). PROC-055's result handling is E22's; the leader adds an E22 follow-up if no E22 bead calls `end_window_pick` (listed in `docs/plan/b7-ui-shell.md`).
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_shell`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E20-001 TlSettings global, SettingKey and SettingValue (settings_global.rs)
description:
## Context
Builds `TlSettings`, the one GPUI Global that holds the parsed `settings.toml` and `state.toml` for the whole UI, with one version counter per settings section so views redraw only for the sections they draw. Every settings write in tl-ui goes through it: it bumps versions, calls the tl-app persist callback and pushes changed `EngineSettings` to the engine. It also defines `SettingKey` and `SettingValue`, which the generic `ToggleSetting` and `SetSetting` Actions (E20-002) carry. Phase P0 because the main window (E20-A1, P0) reads window size, decorations and the start tab from it. Sources: shell.md "Conventions" (Settings, two generic setting actions), ADR-011 (ownership, persist callback, `EngineSettings`), canonical table (a), APP-033, R-071, UI-SHL-131 (language), UI-SHL-132 (motion gate), R-017.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/settings_global.rs` (create; add `pub mod settings_global;` to `crates/tl-ui/src/lib.rs`):

```rust
pub struct SettingsData { pub settings: Settings, pub state: UiState }   // tl_model::settings types

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub enum Section { General, Theme, Appearance, Motion, Units, Processes, Tables, Properties, Performance,
                   Fans, Graphs, History, Window, Tray, Startup, Network, Privilege, Rendering, Services,
                   Lowmem, Debug }
impl Section { pub const ALL: [Section; 21]; pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; } // "general" .. "debug"

pub struct TlSettings {
    data: SettingsData,
    versions: [u64; 21],          // index = Section as usize
    state_version: u64,           // bumps on any UiState change
    persist: Option<Box<dyn Fn(&Settings, &UiState)>>,
}
impl Global for TlSettings {}

impl TlSettings {
    pub fn init(cx: &mut App);                                    // see "Init" below
    pub fn get(cx: &App) -> &TlSettings;                          // cx.global::<TlSettings>()
    pub fn settings(cx: &App) -> &Settings;
    pub fn state(cx: &App) -> &UiState;
    pub fn version(&self, section: Section) -> u64;
    pub fn state_version(&self) -> u64;
    /// Persisting write: run `f`, clamp, bump the versions of every section that changed,
    /// bump `state_version` if UiState changed, call `persist`, and send EngineSettings if they changed.
    pub fn update(cx: &mut App, f: impl FnOnce(&mut SettingsData));
    /// In-memory write for live previews (slider Change events): same as `update` but never calls
    /// `persist` and never calls `EngineClient::set_settings`. A later `update` persists the value.
    pub fn preview(cx: &mut App, f: impl FnOnce(&mut SettingsData));
    pub fn toggle(cx: &mut App, key: SettingKey);                 // flips a Bool key; any other kind: warn!, no change
    pub fn set(cx: &mut App, key: SettingKey, value: SettingValue); // writes one key; kind mismatch or bad string: warn!, no change
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub enum SettingKind { Bool, Int, Str, StrList, Map }

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub enum SettingKey { /* the 85 variants listed below, in that order */ }
impl SettingKey {
    pub const ALL: [SettingKey; 85];               // table (a) order
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str;           // dotted name, for example "motion.animations"; `Fans` is "fans"
    pub fn section(self) -> Section;
    pub fn kind(self) -> SettingKind;
}

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub enum SettingValue { Bool(bool), Int(i64), Str(SharedString), StrList(Arc<[SharedString]>) }

/// "Animations on": motion.animations && !cx.reduce_motion() (R-017, shell.md conventions).
pub fn animations_on(cx: &App) -> bool;
```

`SettingKey` variants (PascalCase of section plus key; kind after each). They mirror canonical table (a) `settings.toml` exactly, 85 keys:
- `[general]`: `GeneralStartTab` Str, `GeneralLanguage` Str.
- `[theme]`: `ThemeActive` Str, `ThemeFollowSystem` Bool, `ThemeLight` Str, `ThemeDark` Str.
- `[appearance]`: `AppearanceUiScalePct` Int, `AppearanceRowHeightPct` Int, `AppearanceDecorations` Str, `AppearanceRoundedCorners` Bool, `AppearanceHeatColoring` Bool, `AppearanceHeatIntensityPct` Int, `AppearanceShadowIntensityPct` Int.
- `[motion]`: `MotionAnimations` Bool, `MotionSmoothGraphs` Bool, `MotionSmoothScroll` Bool, `MotionSmoothScrollAmount` Int, `MotionTabSwitchMs` Int.
- `[units]`: `UnitsNetwork` Str, `UnitsNetworkAutoScale` Bool.
- `[processes]`: `ProcessesIntervalMs` Int, `ProcessesMode` Str, `ProcessesTreeGuideLines` Bool, `ProcessesHighlightNewExited` Bool, `ProcessesFilterIncludeChildren` Bool, `ProcessesHideSystem` Bool, `ProcessesSubtreeTotals` Bool, `ProcessesDumpType` Str.
- `[tables]`: `TablesColumnResize` Str, `TablesColumnSeparators` Bool, `TablesDimZeroValues` Bool.
- `[properties]`: `PropertiesHideUnnamedHandles` Bool, `PropertiesSharedObjectsOnly` Bool, `PropertiesEnvMask` Bool.
- `[performance]`: `PerformanceGraphRangeS` Int, `PerformanceCpuGraphMode` Str, `PerformanceCpuKernel` Bool, `PerformanceCpuSecondaryGraph` Str, `PerformanceGpuOptionalGraphs` StrList, `PerformanceHiddenGpuEngines` StrList, `PerformanceMemoryComposition` Bool, `PerformanceMemorySwapGraph` Bool, `PerformanceShowDisks` Bool, `PerformanceShowGpus` Bool, `PerformanceShowFans` Bool, `PerformanceShowBatteries` Bool, `PerformanceShowNetworkWired` Bool, `PerformanceShowNetworkWireless` Bool, `PerformanceShowNetworkVpn` Bool, `PerformanceShowNetworkVirtual` Bool, `PerformanceShowNetworkOther` Bool, `PerformanceShowDisconnectedFans` Bool, `PerformanceDeviceOrder` StrList, `PerformanceDeviceOverrides` Map, `PerformanceCurvedLines` Bool, `PerformanceNetworkDynamicScale` Bool.
- `[fans]`: `Fans` Map.
- `[graphs]`: `GraphsMinigraphCpu` Bool, `GraphsMinigraphMemory` Bool, `GraphsMinigraphDisk` Bool, `GraphsMinigraphNetwork` Bool, `GraphsMinigraphGpu` Bool, `GraphsMinigraphVram` Bool, `GraphsMinigraphGpuTemperature` Bool, `GraphsKeepDetachedOnClose` Bool.
- `[history]`: `HistoryEnabled` Bool, `HistoryRetentionH` Int, `HistoryPersist` Bool, `HistoryMaxDiskMb` Int.
- `[window]`: `WindowCloseWithEsc` Bool, `WindowAlwaysOnTop` Bool.
- `[tray]`: `TrayCloseToTray` Bool, `TrayMinimizeToTray` Bool, `TrayAlwaysShow` Bool.
- `[startup]`: `StartupStartAtLogin` Bool, `StartupStartMinimized` Bool.
- `[network]`: `NetworkAutoFetchPublicIp` Bool, `NetworkPublicIpNoticeAccepted` Bool.
- `[privilege]`: `PrivilegeUnlockAtLaunch` Bool, `PrivilegePasswordless` Bool.
- `[rendering]`: `RenderingGpu` Str.
- `[services]`: `ServicesUnitTypes` StrList, `ServicesFilterStates` StrList.
- `[lowmem]`: `LowmemEnabled` Bool.
- `[debug]`: `DebugShowFps` Bool.

Rules:
- Init: `TlSettings::init(cx)` takes `settings`, `state` and `persist.take()` from the `BootSettings` Global (E16-A1), clones settings and state, sets every version to 1 and `state_version` to 1, and installs `TlSettings`. `BootSettings` stays installed (E17-007 reads it until it switches to `TlSettings`). Add one line `settings_global::TlSettings::init(cx);` in `crates/tl-ui/src/app.rs` `TasklensUi::init` directly after the step that installs `BootSettings` (chain edit of E16's file, one line).
- `update` and `preview`: clone `data.settings` and `data.state` before `f` (user actions only; never called per frame), run `f`, then `Settings::clamp()` and `UiState::clamp()` (E03-067; log returned keys with `debug!(target: "tasklens::settings", key, "clamped")`). Compare each section struct before and after with `PartialEq`; bump `versions[s] += 1` for each changed one. If `state` changed, `state_version += 1`. If nothing changed, do nothing else (no persist, no engine call, no window refresh).
- `update` only: call `persist(&settings, &state)` once (tl-app debounces 500 ms, ADR-011). Compute `EngineSettings::from(&old)` and `EngineSettings::from(&new)`; if they differ call `cx.global::<EngineGlobal>().0.set_settings(new)`.
- A change of `general.language` inside `update` or `preview` calls `i18n::set_language(cx, &new.general.language)` (UI-SHL-131) after the versions are bumped.
- Observers use `cx.observe_global::<TlSettings>(..)` and compare `version(section)` against the value they last drew; they `cx.notify()` only on a difference. The global is replaced through `cx.update_global`, so observers fire once per `update`.
- `toggle(key)`: `kind() == Bool` flips the field; else `warn!(target: "tasklens::settings", key = key.as_str(), "toggle on non-bool key")` and no change. Goes through `update`.
- `set(key, value)`: Bool to Bool fields; Int to integer fields (cast with `try_from`; out of type range: warn, no change; in range: assigned, then `clamp` applies); Str to `String` fields as is, and to enum fields by parsing the serde name (`"tree"` for `TableMode::Tree`, `"server"` for `Decorations::Server`) with `serde::Deserialize` through `serde::de::IntoDeserializer` on the `&str`; StrList to `Vec<String>` fields and to enum lists by the same parse per item. `Map` keys reject `set` (warn, no change): the windows that edit `fans` and `performance.device_overrides` call `update` directly. Kind mismatch: warn, no change. Goes through `update`.
- `animations_on(cx)`: `settings.motion.animations && !cx.reduce_motion()`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `BootSettings` with `ui_scale_pct = 125` **When** `TlSettings::init` runs **Then** `TlSettings::settings(cx).appearance.ui_scale_pct == 125` and every section version is 1.
- **Given** an installed `TlSettings` **When** `update` sets `motion.animations = false` **Then** only `version(Section::Motion)` goes from 1 to 2, the persist callback ran once and `set_settings` was not called.
- **Given** an installed `TlSettings` **When** `update` sets `processes.hide_system = true` **Then** `version(Section::Processes)` bumps and the fake engine received one `set_settings` with `hide_system == true`.
- **Given** an `update` that writes the same value a field already has **When** it runs **Then** no version changes and persist is not called.
- **Given** `preview` sets `appearance.ui_scale_pct = 150` **When** it runs **Then** the Appearance version bumps, persist is not called, and a following `update` with the same value calls persist once.
- **Given** `update` sets `ui_scale_pct = 203` **When** it runs **Then** the stored value is 200 (clamped).
- **Given** `toggle(SettingKey::WindowCloseWithEsc)` **When** run twice **Then** the value is back to false and persist ran twice.
- **Given** `toggle(SettingKey::ProcessesMode)` (a Str key) **When** run **Then** nothing changes and a warning is logged.
- **Given** `set(SettingKey::ProcessesMode, SettingValue::Str("tree".into()))` **When** run **Then** `processes.mode == TableMode::Tree`; with `"sideways"` nothing changes.
- **Given** `set(SettingKey::Fans, ..)` **When** run **Then** nothing changes and a warning is logged.
- **Given** `SettingKey::ALL` **When** mapped with `as_str` **Then** it yields 85 distinct dotted names in table (a) order, the first `"general.start_tab"` and the last `"debug.show_fps"`.
- **Given** `update` changes the `UiState` field `tabs.last_tab` **When** it runs **Then** `state_version` bumps, no settings section version changes and persist runs once.
- **Given** `motion.animations = true` and `cx.reduce_motion()` true **When** `animations_on(cx)` runs **Then** it is false.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/settings_global.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/lib.rs`: `pub mod settings_global;` (chain edit).
- `crates/tl-ui/src/app.rs`: one `TlSettings::init(cx);` line (chain edit of E16's file).
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`: create (E20 owns it) with the tests below.

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs` (`#[gpui_kit::test]`, FakeEngine from `testing/fake_engine.rs`):
- `settings_init_from_boot`: criterion 1.
- `settings_update_bumps_only_changed_section`: criterion 2.
- `settings_engine_fields_sent`: criterion 3.
- `settings_noop_update_does_nothing`: criterion 4.
- `settings_preview_does_not_persist`: criterion 5.
- `settings_update_clamps`: criterion 6.
- `settings_toggle_bool_and_reject_non_bool`: criteria 7 and 8.
- `settings_set_enum_by_serde_name`: criterion 9.
- `settings_set_rejects_map_key`: criterion 10.
- `setting_key_all_matches_table_a`: criterion 11; also asserts `section()` of each key equals the prefix of `as_str()` before the first dot.
- `settings_state_update_persists`: criterion 12.
- `animations_on_respects_reduce_motion`: criterion 13 (`cx.set_reduce_motion(true)` in the test context).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: bad kinds or values log `warn!` and change nothing; no user text.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: `animations_on` is the single reduced-motion gate for every shell animation (R-017).
- Performance: writes happen on user actions only. The before/after clone is a few kilobytes; never call `update` from `render` or per frame.
- Privacy: never log setting values; log only dotted key names (ADR-015).

## Notes
- `Settings`, `UiState`, `EngineSettings`, `TableMode`, `Decorations` and the other enums come from `tl_model::settings` (E03-065 to E03-067, anchor E03-A2). Field names are the table (a) key names.
- `BootSettings`, `EngineGlobal` come from `crates/tl-ui/src/app.rs` (E16-A1). `i18n::set_language` from E16-002.
- `cx.reduce_motion()` is the gpui-kit `base::reduce_motion` accessor (shell.md conventions). If the method name differs in gpui-kit 0.7.0, use the kit function it wraps and keep `animations_on` as the only caller.
- The `ToggleSetting` and `SetSetting` Actions are declared in `actions.rs` by E20-002, which registers handlers that call `toggle` and `set`.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_shell`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- crates/tl-ui/src/settings_global.rs crates/tl-ui/src/lib.rs crates/tl-ui/src/app.rs crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs` (run `git add` on new files first). Never a bare `git commit`.
- Read `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` in the repo first.

title: E20-028 Close decision row 2: keep detached graph windows
description:
## Context
Adds row 2 of the close decision: when "Keep detached graphs open when the main window closes" is on and at least one detached graph window is open, closing the main window removes it but keeps the app running; the app quits when the last detached graph window closes (unless the main window was reopened). Phase P3, with detached graph windows (E26). Sources: UI-SHL-113 (row 2), APP-045, APP-047, PERF-084, canonical table (a) `graphs.keep_detached_on_close`.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`:
- At the `// close decision: row 2, keep detached graphs (E20-028)` comment in `close_decision` (E20-A1): `if settings.graphs.keep_detached_on_close && registry.has_key(|k| matches!(k, WindowKey::DetachedGraph(_))) { return CloseOutcome::RemoveWindow; }` (`WindowRegistry::has_key` from E16-A2, R-218).
- Quit after the last detached window: when `apply_close(RemoveWindow)` ran because of row 2, observe the `WindowRegistry` entity (`cx.observe`; the registry calls `cx.notify()` on every insert and removal, R-218) from a small app-level task stored in a `DetachedWatch` Global. On each notification: if `ShellState.main_window` is `None`, no `DetachedGraph(_)` key remains, and `tray_available(cx)` is false, call `request_exit(cx, UiExit::Quit)`. Drop the watch when the main window is reopened.
- Row 1 (tray) stays first: E31-009 inserts it above this row.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `keep_detached_on_close = true` and one detached graph window open **When** `CloseWindow` is dispatched **Then** the main window is removed, the detached window stays and the app keeps running.
- **Given** that state **When** the last detached graph window closes **Then** the app exits with `UiExit::Quit`.
- **Given** that state **When** `ShowMainWindow` reopens the main window and then the detached window closes **Then** the app keeps running.
- **Given** `keep_detached_on_close = false` and a detached window open **When** `CloseWindow` is dispatched **Then** the app quits (row 3) and the detached window closes with it.
- **Given** `keep_detached_on_close = true` and no detached window **When** `CloseWindow` is dispatched **Then** the app quits.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`: row 2 and the watch.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`: tests (register a test window under `WindowKey::DetachedGraph(0)` in the registry).

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`:
- `close_keeps_app_with_detached_graph`: criterion 1.
- `last_detached_close_quits`: criterion 2.
- `reopen_cancels_detached_watch`: criterion 3.
- `close_quits_without_keep_setting`: criterion 4.
- `close_quits_without_detached_windows`: criterion 5.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one registry observation while the main window is removed; demand drops to detached graphs (hub hidden rule, ADR-008).
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- `WindowRegistry`, `WindowKey::DetachedGraph`, `GlobalRegistry`, `has_key` and the notify on insert and removal are E16-A2 (R-218). E26-018 wraps the same query as `any_detached_open(cx)` and depends on this bead.

title: E20-029 ToggleAlwaysOnTop for secondary windows through the KWin bridge
description:
## Context
The pin caption button of every secondary window (Settings, Properties, About and the others) dispatches `ToggleAlwaysOnTop { window, caption }` (E16-008). E20-022 handles only the main window. This bead adds the arm for every other `WindowKey`: it asks the KWin bridge to keep that window above others, found by the tasklens pid and the window caption. Secondary windows keep the pin state in memory only (R-073). There is no X11 keep-above in v1 (R-177). Sources: UI-FND-021 (pin), UI-SHL-005, R-073, R-176 (OI-U06), R-177 (OI-U07), PERF-083 (windows found by pid and caption). Phase P2.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`, in the `ToggleAlwaysOnTop` handler that E20-022 registered in `window::main::init`, replace the "any other `WindowKey`" return with:
- When `keep_above_supported(cx)` is false: do nothing (the pin is already drawn disabled with tooltip "Not supported by this desktop" by E16-008).
- Else: `on = !pinned` where `pinned` is the entry for `window` in `ShellState.secondary_pins: FxHashMap<WindowKey, bool>` (missing = false); store `on`; send `Command::KWin(KWinCommand::KeepAbove { pid: std::process::id(), caption: Some(caption.to_string()), on })` through `EngineGlobal`. Nothing is written to settings or state (R-073).
- Add the field `secondary_pins: FxHashMap<WindowKey, bool>` to `ShellState`; remove a key's entry when `WindowRegistry` no longer holds that key (observe the registry entity; it notifies on every removal, R-218).
- `Command::KWin` returning `Err(CommandError::Busy)`: log `warn!(target: "tasklens::ui", "keep above not sent")` and keep the stored state; no toast (UI-SHL-005).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the KWin bridge is up and a Settings window titled "Settings" **When** its pin dispatches `ToggleAlwaysOnTop { window: WindowKey::Settings, caption: "Settings" }` **Then** the fake engine received `KWin(KeepAbove { pid: <own pid>, caption: Some("Settings"), on: true })` and no setting changed.
- **Given** the same window pinned **When** the pin is dispatched again **Then** `KeepAbove { on: false, .. }` is sent.
- **Given** windows validity `Unsupported` **When** a secondary-window pin is dispatched **Then** nothing is sent.
- **Given** a pinned Settings window **When** it closes and opens again **Then** its next pin dispatch sends `on: true`.
- **Given** `WindowKey::Main` **When** dispatched **Then** E20-022's main-window arm runs unchanged.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`: the handler arm, the `secondary_pins` field on `ShellState` (declared in this file by E20-008) and its cleanup.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`: tests.

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`:
- `secondary_pin_sends_keep_above_with_caption`: criteria 1 and 2.
- `secondary_pin_unsupported_sends_nothing`: criterion 3.
- `secondary_pin_forgotten_on_close`: criterion 4.
- `main_pin_unchanged`: criterion 5.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: a failed KWin command is logged; no toast (UI-SHL-005).
- Validity: availability from `Snapshot.windows.header.validity` through `keep_above_supported` (E20-004).
- Accessibility: the pin tooltip states the state in text (E16-008).
- Performance: one map lookup per click.
- Privacy: the caption is a tasklens window title; it holds no process data.

## Notes
- `ToggleAlwaysOnTop { window: WindowKey, caption: SharedString }` and `WindowKey::Main` come from E16-008 (tasklens-fut.12); the pin in `components/window_frame.rs` already passes the exact window title as `caption`, so this bead does not edit that file.
- `KWinCommand::KeepAbove` and the bridge are E14-A2 (tasklens-y6k.2).
- `window/main.rs` is shared by chain edits; edit only the handler arm and the cleanup.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_shell`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`. Never a bare `git commit`.

title: E20-002 Window-level Actions and bind_keys_global (actions.rs)
description:
## Context
Declares every window-level GPUI Action of the shell in one file and binds the Global key context rows of canonical table (b). Menus (E21), toolbar buttons, the tray bridge (E31) and other epics dispatch these Actions, so they must exist before any of those compile. One command is one Action; a menu item, a button and a key dispatch the same one (widgets rule 10). Handlers live with the code that owns the behaviour; this bead registers only the two generic setting handlers. Phase P0 (the P0 main window uses them). Sources: UI-SHL-120 (binding table), canonical table (b) Global rows, R-045, R-128 (one namespace `tasklens`), R-136, D-008, shell.md conventions (Actions, two generic setting actions), INDEX.md "Actions", B5 open items 26 and 27.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/actions.rs` (create; add `pub mod actions;` to `crates/tl-ui/src/lib.rs`):

Unit Actions, `actions!(tasklens, [..])`:
`NextTab`, `PrevTab`, `OpenRunDialog`, `OpenHandleSearch`, `Quit`, `CloseWindow`, `MinimizeWindow`, `ZoomWindow`, `OpenSettings`, `OpenShortcuts`, `FocusFilter`, `ClearFilter`, `FilterEscape`, `FilterAccept`, `RefreshCurrentTab`, `EscapeChain`, `ScaleUp`, `ScaleDown`, `ScaleReset`, `ToggleMiniWindow`, `StartWindowPick`, `CancelWindowPick`, `ToggleHideSystem`, `CycleViewMode`, `ToggleHistoryMode`, `OpenCollectorHealth`, `ShowSystemInformation`, `ShowMainWindow`, `ToggleMainWindow`.

Data Actions, each `#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug, Action)] #[action(namespace = tasklens, no_json)]`:
```rust
pub struct SelectTab(pub usize);                 // index into tl_model::command::Tab::ALL (0 = Processes .. 5 = Information)
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub enum MenuId { File, View, Settings, Help, Debug }
pub struct OpenMenu(pub MenuId);
pub struct SetViewMode(pub TableMode);           // tl_model TableMode: Grouped, Tree, Flat
pub struct ToggleSetting(pub SettingKey);        // settings_global (E20-001)
pub struct SetSetting { pub key: SettingKey, pub value: SettingValue }
```

Not declared here (declared by their owners; do not declare them again, GPUI fails on duplicate names in one namespace): `StartHelperSession`, `EndHelperSession` (E16-010 `components/shield.rs`), `ToggleAlwaysOnTop { window: WindowKey }` and `CloseSecondaryWindow` (E16-008 `components/window_frame.rs`), `OpenProperties` and the other table Actions (E18 `table/actions.rs`), `ActivateTheme` (E17 `theme/store.rs`), page Actions (each page's `actions.rs`). A doc comment at the top of the file lists these owners.

```rust
pub fn bind_keys_global(cx: &mut App);          // the bindings below
pub fn register_global_handlers(cx: &mut App);  // ToggleSetting -> TlSettings::toggle, SetSetting -> TlSettings::set
```

Bindings (`KeyBinding::new(keys, action, Some(context))`), context "Global" unless stated:

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `ctrl-1` .. `ctrl-6`, `alt-1` .. `alt-6` | `SelectTab(0)` .. `SelectTab(5)` |
| `ctrl-tab` / `ctrl-shift-tab` | `NextTab` / `PrevTab` |
| `ctrl-n` | `OpenRunDialog` |
| `ctrl-q` | `Quit` |
| `ctrl-w` | `CloseWindow` |
| `ctrl-,` | `OpenSettings` |
| `ctrl-?` and `ctrl-shift-/` | `OpenShortcuts` |
| `f10` | `OpenMenu(MenuId::File)` |
| `alt-f` / `alt-v` / `alt-s` / `alt-h` / `alt-d` | `OpenMenu(File / View / Settings / Help / Debug)` |
| `ctrl-f` | `FocusFilter` |
| `f5` | `RefreshCurrentTab` |
| `escape` | `EscapeChain` |
| `ctrl-=`, `ctrl-+`, `ctrl-shift-=` | `ScaleUp` |
| `ctrl--` | `ScaleDown` |
| `ctrl-0` | `ScaleReset` |
| `ctrl-shift-m` | `ToggleMiniWindow` |
| `escape` in context "Picker" | `CancelWindowPick` |
| `escape` in context "ShellFilter" | `FilterEscape` |
| `enter`, `down` in context "ShellFilter" | `FilterAccept` |

Every binding is registered now, in P0, including those whose handlers arrive in later phases (an Action with no handler does nothing). "ShellFilter" is the key context the filter box (E20-009) sets on its input; "Picker" is pushed while window picking runs (E20-027).

Wiring: in `crates/tl-ui/src/app.rs` `TasklensUi::init`, at the `// bind_keys_*` comment, add `actions::bind_keys_global(cx); actions::register_global_handlers(cx);` (chain edit of E16's file, one line). `bind_keys_global` runs before any menu is built.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `bind_keys_global` ran **When** the keystroke `ctrl-3` is resolved in context "Global" **Then** it maps to `SelectTab(2)`.
- **Given** the bindings **When** each Global row of the table above is resolved **Then** it maps to the listed Action (every row, both spellings for `OpenShortcuts` and all three for `ScaleUp`).
- **Given** context stack "Global" > "Picker" **When** `escape` is resolved **Then** the Action is `CancelWindowPick`, and with only "Global" it is `EscapeChain`.
- **Given** context stack "Global" > "ShellFilter" **When** `escape`, `enter` and `down` are resolved **Then** they map to `FilterEscape`, `FilterAccept` and `FilterAccept`.
- **Given** `register_global_handlers` ran **When** `ToggleSetting(SettingKey::WindowCloseWithEsc)` is dispatched **Then** `window.close_with_esc` becomes true.
- **Given** `register_global_handlers` ran **When** `SetSetting { key: SettingKey::ProcessesMode, value: SettingValue::Str("flat".into()) }` is dispatched **Then** `processes.mode == TableMode::Flat`.
- **Given** the crate **When** it compiles with E16's `components/shield.rs` and `components/window_frame.rs` present **Then** no duplicate Action name error occurs (this file declares none of their names).

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/actions.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/lib.rs`: `pub mod actions;` (chain edit).
- `crates/tl-ui/src/app.rs`: one line at `// bind_keys_*` (chain edit).
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_keymap.rs`: create (E20 owns it).

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_keymap.rs` (`#[gpui_kit::test]`):
- `keymap_matches_table_b`: a data table of (keys, context stack, expected Action) for every Global row of table (b) above; each resolves to the expected Action (use the keymap lookup GPUI exposes, `cx.bindings_for_action` or `Keymap::bindings_for_input` with the context stack). E20-A2 extends this test with the filter-focused run (U-45); page owners test their own contexts.
- `picker_escape_wins_over_global`: criterion 3.
- `shell_filter_keys`: criterion 4.
- `toggle_setting_action_flips_key`: criterion 5.
- `set_setting_action_writes_enum`: criterion 6.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: every chrome command has a key or a menu path (R-108); this table is the key half.
- Performance: bindings are registered once at init.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- `actions!` and `#[derive(Action)]` with `#[action(namespace = .., no_json)]` are gpui-pre 0.3.7 (`src/action.rs`); gpui-kit re-exports them. `no_json` is used because `SettingValue` holds `SharedString`, and it keeps every shell data Action free of `schemars`. Bindings take the Action value directly, so no JSON is needed.
- `RefreshCurrentTab` is the shell's F5 Action. shell.md UI-SHL-120 writes `RefreshNow`; the E27 and E28 beads already compile against `RefreshCurrentTab`, and `RefreshNow` is also the name of an engine `Command` variant, so this bead uses `RefreshCurrentTab` (listed as an open item in `docs/plan/b7-ui-shell.md`).
- `ShowSystemInformation` is the Help menu target (UI-SYS-096 name; shell.md UI-SHL-041 writes `OpenSystemInformation`). E28 handles it.
- `SetViewMode`, `CycleViewMode`, `ToggleHideSystem` are handled by E20-017; `ToggleHistoryMode` by E20-025; `OpenCollectorHealth` by E21-007; `OpenSettings` by E21-018; `OpenShortcuts` by E21-016; `OpenRunDialog` and `OpenHandleSearch` by E23; `ToggleMiniWindow` by E26; `Quit`, `CloseWindow`, `MinimizeWindow`, `ZoomWindow`, `ShowMainWindow`, `ToggleMainWindow` by E20-A1; `SelectTab`, `NextTab`, `PrevTab`, `RefreshCurrentTab` by E20-008.
- Check the kit keymap for `alt-` bindings in the "Input" context that would shadow `alt-f` while the filter has focus; record what you find in the bead's closing comment (U-45 is settled by E20-A2).
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_keymap`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- crates/tl-ui/src/actions.rs crates/tl-ui/src/lib.rs crates/tl-ui/src/app.rs crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_keymap.rs`. Never a bare `git commit`.
- Read `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` in the repo first.
close_reason: actions.rs: 29 unit Actions, SelectTab/OpenMenu/SetViewMode/ToggleSetting/SetSetting (no_json), bind_keys_global (table (b) Global, Picker, ShellFilter rows, plus bind_keys_components), register_global_handlers; wired in TasklensUi::init (replaces the direct bind_keys_components call; kv_grid::init kept). Tests tests/ui_keymap.rs 6 pass. Kit keymap check: gpui-base Input binds no alt-<letter> on Linux (only alt-backspace/alt-delete/alt-left/right on macOS and shift-alt-up/down), so alt-f is not shadowed while the filter has focus. Input does bind escape, enter and down in context Input. Commit b1da865.

comments.text: Leader: bind_keys_global must also call tl_ui::components::checkbox::bind_keys_components(cx). It binds the checkbox, radio and slider keys (ug9.12, ug9.22, ug9.23). Add a test that a TlSlider gets arrow keys after bind_keys_global.

title: E20-003 Toolbar slot: ToolbarContent, ToolbarModel and Toolbar (toolbar.rs)
description:
## Context
Builds the toolbar row that sits inside the title bar (UI-SHL-003 part 7): a `ToolbarContent` trait each page epic implements for its own buttons (slots 2 and 3), the `ToolbarModel` the title bar keeps current, and the `Toolbar` element that lays the slots out with the measured 24 px buttons and 7 px gap. Slot 1 (shield, P3) and slot 4 (window picker, P3) are drawn by the shell itself and are added by E20-026 and E20-027; in P0 to P2 they take no space. Phase P0 (the P0 title bar renders it). Sources: UI-SHL-010, UI-SHL-003, APP-002, R-031, R-108, PERF-014, PROC-016, 00-epics section 2 (`window/main.rs` holds one `ToolbarContent` registration per page epic).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/window/toolbar.rs` (create; add `pub mod toolbar;` to `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`, chain edit of E16's file):

```rust
pub const TOOLBAR_BUTTON: f32 = 24.0;   // × ui_scale
pub const TOOLBAR_GAP: f32 = 7.0;       // × ui_scale; pitch 31 measured
pub const TOOLBAR_ICON: f32 = 16.0;     // i_md

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub struct ToolbarModel {
    pub tab: Tab,                       // tl_model::command::Tab
    pub history_mode: bool,             // UiState.processes.history_mode
    pub hide_system: bool,              // settings.processes.hide_system
    pub mode: TableMode,                // settings.processes.mode
    pub helper: HelperState,            // HealthSnapshot.helper (Missing before P3)
    pub helper_installed: bool,         // /usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper exists (checked once at startup by E20-026; false until then)
    pub picker_available: bool,         // Snapshot.windows.header.validity != Unsupported
    pub picking: bool,
    pub window_active: bool,
}

/// One per page epic that has page buttons. Registered in `window/main.rs` (`toolbar_for`).
pub trait ToolbarContent: 'static {
    /// Page buttons for slots 2 and 3, left to right, at most 2. Build them with `toolbar_toggle` / `toolbar_icon`.
    fn buttons(&self, model: &ToolbarModel, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App) -> SmallVec<[AnyElement; 2]>;
}
pub struct DefaultToolbar;                                 // no page buttons; used for every tab without a registration
impl ToolbarContent for DefaultToolbar { /* returns an empty SmallVec */ }

/// A toolbar Toggle button: TlButton::Toggle { on }, 24 × 24, icon i_md, `.tab_stop(false)`,
/// tooltip with the Action's key hint, icon colour text_secondary when !model.window_active.
pub fn toolbar_toggle(id: impl Into<ElementId>, icon: TlIcon, on: bool, tooltip: SharedString,
                      action: Box<dyn Action>, model: &ToolbarModel) -> TlButton;
/// A toolbar Icon button: TlButton::Icon, same sizes and rules. `disabled` keeps its tooltip.
pub fn toolbar_icon(id: impl Into<ElementId>, icon: TlIcon, tooltip: SharedString, action: Box<dyn Action>,
                    disabled: bool, model: &ToolbarModel) -> TlButton;

#[derive(IntoElement)]
pub struct Toolbar { model: ToolbarModel, page: SmallVec<[AnyElement; 2]>, shield: Option<AnyElement>, picker: Option<AnyElement> }
impl Toolbar {
    pub fn new(model: ToolbarModel, page: SmallVec<[AnyElement; 2]>) -> Self;
    pub fn shield(self, el: Option<AnyElement>) -> Self;   // slot 1, set by E20-026
    pub fn picker(self, el: Option<AnyElement>) -> Self;   // slot 4, set by E20-027
}
impl RenderOnce for Toolbar { /* h_flex, items centred, gap TOOLBAR_GAP × s: [shield?][page..][picker?] */ }
```

Rules:
- Order left to right: slot 1 shield, slots 2 and 3 page buttons, slot 4 picker. An absent slot takes no space (`.when(..)`, never `.invisible()`), so the drag area grows (PROC-016).
- The row is vertically centred in the 34 px title bar; height 24 × `ui_scale`.
- Toolbar buttons are not Tab stops (R-108). Clicks dispatch the button's Action; mouse-down calls `cx.stop_propagation()` and `window.prevent_default()` so it never starts a title bar drag (UI-SHL-004).
- Tooltips use `TlTooltip` with the 500 ms delay and the key hint of the Action when it has a binding.
- The page content decides its own buttons and their disabled state from `ToolbarModel` (for example the view-mode cycler disabled in History mode, owned by E22).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a `Toolbar` with a test content returning two buttons **When** it renders at `ui_scale_pct = 100` **Then** it has two 24 × 24 children with centres 31 px apart.
- **Given** `DefaultToolbar` and no shield or picker **When** the toolbar renders **Then** it has zero children and zero width.
- **Given** `toolbar_toggle(.., on: true, ..)` **When** rendered **Then** it uses the TlButton Toggle on look and is not focusable with Tab.
- **Given** `toolbar_icon(.., disabled: true, ..)` **When** hovered **Then** the tooltip still shows and a click dispatches nothing.
- **Given** `model.window_active = false` **When** a toolbar button renders **Then** its icon colour is `text_secondary`.
- **Given** a mouse-down on a toolbar button followed by a mouse move **When** handled **Then** `start_window_move` is not called.
- **Given** `ui_scale_pct = 150` **When** the two-button toolbar renders **Then** the buttons are 36 × 36 with centres 46.5 px apart.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/toolbar.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`: `pub mod toolbar;` (chain edit).
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`: add the tests below.

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`:
- `toolbar_two_page_buttons_pitch`: criterion 1.
- `toolbar_default_is_empty`: criterion 2.
- `toolbar_toggle_not_tab_stop`: criterion 3.
- `toolbar_disabled_keeps_tooltip`: criterion 4.
- `toolbar_inactive_icon_colour`: criterion 5.
- `toolbar_button_no_drag`: criterion 6.
- `toolbar_scales`: criterion 7.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: buttons are not Tab stops (R-108); every command they run also has a key or menu path. The tooltip text is each button's accessible name.
- Performance: at most four buttons; no allocation beyond the element tree; tooltip strings are `SharedString` constants.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- `TlButton`, `TlButtonKind`, `TlTooltip`, `TlIcon` come from E15 (anchor E15-A1). If `TlIcon` has no colour setter, set the colour the way E15-005's icon API documents it and say so in the closing comment.
- `HelperState` is `tl_model::health::HelperState`; `TableMode` is `tl_model::table::TableMode`; `Tab` is `tl_model::command::Tab`.
- The per-tab registration function `toolbar_for(tab) -> Box<dyn ToolbarContent>` lives in `window/main.rs` (E20-008), where page epics add one arm each (E22 for Processes).
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_shell`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- crates/tl-ui/src/window/toolbar.rs crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`. Never a bare `git commit`.
- Read `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` in the repo first.
close_reason: toolbar.rs: ToolbarModel, ToolbarContent, DefaultToolbar, toolbar_toggle, toolbar_icon, Toolbar (slots wrapped so mouse-down stops propagation and prevents default). pub mod toolbar in window/mod.rs. title: E20-004 Title bar: drag region, caption buttons and menu bar slot (titlebar.rs, U-44)
description:
## Context
Builds the client-drawn title bar of the main window: app icon, the slot where E21 installs the menu bar, the toolbar, the drag area and the caption buttons (minimize, maximize or restore, close), with the TaskSlinger layout measured from the reference images. tasklens draws its own caption buttons and drag logic unless gpui-kit 0.7.0's `TitleBar` can hide its controls; this bead checks that and records U-44. The pin caption button is P2 (E20-022) and the server-decorations row is E20-014. Phase P0 (the phase-0 CSD checklist drags, double-clicks and resizes this bar). Sources: UI-SHL-003, UI-SHL-004, UI-SHL-005 (minimize, maximize, close), UI-SHL-007, APP-001, APP-002, APP-008, D-006, R-031, R-108, R-125, U-44, ADR-010 (CSD checklist).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/window/titlebar.rs` (create; add `pub mod titlebar;` to `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`, chain edit):

```rust
pub const TITLEBAR_H: f32 = 34.0;          // × ui_scale
pub const CAPTION_W: f32 = 36.0;           // main window caption buttons (secondary windows keep the kit's 34)

/// Slot for the menu bar. E21-A1 sets it in `menubar::init` before the main window opens.
pub struct MenuBarFactory(pub fn(&mut Window, &mut App) -> AnyView);
impl Global for MenuBarFactory {}

pub struct TitleBarView {
    menu_bar: Option<AnyView>,               // created once in `new` from MenuBarFactory, None when the global is absent
    model: ToolbarModel,                     // E20-003
    content: Box<dyn ToolbarContent>,        // the active tab's page buttons
    drag: DragState,                         // should_move flag
    _subs: SmallVec<[Subscription; 4]>,
}
impl TitleBarView {
    pub fn new(window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> Self;
    pub fn set_toolbar(&mut self, model: ToolbarModel, content: Box<dyn ToolbarContent>, cx: &mut Context<Self>); // notify only if model or tab changed
    pub fn set_model(&mut self, model: ToolbarModel, cx: &mut Context<Self>);                                     // notify only if changed
}
impl Render for TitleBarView { .. }

/// True when the pin can work: Snapshot.windows.header.validity is Valid or Stale (KWin bridge up).
pub fn keep_above_supported(cx: &App) -> bool;

/// The Minimize caption button's behaviour. E20-A1's `MinimizeWindow` handler calls it.
pub fn minimize_main(window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App);
```

Layout under `Decorations::Client { .. }` (sizes × `ui_scale`, hairlines 1 physical px), background `titlebar`, height 34, left to right:
1. Left padding 12.
2. App icon 16 × 16, SVG `icons/tasklens.svg` from `TlAssets` (E15-022), vertically centred. Mouse-down propagates (drag part).
3. Gap 8.
4. Menu bar slot: `self.menu_bar` when present (E21 draws the buttons, separators and popups).
5. Gap 4.
6. `Toolbar::new(self.model.clone(), self.content.buttons(&self.model, window, cx))` (E20-003). Slots 1 and 4 are added by E20-026 and E20-027.
7. Drag area: `flex_1()`, minimum width 24, empty.
8. Caption buttons, flush right, no gap, each `CAPTION_W` 36 × 34: minimize (Lucide `minus`, tooltip "Minimize", dispatches `MinimizeWindow`), maximize (Lucide `square`, tooltip "Maximize"; when `window.is_maximized()` Lucide `copy` and tooltip "Restore"; dispatches `ZoomWindow`), close (Lucide `x`, tooltip "Close", dispatches `CloseWindow`). Icons 16, colour `text_primary` when the window is active, `text_secondary` when not. Default background transparent; hover `tab_hover`; close hover `status.danger` with a white (`#FFFFFF`) icon; pressed: the hover background at opacity 0.8. Minimize and maximize are hidden (not disabled) when `window.window_controls().minimize` or `.maximize` is false. The pin cell is added left of minimize by E20-022.

Drag handling (UI-SHL-004), `fn drag_handlers(..)` in this file:
- Left mouse-down on a drag part (padding, icon, gaps, drag area) sets `should_move = true`; the next mouse move calls `window.start_window_move()` and clears it; mouse-up clears it.
- Double-click (click count 2) on a drag part calls `window.zoom_window()`.
- Right-click on a drag part calls `window.show_window_menu(event.position)`.
- Menu, toolbar and caption buttons call `cx.stop_propagation()` and `window.prevent_default()` on mouse-down, so they never drag. Right-click and middle-click on them do nothing.
- The cursor stays the default arrow everywhere on the bar.
- U-44: read gpui-kit 0.7.0 `title_bar.rs` (around lines 326 to 396). If `TitleBar` has a switch that hides its own window controls, build on `TitleBar::new()` with that switch; otherwise use a plain `h_flex` with the copied drag logic above (about 60 lines). Append one sentence to the U-44 row of the "Unverified assumptions" table in `docs/RECONCILIATION.md`: "Verified by <bead id>: <what you found and which path you used>."

`minimize_main(window, cx)`: the first line is the comment `// minimize rule (E31-009): the minimize-to-tray check goes here, before minimize_window`; then `window.minimize_window()`.

Re-render: `TitleBarView` subscribes in `new` to window activation (`cx.observe_window_activation`), window bounds (for the maximized flip, notify only when `is_maximized()` changed), `TlSettings` sections `window` and `debug` (version compare), and the hub's `SnapshotChanged` with `ComponentMask::WINDOWS` where it notifies only when `keep_above_supported` flipped. No other snapshot work.

Under `Decorations::Server` this bead renders the same parts 1 to 6 in a 34 px row with no drag handlers and no caption buttons; E20-014 replaces that branch with the 28 px menu row.

Strings (`assets/locales/en-US.ftl`, chain edit): `shell-titlebar-minimize = Minimize`, `shell-titlebar-maximize = Maximize`, `shell-titlebar-restore = Restore`, `shell-titlebar-close = Close`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** client decorations, a test `MenuBarFactory` view and a toolbar content with two buttons **When** the title bar renders at 1360 px width **Then** its children in order are icon, menu bar slot, toolbar, drag area, minimize, maximize, close, and its height is 34.
- **Given** no `MenuBarFactory` global **When** the title bar renders **Then** it renders without the slot and does not panic.
- **Given** a left mouse-down on the drag area followed by a mouse move **When** handled **Then** `start_window_move` is called once.
- **Given** two clicks on the drag area **When** handled **Then** `zoom_window` is called once.
- **Given** a right-click on the drag area **When** handled **Then** `show_window_menu` is called with the click position; a right-click on the close button calls nothing.
- **Given** a mouse-down on the close button followed by a mouse move **When** handled **Then** `start_window_move` is not called.
- **Given** a click on the close button **When** handled **Then** `CloseWindow` is dispatched once.
- **Given** `window_controls().maximize == false` **When** rendered **Then** only minimize and close are present, flush right.
- **Given** the window is maximized **When** rendered **Then** the maximize button shows Lucide `copy` with tooltip "Restore".
- **Given** the window is inactive **When** rendered **Then** caption icons use `text_secondary` and the background is still `titlebar`.
- **Given** `Snapshot.windows.header.validity == Unsupported` **When** `keep_above_supported` runs **Then** it is false; with `Valid` it is true; with `WarmingUp` it is false.
- **Given** `ui_scale_pct = 150` **When** rendered **Then** the bar is 51 tall and each caption button 54 wide.

- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`: `pub mod titlebar;` (chain edit).

title: E20-005 Tab strip with accent outline and tab selection (tabstrip.rs)
description:
## Context
Builds the main tab strip under the title bar: the six tabs in TaskSlinger order (only the tabs whose page is built in the current phase), the active tab look with its 2 px accent outline joined to the 2 px accent line along the strip's bottom edge, and tab selection by click. It is a custom entity, not the kit `TabBar`, because the kit has no outline joined to a line. The filter box slot (E20-009), the overflow menu (E20-015), the tab switch animation (E20-021) and the tab icons (E20-023, E20-025) are added later. Phase P0 (the P0 main window shows it). Sources: UI-SHL-020, UI-SHL-007, APP-027, R-023, ADR-009 (six tabs, unbuilt tabs absent), widgets §1.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/window/tabstrip.rs` (create; add `pub mod tabstrip;` to `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`, chain edit):

```rust
pub const TAB_STRIP_H: f32 = 30.0;       // × ui_scale, includes the 2 px accent line
pub const TAB_PAD_X: f32 = 22.0;         // measured
pub const ACCENT_W: f32 = 2.0;           // outline and line thickness, × ui_scale

pub struct TabStrip {
    tabs: SmallVec<[Tab; 6]>,             // built tabs in R-023 order
    active: Tab,
    history_mode: bool,                   // Processes label reads "History"
    window_active: bool,
    filter_slot: Option<AnyView>,         // set by E20-009; None = the line runs to the right edge
    label_widths: SmallVec<[(Tab, Pixels); 6]>, // shaped once per language and scale change (used by E20-015)
    rule: Option<(AccentRuleKey, Path<Pixels>)>,
    _subs: SmallVec<[Subscription; 3]>,
}
impl TabStrip {
    pub fn new(tabs: SmallVec<[Tab; 6]>, active: Tab, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> Self;
    pub fn set_active(&mut self, tab: Tab, cx: &mut Context<Self>);     // notify only on change
    pub fn set_tabs(&mut self, tabs: SmallVec<[Tab; 6]>, cx: &mut Context<Self>);
    pub fn set_filter_slot(&mut self, slot: Option<AnyView>, cx: &mut Context<Self>);
    pub fn label(tab: Tab, history_mode: bool, cx: &App) -> SharedString;
}
impl Render for TabStrip { .. }

#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
struct AccentRuleKey { active: Bounds<Pixels>, end_x: Pixels, strip: Bounds<Pixels>, color: Hsla, scale_bits: u32 }
struct AccentRule { .. }                  // implements gpui::Element; paints outline and line in one paint_path
```

Labels (string keys in `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`, chain edit): `shell-tab-processes = Processes`, `shell-tab-history = History`, `shell-tab-performance = Performance`, `shell-tab-services = Services`, `shell-tab-startup = Startup Apps`, `shell-tab-connections = Connections`, `shell-tab-information = Information`. The Processes tab shows "History" while `UiState.processes.history_mode` is true.

Look (sizes × `ui_scale`): strip background `tab_bg`, height 30. Each tab: height 30, padding-x 22, label `t_md`. Inactive tab: label `text_primary` weight 400, no fill; hover and pressed fill `tab_hover`. Active tab: fill `header`, label `text_primary` weight 500, hover unchanged. Tabs are not focusable.

`AccentRule` (an `Element` placed as an absolute overlay of the strip, painted after the tabs):
- Outline: 2 px on the active tab's top, left and right sides, top corners radius `r_md`, bottom open.
- Line: 2 px high along the strip's bottom edge, from x = 0 to the active tab's left edge, and from the active tab's right edge to `end_x`. `end_x` is the filter slot's left edge when a filter slot is shown, else the strip's right edge.
- Where the line meets the active tab's sides (and the filter slot's left side), the joint is an outward curve of radius `r_md`.
- Colour `accent` when the window is active, `divider` when inactive (UI-SHL-007).
- The path is built in `prepaint` from the active tab's and filter slot's laid-out bounds and cached in `TabStrip.rule`; it is rebuilt only when `AccentRuleKey` changes (bounds, colour or scale). About 12 path segments.

Interaction: left click on a tab dispatches `SelectTab(i)` with `i = Tab::ALL` index. Mouse-down on a tab calls `cx.stop_propagation()` (no window drag). Middle-click, right-click and the mouse wheel do nothing. `SelectTab` handling (switching pages, writing `last_tab`) is E20-008's.

Re-render: on `set_active`, `set_tabs`, `set_filter_slot`, window activation (subscribe in `new`), `TlSettings` state version when `history_mode` flips, theme `style_version` changes and language `strings_version` changes (drop `label_widths` and `rule` on either). Zero snapshot subscriptions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** all six tabs built **When** the strip renders **Then** the labels in order are Processes, Performance, Services, Startup Apps, Connections, Information.
- **Given** only Processes and Performance built **When** the strip renders **Then** it shows exactly those two tabs.
- **Given** `history_mode = true` **When** the strip renders **Then** the first label is "History".
- **Given** Processes active and a 220 px test filter slot at x = 1060..1280 in a 1280 px window **When** the rule is built **Then** its line runs from x = 0 to the active tab's left edge and from the active tab's right edge to x = 1060, and no part lies right of 1060.
- **Given** no filter slot **When** the rule is built **Then** the line ends at the strip's right edge.
- **Given** the window is inactive **When** the strip paints **Then** the rule colour equals `theme.divider`; active: `theme.accent`.
- **Given** a click on the Services tab **When** handled **Then** `SelectTab(2)` is dispatched once and no window drag starts.
- **Given** the rule was built **When** the strip re-renders with the same active tab, bounds and colour **Then** the path is not rebuilt.
- **Given** `ui_scale_pct = 150` **When** rendered **Then** the strip is 45 tall and the outline 3 px wide.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/tabstrip.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs`: `pub mod tabstrip;` (chain edit).
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: append the seven tab keys (chain edit).
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`: add the tests below.

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`:
- `tabstrip_order_and_labels`: criterion 1.
- `tabstrip_only_built_tabs`: criterion 2.
- `tabstrip_history_label`: criterion 3.
- `accent_rule_bounds`: criterion 4 (read the cached rule's key and path bounds through a `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-hooks"))]` accessor).
- `accent_rule_to_edge_without_filter`: criterion 5.
- `inactive_window_uses_divider_outline`: criterion 6.
- `tab_click_selects`: criterion 7.
- `accent_rule_cached`: criterion 8 (a build counter behind the same test hook).
- `tabstrip_scales`: criterion 9.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: tabs are not Tab stops; keys Ctrl+1..6, Alt+1..6, Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab (E20-002) select them. Each tab's accessible name is its label.
- Performance: re-renders only on the events listed; the accent path build is O(1); embedded with `.cached(..)` by `MainWindow`.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- `Tab` and `Tab::ALL` are `tl_model::command::Tab` (E03-063). `SelectTab` is E20-002. Theme fields `tab_bg`, `tab_hover`, `header`, `accent`, `divider`, `text_primary` and `r_md` come from `TlTheme` (E17-A1) via `theme::store::current(cx)` and `UiMetrics` (`metrics(cx)`).
- `paint_path` with a `PathBuilder` (gpui-pre 0.3.7 `src/path_builder.rs`) draws the outline and line as one filled path; build the 2 px stroke as a filled outline shape, not a stroked line, so the joins are exact.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_shell`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- crates/tl-ui/src/window/tabstrip.rs crates/tl-ui/src/window/mod.rs assets/locales/en-US.ftl crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shell.rs`. Never a bare `git commit`.
- Read `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` in the repo first.
