title: E32-009 Low-memory rescue window frame, texts, filter, eased state
description:
## Context
The rescue window "tasklens - Low memory" is its own process (`tasklens --low-memory`), started by the watcher. It tells the user memory is critically low, lists the biggest apps and processes (E32-A2), and offers "Open Full tasklens". This bead builds the window, its texts, the filter, the eased state and the keys; the list rows are E32-A2. Sources: UI-PWN-032, PROC-098, PROC-097, R-062, R-073, R-120 and table (b) row `LowMemory`, UI-FND-021 (frame), R-132 (strings).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/windows/low_memory.rs`:

```rust
pub struct LowMemoryWindow { /* engine, filter input, list state, pressure history, focus */ }
impl LowMemoryWindow {
    /// Opens the window through TlSecondaryWindow::open with WindowKind::Floating and no parent.
    pub fn open(cx: &mut App, engine: Arc<dyn EngineClient>) -> WindowHandle<Self>;
}
pub fn bind_keys_low_memory(cx: &mut App);
/// Minimal init for the rescue process (R-243): called by `tl_ui::run` instead of `TasklensUi::init` when `UiLaunch.open == OpenMode::LowMemory` (E32-013, tasklens-m1f.15).
pub fn init_low_memory(cx: &mut App, client: Arc<dyn EngineClient>, init: UiInit);
actions!(tasklens, [LowMemEndTask, OpenFullTasklens, LowMemClose, LowMemClearOrClose]);
```

Layout (420 x 560 logical px, minimum 360 x 400, padding `sp6`):

```text
+--------------------------------------------------+
| tasklens - Low memory                [pin] [x]   | title bar, pin shown on
| Your device is running on critically low memory. | t_md 14 semibold, status.danger
| We recommend you close some of the processes     | t_base, text_secondary
| below.                                           |
| [Filter...                                   ]   | TlTextInput md, 28 high
| (list, E32-A2)                                   | rows 32
| [Open Full tasklens]                             | footer 52, Primary button on the left
+--------------------------------------------------+
```

- Title exactly "tasklens - Low memory". The pin starts toggled on; it can be turned off (PROC-056, R-073). Keep-above goes through `KWinCommand::KeepAbove`: in `EngineMode::LowMemory` the engine runs the `KWin` worker for that command only (R-152 OI-9); elsewhere the pin is disabled (R-073).
- Minimal build: no charts, no process or app icons, only the pin and close frame icons (embedded SVGs); fonts Noto Sans Regular and SemiBold only, loaded by `init_low_memory` (R-243).
- `init_low_memory` (R-243) performs the steps of `TasklensUi::init` (E16-A1, fut.1) with these differences: fonts are `assets/fonts/NotoSans-Regular.ttf` and `NotoSans-SemiBold.ttf` only, added with `cx.text_system().add_fonts(vec![Cow::Borrowed(include_bytes!(..)), ..])` (no `NotoSans-Medium`, no `NotoSansMono`); no icon loading (the pin and close SVGs are embedded here); `bind_keys_low_memory(cx)` is the only key-binding call; no page registration; the theme store is installed without user themes (`init.themes_json` is ignored); it sets `cx.global_mut::<OpenHooks>().low_memory = Some(Box::new(move |cx| { LowMemoryWindow::open(cx, client.clone()); }))` so `open_first` (fut.15) opens this window. It installs everything the frame, the filter, toasts and the action tracker need (`AppEnv`, settings and state Globals, `Strings`, `SnapshotHub`, `ActionTracker`), as `init` does.
- Filter: placeholder "Filter...", case-insensitive match on the row name. No match: the list area shows "No processes match the filter.".
- Eased state: when every pressure sample of the last 10 s is below the threshold (full share at most 10% and MemAvailable at least 3% of MemTotal), the two top lines are replaced by one line in `status.success`: "Memory pressure has eased. You can open the full tasklens or close this window." The list stays usable. When a sample is critical again, the two original lines return.
- "Open Full tasklens" (`OpenFullTasklens`, `TlButton` Primary): starts the main instance; the rescue window stays open. Route (R-152 OI-11): `Command::Action` with `ActionKind::Launch(LaunchSpec { what: LaunchWhat::Command("tasklens".into()), as_admin: false, cwd: None })`, since a second `tasklens` activates the running instance and exits (APP-011). The actions region and the launcher (E14-A3, y6k.3) run in both engine modes.
- Keys, context `LowMemory` (table (b)): Esc clears the filter if it has text, else closes (`LowMemClearOrClose`); Ctrl+W closes (`LowMemClose`); a printable character with focus in the list starts filtering (focus moves to the filter with that character). Closing the window ends the `--low-memory` process (`cx.quit()`).
- Tab order: filter, list (one focus stop), Open Full tasklens, pin, close.
- Strings: append to `assets/locales/en-US.ftl` (R-132 chain edit), keys:
  `lowmem-window-title = tasklens - Low memory`, `lowmem-text-critical = Your device is running on critically low memory.`, `lowmem-text-recommend = We recommend you close some of the processes below.`, `lowmem-text-eased = Memory pressure has eased. You can open the full tasklens or close this window.`, `lowmem-filter-placeholder = Filter...`, `lowmem-filter-empty = No processes match the filter.`, `lowmem-button-open-full = Open Full tasklens`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a FakeEngine with a critical sample **When** the window opens **Then** the title is "tasklens - Low memory" and both critical lines show, the first in `status.danger`.
- **Given** the window open **When** it first renders **Then** the pin is toggled on.
- **Given** FakeEngine samples below the threshold for 10 s of fake time **When** the next sample arrives **Then** the eased line replaces the two lines.
- **Given** the eased state **When** a critical sample arrives **Then** the two original lines return.
- **Given** samples below the threshold for only 8 s **When** the next sample arrives **Then** the critical lines still show.
- **Given** filter text "fire" **When** Esc is pressed **Then** the filter is cleared and the window stays open; **When** Esc is pressed again **Then** the window closes.
- **Given** the window **When** "Open Full tasklens" is clicked **Then** the FakeEngine records one launch command and the window stays open.
- **Given** a filter that matches nothing **When** the list renders **Then** "No processes match the filter." shows.
- **Given** `init_low_memory` ran with a FakeEngine **When** the Globals are inspected **Then** `OpenHooks.low_memory` is `Some`, `OpenHooks.main` is `None`, and the text system has the `Noto Sans` Regular and SemiBold faces and no Medium face (R-243).

## Files

- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_low_memory.rs`: create.

All use `#[gpui_kit::test]` and `testing/fake_engine.rs` (ADR-013).

## Cross-cutting

title: Low-memory watcher as its own small binary tl-watch, under 4 MiB RSS and fully locked
description:
Files: crates/tl-watch/ (new crate: Cargo.toml, src/main.rs, src/watch_memory.rs moved from tl-app), crates/tl-app/src/watch_memory.rs (removed), crates/tl-app/src/main.rs (the --watch-memory arm execs tl-watch), crates/tl-app/tests/watch_memory.rs (moved to crates/tl-watch/tests/), Cargo.toml (workspace member), Cargo.lock, packaging/PKGBUILD (install the binary), packaging/tasklens-lowmem.service.in (ExecStart), crates/tl-app/src/lowmem_unit.rs (unit text if it names the command), docs/spec/merged/sys-app.md and proc.md (the --watch-memory lines).
Why: m1f.5 (da6f444, 4cddd56) measured the watcher inside the tasklens binary at 14.5 MiB VmRSS (target 4 MiB): 11.5 MiB of file pages from the 568 MB debug binary, about 3 MiB of relocated RELRO, about 280 .init_array constructors from dependencies. mlockall(CURRENT|FUTURE) fails with ENOMEM under the 8 MiB RLIMIT_MEMLOCK because the whole binary is mapped. The watcher exists to keep running under memory pressure, so it must be small and locked.
Leader decision: a separate binary tl-watch (installed as /usr/bin/tasklens-watch) with std plus libc only: no gpui, no asupersync, no tracing, no zbus. Logging to stderr (journald captures it). D-Bus single-instance check: keep it if it can be done with a minimal hand-written call on the session bus socket, else use a lock file in XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. The rescue launch spawns `tasklens --low-memory` as today. The unit runs tasklens-watch directly. `tasklens --watch-memory` stays as a compatibility arm that execs tasklens-watch (found next to current_exe, then on PATH). Release profile for tl-watch: opt-level "z", panic abort, strip; no PIE overhead tweaks unless needed.
AC: real_rss_under_4mib passes on the release build (VmRSS < 4 MiB after 2 s) and mlockall succeeds under an 8 MiB RLIMIT_MEMLOCK; exactly 1 thread; all moved watch_memory tests pass; `tasklens --watch-memory` execs the new binary; PKGBUILD installs it (makepkg not required, a package() dry check is enough). clippy clean for tl-watch and tl-app --all-targets -D warnings.
close_reason: New crate tl-watch, binary tasklens-watch, std plus libc only (4b1b8ee, 96c753c). Release VmRSS 3776 kB after 2 s, VmLck 3768 kB (mlockall ok under 8 MiB memlock), 1 thread. tasklens --watch-memory execs it; unit runs it directly; PKGBUILD installs it. Lock file in XDG_RUNTIME_DIR for single instance. panic=abort not set: cargo forbids panic in a package override.

title: E32-A2 Rescue window and low-memory engine
description:
## Context
Anchor of E32. Finishes the rescue window with its process list (UI-PWN-033): at most 30 apps and processes sorted by memory, each with "Memory 12.0%" of MemTotal and an "End Task" button that kills without confirmation, because a graceful stop under memory pressure makes thrashing worse. When this bead closes, `workers/lowmem.rs` (E32-006, E32-007) and `windows/low_memory.rs` are complete. Sources: UI-PWN-033, UI-PWN-032, PROC-098, PROC-001 (identity), ADR-006 (KillGroup on an app cgroup writes `cgroup.kill`), R-137.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/low_memory.rs`, the list: a plain `v_flex` of at most 30 rows (no `TlTreeTable`).

- Rows: apps (App groups from the low-memory update) and processes not in an App group. Memory: processes use `rss_anon_bytes + swap_bytes`; apps use cgroup `memory.current`. Sorted by memory descending, cut at 30.
- Row: 32 logical px high times UI scale (not affected by the row-height setting), padding `sp4` horizontal, 1 px bottom border `divider`.
  - Name: `t_base`, `text_primary`, end ellipsis. Apps: `{app name} ({process count})`. Processes: their display name.
  - "Memory 12.0%": `t_sm`, `text_secondary`, right aligned, width 100, tabular numbers. Percent of MemTotal with one decimal (`format!("Memory {:.1}%", pct)` through `tl_model::units` if it has a percent formatter).
  - `TlButton` Danger sm "End Task", width 84, tooltip "Ends immediately, unsaved work is lost". Accessible name "End Task: {name}".
- Order hold: while the pointer is over the list or a row has keyboard focus, the order is held and only values update. It re-sorts when the pointer leaves and focus moves out.
- Other users' rows (`OTHER_USER`, or an app group whose uid is not the current uid): shown, button disabled, tooltip "Needs administrator rights".
- End Task (`LowMemEndTask`), no confirmation:
  - process: `Command::Action(ActionRequest { kind: ActionKind::Signal(Signal::Kill), targets: [ActionTarget::Process(key)], privileged: false, .. })`;
  - app: `ActionKind::KillGroup` with `ActionTarget::Cgroup(CgroupRef { rel_path, cgroup_id })`, which `tl-ops` runs as a `cgroup.kill` write after `open_validated` (ADR-006). PROC-098 and UI-PWN-033 say `KillUnit(name, "all", SIGKILL)`; ADR-006 takes precedence for app cgroups under `app.slice`, and the systemd worker does not run in `LowMemory` mode.
  - While in flight the button shows loading. On success the row goes at the next sweep.
  - Failure: Error toast, title "End Task Failed", message "kill failed: {errno text}" (the `ActionError` OS error text).
- Keyboard in the list: Up and Down move a highlight (`row_selected`); Enter or Delete presses End Task on the highlighted row.
- Strings appended to `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: `lowmem-row-memory = Memory { $pct }%`, `lowmem-button-end-task = End Task`, `lowmem-tooltip-end-task = Ends immediately, unsaved work is lost`, `lowmem-tooltip-needs-admin = Needs administrator rights`, `lowmem-toast-end-failed-title = End Task Failed`, `lowmem-toast-end-failed-text = kill failed: { $error }`, `lowmem-a11y-end-task = End Task: { $name }`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a FakeEngine update with 40 processes **When** the list renders **Then** 30 rows show, sorted by memory descending.
- **Given** an app group with 34 processes and `memory.current` of 12% of MemTotal **When** the list renders **Then** its row reads "Firefox (34)" and "Memory 12.0%".
- **Given** the pointer over the list **When** an update changes the order **Then** the rows keep their order and only the values change; **When** the pointer leaves and nothing has focus **Then** the list re-sorts.
- **Given** a process with `OTHER_USER` **When** the list renders **Then** its End Task button is disabled with tooltip "Needs administrator rights".
- **Given** a process row **When** End Task is clicked **Then** no dialog opens and the FakeEngine records one `Signal(Kill)` action with that `ProcessKey`.
- **Given** an app row **When** End Task is clicked **Then** the FakeEngine records one `KillGroup` action on that app's `CgroupRef`.
- **Given** a `Failed(ActionError)` event with errno text "Operation not permitted" **When** it arrives **Then** an Error toast shows "End Task Failed" and "kill failed: Operation not permitted".
- **Given** the highlight on row 2 **When** Delete is pressed **Then** End Task runs for row 2.
- **Given** a `ProcessKey` whose start time changed since capture (identity changed) **When** End Task runs **Then** the engine rejects it with `IdentityChanged` and nothing is killed (regression test, PROC-001).

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/windows/low_memory.rs`: the list, End Task, order hold, keyboard.
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: chain edit, the seven keys above.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_low_memory.rs`: tests.

## Tests
- `tests/ui_low_memory.rs::lowmem_list_caps_30_sorted`.
- `tests/ui_low_memory.rs::lowmem_app_row_name_and_percent`.
- `tests/ui_low_memory.rs::lowmem_order_held_while_hovered`.
- `tests/ui_low_memory.rs::lowmem_other_user_disabled_tooltip`.
- `tests/ui_low_memory.rs::lowmem_end_task_no_confirmation`.
- `tests/ui_low_memory.rs::lowmem_end_task_app_uses_kill_group`.
- `tests/ui_low_memory.rs::lowmem_end_task_failure_toast`.
- `tests/ui_low_memory.rs::lowmem_keyboard_delete_ends_highlighted`.
- `tests/ui_low_memory.rs::lowmem_identity_changed_not_killed` (security regression: the request carries the captured key; FakeEngine answers `Rejected(IdentityChanged)` and the row stays with no toast other than the rejection text from `ActionTracker`).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: "End Task Failed" / "kill failed: {errno text}" toast; rejections use `ActionTracker::message` (E16-A3).
- Validity: rows show values only when `Valid`; a row whose memory is not `Valid` sorts last and shows the validity glyph from `TlValidityGlyph`.
- Accessibility: list is one focus stop; Up, Down, Enter, Delete; button accessible names "End Task: {name}".
- Performance: 30 rows; strings re-formatted only when the percent changes; one re-render per 2 s sweep.
- Privacy: names are already sanitized by the engine; never log them.

## Notes
- No confirmation is the spec's choice (PROC-098); do not add one.
- `security` label: this bead sends SIGKILL and cgroup kills; targets must be the captured keys, never re-looked-up by pid.
- Settled: OI-1 (R-150 item 2): the low-memory data is `ProcessSnapshot.low_memory: Option<Arc<LowMemoryInfo>>`, filled from `ProcessSweep.low_memory`.
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...`.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git add <new files>`, then `git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`. One bead, one commit.

title: E32: add --watch-memory arm and module lines to tl-app/src/main.rs
description:
## Context
Chain edit to `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`, owned by E33 (00-epics section 2: "`--low-memory` and `--watch-memory` arms (E32), each depends on E33-A1"). `args.rs` already declares every APP-052 argument (E33-A1). This bead routes `--watch-memory` to the watcher before anything else starts: no GPUI, no engine, no settings load (PROC-097, UI-SHL-110). Sources: APP-052, PROC-097, UI-SHL-110.

## Deliverable
Exactly these changes to `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`, and no other change to that file:

1. Two module lines next to the other `mod` lines:
```rust
mod lowmem_unit;
mod watch_memory;
```
2. One `if` placed directly after the clap parse (step 3 of the UI-SHL-110 order) and before the NVIDIA X11 rule, single instance, settings load and engine start:
```rust
if args.watch_memory {
    return watch_memory::run_watch_memory();
}
```
Use the field name E33-A1 gave the `--watch-memory` flag in `args.rs` (expected `watch_memory: bool`). If `main` does not return `ExitCode`, wrap the call the way the existing arms do.

Logging for this mode (R-152 OI-4): the arm runs before the file logger is set up, and the watcher's `warn!` lines go to stderr through a minimal `tracing_subscriber::fmt().with_writer(std::io::stderr)` subscriber set up inside `run_watch_memory`, so the journal of the user unit holds them.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the built binary **When** run as `tasklens --watch-memory` **Then** no window opens, no engine threads start, and the process stays running.
- **Given** the built binary **When** run as `tasklens --watch-memory` while a normal tasklens instance owns `io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens` **Then** the watcher still runs (it does not do the single-instance hand-off).
- **Given** the built binary **When** run without `--watch-memory` **Then** startup is unchanged.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: chain edit, the lines above only.

## Tests
- `tests/watch_memory.rs::real_rss_under_4mib` (from E32-A1, `#[ignore]`) now passes against the real binary.
- `tests/watch_memory.rs::watch_memory_no_single_instance` (`#[ignore]`): with a fake owner of the bus name (a zbus blocking connection that requests `io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens`), `tasklens --watch-memory` keeps running for 2 s.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: the arm runs before any allocation-heavy start step.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- The `tests/watch_memory.rs` file is E32's (00-epics section 2), so adding the ignored test there is allowed.
- Settled: OI-4 (R-152). ADR-015 gains the sentence that the watcher logs `warn` and above to stderr only, with no file appender.
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git add <new files>`, then `git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`. One bead, one commit.

title: E32-004 Install or remove the lowmem unit when lowmem.enabled changes
description:
## Context
`lowmem.enabled` (canonical table (a), section `[lowmem]`, default `false`, P3) is the switch "Open rescue window on critical memory pressure" in the Settings menu (UI-SHL-040, owned by E21) and the Settings window page "Startup and window" (UI-SHL-069). When it turns on, tasklens installs and enables `tasklens-lowmem.service`; when it turns off, it disables and removes it (PROC-097). tl-ui holds settings and calls a `Box<dyn Fn(&Settings, &State)>` persist callback given by tl-app (ADR-011). This bead hooks that callback. Sources: PROC-097, ADR-011 (ownership), canonical table (a).

## Deliverable
1. In `crates/tl-app/src/lowmem_unit.rs`:
```rust
/// Wraps the persist callback. Keeps the last seen `settings.lowmem.enabled` (starting at
/// `initial`). When the value changes, it starts one std::thread named "tl-lowmem-unit" that
/// runs install_and_enable() (false -> true) or disable_and_remove() (true -> false), then
/// calls `inner` as before. At most one such thread runs at a time; a change that arrives
/// while one runs is applied after it finishes, using the newest value.
pub fn wrap_persist(inner: PersistFn, initial: bool) -> PersistFn;
```
`PersistFn` is the callback type E33-A2 defines for the persist callback (`Box<dyn Fn(&Settings, &State)>`). Use E33's alias if it has one.
2. Chain edit to `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: one line where the persist callback is built, before it is passed to tl-ui:
```rust
let persist = lowmem_unit::wrap_persist(persist, settings.lowmem.enabled);
```
No other change to `main.rs`.
3. Results: success and errors are logged at `info` and `warn` on target `tasklens::engine`. On an install or remove failure (R-152 OI-7): set `lowmem.enabled` back to its previous value, save the settings, and send the desktop notification "Could not set up the rescue window" through E33-010 (cr0.13). After a successful install, write `Installed.oom_score_adjust` to `state.toml` `[lowmem] oom_score_adjust` (0 means the fallback was used; E32-011 shows the extra tooltip sentence " The watcher runs with normal OOM priority.").
4. Startup reconciliation (R-152 OI-7): at launch, when `lowmem.enabled` is true and the unit file is missing, install it again on the "tl-lowmem-unit" thread. When the setting is false and the file exists, nothing is done.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `initial = false` and a fake install function **When** the callback is called with `lowmem.enabled = true` **Then** install runs once and `inner` is called once.
- **Given** `initial = true` **When** the callback is called with `lowmem.enabled = true` again **Then** neither install nor remove runs.
- **Given** `initial = true` **When** the callback is called with `false` **Then** remove runs once.
- **Given** an install still running **When** the value goes true, false, true **Then** after the first install ends exactly zero further calls run (newest value equals the installed state).
- **Given** a failing install **When** the callback is called **Then** `inner` is still called and a `warn` line is logged.
- **Given** a fake install function that fails **When** the callback is called with `lowmem.enabled = true` **Then** the setting is saved back as false and one notification "Could not set up the rescue window" is sent.
- **Given** a fake install that returns `Installed { oom_score_adjust: 0 }` **When** it succeeds **Then** `state.toml` holds `[lowmem] oom_score_adjust = 0`.
- **Given** `lowmem.enabled = true` at launch and no unit file **When** tl-app starts **Then** the install runs once.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/lowmem_unit.rs`: add `wrap_persist` and a private seam that lets the test swap install and remove for counters.
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: chain edit, the one line above.
- `crates/tl-app/tests/watch_memory.rs`: tests.
- `crates/tl-model/src/settings.rs`: chain edit, add the `[lowmem]` section with `oom_score_adjust: Option<i32>` to `UiState` (R-262).

## Tests
- `tests/watch_memory.rs::wrap_persist_installs_on_enable`.
- `tests/watch_memory.rs::wrap_persist_no_op_on_same_value`.
- `tests/watch_memory.rs::wrap_persist_removes_on_disable`.
- `tests/watch_memory.rs::wrap_persist_coalesces_while_busy`.
- `tests/watch_memory.rs::wrap_persist_inner_called_on_failure`.
- `failure_reverts_setting_and_notifies`, `oom_score_adjust_written_to_state`, `startup_reinstalls_missing_unit` (same test file as the other tests of this bead).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: install or remove errors are logged, the setting is reverted and the notification is sent (R-152 OI-7).
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: the callback never blocks the GPUI main thread; D-Bus work runs on the "tl-lowmem-unit" thread.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- The persist callback may be called often (debounced saves); the change check keeps it cheap.
- Startup reconciliation follows step 4 (R-152 OI-7).
- Settled: OI-7 (R-152). Table (a) gains the state key `[lowmem] oom_score_adjust`; UI-SHL-069 gains the tooltip texts.
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git add <new files>`, then `git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`. One bead, one commit.

title: E32: add mod lowmem to tl-engine/src/workers/mod.rs
description:

title: E32-006 LowMemSource stripped process sweep
description:
## Context
In `EngineMode::LowMemory` (the `tasklens --low-memory` rescue process) only the `Processes` worker runs, with a stripped sweep every 2 s: `/proc/<pid>/stat`, `/proc/<pid>/status`, the cgroup path from `/proc/<pid>/cgroup`, and cgroup `memory.current` for app scopes, plus the memory pressure state. The engine publishes `Snapshot.processes` and `Snapshot.health` only. Actions still go through the ADR-006 pipeline with identity revalidation, so `ProcessKey` must be the same key the full sweep would build (U-50). Sources: ADR-004 (engine modes), PROC-098, UI-PWN-032, UI-PWN-033, R-137 (`memory.current` only in `EngineMode::LowMemory`; cgroup files opened with `openat` from a dirfd on `/sys/fs/cgroup` and closed in the same sweep), R-119, U-50, ADR-015 (sanitize).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/workers/lowmem.rs`:

```rust
pub const LOWMEM_PERIOD: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);
pub const LOWMEM_PSI_FULL_PCT: f32 = 10.0;   // R-062
pub const LOWMEM_MEMAVAIL_MIN_PCT: u64 = 3;  // R-062

pub struct LowMemSource { /* SysRoot, cgroup dirfd, previous PSI full total and its time */ }

impl LowMemSource { pub fn new(root: SysRoot) -> Self; }

impl Source for LowMemSource {
    fn id(&self) -> SourceId { SourceId::Processes }
    /// Always Some(LOWMEM_PERIOD): the rescue window is always visible and ignores the hidden
    /// policy and processes.interval_ms.
    fn period(&self, _: &Demand, _: &EngineSettings) -> Option<Duration>;
    fn sample(self) -> (Self, SourceUpdate);
}
```

Per sweep, on the blocking pool:
1. List `/proc` numeric entries. For each pid read `stat` (parsed from the last `)`: ppid, state, `start_ticks` = field 22) and `status` (`Uid` real uid, `RssAnon`, `VmSwap`, `Threads`), and `cgroup` (the `0::` line). Use the tl-collect readers from E05-A1 (`proc/pid_stat.rs`, `proc/status.rs`, `proc/cgroup.rs`); do not write new parsers.
2. Build `ProcessKey` exactly as the full sweep does (pid, `start_ticks`, `boot_id`).
3. `ProcessMeta`: `comm` sanitized by `tl_collect::sanitize` (ADR-015), `name` = sanitized `comm`, `user` from the uid, `cgroup` path, `app_id` from the scope name parsed by E05-A2's `apps/cgroup_app.rs`; `exe`, `cmdline`, `icon`, `description` are `None`; no desktop-file index is loaded; the app name is the app id parsed from the scope name (R-152 OI-8).
4. Flags: `OTHER_USER` when uid differs from `getuid()`, `KERNEL_THREAD`, `IS_SELF`, `PROTECTED` with the same rules as the full sweep (ADR-006 protected list).
5. Groups: classify with E05-A2's `apps/classify.rs` (App, Background, System, Ungrouped). For each App group, open its cgroup directory with `openat` from the `/sys/fs/cgroup` dirfd, `fstat` it for the inode (the `CgroupRef.cgroup_id`), read `memory.current`, close it.
6. `/proc/meminfo` `MemTotal` and `MemAvailable`; `/proc/pressure/memory` line `full ... total=<us>`: full share = delta total / delta wall time over the sweep interval, in percent.
7. Fields not read in this mode (`cpu_pct`, `io_*`, `net_*`, `gpu_*`, `pss_bytes`, `uss_bytes`, `rss_bytes`) are 0 with `Validity::Unsupported` in `FieldValidity`, never shown as measured zeros.
8. Emit one ordinary `SourceUpdate::Processes(ProcessSweep)` with the records and `low_memory: Some(Arc<LowMemoryInfo>)` (R-150 item 2). `LowMemoryInfo { groups: Arc<[LowMemGroup]>, mem_total, mem_available, psi_full_pct: Option<f32>, critical: bool }` and `LowMemGroup { group: GroupKey, name, process_count, uid, cgroup: CgroupRef, memory_current }` are the tl-model types in `process.rs` (E03-072, tasklens-as2.38). The reducer copies the field into `ProcessSnapshot.low_memory`. `extras`, `extras_p2` and `app_stats` stay empty.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake root with 3 processes, one in `user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/app-org.kde.konsole-1234.scope` **When** `sample` runs with uid 1000 **Then** the update has 3 records and 1 app group whose `memory.current` equals the fake file value.
- **Given** a fake root and the same pid **When** the full sweep (E05-A1) and `LowMemSource` both run **Then** both build the same `ProcessKey` (U-50).
- **Given** a process owned by uid 0 and the sweep running as uid 1000 **When** `sample` runs **Then** that record has `OTHER_USER`.
- **Given** a `comm` with control characters **When** `sample` runs **Then** the record's name is the sanitized text (ADR-015).
- **Given** a pid that exits between listing and reading `stat` **When** `sample` runs **Then** it is skipped without error.
- **Given** `/proc/pressure/memory` missing **When** `sample` runs **Then** the pressure state is computed from MemAvailable only, and no error is returned.
- **Given** two samples 2 s apart with `full total` growing by 300000 us **When** the second `sample` runs **Then** the full share is 15.0% and the state is critical.
- **Given** any demand and settings **When** `period` is called **Then** it returns `Some(2 s)`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/lowmem.rs`: fill.
- Tests: `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `lowmem.rs`, using a fake root built in a `tempfile::TempDir` (dev-dependency `tempfile = "3.27.0"`, ADR-002).

## Tests
- `workers::lowmem::tests::sweep_fake_root_records_and_groups`.
- `workers::lowmem::tests::key_matches_full_sweep` (U-50).
- `workers::lowmem::tests::other_user_flag`.
- `workers::lowmem::tests::sanitized_names`.
- `workers::lowmem::tests::vanished_pid_skipped`.
- `workers::lowmem::tests::psi_missing_falls_back_to_memavailable`.
- `workers::lowmem::tests::psi_full_share_from_total_delta`.
- `workers::lowmem::tests::period_always_two_seconds`.
- `workers::lowmem::tests::unread_fields_unsupported`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: per-pid read errors skip the pid; a failed `/proc` listing returns the update with `Validity::Failed` and the error in `SourceHealth.last_error`.
- Validity: records use `Valid`, `Restricted` (other users' `status` fields when unreadable) and `Unsupported` (fields not read in this mode).
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one sweep under 15 ms for 2,000 processes (the E05 sweep gate); no `smaps`, no fd counting, no metadata refresh, no icon or desktop lookup; buffers reused across sweeps.
- Privacy: untrusted process text goes through `sanitize`; never log names, command lines or environment.

## Notes
- E10's processes worker selects this source by `EngineMode` in the chain-edit bead E32-007. E09's session must start only the `Processes` worker in `LowMemory` mode (ADR-004); if it starts others, report it to the leader rather than editing E09 files.
- The pressure rule matches the watcher: full share above 10% over the interval, or MemAvailable below 3% of MemTotal. The rescue window's "eased" state is computed in the UI from these samples (E32-009).
- Settled: OI-1 (R-150 item 2), OI-8 (R-152).
- Large-file rule: commit the new file before you build or test it. Fix-ups go in a follow-up commit, never an amend.
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...`.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git add <new files>`, then `git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`. One bead, one commit.

title: E13-A1 Probe binary
description:
## Context
Anchor E13-A1 "Probe binary": `tl-gpu-probe` answers `Hello`, `Sample` and `Shutdown` over fd 3 with the shared framing, reports NVML init failures by kind, ships the `--fake <script>` test double, and the framing path is proven end to end against the real binary. E13-A2 (the engine worker) and E33 (packaging installs `/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-gpu-probe`) depend on it. Sources: ADR-007, ADR-001 (`tl-gpu-probe` row, no `unsafe`), ADR-013 (real-system row "NVML `Hello` and samples"), E13-001 to E13-005.

1. `crates/tl-gpu-probe/tests/probe_bin.rs` (no feature needed): spawns `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_tl-gpu-probe")` with `--fd <inherited socket>`:

   - `shutdown_exits_zero_fast`: after `Hello`, `Shutdown` → exit 0 within 200 ms.
   - `eof_exits_zero`: dropping the socket → exit 0 within 200 ms.

2. `cargo clippy -p tl-gpu-probe --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` passes; `rg -n unsafe crates/tl-gpu-probe/src` prints nothing (until open item 13 for `api_versions.rs` is decided); `cargo xtask check-deps` passes (no banned crate in the probe's resolved graph).

title: E13: gpu/spawn.rs: socketpair, pre_exec dup2, death signal (the one unsafe file)
description:
## Context
Spawning the probe child: a `SOCK_STREAM` socketpair, `std::process::Command` with a cleared environment, and a `pre_exec` hook that moves the child end to fd 3 and sets the parent-death signal to SIGKILL so a crashed engine never leaves a probe behind. This is one of the three files allowed to contain `unsafe` (ADR-001 rule 4), and the only `unsafe` in `tl-engine`. `asupersync::process` is never used (zombie bug `bi2462.114`). Sources: ADR-007 ("Spawn" steps 1 to 4), ADR-001 (rule 4: file-level allow, `// SAFETY:` per block), ADR-015 (`RUST_LOG` from `TASKLENS_LOG`), E13-007.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/gpu/spawn.rs`:

```rust
#![allow(unsafe_code)]   // ADR-001 rule 4: this file only
pub const CHILD_FD: RawFd = 3;
pub struct ProbeChild { pub child: std::process::Child, pub sock: OwnedFd /* parent end, CLOEXEC */ }
pub fn spawn_probe(probe: &Path, extra_args: &[&OsStr]) -> Result<ProbeChild, ProbeError>;   // blocking; callers run it inside spawn_blocking
pub fn child_env() -> Vec<(&'static str, OsString)>;   // PATH and LANG copied from the engine's environment when set; RUST_LOG = $TASKLENS_LOG when set
```

`spawn_probe`:
1. `rustix::net::socketpair(AddressFamily::UNIX, SocketType::STREAM, SocketFlags::CLOEXEC, None)` → `(parent, child_end)`.
2. `Command::new(probe).arg("--fd").arg("3").args(extra_args)`; `stdin(Stdio::null())`, `stdout(Stdio::null())`, `stderr(Stdio::inherit())`; `env_clear()` then `envs(child_env())`.
3. `unsafe { cmd.pre_exec(move || { dup2(child_raw, 3); set_parent_process_death_signal(Some(Signal::Kill)); Ok(()) }) }` with a `// SAFETY:` comment: the closure calls only async-signal-safe functions (`dup2`, `prctl`), allocates nothing and touches no locks. `rustix::io::dup2` clears `CLOEXEC` on the new fd 3 as required; if `child_raw == 3` already, call `fcntl_setfd(3, FdFlags::empty())` instead. `rustix::process::set_parent_process_death_signal(Some(Signal::Kill))`.
4. `cmd.spawn()` → `ProbeError::Spawn(e.to_string())` on error; drop `child_end` in the parent after spawn; return `ProbeChild { child, sock: parent }`.
A `ProbeChild` whose `child` is dropped without `wait()` would leak a zombie: `impl Drop for ProbeChild` sends `SIGKILL` and calls `child.wait()` (blocking, bounded by the kill) when `try_wait()` says it is still running. The orderly shutdown path (E13-009) waits before drop.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the fake probe binary (`--fake normal`, built with `--features fake`) **When** `spawn_probe` runs **Then** `child.id() > 0`, writing `Hello { proto: 1 }` on `sock` and reading one frame gives `Hello { proto: 1, .. }` (so fd 3 is the socket in the child).
- **Given** the spawned child **When** `/proc/<child>/environ` is read **Then** it holds only `PATH`, `LANG` and `RUST_LOG` (those that were set), nothing else.
- **Given** the spawned child **When** `/proc/<child>/fd/` is listed **Then** it has exactly 0, 1, 2 and 3 (no leaked engine fds).
- **Given** a short-lived parent process (`tests/probe_integration.rs` spawns a helper test binary that spawns the probe and exits without killing it) **When** the parent is gone **Then** the probe is gone within 100 ms (`PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` worked).
- **Given** a `ProbeChild` dropped while the child runs **When** 200 ms pass **Then** `/proc/<pid>` is absent and no zombie remains (`/proc/<pid>/stat` state is never `Z` after drop).
- **Given** a path that does not exist **When** `spawn_probe` runs **Then** `Err(Spawn(..))` and no socket fd leaks (fd count before and after is equal).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/gpu/spawn.rs`: create

## Tests
- `gpu/spawn.rs::tests::fd3_is_the_socket` (needs the fake probe; `cargo test -p tl-engine --features probe-tests` builds `tl-gpu-probe` with `fake` as a build dependency of the tests, or the test locates it through `TASKLENS_GPU_PROBE`; see E13-012 for the harness)
- `gpu/spawn.rs::tests::child_env_is_minimal`
- `gpu/spawn.rs::tests::no_leaked_fds`
- `gpu/spawn.rs::tests::drop_kills_and_reaps`
- `gpu/spawn.rs::tests::missing_binary_leaks_nothing`
- `tests/probe_integration.rs::pdeathsig_kills_orphan` (E13-012)

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `ProbeError::Spawn` only.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one fork and exec per generation.
- Privacy: the child sees no environment beyond the three variables; nothing from the user's session leaks into a process that loads a vendor library.
- Security: `env_clear` plus `pre_exec` with async-signal-safe calls only; `// SAFETY:` on the one block; `cargo xtask check-deps` confirms no other file in the crate uses `unsafe`.

## Notes
Depends on E13-007. `rustix::io::dup2(fd, &mut target)` takes an `OwnedFd`-like target; in `pre_exec` use `rustix::io::dup2_with(fd, target, DupFlags::empty())`-style raw call or `libc::dup2` via rustix's `io::dup2`; both are async-signal-safe. `std::os::unix::process::CommandExt::pre_exec` is the `unsafe` API. Phase P1. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E13: gpu/client.rs: one outstanding request, poll, deadlines, kill and reap
description:
## Context
The blocking probe client: exactly one outstanding request, written as a frame and answered after `poll` says the socket is readable, each with its deadline (Hello 3000 ms, Sample 500 ms); a missed deadline kills the child, reaps it and reports `Err` so the supervisor restarts the worker; `Shutdown` is sent at worker end with a 200 ms grace, then SIGKILL and `wait()`. All of it runs inside one `spawn_blocking` job per request. Sources: ADR-007 ("Request rules", "Failure and restart", "Shutdown"), E03-068 (`read_frame`, `write_frame`), E03-069 (messages), E13-007, E13-008.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/gpu/client.rs`:

```rust
pub struct ProbeClient { child: ProbeChild, file: std::fs::File /* dup of sock for Read/Write */, pub info: Option<HelloInfo>, seq: u32 }
pub struct HelloInfo { pub proto: u16, pub driver: Arc<str>, pub nvml: Arc<str>, pub devices: Arc<[GpuDeviceInfo]> }
pub enum HelloOutcome { Ready(HelloInfo), InitFailed { kind: InitFailure, message: Arc<str> } }

impl ProbeClient {
    pub fn start(probe: &Path) -> Result<ProbeClient, ProbeError>;          // spawn_probe + Hello under HELLO_DEADLINE
    pub fn hello(&mut self) -> Result<HelloOutcome, ProbeError>;              // writes Hello { proto: 1 }; reads one frame; proto != 1 → VersionMismatch; InitFailed → Ok(InitFailed)
    pub fn sample(&mut self, processes: bool) -> Result<ProbeResponseSample, ProbeError>;   // seq += 1; Sample { seq, processes }; the reply's seq must equal; a stale seq is a Protocol error
    pub fn shutdown(self);                                                      // write Shutdown (errors ignored); wait up to SHUTDOWN_GRACE with try_wait polling every 10 ms; then kill + wait
    fn request<T>(&mut self, req: &ProbeRequest, deadline: Duration) -> Result<ProbeResponse, ProbeError>;
    fn kill_and_reap(&mut self) -> Arc<str>;   // SIGKILL, wait(), returns "status N" or "signal N"
}
pub struct ProbeResponseSample { pub seq: u32, pub t_ns: u64, pub devices: Vec<GpuDeviceSample>, pub processes: Option<Vec<GpuProcessSample>> }
```

`request`: `write_frame(&mut file, req, MAX_PROBE_FRAME)` (an `EPIPE` → check `try_wait`: exited → `Exited(status)`, else `Protocol`); then `rustix::event::poll(&mut [PollFd::new(&sock, PollFlags::IN)], deadline_remaining)` in a loop that subtracts elapsed time and retries on `EINTR`; `0` ready → `kill_and_reap()` and `Err(Deadline(d))`; `HUP` without `IN` → `kill_and_reap()` and `Err(Exited(status))`; readable → `read_frame::<ProbeResponse>(&mut file, MAX_PROBE_FRAME)` (the payload read may block briefly after the prefix; a `Truncated` or `Eof` → `kill_and_reap()` and `Err(Exited(..))`; `TooLarge | Decode` → `kill_and_reap()` and `Err(Protocol(text))`). Only one request is ever in flight: `&mut self` enforces it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the fake probe `normal` **When** `start` runs **Then** `Ok(client)` with `info.devices.len() == 1` and `info.driver` non-empty; three `sample(false)` calls return `seq` 1, 2, 3 with `processes: None`; `sample(true)` returns `processes: Some(1 row)`.
- **Given** `sleep-on-sample` **When** `sample` runs **Then** `Err(Deadline(500 ms))` after 500 ms (±50 ms wall time), the child is dead and reaped (`/proc/<pid>` absent, no zombie), and the whole call took under 700 ms.
- **Given** `sleep-on-hello` **When** `start` runs **Then** `Err(Deadline(3000 ms))` after 3 s and no process remains.
- **Given** `segv-on-sample` **When** `sample` runs **Then** `Err(Exited("signal 11"))` and the child is reaped.
- **Given** `oversize-on-sample` **When** `sample` runs **Then** `Err(Protocol(..))` and the child is reaped.
- **Given** `proto-mismatch` **When** `start` runs **Then** `Err(VersionMismatch(99))`.

- **Given** `exit-after-3` **When** the fourth `sample` runs **Then** `Err(Exited("status 0"))`.

title: E13: GpuNvidia worker with the failure table and Unsupported states (workers/gpu_nvidia.rs)
description:
## Context
The `GpuNvidia` worker (`SourceId::GpuNvidia`): a custom worker body (not `source::run`, because it owns a child process and must return `Err` to restart per the ADR-007 failure table) that starts the probe, publishes `GpuInfo` once per generation, samples at 1 Hz while GPUs are demanded (device totals), asks for per-process data only while `gpu_process` is demanded, and maps `Reading<T>` into `GpuTotals` with `Metric` validities. A missing probe and `InitFailed { LibraryNotFound | DriverNotLoaded }` give health `SourceState::Unsupported` with `last_error` "GPU probe not installed", "LibraryNotFound" or "DriverNotLoaded": a terminal state that neither the worker nor the controller retries (R-155 item 4). Sources: ADR-007 (rates, failure table, retry, shutdown, pid mapping is the reducer's), ADR-008 (schedule rows "GPU totals (NVML)" and "GPU per process", hidden policy, "after resume the GPU probe is not restarted"), ADR-004 (worker contract, expected conditions are not failures), E08-003 (`GpuSample`, `GpuInfoUpdate`, `GpuStaticInfo`), E08-004 (`WorkerIo`, `WorkerControl`, interval pattern), E03-009 (`GpuTotals`, `Metric`), E03-010 (`DeviceIdentity::Gpu`), E13-009, R-155 items 3, 4, 7 and 8.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/workers/gpu_nvidia.rs`:

```rust
pub const PERIOD: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);   // never faster; the Refresh setting does not apply (R-026)
pub fn spec() -> WorkerSpec;   // id GpuNvidia, name "gpu-nvidia", modes &[EngineMode::Full]
pub fn factory(cfg: Arc<EngineConfig>, io: WorkerIo) -> WorkerFactory;
pub async fn run(cx: Cx, io: WorkerIo, cfg: Arc<EngineConfig>, locate: fn() -> Option<PathBuf>) -> Outcome<(), WorkerError>;
pub fn wanted(d: &Demand) -> (bool /* totals */, bool /* processes */);   // totals = any_surface_visible && d.gpus, or d.recording; processes = any_surface_visible && d.gpu_process, or d.recording (ADR-008 hidden column: "1 Hz if recording includes GPU")
pub fn identity(info: &GpuDeviceInfo) -> DeviceIdentity;   // Gpu { uuid: info.uuid, pci_bus_id: info.pci_bus_id.as_str().into() }
pub fn to_totals(s: &GpuDeviceSample, info: &GpuDeviceInfo) -> GpuTotals;
pub fn to_static(info: &GpuDeviceInfo, hello: &HelloInfo, supports_process_util: bool) -> GpuStaticInfo;   // persistent_key = "gpu:<NVML UUID>" (PERF-005, R-155 items 7 and 8)
```

`to_totals` (`device: DeviceIdx::PLACEHOLDER`, the reducer assigns the index from the identity, R-155 item 8): `util_pct`, `mem_util_pct`, `enc_pct`, `dec_pct`, `fan_pct` from the `Reading<u32>` as `Metric<f32>` with `Reading::validity()`; `mem_used` from `Reading<u64>`; `mem_total = Metric::valid(info.mem_total)`; `shared_used`, `shared_total` → `Metric::with(Unsupported)` (NVML has no GTT, PERF-064); `temp_c` from `temp_c`; `power_w = power_mw / 1000.0`; `power_limit_w` from `info.power_limit_mw` (`None` → `Unsupported`); `clock_gfx_mhz`, `clock_mem_mhz` as is. `pcie_rx_bps` and `pcie_tx_bps` (R-155 item 3) from `pcie_rx_kbps` and `pcie_tx_kbps` × 1024 as `Metric<f32>` with `Reading::validity()` (NVML reports KB/s).

`run`:
1. `let Some(probe) = locate() else { send Health { state: Unsupported, last_error: Some(NOT_INSTALLED) }; park forever (checkpoint loop every 60 s) }`. No retry and no second `locate` call: `Unsupported` is terminal and the controller never retries it (R-155 item 4). This is not `Outcome::Err`, so no backoff loop.
2. `let client = cx.spawn_blocking(move |_| ProbeClient::start(&probe))?.join(&cx).await?`; `Err(VersionMismatch)` → `send Health { Failed, last_error: VERSION_MISMATCH }` and park forever (checkpoint loop every 60 s; "no restart until the app restarts"); other `Err` → `Outcome::Err(e.into())` (supervisor backoff); `Ok(client)` with `info == None` (init failed): kind `LibraryNotFound | DriverNotLoaded` → `send Health { Unsupported, last_error: "<kind>" }`, `client.shutdown()`, park forever (checkpoint loop every 60 s), no retry (R-155 item 4; the UI tooltip text is E24's); kind `NoPermission | Other` → `Outcome::Err(ProbeError::InitFailed { .. }.into())`.
3. `send GpuInfo(GpuInfoUpdate { devices: info.devices.map(to_static) })` with `supports_process_util = true` until a `Sample { processes: true }` returns `processes: Some(..)` whose rows are all `Unsupported` (then resend once with `false`); `send Health { Running }`.
4. Loop with the E08-004 interval pattern (`interval(cx.now(), PERIOD)`, `MissedTickBehavior::Skip`, new `Sleep` each turn, `checkpoint`): read `io.demand.borrow_and_clone()`; `wanted` gives `(totals, processes)`; neither → skip the turn (no request; an idle probe costs nothing); else `cx.spawn_blocking(move |_| client.sample(processes))` joined; `Ok(s)` → `send Source(Gpu(GpuSample { t_ns: s.t_ns, devices: s.devices.map(|d| (identity, to_totals(d, info))), processes: s.processes }))`; `Err(e)` → `Outcome::Err(e.into())` (the client already killed and reaped the child; the supervisor restarts with 0.5 s backoff; the reducer's stale marking covers the gap, so the UI shows `Stale` then `Failed`). `WorkerControl.reset_generation` changes are ignored (ADR-008: the probe is not restarted after resume). `RefreshNow` forces one sample.
5. On cancel (checkpoint `Err`): `cx.spawn_blocking(move |_| client.shutdown())` is not possible after cancel; call `client.shutdown()` inline (it blocks at most 200 ms plus the kill) and return `Outcome::Ok(())`.
The `ProbeClient` lives in the worker task between jobs and is moved into each `spawn_blocking` closure and back (same pattern as `Source::sample(self)`).

`crates/tl-engine/src/workers/mod.rs`: `pub mod gpu_nvidia;` and the `gpu_nvidia::spec()` entry in `all_workers()` (chain edit on E08-A1) are E13-A2's.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `Demand { any_surface_visible: true, gpus: true, gpu_process: false, .. }` **When** `wanted` runs **Then** `(true, false)`; `gpus: false` → `(false, false)`; `any_surface_visible: false, recording: true` → `(true, true)`; `any_surface_visible: false, recording: false, gpus: true` → `(false, false)`.
- **Given** a `GpuDeviceSample` with `util_pct Ok(37)`, `fan_pct Unsupported`, `power_mw Ok(31_900)`, `temp_c Failed` **When** `to_totals` runs **Then** `util_pct == Metric { 37.0, Valid }`, `fan_pct.validity == Unsupported`, `power_w == Metric { 31.9, Valid }`, `temp_c.validity == Failed`, `shared_used.validity == Unsupported`, `mem_total == Metric::valid(info.mem_total)`.
- **Given** `locate` returns `None` **When** `run` runs in LabRuntime **Then** one `Health { Unsupported, "GPU probe not installed" }` is sent, no `spawn_blocking` for the probe happens, `locate` is called once, and the task is still alive after 10 minutes of virtual time (parked, no `Err`).
- **Given** a fake client (trait `ProbeLink` with `start`, `sample`, `shutdown` injected into `run` for tests; `ProbeClient` implements it) that returns `InitFailed { DriverNotLoaded }` **When** run **Then** one `Health { Unsupported, "DriverNotLoaded" }` at 0 s, `shutdown` is called once, and `start` is not called again within 30 minutes of virtual time (R-155 item 4).
- **Given** the fake client returns `InitFailed { LibraryNotFound }` **When** run **Then** one `Health { Unsupported, "LibraryNotFound" }` and no second `start`.
- **Given** `Ready` and demand `gpus: true` **When** 10 s pass **Then** 10 `Gpu` samples at 1 s steps with `processes: None`; after `gpu_process: true` the next requests carry `processes: true`.
- **Given** demand off **When** 60 s pass **Then** zero sample requests.
- **Given** the fake `sample` returns `Err(Deadline)` **When** run **Then** `run` returns `Outcome::Err(WorkerError::Probe(..))`.
- **Given** a cancel **When** it arrives mid-loop **Then** `shutdown` was called exactly once and `run` returned `Ok(())`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/gpu_nvidia.rs`: create

## Tests
- `workers/gpu_nvidia.rs::tests::wanted_table`
- `workers/gpu_nvidia.rs::tests::to_totals_mapping`
- `tests/probe_integration.rs` (E13-012): `worker_not_installed_parks`, `worker_init_failed_unsupported_no_retry`, `worker_library_not_found_unsupported`, `worker_samples_at_1hz_and_process_flag`, `worker_idle_sends_nothing`, `worker_sample_error_restarts`, `worker_cancel_shuts_down_once` (LabRuntime with the fake `ProbeLink`).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: expected conditions are health states, never `Err`: `NotInstalled`, `LibraryNotFound`, `DriverNotLoaded` give `Unsupported` (terminal, never retried, R-155 item 4); `VersionMismatch` gives `Failed` and parks; deadlines, crashes, `NoPermission`, `Other` are `Err` and go through the supervisor (five per minute, then 60 s off).
- Validity: every field through `Reading::validity`; nothing is zero when missing.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one request per second, about 2 KB; the blocking thread is held for the request duration only (under 50 ms normally, 500 ms worst case).
- Privacy: logs device names at debug only; pids are not logged.
- Security: the probe runs with a cleared environment (E13-008); its output is bounded (E03-068).

## Notes
Depends on E13-009, E08-A1 (`WorkerIo`, `WorkerSpec`, `WorkerFactory`, `SourceUpdate`), E03-A2. `DeviceIdx::PLACEHOLDER` is whatever E03-004 names the "not yet assigned" index (the reducer calls `devices.ensure` per identity on `Gpu` and `GpuInfo` and overwrites `GpuTotals.device`, R-155 item 8); if E03 has no such value, use `DeviceIdx(u16::MAX)` and say so in the commit. This worker no longer uses `INIT_RETRY` (E13 `ProbeError` constants); R-155 item 4 replaced the 300 s retry. Phase P1. Large-file rule: commit before building. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E13: api-versions run once at start with a 5 s deadline
description:
## Context
Once per engine start, the `GpuNvidia` worker's first generation runs `tl-gpu-probe --api-versions` in its own short-lived process on the blocking pool with a 5 s deadline and publishes the Vulkan and OpenGL versions per GPU as `SourceUpdate::GpuApiVersions`. A crash, timeout or non-zero exit gives nothing (the UI shows `Unknown`) and is not retried. Sources: ADR-007 ("API versions mode"), R-087, PERF-071, E08-003 (`SourceUpdate::GpuApiVersions(ApiVersions)`), E03-069 (`ApiVersions`), E13-006, E13-009.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/gpu/client.rs`:

```rust
pub fn api_versions(probe: &Path, deadline: Duration) -> Result<ApiVersions, ProbeError>;   // blocking
```

`Command::new(probe).arg("--api-versions")`, `stdin null`, `stdout piped`, `stderr inherit`, `env_clear` + `child_env()` (E13-008; no `pre_exec` needed, so no `unsafe` here); spawn; read stdout in a thread-free way: `poll` the pipe with the remaining deadline and read until EOF into a `Vec<u8>` capped at `MAX_PROBE_FRAME + 4` (more → kill, `Protocol("api-versions output too large")`); deadline passed → kill, `wait`, `Err(Deadline)`; EOF → `wait()` → non-zero or signal → `Err(Exited(..))`; else `read_frame::<ApiVersions>(&mut &buf[..], MAX_PROBE_FRAME)`.

Additions to `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/gpu_nvidia.rs::run`: after step 3 (`GpuInfo` sent) in the first generation of the session only (`io` carries no generation counter, so the worker keeps a `static ONCE_PER_PROCESS: AtomicBool`; a session restart does not re-run it, which is fine because the result is static): `cx.spawn_blocking(move |_| api_versions(&probe, API_VERSIONS_DEADLINE))` joined; `Ok(v)` → `send Source(GpuApiVersions(v))`; `Err(e)` → `tracing::info!(target: "tasklens::probe", %e, "api versions unavailable")` and nothing else. The sampler loop starts after this call returns (at most 5 s later).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the fake probe (`--fake` builds also answer `--api-versions` with one device `pci_bus_id "00000000:2D:00.0"`, `vulkan_api Some("1.4.312")`, `vulkan_driver Some("NVIDIA 615.71.09")`, `opengl Some("4.6.0 NVIDIA 615.71.09")` when `TL_FAKE_API_VERSIONS=1` is set; E13-005's binary gets this arm) **When** `api_versions` runs **Then** `Ok` with that device.
- **Given** `TL_FAKE_API_VERSIONS=sleep` **When** run with a 5 s deadline **Then** `Err(Deadline)` after 5 s and the child is reaped.
- **Given** `TL_FAKE_API_VERSIONS=crash` **When** run **Then** `Err(Exited("signal 11"))`.
- **Given** the worker in LabRuntime with a fake `ProbeLink` whose `api_versions` returns `Ok(v)` **When** the first generation starts **Then** exactly one `GpuApiVersions(v)` message precedes the first `Gpu` sample; after a simulated restart (second generation) no second `GpuApiVersions` is sent.
- **Given** the fake returns `Err` **When** run **Then** no message and the sampler loop still starts.
- **Given** the owner machine (`#[ignore]`, `tests/real_nvml.rs`) **When** `api_versions` runs on the real binary **Then** `Ok` with `vulkan_api` starting `"1."` and `opengl` starting `"4."`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/gpu/client.rs`: extend
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/gpu_nvidia.rs`: extend
- `crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/fake.rs`: the `TL_FAKE_API_VERSIONS` arm (E13 owns both crates)

## Tests
- `tests/probe_integration.rs` (E13-012): `api_versions_fake_ok`, `api_versions_deadline`, `api_versions_crash`, `worker_api_versions_once`, `worker_api_versions_error_is_quiet`.
- `tests/real_nvml.rs` (E13-013): `real_api_versions`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: never surfaced as health; `info` log only.
- Validity: missing versions are `None` in the payload; the UI shows `Unknown` (PERF-071).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one extra process per app start, under 5 s, before the first GPU sample.
- Privacy: N/A
- Security: output is bounded and parsed with the length-checked reader; the child gets the minimal environment.

## Notes
Depends on E13-009, E13-006 (the real mode; the fake arm lets the engine tests run without Vulkan). Phase P2. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E13: probe_integration.rs: client, worker and supervisor cases
description:
## Context
The engine-side integration tests for the probe: the `ProbeClient` cases against the real fake binary (deadline kills, crash, oversize, shutdown, no zombies), the `GpuNvidia` worker cases in LabRuntime with a fake `ProbeLink`, the supervisor interplay (stale then restart, backoff 0.5 s then 1 s), and the orphan test for `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`. Sources: ADR-007 (verification list), ADR-013 (engine LabRuntime tests, `explore_seeds`), ADR-004 (backoff), E13-008 to E13-011.

fn fake_probe() -> PathBuf;   // $TASKLENS_GPU_PROBE if set, else the workspace target dir binary built by `cargo build -p tl-gpu-probe --features fake` (the test runs that build once through std::process::Command on `cargo` with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` inherited; failure → panic with the command to run)

title: E13: real_nvml.rs: Hello, samples, process rows, kill and restart on the owner machine
description:
## Context
Real-system tests (`#[ignore]`, owner machine, RTX 5070 on driver 615.71.09) for the engine's probe path: a real `Hello` with the real binary, ten real samples at 1 Hz, per-process rows for a running GPU process, the probe kill and restart on a real child, and the `--api-versions` run. Sources: ADR-013 (real-system rows "NVML `Hello` and samples", "GPU probe kill and restart"), ADR-007 (verification), U-12, U-35, E13-009 to E13-011.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/tests/real_nvml.rs` (`#[ignore]` on every test; the binary from `gpu::locate()` with `TASKLENS_GPU_PROBE` pointing at a release build):
- `real_hello_5070`: `ProbeClient::start` → `Ready`; one device whose `name` contains `"5070"`; `driver` starts with `"615."`; `pci_bus_id == "00000000:2D:00.0"`; `power_limit_mw.is_some()` (prints the value for U-35).

title: GPU probe spawn: close every fd above 3 in the child (close_range)
description:
Files: crates/tl-engine/src/gpu/spawn.rs, crates/tl-engine/Cargo.toml (libc), Cargo.lock, xtask/src/check_deps.rs (allow libc for tl-engine), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (tl-engine row: libc, for close_range in the probe child only), docs/RECONCILIATION.md (new R entry).
Why: zbus 5.19.0 receives fds with recvmsg and RecvFlags::empty() (zbus-5.19.0/src/connection/socket/unix.rs:284), so an fd received over D-Bus is open without O_CLOEXEC until zvariant dups it. A probe spawned in that window inherits it. fix-fdleak saw gpu::spawn::tests::no_leaked_fds fail with a /usr fd from the opener tests (commits 4882181, 5146695, c21eeeb, b0d4e0a fixed the other causes). rustix 1.1.5 has no close_range. Leader decision: option (b), defence in depth in the child. Patching zbus upstream is a separate follow-up for the owner.
Deliverable: in the child pre_exec hook, after the fd 3 dup2, call close_range(4, u32::MAX, 0) through libc. If it fails with ENOSYS, close 4..=1024 one by one. Async-signal-safe only: no allocation in the hook. A SAFETY comment explains it.
AC: Given an fd opened in the test process with FD_CLOEXEC cleared, when the probe is spawned, then the probe's /proc/<pid>/fd holds only 0 to 3 (allowing the probe's own short-lived fds as no_leaked_fds already does). no_leaked_fds passes 10 runs in a row through heavy-build. check-deps and clippy pass.

title: E13: tl-gpu-probe crate, argument modes and the fd 3 sampler loop (main.rs, sampler.rs)
description:
## Context
`tl-gpu-probe` is the only process that loads NVML, so an NVML crash or hang cannot take down tasklens. This bead builds the binary's shell: argument parsing for its three modes, the fd 3 sampler loop that reads `ProbeRequest` frames and writes `ProbeResponse` frames with the shared `tl-model::wire` framing, and a `Backend` trait that the NVML backend (E13-002 to E13-004) and the fake backend (E13-005) implement. Synchronous, no async runtime, no logging framework (stderr is inherited). Sources: ADR-007 (process, framing, messages, request rules, exit rules), ADR-001 (`tl-gpu-probe` row: `tl-model`, `nvml-wrapper`, `rustix`, `postcard`, `serde`, `ash`, `khronos-egl`; `unsafe` denied), ADR-002 (pins), E03-068 (`wire`), E03-069 (`gpu_proto`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-gpu-probe/Cargo.toml`: `[package] name = "tl-gpu-probe"`, `[[bin]] name = "tl-gpu-probe"`, dependencies `tl-model`, `nvml-wrapper` (`workspace = true`, `=0.13.0`, `default-features = false`), `rustix` (features `process`, `fs`, `event`), `postcard`, `serde` (all workspace pins); `ash` and `khronos-egl` behind feature `api-versions` (default on; E13-006 adds them); feature `fake` (off by default) for the fake backend; `[lints] workspace = true` (`unsafe_code = "deny"`, no file-level allow in this crate).

`crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/main.rs`:

```rust
pub enum Mode { Sampler { fd: i32 }, ApiVersions, Fake { script: String, fd: i32 } }
pub fn parse_args(args: &[String]) -> Result<Mode, String>;
// "--fd <n>" → Sampler; "--api-versions" → ApiVersions; "--fake <script> [--fd <n>]" (feature fake; default fd 3) → Fake; anything else → Err(usage text)
fn main() -> std::process::ExitCode;   // Err from parse_args → prints usage to stderr, exit 2; Sampler → exit 3 with "nvml backend not built" until E13-002 (ndy.4) adds `mod nvml;` and replaces the arm with sampler::run(fd, nvml::NvmlBackend::new) (R-262); ApiVersions → api_versions::run() (E13-006; before it: exit 3 with "api-versions not built"); Fake → exit 3 with "fake backend not built" until E13-005 (ndy.7) adds the arm sampler::run(fd, fake::FakeBackend::from_script) (R-262)
```

`crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/sampler.rs`:

```rust
pub const PROTO: u16 = tl_model::gpu_proto::GPU_PROTO_VERSION;   // 1
pub trait Backend {
    fn hello(&mut self) -> Result<HelloInfo, InitFailed>;   // HelloInfo { driver: String, nvml: String, devices: Vec<GpuDeviceInfo> }; InitFailed { kind: InitFailure, message: String }
    fn sample(&mut self, seq: u32, processes: bool) -> (u64 /* t_ns CLOCK_BOOTTIME */, Vec<GpuDeviceSample>, Option<Vec<GpuProcessSample>>);
}
pub fn run<B: Backend>(fd: i32, make: impl FnOnce() -> B) -> std::process::ExitCode;
```

`run`: wrap `fd` in an `OwnedFd` (`rustix::fd::BorrowedFd` → `std::fs::File` is fine for blocking reads and writes); loop `read_frame::<ProbeRequest>(&mut f, MAX_PROBE_FRAME)`: `Hello { proto }` → `proto != PROTO` → write `Hello { proto: PROTO, driver: "", nvml: "", devices: [] }` and exit 0 (the engine treats the mismatch, ADR-007); else `make()` the backend once, `backend.hello()` → write `Hello { proto, driver, nvml, devices }` or `InitFailed { kind, message }`; `Sample { seq, processes }` before a successful `Hello` → write `InitFailed { Other, "sample before hello" }` and exit 0; after → write `Sample { seq, t_ns, devices, processes }`; `Shutdown` → exit 0; `Err(Eof)` → exit 0; any other `WireError` → exit 0 (protocol error: silent exit, the engine restarts). Writes go through `write_frame(.., MAX_PROBE_FRAME)`; a write error (EPIPE) → exit 0. `SIGPIPE` is set to `SIG_IGN`-equivalent by handling the `EPIPE` error (Rust ignores SIGPIPE by default). `t_ns` is `rustix::time::clock_gettime(ClockId::Boottime)` in nanoseconds.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `["--fd", "3"]` **When** parsed **Then** `Sampler { fd: 3 }`; `["--api-versions"]` → `ApiVersions`; `["--fake", "normal"]` → `Fake { script: "normal", fd: 3 }`; `[]` and `["--fd", "x"]` → `Err`.
- **Given** a socketpair and a `Backend` test double **When** the client writes `Hello { proto: 1 }` **Then** the probe answers `Hello { proto: 1, .. }` with the double's devices.
- **Given** `Hello { proto: 2 }` **When** sent **Then** the probe answers `Hello { proto: 1, devices: [] }` and exits 0 without calling `make()`.
- **Given** `Sample` before `Hello` **When** sent **Then** `InitFailed { Other, "sample before hello" }` and exit 0.
- **Given** `Hello` then `Sample { seq: 7, processes: false }` **When** sent **Then** the answer is `Sample { seq: 7, processes: None, .. }` with `t_ns > 0`.
- **Given** `Shutdown` **When** sent **Then** the probe exits 0 within 100 ms; the same when the client closes its end.
- **Given** a frame whose prefix says 2 MiB **When** sent **Then** the probe exits 0 without reading the payload.

## Files
- `crates/tl-gpu-probe/Cargo.toml`: fill (E02-A1 created the skeleton)
- `crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/main.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/sampler.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/lib.rs` is not created: the tests drive `sampler::run` through a `#[cfg(test)]` module in `sampler.rs` with a thread on the other socket end

## Tests
- `main.rs::tests::parse_args_table`
- `sampler.rs::tests::hello_roundtrip_with_double`
- `sampler.rs::tests::proto_mismatch_exits_without_backend`
- `sampler.rs::tests::sample_before_hello_is_init_failed`
- `sampler.rs::tests::sample_echoes_seq`
- `sampler.rs::tests::shutdown_and_eof_exit_zero`
- `sampler.rs::tests::oversize_frame_exits`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: every protocol error is a silent exit 0; the engine owns the restart (ADR-007 failure table).
- Validity: N/A here; per-metric `Reading` is the backend's job.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one frame read and one write per request; no allocation beyond the payloads.
- Privacy: the probe never logs; stderr is inherited and used only by NVML itself.
- Security: the probe treats fd 3 input as untrusted: `read_frame` checks the length before allocating (E03-068); no other input.

## Notes
Depends on E02-A1, E03-A2. Wrapping fd 3 without `unsafe` (`FromRawFd` and `BorrowedFd::borrow_raw` are both `unsafe`): open `/proc/self/fd/<n>` with `rustix::fs::open(.., OFlags::RDWR | OFlags::CLOEXEC, Mode::empty())`, which returns an `OwnedFd` on the same socket; then `std::fs::File::from(owned_fd)`. Put a comment on that line saying why. Phase P1. Build rule applies (`heavy-build cargo test -p tl-gpu-probe`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Owner note (R-264): `sampler::HelloInfo { driver: String, nvml: String, devices: Vec<GpuDeviceInfo> }` is this crate's own struct, defined in `sampler.rs` by this bead, returned by `Backend::hello` and written into tl-model's `ProbeResponse::Hello { proto, driver, nvml, devices }` (as2.35) by the loop. The engine's `client::HelloInfo` (ndy.11) is a different struct; neither crate imports the other's.
