title: E13: NVML init, device enumeration and Hello (nvml.rs part 1)
description:
## Context
The NVML backend's initialisation and device enumeration: `nvmlInit_v2`, driver and NVML versions, every device's UUID, name, PCI bus id, memory total and power limit, mapped to the `Hello` response; an init failure becomes `InitFailed` with the ADR-007 kind so the engine can tell "no NVIDIA here" (`LibraryNotFound`, `DriverNotLoaded`: terminal `Unsupported` in the engine, never retried, R-155) from a real failure. Sources: ADR-007 (`Hello`, `InitFailure`, `GpuDeviceInfo`), PERF-062 (NVML calls for discovery), PERF-071 (driver version, CUDA version, VBIOS, architecture; see open item 12), E13-001 (`Backend`), E03-069.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/nvml.rs` (part 1):

```rust
pub struct NvmlBackend { nvml: Nvml, devices: Vec<DeviceSlot> }   // DeviceSlot { index: u32, uuid: [u8; 16], last_process_ts: u64 }
impl NvmlBackend { pub fn new() -> Self; }   // does not init; `hello` does, so the engine's 3 s Hello deadline covers nvmlInit
pub fn parse_uuid(s: &str) -> Option<[u8; 16]>;   // "GPU-xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx" → 16 bytes; "MIG-…" or malformed → None
pub fn classify_init_error(e: &NvmlError) -> (InitFailure, String);
// LibraryNotFound / LibloadingError → LibraryNotFound; DriverNotLoaded → DriverNotLoaded; NoPermission → NoPermission; everything else → Other; message = e.to_string()
impl Backend for NvmlBackend {
    fn hello(&mut self) -> Result<HelloInfo, InitFailed> {
        // Nvml::init() (nvmlInit_v2) → Err → classify; nvml.sys_driver_version(); nvml.sys_nvml_version();
        // device_count(); for i in 0..count: device_by_index(i): uuid (parse_uuid; a device whose UUID does not parse is skipped), name(), pci_info().bus_id (as returned, e.g. "00000000:2D:00.0"), memory_info().total, power_management_limit() (mW; Err(NotSupported) → None)
    }
    fn sample(..) { /* E13-003 */ }
}
```

PERF-071 also wants CUDA driver version (`nvml.sys_cuda_driver_version()`), VBIOS (`device.vbios_version()`), architecture (`device.architecture()`) and the kernel module version; `GpuDeviceInfo` (ADR-007) has no fields for them. Open item 9 recommends adding `cuda_version: Option<String>`, `vbios: Option<String>`, `architecture: Option<String>` to `GpuDeviceInfo` and `cuda` to `Hello`; this bead reads them into the response only when E03-069 has added the fields, otherwise it skips them and leaves a `// PERF-071: open item 12` comment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `"GPU-0a1b2c3d-4e5f-6071-8293-a4b5c6d7e8f9"` **When** parsed **Then** the 16 bytes `0a 1b 2c 3d 4e 5f 60 71 82 93 a4 b5 c6 d7 e8 f9`; `"MIG-…"` and `"GPU-zz"` → `None`.
- **Given** `NvmlError::LibraryNotFound` **When** classified **Then** `(LibraryNotFound, ..)`; `DriverNotLoaded` → `DriverNotLoaded`; `NoPermission` → `NoPermission`; `Unknown` → `Other`.
- **Given** the owner machine (`#[ignore]`) **When** `hello()` runs **Then** `Ok` with one device whose `name` contains `"5070"`, a 16-byte UUID, `pci_bus_id` ending in `2D:00.0`, `mem_total > 8 GiB`, `power_limit_mw` `Some` (U-35 recorded in the test output).
- **Given** a machine without `libnvidia-ml.so.1` (CI) **When** `hello()` runs **Then** `Err(InitFailed { kind: LibraryNotFound, .. })` and the process does not crash.

## Files
- `crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/nvml.rs`: create (part 1)
- `crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/main.rs`: `mod nvml;` and the `Sampler` arm `sampler::run(fd, nvml::NvmlBackend::new)` replacing E13-001's exit 3 placeholder (R-262)

## Tests
- `nvml.rs::tests::parse_uuid_table`
- `nvml.rs::tests::classify_init_error_table`
- `nvml.rs::tests::real_hello_5070` (`#[ignore]`, owner machine)
- `nvml.rs::tests::hello_without_library_is_init_failed` (runs where the library is absent; skips with a note when NVML initialises)

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `InitFailed` kinds as above; a per-device read error during `hello` skips that device (never a crash).
- Validity: N/A here.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: `nvmlInit` takes up to 2 s on first load; the engine's Hello deadline is 3 s.
- Privacy: N/A
- Security: NVML output is trusted as far as types go; strings are bounded by `String` from the wrapper.

## Notes
Depends on E13-001. `nvml-wrapper 0.13.0`: `Nvml::init()`, `Nvml::sys_driver_version()`, `sys_nvml_version()`, `sys_cuda_driver_version()`, `device_count()`, `device_by_index(u32) -> Device<'_>`, `Device::uuid()`, `name()`, `pci_info() -> PciInfo { bus_id, .. }`, `memory_info() -> MemoryInfo { total, used, free }`, `power_management_limit()`, `vbios_version()`, `architecture()`; errors `NvmlError::{LibraryNotFound, DriverNotLoaded, NoPermission, NotSupported, Unknown, LibloadingError(..)}`. Phase P1. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- `HelloInfo` here is `sampler::HelloInfo` from E13-001 (ndy.3), the probe's own struct (R-264).
close_reason: nvml.rs part 1: NvmlBackend, parse_uuid, classify_init_error, hello with CUDA/VBIOS/architecture; main.rs wires sampler::run; commits f147d25 a1884b5

title: E13: NVML per-device sample with Reading per metric
description:
## Context
Per-device totals for one `Sample`: utilisation, memory, encoder and decoder, temperature, power, clocks, fan and PCIe throughput, each as `Reading<T>` so an unsupported or failed metric is never encoded as zero. Sources: ADR-007 (`GpuDeviceSample`, `Reading`), PERF-063 (utilisation rates), PERF-064 (`nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo_v2`), PERF-065 (encoder, decoder), PERF-066 (clocks), PERF-067 (power), PERF-068 (temperature, fan), PERF-070 (PCIe throughput), E13-002.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/nvml.rs`:

```rust
pub fn reading<T>(r: Result<T, NvmlError>) -> Reading<T>;   // Ok → Ok; Err(NotSupported) → Unsupported; any other Err → Failed
pub fn device_sample(dev: &Device<'_>, uuid: [u8; 16]) -> GpuDeviceSample;
```

`device_sample` field by field (each call independent; one failure never skips the others):
- `util_pct`, `mem_util_pct`: `dev.utilization_rates()` → `.gpu`, `.memory` (one call, both fields share its `Reading`).
- `mem_used`: `dev.memory_info()` `.used` (the wrapper calls `nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo_v2` when available).
- `enc_pct`: `dev.encoder_utilization()` `.utilization`; `dec_pct`: `dev.decoder_utilization()` `.utilization`.
- `temp_c`: `dev.temperature(TemperatureSensor::Gpu)`.
- `power_mw`: `dev.power_usage()`.
- `clock_gfx_mhz`: `dev.clock_info(Clock::Graphics)`; `clock_mem_mhz`: `dev.clock_info(Clock::Memory)`.
- `fan_pct`: `dev.fan_speed(0)`; `Err(NotSupported)` on a fanless card → `Unsupported`.
- `pcie_rx_kbps`: `dev.pcie_throughput(PcieUtilCounter::Receive)`; `pcie_tx_kbps`: `.. ::Send` (NVML reports KB/s over a 20 ms window).
`Backend::sample` (part): `t_ns` from `CLOCK_BOOTTIME`, then `device_sample` for every slot in index order; `processes` is E13-004.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `Ok(5u32)` **When** `reading` runs **Then** `Reading::Ok(5)`; `Err(NotSupported)` → `Unsupported`; `Err(Unknown)` → `Failed`; `Err(GpuIsLost)` → `Failed`.
- **Given** the owner machine (`#[ignore]`) **When** `device_sample` runs on device 0 **Then** `util_pct`, `mem_used`, `temp_c`, `power_mw`, `clock_gfx_mhz`, `clock_mem_mhz` are `Ok(_)`, `temp_c` is between 10 and 110, `mem_used <= mem_total`, and `fan_pct` is `Ok(_)` or `Unsupported` (the test prints which, for U-35).
- **Given** two consecutive samples 1 s apart on the owner machine **When** compared **Then** both complete in under 50 ms each (printed), so the 500 ms deadline has margin.

## Files
- `crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/nvml.rs`: extend

## Tests
- `nvml.rs::tests::reading_mapping`
- `nvml.rs::tests::real_device_sample_fields` (`#[ignore]`)
- `nvml.rs::tests::real_sample_under_50ms` (`#[ignore]`)

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: per metric `Reading::Failed`; a device that returns `GpuIsLost` on every call still produces a sample of `Failed` readings (the engine shows `Failed`, never zero).
- Validity: `Reading` → `Validity` mapping is `tl-model`'s (`Reading::validity`).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: 11 NVML calls per device per second; well under the 500 ms deadline.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
Depends on E13-002. nvml-wrapper 0.13.0 enums: `enum_wrappers::device::{TemperatureSensor, Clock, PcieUtilCounter}`; `Device::utilization_rates() -> Utilization { gpu, memory }`, `encoder_utilization() -> UtilizationInfo { utilization, sampling_period }`, `decoder_utilization()`, `temperature(sensor)`, `power_usage()` (mW), `clock_info(clock)` (MHz), `fan_speed(index)`, `pcie_throughput(counter)` (KB/s). Phase P1. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
close_reason: reading() and device_sample() in nvml.rs; Backend::sample fills device samples in index order (668f517). Test limit raised to 100 ms per R-277 with a comment on the 20 ms NVML PCIe window (4772e7b). U-35: fan_pct reads Ok(0) at idle on the RTX 5070 Ti.

title: E13: NVML per-process utilisation and memory rows
description:
## Context
Per-process GPU data for the GPU, VRAM, GPU engine, encode and decode columns: utilisation from `process_utilization_stats(last_seen_timestamp)` and memory from the running graphics and compute process lists, summed per pid across devices by the engine. Requested only when a GPU process column is visible (`Sample { processes: true }`). U-12 (per-process utilisation works unprivileged on driver 615) is recorded by the real test. Sources: ADR-007 (per-process data, `GpuProcessSample`), PROC-033 (GPU column sources), U-12, E13-003.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/nvml.rs`:

```rust
pub fn process_samples(dev: &Device<'_>, uuid: [u8; 16], last_seen: &mut u64) -> Vec<GpuProcessSample>;
pub fn merge_process_rows(util: &[ProcessUtilizationSample], graphics: &[ProcessInfo], compute: &[ProcessInfo], uuid: [u8; 16], util_supported: Reading<()>) -> Vec<GpuProcessSample>;   // pure, tested with fixtures
```

`process_samples`: `let util = dev.process_utilization_stats(*last_seen)`; on `Ok(v)` set `*last_seen` to the max `timestamp` in `v` (NVML returns samples newer than `last_seen`; a first call with 0 returns the recent window); `Err(NotSupported)` → `util_supported = Unsupported`; `Err(NotFound)` (no process ran since `last_seen`) → empty util list, still `Ok`; other `Err` → `Failed`. `graphics = dev.running_graphics_processes()`, `compute = dev.running_compute_processes()` (both `Err` → empty lists and memory readings `Failed`). `merge_process_rows`: one row per distinct pid over the three lists; `sm_pct`, `mem_pct`, `enc_pct`, `dec_pct` from the util sample of that pid (several samples for one pid in the window → the newest), or `util_supported`'s state when the pid has no sample (`Unsupported` or `Failed`), or `Ok(0)` when util is supported and the pid simply had no activity; `mem_used`: `UsedGpuMemory::Used(bytes)` summed over the graphics and compute entries of that pid (a pid can be in both lists; sum them, that is what MC and nvidia-smi show), `UsedGpuMemory::Unavailable` → `Unsupported`; a pid only in the util list → `mem_used: Unsupported`. Pid 0 rows are dropped. `Backend::sample(.., processes: true)` collects `process_samples` for every slot into `Some(vec)`; `processes: false` → `None` and `last_seen` is left untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** util samples for pid 100 (sm 30, enc 0, dec 0, mem 10) and pid 200, graphics `[100: Used(1 GiB)]`, compute `[100: Used(512 MiB), 300: Unavailable]` **When** merged with util supported **Then** rows for 100 (`sm Ok(30)`, `mem_used Ok(1.5 GiB)`), 200 (`mem_used Unsupported`), 300 (`sm Ok(0)`, `mem_used Unsupported`), in pid order.
- **Given** two util samples for pid 100 with timestamps 5 and 9 **When** merged **Then** the row uses the timestamp-9 values.
- **Given** `util_supported = Unsupported` and graphics `[100: Used(1 GiB)]` **When** merged **Then** row 100 has `sm Unsupported` and `mem_used Ok(1 GiB)`.
- **Given** a util sample with pid 0 **When** merged **Then** no row for pid 0.
- **Given** the owner machine with a running GPU process (`#[ignore]`, the test starts `glxgears` or skips with a note) **When** two samples 1 s apart run with `processes: true` **Then** the second has a row for that pid with `sm_pct` `Ok(_)` (U-12 recorded as verified) and `last_seen` increased.

## Files
- `crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/nvml.rs`: extend

## Tests
- `nvml.rs::tests::merge_rows_sum_memory_and_newest_util`
- `nvml.rs::tests::merge_newest_sample_wins`
- `nvml.rs::tests::merge_util_unsupported_keeps_memory`
- `nvml.rs::tests::merge_drops_pid_zero`
- `nvml.rs::tests::real_process_utilization_u12` (`#[ignore]`)

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: as above; never divides device utilisation among processes (ADR-007).
- Validity: per field `Reading`.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: three NVML calls per device per second when requested; `process_utilization_stats` allocates its sample buffer per call (the wrapper sizes it from a count query).
- Privacy: pids only; the probe never reads `/proc`.

## Notes
Depends on E13-003. nvml-wrapper 0.13.0: `Device::process_utilization_stats(last_seen_timestamp: u64) -> Result<Vec<ProcessUtilizationSample { pid, timestamp, sm_util, mem_util, enc_util, dec_util }>>`, `running_graphics_processes() -> Vec<ProcessInfo { pid, used_gpu_memory: UsedGpuMemory::{Used(u64), Unavailable}, .. }>` (uses the `_v3` entry point when present), `running_compute_processes()`. Phase P1. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
close_reason: process_samples, merge_process_rows and Backend::sample(processes: true) in nvml.rs; 4 merge tests plus real U-12 test pass on driver 615.71.09. Commit 426c921

title: E13: --fake <script> backend and fake_scripts.rs
description:
## Context
`tl-gpu-probe --fake <script>` (feature `fake`) is the test double the engine's integration tests drive: it replies like a one-GPU machine, or sleeps 2 s on a request, or crashes with SIGSEGV, or sends an oversize frame, or reports an init failure. It uses the same `sampler::run` loop, so the framing path is the real one. Sources: ADR-007 (verification: fake probe scripts "replies normally, sleeps 2 s, crashes with SIGSEGV, or sends an oversize frame"), E13-001 (`Backend`, `Mode::Fake`), E13-012 (the consumer).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/fake.rs` (`#[cfg(feature = "fake")]`):

```rust
pub const SCRIPTS: &[&str] = &["normal", "sleep-on-sample", "sleep-on-hello", "segv-on-sample", "segv-on-hello", "oversize-on-sample", "init-library-not-found", "init-driver-not-loaded", "init-no-permission", "exit-after-3", "proto-mismatch"];
pub struct FakeBackend { script: Script, samples: u32 }
impl FakeBackend { pub fn from_script(s: &str) -> Self; }   // unknown script → prints the list to stderr and exits 2
```

Behaviour per script (the fake device: uuid `[0x42; 16]`, name `"Fake GPU 5070"`, `pci_bus_id "00000000:2D:00.0"`, `mem_total` 16 GiB, `power_limit_mw Some(300_000)`; sample values: `util_pct Ok(seq % 100)`, `mem_used Ok(2 GiB + seq MiB)`, `temp_c Ok(45)`, `power_mw Ok(31_900)`, `clock_gfx_mhz Ok(1905)`, `clock_mem_mhz Ok(7001)`, `fan_pct Unsupported`, `enc_pct Ok(0)`, `dec_pct Ok(0)`, `mem_util_pct Ok(seq % 50)`, `pcie_rx_kbps Ok(1000)`, `pcie_tx_kbps Ok(2000)`; with `processes: true` one row `pid = std::process::id()` of the probe's parent (`getppid()`), `sm_pct Ok(12)`, `mem_used Ok(256 MiB)`, so the engine test maps a live pid):
- `normal`: always answers.
- `sleep-on-sample`: the first `Sample` sleeps 2 s before answering (the engine's 500 ms deadline fires); later samples answer at once.
- `sleep-on-hello`: `hello()` sleeps 5 s (the 3 s Hello deadline fires).
- `segv-on-sample` / `segv-on-hello`: raise `SIGSEGV` on itself with `rustix::process::kill_process(rustix::process::getpid(), rustix::process::Signal::Segv)` (no `unsafe`), on the first `Sample` or inside `hello()`.
- `oversize-on-sample`: on the first `Sample` write a frame whose prefix says `MAX_PROBE_FRAME + 1` followed by 16 zero bytes, then exit 0.
- `init-*`: `hello()` returns the matching `InitFailed`.
- `exit-after-3`: answers three samples, then exits 0 on the fourth request (clean child exit).
- `proto-mismatch`: handled in `sampler::run` by answering `Hello { proto: 99 }` when this script is active (a hook `Backend::hello_proto() -> u16` with default `PROTO`).

`crates/tl-gpu-probe/tests/fake_scripts.rs` (feature `fake`, uses `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_tl-gpu-probe")`): spawns the binary with `--fake <script> --fd <n>` over a socketpair. Tests may not use `unsafe`, so no `pre_exec` and no `dup2`: the test clears `CLOEXEC` on the child's socket end with `rustix::io::fcntl_setfd(fd, FdFlags::empty())` and passes that fd number as `--fd <n>`; the child inherits it. Cases: `normal` Hello and 3 samples with increasing `seq`; `proto-mismatch` answers proto 99; `init-library-not-found` answers `InitFailed { LibraryNotFound }`; `segv-on-sample` dies with signal 11 (`ExitStatus::signal() == Some(11)`); `oversize-on-sample` makes `read_frame` return `TooLarge` and the child exits 0; `exit-after-3` exits 0 on the fourth request; `sleep-on-sample` takes at least 2 s to answer the first sample.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** each script in `SCRIPTS` **When** `from_script` runs **Then** it returns a backend; `"bogus"` exits 2 with the list on stderr.
- **Given** `cargo test -p tl-gpu-probe --features fake --test fake_scripts` **When** run **Then** every case above passes in under 20 s total.
- **Given** `cargo build -p tl-gpu-probe` (no `fake` feature) **When** run **Then** `--fake` is rejected with the usage text and exit 2.

## Files
- `crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/fake.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/main.rs`: `#[cfg(feature = "fake")] mod fake;`, the `Fake` arm `sampler::run(fd, fake::FakeBackend::from_script)` replacing E13-001's exit 3 placeholder (R-262)
- `crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/sampler.rs`: the `hello_proto` hook
- `crates/tl-gpu-probe/tests/fake_scripts.rs`: create

## Tests
- `fake.rs::tests::every_script_builds`
- `tests/fake_scripts.rs::normal_hello_and_samples`, `proto_mismatch_99`, `init_failure_kinds`, `segv_dies_with_signal_11`, `oversize_frame_is_too_large`, `exit_after_three`, `sleep_on_sample_delays`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: N/A
- Security: the `fake` feature is off in release builds and the packaged binary (E33 PKGBUILD builds without it); the engine never passes `--fake`.

## Notes
Depends on E13-001. The `--fd <n>` inheritance trick keeps tests free of `unsafe`; the engine's real spawn uses `pre_exec` + `dup2` in `gpu/spawn.rs` (E13-008), the one allowed `unsafe` file. Phase P1. Build rule applies (`heavy-build cargo test -p tl-gpu-probe --features fake`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
close_reason: fake.rs FakeBackend with 11 scripts, Backend::hello_proto hook, main.rs Fake arm, tests/fake_scripts.rs (8 cases). Commits d82a8b8, c4a61ca, 9a5eafe

title: E13: --api-versions one-shot mode with ash and khronos-egl
description:
## Context
`tl-gpu-probe --api-versions` is the one-shot mode that reads the Vulkan and OpenGL versions per GPU for the Information tab and the GPU page static rows, in its own short-lived process so a driver crash only costs those two rows. It loads Vulkan through `ash` and EGL through `khronos-egl` at run time, writes one `ApiVersions` frame to stdout and exits 0. Sources: ADR-007 ("API versions mode"), R-087, PERF-071, E03-069 (`ApiVersions`, `GpuApiVersions`), E13-001 (`Mode::ApiVersions`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/api_versions.rs` (feature `api-versions`, default on):

```rust
pub fn run() -> std::process::ExitCode;   // collect(), write_frame(stdout, &ApiVersions { devices }, MAX_PROBE_FRAME), exit 0; any panic is caught with catch_unwind and still exits 0 with an empty list
pub fn collect() -> Vec<GpuApiVersions>;
pub fn vulkan_devices() -> Vec<(String /* pci_bus_id */, String /* api */, Option<String> /* driver info */)>;
pub fn opengl_version(pci_bus_id: &str) -> Option<String>;
pub fn pci_bus_id_from_vk(domain: u32, bus: u32, device: u32, function: u32) -> String;   // "{domain:08X}:{bus:02X}:{device:02X}.{function}" so it matches NVML's "00000000:2D:00.0"
pub fn version_string(v: u32) -> String;   // ash::vk::api_version_major/minor/patch → "1.4.312"
```

`vulkan_devices`: `ash::Entry::load()` (`Err` → empty); `create_instance` with `VK_API_VERSION_1_1` and no layers; `enumerate_physical_devices`; for each: `get_physical_device_properties2` with `PhysicalDevicePCIBusInfoPropertiesEXT` chained (skip devices whose extension list lacks `VK_EXT_pci_bus_info`) and `PhysicalDeviceDriverProperties` chained (`driverInfo` as the driver string, `None` when the extension is missing); `apiVersion` → `version_string`. Destroy the instance.
`opengl_version`: `khronos_egl::DynamicInstance::<EGL1_5>::load_required()` (`Err` → `None`); query `EGL_EXT_platform_device` via `eglQueryDevicesEXT`; for each device read `EGL_DRM_DEVICE_FILE_EXT` and match it to the GPU by reading `/sys/class/drm/<card>/device` → PCI slot name equal to `pci_bus_id` (after normalising to the NVML form); `eglGetPlatformDisplayEXT(EGL_PLATFORM_DEVICE_EXT, dev)`, `eglInitialize`, `eglBindAPI(EGL_OPENGL_API)`, a config with `EGL_SURFACE_TYPE = EGL_PBUFFER_BIT`, `eglCreateContext`, `eglMakeCurrent` with `EGL_NO_SURFACE` (needs `EGL_KHR_surfaceless_context`; without it a 1x1 pbuffer), then `glGetString(GL_VERSION)` loaded through `eglGetProcAddress("glGetString")`; the string as `String`; everything torn down. Any step failing → `None`.
`collect`: for each Vulkan device: `GpuApiVersions { pci_bus_id, vulkan_api: Some(api), vulkan_driver, opengl: opengl_version(&pci_bus_id) }`; GPUs seen only by EGL are added with `vulkan_api: None`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `(0, 0x2d, 0, 0)` **When** `pci_bus_id_from_vk` runs **Then** `"00000000:2D:00.0"`.
- **Given** `ash::vk::make_api_version(0, 1, 4, 312)` **When** `version_string` runs **Then** `"1.4.312"`.
- **Given** the owner machine (`#[ignore]`) **When** `tl-gpu-probe --api-versions` runs **Then** it exits 0 within 5 s and the frame holds one device with `pci_bus_id "00000000:2D:00.0"`, `vulkan_api` starting with `"1."`, `vulkan_driver` containing `"615"`, and `opengl` starting with `"4."`.
- **Given** a machine with no Vulkan ICD and no EGL (CI) **When** the mode runs **Then** it exits 0 with an empty device list.
- **Given** `cargo build -p tl-gpu-probe --no-default-features` **When** run **Then** `--api-versions` exits 3 with "api-versions not built".

## Files
- `crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/api_versions.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/main.rs`: `#[cfg(feature = "api-versions")] mod api_versions;`, the arm
- `crates/tl-gpu-probe/Cargo.toml`: `ash` and `khronos-egl` under the feature (workspace pins; both `default-features = false` with the dynamic-loading feature: `ash` feature `loaded`, `khronos-egl` feature `dynamic`)

## Tests
- `api_versions.rs::tests::pci_bus_id_format`
- `api_versions.rs::tests::version_string_format`
- `api_versions.rs::tests::real_api_versions_owner` (`#[ignore]`)
- `api_versions.rs::tests::no_drivers_gives_empty` (runs where neither library loads; skips otherwise)

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: never an error exit for missing drivers; the engine maps a crash, timeout or non-zero exit to `Unknown` fields (E13-011).
- Validity: a missing value is `None`, shown as `Unknown` (PERF-071).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one Vulkan instance and one EGL context per GPU, once per app start; under 5 s.
- Privacy: N/A
- Security: `ash` and `khronos-egl` with dynamic loading need no `unsafe` in this crate's code only if their safe wrappers suffice; `ash` calls are `unsafe` by design. ADR-001 rule 4 lists `crates/tl-gpu-probe/src/api_versions.rs` as the fourth file allowed to hold `unsafe` (R-143): it starts with `#![allow(unsafe_code)]` and every `unsafe` block has a `// SAFETY:` comment.

## Notes
Depends on E13-001. The `unsafe` allowance for `api_versions.rs` is settled (R-143). `khronos-egl` 6 `DynamicInstance`; `ash` 0.38 `Entry::load`, `vk::PhysicalDevicePCIBusInfoPropertiesEXT`, `vk::PhysicalDeviceDriverProperties`. Phase P2. Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc command through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
close_reason: api_versions.rs with ash =0.38.0 and khronos-egl =6.0.0, wired into main.rs; ed506c4, fix-up 3756c6a

title: E13: gpu/mod.rs: probe lookup order, ProbeError, deadlines
description:
## Context
The engine side of the GPU probe starts with the module root: where the probe binary is looked up (`$TASKLENS_GPU_PROBE`, the running binary's directory, `/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-gpu-probe`), the engine's `ProbeError` type, and the deadline constants every later bead uses. A missing binary is the expected condition "GPU probe not installed", not a failure. Sources: ADR-007 (process lookup, deadlines, failure table), ADR-015 (`ProbeError` is one of the named error enums), PERF-062 (lookup order, "GPU probe not installed"), E08-A1 (`lib.rs` chain edit).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/gpu/mod.rs`:

```rust
pub mod spawn; pub mod client;   // E13-008, E13-009 add their files; this bead adds the `mod` lines with empty files
pub const PROBE_ENV: &str = "TASKLENS_GPU_PROBE";
pub const PROBE_NAME: &str = "tl-gpu-probe";
pub const PROBE_SYSTEM_PATH: &str = "/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-gpu-probe";
pub const HELLO_DEADLINE: Duration = Duration::from_millis(3000);
pub const SAMPLE_DEADLINE: Duration = Duration::from_millis(500);
pub const SHUTDOWN_GRACE: Duration = Duration::from_millis(200);
pub const API_VERSIONS_DEADLINE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);
pub const NOT_INSTALLED: &str = "GPU probe not installed";
pub const VERSION_MISMATCH: &str = "probe version mismatch";

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum ProbeError {
    #[error("{NOT_INSTALLED}")] NotInstalled,
    #[error("spawn: {0}")] Spawn(Arc<str>),
    #[error("protocol: {0}")] Protocol(Arc<str>),          // WireError text
    #[error("deadline {0:?} missed")] Deadline(Duration),
    #[error("probe exited: {0}")] Exited(Arc<str>),        // "status 0", "signal 11", ...
    #[error("{VERSION_MISMATCH}: got {0}")] VersionMismatch(u16),
    #[error("init failed: {kind:?}: {message}")] InitFailed { kind: InitFailure, message: Arc<str> },
}
impl From<ProbeError> for WorkerError { fn from(e: ProbeError) -> Self { WorkerError::Probe(e.to_string().into()) } }

pub fn locate_probe(env: Option<&OsStr>, current_exe: Option<&Path>) -> Option<PathBuf>;
// 1. env set and non-empty → that path if it is a regular file (else None: an explicit override that is wrong is not silently replaced)
// 2. current_exe.parent()/tl-gpu-probe if it is an executable regular file
// 3. PROBE_SYSTEM_PATH if it is an executable regular file
pub fn locate() -> Option<PathBuf>;   // locate_probe(std::env::var_os(PROBE_ENV).as_deref(), std::env::current_exe().ok().as_deref())
```

`crates/tl-engine/src/lib.rs`: `pub mod gpu;` (chain edit, one line).

title: E25: MemoryPage: Physical memory, Commit and Swap charts, page menu checks, demand (pages/performance/memory.rs)
description:
## Context
The Memory page stacks up to three charts (Physical memory, Commit, Swap) above the composition bar and the Details grid. This bead writes the page entity, its charts, the two page-menu check items and its demand; the bar is E25-002 and the Details rows E25-003. Sources: PERF-041, PERF-026 (legend), PERF-018, UI-PRF-026 (anatomy, interaction, data binding), UI-PRF-020 (frame), table (a) `performance.memory_composition`, `performance.memory_swap_graph`, table (d).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/memory.rs`:

```rust
pub struct MemoryPage {
    key: DeviceKey, row: DeviceRow,
    physical: Entity<ChartView>, commit: Entity<ChartView>, swap: Entity<ChartView>,
    // E25-002: bar: Option<CompositionBarState> (added by o55.3 as a chain edit, R-262)
    details: KeyValueModel,                    // E25-003 fills the rows
    show_composition: bool, show_swap: bool,   // settings mirrors
    swap_total: u64,
    hub, demand, active: bool,
    #[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-hooks"))] pub render_count: Cell<u32>,
}
impl MemoryPage { pub fn new(key, row, hub, demand, cx) -> Self; pub fn set_active(&mut self, on: bool, cx); }
impl DevicePage for MemoryPage { .. }
impl Render for MemoryPage { .. }   // DevicePageFrame { page: self, .. }
```

Charts (each `W × GRAPH_H_STACKED` 150, `sp4` apart, `background: Window`, grid lines on, `range_ns` from `performance.graph_range_s`, `smooth` from `motion.smooth_graphs`):
1. Physical memory: `ChartSpec { series: [used: fill mem_fill, line mem_line; committed: no fill, line mem_line, dashed; dirty: no fill, line mem_line at alpha 0.6, line_width 1 px], y: FixedTotal(MemTotal) }`, `ChartLabels { heading: Some("Physical memory"), value_fmt: Bytes, value_align: Right, range_word: "Memory usage", legend: [("Used", Solid), ("Committed", Dashed)], show_axis_max: false }`. Value = used bytes (`34.68 GiB`). The dirty series has no legend entry.
2. Commit: `series: [commit: fill mem_fill, line mem_line]`, `y: Commit(CommitLimit)`, labels `heading: Some("Commit")`, `value_fmt: Percent`, `range_word: "Commit"`, `show_axis_max: true` (the axis text shows when the peak is above 100%). Value = `Committed_AS / CommitLimit` (`69.0%`). Heading tooltip `Committed memory against the commit limit. It can exceed 100%.`
3. Swap: `series: [swap used: fill mem_fill, line mem_line]`, `y: FixedTotal(SwapTotal)`, labels `heading: Some("Swap")`, `value_fmt: Bytes`, `range_word: "Swap usage"`. Hidden when `SwapTotal == 0` or `show_swap == false`.

Series ids: `SeriesId { device: row.idx, metric }` with `MetricId::MEM_USED`, `MetricId::MEM_COMMIT` (committed bytes), `MetricId::SWAP_USED`, and the dirty-bytes constant from E03-A1 (plan open item 1; until it exists the dirty series is omitted behind a `// TODO(E03-A1)`). The commit chart draws `MEM_COMMIT` against `Commit(limit)`; the percent value is computed from the newest sample and `CommitLimit`. Totals (`MemTotal`, `CommitLimit`, `SwapTotal`) come from `Snapshot.system` memory totals (`SYSTEM`); a change rebuilds the specs through `ChartView::set_spec`.

Behaviour:
- `header()` = `("Memory", "")`. `toggles()` = empty. `graphs()` = the visible charts in a `v_flex` with `sp4` gaps; the composition bar (E25-002) below after `sp6` when `show_composition`.
- Hiding and showing a chart or the bar animates height 150 → 0 over `m_base` with `with_animation`; instant under `cx.reduce_motion()` or `motion.animations == false`.
- `menu_items`: `Show memory composition` check item (checked when `show_composition`) → `PerfToggleMemoryComposition`; `Show swap usage` check item → `PerfToggleMemorySwapGraph`. Handlers on the page root flip `settings.performance.memory_composition` / `memory_swap_graph` through `TlSettings::update`; the page observes the `performance` section and mirrors both flags.
- Demand (this page's surface, while `active`): `memory: true`; everything else false. `set_active(false)` removes the surface.
- `set_state` on every chart follows `Snapshot.health` for `SourceId::Memory` (`Failed(last_error)` → `ChartState::Failed`); the charts derive WarmingUp and Stale themselves.
- `focus_order()` = empty. `copy_text` is E25-029 (until then: header plus `details.copy_into`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `SwapTotal = 0` **When** rendered **Then** only two charts are in the graph area (`memory_swap_graph_hidden_without_swap`).
- **Given** `SwapTotal = 32 GiB` and `memory_swap_graph = false` **When** rendered **Then** the Swap chart is absent; after `PerfToggleMemorySwapGraph` it is present and the setting is true.
- **Given** a commit series whose peak in view is 112% of `CommitLimit` **When** rendered **Then** the Commit chart's axis max text reads `112%` (`commit_axis_text_above_100`).
- **Given** `MemTotal = 63.16 GiB` and newest used `34.68 GiB` **When** rendered **Then** the Physical memory value text is `34.68 GiB` and the chart's `y == FixedTotal(63.16 GiB bytes)`.
- **Given** the page active **When** demand is read **Then** `memory == true` and `disks == false`; inactive, the surface contributes nothing.
- **Given** `cx.reduce_motion() == true` **When** the Swap chart is hidden **Then** the height change is instant (no animation frames requested).


Flow: `PerfEject { key }` (handler in `disk.rs`) sends the eject command (plan open item E25-OI-1: `Command::Eject(DeviceIdx)`; stop and report if absent). The engine answers through the disk record's eject state in `Snapshot.system`: `Idle`, `Running`, `Blocked(groups)`, `Done`, `Failed(reason)`. `Blocked` opens this window (or updates it); `Done` closes it and shows the toast `Disk ejected`; `Failed` shows the toast `Could not eject the disk: {reason}`.

Content: line `These programs are using Disk 1 (SanDisk Ultra):` (`t_base`), then per app a group header row (app icon 16 px, app name `t_sm` 500) and process rows 28 px (name, PID in `text_secondary`, open paths joined with `, ` in `t_xs` `text_secondary`, end ellipsis, tooltip with all paths), each with an `End Task` `TlButton` small danger-outline (`Secondary` with `status.danger` text and border) at the right; while Shift is held (`window.modifiers().shift`, tracked through `on_modifiers_changed`) every row button reads `End Process`. Footer right-aligned: `Close` (default, `Secondary`), `Retry` (`Secondary`), `End All` (`Danger`). A note `Processes of other users may also hold this disk` (`text_secondary`) above the footer when `eacces_note`.

Actions: `End Task` = `ActionKind::Signal(Term)` on that `ProcessKey`, `End Process` = `Signal(Kill)`, `End All` = `Signal(Term)` (or `Kill` with Shift) on every listed key; all through `ActionTracker::track` (E16-A3) with the E22-A2 process toast texts. Confirmation (R-036, D-009): `End All` with more than one process, and any action on another user's or a PROTECTED process, first opens the E22-A2 confirmation dialog with its texts (`End 3 processes?` form for multi-target; the protected text for protected); a single End Task on the user's own non-protected process does not ask. After an end action's summary event, `Retry` runs automatically after 500 ms (`cx.background_executor().timer`), once per action. `Retry` re-sends the eject command. `Close` closes the window; Esc = Close.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the disk record turns `Blocked` with 2 apps and 3 processes **When** installed **Then** the window opens with 2 group headers and 3 rows, each with `End Task` (`disk_in_use_layout`).
- **Given** Shift pressed **When** modifiers change **Then** every row button reads `End Process`; released, `End Task` (`disk_in_use_shift_relabels`).
- **Given** `End Task` on the user's own non-protected process **When** clicked **Then** `ActionRequest { kind: Signal(Term), targets: [key] }` is tracked with no dialog.
- **Given** `End All` with 3 processes **When** clicked **Then** the confirmation dialog opens first; confirming tracks one request with 3 targets.
- **Given** an action summary `Succeeded` **When** received **Then** the eject command is re-sent after 500 ms.
- **Given** the record turns `Done` **When** installed **Then** the window closes and the toast `Disk ejected` is pushed.
- **Given** `eacces_note = true` **When** rendered **Then** the note line is present above the footer.

title: E25: memory composition bar element: five segments, hatching, min width, labels, tooltips, hover (pages/performance/memory_bar.rs)
description:
## Context
Under the memory charts a 24 px bar shows In use, In use (compressed), Modified, Standby and Free as proportional segments with tooltips. This bead writes the custom element and its geometry. Sources: PERF-042 (segments, tooltip rule), UI-PRF-027 (anatomy, colours, min width, labels, hatching, tooltips, states), UI-FND-019 (`TlTooltip`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/memory_bar.rs`:

```rust
pub struct Composition { pub in_use: u64, pub compressed: u64, pub modified: u64, pub standby: u64, pub free: u64, pub total: u64 }
pub struct Segment { pub kind: SegmentKind, pub x0: f32, pub x1: f32 }   // logical px, chart-local
pub enum SegmentKind { InUse, Compressed, Modified, Standby, Free }
pub fn layout(c: &Composition, width: f32) -> SmallVec<[Segment; 5]>;   // proportional to bytes / total; a non-zero segment is at least 2 px; widths rebalanced from the largest segment so the sum stays `width`
pub fn tooltip_text(kind: SegmentKind, bytes: u64) -> SharedString;
pub struct CompositionBar { pub composition: Option<Composition> /* None = WarmingUp */, pub hover: Option<SegmentKind> }
impl Element for CompositionBar { .. }  // request_layout: height 24 × ui_scale, width fill; prepaint: one hitbox per segment only while the pointer is inside the bar bounds; paint: quads plus one hatch path
pub struct CompositionBarState { pub composition: Option<Composition>, pub hover: Option<SegmentKind>, pub hatch: Option<gpui::Path<Pixels>>, pub hatch_key: (u32, u32) }  // kept by MemoryPage; hatch rebuilt when the compressed segment's physical x0..x1 changes
```

Values (PERF-042, from `Snapshot.system` memory fields, `SYSTEM`): `free = MemFree`; `modified = Dirty + Writeback`; `compressed = zram mem_used_total + Zswap`, clamped to `in_use`; `in_use = MemTotal − MemAvailable − compressed`; `standby = MemTotal − in_use − compressed − modified − free`, clamped at 0.

Rendering (× `ui_scale`): caption `Memory composition` `t_sm` 400 `text_secondary` above the bar; bar height 24, radius `r_sm`, 1 px `divider` outline; segments left to right In use (`mem_line` alpha 1.0), In use (compressed) (`mem_line` alpha 0.8 with hatching: 1 px diagonal lines every 4 px in `window_bg` at alpha 0.5, one `paint_path` per rebuild), Modified (`status.warning` alpha 0.8), Standby (`mem_line` alpha 0.35), Free (`window_bg`). Segment label (`t_xs` 400, `text_selected_primary` on the dark segments, `text_secondary` on Free) drawn only when the segment is at least 72 px wide. Hover: that segment at alpha +0.15 and its tooltip. `WarmingUp` (`composition == None`): outline only, caption `Collecting…`.

Tooltips (exact, sizes in table (d) IEC form):
- `In use: 20.11 GiB. Memory used by running programs and the kernel.`
- `In use (compressed): 1.02 GiB. Memory held compressed in zram or zswap.`
- `Modified: 120.00 MiB. Dirty pages waiting to be written to disk.`
- `Standby: 12.40 GiB. Cache the kernel can drop.`
- `Free: 28.60 GiB. Unused memory.`

`MemoryPage` (E25-001) owns `CompositionBarState`, recomputes `Composition` on `SYSTEM` and renders the bar below the charts when `show_composition`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a composition whose five values sum to `total` **When** `layout(c, 600)` runs **Then** the segment edges are contiguous from 0 to 600 and each width is within 0.5 px of `bytes / total × 600` except where the 2 px rule applies (`composition_segments_sum_to_total`).
- **Given** `modified = 1 KiB` out of 64 GiB **When** laid out at 600 px **Then** the Modified segment is exactly 2 px wide and the largest segment gives up the difference (`composition_min_width_2px`).
- **Given** `in_use = 20.11 GiB` **When** `tooltip_text(InUse, ..)` runs **Then** the text is `In use: 20.11 GiB. Memory used by running programs and the kernel.` (`composition_tooltip_texts` covers all five).
- **Given** a segment 60 px wide **When** painted **Then** no label is drawn for it; at 72 px the label is drawn.
- **Given** `composition == None` **When** painted **Then** only the outline is drawn and the caption reads `Collecting…`.
- **Given** the pointer outside the bar **When** prepaint runs **Then** no hitboxes are inserted.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/memory_bar.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/memory.rs`: change (add the field `bar: Option<CompositionBarState>` to `MemoryPage` at the `// E25-002` comment with `None` init, R-262; owns the state, renders the bar)

Memory used by running programs and the kernel.`, `perf-mem-tip-compressed = In use (compressed): {$size}. Memory held compressed in zram or zswap.`, `perf-mem-tip-modified = Modified: {$size}. Dirty pages waiting to be written to disk.`, `perf-mem-tip-standby = Standby: {$size}. Cache the kernel can drop.`, `perf-mem-tip-free = Free: {$size}. Unused memory.` (chain edit)
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_device_pages.rs`: change

## Tests

- `memory_bar::tests::composition_min_width_2px`
- `memory_bar::tests::composition_tooltip_texts`
- `ui_device_pages.rs::composition_label_min_72px`

title: E25: SMART window smartctl fallback button "Read with smartctl (admin)"
description:

title: E25: Memory Details grid P1 rows (In use to Kernel slab, Swap, Compressed, Savings, Huge pages) with hidden-row rules
description:
## Context
The Memory Details grid has 16 rows; this bead fills the 11 P1 rows from `/proc/meminfo` and zram data and applies the hidden-when-missing rules. The five DIMM rows are E25-011. Sources: PERF-043 (rows, formulas), UI-PRF-028 (row table, tooltips, phases), PERF-013 (words), table (d).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/performance/memory.rs`:

```rust
pub fn memory_details_model() -> KeyValueModel;   // 16 rows in UI-PRF-028 order; rows 7 to 11 start hidden until E25-011 fills them
pub fn update_memory_details(model: &mut KeyValueModel, mem: &<SystemSnapshot memory record>, zram: &<zram totals>) -> bool;  // returns true when any row changed
```

Rows (label, example, rule), grid order 1 to 16:
1. `In use` `20.11 GiB` (MemTotal − MemAvailable; MemFree when Available > Total)
2. `Available` `41.20 GiB` (MemAvailable)
3. `Committed` `46.20 GiB / 67.20 GiB` (Committed_AS / CommitLimit)
4. `Cached` `12.40 GiB` (Cached)
5. `Kernel slab (reclaimable)` `1.10 GiB` tooltip `SReclaimable`
6. `Kernel slab (unreclaimable)` `420.00 MiB` tooltip `SUnreclaim`
7 to 11. `Speed`, `Slots used`, `Form factor`, `Type`, `Hardware reserved`: E25-011 (hidden here)
12. `Swap used` `1.20 GiB` (SwapTotal − SwapFree)
13. `Swap available` `30.80 GiB` (SwapFree)
14. `Compressed` `1.02 GiB` (zram mem_used_total + Zswap); shown only when ≥ 1 MiB compressed, else hidden
15. `Savings` `2.30 GiB` ((zram orig_data_size + Zswapped) − (zram compr_data_size + Zswap)); shown with Compressed
16. `Huge pages` `2 048 × 2 MiB` (HugePages_Total × Hugepagesize; count with thin-space grouping); shown only when non-zero

All sizes in IEC form (table (d)). Each row uses `KeyValueModel::set_valid(label, bits, write)` with `bits` = the raw byte value (or the two values hashed for row 3) so text re-formats only on change. Validity: when the memory component is `WarmingUp` every row shows `Collecting…`; `Failed` rows show `Unavailable` with `Could not read: {last_error}`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the fake memory record from `FakeEngine` **When** `update_memory_details` runs **Then** `to_kv_rows` yields the labels in the order 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 with rows 7 to 11 absent (`memory_details_order`).
- **Given** compressed = 512 KiB **When** updated **Then** rows `Compressed` and `Savings` are hidden; with 1 MiB they are visible (`memory_hidden_rows_rule`).
- **Given** `HugePages_Total = 0` **When** updated **Then** `Huge pages` is hidden; with 2048 × 2 MiB the value is `2 048 × 2 MiB`.
- **Given** Committed_AS = 46.20 GiB and CommitLimit = 67.20 GiB **When** updated **Then** row 3 reads `46.20 GiB / 67.20 GiB`.
- **Given** the same record twice **When** updated **Then** the second call returns false and no `SharedString` is reallocated.

title: E22-A1 Process table renders: ProcessesPage with the process delegate
description:
## Context
Anchor E22-A1. `ProcessesPage`, the entity behind the Processes tab: it subscribes to `SnapshotHub`, owns the `TlTreeTable<ProcessDelegate>`, sends table queries, accepts matching views and renders the table with its two-line header. Driven by `FakeEngine` it renders 2,000 rows, which the phase-0 `table-2000` scene (E01) measures. Other epics build on this page: E23 registers Properties and dialog handlers here, E26 mounts the minigraph panel, E30 mounts History mode, E27 and E28 reuse `ProcessRowCells` and the delegate cells. Sources: ADR-009 (entity structure, nothing notifies in render, tree-table), ADR-005 (hub), UI-PRC-001, UI-PRC-002 (data binding), UI-PRC-023, PROC-013, PROC-021 (no skeleton), UI-PRC-024 (first sweep).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs` (module lines from E22-010, E22-001 to E22-009 already present):
```rust
pub struct ProcessesPage {
    table: Entity<TlTreeTable<ProcessDelegate>>,
    hub_sub: Subscription,           // created in new(), never in render
    focus: FocusHandle,              // the table body focus (track_focus)
    client: Arc<dyn EngineClient>,
}
impl ProcessesPage {
    pub fn new(window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> Self;
    pub fn table(&self) -> &Entity<TlTreeTable<ProcessDelegate>>;
    /// For the E01 `table-2000` bench scene (E01-OI-8): a clone of E18-A1's handle.
    pub fn scroll_handle(&self, cx: &App) -> UniformListScrollHandle;
    pub fn focus_table(&self, window: &mut Window);
}
impl Render for ProcessesPage { /* key_context("ProcessTable") on the page div, containing the table (key_context "Table") */ }
```
Behaviour:
- `new` creates the table entity, sends the first `SetTableQuery` (generation 1) and subscribes to the hub. On a hub change whose `ComponentMask` intersects `PROCESSES | TABLE | WINDOWS | SETTINGS | DEVICES`, the page hands the new snapshot to the delegate; when `ProcessQuery::accept` returns true it calls `table.update(cx, |t, cx| cx.notify())`. Other changes are ignored. Nothing calls `notify` inside `render`.
- Double-click on a row toggles expansion on a row with children and does nothing on a leaf; it never opens Properties (R-216, D-008: Properties open with Enter, Alt+Enter, Ctrl+I and the menu). `ProcessDelegate` overrides `fn double_click_expands(&self) -> bool { true }` (E18 trait default `false`), and the table's double-click path calls `on_toggle_expand` (`ToggleExpand`).
- Registers `.on_action` for the E18 shared `CollapseAll` on the page div: `ProcessQuery::collapse_all` then send (PROC-020, Ctrl+L).
- First sweep not yet installed (`shown == None`): the header renders with `…` totals and the body is plain `list_bg` with no text, no skeleton, no spinner (PROC-021, UI-PRC-024).
- Settings observation: changes to `processes.mode` call `set_mode` and send; changes to `appearance.*`, `units.*`, `tables.*` clear the delegate's text cache through E18's `CellTextCache` clear on `style_version` (ADR-009).
- The page is constructed on first visit and kept (ADR-009); E22-011 registers it in `MainWindow`.
- `scroll_handle` returns `self.table.read(cx).scroll_handle().clone()` (E18-A1 `TlTreeTable::scroll_handle`). It is the same handle the table's `uniform_list` tracks, so scrolling through it moves the production table. The E01 `table-2000` scene (E01-008, tasklens-wlf.10) drives its scroll through this method.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a FakeEngine that publishes a 2,000-row view **When** the page renders in a 720 px viewport **Then** at most 27 row elements are built.
- **Given** the page is created **When** the FakeEngine log is read **Then** one `SetTableQuery` with generation 1 was sent.
- **Given** a hub change with only `SERIES` **When** handled **Then** the table is not notified (render counter unchanged).
- **Given** a hub change with `TABLE` and a matching generation **When** handled **Then** the table is notified once.
- **Given** no view yet **When** rendered **Then** the header shows `…` in CPU line 2 and the body has no row elements and no skeleton.
- **Given** a page with a 2,000-row view **When** `scroll_handle(cx)` is used to scroll to item 1,000 and the page renders **Then** the table's first visible row index is within 27 of 1,000.
- **Given** expanded app rows **When** `CollapseAll` is dispatched **Then** one query is sent whose `expanded` holds only the group headers.
- **Given** an app row with children **When** it is double-clicked **Then** it expands (one query sent) and `OpenProperties` is not dispatched (R-216).
- **Given** a leaf process row **When** it is double-clicked **Then** nothing is dispatched and no query is sent.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs`: add `ProcessesPage`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/delegate.rs`: one method, `fn double_click_expands(&self) -> bool { true }` (R-216).
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_processes.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
- `ui_processes::tree_table_renders_visible_range_only_2000` (TestAppContext, FakeEngine scripted snapshot, seed 42).
- `ui_processes::first_query_sent_on_create`.
- `ui_processes::notifies_only_on_drawn_components` (render counter from E16 testing helpers).
- `ui_processes::no_skeleton_on_processes_tab` (UI-PRC-024).
- `ui_processes::collapse_all_action_sends_query`.
- `ui_processes::scroll_handle_drives_table` (the access path E01-008 uses).
- `ui_processes::double_click_toggles_expand_not_properties`: the two double-click criteria (R-216).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: an engine error never empties the table; the last view stays with stale dimming (ADR-003) and the shell health item reports the worker (UI-PRC-024).
- Validity: WarmingUp `…` before the second sweep in rate cells; Stale dims.
- Accessibility: page div carries `key_context("ProcessTable")`; the table body has `tab_index(0)` (E18).
- Performance: ADR-014 `table-2000`: UI thread p99 ≤ 2.0 ms per frame while scrolling at 1,200 px/s with 1 Hz changes; this bead must not add per-frame allocation (the gate run is E22-028).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Anchor: E27, E28, E23, E26, E30 and E01 depend on this bead. Keep `ProcessesPage::new`, `table()`, `scroll_handle()`, `ProcessDelegate` and `ProcessRowCells` public.
- Hub and FakeEngine: E16-A1 (`hub.rs`, `testing/fake_engine.rs`). Tree table: E18-A1.
- The table handles the header-menu actions `HideColumn`, `ResetColumns` (after the owner called `set_default_layout`) and `ResizeColumnsToFit` itself (E18). This page implements `on_activate` and `context_menu` on its delegate and does not re-handle those table actions (R-184).
- gpui `uniform_list` and `track_scroll`: gpui-pre-0.3.7 `src/elements/uniform_list.rs:22`, `:683`.

title: Process header line 2 system totals
description:
## Context
Header line 2 for the process table: the system total under each column that has one, formatted like the cells and right-aligned in `text_secondary`. The two-line header element itself is E18's; this bead supplies `header_total` for the process delegate. Sources: PROC-038, UI-PRC-005 (line 2 rules), PROC-033 (GPU N totals), PROC-003 (formats), R-050.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/header_totals.rs` (with `pub mod header_totals;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub fn header_total(col: &ProcColumn, totals: &TableTotals, settings: &Settings, out: &mut CellOut) -> bool;
```
Returns false (no line 2) for every column that has no total. Totals (PROC-038), each read from the `TableTotals` field with that meaning:
- CPU: total utilisation %, one decimal (`11.9%`).
- Memory: (MemTotal − MemAvailable) / MemTotal %.
- Swap: used %.
- Disk: highest busy % among physical disks.
- Network: total physical-interface throughput as % of the summed link speed; when the link speed is unknown, the rate in the `units.network` format.
- GPU: highest utilisation among GPUs; GPU N: that adapter's utilisation; VRAM: used / total % over all GPUs. With no GPU each of these writes `Validity::Unsupported` (drawn `n/a`).
- Threads: system thread count (Count format). Handles: `/proc/sys/fs/file-nr` field 1 (Count format).
- Every other column, including Name, User, PID, Description and Power usage: returns false.
- Before the second sample the rates write `Validity::WarmingUp` (drawn `…`).
- Header text style (applied by E18's header): `t_base` regular `text_secondary`, always right-aligned, same validity glyph rules as cells.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** totals with CPU 11.94 **When** `header_total` runs for `cpu` **Then** it returns true and text is `11.9%`.
- **Given** the `name`, `user`, `pid`, `description` columns **When** called **Then** it returns false.
- **Given** no GPU in the catalog **When** called for `gpu`, `gpu_mem_dedicated` and `gpu_0` **Then** each returns true with validity Unsupported.
- **Given** link speed unknown and 287_500 B/s total in bits mode **When** called for `network` **Then** text is `2.3 Mbps`.
- **Given** Handles total 41_234 **When** called **Then** text is `41 234` (U+2009).

title: Process table query state, generations and expansion
description:
## Context
The process table's query state: it owns the `TableQuery` the UI sends to the engine (mode, sort, filter, expansion, generation) and the rule that a view is shown only when its `query_generation` equals the last sent generation. The engine sorts, filters, groups and flattens; the UI never does (ADR-009, PROC-013). Sources: ADR-009 "Process tree-table", ADR-005 `Command::SetTableQuery`, PROC-004 (group expand persists), PROC-009 (Kernel threads row collapsed by default), PROC-014 (modes, expand state kept per identity for the session), PROC-020 (Collapse all), PROC-047 (sort, persistence), R-010, R-011, UI-PRC-002 data binding, UI-PRC-016 (generations).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/table.rs` (with `pub mod table;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub struct ProcessQuery {
    generation: u64,                     // starts at 0; +1 for every query sent
    mode: TableMode,                     // from processes.mode: grouped -> Grouped, tree -> Tree, flat -> Flat
    sort: SortSpec,                      // from state.toml [sort.processes]; default column "pid", ascending
    filter: Arc<str>,                    // lowercase, set by E22-021
    expanded: FxHashSet<NodeId>,         // session state per identity
    collapsed_by_user: FxHashSet<NodeId>,// rows the user collapsed, so defaults do not re-expand them
    shown: Option<Arc<ProcessTableView>>,// the view on screen
}
impl ProcessQuery {
    pub fn new(settings: &Settings, state: &UiState) -> Self;
    pub fn to_query(&self) -> TableQuery;             // expanded as Arc<[NodeId]>
    pub fn bump_and_send(&mut self, client: &dyn EngineClient); // generation += 1, then client.send(Command::SetTableQuery(self.to_query()))
    pub fn accept(&mut self, view: &Arc<ProcessTableView>) -> bool; // true and stores it when view.query_generation == generation
    pub fn set_mode(&mut self, m: TableMode);
    pub fn set_sort(&mut self, col: ColumnId, kind: ProcColumnKind) -> SortSpec; // first click: descending for numeric kinds, ascending for Text and PowerClass; same column again flips
    pub fn set_filter(&mut self, lower: Arc<str>);
    pub fn toggle(&mut self, id: NodeId);
    pub fn expand_path(&mut self, ids: &[NodeId]);    // used by the jump target (E22-A3)
    pub fn collapse_all(&mut self);                   // clears every expansion except the three group headers (PROC-020)
    pub fn shown(&self) -> Option<&Arc<ProcessTableView>>;
}
```
Rules:
- Initial expansion: the three group headers follow `state.toml [processes] group_expanded = { apps, background, system }` (default all true); the "Kernel threads (N)" row starts collapsed; every app and unit row starts collapsed. Expansion of process and app rows lives for the session only; group header expansion writes back to `group_expanded` through the state persist path (500 ms debounce, ADR-011).
- Every change of mode, sort, filter or expansion calls `bump_and_send` once.
- `accept` keeps the previous `shown` view when the generation does not match (stale results are ignored).
- Sort persists to `state.toml [sort.processes]` (`column`, `ascending`) on every change; it always persists (no "remember sorting" option).
- Mode changes come from `processes.mode` (written by E20/E21 actions); this bead observes the setting and calls `set_mode` plus `bump_and_send`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fresh state **When** `new` runs **Then** mode is Grouped, sort is pid ascending, the three groups are expanded and the Kernel threads row is not in `expanded`.
- **Given** generation 4 sent **When** a view with `query_generation = 3` arrives **Then** `accept` returns false and `shown` is unchanged.
- **Given** a view with generation 4 **When** it arrives **Then** `accept` returns true and `shown` is that view.
- **Given** sort pid ascending **When** `set_sort(cpu, Percent)` **Then** the new sort is cpu descending; again **Then** cpu ascending.
- **Given** sort by `name` (Text) **When** first clicked **Then** it is ascending.
- **Given** expanded app rows and groups **When** `collapse_all` **Then** only the three group headers stay expanded.
- **Given** the user collapses "Apps" **When** the state is saved **Then** `group_expanded.apps = false`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/table.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs`: add the `mod` line.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_processes.rs`: create with these tests (FakeEngine records the sent commands).

## Tests
- `ui_processes::query_defaults_from_settings_and_state`.
- `ui_processes::stale_generation_results_ignored`.
- `ui_processes::sort_first_click_desc_numeric_asc_text`.
- `ui_processes::collapse_all_keeps_group_headers`.
- `ui_processes::group_expand_persists_to_state`.
- `ui_processes::each_change_sends_one_query`: mode, sort, filter and toggle each produce exactly one `SetTableQuery` in the FakeEngine log with increasing generation.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: `to_query` allocates one `Arc<[NodeId]>` per sent query, never per frame.
- Privacy: the filter text is never logged.

## Notes
- `TableQuery`, `TableMode`, `SortSpec`, `NodeId`, `Command` are tl-model types (ADR-009, ADR-005). `EngineClient` and `FakeEngine` come from E16-A1.
- App and unit rows start collapsed because the UI-PRC-002 sketch draws them with `▸` ("Firefox (14)").
- Build rule: run every cargo build, check, clippy or test through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_processes` (it takes the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope; the wait can be long, so run it in the background when your tool call has a timeout). On an OOM kill (exit 137) retry once, then report.
- Strings: every user-visible string in this bead is appended to `assets/locales/en-US.ftl` in this bead (R-132), key `processes-<entry>-<slug>` (for example `processes-menu-end-task`), and read through `tr(key)` / `tr_args(key, args)` from `src/i18n.rs`. The English text in this bead is the value, exactly.

title: ProcessDelegate: TreeTableDelegate for the process table
description:
## Context
`ProcessDelegate`, the `TreeTableDelegate` implementation for the process table. It maps the engine's finished `ProcessTableView` rows to row kinds, flags, Name cells and metric cells, reports visible keys as demand, and forwards sort, expand, column and activation events. Other tables (Services child rows, E27) reuse its cell code through `ProcessRowCells`. Sources: UI-PRC-001 (delegate trait), UI-PRC-002 (row kinds and data binding), UI-PRC-010 (visible demand), UI-PRC-005 (GPU N tooltip), ADR-009 (tree-table, visible demand, text cache), PROC-013, PROC-018, PROC-022, PROC-033, D-008.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/delegate.rs` (with `pub mod delegate;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub struct ProcessDelegate {
    query: ProcessQuery,                        // E22-008
    snapshot: Arc<Snapshot>,                    // the snapshot the rows came from (or the paused one, E22-024)
    row_index: FxHashMap<NodeId, u32>,          // rebuilt when view.header.version changes
    sibling: Vec<(bool /*last*/, u64 /*ancestor bits*/)>, // E22-006 pass, per row
    layout: ColumnLayout,                       // from state.toml [columns.processes]
    specs: FxHashMap<ColumnId, ColumnSpec>,     // built from PROCESS_COLUMNS for the offered columns
    name_cache: FxHashMap<NodeId, (SharedString, SharedString)>, // primary, secondary
}
impl TreeTableDelegate for ProcessDelegate { type RowId = NodeId; ... }
pub struct ProcessRowCells;  // reusable: fn fill(record: &ProcessRecord, kind: RowKind, col: ColumnId, ctx: &CellCtx, out: &mut CellOut)
                             //            fn render(out: &CellOut, col: ColumnId, width: Pixels, st: PaintState, theme, cx) -> impl IntoElement
```
Trait methods:
- `row_count` = `view.rows.len()`; `row_id(ix)` = `rows[ix].node`; `row_index` from the map.
- `row_kind`: `NodeId::Group` rows map by the `GroupRow` kind to `GroupHeader` (the three Task Manager groups), `App`, or `Unit`; `NodeId::Process` rows map to `KernelThread` when `ProcFlags::KERNEL_THREAD`, `Pseudo` for the two pseudo rows, else `Process`. The "Kernel threads (N)" row is a `Unit`-shaped row with the `cpu` icon.
- `row_depth` = `rows[ix].depth`; `row_expandable` = `has_children.then_some(expanded)`.
- `row_flags`: NEW, EXITED from `ProcFlags`; STALE when the component header validity is Stale; RESTRICTED when any field validity is Restricted; SUSPENDED when `state == Stopped`; FROZEN (P2, E22-032); LAST_SIBLING and ANCESTOR_CONTINUES from `sibling`.
- `columns` / `column_spec`: offered columns are those of `PROCESS_COLUMNS` with `phase <=` the current shipped phase constant `SHIPPED_PHASE: u8 = 1` in this file (later beads raise it), plus `gpu_N` only for adapters present in `Snapshot.devices` (numbered by PCI bus address ascending, PROC-033). GPU N header tooltip: `"<adapter name> (<PCI address>)"`.
- `cell` → `ProcessRowCells::fill` (E22-003); `name_cell` → `NameCellData` (E22-005) with primary `"<name> (N)"` for app and unit rows (N = member count), process rows `meta.name`.
- `header_total` → E22-007. `sort` / `on_sort` → `ProcessQuery::set_sort` then send. `on_toggle_expand` → `ProcessQuery::toggle` then send.
- `selectable(ix)`: false for `GroupHeader`.
- `on_columns_changed`: writes `[columns.processes]` (`order`, `visible`, `widths`) to `UiState` through the persist path (500 ms debounce).
- `on_visible_range(ids)`: forwards the process keys among `ids` (at most 512) to `DemandAggregator` as `Demand::ProcessDetail { keys }` (ADR-008, E16-A1 `demand.rs`).
- `on_activate(id)`: on a GroupHeader toggles expansion; on process, app and unit rows dispatches `OpenProperties` (D-008; the handler is E23's). Exited rows: E22-012.
- `row_tooltip` → None here (E22-013 fills it). `context_menu` → returns the menu unchanged here (E22-A2 fills it). `empty_text` → None here (E22-021).
- `header_lines` → `HeaderLines::Two`; `columns_fixed` → false.
- On every accepted view: rebuild `row_index` and `sibling` when `view.header.version` changed; prune `name_cache` keys not in the view.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake view with one row of every kind **When** the delegate answers **Then** kinds are GroupHeader, App, Unit, Process, KernelThread, Pseudo in that order, and `selectable` is false only for the group header.
- **Given** an app row with 14 members named Firefox **When** `name_cell` runs **Then** primary is "Firefox (14)".
- **Given** rows reordered in a new view version **When** `row_index(id)` is called **Then** it returns the new index.
- **Given** a scroll that shows 40 rows **When** `on_visible_range` is called with 120 ids **Then** DemandAggregator receives the process keys among them, at most 512.
- **Given** one GPU present **When** `columns` is built **Then** `gpu_0` is offered and `gpu_1` is not.
- **Given** a column of phase 2 and `SHIPPED_PHASE = 1` **When** columns are built **Then** it is not offered.
- **Given** Enter on a process row **When** `on_activate` runs **Then** `OpenProperties` is dispatched; on a group header the row toggles.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/delegate.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs`: add the `mod` line.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_processes.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
- `ui_processes::process_rows_render_each_kind`: kinds, icon sizes 24 app and 16 others, PID blank for app, unit, group and pseudo rows, `+N` only on the collapsed parent.
- `ui_processes::group_header_row_not_selectable`.
- `ui_processes::row_index_rebuilt_per_version`.
- `ui_processes::visible_demand_forwarded_capped_512`.
- `ui_processes::gpu_slots_only_for_present_adapters`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: per cell (E22-003, E22-004); stale component dims the whole row's metric cells.
- Accessibility: group headers are skipped by keyboard selection (`selectable`).
- Performance: no allocation per visible row per frame once caches are warm; `row_index` rebuild is O(rows) only on a version change (≈ 60 µs at 2,000 rows, UI-PRC-023).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- The trait, `ColumnLayout`, `ColumnSpec`, `RowKind`, `RowFlags`, `HeaderLines` are E18-A1/E18-A2. If the trait signature differs from UI-PRC-001, follow E18's code and keep these behaviours.
- `GroupRow` field names (kind, member count, label) are E03-A2's (open item 1).
- Build rule: run every cargo build, check, clippy or test through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_processes` (it takes the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope; the wait can be long, so run it in the background when your tool call has a timeout). On an OOM kill (exit 137) retry once, then report.

The English text in this bead is the value, exactly.

title: Tree connector lines in the Name cell
description:
## Context
Tree connector lines in the Name cell (View > Process View > "Tree Connector Lines", `processes.tree_guide_lines`, default off). They show the ppid tree structure in Tree View and inside groups. Sources: PROC-017, UI-PRC-003 (connector anatomy), UI-PRC-001 (`RowFlags::LAST_SIBLING`, `ANCESTOR_CONTINUES`).

## Deliverable
In `pages/processes/name_cell.rs`: `fn paint_connectors(depth: u8, last_sibling: bool, ancestor_continues: u64, in_group: bool, bounds: Bounds<Pixels>, theme: &TlTheme, window: &mut Window)` drawn in a `canvas` before the icon, called from `render_name_cell` only when `processes.tree_guide_lines` is true.
- For each ancestor depth k < depth − 1 whose bit k is set in `ancestor_continues`: a 1 px vertical `divider` quad at x = 8 + k × 18 + 8 over the full row height.
- For the row's own depth: a vertical quad at x = 8 + (depth − 1) × 18 + 8 from the row top to the row centre, continuing to the row bottom when not `last_sibling`; plus a horizontal quad from that x to the chevron's left edge at the row centre.
- Depth-0 rows under a group header draw from the group chevron centre x = 16. Group header rows draw none.
- Every quad snaps to 1 physical px (`window.pixel_snap` or rounding with `window.scale_factor()`).
- In the delegate (E22-009 owns the struct; this bead adds the computation): `last_sibling` and `ancestor_continues` are computed once per table version in one reverse pass over `view.rows` (a row is the last sibling when no later row at the same depth appears before a row of smaller depth; bit k of a row is set when its ancestor at depth k is not the last sibling).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `tree_guide_lines = false` **When** a depth-2 row renders **Then** no connector quad is drawn.
- **Given** it is true and a depth-2 row that is not the last sibling, whose depth-0 ancestor also continues (bit 0 set) **When** rendered **Then** 3 quads are drawn: a full-height vertical at x 16 (depth-0 ancestor), a full-height vertical at x 34 (own connector), and a horizontal at the row centre from x 34 to x 44 (the chevron's left edge).
- **Given** a depth-2 row that is the last sibling **When** rendered **Then** its own vertical quad ends at the row centre.
- **Given** rows A(d0), B(d1), C(d2), D(d1) **When** the pass runs **Then** B and C are not last for depth 1 ancestry (D follows), C is last sibling, D is last sibling.
- **Given** a group header row **When** rendered **Then** no connector is drawn.

title: New and exited row highlight with linger and fade
description:
## Context
New and exited row highlight: NEW rows get a green tint, EXITED rows a red tint with greyed text, for the linger time, fading over the last 300 ms. Exited rows stay in place and are not actionable. Sources: PROC-043, R-041, UI-PRC-011, ADR-009 highlight bullet and animation driver, UI-PRC-008 (selection wins), D-008.

## Deliverable
In `pages/processes/cells.rs`: `pub fn row_tint(flags: ProcFlags, flag_since_ns: TimeNs, now_ns: TimeNs, interval_ms: u32, animations: bool, enabled: bool) -> Option<(TintKind, f32 /*alpha*/)>` and the row-background quad drawn by the delegate's row renderer; in `pages/processes/delegate.rs`: the call per visible row and the frame request.
- Linger `L = clamp(2 × processes.interval_ms, 1000, 3000)` ms, measured from the engine timestamp of the flag's first appearance (not UI time).
- NEW: `status.success` at alpha 0.35. EXITED: `status.danger` at alpha 0.35; all row text `text_secondary`; icons at 60 % opacity; the chevron stays.
- Fade: during the last 300 ms the alpha goes 0.35 to 0 with `ease_out_cubic`. With `motion.animations = false` or `App::reduce_motion()` true, the tint stays 0.35 and switches off at L.
- Layer order: zebra (`list_bg` even, `row_alt` odd, counted on the flattened index), then this tint, then heat (E22-004), then the selection fill. A selected row hides the tint: new-and-selected shows only the selection fill; exited-and-selected uses the selection fill with `text_selected_secondary` text.
- `processes.highlight_new_exited = false`: no tints; exited rows still linger and are still not actionable.
- Frames: the delegate calls E19's `AnimationDriver::request` only while at least one visible row is inside its 300 ms fade window; otherwise nothing is requested.
- Exited rows not actionable: `on_activate` on an EXITED row (Enter, double-click) shows the Warning toast "Process exited" through `ToastQueue::push(Warning, ..)` and does not dispatch `OpenProperties`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** interval 1000 ms and a NEW flag 500 ms old **When** `row_tint` runs **Then** it returns (New, 0.35).
- **Given** a NEW flag 1850 ms old (L = 2000) **When** run with animations on **Then** alpha is between 0 and 0.35 per `ease_out_cubic` at t = 150/300.
- **Given** the same with reduce motion **When** run **Then** alpha is 0.35; at 2000 ms it returns None.
- **Given** interval 250 ms **When** L is computed **Then** it is 1000 ms; interval 5000 ms gives 3000 ms.
- **Given** an exited row **When** rendered **Then** its text uses `text_secondary` and its icon opacity is 0.6.
- **Given** `highlight_new_exited = false` **When** rendered **Then** no tint quad is drawn.
- **Given** no visible row in a fade window **When** a frame ends **Then** no animation frame is requested.
- **Given** Enter on an exited row **When** handled **Then** the toast "Process exited" shows and no Properties action is dispatched.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/cells.rs`: `row_tint`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/delegate.rs`: tint drawing, frame request, exited `on_activate`.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_process_cells.rs`: tests.

## Tests
- `ui_process_cells::highlight_alpha_timeline`: 0.35 until L − 300 ms, 0 at L, the reduce-motion step.
- `ui_process_cells::linger_clamped_1_to_3_s`.
- `ui_process_cells::exited_row_text_and_icon_dimmed`.
- `ui_process_cells::driver_idle_when_no_fade_active`.
- `ui_processes::exited_row_enter_toasts_process_exited`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: the exited state is carried by grey text and the "Process exited" toast and tooltip, not colour alone.
- Performance: one quad per flagged visible row; the animation driver is armed only during fades (≤ 300 ms per row event).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- The flag timestamp: ADR-003 `ProcessRecord` has `flags` but no "since" time. Use the E03 field that carries it; if none exists, stop and report (open item 1).
- `AnimationDriver` is E19-A1 (`anim.rs`). This dependency is not in the E22 row of 00-epics.md section 4 (open item 5); it adds no cycle.
- `App::reduce_motion`: gpui-pre-0.3.7 `src/app.rs:1141`.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, check, clippy or test through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_processes` (it takes the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope; the wait can be long, so run it in the background when your tool call has a timeout). On an OOM kill (exit 137) retry once, then report.
- Strings: every user-visible string in this bead is appended to `assets/locales/en-US.ftl` in this bead (R-132), key `processes-<entry>-<slug>` (for example `processes-menu-end-task`), and read through `tr(key)` / `tr_args(key, args)` from `src/i18n.rs`. The English text in this bead is the value, exactly.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <the files of this bead>`.

Commits 8369ce1, 09caa37, and the lint fix.

title: Process row hover tooltip
description:
## Context
The row hover tooltip on the Name cell: command line, path, user, unit, cgroup, package, desktop file and a restricted note, built only when shown. Sources: PROC-039, R-009, PROC-012 (pseudo-row sentences), UI-PRC-012, UI-FND-019 (`TlTooltip::lines`, 560 wide).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/tooltip.rs` (with `pub mod tooltip;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`): `pub fn row_tooltip_lines(row: RowRef, view: &ProcessTableView, out: &mut Vec<(Option<SharedString> /*label*/, SharedString /*value*/)>)` and the delegate's `row_tooltip` returning a `TlTooltip::lines` view.
Lines in this order, each only when it applies (labels `text_secondary`, values `text_primary`, `t_sm` 12, each line its own `div` so it wraps alone):
1. Command line: first 512 characters of `meta.cmdline`, no label. Kernel threads: `[comm]` instead.
2. `path: <exe>`, or `path: restricted` when `meta.exe` is None.
3. `user: <name> (uid N)`.
4. `Unit: <unit> (<Description>)` when the cgroup names a unit (Description from the services data when known, else `Unit: <unit>`).
5. `cgroup: <path>`.
6. `Package: <name> <version>` when known (P2; omitted until the package data exists).
7. `Desktop file: <path>` on app rows only.
8. `Some values need administrator access.` in `status.warning` on rows with any Restricted field.
- Pseudo rows show one line only: Interrupts "CPU time spent in hardware and software interrupts"; Memory compression "Memory held by zram compressed swap devices".
- Group headers: no tooltip.
- Show after 600 ms hover over the Name cell with no mouse button down; hide on mouse-down, on leaving the cell, on scroll and on any key. No grace switching between rows.
- Tooltip box: max width 560, padding `sp4` 8, `menu_bg` fill, 1 px `divider` border, radius `r_sm`.
- Wiring: `.id(("name", node)).tooltip(move |w, cx| ...).tooltip_show_delay(Duration::from_millis(600))` on the Name cell div; the delegate's `row_tooltip` builds the view lazily.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a process row with all fields and no restriction **When** the lines are built **Then** they are lines 1 to 5 in order.
- **Given** an app row **When** built **Then** the Desktop file line is present.
- **Given** a row with a Restricted field **When** built **Then** the last line is "Some values need administrator access." in `status.warning`.
- **Given** a 2,000-character command line **When** built **Then** line 1 has exactly 512 characters.
- **Given** a kernel thread `kworker/0:1` **When** built **Then** line 1 is `[kworker/0:1]`.
- **Given** the Interrupts row **When** built **Then** there is exactly one line, the Interrupts sentence.
- **Given** a hover of 500 ms **When** the pointer stays **Then** no tooltip; at 600 ms it shows.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: `path: restricted` for an unreadable exe.
- Accessibility: the same text is in "Copy all metrics" (E22-019).
- Performance: built only on show; the Name cell id is the only per-row element id.
- Privacy: the command line is shown, never logged (ADR-015).

title: Process cell tooltips
description:
## Context
