title: Process action confirmation dialogs
description:
## Context
The process-action confirmation dialogs, in one helper that the Processes page, the Properties windows and Handle Search (E23) call. Every confirmation is a `TlDialog::confirm` window titled "tasklens", width 420, focus on Cancel, Esc cancels. Sources: UI-PRC-014 (texts), UI-PWN-025 (several-targets signal text), PROC-059, PROC-062, PROC-064, PROC-066, PROC-074, PROC-075, PROC-055, R-036, D-009, UI-FND-021, APP-045.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/confirm.rs` (with `pub mod confirm;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub enum ConfirmKind {
    Protected { action: SharedString /*e.g. "End"*/, tree_count: Option<u32> },
    EndTree { count: u32 },
    KillApp { app: SharedString, count: u32 },
    EndMany { count: u32, kill: bool },
    OtherUser { action: SharedString, name: SharedString, pid: u32, user: SharedString, destructive: bool },
    Realtime,
    SignalMany { count: u32, signal_name: SharedString, ends_process: bool },
    LargeDump { name: SharedString, size: SharedString },
    VirusTotalFirstUse,
    Picked { name: SharedString, pid: u32 },
}
pub enum ConfirmResult { Confirmed, Second /* only Picked: Terminate */, Cancelled }
pub fn confirm(kind: ConfirmKind, parent: AnyWindowHandle, cx: &mut App, done: impl FnOnce(ConfirmResult, &mut App) + 'static);
pub fn texts(kind: &ConfirmKind) -> ConfirmTexts; // { title, description, confirm_label, confirm_danger, second: Option<(label, danger)> }
```
Texts (title / description / confirm button / kind):
- Protected: "End <name>?" / "Ending <name> will end your desktop session. End it anyway?" / "End anyway" danger. With `tree_count = Some(N)` the description is "Ending <name> will end your desktop session. End N processes in this tree anyway?" (protected wins over the tree text and keeps N).
- EndTree: "End process tree?" / "End N processes in this tree?" / "End tree" danger.
- KillApp: "Kill <App>?" / "Kill all N processes of <App>?" / "Kill app" danger.
- EndMany (SIGTERM): "End N processes?" / "End N selected processes?" / "End tasks" danger. EndMany (SIGKILL): "End N processes?" / "End N selected processes immediately?" / "End processes" danger.
- OtherUser: "Act on another user's process?" / "<Action> on <name> (PID n), owned by <user>. Continue?" / "<Action label>", danger for End and Kill, primary otherwise.
- Realtime: "Set realtime priority?" / "Realtime priority can freeze the desktop if the process spins. Set it anyway?" / "Set realtime" danger.
- SignalMany: "Send signal to N processes?" / "Send SIG<NAME> to N selected processes?" / "Send signal", danger when the signal ends processes, primary otherwise.
- LargeDump: "Create a large dump?" / "<name> uses 3.4 GiB. The process pauses while the core is written and the file will be about that size. Continue?" / "Create dump" primary.
- VirusTotalFirstUse: "Open VirusTotal?" / "This opens virustotal.com with the file's hash. The file is not uploaded." / "Open" primary.
- Picked: "Picked <name> (PID n)" / "What do you want to do with this process?" / "Select" primary, second "Terminate" danger.
Every dialog: window title "tasklens"; Cancel `TlButton::Secondary` left of the action; destructive dialogs focus Cancel first, non-destructive focus the action button (UI-FND-021); Enter activates the focused button; Tab moves between buttons; Esc cancels; modal to `parent`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** each kind **When** `texts` runs **Then** title, description and labels equal the list above exactly.
- **Given** a protected target and End Process Tree with 7 processes **When** `texts(Protected { tree_count: Some(7) })` runs **Then** the description is "Ending plasmashell will end your desktop session. End 7 processes in this tree anyway?".
- **Given** an EndTree dialog **When** it opens **Then** focus is on Cancel and pressing Enter returns `Cancelled`.
- **Given** an EndTree dialog **When** Tab then Enter **Then** it returns `Confirmed`.
- **Given** a VirusTotalFirstUse dialog **When** it opens **Then** focus is on "Open".
- **Given** any dialog **When** Esc **Then** it returns `Cancelled` and the window closes.
- **Given** a Picked dialog **When** "Terminate" is clicked **Then** it returns `Second`.

- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs`: add the `mod` line.

## Tests

- `ui_process_menu::confirm_focus_starts_on_cancel_enter_activates_focused`.
- `ui_process_menu::protected_wins_over_tree_text`.
- `ui_process_menu::non_destructive_focus_on_action`.
- `ui_process_menu::picked_second_button_terminate`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: plain-text title and description; buttons name the result; keyboard only flow Tab, Enter, Esc.
- Performance: one small window per confirmation.
- Privacy: dialog texts hold names and PIDs only, never command lines.

## Notes
- `TlDialog::confirm(..).heading(text)` and window kinds: E16-A2 (`components/dialog.rs`, `window_frame.rs`).
- The caller re-dispatches its action with the confirmation result; revalidation of identities still happens in the engine after confirm (PROC-058).

On an OOM kill (exit 137) retry once, then report.

The English text in this bead is the value, exactly.

title: Process action toast texts and request submission
description:
## Context
The toast texts and kinds for process actions, keyed per request so later states replace the same toast in place. The page builds the texts when it submits an `ActionRequest`; E16's `ActionTracker` shows them as `ActionEvent`s arrive. Sources: UI-PRC-015 (table), PROC-058, PROC-059 (refusals), PROC-060 to PROC-064, PROC-066 to PROC-069, R-035, ADR-005 (event order, ActionTracker, "Outcome unknown"), UI-FND-020 (kinds and durations).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/toasts.rs` (with `pub mod toasts;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub struct ActionToastTexts {
    pub requested: Option<(ToastKind, SharedString)>, // shown on Started
    pub success: (ToastKind, SharedString),            // final Succeeded for the whole request
    pub failure: (ToastKind, SharedString),            // final Failed when every target failed
    pub partial: Option<fn(done: u32, total: u32, failed: &[(u32, SharedString)]) -> SharedString>, // multi-target mixed result
}
pub fn texts_for(kind: &ActionKind, t: &CapturedTargets) -> ActionToastTexts;
pub fn refusal_text(reason: RejectReason, t: &CapturedTarget) -> Option<SharedString>;
pub fn submit(page: &mut ProcessesPage, req: ActionRequest, texts: ActionToastTexts, cx: &mut Context<ProcessesPage>);
```
`submit` sends `Command::Action(req)` through the client and registers the texts with the E16-A3 `ActionTracker` under `ToastKey(req.id.0)`, so every state of one request replaces one toast.
Texts (kind in brackets; Info 5 s, Success 5 s, Warning 5 s, Error 8 s, with a button 15 s, per UI-FND-020):
- End Task single: requested "End task requested." [Info]; success "Process terminated" [Success]; failure "Could not end task." [Error].
- End Process single: "End process requested." [Info]; "Process terminated" [Success]; "Could not end process." [Error].
- End Process Tree: "End process tree requested." [Info]; "Process tree terminated" [Success]; partial result in one toast.
- End Task or End Process with 2+ targets: requested "End task requested for selected processes." [Info]; result "Ended 4 of 5 processes (1 permission denied)" [Warning when any failed, else Success].
- Suspend / Resume: "Process suspended." / "Process resumed." [Success].
- Freeze App / Thaw App / Kill App: "App frozen" / "App thawed" / "App killed" [Success].
- Priority single: "Priority updated" [Success]. Multi: all ok "Selected process priority updated." [Success]; all failed "Could not update selected process priority." [Error]; partial "Priority updated for 3 of 4 processes. 1 failed: permission denied" [Warning].
- Affinity: single "Affinity updated" [Success]; multi all ok "Selected process affinity updated." [Success]; failure "Could not update selected process affinity." [Error]; partial in the priority form with "Affinity updated for …".
- I/O priority: single "I/O priority updated" [Success]; multi "Selected process I/O priority updated." [Success]; failure "Could not update selected process I/O priority." [Error]; partial "I/O priority updated for …".
- Identity mismatch (`Rejected(IdentityChanged)`): "The selected process changed; wait for the list to update and try again." [Warning].
- EPERM (`Failed` with the permission-denied `ActionError`): "Permission denied" [Error] (the P3 "Retry as administrator" button is E22-040).
- Outcome unknown: "Outcome unknown" [Warning] (the tracker's deadline + 5 s rule, ADR-005).
- Refusals, no dialog, no request sent (`refusal_text`, PROC-059): `IS_SELF` "Refusing to end tasklens itself."; PID 1 "PID 1 (systemd) cannot be ended."; `KERNEL_THREAD` "Kernel threads cannot be signalled." [Warning each].
- Exited row activated: "Process exited" [Warning].
- Partial reason text: "permission denied" for the permission `ActionError`; for any other error the reason is the first sentence of `ActionTracker::message(&err)` in lower case without the full stop. Several reasons join with ", " in the order of first occurrence.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** End Task on one process **When** `texts_for` runs **Then** requested is (Info, "End task requested.") and success is (Success, "Process terminated").
- **Given** End Task on 5 targets with 4 Succeeded and 1 EPERM **When** the summary arrives **Then** one toast reads "Ended 4 of 5 processes (1 permission denied)" as Warning, replacing the "End task requested for selected processes." toast in place.
- **Given** a priority change on 4 targets with 3 ok and 1 EPERM **When** done **Then** the toast is "Priority updated for 3 of 4 processes. 1 failed: permission denied".
- **Given** a target with `IS_SELF` **When** `refusal_text` runs **Then** it is "Refusing to end tasklens itself." and no request is sent.
- **Given** `Rejected(IdentityChanged)` **When** the event arrives **Then** the toast text is "The selected process changed; wait for the list to update and try again.".
- **Given** two requests in flight **When** their events interleave **Then** each updates only its own toast (keys `ToastKey(id.0)` differ).

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/toasts.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs`: add the `mod` line.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_process_menu.rs`: tests.

## Tests

- `ui_process_menu::action_toast_replaces_in_place_per_request`.
- `ui_process_menu::multi_target_result_counts_and_reasons`.
- `ui_process_menu::refusals_send_no_request`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: every failure path has a toast; nothing fails silently.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: text first, icon second; colour never carries the meaning alone.
- Performance: at most 4 visible toasts and a 16-entry wait list (UI-FND-020).
- Privacy: action logs record kind, target PID and result only (ADR-015); toast texts hold names and PIDs, never command lines.

## Notes
- `ToastQueue`, `ToastKind`, `ToastKey` are E16-A2; `ActionTracker` and `message(&ActionError)` are E16-A3. If E16-A3's submission API has another name, use it and keep these texts.
- The reason wording for failures other than permission denied is open item 6 in docs/plan/b8-ui-tables.md.

description:
## Context

Confirmations (E22-015), toasts (E22-016) and the P1 handlers (E22-017 to E22-019) already exist; this bead builds the menu that dispatches them. ```
and the delegate's `context_menu` (E22-009) calling them after storing `targets` in `ProcessesPage.menu_targets`.

P1 items in order (P = process row, M = 2+ rows; hidden = not built; disabled items keep a tooltip):
1. "End Task" (M: "End Selected Tasks") → `EndTask`; app and unit rows in P1: "End App" → `EndTask`.
2. "End Process" (M: "End Selected Processes") → `EndProcess`; hidden on app and unit rows in P1. Tooltip "Ends the process immediately (SIGKILL)".
3. "End Process Tree" → `EndProcessTree`; hidden on app, unit and M.
(separator)
4. "Suspend Process" / "Resume Process" by State T (M: "Suspend Selected Tasks" / "Resume Selected Tasks", Resume only when every target is stopped, E22-018 `suspend_or_resume`); hidden on app and unit rows in P1.
6. "Set Priority >" submenu (same label on app and unit rows, tooltip "Applies to the app's current processes"): first line a disabled `text_secondary` item "With autogroup on, nice only orders processes within the same session.", then "High", "Above normal", "Normal", "Below normal", "Low" → `SetPriority { class }`; a check mark (Lucide `check` 14 px, left side) on the current class, on multi-select only when every target shares it.
(separator)
11. "Copy" → `CopyCell { col: clicked_col }` (built only when `clicked_col` is Some).
12. "Copy details" → `CopyDetails`.
13. "Copy all metrics" → `CopyAllMetrics`.
14. "Copy rows as table" → `CopyRowsAsTable`.
(separator)
21. "Open file location" → `OpenFileLocation`; P only (hidden on app, unit, M); disabled with tooltip "Executable deleted" when `exe_deleted` (E22-020).
(separator)
24. "Go to parent process" → `GoToParent`; P only; hidden when ppid is 0.
Rules:
- Exited rows (any target EXITED): every item disabled with tooltip "Process exited" except 11 to 14.
- Pseudo rows: only items 11, 12, 13.
- Kernel-thread rows: items as a process row (actions refuse with a toast).
- Protected targets keep the same labels (the confirmation warns).
- Group header rows: `group_header_menu` with one item "Expand" or "Collapse" → `ToggleExpand`.
- Right-click on an unselected row selects it first (E18); right-click inside the selection keeps it. Shift+F10 and the Menu key open the menu at the focus row's Name cell (E18 `OpenContextMenu`).

title: End Task, End Process and End Process Tree handlers
description:
## Context
Handlers for End Task (SIGTERM), End Process (SIGKILL) and End Process Tree on process, app and unit rows: target capture, refusals, confirmations and the request. Keys and menu items dispatch the same actions (E22-026, E22-A2). Sources: PROC-001, PROC-010 (bwrap unwrap), PROC-058, PROC-059, PROC-060, PROC-061, PROC-062, PROC-069 (multi End), R-034 to R-037, D-009, ADR-005 (ActionRequest), ADR-006 (KillTree), UI-PRC-013, UI-PRC-014, UI-PRC-015.

## Deliverable
In `pages/processes/mod.rs` (`ProcessesPage`):
- `pub fn capture_targets(&self, clicked_col: Option<ColumnId>, cx: &App) -> CapturedTargets`: the selection set in current view order, group headers excluded, at most 256 items (`truncated` set beyond that), built from the shown (or paused) snapshot.
- `menu_targets: Option<CapturedTargets>`: set by the row menu when it opens (E22-A2); a handler uses and clears it, else calls `capture_targets(None, cx)`.
- `.on_action` handlers for `EndTask`, `EndProcess`, `EndProcessTree`, each running these steps:
  1. Targets empty: do nothing. Pseudo rows are dropped. Exited targets are dropped; if every target was exited, Warning toast "Process exited" and stop.
  2. Refusals (no dialog, no request; one toast per distinct reason, E22-016 `refusal_text`): `IS_SELF` "Refusing to end tasklens itself."; pid 1 "PID 1 (systemd) cannot be ended."; `KERNEL_THREAD` "Kernel threads cannot be signalled.". Refused targets are dropped; stop if none remain.
  3. Targets: process rows give `ActionTarget::Process(key)`. App and unit rows (End Task only) give their primary processes: members whose ppid is not a member; a primary whose exe basename is `bwrap` is replaced by its first non-bwrap descendant (PROC-010, walking `ProcessSnapshot.records` by ppid). App and unit rows are skipped by End Process until E22-035 adds Kill App.
  4. End Process Tree: target set = the selected process plus every descendant found by walking `ProcessSnapshot.records` by ppid from the root's pid (matching each parent by pid among non-exited records), capped at 256 keys.
  5. Confirmation (E22-015), first matching rule wins: any target `PROTECTED` → `Protected { action: "End", tree_count }` (tree_count = Some(N) for End Process Tree); End Process Tree → `EndTree { count: N }`; 2+ targets → `EndMany { count, kill }`; any target `OTHER_USER` → `OtherUser { action: "End task" or "End process", name, pid, user, destructive: true }`. No dialog for one own, unprotected target (D-009). Cancel sends nothing.
  6. Request: `ActionRequest { id: next ActionId, kind, targets, privileged: false }` with `kind` = `Signal(Term)` (End Task), `Signal(Kill)` (End Process), `KillTree` (End Process Tree), sent through E22-016 `submit` with `texts_for`. Process actions pass `summary_min_targets = 2` (R-197). The reason in a partial summary ("Ended 4 of 5 processes (1 permission denied)") is `action_tracker::short_reason(&err)` (E16-A3): the first sentence of `message()` lower-cased without its full stop (R-196).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** one own unprotected process selected **When** `EndProcess` is dispatched **Then** no dialog opens and one request `Signal(Kill)` with one target is sent; the toast reads "End process requested.".
- **Given** a `PROTECTED` target (plasmashell) **When** `EndTask` **Then** the Protected dialog opens; Cancel sends nothing.
- **Given** 3 own processes selected **When** `EndTask` **Then** the EndMany dialog "End 3 processes?" opens; confirming sends one request with 3 targets.
- **Given** the tasklens process selected **When** `EndTask` **Then** the toast "Refusing to end tasklens itself." shows and nothing is sent.
- **Given** a process with 7 descendants **When** `EndProcessTree` **Then** the EndTree dialog says "End 8 processes in this tree?" and the request is `KillTree` with 8 targets.
- **Given** an app row whose primary is `bwrap` with child `firefox` **When** `EndTask` **Then** the request targets firefox's key, not bwrap's.
- **Given** an other-user process **When** `EndTask` **Then** the OtherUser dialog opens with "End task on <name> (PID n), owned by <user>. Continue?".
- **Given** the menu captured target X and the rows moved before the click **When** the item runs **Then** the request targets X's key.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs`: `capture_targets`, `menu_targets`, three handlers.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_process_menu.rs`: tests.

## Tests
- `ui_process_menu::single_end_process_own_unprotected_has_no_dialog` (D-009).
- `ui_process_menu::protected_target_confirms`.
- `ui_process_menu::multi_end_confirms_with_count`.
- `ui_process_menu::refusals_self_pid1_kthread`.
- `ui_process_menu::end_tree_collects_descendants_capped_256`.
- `ui_process_menu::end_app_unwraps_bwrap`.
- `ui_process_menu::row_menu_targets_captured_on_open`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: refusals and failures show the E22-016 toasts.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: keyboard path Delete / Ctrl+E and Shift+Delete / Ctrl+X (E22-026); dialogs focus Cancel.
- Performance: descendant walk O(records) once per action; no work per frame.
- Privacy: requests carry keys only; logs record kind, PID and result (ADR-015).
- Security: identity is captured as `ProcessKey` and revalidated by the engine before acting (PROC-001, ADR-006); the UI never signals by bare PID.

## Notes
- The rule order of step 5 is settled (R-198: Protected, then End tree, then Kill app, then several targets, then another user's process) and so is the descendant walk (R-192: breadth first by `ppid` over non-exited records, capped at 256 keys).
- Build rule: run every cargo build, check, clippy or test through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_processes` (it takes the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope; the wait can be long, so run it in the background when your tool call has a timeout). On an OOM kill (exit 137) retry once, then report.
- Strings: every user-visible string in this bead is appended to `assets/locales/en-US.ftl` in this bead (R-132), key `processes-<entry>-<slug>` (for example `processes-menu-end-task`), and read through `tr(key)` / `tr_args(key, args)` from `src/i18n.rs`. The English text in this bead is the value, exactly.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <the files of this bead>`.

title: Suspend, Resume and Set Priority nice-class handlers
description:
## Context
Handlers for Suspend Process, Resume Process and the P1 Set Priority classes (High, Above normal, Normal, Below normal, Low) on process rows and multi-selections, plus nice classes on app rows. Sources: PROC-063, PROC-066 (nice classes), PROC-069 (multi priority), PROC-059 (confirmations), R-034, R-038, ADR-006 (SetNice on every TID, Suspend and Resume through the pidfd), UI-PRC-013 item 4 and 6, UI-PRC-015.

## Deliverable
`.on_action` handlers in `pages/processes/mod.rs` for `SuspendProcess`, `ResumeProcess` and `SetPriority { class }`, using `capture_targets` / `menu_targets` (E22-017):
- Common steps 1 and 2 of E22-017 (drop pseudo and exited targets; refusals: `IS_SELF` "Refusing to end tasklens itself." applies to Suspend only; PID 1 "PID 1 (systemd) cannot be ended." applies to Suspend only; `KERNEL_THREAD` "Kernel threads cannot be signalled." applies to Suspend and Resume).
- Suspend / Resume: `ActionKind::Suspend` / `ActionKind::Resume`, one `ActionTarget::Process` per target. Confirmation: `PROTECTED` target → `Protected { action: "Suspend", tree_count: None }`; `OTHER_USER` target → `OtherUser { action: "Suspend" or "Resume", destructive: false }`. No confirmation for own processes, even with several targets. App and unit rows are skipped (Freeze App is E22-035).
- Set Priority High, AboveNormal, Normal, BelowNormal, Low: `ActionKind::SetNice(class.nice())` with nice -10, -5, 0, 5, 19. Targets: process rows; app and unit rows expand to every current member process ("Applies to the app's current processes"). Confirmation only for `OTHER_USER` targets (`OtherUser { action: "Set priority", destructive: false }`). Realtime and Idle are E22-036; Custom… is E23's.
- Toasts through E22-016: "Process suspended.", "Process resumed.", "Priority updated", multi "Selected process priority updated.", "Could not update selected process priority.", partial "Priority updated for 3 of 4 processes. 1 failed: permission denied".
- Menu label rule data for E22-A2: `fn suspend_or_resume(t: &CapturedTargets) -> SuspendLabel` returning `Resume` when every target has State T, else `Suspend` (multi: "Resume Selected Tasks" only when every target is stopped).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a running own process **When** `SuspendProcess` **Then** one request `Suspend` is sent with no dialog and the success toast is "Process suspended.".
- **Given** two stopped and one running process **When** `suspend_or_resume` runs **Then** it returns Suspend.
- **Given** two stopped processes **When** it runs **Then** it returns Resume.
- **Given** an app row with 3 members **When** `SetPriority { High }` **Then** one request `SetNice(-10)` with 3 process targets is sent.
- **Given** a kernel thread **When** `SuspendProcess` **Then** the toast "Kernel threads cannot be signalled." shows and nothing is sent.

- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: menu items and their keys reach every handler.
- Performance: N/A

title: Process copy commands: Copy, Copy details, Copy all metrics, Copy rows as table
description:
## Context
The four copy commands of the process table: Copy (clicked cell), Copy details (Ctrl+C), Copy all metrics and Copy rows as table (Ctrl+Shift+C). They work on exited rows too. Sources: PROC-070, R-012, R-091, R-094, ADR-015 (deliberate export; command lines only in Copy all metrics and the Command line cell), UI-PRC-011 (copy enabled on exited rows), UI-PRC-015 (copy toasts).

## Deliverable
In `pages/processes/cells.rs`: pure text builders
```rust
pub fn copy_cell(rows: &[RowRef], col: &ProcColumn, ctx: &CellCtx) -> String;     // one displayed value per line, view order
pub fn copy_details(rows: &[RowRef], ctx: &CellCtx) -> String;                     // fixed block per row, blank line between rows
pub fn copy_all_metrics(rows: &[RowRef], ctx: &CellCtx) -> String;                 // Label: value lines, picker order, ending "Command line: …"
pub fn copy_rows_as_table(rows: &[RowRef], visible: &[ColumnId], ctx: &CellCtx) -> String; // TSV with a header line of labels
```
and in `pages/processes/mod.rs` `.on_action` handlers for E18's shared `CopyCell { col }`, `CopyDetails`, `CopyRowsAsTable` and this page's `CopyAllMetrics`, writing with `cx.write_to_clipboard(ClipboardItem::new_string(text))` and toasting.
Copy details block (exact field order and labels):
```
Name: firefox
PID: 4321
Parent PID: 2010
CPU: 3.27%
Memory: 812 MiB
Private bytes: 1490 MiB
Working set: 1104 MiB
Threads: 97
Handles: 412
Priority: Normal (0)
```
CPU is `%.2f%%` of the whole machine (R-094, the only two-decimal percent). Memory is RssAnon, Private bytes is VmData + VmStk, Working set is VmRSS, each in whole MiB (bytes / 1 048 576 rounded to the nearest integer). Handles is the fd count. Priority is the PROC-029 class with the nice value in parentheses. A Restricted value prints "restricted", an Unsupported one "n/a"; never 0.
Copy all metrics: per row one `Label: value` line for every registry column (E22-002 order) whose value is Valid, using the cell's displayed text, then `Command line: <full cmdline>` last; rows separated by a blank line. Environment values are never included.
Copy rows as table: header line of the visible column labels joined by tab, then one line per row of the displayed cell texts joined by tab; Restricted cells "restricted", Unsupported "n/a", other non-Valid cells empty.
Toasts (Success, E22-016 queue): Copy one row "Copied to clipboard", several rows "Selected process values copied."; Copy details "Process details copied."; Copy all metrics one row "Copied metrics to clipboard", several "Selected process metrics copied."; Copy rows as table "Copied to clipboard".
Targets: the captured targets (E22-017), group headers excluded; exited rows included.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the fixture row above **When** `copy_details` runs **Then** the output equals `tests/golden/copy_details.txt` byte for byte.
- **Given** two rows **When** `copy_details` runs **Then** the blocks are separated by exactly one blank line.
- **Given** a Restricted Handles value **When** `copy_details` runs **Then** the line is `Handles: restricted`.
- **Given** a row with a command line **When** `copy_all_metrics` runs **Then** the last line starts with `Command line: ` and no line contains environment data.
- **Given** 3 selected rows and right-click on the CPU cell **When** Copy runs **Then** the clipboard has 3 lines and the toast is "Selected process values copied.".

title: Go to parent process and Open file location
description:
## Context

title: Process filter binding, Include children and no-match state
description:
## Context
The Processes tab's side of the shell filter box: each (already debounced) `FilterChanged` becomes one `SetTableQuery`, the "Include children" checkbox visibility and toasts, and the no-match empty state with "Clear filter". The input itself, Esc, Enter, Ctrl+F and type-to-filter routing are the shell's (E20-A2). Sources: PROC-044, PROC-045, R-043, APP-028, UI-PRC-016, UI-PRC-024, UI-SHL-024, UI-SHL-025, ADR-009 (generations).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/filter.rs` (with `pub mod filter;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`):
- `pub struct FilterBinding { _sub: Subscription }`: subscribes in `ProcessesPage::new` to the shell `FilterChanged { tab: Processes, text }` event (UI-SHL-024). The shell already debounces 100 ms before it emits `FilterChanged` (UI-SHL-024, UI-SYS-002), so this bead adds no debounce of its own (R-188): on every event it lowercases the text (`str::to_lowercase`) and calls `ProcessQuery::set_filter` and `bump_and_send` (E22-008) at once.
- The table keeps showing the previous rows until the view with the matching generation arrives (E22-008 `accept`).
- Include children: `pub fn include_children_visible(filter_nonempty: bool, mode: TableMode) -> bool` = `filter_nonempty || mode == Tree`; the page reports it to the shell's checkbox slot (UI-SHL-025). Toggling dispatches `ToggleSetting(ProcessesFilterIncludeChildren)` (E20); this page observes `processes.filter_include_children` and pushes the Info toast "Including filtered process children." when it turns on and "Hiding unmatched filtered process children." when it turns off.
- Empty state (UI-PRC-024): when the shown view has zero rows and the filter is non-empty, the delegate's `empty_text` returns "No processes match the filter" and the table shows the E15 `TlEmptyState` centred horizontally at y = 96 from the body top, text `t_base` `text_secondary`, with a `TlButton::Secondary` "Clear filter" that dispatches `ClearFilter` (E20). Group headers are not shown when nothing matches at all; when some group matches, a group with zero matches shows "(0)" with no children (engine output, drawn as is).
- History mode: the same filter applies to the History table (E30 reads the same text).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** one `FilterChanged { tab: Processes, text: "FireFox" }` event **When** it is handled **Then** exactly one `SetTableQuery` is sent at once with the filter "firefox" and a new generation (R-188).
- **Given** a filter "FiReFox" **When** sent **Then** `TableQuery.filter` is "firefox".
- **Given** filter text and Grouped mode **When** visibility is computed **Then** the checkbox is visible; empty filter in Flat mode **Then** hidden; empty filter in Tree mode **Then** visible.
- **Given** the include-children setting turns on **When** observed **Then** the toast "Including filtered process children." shows.
- **Given** a filter that matches nothing **When** the view arrives **Then** "No processes match the filter" and the "Clear filter" button show and no group header row is drawn.
- **Given** "Clear filter" is pressed **When** handled **Then** `ClearFilter` is dispatched.

title: Hold Ctrl to pause the process table
description:
## Context
Hold Ctrl to pause: while Ctrl is held and the main window is active, the process table freezes rows, order, values and header totals; collection keeps running. Sources: PROC-050, R-042, ADR-009 Ctrl-pause, ADR-005 (at most one extra retained snapshot), UI-PRC-017, UI-PRC-010 (anchoring once on resume).

## Deliverable
In `pages/processes/mod.rs`:
- Field `paused: Option<Arc<Snapshot>>` and `pub fn is_paused(&self) -> bool`.
- `window.on_modifiers_changed` (registered once in `new`): pause starts when `modifiers.control` becomes true with no other modifier held and `window.is_window_active()`; it ends when `control` becomes false. `cx.observe_window_activation` ends the pause when the window deactivates.
- On pause start: `paused = Some(current snapshot Arc)`; the delegate draws from it; hub changes are ignored (no table notify). Opening a menu or dialog does not end the pause.
- On pause end: `paused = None`; the delegate takes the latest hub snapshot and accepted view, notifies the table once, and E18's scroll anchoring runs once.
- Actions started while paused capture targets from the paused snapshot (E22-017 `capture_targets` reads the delegate's snapshot); the engine revalidates identities.
- The page emits `StatusChanged` on pause start and end so the shell's status chip appends " [PAUSED - Ctrl]" in `accent` (UI-SHL-050 draws it).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the window is active **When** Ctrl goes down **Then** `is_paused()` is true and a new snapshot with changed rows does not change the rendered rows.
- **Given** Ctrl+Shift down **When** handled **Then** no pause starts.
- **Given** paused **When** Ctrl goes up **Then** the table renders the latest view once.
- **Given** paused **When** the window deactivates **Then** the pause ends.
- **Given** paused and the row menu opened **When** End Task is chosen **Then** the request targets the paused snapshot's identity.
- **Given** paused **When** five snapshots arrive **Then** the table render count does not increase.

- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs`: pause state and observers.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/delegate.rs`: draw from the paused snapshot.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_processes.rs`: tests.

title: Processes status chip text
description:
## Context
The Processes tab's text in the shell's floating status chip: counts, filtered counts, selection size, the restricted count. Sources: PROC-051, PROC-048, PROC-050, PROC-076, UI-PRC-018, UI-SHL-050 (chip, `status_text`, `StatusChanged`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/status.rs` (with `pub mod status;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`) and `ProcessesPage::status_text(&self, out: &mut String)` per the UI-SHL-050 page method, emitting `StatusChanged` when the text changes:
- Segment 1: "296 Processes" (no filter) or "41 / 296 Processes" (filter set). The count excludes pseudo rows and includes kernel threads only when they are shown.
- Segment 2, 2 or more selected rows: " | 3 processes selected" (selected identities hidden by the filter are not counted).
- Segment 3, paused: drawn by the shell from `is_paused()` (" [PAUSED - Ctrl]" in `accent`); not written here.
- Segment 4, restricted rows exist: " | 42 restricted", plain text before P3 with tooltip "Some values for other users' processes need administrator rights." (the clickable P3 form is E22-041).
- Separators " | " drawn `text_secondary`, text `t_sm` 12 `text_primary` (shell).
- Counts (`total`, `shown`, `restricted`) come from the accepted `ProcessTableView` fields of that meaning (E03-A2).
- The text is rebuilt only when a count, the filter state or the selection size changes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 296 processes and no filter **When** `status_text` runs **Then** it is "296 Processes".
- **Given** a filter showing 41 **When** run **Then** it is "41 / 296 Processes".
- **Given** 3 selected rows **When** run **Then** " | 3 processes selected" is appended.
- **Given** 1 selected row **When** run **Then** no selection segment.
- **Given** 42 restricted rows **When** run **Then** " | 42 restricted" is appended and its tooltip is the pre-P3 text.
- **Given** 2 pseudo rows and hidden kernel threads **When** counted **Then** neither is in segment 1.
- **Given** nothing changed **When** a snapshot arrives **Then** `StatusChanged` is not emitted.

title: E22-A3 Jump target: ProcessesPage::select_by_key
description:
## Context
Anchor E22-A3. The Processes tab's one "select process by identity" entry point, used by Go to parent, the Properties PPID link, Services and Connections "Jump to process", Handle Search "Go to process", the window picker, the History table, `--select-pid` and D-Bus `select-pid`. It switches to the tab, leaves History mode, expands the path, selects the row and centres it, or explains why it cannot. Sources: PROC-071, PROC-055 (picker result), PROC-088 (History row), UI-PRC-022, UI-PRC-010 (centre scroll), UI-PRC-015 (jump toasts and "Show" button), SYS-010, SYS-033.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/jump.rs` (with `pub mod jump;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub struct JumpTexts {
    pub switched_tab: Option<SharedString>, // shown when the tab changed; None = "Switched to Processes tab"
    pub success: Option<SharedString>,      // caller's success toast, replaces switched_tab when set (e.g. "Switched to owning process.")
    pub not_found: SharedString,            // default "Process not found in current view"
    pub hidden: Option<SharedString>,       // caller's "not visible" text; None = not_found text; always shown with a "Show" button
}
impl Default for JumpTexts { /* switched_tab None, success None, not_found "Process not found in current view", hidden None */ }
impl ProcessesPage {
    pub fn select_by_key(&mut self, key: ProcessKey, texts: JumpTexts, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>);
    pub fn select_by_pid(&mut self, pid: u32, texts: JumpTexts, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut Context<Self>); // resolves pid to the current non-exited record's key, then select_by_key; no record: not_found toast
}
```
Steps of `select_by_key`:
1. If the Processes tab is not active, dispatch E20's `SelectTab` for Processes; remember that the tab changed. If `UiState.processes.history_mode` is true, set it false (the live table is the only place a live identity can be shown).
2. Look the key up in the current `ProcessSnapshot.records`. Absent or EXITED: Warning toast `not_found`; stop.
3. Present but not in the current view (filtered out or hidden by Hide system processes): Warning toast `hidden.unwrap_or(not_found)` with a `ToastAction { label: "Show", action: ProcessesShowHidden }`. The page stores the pending key. On "Show": clear the filter (E20 FilterBox clear), set `processes.hide_system = false`, wait for the view with the matching generation, then continue at step 4.
4. Expand the path: in Grouped mode the record's group header and every collapsed ancestor; in Tree mode every collapsed ancestor (ancestors by ppid walk over the records). One `ProcessQuery::expand_path` and one `SetTableQuery`; the page keeps `pending_jump: Option<(ProcessKey, JumpTexts, bool /*tab changed*/)>`.
5. When a view with a matching generation contains the row: selection = {key} (anchor and focus = key), `scroll_to_item_strict(ix, ScrollStrategy::Center)`, focus the table. Toast (Info): `success`, else `switched_tab` or "Switched to Processes tab" when the tab changed, else no toast.
6. If the matching view still lacks the row: Warning toast `not_found`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the Services tab is active and a process inside a collapsed app in Grouped mode **When** `select_by_key` runs **Then** the tab becomes Processes, the app row is expanded, the row is selected, centred, the table focused, and the toast reads "Switched to Processes tab".
- **Given** a caller success text "Switched to owning process." **When** the jump succeeds from another tab **Then** that text is the only toast.
- **Given** a key whose process exited **When** called **Then** the toast is "Process not found in current view".
- **Given** a process hidden by the filter "foo" **When** called with hidden text "Owning process not visible in the current view." **Then** that toast shows with a "Show" button; pressing Show clears the filter, keeps hide_system false, and selects the row when the matching view arrives.
- **Given** History mode is on **When** called **Then** `history_mode` becomes false.
- **Given** Tree mode with two collapsed ancestors **When** called **Then** one query is sent whose `expanded` contains both.
- **Given** pid 4321 with a live record **When** `select_by_pid(4321, ..)` **Then** it behaves as `select_by_key` with that record's key.

title: Process table meets the table-2000 performance gate
description:
## Context
Performance gate for the production process table: with highlight, tooltips and every P1 cell in place, the ADR-014 `table-2000` scene must still pass. Sources: ADR-014 (`table-2000` gate: UI thread p99 ≤ 2.0 ms per frame while scrolling at 1,200 px/s with 1 Hz value changes and re-sorts; 0 missed frames in the median run; RSS ≤ 150 MB; a regression above 20 % blocks the phase), UI-PRC-023 (budget split, rules 1 to 8, in-GPUI fallback order), PROC-013, ADR-009 text cache.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_processes.rs`: an allocation and cache test using the FakeEngine with the E01 seed-42 synthetic 2,000-row source:
  - `CellTextCache` hit rate above 95 % over 10 identical table versions;
  - zero `CellOut` text writes for unchanged cells across two installs of the same values;
  - at most 27 row elements built per frame in a 720 px viewport;
  - no element id on metric cells (only row hitbox, Name cell and window button ids).
- Run `tasklens --bench table-2000 --duration 30 --warmup 5 --json out.json` three times through `cargo xtask bench` (E01-A1) and record p50, p99, missed frames and RSS in the commit message.
- If the gate fails, apply the in-GPUI fallback in this order and re-measure after each step, in the E22 page files only: (1) column culling: the row builder skips columns whose `[x, x + w)` misses the viewport (if E18 does not already); (2) merge heat quads per row into one quad with the max alpha; (3) drop zebra quads for one `list_bg` fill plus 1 px row dividers; (4) report to the leader with the numbers if it still fails (ADR-014 decision rule, no further change here).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the seed-42 2,000-row scene **When** the bench runs 3 times **Then** the median run has UI thread p99 ≤ 2.0 ms, 0 missed frames and RSS ≤ 150 MB.
- **Given** 10 identical table versions **When** rendered **Then** the text cache hit rate is above 95 %.
- **Given** two installs with equal values **When** rendered **Then** no cell text is formatted.

App rows show the title of the app's most recently active window as dimmed secondary text after the name, when the KWin bridge is up. Sources: PROC-008, PROC-053, UI-PRC-003 (secondary text rules), ADR-004 KWin bridge, `WindowsSnapshot`.

## Deliverable
In `pages/processes/name_cell.rs` and `delegate.rs`: `NameCellData` gains `secondary: Option<SharedString>`. For app rows, the delegate looks up the member PIDs in `Snapshot.windows` and uses the caption of the most recently active window (the entry order or activation field E14 provides). Rendering: after an `sp4` 8 px gap on the same line, `t_base` regular `text_secondary` (selected: `text_selected_secondary`), ellipsis shared with the primary text so the primary text never truncates before the secondary text is gone; the secondary text is hidden entirely when the cell is narrower than primary text width + 8 + 40 px. No bridge (`windows` validity Unsupported): no secondary text. The delegate's name cache stores `(primary, secondary)` and re-shapes only when either string changes; the page re-renders on `ComponentMask::WINDOWS`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** Firefox with a window "Mozilla Firefox - Inbox" **When** rendered at 400 px **Then** the Name cell reads "Firefox (14)" then "Mozilla Firefox - Inbox" in `text_secondary`.
- **Given** a cell narrower than primary + 48 px **When** rendered **Then** the secondary text is not drawn.
- **Given** a narrow cell that fits primary + 48 but not both texts **When** rendered **Then** the secondary text is ellipsised and the primary text is whole.
- **Given** no bridge **When** rendered **Then** no secondary text.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/name_cell.rs`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/delegate.rs`.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_process_cells.rs`.

## Tests
- `ui_process_cells::app_window_title_secondary_text`.
- `ui_process_cells::secondary_hidden_below_threshold`.
- `ui_process_cells::secondary_truncates_before_primary`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: Unsupported bridge gives no text, not an error.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one cache entry per app row; no per-frame string work.
- Privacy: window captions are display only, never logged.

## Notes
- "Most recently active" ordering comes from the `WindowsSnapshot` contract (E03, filled by E14-A2). If it carries no activation order, stop and report.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, check, clippy or test through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_processes` (it takes the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope; the wait can be long, so run it in the background when your tool call has a timeout). On an OOM kill (exit 137) retry once, then report.

title: Name-cell window button and window popup
description:
## Context
The Name-cell window button: on hover and on selected rows that own top-level windows, a small button opens a popup listing the windows; choosing one activates it through the KWin bridge. Sources: PROC-053, PROC-054 (toasts), UI-PRC-003 (button and popup), ADR-005 (`Command::KWin(KWinCommand::Activate)`).

## Deliverable
- `pages/processes/name_cell.rs`: a `TlButton::Icon` 20 × 20 with Lucide `app-window` 14 px at the cell's right edge inset `sp2` 4 px, vertically centred, `.id(("winbtn", node))`; visible on the hovered row and on selected rows when the row owns at least one top-level window (process rows: own PID; app rows: any member PID); tooltip "Windows (N)". It is a Tab stop only while visible on the focused row.
- `pages/processes/menu.rs`: `pub fn window_popup(menu: TlMenu, windows: &[WindowEntry]) -> TlMenu`, anchored below the button, one item per window, label = caption or "Untitled window", no icon, `min_w(240)`, `max_w(480)`, captions ellipsised; each item dispatches `ActivateWindow { internal_id }`.

Enter in the popup activates; Esc closes and returns focus to the table.

- **Given** a hovered process row owning 2 windows **When** rendered **Then** the button shows with tooltip "Windows (2)".
- **Given** a row with no window **When** hovered **Then** no button.

title: Freeze App, Thaw App and Kill App
description:
## Context
P2 app and unit row actions: Freeze App, Thaw App and Kill App (all processes), and End Process on app and unit rows mapping to Kill App. Sources: PROC-064, PROC-061 (Kill App label on app rows), PROC-059 (Kill App confirmation), R-033, R-040, R-092 (target type by cgroup location), ADR-006 (cgroup operations, units outside `app.slice`), UI-PRC-013 items 2 and 4, UI-PRC-014 (Kill App text), UI-PRC-015 (toasts).

## Deliverable
- `pages/processes/menu.rs`: on app and unit rows, item 2 "Kill App (all processes)" → `KillApp`; item 4 "Freeze App" or "Thaw App" (Thaw when the row is frozen) → `FreezeApp` / `ThawApp`. Exited rule as in E22-A2.
- `pages/processes/mod.rs` handlers:
  - Target per app or unit row: `ActionTarget::Cgroup(CgroupRef)` when the group's cgroup is under `user@<uid>.service/app.slice/`; `ActionTarget::Unit(UnitRef)` for every other unit (R-092). The refs come from the `GroupRow` fields of that meaning.
  - `FreezeApp` → `ActionKind::FreezeGroup`; `ThawApp` → `ThawGroup`; `KillApp` → `KillGroup`.
  - `EndProcess` on an app or unit row now dispatches the `KillApp` flow.
  - Confirmation: Kill App always → `KillApp { app: name, count: member_count }` ("Kill <App>?" / "Kill all N processes of <App>?" / "Kill app"); Freeze on a row containing a `PROTECTED` member → `Protected { action: "Freeze", tree_count: None }`.
  - Toasts (E22-016): "App frozen", "App thawed", "App killed" [Success]; failures through the tracker message.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** an app row under `app.slice` **When** Freeze App is chosen **Then** one request `FreezeGroup` with an `ActionTarget::Cgroup` is sent and "App frozen" shows on success.
- **Given** a unit row in `session.slice` **When** Freeze App is chosen **Then** the target is `ActionTarget::Unit`.
- **Given** an app with 14 processes **When** Kill App is chosen **Then** the dialog "Kill all 14 processes of Firefox?" opens; confirming sends `KillGroup`.
- **Given** a frozen app row **When** the menu opens **Then** item 4 reads "Thaw App".
- **Given** Shift+Delete on an app row **When** handled **Then** the Kill App dialog opens.

title: Set Priority Realtime and Idle, Set I/O Priority submenu
description:
## Context
P2 priority items: Set Priority > Realtime and Idle, and the Set I/O Priority submenu. Custom… is E23's. Sources: PROC-066 (Realtime SCHED_RR 1 with reset on fork, Idle SCHED_IDLE), PROC-068 (I/O classes, scheduler note, Realtime needs the helper), PROC-069 (check marks), R-038, R-093, UI-PRC-020, UI-PWN-024 (Realtime confirmation), UI-PRC-015 (toasts).

## Deliverable
- `pages/processes/menu.rs`: in `priority_submenu`, add "Realtime" above "High" and "Idle" below "Low" (order: note line, Realtime, High, Above normal, Normal, Below normal, Low, Idle; E23 adds separator and Custom… after Idle). New `pub fn ioprio_submenu(menu, targets, caps, cx) -> TlMenu` added as item 8 "Set I/O Priority >" after item 6 (item 7 Set Affinity… is E23's): first a disabled `text_secondary` line "Scheduler: <name>" (the active block scheduler of the device holding the root filesystem, e.g. "Scheduler: bfq"), then "Realtime", "High", "Normal", "Low", "Idle", separator, "Default (follows nice)" → `SetIoPriorityClass { class }`; the current class is checked (multi: only when all share it). "Realtime" is disabled without a helper session, tooltip "Needs administrator access.", or "Needs administrator helper (not installed)" when `/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper` is absent.

- **Given** Realtime chosen **When** handled **Then** the dialog "Set realtime priority?" opens with focus on Cancel; confirming sends `SetSched { Rr, 1 }`; Cancel sends nothing.

title: Retry as administrator on permission-denied toasts
description:
## Context
P3: the "Retry as administrator" button on process-action toasts that failed with EPERM. It re-sends the same request with `privileged = true` for the failed targets only, which the engine routes to the helper (E29). Sources: PROC-058, R-035, UI-PRC-015 (button rows), ADR-005 (`privileged`), ADR-006 helper boundary.

## Deliverable
In `pages/processes/toasts.rs`: when a request's final state has one or more targets with the permission-denied `ActionError`, the result toast gets `ToastAction { label: "Retry as administrator", action: RetryPrivileged { request: ActionId } }` (data action declared here with namespace `tasklens`). The page keeps the last 16 requests' `ActionRequest`s in a ring (`VecDeque`, capacity 16) for this purpose. The handler builds a new `ActionRequest` with a new `ActionId`, the same `kind`, only the EPERM targets, and `privileged: true`, and submits it with the same texts. Toasts with a button stay 15 s (UI-FND-020). No automatic retry ever.

title: E22-045 Window-pick result on the Processes page: select, Picked dialog, toasts
description:
## Context
The window picker "+" (PROC-055) is started and cancelled by the shell (E20-027): it sends `KWinCommand::Pick`, shows the start toast and enters the Picker key context. Nothing handled the result. This bead is the Processes page's half (R-239): it reads the pick result from the windows snapshot, ends picking, and either selects the picked process, ends it after a confirmation, or shows the matching toast. Phase P3. Sources: PROC-055, UI-SHL-014, PROC-071 (jump target), UI-PRC-014 (Picked confirmation), R-046, R-239, OI-E11 (pick result path, R-149).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/pick.rs` (new; `mod pick;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`, chain edit):
- `pub struct PickWatch { last_seq: u64 }`, a field of `ProcessesPage`, fed from the page's existing hub subscription on `ComponentMask::WINDOWS` changes.
- The result is `Snapshot.windows.pick: Option<PickResult { seq: u64, outcome: PickOutcome }>` with `PickOutcome::{Picked { pid: u32 }, NoWindow, Cancelled }` (engine side, OI-E11). A result is handled once: only when `seq > last_seq`; then `last_seq = seq`.
- Handling, in order:
  1. End picking in the shell: through `ShellState.main_window`, `main.update(cx, |mw, cx| mw.end_window_pick(cx))` (E20-027). This removes the start toast and the Picker context.
  2. `NoWindow`: Info toast "No window found" with key `PICK_TOAST` (E20-027 constant) in the main window. Stop.
  3. `Cancelled`: Info toast "No window selected" with key `PICK_TOAST` (same text and key as E20-027's Esc path, so a second push replaces the first). Stop.
  4. `Picked { pid }`: find the non-exited record with that pid in the current process snapshot. None: Info toast "Unknown process" with key `PICK_TOAST`. Stop. Picking a tasklens window simply finds the tasklens process.
  5. Modifier: when the main window is active (`window.is_window_active()`), read Ctrl from `window.modifiers().control` at handling time. Active and Ctrl held: run End Task on that key (dispatch `EndTask` with `menu_targets` set to that one key, so E22-017's refusals and confirmation rules apply). Active and Ctrl not held: select (step 6).
  6. Main window not active (tasklens cannot see the modifier, PROC-055): open the Picked confirmation (E22-015, `ConfirmKind::Picked { name, pid }`: "Picked <name> (PID n)" / "What do you want to do with this process?", primary "Select", second "Terminate" danger). `Confirmed` → select; `Second` → End Task as in step 5; `Cancelled` → nothing.
  - Select: `ProcessesPage::select_by_key(key, JumpTexts::default(), window, cx)` (E22-A3), which switches to the Processes tab, clears a filter that hides the row and scrolls to it (PROC-071).
- String keys appended to `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: `prc-055-no-window-found` "No window found", `prc-055-unknown-process` "Unknown process" ("No window selected" is E20-027's key).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** picking is on and a snapshot with `pick = Some(PickResult { seq: 1, outcome: Picked { pid: 4242 } })` while the main window is not active **When** handled **Then** `end_window_pick` ran and the Picked dialog "Picked firefox (PID 4242)" opens.
- **Given** that dialog **When** "Select" is chosen **Then** the Processes tab is active and pid 4242's row is selected and visible.
- **Given** that dialog **When** "Terminate" is chosen **Then** an End Task request (`Signal(Term)`) for pid 4242's key is sent, through E22-017's rules.
- **Given** the main window is active and Ctrl is held **When** a `Picked` result arrives **Then** End Task runs on that key with no Picked dialog.
- **Given** the main window is active and Ctrl is not held **When** a `Picked` result arrives **Then** the row is selected with no dialog.
- **Given** `outcome = NoWindow` **When** handled **Then** the Info toast "No window found" shows and picking ends.
- **Given** `outcome = Cancelled` **When** handled **Then** the Info toast "No window selected" shows once (key `PICK_TOAST`).
- **Given** `Picked { pid: 99999 }` with no such record **When** handled **Then** the Info toast "Unknown process" shows.
- **Given** a result with `seq = 1` was handled **When** a later snapshot carries the same `seq = 1` **Then** nothing happens.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/pick.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs`: `mod pick;`, the `PickWatch` field and the call from the hub handler (chain edit).
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: two keys (chain edit).
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_processes.rs`: tests.

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_processes.rs` (FakeEngine windows snapshots with `pick` set):
- `pick_result_opens_picked_dialog_when_inactive`: criterion 1.
- `pick_select_jumps_to_row`: criterion 2.
- `pick_terminate_sends_end_task`: criterion 3.
- `pick_ctrl_active_ends_task`: criterion 4.
- `pick_plain_active_selects`: criterion 5.
- `pick_no_window_toast`: criterion 6.
- `pick_cancelled_toast_once`: criterion 7.
- `pick_unknown_process_toast`: criterion 8.
- `pick_same_seq_ignored`: criterion 9.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the three Info toasts above; action errors through E22-016 and the ActionTracker.
- Validity: a `Restricted` or exited row is handled by the jump target and E22-017 as for any other caller.
- Accessibility: the Picked dialog is keyboard operable (E22-015: focus on Cancel, Esc cancels).
- Performance: one comparison per `WINDOWS` change.
- Privacy: logs only the outcome kind and pid.

## Notes
- The pick result type and `KWinCommand::Pick { seq }` / `CancelPick { seq }` are engine side (OI-E11, R-149; tl-model `WindowsSnapshot.pick`). If `WindowsSnapshot.pick` does not exist when you start, stop and report.
- `end_window_pick`, `PICK_TOAST` and the picking state are E20-027 (tasklens-jqk.29). `select_by_key` and `JumpTexts::default()` are E22-A3 (tasklens-pdu.3). The Picked dialog is E22-015 (tasklens-pdu.18). End Task is E22-017 (tasklens-pdu.20).
- The rule "dialog when the main window is not active" applies PROC-055's "when it cannot see the modifier": GPUI reports modifiers only while tasklens has focus, and during a KWin pick it usually does not.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_processes`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/pick.rs crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs assets/locales/en-US.ftl crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_processes.rs`. Never a bare `git commit`.

title: Process cells: index each app group's first member once per view, not a scan per cell
description:
Files: crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/cells.rs, crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/table.rs, crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_process_cells.rs.
Why: pdu.7 (53f0ad6) cells.rs first_member() walks ctx.records with find() for every User, Description, Command line and Start time cell of every app row, on every frame. With 500 processes and 20 visible app rows that is about 40 000 comparisons per frame for nothing. Rendering speed comes first.
Leader decision: build a small index (group key to record index of the earliest-started member) once when a new view generation is accepted (pdu.11 table.rs accept), keep it beside the view, and pass it in CellCtx. first_member becomes one hash lookup. No index rebuild while the generation is unchanged.
AC: test hook counts index builds: 60 frames over an unchanged view build it once; a new generation builds it once more. App-row text cells show the same values as before. Existing ui_process_cells and ui_processes tests pass. clippy clean with and without test-hooks.
close_reason: Covered by pdu.7 commit 5713b4c: GroupMembers index in cells.rs, rebuilt only on view version or records change; test group_member_index_built_once_per_view checks 60 frames build once and a new generation builds once more. Tests, clippy (with and without test-hooks) and fmt pass.

title: Processes page Actions and captured target types
description:
## Context
Declares every Processes-page GPUI Action and the captured-target types that the row menu, the keymap and the handlers share. One command is one Action: key binding, menu item and toolbar button dispatch the same Action (table b, PROC-013, PROC-057). Shared table actions (`OpenProperties`, `CopyCell { col }`, `CopyDetails`, `CopyRowsAsTable`, `SelectAll`, `CollapseAll`, `ToggleExpand`, `OpenContextMenu`, `MoveFocus*`) belong to E18 `table/actions.rs`; window-level actions (`FocusFilter`, `ClearFilter`, `ToggleHideSystem`, `CycleViewMode`, `SetViewMode`, `ToggleSetting`, `StartHelperSession`) belong to E20 `actions.rs` (docs/ui/INDEX.md "Actions"). Sources: UI-PRC-009, UI-PRC-013, UI-PRC-020, PROC-001, R-128, ADR-005, ADR-009.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/actions.rs`, plus the line `pub mod actions;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`.

Unit actions via `gpui::actions!(tasklens, [ ... ])`:
`EndTask`, `EndProcess`, `EndProcessTree`, `KillApp`, `SuspendProcess`, `ResumeProcess`, `FreezeApp`, `ThawApp`, `ShowWindow`, `CopyAllMetrics`, `FileProperties`, `OpenFileLocation`, `OpenVirusTotal`, `CreateDump`, `GoToParent`, `ProcessesShowHidden`.

Data actions (`#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Deserialize, JsonSchema, Action)] #[action(namespace = tasklens)]`):
- `SetPriority { class: PriorityClass }` with `pub enum PriorityClass { Realtime, High, AboveNormal, Normal, BelowNormal, Low, Idle }` and `fn nice(self) -> Option<i8>`: High -10, AboveNormal -5, Normal 0, BelowNormal 5, Low 19; Realtime and Idle return None (they map to `SetSched`, see E22-036).
- `SetIoPriorityClass { class: IoClass }` with `pub enum IoClass { Realtime, High, Normal, Low, Idle, Default }` and `fn to_model(self) -> tl_model::actions::IoPriority`: Realtime -> `Realtime(0)`, High -> `BestEffort(0)`, Normal -> `BestEffort(4)`, Low -> `BestEffort(7)`, Idle -> `Idle`, Default -> `None` (PROC-068, R-093).
- `RestartUnit { unit: tl_model::table::UnitRef }`.
- `ActivateWindow { internal_id: SharedString }`.

Captured targets (PROC-001: captured when the menu opens or the key is pressed, max 256):
```rust
pub const MAX_TARGETS: usize = 256;
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct CapturedTarget {
    pub node: NodeId,               // identity, never an index
    pub kind: RowKind,              // App | Unit | Process | KernelThread | Pseudo (never GroupHeader)
    pub name: SharedString,         // display name as drawn in the Name cell, without the " (N)" count
    pub pid: Option<u32>,           // None for app, unit and pseudo rows
    pub uid: u32,
    pub user: SharedString,
    pub flags: ProcFlags,           // NEW, EXITED, KERNEL_THREAD, OTHER_USER, IS_SELF, PROTECTED
    pub member_count: u32,          // processes of an app or unit row, 1 for a process row
}
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct CapturedTargets {
```

title: Process column registry: ids, labels, groups, kinds, widths
description:
## Context
The process column registry: one static entry per process-table column with its id, label, picker group, kind, alignment, width template, default width, sort rule, heat reference and phase. The delegate (E22-009) returns `ColumnSpec`s built from it, the column picker (E18-A2) lists it, and the cell formatter (E22-003) dispatches on its kind. Sources: PROC-022 to PROC-036, PROC-047 (unsortable columns), PROC-040 and R-059 (heat references), R-006 (default set and widths), R-007 (ids and labels), R-065 (aliases), UI-PRC-004, UI-PRC-005 (header tooltips), UI-PRC-007 (groups).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/cells.rs` (created here; later beads add to it), plus `pub mod cells;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`:

```rust
pub enum ProcColumnKind { Text, IntegerId, Percent, MemorySize, DiskRate, NetRate, Count, BytesCumulative, Duration, Time, PowerClass }
pub enum HeatRef { CpuMachine, CpuOneCore, Memory, DiskIo, Network, GpuPercent, Vram, Power, None }
pub enum PickerGroup { Image, Identity, Security, Scheduling, Cpu, Memory, Io, Disk, Network, Gpu, Power, Objects, Linux }
pub struct ProcColumn {
    pub id: ColumnId,              // tl-model ColumnId, string from R-007
    pub label: &'static str,       // header line 1 and picker label
    pub alias: Option<&'static str>, // picker full name, shown as `<alias> - "<label>"`
    pub group: PickerGroup,
    pub kind: ProcColumnKind,
    pub template: Option<&'static str>, // PROC-023 width template
    pub default_width: Option<f32>,     // logical px at 100%
    pub sortable: bool,
    pub heat: HeatRef,
    pub phase: u8,                      // 1..=4; columns of a later phase are not offered
    pub header_tooltip: Option<&'static str>,
}
pub static PROCESS_COLUMNS: &[ProcColumn];
pub fn process_column(id: ColumnId) -> &'static ProcColumn;
pub const DEFAULT_VISIBLE: [&str; 9] = ["name","user","pid","cpu","memory","disk","network","gpu","description"];
```

Alignment: `Text` and `PowerClass` left; every other kind right. Minimum width (PROC-023): measured template width + 2 × 8 padding (+ 12 on the active sort column, applied by E18); kinds without a template use 60 px.

Templates: PID, Parent PID, SID `"999999 +99"`; every Percent column `"100.0%"`; NetRate `"xxx Mbps"` when `units.network = "bits"`, `"xxx MiB/s"` when `"bytes"`; DiskRate `"xxx GiB/s"`; MemorySize `"999 MiB"`; Count `"999999"`; Duration `"999:59:59"`; Text none (60 px minimum).

Default widths: name 248, user 92, pid 96, cpu 63, memory 92, disk 82, network 92, gpu 72, description 342, power 101. Every other column: max(minimum, header label width + 16).

Unsortable (PROC-047): pss, uss, cycles, cycles_delta, ctx_switches, ctx_switches_delta; their header tooltip is "Only measured for visible rows".

Header tooltips (UI-PRC-005): memory "Private memory (RssAnon). Shared and file-backed pages are not counted."; ws_total "Resident set size (VmRSS)"; network "Attributed TCP traffic. UDP and other users' sockets are not counted."; handles "Open file descriptors". GPU N tooltips are built at run time (E22-009).

Aliases: memory `Working set private`, gpu_mem_dedicated `GPU memory dedicated`.

The registry rows (id | label | group | kind | heat | phase):
- Image: name | Name | Text | None | 1; name_display | Name display | Text | 1; image_name | Image name | Text | 1; image_path | Image path | Text | 1; cmdline | Command line | Text | 1; description | Description | Text | 1; type | Type | Text | 1; start_time | Start time | Time | 1; version | Version | Text | 2; timestamp | Build date | Time | 2; file_mtime | File modified time | Time | 2; file_size | File size | MemorySize | Memory | 2; company | Package | Text | 2; signer | Packager | Text | 2; signature | Package status | Text | 2; architecture | Architecture | Text | 2.
- Identity: user | User | Text | 1; pid | PID | IntegerId | 1; ppid | Parent PID | IntegerId | 1; session | Session | Text | 2.
- Security: security_label | Security label | Text | 2; elevation | Elevated | Text | 2; sandbox | Sandbox | Text | 2.
- Scheduling: priority | Priority | Text | 1; affinity | Affinity | Text | 1.
- Cpu: cpu | CPU | Percent | CpuMachine | 1; cpu_kernel | CPU (kernel) | Percent | CpuMachine | 1; cpu_user | CPU (user) | Percent | CpuMachine | 1; cpu_relative | CPU (one core = 100%) | Percent | CpuOneCore | 1; cpu_time | CPU time | Duration | 1; cpu_time_kernel | CPU time kernel | Duration | 1; cpu_time_user | CPU time user | Duration | 1; cycles | Cycles | Count | 4; cycles_delta | Cycles delta | Count | 4; ctx_switches | Context switches | Count | 2; ctx_switches_delta | Context switches delta | Count | 2.
- Memory (heat Memory for every MemorySize row): memory | Memory | 1; ws_total | Working set total | 1; ws_peak | Working set peak | 1; ws_shared | Working set shared | 1; commit | Commit size | 1; commit_peak | Commit size peak | 2; commit_delta | Commit size delta | 2; vsize | Virtual size | 1; vsize_peak | Virtual size peak | 1; page_tables | Page tables | 2; page_faults | Page faults | Count | 1; page_faults_delta | Page faults delta | Count | 1; major_faults | Major faults | Count | 2; major_faults_delta | Major faults delta | Count | 2; swap | Swap | 1; pss | PSS | 2; uss | USS | 2.
- Io: io_read_bytes | I/O read bytes | BytesCumulative | 2; io_write_bytes | I/O write bytes | BytesCumulative | 2; io_read_delta | I/O read bytes delta | BytesCumulative | 2; io_write_delta | I/O write bytes delta | BytesCumulative | 2; io_read_rate | I/O read rate | DiskRate | DiskIo | 2; io_write_rate | I/O write rate | DiskRate | DiskIo | 2; io_read_ops | I/O read ops | Count | 2; io_write_ops | I/O write ops | Count | 2.
- Disk: disk | Disk | DiskRate | DiskIo | 1; disk_read_rate | Disk read rate | DiskRate | DiskIo | 1; disk_write_rate | Disk write rate | DiskRate | DiskIo | 1; disk_total_rate | Disk total rate | DiskRate | DiskIo | 1; disk_read_bytes | Disk read bytes | BytesCumulative | 2; disk_write_bytes | Disk write bytes | BytesCumulative | 2; disk_total_bytes | Disk total bytes | BytesCumulative | 2; disk_read_delta | Disk read bytes delta | BytesCumulative | 2; disk_write_delta | Disk write bytes delta | BytesCumulative | 2; disk_total_delta | Disk total bytes delta | BytesCumulative | 2; disk_reads | Disk reads | Count | 2; disk_writes | Disk writes | Count | 2; disk_reads_delta | Disk reads delta | Count | 2; disk_writes_delta | Disk writes delta | Count | 2.
- Network: network | Network | NetRate | Network | 1; net_send_rate | Network send | NetRate | Network | 1; net_recv_rate | Network receive | NetRate | Network | 1.
- Gpu: gpu | GPU | Percent | GpuPercent | 1; gpu_mem_dedicated | VRAM | MemorySize | Vram | 1; gpu_mem_shared | GPU memory shared | MemorySize | Memory | 2; gpu_engine | GPU engine | Text | 2; gpu_encode | GPU encode | Percent | GpuPercent | 2; gpu_decode | GPU decode | Percent | GpuPercent | 2; gpu_0 .. gpu_15 | GPU 0 .. GPU 15 | Percent | GpuPercent | 2.
- Power: power | Power usage | PowerClass | Power | 2; power_trend | Power usage trend | PowerClass | Power | 2.
- Objects: handles | Handles | Count | 1; threads | Threads | Count | 1; windows | Windows | Count | 3; x11_resources | X11 resources | Count | 4.
- Linux: state | State | Text | 1; nice | Nice | IntegerId | 1; sched_policy | Scheduling policy | Text | 2; io_priority | I/O priority | Text | 2; unit | Unit | Text | 1; cgroup | Cgroup | Text | 2; app_id | App ID | Text | 2; oom_score | OOM score | IntegerId | 2; oom_score_adj | OOM adj | IntegerId | 2; tty | TTY | Text | 2; cwd | Working directory | Text | 2; pgrp | Process group | IntegerId | 4; sid | SID | IntegerId | 4; last_cpu | Last CPU | IntegerId | 4; container | Container | Text | 4.
Rows without a heat value above use `HeatRef::None`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Given** the six unsortable ids **When** looked up **Then** `sortable` is false and `header_tooltip` is "Only measured for visible rows".

title: Process cell values and table (d) formatting
description:
## Context
Fills a cell's value bits, validity and text for every process-table row kind and column, using the registry (E22-002) and the table (d) formatters in `tl_model::units`. The cell text is produced only when `(value_bits, validity)` changed, so steady-state rendering formats nothing (ADR-009 text cache, UI-PRC-023 rule 2). Sources: PROC-003 (formats, canonical table d), PROC-008 (app row values), PROC-009 (unit rows), PROC-018 (PID +N), PROC-027 to PROC-036 (column sources), R-005, R-013 to R-015, R-050, UI-PRC-004 (content per kind), ADR-003 (ProcessRecord, FieldValidity), ADR-009 (CellTextCache).

## Deliverable
In `pages/processes/cells.rs`:
```rust
pub struct CellCtx<'a> {
    pub view: &'a ProcessTableView,
    pub records: &'a [ProcessRecord],   // ProcessSnapshot.records
    pub settings: &'a Settings,         // units.network, units.network_auto_scale
    pub ncpu: u16,                      // online CPUs, for heat (E22-004)
    pub mem_total: u64,                 // MemTotal bytes, for heat
    pub vram_total: u64,                // sum of GPU VRAM bytes, for heat; 0 when no GPU
}
pub enum RowRef<'a> { Group(&'a GroupRow, RowKind), Record(&'a ProcessRecord, RowKind) }
pub fn fill_cell(row: RowRef, col: &ProcColumn, ctx: &CellCtx, out: &mut CellOut);
```
`CellOut` is E18-A1's buffer (value bits `u64`, `Validity`, text `String` written only on change, plus optional secondary text). Rules:
- Value bits: numeric values `f32::to_bits` or the `u64` itself; text values the address of the backing `Arc<str>` (`Arc::as_ptr as *const u8 as u64`), so a new metadata `Arc` re-formats and an unchanged one never does.
- Formats (table d), all through `tl_model::units` into `out.text`: Percent `%.1f%%`, a value that rounds to 0.0 is `0%`; MemorySize and BytesCumulative IEC base 1024 with 2 decimals from 1 KiB (`16.00 KiB`, `1.22 GiB`), below 1 KiB `512 B`, zero `0 B`; DiskRate fixed MiB/s 1 decimal (`0.4 MiB/s`, zero `0 MiB/s`); NetRate per `units.network`: bits SI fixed Mbps 1 decimal (`2.3 Mbps`, zero `0 Mbps`) or with auto-scale Kbps/Mbps/Gbps; bytes IEC fixed MiB/s or with auto-scale KiB/s/MiB/s/GiB/s; Count digits grouped with U+2009 thin space (`12 345`), zero `0`; Duration `h:mm:ss`, past 999:59:59 `Nd hh:mm`, zero `0:00:00`; Time today `HH:MM:SS`, else `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`; IntegerId plain digits.
- PID column: collapsed parent with descendants writes `"11528"` as primary text and `" +18"` as secondary text (drawn `text_secondary` by E22-004); expanded parent and leaf write the PID only (PROC-018).
- Blank cells (empty text, `Validity::Valid`): PID, Parent PID and Image name on app and unit rows; PID on pseudo rows; every column on group header rows.
- App and unit rows (PROC-008, PROC-009): Type "App" / "Unit"; User the owner name; Image path the desktop file path for apps; Memory the group's cgroup `anon` value; CPU, Disk, Network, GPU the group sums from `GroupRow`.
- Process rows: Type "App" for an app's primary process, else "Background process", "System process", "Kernel thread" by the record's group class and `KERNEL_THREAD` flag; "Pseudo" on pseudo rows (R-007).
- Image name: basename of `meta.exe`; Wine processes take the `.exe` name per PROC-007 (already in `meta.name` by E05; this cell reads `meta.exe`). A " (deleted)" suffix is kept in the text (coloured by E22-004).
- Validity: numeric fields take `record.validity.0[ProcessField::..]`; `meta.exe == None` gives `Validity::Restricted` for image_name and image_path; `meta.cmdline == None` gives Restricted for cmdline. Never write a zero for a non-valid value (ADR-003).
- Command line cell text: first 512 characters of `meta.cmdline` (R-008).
- Source fields: each column reads the `ProcessRecord`, `ProcessMeta` or `GroupRow` field with the meaning in PROC-027 to PROC-036. The fields named in ADR-003 cover: name, description, user, pid, ppid, image_name, image_path, cmdline, type, cpu (`cpu_pct`), memory (`rss_anon_bytes`), ws_total (`rss_bytes`), pss, uss, swap, disk (`io_read_bps + io_write_bps`), disk_read_rate, disk_write_rate, network (`net_rx_bps + net_tx_bps`), net_send_rate (`net_tx_bps`), net_recv_rate (`net_rx_bps`), gpu (`gpu_util_pct`), gpu_mem_dedicated (`gpu_mem_bytes`), threads, nice, state (`ProcState`: Running "Running", Sleeping "Sleeping", DiskSleep "Disk sleep", Stopped "Stopped", Zombie "Zombie", Idle "Idle", Other "Dead"). For any other column of phase 1, use the E03 field of that meaning; if E03-A1/E03-A2 has none, stop and report the column id to the leader (do not invent a source).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a record with `cpu_pct = 3.27` **When** the CPU cell is filled **Then** the text is `3.3%`.
- **Given** `cpu_pct = 0.04` and Valid **When** filled **Then** the text is `0%`.
- **Given** `rss_anon_bytes = 1_310_720_000` **When** the Memory cell is filled **Then** the text is `1.22 GiB`.
- **Given** `rss_anon_bytes = 512` **When** filled **Then** the text is `512 B`.
- **Given** `units.network = "bits"`, auto-scale off and 287_500 B/s **When** the Network cell is filled **Then** the text is `2.3 Mbps`.
- **Given** threads = 12345 **When** filled **Then** the text is `12 345` with U+2009.
- **Given** the `Memory` validity is `WarmingUp` **When** filled **Then** `out.validity` is WarmingUp and no number is written.
- **Given** an app row **When** the PID cell is filled **Then** the text is empty.
- **Given** a collapsed parent with 18 descendants **When** the PID cell is filled **Then** primary is `11528` and secondary is ` +18`; expanded, secondary is empty.
- **Given** an unchanged record and an existing cache entry **When** `fill_cell` runs **Then** `out.text` is not written (value bits and validity equal).
- **Given** `meta.exe = None` **When** the Image path cell is filled **Then** validity is Restricted.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/cells.rs`: add `CellCtx`, `RowRef`, `fill_cell`.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_process_cells.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
- `ui_process_cells::cell_formats_match_table_d`: one assertion per kind and per zero form (the criteria above).
- `ui_process_cells::validity_glyphs_never_show_zero`: every non-Valid state writes no digits.
- `ui_process_cells::pid_plus_n_only_on_collapsed_parent`.
- `ui_process_cells::app_and_unit_rows_blank_pid_and_type_text`.
- `ui_process_cells::cell_text_written_only_on_change`.
- proptest `ui_process_cells::prop_percent_one_decimal`: any finite f32 in 0..=100 gives text matching `^(0|\d+\.\d)%$`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: Valid, WarmingUp, Restricted, Unsupported, Missing, Failed, Stale are passed through to `out.validity`; glyphs are drawn by E22-004.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: no `format!`; units functions write into `out.text` (a reused `String`); no allocation when bits and validity are unchanged.
- Privacy: the command line goes only into the visible cell text, never into logs (ADR-015).

## Notes
- `CellOut`, `CellTextCache` are E18-A1 (`table/cells.rs`, `text_cache.rs`). The process-specific painters stay in this page file (00-epics.md section 2, `src/table/*` row).
- `ProcessField` index list (ADR-003): Cpu, RssAnon, Rss, Pss, Uss, Swap, IoRead, IoWrite, NetRx, NetTx, GpuUtil, GpuMem, Threads.
- The descendant count N for "PID +N" is computed by the engine projection (PROC-018). ADR-009 `TableRow` has no such field; use the E03-A2 field that carries it, or stop and report (open item 1 in docs/plan/b8-ui-tables.md).
- Build rule: run every cargo build, check, clippy or test through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_processes` (it takes the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope; the wait can be long, so run it in the background when your tool call has a timeout). On an OOM kill (exit 137) retry once, then report.
- Strings: every user-visible string in this bead is appended to `assets/locales/en-US.ftl` in this bead (R-132), key `processes-<entry>-<slug>` (for example `processes-menu-end-task`), and read through `tr(key)` / `tr_args(key, args)` from `src/i18n.rs`.
