title: Process cell painting: heat, validity glyphs, stale, selection text
description:
## Context
Paints a filled process-table cell: alignment, tabular figures, the heat tint, validity glyphs, stale dimming, selected-row text colours and the deleted-image suffix colour. Used by the process delegate for every non-Name cell. Sources: UI-PRC-004 (anatomy, heat, glyphs), UI-PRC-002 (stale at 60%, selected text), UI-PRC-008 (selected row hides heat), PROC-040, R-059, R-050, ADR-003 validity glyph table, ADR-009 heat bullet.

## Deliverable
In `pages/processes/cells.rs`:
```rust
pub struct PaintState { pub selected: bool, pub exited: bool, pub heat_on: bool, pub heat_intensity_pct: u8 }
pub fn heat_alpha(col: &ProcColumn, value: f64, ctx: &CellCtx, intensity_pct: u8) -> f32;
pub fn render_metric_cell(out: &CellOut, col: &ProcColumn, width: Pixels, st: PaintState, theme: &TlTheme, cx: &App) -> impl IntoElement;
```
- Layout: a fixed-width `div` (`w(width)`, `h(row_h)`), padding 8 left and right, `overflow_hidden`, `whitespace_nowrap`, `text_ellipsis`; text `t_base` 13 regular; numeric kinds `text_right()` and font features `tnum` (the `TNUM` constant of E15 `text/style.rs`).
- Text colour: `text_primary`; secondary parts (`" +N"`, the " (deleted)" suffix excepted) `text_secondary`; on a selected row `text_selected_primary` and `text_selected_secondary`; on an exited row every part `text_secondary` (E22-012 owns the rest of exited styling).
- " (deleted)" at the end of an Image path value draws in `status.danger` (UI-PRC-004).
- Heat (PROC-040): only for kinds Percent, MemorySize, DiskRate, NetRate and PowerClass, only when `appearance.heat_coloring` is on, `out.validity == Valid` and the value is non-zero. One quad filling the whole cell bounds (no inset, no radius) in `value_heat` with `alpha = heat_intensity_pct/100 × clamp(value / reference, 0, 1)`. References: CpuMachine `400 / ncpu` %, CpuOneCore 400 %, Memory 10 % of MemTotal, DiskIo 100 MiB/s, Network 10 MiB/s in bytes mode or 80 Mbps in bits mode, GpuPercent 100 %, Vram 25 % of total VRAM, Power 25 W. Drawn above the zebra and highlight tints and below the selection fill; selected rows draw no heat. Counts, ids, text and durations are never tinted. With `vram_total = 0` the Vram reference gives alpha 0.
- Validity glyphs replace the content with the column's alignment, through E15 `TlValidityGlyph`: WarmingUp `…` in `text_secondary`; Restricted Lucide `lock` 12 px `text_secondary` with tooltip "Needs administrator access."; Unsupported `n/a` `text_secondary` (tooltip text from the column, E22-014); Missing `-` `text_secondary`; Failed `!` in `status.warning` with the error text as tooltip; Stale: the normal text at 60 % opacity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** ncpu = 32 (reference 12.5 %), intensity 50 and CPU 25 % **When** `heat_alpha` runs **Then** it returns 0.5 (ratio clamped to 1).
- **Given** the same reference and CPU 6.25 % **When** `heat_alpha` runs **Then** it returns 0.25.
- **Given** a selected row with CPU 25 % **When** rendered **Then** no heat quad is drawn.
- **Given** `appearance.heat_coloring = false` **When** rendered **Then** no heat quad is drawn.
- **Given** a Threads cell (Count) of 500 **When** rendered **Then** no heat quad is drawn.
- **Given** validity Restricted **When** rendered **Then** the cell shows the lock glyph and no text, aligned like the column.
- **Given** validity Stale and text `3.3%` **When** rendered **Then** the text draws at opacity 0.6.
- **Given** Image path `/usr/bin/foo (deleted)` **When** rendered **Then** " (deleted)" uses `status.danger`.
- **Given** a CPU cell **When** rendered **Then** text is right-aligned with the `tnum` feature.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/cells.rs`: add painting.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_process_cells.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
- `ui_process_cells::heat_alpha_clamped_and_intensity_scaled`: the two CPU cases, a value above the reference clamps to intensity, value 0 gives 0, Vram with total 0 gives 0.
- `ui_process_cells::heat_hidden_on_selected_and_when_off` (TestAppContext render, count `value_heat` quads).
- `ui_process_cells::validity_glyph_per_state`: each state draws its glyph.
- `ui_process_cells::stale_text_dimmed_60`.
- `ui_process_cells::deleted_suffix_danger_colour`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: Failed cells carry the error text in a tooltip.
- Validity: all seven states of ADR-003 as listed.
- Accessibility: heat is additive to the number; colour is never the only signal. Glyph tooltips carry the meaning as text.
- Performance: per visible cell one `SharedString` clone, zero or one quad; no `format!`, no element id on the cell (UI-PRC-023 rule 3).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- The restricted tooltip changes to "Needs administrator access. Click the shield to grant it." in P3; that change is E29's (helper epic) concern through the same constant.
- gpui `paint_quad`: gpui-pre-0.3.7 `src/window.rs:4502`. Prefer a background `div` child over a canvas unless E18-A1 gives a canvas hook.

On an OOM kill (exit 137) retry once, then report.

title: Process Name cell: indent, chevron, icon, text, state glyphs
description:
## Context
The Name cell of the process table: indent by depth, the chevron with its reserved width, the 24 px app icon or 16 px icon, the primary text with count and qualifiers, and the state glyphs. Connector lines (E22-006), window titles (E22-033) and the window button (E22-034) build on it. Sources: UI-PRC-002 (row anatomy per kind), UI-PRC-003 (Name cell), PROC-006 (icon sizes), PROC-007 (names), PROC-008 (app Name cell), PROC-009 (unit rows), PROC-063 (pause glyph), D-011 (group header row).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/name_cell.rs` (with `pub mod name_cell;` in `pages/processes/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub struct NameCellData { pub kind: RowKind, pub depth: u8, pub expandable: Option<bool>, pub icon: NameIcon,
                          pub primary: SharedString, pub state_glyph: Option<StateGlyph>, pub exited: bool }
pub enum NameIcon { File(Arc<str>), Lucide(IconName) }
pub enum StateGlyph { Suspended, Frozen }
pub fn render_name_cell(d: &NameCellData, width: Pixels, selected: bool, node: NodeId, theme: &TlTheme, cx: &mut App) -> AnyElement;
pub fn render_group_header(label: SharedString, expanded: bool, first: bool, theme: &TlTheme) -> AnyElement;
```
Geometry (logical px × ui_scale):
- Content starts at x = 8 + depth × 18 (8 is the cell padding).
- Chevron box 16 × 16, hit area 20 × `row_h`; Lucide `chevron-right` when collapsed, `chevron-down` when expanded; colour `text_secondary`, `text_primary` while its hit area is hovered; tooltip "Expand" / "Collapse". When the row has no children (`expandable == None`) nothing is drawn but the 16 px width is still reserved.
- Icon: app rows 24 × 24, vertically centred; every other row 16 × 16. `NameIcon::File(path)` draws `img(path)`; a missing file draws Lucide `binary` in `text_secondary`. Unit rows Lucide `cog`; "Kernel threads (N)" row and kernel-thread rows Lucide `cpu`. Gap after the icon `sp3` = 6.
- Primary text: `t_base` regular `text_primary` (selected: `text_selected_primary`; exited: `text_secondary`), one line, ellipsis. The count " (N)" and qualifiers "(Flatpak)", "(Snap)", "(Wine)" are part of the same string (format `%s (%s) (%s)`), built by the delegate.
- State glyph after the primary text, gap `sp2` = 4: `Suspended` Lucide `pause` 12 px `text_secondary`, tooltip "Suspended"; `Frozen` Lucide `snowflake` 12 px `text_secondary`, tooltip "Frozen" (Frozen is P2, drawn when the delegate sets it).
- Exited rows: icon at 60 % opacity; chevron unchanged.
- Group header row (D-011): full row width band in `header` colour, height `row_h`, 1 px `divider` line at the top edge except for the first row; chevron at x 8 (16 px, `text_primary`); label at x 30, `t_md` 14 semibold 600 `text_primary`, text like "Apps (11)", "Background processes (99)", "System processes (14)". No zebra, no hover fill, no other cell.
- Element ids: the Name cell div carries `.id(("name", node))` (the only per-row id besides the row hitbox, UI-PRC-023 rule 3).
- Chevron click calls the table's toggle (E18 `ToggleExpand { id }` path) and does not change the selection.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a process row at depth 2 with a 16 px icon **When** rendered **Then** the text starts at x = 8 + 36 + 16 + 6 + 16 + 6 relative to the cell (indent, chevron box, gap, icon, gap) with `ui_scale = 1`.
- **Given** a leaf process row **When** rendered **Then** no chevron is drawn and the icon x equals that of an expandable sibling.
- **Given** an app row **When** rendered **Then** the icon is 24 px; a unit row icon is 16 px Lucide `cog`.
- **Given** a process in State T **When** the delegate sets `StateGlyph::Suspended` **Then** a 12 px `pause` glyph with tooltip "Suspended" follows the text.
- **Given** an icon path that does not exist **When** rendered **Then** the `binary` glyph is drawn.
- **Given** a group header that is not first **When** rendered **Then** a 1 px `divider` top line and the `header` band are drawn and the label is semibold 14.
- **Given** a chevron click **When** handled **Then** the row toggles and the selection set is unchanged.

- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/mod.rs`: add `pub mod name_cell;`.

title: E29-A1 Helper binary
description:
## Context
Anchor E29-A1: the finished `tl-helper` binary. It runs as root under `pkexec /usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper --session`, reads framed requests on stdin, answers on stdout, accepts only the ADR-006 allowlist with the R-004 extensions, re-verifies every process target, sets `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG = SIGKILL`, and exits after 300 s without a request or at stdin EOF (ADR-006, R-003, R-004, PROC-076, APP-003). This bead adds the session loop and the dispatch table over the operation modules written in E29-002 to E29-009 (the P4 `NetnsSockDiagDump` arm is added by E29-010). Sources: ADR-006, ADR-007 (framing), R-002 to R-004, R-098, PROC-076, APP-003.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-helper/src/main.rs`:
  1. Argument check from E29-001 (`--session` only, else exit 2).
  2. First action: `rustix::process::set_parent_process_death_signal(Some(Signal::Kill))`; then if `getppid() == 1` (parent already gone) exit 0.
  3. `umask(0o022)`. Read the boot id once from `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`.
  4. Loop: `poll` fd 0 for readability with the remaining idle time (300 s, reset after each request; test override `TL_HELPER_IDLE_MS` read once at start, used only when set). Timeout: exit 0. EOF: exit 0.
  5. Read one frame with `tl_model::wire` (max payload `MAX_HELPER_FRAME = 65_536`), receiving ancillary fds as in E29-006. Oversize length, short read or postcard error: write one line `tl-helper: protocol error` to stderr and exit 3.
  6. The first request must be `Hello { proto }` with `proto == HELPER_PROTO_VERSION`; reply `Hello { proto: HELPER_PROTO_VERSION }` with the frame's `seq`. Any other first request, or a version mismatch, replies `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "protocol version") and exits 3.
  7. Every later request goes to `dispatch::handle(frame, &mut Ctx, &mut Writer)`.
  8. Replies go out through the `tl_model::wire` multi-frame writer on fd 1 (64 KiB frames). The 4 MiB cap (4_194_304 bytes encoded) is per reply message for `ScanStrings` and `NetnsSockDiagDump` and total per request for the rest (R-157); over it the reply is replaced by `Err(TooLarge)`.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/dispatch.rs` (new; `mod dispatch;`): one `match` over `HelperRequest`, every arm explicit, no wildcard arm:
  - `Signal`, `SetNice`, `SetSched`, `SetAffinity`, `SetIoPriority` to `ops::run_process_op`;
  - `FreezeGroup`, `ThawGroup`, `KillGroup` to `ops::run_cgroup_op`;
  - `ReadProcessFiles` to `files::read_process_files`;
  - `ScanStrings` to `files::scan_strings` with the stdin cancel poll; `CancelScan` outside a scan replies `Ok`;
  - `Dump` to `ops::run_dump` with the received fd;
  - `ResolveSocketInodes` to `sockets::resolve_socket_inodes`;
  - `SockDestroy` to `sockets::sock_destroy`;
  - `WriteServiceDropIn` to `dropin::write_service_dropin`;
  - `NetnsSockDiagDump`: `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "unsupported") until the P4 bead E29-010 replaces this arm;
  - `Hello` after the first: `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "hello twice");
- Requests are handled one at a time in arrival order; the reply frames of one request are never interleaved with another's.
- The helper writes nothing else to stdout and logs nothing; tl-helper has no tracing dependency (ADR-001 row).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the built helper on a socketpair, started as the test user **When** the test sends `Hello { proto: HELPER_PROTO_VERSION }` **Then** it receives `Hello { proto: HELPER_PROTO_VERSION }` with the same `seq`.
- **Given** a fresh helper **When** the first request is `Signal{..}` **Then** it replies `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "protocol version") and exits with status 3.
- **Given** a fresh helper **When** the test writes a frame header announcing 65_537 bytes **Then** the helper exits 3 without reading the payload.
- **Given** a running session **When** the test closes its end **Then** the helper exits 0 within 100 ms.
- **Given** `TL_HELPER_IDLE_MS=200` **When** no request arrives **Then** the helper exits 0 after 200 to 400 ms.
- **Given** the helper started by an intermediate parent `/bin/sh -c '<helper> --session & echo $! >&2; sleep 30'` (stdin and stdout on the socketpair) **When** the test SIGKILLs that `sh` **Then** the helper pid it printed on stderr is gone within 1 s (`PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`).
- **Given** a running session **When** `ReadProcessFiles` for a child of the test is sent **Then** the reply arrives in one or more frames, each payload at most 65_536 bytes, and decodes to `File { .. }` bodies, the last with `last: true`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-helper/src/main.rs`: session loop.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/dispatch.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-helper/tests/helper_proto.rs`: create (spawns `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_tl-helper")` with both stdin and stdout set to one end of a `socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM | SOCK_CLOEXEC)`).

## Tests
- `tests/helper_proto.rs::hello_handshake`
- `tests/helper_proto.rs::first_request_must_be_hello` (security regression)
- `tests/helper_proto.rs::oversize_frame_exits` (security regression)
- `tests/helper_proto.rs::eof_exits`
- `tests/helper_proto.rs::idle_exit`
- `tests/helper_proto.rs::parent_death_kills_helper`
- `tests/helper_proto.rs::multi_frame_reply`
- `tests/helper_proto.rs::every_request_variant_has_an_arm`: sends one well-formed request of each of the 17 variants (R-157; `ReadProcessDetail` is dropped) (targets the test's own child, a temp fd for `Dump`, a `user.slice` path that fails validation for the cgroup kinds) and checks that every reply decodes; none is a protocol error.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: protocol failure exits 3; operation errors are replies.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: idle helper uses no CPU (blocking poll).
- Privacy: no logging; stderr only for the one protocol error line.
- Security: this is the root boundary. No path, command or free-form file argument reaches any handler (R-004). Every process target is re-verified inside the handler (ADR-006).

## Notes
- Protocol names are those of `tl-model/src/helper_proto.rs` (E03-070, as2.36, the type owner; R-157). Requests travel as `HelperFrame { seq: u32, request: HelperRequest }` (the engine picks `seq`) and replies as `HelperReply { seq: u32, last: bool, body: HelperReplyBody }` (the helper echoes `seq`; `last: true` marks the final reply of a request). `HelperRequest` has 17 variants: `Hello { proto }`, `Signal { target, signal }`, `SetNice { target, nice }`, `SetSched { target, policy, rt_prio }`, `SetAffinity { target, set }`, `SetIoPriority { key, prio }`, `FreezeGroup(HelperCgroup)`, `ThawGroup(HelperCgroup)`, `KillGroup(HelperCgroup)`, `ReadProcessFiles { key, files: ProcFiles }`, `ScanStrings { key, opts }`, `Dump { key, mode }` (the output fd travels as `SCM_RIGHTS` ancillary data with this frame, R-145 item 3), `ResolveSocketInodes { inodes }`, `SockDestroy { family, proto, four_tuple, cookie }`, `WriteServiceDropIn { unit, keys: Vec<(DropInKey, String)> }`, `NetnsSockDiagDump { netns_ino }`, `CancelScan { seq: u32 }`; `target` is `HelperTarget::{Process(ProcessKey), Thread { process: ProcessKey, tid: u32 }}`. `HelperReplyBody`: `Hello { proto }`, `Ok`, `Err(HelperError)`, `File { file: ProcFiles, data: Vec<u8> }` (one bit per reply, chunked), `Strings(Vec<(u64, StringEncoding, String)>)`, `SocketOwners(Vec<(u64, ProcessKey)>)`, `NetlinkDump(Vec<u8>)`. `HelperError::{IdentityChanged, PermissionDenied, NoSuchProcess, NotAllowed, Partial { done, total }, Os(i32), TooLarge}`. `NotAllowed` carries no text: a quoted rule after `Err(NotAllowed)` in this bead names the check for code comments and test names and is never sent. `HELPER_PROTO_VERSION = 1`; frames are at most 64 KiB; the 4 MiB cap is per reply message for the streamed requests (`ScanStrings`, `NetnsSockDiagDump`) and total for the rest (R-157). Handlers return a `HelperReplyBody`; `dispatch` (E29-A1) wraps each one in a `HelperReply` with the frame's `seq` and the `last` flag.
- Commit `dispatch.rs` before building (it is the largest new file of the crate), then build and test.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-helper`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec (`git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`), one commit for this bead.

title: E29-007 Helper ResolveSocketInodes
description:
## Context
`ResolveSocketInodes { inodes }` maps socket inodes to the processes that hold them, for sockets of other users whose `/proc/<pid>/fd` the engine cannot read (SYS-030, PROC-032, R-004). The engine sends the inodes it could not attribute; the helper walks `/proc/*/fd` as root. Sources: SYS-030, ADR-016 (socket to pid map), R-004.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-helper/src/sockets.rs` (new; add `mod sockets;` to `main.rs`):
- `pub fn resolve_socket_inodes(inodes: &[u64], boot: BootId) -> HelperReplyBody`.
- Build a `FxHashSet`-free sorted `Vec<u64>` of the requested inodes (tl-helper has no rustc-hash; use `sort_unstable` plus `binary_search`).
- Walk `/proc` numeric entries; for each pid open `/proc/<pid>` as a dirfd, read `stat` field 22 (`start_ticks`, parsed after the last `)`), `readdir` its `fd/`, `readlinkat` each entry; a target of the form `socket:[<n>]` with `n` in the set adds `(n, ProcessKey { pid, start_ticks, boot_id: boot })`.
- Pids that vanish mid-walk are skipped. Kernel threads have no fds and cost one readdir.
- Reply `SocketOwners(Vec<(u64, ProcessKey)>)` (as2.36 name, R-157) sorted by inode then pid; an inode held by several processes appears once per process (shared sockets after fork, SYS-030 "pid +N"). Inodes with no holder are absent.
- An empty request replies `SocketOwners([])` without walking.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the test opens a TCP listener and a UDP socket **When** their inodes (from `fstat`) are resolved **Then** both map to the test's own pid and `start_ticks`.
- **Given** a socket shared by the test and a forked child **When** resolved **Then** two entries with the same inode appear, one per pid.
- **Given** an inode no process holds (for example 1) **When** resolved **Then** the reply has no entry for it.
- **Given** an empty list **When** resolved **Then** the reply is `SocketOwners([])`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-helper/src/sockets.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/main.rs`: add `mod sockets;`.

## Tests
- `sockets.rs::tests::resolves_own_sockets`
- `sockets.rs::tests::shared_socket_lists_both_pids`
- `sockets.rs::tests::unknown_inode_absent`
- `sockets.rs::tests::empty_request_no_walk`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: none beyond skipped pids; the walk never fails as a whole except on `/proc` open failure (`Err(Os(errno))`).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one walk per request; the engine sends at most one request per 2 s rebuild (SYS-030 cadence) and only while connections are demanded.
- Privacy: fd targets other than `socket:[n]` are discarded immediately and never logged or returned.
- Security: no path argument; only `socket:[n]` matches leave the helper.

## Notes
- Protocol names are those of `tl-model/src/helper_proto.rs` (E03-070, as2.36, the type owner; R-157). title: E29-008 Helper SockDestroy over raw netlink
description:
## Context
`SockDestroy { family, proto, four_tuple, cookie }` closes one TCP connection as root by sending a netlink `SOCK_DESTROY` message (SYS-031, R-004). The kernel matches the socket cookie, so a reused 4-tuple cannot be hit. tl-helper's dependency row has no netlink crates (ADR-001: tl-model, tl-ops, tl-collect | rustix, postcard, serde; R-142 item 14), so the message is built by hand on a rustix netlink socket. Sources: SYS-031, ADR-006, R-004.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-helper/src/sockets.rs`: `pub fn sock_destroy(family: Family, proto: Proto, t: &FourTuple, cookie: u64) -> HelperReplyBody`:
- Only `Proto::Tcp` is allowed (`Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "only tcp") otherwise); `family` is `Family::V4` or `Family::V6`.
- Socket: `rustix::net::socket(AddressFamily::NETLINK, SocketType::RAW, Some(Protocol::from_raw(NETLINK_SOCK_DIAG = 4)))` with `SOCK_CLOEXEC`.
- Message (all little-endian host order except ports and addresses, which are network order), 88 bytes:
  - `nlmsghdr` (16 bytes): `nlmsg_len = 88`, `nlmsg_type = SOCK_DESTROY = 21`, `nlmsg_flags = NLM_F_REQUEST | NLM_F_ACK = 0x0001 | 0x0004`, `nlmsg_seq = 1`, `nlmsg_pid = 0`.
  - `inet_diag_req_v2` (56 bytes): `sdiag_family` = `AF_INET` 2 or `AF_INET6` 10; `sdiag_protocol = IPPROTO_TCP = 6`; `idiag_ext = 0`; `pad = 0`; `idiag_states = 0xFFFF_FFFF`; `inet_diag_sockid`: `idiag_sport` (be16), `idiag_dport` (be16), `idiag_src` `[be32; 4]` (IPv4 uses the first word, rest 0), `idiag_dst` `[be32; 4]`, `idiag_if = 0`, `idiag_cookie = [cookie as u32, (cookie >> 32) as u32]`.
- Send to the kernel (`SocketAddrNetlink::new(0, 0)`), then receive the `NLMSG_ERROR` ack: `error == 0` replies `Ok`; `-EOPNOTSUPP (95)` replies `Err(Os(95))` (UI: "Kernel lacks CONFIG_INET_DIAG_DESTROY"); `-ENOENT (2)` replies `Err(NoSuchProcess)` (connection already gone); any other negative errno `Err(Os(errno))`. A receive timeout of 2 s (`SO_RCVTIMEO`) gives `Err(Os(ETIMEDOUT = 110))`.
- A pure builder `fn build_destroy_msg(family, t, cookie) -> [u8; 88]` is separate so it can be tested byte for byte.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** family V4, sport 40000, dport 443, src 192.168.1.5, dst 1.2.3.4, cookie `0x0000_0001_0000_00AB` **When** `build_destroy_msg` runs **Then** the bytes equal the committed expected array in the test (length 88, type 21, flags 5, family 2, protocol 6, ports `0x9C40` and `0x01BB` big-endian, cookie words `0xAB` and `1`).
- **Given** family V6 with `::1` addresses **When** built **Then** family is 10 and all four address words are filled.
- **Given** `Proto::Udp` **When** `sock_destroy` runs **Then** `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "only tcp") and no socket is opened.
- **Given** the test as an ordinary user and a real loopback TCP connection it owns **When** `sock_destroy` runs **Then** the reply is `Err(PermissionDenied)` or `Err(Os(1))` (CAP_NET_ADMIN missing), never `Ok`; the root case is in `real_helper_root.rs` (E29-012).

## Files
- `crates/tl-helper/src/sockets.rs`: add `sock_destroy` and `build_destroy_msg`.

## Tests
- `sockets.rs::tests::destroy_msg_v4_bytes`
- `sockets.rs::tests::destroy_msg_v6_bytes`
- `sockets.rs::tests::destroy_udp_refused` (security regression: only TCP)
- `sockets.rs::tests::destroy_without_cap_fails`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: as listed.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one socket per call, closed on return.
- Privacy: addresses are not logged above `debug`; never log the cookie.
- Security: the cookie is always set, so the kernel refuses a socket that only matches the 4-tuple.

title: E29-009 Helper WriteServiceDropIn
description:
## Context
`WriteServiceDropIn { unit, keys: Vec<(DropInKey, String)> }` (the manager is always System, as2.36) lets the Recovery tab editor change `Restart*`, `StartLimit*`, `FailureAction` and `OnFailure` of a system service by writing the fixed file `/etc/systemd/system/<unit>.d/50-tasklens-recovery.conf` as root; an empty key set deletes that file (`UnitRemoveRecovery`) (SYS-013, R-004, R-119, table (c)). The engine then calls `Manager.Reload()` (E11). The helper builds the file text itself from typed keys; it never accepts file text. The text comes from one renderer shared with the user-unit path of E11-020 (R-168 E29-OI-10). Sources: SYS-013, UI-SYS-034 (ranges and the unit-name pattern), R-004, R-119, R-168, ADR-011 (atomic write).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ops/src/dropin.rs` (new; an E29-owned file inside tl-ops, R-168 E29-OI-10; add `pub mod dropin;` to `crates/tl-ops/src/lib.rs`, the only change there): `pub const HEADER: &str = "# Written by tasklens. Edit it in the Service Properties Recovery tab or delete this file.\n";` and `pub fn render(keys: &[(DropInKey, String)]) -> String` (R-248), the file text below. E11-020 (i3o.22) re-exports both and calls `render` for the user-unit drop-in, so both paths write the same text.

`crates/tl-helper/src/dropin.rs` (new; add `mod dropin;` to `main.rs`):
- `pub fn write_service_dropin(unit: &str, keys: &[(DropInKey, String)]) -> HelperReplyBody`:
  - First `tl_model::helper_proto::validate_drop_in(unit, keys)` (as2.36, shared with the engine; the helper never trusts the engine's check). Failure: `Err(NotAllowed)`.

A key given twice, or a value that does not parse, is `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "bad key value"). Values are in the form E11-020's `keys_of` writes them: words, decimal integers, `<n>us` for the time keys, unit names joined by one space for `OnFailure`.

  - `unit` matches `^[A-Za-z0-9:_.\\@-]{1,255}\.service$`, does not start with `.`, and contains no `/` ("bad unit name").
  - `restart` is one of `no`, `on-success`, `on-failure`, `on-abnormal`, `on-watchdog`, `on-abort`, `always` ("bad Restart value").
  - `restart_usec` and `restart_max_delay_usec` in `0..=3_600_000_000` us, `restart_steps` in `0..=1000` ("Restart* out of range"; the value text is `<n>us`, R-248).
  - `start_limit_burst` in `0..=1000`; `start_limit_interval_usec` in `0..=86_400_000_000` us ("StartLimit out of range").
  - `start_limit_action` and `failure_action` each one of `none`, `reboot`, `reboot-force`, `reboot-immediate`, `poweroff`, `poweroff-force`, `poweroff-immediate`, `exit`, `exit-force` ("bad action value").
  - every `on_failure` token matches `^[A-Za-z0-9:_.\\@%-]{1,255}\.(service|socket|target|timer|mount|path|slice|scope)$`; at most 32 tokens ("bad OnFailure unit").
- File text (`tl_ops::dropin::render(keys: &[(DropInKey, String)]) -> String`, R-248): `HEADER` first, then only the keys present, values written verbatim (the engine's `keys_of` gives `<n>us` for the time keys), sections omitted when empty, no blank lines, LF line ends, no trailing spaces, every line `Key=value\n`:
  ```
  # Written by tasklens. Edit it in the Service Properties Recovery tab or delete this file.
  [Unit]
  StartLimitIntervalSec=<n>us
  StartLimitBurst=<n>
  StartLimitAction=<word>
  FailureAction=<word>
  OnFailure=<unit> <unit>
  [Service]
  Restart=<word>
  RestartSec=<n>us
  RestartSteps=<n>
  RestartMaxDelaySec=<n>us
  ```
  The helper renders from the validated key list (`render(keys)`), never from free text.
- Write: open `/etc/systemd/system` as a dirfd; `mkdirat(<unit>.d, 0o755)` if missing (an existing non-directory or symlink at that name gives `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "drop-in directory is not a directory"), checked with `fstatat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)`); write `50-tasklens-recovery.conf` with mode 0644 through `tl_ops::fs::write_atomic` (E07-A3) relative to that directory.
- Empty `keys`: `unlinkat` the file (absent is fine), then `unlinkat(<unit>.d, AT_REMOVEDIR)` only if the directory is now empty. Reply `Ok`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** keys `[(Restart, "on-failure"), (RestartSec, "100000us")]` **When** `render` runs **Then** the text is exactly `HEADER + "[Service]\nRestart=on-failure\nRestartSec=100000us\n"`.
- **Given** keys `[(StartLimitBurst, "5"), (StartLimitIntervalSec, "10000000us"), (OnFailure, "failure-notify@%n.service")]` **When** rendered **Then** the text is `HEADER + "[Unit]\nStartLimitIntervalSec=10000000us\nStartLimitBurst=5\nOnFailure=failure-notify@%n.service\n"` (key order fixed, no `[Service]` section).
- **Given** unit `../../etc/passwd` or `sshd.service/x` or `.hidden.service` **When** written **Then** `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "bad unit name").
- **Given** a value containing a newline (`restart = "always\nExecStart=/bin/sh"`) **When** written **Then** `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "bad Restart value") (security regression: no key injection).
- **Given** an `on_failure` token `a.service\n[Service]` **When** written **Then** `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "bad OnFailure unit").
- **Given** `keys` with `Restart` twice **When** written **Then** `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "bad key value") and no file is touched.
- **Given** a temp root (test-only constructor `write_service_dropin_in(dir_fd, ..)`) **When** a write and then an empty-keys call run **Then** the file exists with mode 0644 after the first and the file and the then-empty directory are gone after the second.
- **Given** `<unit>.d` is a symlink in the temp root **When** written **Then** `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "drop-in directory is not a directory") and nothing is written through the link.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ops/src/dropin.rs`: create (`render` and its tests; R-168 E29-OI-10).
- `crates/tl-ops/src/lib.rs`: add `pub mod dropin;`.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/dropin.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/main.rs`: add `mod dropin;`.

## Tests
- `crates/tl-ops/src/dropin.rs::tests::render_service_only`
- `crates/tl-ops/src/dropin.rs::tests::render_unit_only`
- `dropin.rs::tests::unit_name_rules` (security regression)

- `dropin.rs::tests::symlinked_dropin_dir_refused` (security regression)

- Security: root write to `/etc`; fixed directory and file name, typed and range-checked values only.

description:
## Context
End-to-end check of the real helper path on the owner machine: tasklens's engine starts `pkexec /usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper --session`, the owner answers the polkit prompt, and privileged requests work; a dismissed prompt and the 300 s idle exit behave as APP-003 and R-117 say (ADR-013 real-system layer, `#[ignore]`). Sources: ADR-006, ADR-013, R-003, R-117, APP-003, PROC-076.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/tests/real_helper.rs`, every test `#[ignore]`, each skipping with a printed reason unless `/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper`, `/usr/bin/pkexec` and the installed policy `/usr/share/polkit-1/actions/io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.policy` exist. They run a real `Engine::start` (public API) and drive it through `EngineClient`:
- `unlock_and_signal_other_user`: before the test the owner runs `sudo systemd-run --uid=nobody --unit=tasklens-test-nobody sleep 300` (the test prints this instruction and waits up to 60 s for the unit's pid to appear in the snapshot). The test sends `Command::StartHelperSession` (the owner authenticates), waits up to 120 s for `health.helper == Unlocked`, sends a privileged `Signal(Term)` action for that pid, and expects `Succeeded`.
- `dismissed_prompt_locks_again`: the owner presses Cancel on the prompt; `health.helper` goes `Starting` then `Locked`, and `helper_start` carries `Cancelled`.
- `idle_exit_relocks`: after unlocking, no requests for 305 s; `health.helper` becomes `Locked`.
- `end_session_locks`: `Command::EndHelperSession` gives `Locked` within 1 s and the helper pid is gone.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the owner machine with the package installed **When** the four tests run with `-- --ignored --test-threads=1` and the owner answers prompts as each test prints **Then** all pass and nothing is left running (a cleanup guard runs `systemctl stop tasklens-test-nobody` through the helper's own `Signal`, or prints the command for the owner).
- **Given** a machine without the installed helper **When** run **Then** each test prints "skipped: helper not installed" and passes.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/real_helper.rs`: create.

- The four tests above.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: N/A
- Security: exercises the real polkit path; no password is ever stored or scripted.

title: E29-012 Helper real-system tests as root
description:
## Context
Real-system tests of the helper binary as root on the owner machine (ADR-013 real-system layer, `#[ignore]`). They prove the root paths that the unprivileged unit tests cannot: another user's process, another user's cgroup, `SOCK_DESTROY`, and the system drop-in write. Sources: ADR-013, ADR-006 verification, R-004, SYS-031, SYS-013.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-helper/tests/real_helper_root.rs`, every test `#[ignore]` and skipped with a printed reason unless `rustix::process::geteuid().is_root()`. Run on the owner machine with `sudo -E cargo test -p tl-helper --test real_helper_root -- --ignored` (through the build rule; `sudo` is the owner's step, never an agent's). Each test spawns the built helper (`env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_tl-helper")`) directly as root on a socketpair (no pkexec) and sends real frames:
- `signal_other_users_process`: `runuser -u nobody -- sleep 60` child; capture its key; `Signal(Term)` gives `Done`; the child is gone.
- `stale_key_other_user_rejected`: same child, `start_ticks + 1`: `Error(IdentityChanged)`; child alive.
- `read_files_other_user`: `ReadProcessFiles { ENVIRON | IO | EXE }` of the nobody child gives `Ok` for all three.
- `freeze_other_users_scope`: `runuser -u nobody -- systemd-run --user --scope` is not available for nobody, so use `systemd-run --scope --unit=tasklens-test-freeze sleep 60` (a system scope under `system.slice`): `FreezeGroup` gives `Done` and `frozen 1`; `ThawGroup`; `KillGroup` ends it.
- `sock_destroy_loopback`: the test opens a loopback TCP connection, gets its cookie from a `sock_diag` dump, `SockDestroy` gives `Done`, and a read on the client side returns an error (ECONNABORTED or ECONNRESET).
- `dropin_write_and_remove`: on the test unit `tasklens-test.service` (table (c); the test installs `/etc/systemd/system/tasklens-test.service` with `ExecStart=/usr/bin/sleep 600` first and removes it at the end), `WriteServiceDropIn { restart: on-failure }` creates `/etc/systemd/system/tasklens-test.service.d/50-tasklens-recovery.conf` with mode 0644 and the exact text; the empty set removes the file and the directory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** root on the owner machine **When** the six tests run **Then** all pass and no test unit, scope, drop-in or child is left behind (each test cleans up in a guard's `Drop`).
- **Given** a non-root run **When** the tests run with `--ignored` **Then** each prints "skipped: needs root" and passes.

## Files
- `crates/tl-helper/tests/real_helper_root.rs`: create.

## Tests
- The six tests above.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: N/A
- Security: the tests touch `/etc/systemd/system` only for `tasklens-test.service`.

## Notes

It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E29-013 Engine helper link: pkexec spawn, handshake, calls
description:
## Context
The engine's synchronous link to one running helper process: spawning `pkexec /usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper --session`, the `Hello` handshake that also tells a dismissed polkit prompt from a denial, and one request at a time with deadlines (ADR-006, R-003, R-117, APP-003). The async session task that owns it is E29-A2. Sources: ADR-006 (helper boundary), ADR-007 (framing, one outstanding request, kill and reap), R-003, R-117 (pkexec exit 126 dismissed, 127 not authorized), R-145 item 3 (socketpair transport), R-148 (start outcomes), R-157 (frame and reply shapes).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/helper/session.rs` and a module stub `crates/tl-engine/src/helper/mod.rs` containing `mod session;` (E29-A2 fills `mod.rs`); `crates/tl-engine/src/lib.rs` gets `mod helper;` (chain edit to an E08 file, the only change to it in this bead; depends on E08-A1).

```rust
pub(crate) const HELPER_PATH: &str = "/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper";
pub(crate) const PKEXEC_PATH: &str = "/usr/bin/pkexec";
pub(crate) const START_DEADLINE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(120); // any call that may show a polkit prompt (ADR-006)

pub(crate) trait HelperLink: Send {               // real process or the test fake
    fn send(&mut self, frame: &HelperFrame, fd: Option<BorrowedFd<'_>>) -> io::Result<()>;
    fn recv(&mut self, timeout: Duration) -> Result<HelperReply, LinkError>;
    fn exit_status(&mut self, wait: Duration) -> Option<i32>; // reaps; None if still running after `wait`
    fn kill(&mut self);                                       // SIGKILL then wait()
    fn close(&mut self);                                      // shut down the write half (helper sees EOF)
}
pub(crate) enum LinkError { Timeout, Eof, Protocol }
pub(crate) enum StartError { Cancelled, NotAuthorized, Missing, Failed(Arc<str>) } // Cancelled, NotAuthorized, Failed map one to one to HelperStartOutcome (R-148 item 2)
pub(crate) enum CallError { Timeout, Exited, Protocol }

pub(crate) struct ProcLink { child: std::process::Child, sock: OwnedFd }
impl ProcLink { pub(crate) fn spawn() -> Result<ProcLink, StartError>; }

pub(crate) struct HelperSession<L: HelperLink> { link: L, next_seq: u32 }
impl<L: HelperLink> HelperSession<L> {
    pub(crate) fn start(link: L) -> Result<Self, StartError>;   // Hello with START_DEADLINE
    pub(crate) fn call(&mut self, req: HelperRequest, fd: Option<BorrowedFd<'_>>, deadline: Duration,
                       on_reply: &mut dyn FnMut(HelperReply) -> ControlFlow<()>) -> Result<(), CallError>;
    pub(crate) fn end(self);                                     // close, wait 500 ms, then kill
    pub(crate) fn is_alive(&mut self) -> bool;                   // exit_status(Duration::ZERO).is_none()
}
```
- `ProcLink::spawn`: `HELPER_PATH` or `PKEXEC_PATH` not a regular file gives `StartError::Missing`. `rustix::net::socketpair(UNIX, STREAM, CLOEXEC)`; `std::process::Command::new(PKEXEC_PATH).arg(HELPER_PATH).arg("--session")`, `env_clear()`, `stdin` and `stdout` both from the child end (`Stdio::from(OwnedFd)`, one `try_clone`), `stderr` inherited. No `pre_exec`, no `unsafe` (the helper sets its own death signal). Never `asupersync::process` (zombie bug `bi2462.114`).
- `send` writes with `tl_model::wire` framing; with an fd it uses `rustix::net::sendmsg` with one `SCM_RIGHTS` fd on the frame's first byte (only the `Dump` frame carries an fd, R-145 item 3).
- `recv` polls the socket (`rustix::event::poll`) up to `timeout`, then reads one `HelperReply` with the `tl_model::wire` multi-frame reader (frames of at most 65_536 bytes, one reply message at most 4 MiB, R-157).
- `start`: sends `Hello { proto: HELPER_PROTO_VERSION }` with `seq = 0`, waits up to `START_DEADLINE`. `Eof` before the reply: reap and map the exit status: 126 (prompt dismissed) gives `Cancelled`, 127 (not authorized) gives `NotAuthorized` (R-148 item 3), anything else `Failed("helper exited with status <n>")`. Timeout: `kill()` and `Failed("no answer from the helper")`. A `Hello` with another `proto`: `end()` and `Failed("helper version mismatch")`.
- `call`: `seq` values count up from 1 and wrap, skipping 0 (only the `Hello` uses 0); a reply whose `seq` differs from the current request's `seq` is a `Protocol` error. Calls `on_reply` for each reply; a reply with `last: false` keeps reading, `last: true` ends the call. `on_reply` returning `Break` during a `ScanStrings` call sends a new frame `CancelScan { seq: <the scan's seq> }` under the next `seq` and keeps reading: first the scan's replies up to its `last: true`, then exactly one `Ok` reply carrying the cancel frame's `seq` (the helper rule in E29-005, R-157). The deadline covers the whole call; on `Timeout` the link is killed and reaped and the session is unusable (`CallError::Timeout`); `Eof` gives `CallError::Exited`.
- `end`: `close()`, `exit_status(500 ms)`, else `kill()`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a `FakeLink` that answers `Hello` correctly **When** `start` runs **Then** it returns a session and the fake saw one `Hello` frame with `seq = 0`.
- **Given** a `FakeLink` that reports EOF and exit status 126 **When** `start` runs **Then** `StartError::Cancelled`; status 127 gives `NotAuthorized`; status 1 gives `Failed("helper exited with status 1")`.
- **Given** a `FakeLink` answering `Hello { proto: 99 }` **When** `start` runs **Then** `Failed("helper version mismatch")` and `close` was called.
- **Given** a session **When** `call(Signal ..)` gets `Ok` **Then** `on_reply` saw exactly one reply and the call returned `Ok`.
- **Given** a session **When** a `ScanStrings` call gets three `Strings` replies with `last: false` then one with `last: true` **Then** `on_reply` ran four times.
- **Given** `on_reply` returns `Break` on the first batch **When** the call continues **Then** the fake received a frame `CancelScan { seq: <scan seq> }` under the next `seq`, and the call returns `Ok` after the scan's `last: true` reply and the cancel frame's `Ok` reply (R-157).
- **Given** a fake that never answers **When** `call` with deadline 2 s runs **Then** `CallError::Timeout` and `kill` was called.
- **Given** a reply with a wrong `seq` **When** read **Then** `CallError::Protocol`.
- **Given** a socketpair and a `Dump` frame sent with an fd **When** the other end reads with `recvmsg` **Then** it gets the frame bytes and exactly one fd (R-145 item 3).
- **Given** `HELPER_PATH` absent (test override of the two path constants through a `#[cfg(test)]` constructor `ProcLink::spawn_at(pkexec, helper)`) **When** spawned **Then** `StartError::Missing`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/helper/session.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/helper/mod.rs`: create with `mod session;` only.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/lib.rs`: add `mod helper;` (chain edit).

## Tests
- `helper/session.rs::tests::start_ok`
- `helper/session.rs::tests::start_exit_codes_map` (126, 127, 1)
- `helper/session.rs::tests::start_version_mismatch`
- `helper/session.rs::tests::call_single_reply`
- `helper/session.rs::tests::call_streams_until_last`
- `helper/session.rs::tests::break_sends_cancel`
- `helper/session.rs::tests::call_timeout_kills`
- `helper/session.rs::tests::wrong_seq_is_protocol_error` (security regression)
- `helper/session.rs::tests::dump_fd_travels_as_scm_rights` (R-145 item 3)
- `helper/session.rs::tests::missing_paths`
- `helper/session.rs::tests::proc_link_socketpair_roundtrip`: a `#[cfg(test)]` constructor `ProcLink::spawn_program("/bin/cat", &[])` runs `cat` with stdin and stdout on the socketpair; a frame sent with `send` comes back byte-identical through the raw socket (proves both fds are wired to one socket).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `StartError` and `CallError` as listed; E29-A2 turns them into health state and action results.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: all functions block; callers run them inside `cx.spawn_blocking` (ASX section 4).
- Privacy: requests and replies are never logged; log only the request kind, `seq` and result at `debug` on target `tasklens::action`.
- Security: the helper path and pkexec path are fixed constants; no environment is passed.

## Notes
- Settled: the helper's fds 0 and 1 are one socketpair so the `Dump` fd can travel as `SCM_RIGHTS` (R-145 item 3). Frame and reply shapes are as2.36's (R-157): `HelperFrame { seq: u32, request }`, `HelperReply { seq: u32, last: bool, body: HelperReplyBody }`, bodies `Hello { proto }`, `Ok`, `Err(HelperError)`, `File`, `Strings`, `SocketOwners`, `NetlinkDump`.
- `StartError::{Cancelled, NotAuthorized, Failed}` become `HelperStartOutcome { Cancelled, NotAuthorized, Failed(Arc<str>) }` (as2.13); E29-A2 publishes it with a `seq` in `HealthSnapshot.helper_start` (R-148 item 2). For an action, pkexec 126 is `ActionError::AuthCancelled` and 127 is `ActionError::NotAuthorized` (R-148 item 3, E29-014).
- tl-engine may use rustix (ADR-001 row). No new dependency.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec (`git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`), one commit for this bead.
close_reason: helper/session.rs: ProcLink (pkexec spawn on one socketpair, SCM_RIGHTS send, deadline recv), HelperSession start/call/end with seq checks and CancelScan; mod helper in lib.rs. Commits 980eb2e, 43bcbd3

title: E29-014 E29: add privileged routing arm and actions/helper.rs to actions/mod.rs
description:
## Context
Routes actions the user asked to run as administrator (`ActionRequest.privileged == true`, sent by "Retry as administrator" and by privileged menu items) to the helper instead of the unprivileged `tl-ops` calls, with the same per-target events, summary and deadlines as E11's pipeline (PROC-058, PROC-076, ADR-005, ADR-006). There is no automatic retry and no automatic escalation. It also provides the helper hook that E11's `actions/{socket,recovery,dump}.rs` call for `SockDestroy`, `UnitWriteRecovery`/`UnitRemoveRecovery` on system units and privileged `Dump`. Sources: ADR-005 (event order, summary rule), ADR-006 (deadlines, helper allowlist, protected rules), R-004, R-117, PROC-058, PROC-060 to PROC-068, PROC-075, SYS-013, SYS-031.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/helper.rs` (new):
  - `pub(crate) async fn run_privileged(cx: &Cx, req: &ActionRequest, helper: &dyn PrivilegedOps, ev: &EventSink)`: called after admission (E11 admission still applies: 16 in flight, 256 targets, identity, kernel thread; protected targets still need the UI confirmation, which happened before the request was sent).
  - Kind mapping per target: `Signal(s)` to `Signal { target, signal: s }`; `Suspend` to `Signal(Stop)`; `Resume` to `Signal(Cont)`; `SetNice`, `SetSched`, `SetAffinity`, `SetIoPriority` to the same-named requests; `ActionTarget::Thread` maps to `HelperTarget::Thread` (allowed for `Signal`, `SetNice`, `SetSched`, `SetAffinity`); `FreezeGroup`, `ThawGroup`, `KillGroup` on `ActionTarget::Cgroup` to the cgroup requests. `KillTree`: first a `Signal(Stop)` to every target, then `Signal(Kill)` to every target, in two passes, like E11's unprivileged tree (ADR-006). Any other kind or target type with `privileged = true` gives `Rejected(Unsupported)` for the request.
  - Deadlines: 2 s per target (ADR-006); when the session is `Locked` when the action starts, the first target also gets `START_DEADLINE` (120 s) for the polkit prompt.
  - Result mapping: `Ok` to `Succeeded`; `Err(IdentityChanged)` to `Rejected(IdentityChanged)`; `NoSuchProcess` to `Failed(NoSuchProcess)`; `PermissionDenied` to `Failed(PermissionDenied)`; `Partial { done, total }` to `Failed(Partial { done, total })`; `Os(3)` (ESRCH after the call) to `OutcomeUnknown("process exited during the change")`; `Os(115)` to `OutcomeUnknown("freeze still in progress")`; other `Os(n)` to `Failed(Os(n))`; `NotAllowed` (no text, as2.36) to `Failed(Internal("refused by the administrator helper"))`; call `Timeout` to `OutcomeUnknown("no answer from the administrator helper")`; `Exited` or `Protocol(_)` to `Failed(Internal("administrator helper stopped"))`; `HelperCallError::Cancelled` (pkexec 126, prompt dismissed) to `Failed(ActionError::AuthCancelled)` and `HelperCallError::NotAuthorized` (pkexec 127) to `Failed(ActionError::NotAuthorized)` (R-148 item 3; UI texts "Authentication cancelled" and "<failure text>: not authorized", R-117), applied to every remaining target; `Missing` to `Rejected(Unsupported)`; `StartFailed(reason)` (an implicit session start that failed, R-246) to `Failed(ActionError::Internal(reason))`.
  - Events in ADR-005 order: `Started`, one final state per target, then the summary with `target: None` (Succeeded only if every target succeeded; otherwise the worst in the order Failed, OutcomeUnknown, Rejected).
  - Hook for E11's P3 files (R-147): implement E11-002's (i3o.4) `trait PrivilegedOps: Send + Sync + 'static { fn call(&self, cx: &Cx, req: HelperRequest, fd: Option<OwnedFd>, deadline: Duration) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Vec<HelperReply>, HelperCallError>> + Send + '_>>; fn state(&self) -> HelperState; }` for `HelperHandle`, with `HelperCallError { Missing, Cancelled, NotAuthorized, StartFailed(Arc<str>), Timeout, Exited, Protocol(Arc<str>) }` from `actions/mod.rs` (R-246). The `fd` argument carries the `Dump` fd (R-145 item 3). E11's `actions/{socket,recovery,dump}.rs` call it through `ActionCtx.helper`.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/mod.rs` (E11 file, chain edit; the only change in it): `mod helper;`; in `run_action` the `if req.privileged { .. }` body that E11-002 wrote (`Rejected(Unsupported)` while no helper exists) becomes: `actx.helper` is `Some(h)` → `helper::run_privileged(&cx, &req, h.as_ref(), &events).await; return;`, `None` → the E11-002 `Rejected(Unsupported)` path unchanged (R-147). Plus the installation of the `HelperHandle` as `ActionCtx.helper: Option<Arc<dyn PrivilegedOps>>` (R-147).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a LabRuntime engine with the fake helper and a privileged `Signal(Term)` on two targets **When** run **Then** the fake receives two `Signal` requests and the UI receives `Started`, two `Succeeded` and a summary `Succeeded`.
- **Given** the fake answers `Err(PermissionDenied)` for target 2 **When** run **Then** target 2 is `Failed(PermissionDenied)` and the summary is `Failed(PermissionDenied)`.
- **Given** a privileged `KillTree` on three targets **When** run **Then** the fake sees three `Signal(Stop)` requests before any `Signal(Kill)`.
- **Given** the session is `Locked` and the fake start returns 126 **When** a privileged `SetNice` runs **Then** every target ends `Failed(AuthCancelled)` and no `SetNice` frame is sent (R-148 item 3).
- **Given** the session is `Locked` and the fake start returns 127 **When** a privileged `SetNice` runs **Then** every target ends `Failed(NotAuthorized)` (R-148 item 3).
- **Given** a fake that does not answer target 1 **When** 2 s pass **Then** target 1 is `OutcomeUnknown("no answer from the administrator helper")`.
- **Given** `privileged = true` with `UnitStart` **When** admitted **Then** a single `Rejected(Unsupported)`.
- **Given** `privileged = false` **When** any action runs **Then** the fake helper receives nothing (no automatic escalation; security regression).
- **Given** the helper is `Missing` **When** a privileged action runs **Then** `Rejected(Unsupported)` and no spawn.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/helper.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/actions/mod.rs`: chain edit (mod line, privileged arm, hook installation).
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_helper.rs`: add the action cases.

## Tests
- `lab_helper.rs::privileged_signal_two_targets`
- `lab_helper.rs::privileged_partial_failure_summary`
- `lab_helper.rs::privileged_kill_tree_stops_first`
- `lab_helper.rs::privileged_auth_cancelled_all_targets`
- `lab_helper.rs::privileged_not_authorized_all_targets`
- `lab_helper.rs::privileged_timeout_outcome_unknown` with `#[explore_seeds(seeds = 0..16, workers = 2, chaos)]`
- `lab_helper.rs::privileged_unit_kind_unsupported`
- `lab_helper.rs::unprivileged_never_touches_helper` (security regression)
- `lab_helper.rs::privileged_missing_helper_rejected`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: as mapped above; UI texts come from `ActionTracker::message` (E16).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: requests are serial through the helper queue; 256 targets at 2 s each is the worst case and runs in the action's own task.
- Privacy: action logs record kind, target pid and result only (ADR-015).
- Security: privileged routing only when the request says so; the helper re-verifies every target.

## Notes
- Settled: the hook is E11-002's `PrivilegedOps` and `ActionCtx.helper` (R-147; this bead depends on i3o.4). The auth values are `ActionError::AuthCancelled` (pkexec 126) and `ActionError::NotAuthorized` (pkexec 127) (R-148 item 3).
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec (`git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`), one commit for this bead.

title: E29-015 E29: add helper reads to workers/process_detail.rs
description:
## Context
Once the helper runs, Properties tabs and PSS/USS of other users' processes fill in instead of showing Restricted (PROC-076, PROC-078 to PROC-084, UI-PWN-018 "Granted: the tab reloads through the helper"). This bead adds the helper call sites to the `ProcessDetail` worker (E10), which section 2 of 00-epics.md allows as an E29 chain edit. Sources: PROC-076 (1 Hz, only while shown), PROC-078 to PROC-084 (which files per tab), R-004, R-098, ADR-008 (detail rates), UI-PWN-002, UI-PWN-018.

## Deliverable
Chain edit to `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/process_detail.rs` (E10 file; this bead changes only the restricted-read path in it):
- When a direct read for a demanded target gives `Restricted` (EACCES or EPERM) and `HelperHandle::state() == Unlocked`, read through `HelperHandle::call(ReadProcessFiles { key, files })` with a 2 s deadline, with `files` per tab:
  - PSS and USS for `Demand.detail_keys`: `SMAPS_ROLLUP`.
  - General: `EXE | CWD | IO | SMAPS_ROLLUP | STATUS | ROOT` (`ROOT` for the Root row of PROC-078, R-157).
  - File descriptors (Fds): `FD_LIST | FDINFO`.
  - Memory maps: `MAPS | SMAPS`.
  - Security: `NS | STATUS`.
  - Environment: `ENVIRON` (only on open and on `DetailRefresh`, as UI-PWN-002 says for the direct path).
- Strings: a `Command::StringScan` whose direct scan gives `Restricted` (or `ptrace_scope = 1` for a non-child, PROC-084) uses `HelperHandle::call_stream(ScanStrings { key, opts })`; `CancelStringScan` breaks the stream (sends `CancelScan { seq }` with the scan frame's `seq`, R-157).
- Rate: at most one helper read per (target, tab) per second (PROC-076: 1 Hz), and only while the tab or column is demanded. While the helper is `Locked` or `Missing`, no helper call is made and the payload keeps `Restricted` (no automatic start: only the Grant access button starts a session).
- Grant access (R-170 item 13): `DetailDemand` has no flag for it. When `HealthSnapshot.helper` becomes `Unlocked`, the UI sends `Command::DetailRefresh { target, tab }` once; for a target whose direct read is Restricted, this worker serves that refresh with one helper `ReadProcessFiles` for the tab's files (the same files as above).
- The reply bodies are read as E29-004 sends them: `File { file, data }` bodies per file in ascending bit order, one `Err(Os(_))` body per failed file, postcard lists for `FD_LIST`, `FDINFO` and `NS`. The bytes go through the same E05-A3 parsers the direct path uses (byte-slice entry points); a per-file `Err(Os(13))` (EACCES) stays `Restricted`, `Err(Os(2))` or `Err(Os(3))` (ENOENT, ESRCH) gives `Missing`, `Err(Os(27))` (EFBIG) gives `Failed` with `last_error` "too large to read through the helper".
- A helper `Err(IdentityChanged)` or `NoSuchProcess` marks the target exited (the existing exited path).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a LabRuntime engine with a fake helper `Unlocked` and a demanded Environment tab for a target whose direct read is Restricted (fake collect root) **When** the tab is opened **Then** one `ReadProcessFiles { ENVIRON }` is sent and the payload validity becomes `Ok` with the parsed variables.
- **Given** the helper is `Locked` **When** the same tab is demanded **Then** no helper request is sent and the payload stays `Restricted`.
- **Given** the Memory maps tab stays demanded for 5 s of virtual time **When** the worker runs at 1 Hz **Then** at most 5 `ReadProcessFiles { MAPS | SMAPS }` requests are sent.
- **Given** a direct-readable target (own process) **When** any tab is demanded **Then** no helper request is sent.
- **Given** a privileged string scan and `CancelStringScan` after the first batch **When** processed **Then** the fake receives `CancelScan` and the scan state ends `Cancelled`.
- **Given** the helper becomes `Unlocked` while the Environment tab of a Restricted target is shown **When** the UI sends `Command::DetailRefresh { target, tab: Environment }` **Then** one `ReadProcessFiles { ENVIRON }` is sent and the payload validity becomes `Ok` (R-170 item 13).
- **Given** the fake answers `Err(Os(27))` for `smaps` **When** parsed **Then** the Maps payload is `Failed` with "too large to read through the helper".

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/process_detail.rs`: chain edit.
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_helper.rs`: add the detail cases.

## Tests
- `lab_helper.rs::detail_environment_through_helper`
- `lab_helper.rs::detail_locked_stays_restricted` (security regression: no automatic start)
- `lab_helper.rs::detail_helper_reads_at_1hz`
- `lab_helper.rs::detail_own_process_no_helper`
- `lab_helper.rs::strings_through_helper_cancel`
- `lab_helper.rs::detail_refresh_after_unlock_reads_through_helper` (R-170 item 13)

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: as listed.
- Validity: Restricted, Missing, Failed, Ok as listed.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: at most 1 helper request per demanded (target, tab) per second.
- Privacy: environment, maps and paths never logged.
- Security: helper reads happen only after the user granted access.

title: E29-016 E29: add helper path to workers/handle_search.rs
description:
## Context
"Search all" in Search File Handles restarts the search with `privileged = true` after the helper starts, so other users' processes are searched too (PROC-096, UI-PWN-030, UI-PWN-031 footer "Searched 412 of 530 processes. 118 need administrator rights."). This bead adds the helper path to the handle-search task (E10), an E29 chain edit allowed by section 2. Sources: PROC-096, R-004 (`ReadProcessFiles { fd_list, maps, cwd, exe }`), ADR-006.

## Deliverable
Chain edit to `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/handle_search.rs` (E10 file; only the privileged path changes):
- `Command::HandleSearch { privileged: true, .. }`: for each pid the direct walk skips as unreadable (the ones counted in `skipped`), call `HelperHandle::call(ReadProcessFiles { key, files: FD_LIST | CWD | EXE | ROOT | (MAPS if include_maps) })` with a 2 s deadline, and match the returned paths with the same matcher and the same `HandleHit` construction as the direct walk.
- Progress counts these pids as searched; `skipped` counts only pids the helper also could not read.
- Cancel (`CancelHandleSearch`) is checked between pids, as in the direct walk.
- With `privileged: true` while the helper is `Locked`, the first helper call starts the session (one polkit prompt; the UI already dispatched `StartHelperSession` per UI-PWN-031). With the helper `Missing` the search runs unprivileged and keeps `skipped`.
- `root` is in the R-004 file set (`ProcFiles::ROOT = 1 << 11`, R-157), so the `root` link of other users' processes is matched like `cwd` and gives hits of type `root` (PROC-096).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake collect root with 3 unreadable pids and a fake helper whose replies hold `/tmp/tl-marker` for pid 2 **When** a privileged search for `tl-marker` runs **Then** one hit for pid 2 arrives and `skipped == 0`.
- **Given** the same search with `privileged: false` **When** run **Then** no helper request is sent and `skipped == 3`.
- **Given** `CancelHandleSearch` after the first helper reply **When** processed **Then** no further helper request is sent and the phase is `Cancelled`.
- **Given** `include_maps = false` **When** helper requests are sent **Then** their `files` do not include `MAPS`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/handle_search.rs`: chain edit.
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_helper.rs`: add the search cases.

## Tests
- `lab_helper.rs::handle_search_all_uses_helper`

- `lab_helper.rs::handle_search_cancel_stops_helper_calls`
- `lab_helper.rs::handle_search_maps_flag`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: helper errors count the pid as skipped.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: helper calls are serial; cancel is checked between pids.
- Privacy: fd paths are matched and returned only as hits; never logged.
- Security: helper reads only when the user chose Search all.

title: E29-A2 Helper session in the engine
description:
## Context
Anchor E29-A2: the helper session inside the engine. One task owns at most one running helper, starts it on `StartHelperSession` or on the first privileged request (one polkit prompt), ends it on `EndHelperSession`, notices the helper's 300 s idle exit, and publishes the shield state `HealthSnapshot.helper: HelperState { Missing, Locked, Starting, Unlocked }` so the UI shield, Grant access and Retry buttons follow it (APP-003, PROC-076, UI-FND-028, UI-SHL-011). Every privileged engine path (actions, Properties reads, handle search, socket attribution) calls the helper through the `HelperHandle` defined here. Sources: ADR-006, ADR-004 (task tree, no asupersync types in public API), ASX sections 4 to 6 (spawn_blocking, timeout, channels), R-003, R-117, APP-003, PROC-076, UI-FND-028.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/helper/mod.rs`:
```rust
pub(crate) enum HelperMsg {
    Start,                                   // Command::StartHelperSession (R-148 item 1)
    End,                                     // Command::EndHelperSession
    SetupStatus,                             // Command::SetupStatus (R-247); handled by E29-019's probe
    RunSetup(SetupStep),                     // Command::RunSetup { step } (R-247); handled by E29-019's runner
    Call { req: HelperRequest, fd: Option<OwnedFd>, deadline: Duration,
           replies: async_channel::Sender<HelperReply>, done: oneshot::Sender<Result<(), HelperCallError>> },
}
pub(crate) use crate::actions::HelperCallError;   // { Missing, Cancelled, NotAuthorized, StartFailed(Arc<str>), Timeout, Exited, Protocol(Arc<str>) }: one enum, defined by E11-002 (i3o.4); no copy here (R-246)

#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) struct HelperHandle { tx: mpsc::Sender<HelperMsg> }   // mpsc capacity 64
impl HelperHandle {
    /// Queues the request; starts the session first when Locked (one polkit prompt, 120 s).
    /// Returns every reply in order. Err(Busy) if the queue is full.
    pub(crate) async fn call(&self, cx: &Cx, req: HelperRequest, fd: Option<OwnedFd>, deadline: Duration)
        -> Result<Vec<HelperReply>, HelperCallError>;
    /// Streaming form for ScanStrings and NetnsSockDiagDump.
    pub(crate) async fn call_stream(&self, cx: &Cx, req: HelperRequest, deadline: Duration)
        -> Result<async_channel::Receiver<HelperReply>, HelperCallError>;
    pub(crate) fn state(&self) -> HelperState;     // last published state, from a shared AtomicU8
}
pub(crate) async fn helper_task(cx: Cx, rx: mpsc::Receiver<HelperMsg>, updates: mpsc::Sender<EngineMsg>);
```
- `helper_task` runs in the engine session's region (spawned beside the action region by `session.rs`; E29-020 adds that spawn line as an allowed chain edit, R-150 item 4) and processes messages one at a time:
  - State at start: `Missing` if `/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper` or `/usr/bin/pkexec` is not a regular file, else `Locked`. Re-checked on every `Start`.
  - `Start` while `Locked`: publish `Starting`; run `HelperSession::start(ProcLink::spawn()?)` inside `cx.spawn_blocking`, wrapped in `time::timeout(START_DEADLINE + 5 s)`. Ok: `Unlocked`. `Cancelled`, `NotAuthorized`, `Failed`: back to `Locked` with a start outcome. `Missing`: `Missing`. `Start` while `Starting` or `Unlocked` is ignored.
  - `End` while `Unlocked`: `session.end()` in `spawn_blocking`; `Locked`; no start outcome (no toast).
  - `Call`: if `Missing`, answer `Missing`. If `Locked`, run the `Start` steps first without publishing a start outcome, and answer `Cancelled`, `NotAuthorized` or `StartFailed(reason)` when that start fails (R-246: the action's own toast reports it, so `helper_start` stays unset). Then move the session into `spawn_blocking`, run `call` with the request's deadline, forward each reply to `replies`, move the session back. `Timeout`, `Exited` or `Protocol` drop the session and publish `Locked`.
  - `SetupStatus` and `RunSetup(step)` (R-247): `helper_task` owns the `SetupState` and runs E29-019's `probe_status` and `run_step` inside `cx.spawn_blocking`, one message at a time; a `Call` or `Start` that arrives during a setup run waits in the queue (the UI disables the setup buttons while a run is in progress; two polkit prompts never overlap). Details in E29-019 (qfx.22).
  - Idle watch: while `Unlocked` and no message arrives, every 1 s check `session.is_alive()`; a helper that exited (its 300 s idle exit) publishes `Locked` with no start outcome (APP-003: no toast).
  - Cancellation (engine shutdown): `session.end()` then return `Outcome::Cancelled`; the helper also dies through `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`.
- Publishing: each state change sends `EngineMsg::Source(SourceUpdate::Helper(HelperUpdate { state, start }))` with `start: Option<(u64, HelperStartOutcome)>` (R-150 item 1). `start` is set only on a failed start that `HelperMsg::Start` requested (shield, Grant access, unlock at launch), never on an implicit start from a `Call` (R-246), with `HelperStartOutcome { Cancelled, NotAuthorized, Failed(Arc<str>) }` and a `seq` that `helper_task` counts up from 1. The reducer stores `state` in `HealthSnapshot.helper` and `start` in `HealthSnapshot.helper_start: Option<(u64 /* seq */, HelperStartOutcome)>` (as2.13, R-148 item 2); the UI toasts once per new `seq`.
- Deadlines: the start is bounded by `START_DEADLINE` (120 s, ADR-006 "any call that may show a polkit prompt"); each call by its own deadline; `time::timeout` around every `spawn_blocking` join (ASX section 6; a stuck blocking job is not interrupted, its result is discarded).
- Never use `select!`, `race!`, `GenServer` or asupersync signals (ASX section 10).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a LabRuntime engine with a `FakeLink` factory (test hook replacing `ProcLink::spawn`) **When** `Start` arrives **Then** the published states are `Starting` then `Unlocked`.
- **Given** the fake reports exit 126 **When** `Start` arrives **Then** states `Starting` then `Locked` with `start = Some(Cancelled)`.
- **Given** the helper files are absent (fake path check) **When** the task starts **Then** the state is `Missing`, and a `Call` answers `HelperCallError::Missing` without spawning.
- **Given** `Locked` **When** a `Call(Signal..)` arrives **Then** one start happens, then the call, and exactly one `Starting` then `Unlocked` is published.
- **Given** `Unlocked` **When** `End` arrives **Then** the fake saw `close`, and `Locked` is published with `start = None`.
- **Given** `Unlocked` and a fake whose process exits by itself **When** 1 s of virtual time passes **Then** `Locked` is published with `start = None`.
- **Given** a fake that never answers a call **When** the call's 2 s deadline passes **Then** the caller gets `Timeout` and the state is `Locked`.
- **Given** two `Call`s queued **When** processed **Then** the second's frames are sent only after the first's final reply.
- **Given** the engine shuts down while `Unlocked` **When** the region drains **Then** `end()` ran and the drain is `Quiescent`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/helper/mod.rs`: fill in.
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_helper.rs`: create.

## Tests (LabRuntime, `LabConfig::new(seed).max_steps(1_000_000)`, `run_with_auto_advance()`, each ending with `run_until_quiescent_with_report().lab_test_passed()`)
- `lab_helper.rs::start_publishes_starting_then_unlocked`
- `lab_helper.rs::start_cancelled_126_back_to_locked`
- `lab_helper.rs::missing_helper_never_spawns`
- `lab_helper.rs::call_while_locked_starts_once`
- `lab_helper.rs::end_closes_and_locks_without_toast`
- `lab_helper.rs::idle_exit_detected_within_1s`
- `lab_helper.rs::call_timeout_drops_session`
- `lab_helper.rs::calls_are_serial`
- `lab_helper.rs::shutdown_ends_session` with `#[explore_seeds(seeds = 0..16, workers = 2, chaos)]`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: start outcomes and call errors as listed.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: idle cost one 1 s timer while `Unlocked`; nothing while `Locked`.
- Privacy: no request content in logs; `info!` on target `tasklens::action` for session start and end only (no user names).
- Security: no automatic escalation: a session starts only on a user action (shield, Retry as administrator, Grant access, Search all, restricted count, unlock at launch) because only those send `Start` or a privileged call (ADR-006 consequence).

## Notes
- Settled: `Command::StartHelperSession` and `Command::EndHelperSession`, `HealthSnapshot.helper: HelperState`, `HealthSnapshot.helper_start` and `HelperStartOutcome` (R-148 items 1 and 2). E08 writes `SourceUpdate::Helper(HelperUpdate)` up front and E09 writes its reducer arm, which only logs until E29-020 (R-150 items 1 and 4). E29-020 spawns `helper_task` in `session.rs` and connects `Reducer.helper_tx: Option<mpsc::Sender<HelperCommand>>` (`HelperCommand { Start, End }`) to `HelperMsg::Start` and `End` (R-148 item 1). For actions, a dismissed prompt (pkexec 126) is `ActionError::AuthCancelled` and a denial (127) `ActionError::NotAuthorized` (R-148 item 3).
- Test access to engine internals: use the same test-only access path E08's `tests/lab_*.rs` use.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec (`git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`), one commit for this bead.

title: E29-017 E29: add restricted-cell helper reads to workers/processes.rs
description:
## Context
PROC-076: once the helper runs, restricted process table cells fill in: Handles, I/O, Disk, Image path, Working directory (and PSS and USS, which E29-015 covers). Those cells come from the `Processes` worker's sweep (E10, `workers/processes.rs`), and section 2 of 00-epics.md allows this one E29 chain edit there besides E32's (R-168 E29-OI-12). Sources: PROC-076, PROC-027 to PROC-031 (cells), PROC-035, PROC-036, R-004, ADR-016 (Restricted, not zero).

## Deliverable
Chain edit to `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/processes.rs` (the only change in it):
- After each sweep, while `HelperHandle::state() == Unlocked`, collect the keys of rows that are both Restricted for a demanded column and visible (`Demand` visible-row keys and visible columns): I/O and Disk columns need `IO`; Handles needs `FD_LIST`; Image path and Image name need `EXE`; Working directory needs `CWD`.
- At most once per second (PROC-076: 1 Hz), send one `ReadProcessFiles` per such key with the union of the needed files, deadline 2 s each, at most 64 keys per second (the visible rows; extra keys wait for the next second in key order).
- Read the reply bodies as E29-004 sends them (`File { file, data }` per file in ascending bit order, one `Err(Os(_))` body per failed file) and feed the bytes to the same E05-A1 readers the direct sweep uses (byte-slice entry points) and apply the values to the next published `ProcessRecord`s with their `FieldValidity` set `Ok`; I/O rates use the same counter rules (first helper value gives `WarmingUp`).
- Helper `Locked` or `Missing`: nothing changes, cells keep the lock glyph.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake collect root with a Restricted `io` for pid 42, the I/O column visible and a fake helper `Unlocked` **When** two sweeps run 1 s apart **Then** pid 42's I/O validity is `WarmingUp` after the first helper reply and `Ok` with a rate after the second.
- **Given** the helper `Locked` **When** sweeps run **Then** no helper request is sent.
- **Given** 100 restricted visible rows **When** one second passes **Then** at most 64 helper requests are sent.
- **Given** pid 42 is not visible **When** sweeps run **Then** no request for pid 42 is sent.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/processes.rs`: chain edit.
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_helper.rs`: add the sweep cases.

## Tests

- `lab_helper.rs::sweep_locked_no_helper` (security regression)
- `lab_helper.rs::sweep_helper_cap_64_per_second`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: helper errors leave the cell Restricted.
- Validity: WarmingUp, Ok, Restricted.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: helper calls happen after the sweep, never inside the 15 ms sweep budget; at most 64 per second.
- Privacy: exe and cwd paths of other users are never logged (ADR-015).
- Security: reads only after the user unlocked.

- Chain edit allowed (R-168 E29-OI-12; 00-epics section 2 row for `workers/processes.rs`).

title: E29-018 E29: add ResolveSocketInodes to workers/connections.rs
description:
## Context
SYS-030 and PROC-032: from P3, sockets of other users get their owning process through the helper (`ResolveSocketInodes`) instead of the restricted glyph. The socket to pid map is rebuilt by the `Connections` worker (E14, `workers/connections.rs`), where section 2 allows this one E29 chain edit (R-168 E29-OI-12). Sources: SYS-030 (rebuild every 2 s while demanded, one job at a time), PROC-032, R-004.

## Deliverable
Chain edit to `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/connections.rs` (the only change in it):
- After each 2 s socket map rebuild, collect the inodes of sockets whose owner is unknown because `/proc/<pid>/fd` was unreadable (not the inode-0 TIME-WAIT and orphan sockets, which stay "No owner (kernel)").
- While `HelperHandle::state() == Unlocked` and inodes remain, send one `ResolveSocketInodes { inodes }` (at most 4,096 inodes per request, the rest next round) with a 2 s deadline, as part of the same single outstanding rebuild job (SYS-030: one job at a time).
- Merge the `(inode, ProcessKey)` pairs of the `SocketOwners` reply (as2.36, R-157) into the map; several keys per inode give the "pid +N" form. Unresolved inodes keep PID "?" with the restricted glyph.
- The same map feeds the process TCP Network column, so those cells fill in too.
- Helper `Locked` or `Missing`: no request.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake socket dump with 3 unattributed inodes and a fake helper `Unlocked` resolving 2 of them **When** a rebuild runs **Then** 2 rows carry their `ProcessKey` and 1 keeps "?".
- **Given** the helper `Locked` **When** rebuilds run **Then** no helper request is sent.
- **Given** one inode resolved to two keys **When** published **Then** the row lists both (pid +1).
- **Given** 5,000 unattributed inodes **When** one rebuild runs **Then** exactly one request with 4,096 inodes is sent.

## Files

- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_helper.rs`: add the connection cases.

- Accessibility: N/A
