title: E29-019 Setup status probe and tasklens-setup runner in the engine
description:
## Context
The engine side of the Additional Setup window: `Command::SetupStatus` (journal group, lm_sensors, RAPL readability, helper presence, hwmon fans) and `Command::RunSetup { step }`, which runs `pkexec /usr/lib/tasklens/tasklens-setup <subcommand>` on the blocking pool and reports its output (ADR-005 Command list, UI-PRF-052, PERF-105 to PERF-108, APP-042, APP-049, R-028, R-029). The UI reads no system files itself (ADR-001 rule 1). The answer reaches the UI in `HealthSnapshot.setup: Arc<SetupState>`, shipped as `SourceUpdate::Setup(Arc<SetupState>)` from the setup runner (R-149 items 1 and 4, R-150 item 1). `helper/setup.rs` is an E29 file (R-168 E29-OI-13). Sources: ADR-005, UI-PRF-052, PERF-105, PERF-106, PERF-108, APP-049, R-028, R-029, R-117, R-149, R-150, R-168, table (c).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/helper/setup.rs` (new; `mod setup;` in `helper/mod.rs`):
- `pub(crate) fn probe_status(root: &SysRoot) -> SetupStatus` (blocking), with the as2.29 fields (R-149 item 1):
  - `rapl`: `NoZone` when no `/sys/class/powercap/intel-rapl:*` directory with an `energy_uj` file exists; `Readable { tasklens_rule }` when every zone's `energy_uj` opens for reading, with `tasklens_rule = /etc/udev/rules.d/99-tasklens-powercap.rules exists`; `NotReadable` otherwise. `/etc/udev/rules.d/99-powercap.rules` is never opened for writing and only its existence may be read.
  - `journal_group`: the current process's supplementary groups (`getgroups`) contain the gid of `systemd-journal` from `/etc/group`.
  - `helper_installed`: `/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper` is a regular file.
  - `lm_sensors`: `/usr/bin/sensors-detect` is a regular file.
  - `hwmon_fan`: any `/sys/class/hwmon/hwmon*/fan*_input` exists.
  - `sensors_conf`: `/etc/modules-load.d/tasklens-sensors.conf` exists.
- `pub(crate) fn run_step(step: SetupStep, out: &mut dyn FnMut(&str)) -> SetupPhase` (blocking; returns the final phase `Succeeded`, `Cancelled` or `Failed(Arc<str>)`): the arguments are `step.args()` (as2.29, R-149 item 2): `RaplEnable` `["rapl-enable"]`, `RaplRevert` `["rapl-revert"]`, `SensorsDetect` `["sensors-detect"]`, `SensorsRevert` `["sensors-revert"]`, `PolkitRule { on }` `["polkit-rule", "on" | "off"]`. Runs `std::process::Command::new("/usr/bin/pkexec").arg("/usr/lib/tasklens/tasklens-setup").args(step.args())` with `env_clear()`, stdin null, stdout and stderr both to one pipe, reading lines as they come (`out` per line; the captured output is capped at 64 KiB with the last lines kept: whole oldest lines are dropped until it fits, R-149 item 1). Because of `env_clear()`, `TASKLENS_SETUP_ROOT` never reaches the script; the script honours it only when not root (E29-022, R-168 E29-OI-13). Deadline 120 s (ADR-006 polkit row): past it, SIGKILL and wait, outcome `Failed("timed out")`. Exit 0: `Succeeded`; 126 or 127: `Cancelled` (UI-PRF-052: no failure block, status unchanged); other: `Failed(<captured output>)`. Never `asupersync::process`.
- Command handling (R-247): the commands reach `helper_task` (E29-A2, qfx.2) as `HelperMsg::SetupStatus` and `HelperMsg::RunSetup(step)`, forwarded from `HelperCommand` by E29-020. `helper_task` keeps the current `SetupState { status, run }` and publishes every change as `EngineMsg::Source(SourceUpdate::Setup(Arc<SetupState>))` (R-149 item 4, R-150 item 1). `SetupStatus` runs `probe_status` in `cx.spawn_blocking` and publishes `status: Some(..)`. `RunSetup(step)` publishes `run: Some(SetupRun { seq, step, phase: SetupPhase::Running, output: "" })` with `seq: u64` counting up from 1, runs `run_step` in `cx.spawn_blocking`, where the `out` closure updates `output` and sends the updated state at most every 100 ms through a clone of the `updates` sender with `try_send`, then publishes the final phase, then runs `probe_status` again and publishes it. A second `RunSetup` while one is running is ignored (the UI disables the buttons); other helper messages wait in the queue until the run ends. Put the two handlers in this file as `pub(crate) async fn handle_setup_status(..)` and `handle_run_setup(..)` taking `&Cx`, `&mut SetupState` and the `updates` sender, so `helper_task` only calls them.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake `SysRoot` with two RAPL zones, both readable, and no tasklens rule file **When** `probe_status` runs **Then** `rapl == Readable { tasklens_rule: false }` ("Enabled (existing rule)").
- **Given** a fake root with one unreadable zone (mode 0400 file owned by another user is not possible in a temp dir, so the test uses a missing read permission bit: mode 0200) **When** probed **Then** `NotReadable`.
- **Given** no powercap directory **When** probed **Then** `NoZone`.
- **Given** a fake script path (test-only `run_step_with(program, args, ..)`) that prints two lines and exits 0 **When** run **Then** `out` saw both lines and the outcome is `Succeeded`.
- **Given** the fake exits 126, then 127 **When** run **Then** both give `Cancelled`.
- **Given** the fake prints "boom" and exits 1 **When** run **Then** `Failed("boom\n")`.
- **Given** the fake prints 100 KiB **When** run **Then** the captured output is at most 65_536 bytes, starts at a line start and ends with the last line printed (R-149 item 1).
- **Given** each `SetupStep`, `SensorsRevert` and `PolkitRule { on: false }` included **When** `run_step_with` builds the command **Then** its arguments after the script path equal `step.args()` (R-149 item 2).
- **Given** the fake sleeps 200 s **When** run (deadline lowered to 1 s in the test constructor) **Then** `Failed("timed out")` and no zombie remains (`/proc/<child>` absent).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/helper/setup.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/helper/mod.rs`: add `mod setup;`.
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_helper.rs`: add one LabRuntime case `run_setup_publishes_running_then_outcome` with a fake runner.

## Tests
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::rapl_existing_rule`
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::rapl_not_readable`
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::rapl_no_zone`
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::run_ok_streams_lines`
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::run_126_127_cancelled`
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::run_failure_output`
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::run_output_cap` (last lines kept)
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::run_uses_step_args`
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::run_timeout_reaps`
- `lab_helper.rs::run_setup_publishes_running_then_outcome`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: outcomes as listed; the UI shows "Setup failed" with the output.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: probe reads a few dozen sysfs entries once per window open.
- Privacy: script output can contain paths of this machine only; it is shown in the window and never logged above `debug`.
- Security: fixed pkexec path, fixed script path, subcommand from a closed enum; no user text reaches the command line.

## Notes
- Settled: `SetupState`, `SetupStatus`, `RaplStatus`, `SetupRun`, `SetupPhase` and `SetupStep` are as2.29's, exactly as written there (R-149 items 1 and 2); they travel as `SourceUpdate::Setup(Arc<SetupState>)` into `HealthSnapshot.setup` (R-149 item 4, R-150 item 1). `helper/setup.rs` is an E29 file (R-168 E29-OI-13).
- `SetupStep::SensorsRevert` (Fan sensors "Revert", PERF-108) runs the `sensors-revert` subcommand, which table (c) now lists (R-149 item 2); its script branch is E29-023 (P4).
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec (`git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`), one commit for this bead.
close_reason: helper/setup.rs: probe_status, run_step (pkexec tasklens-setup, env_clear, 64 KiB cap, 120 s kill), handle_setup_status and handle_run_setup wired into helper_task via LinkEnv setup_probe and setup_runner; lab test run_setup_publishes_running_then_outcome. Commits a84bb56, acdd1c6

title: E29-020 E29: route helper and setup commands and health in session.rs and the reducer
description:
## Context
The engine's command handling and the reducer must route the new P3 commands and updates: `StartHelperSession`, `EndHelperSession`, `SetupStatus` and `RunSetup` to the helper task (E09 already forwards all four as `HelperCommand`, R-247), and the helper task's state and setup results into `HealthSnapshot` (APP-003, UI-FND-028, UI-PRF-052). `session.rs` and `reducer/apply.rs` are E09 files; section 2 allows this bead's chain edits at named insertion points (R-150 item 4): the `// E29-020: helper spawn` point in `session.rs` (8q0.18), and the `Helper` and `Setup` arms that E09 wrote up front in `apply.rs` and that only log until this bead (8q0.9). E09 already routes `StartHelperSession`, `EndHelperSession`, `SetupStatus` and `RunSetup` to `Reducer.helper_tx: Option<mpsc::Sender<HelperCommand>>` with `HelperCommand { Start, End, SetupStatus, RunSetup(SetupStep) }`, and drops them while it is `None` (R-148 item 1, R-247).

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-engine/src/session.rs`, at the `// E29-020: helper spawn` point right after the reducer is built: create `mpsc::channel::<HelperMsg>(64)` and spawn `helper::helper_task` in the session region; create `mpsc::channel::<HelperCommand>(64)`, set `reducer.helper_tx = Some(tx)` (R-148 item 1), and spawn one forwarding task in the same region that turns each `HelperCommand` into the same-named `HelperMsg` (`Start`, `End`, `SetupStatus`, `RunSetup(step)`; R-247) on the helper queue (no `select!`; ASX section 10). Pass the `HelperHandle` to the actions context and the workers that need it (`ProcessDetail`, handle search, `Processes`, `Connections`).
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/apply.rs`, only in the arms E09 wrote up front (R-150 item 4): the `SourceUpdate::Helper(HelperUpdate { state, start })` arm stores `state` in `HealthSnapshot.helper` and, when `start` is `Some((seq, outcome))`, sets `helper_start = Some((seq, outcome))` (the helper task counts `seq`, R-150 item 1, R-148 item 2); the `SourceUpdate::Setup(state)` arm replaces `HealthSnapshot.setup` with `state: Arc<SetupState>` (R-149 item 4). Each arm marks `HEALTH` only when a value changed, so `health` keeps its `Arc` otherwise. The `StartHelperSession`, `EndHelperSession`, `SetupStatus` and `RunSetup` arms stay as E09 wrote them (R-247): a full helper queue (`try_send` error) is logged at `debug` and dropped (the user can click again).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a LabRuntime engine with the fake helper link **When** the UI sends `Command::StartHelperSession` **Then** within one publish the snapshot's `health.helper` is `Starting`, then `Unlocked`.
- **Given** the fake start fails with 126 **When** published **Then** `health.helper_start` is `Some((1, Cancelled))` and a second failure gives `Some((2, Cancelled))`.
- **Given** `Command::SetupStatus` **When** processed **Then** `health.setup.status` is `Some(..)` within one publish after the probe.
- **Given** a snapshot change that touches only CPU series **When** published **Then** `health` reuses its `Arc` (no HEALTH bit for the UI).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/session.rs`: chain edit (spawn, `helper_tx`, forwarding task, hand out the handle).
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/apply.rs`: chain edit (the two arms named above).
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_helper.rs`: add the routing cases.

## Tests
- `lab_helper.rs::command_start_reaches_helper`
- `lab_helper.rs::start_failure_seq_counts`
- `lab_helper.rs::setup_status_published`
- `lab_helper.rs::health_arc_reused_when_unchanged`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: dropped commands on a full queue are logged only.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: no new allocation per publish when helper state is unchanged.
- Privacy: N/A
- Security: N/A

## Notes
- Chain edits allowed (R-150 item 4, 00-epics section 2): `session.rs` at the `// E29-020: helper spawn` point and `reducer/apply.rs` in the arms named here, nothing else in E09 files.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E29-021 Polkit policy file with three actions
description:
## Context
The polkit policy file with exactly three tasklens actions (R-002, table (c), ADR-006): the helper, the setup script, and the reserved network monitor. pkexec maps a program to its action through the `org.freedesktop.policykit.exec.path` annotation, so each action names its fixed binary. Sources: R-001, R-002, ADR-006, table (c), APP-003, PERF-105.

## Deliverable
`packaging/io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.policy`, installed by the PKGBUILD (E33) to `/usr/share/polkit-1/actions/io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.policy`:
```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE policyconfig PUBLIC "-//freedesktop//DTD PolicyKit Policy Configuration 1.0//EN"
 "http://www.freedesktop.org/standards/PolicyKit/1/policyconfig.dtd">
<policyconfig>
  <vendor>tasklens</vendor>
  <icon_name>io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens</icon_name>
  <action id="io.github.oysteinkrog.tasklens.helper">
    <description>Run tasklens administrator actions</description>
    <message>Authentication is required to let tasklens act on other users' processes, system services and network connections.</message>
    <defaults><allow_any>auth_admin</allow_any><allow_inactive>auth_admin</allow_inactive><allow_active>auth_admin_keep</allow_active></defaults>
    <annotate key="org.freedesktop.policykit.exec.path">/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper</annotate>
  </action>
  <action id="io.github.oysteinkrog.tasklens.setup">
    <description>Change tasklens system setup</description>
    <message>Authentication is required to change system settings for tasklens.</message>
    <defaults><allow_any>auth_admin</allow_any><allow_inactive>auth_admin</allow_inactive><allow_active>auth_admin_keep</allow_active></defaults>
    <annotate key="org.freedesktop.policykit.exec.path">/usr/lib/tasklens/tasklens-setup</annotate>
  </action>
  <action id="io.github.oysteinkrog.tasklens.netmon">
    <description>Run the tasklens network monitor</description>
    <message>Authentication is required to run the tasklens network monitor.</message>
    <defaults><allow_any>auth_admin</allow_any><allow_inactive>auth_admin</allow_inactive><allow_active>auth_admin_keep</allow_active></defaults>
    <annotate key="org.freedesktop.policykit.exec.path">/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-netmon</annotate>
  </action>
</policyconfig>
```
The owner confirmed the three description and message texts as written (D-019; R-168 E29-OI-16). Use them byte for byte.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the file **When** `xmllint --noout` runs (skip when xmllint is absent) **Then** it is well formed.
- **Given** the file **When** the test scans it **Then** it has exactly three `<action id=` entries with the three ids above, each `allow_active` is `auth_admin_keep`, and each exec path matches table (c).
- **Given** the file **When** searched **Then** it has no other action id and no `>yes<` default.
- **Given** the file **When** the test reads the three `<description>` and `<message>` texts **Then** they equal the D-019 texts above byte for byte.

## Files
- `packaging/io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.policy`: create.
- `crates/tl-helper/tests/helper_proto.rs`: add `policy_file_has_three_actions` (reads `../../packaging/io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.policy` relative to `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`).

## Tests
- `tests/helper_proto.rs::policy_file_has_three_actions` (security regression: no extra action, no `yes` default; also checks the six D-019 texts).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: N/A
- Security: one action per binary; nothing defaults to `yes`.

## Notes
- Installing this file, `tl-helper` (mode 0755, `/usr/lib/tasklens/tl-helper`) and `tasklens-setup` (mode 0755, `/usr/lib/tasklens/tasklens-setup`) is the PKGBUILD's job: E33-015 (cr0.18) adds those lines and depends on this bead and on E29-022 (qfx.34) as well as E29-A1 (R-168 E29-OI-17).

It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E29-023 tasklens-setup sensors-detect and sensors-revert
description:
## Context
P4 branch of `tasklens-setup`: `sensors-detect` runs `sensors-detect --auto`, writes the modules it finds to `/etc/modules-load.d/tasklens-sensors.conf` and loads them with `modprobe`, so fan pages appear and survive a reboot (PERF-108, table (c)). PERF-108's "Revert" removes that file through the `sensors-revert` subcommand, which table (c) lists; it is P4 like the button (R-149 item 2). This bead adds both.

## Deliverable
In `packaging/tasklens-setup` (same root and test-mode rules as E29-022):
- `sensors-detect`:
  - Test mode for this branch: the presence check looks at `$ROOT/usr/bin/sensors-detect`, and `sensors-detect --auto` is replaced by printing `would run: sensors-detect --auto` followed by the content of `$ROOT/sensors-detect.out`.
  - If `/usr/bin/sensors-detect` is missing: print `Install lm_sensors to detect fan sensors`, exit 3.
  - Run `sensors-detect --auto` and keep its output; print it.
  - Collect module names from output lines matching `^MODULE_[0-9]+=` (value after `=`, surrounding quotes removed); each name must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`, others are skipped with a line `skipped module name: <name>`.
  - No modules: print `No sensor modules found`, exit 0, and write nothing.
  - Else write one name per line to `$ROOT/etc/modules-load.d/tasklens-sensors.conf.tmp`, `chmod 0644`, `mv -f` to `tasklens-sensors.conf`, run `modprobe <name>` for each, print `Enabled`.
- `sensors-revert` (table (c), PERF-108, R-149 item 2): `rm -f "$ROOT/etc/modules-load.d/tasklens-sensors.conf"`, print `Reverted. The modules stay loaded until the next reboot.`
- The usage line gains `sensors-revert`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** test mode with `$ROOT/usr/bin/sensors-detect` present and `$ROOT/sensors-detect.out` holding `MODULE_0=nct6775` and `MODULE_1="coretemp"` **When** `sensors-detect` runs **Then** the conf file holds `nct6775\ncoretemp\n`, stdout has `would run: modprobe nct6775` and `would run: modprobe coretemp`, and the last line is `Enabled`.
- **Given** an output line `MODULE_2=evil;rm` **When** parsed **Then** it is skipped with `skipped module name: evil;rm` (security regression).
- **Given** no `MODULE_` lines **When** run **Then** `No sensor modules found`, exit 0, no file.
- **Given** test mode and no `usr/bin/sensors-detect` under the root **When** run **Then** exit 3 with the lm_sensors line.
- **Given** an existing conf **When** `sensors-revert` runs **Then** the file is gone.

## Files
- `packaging/tasklens-setup`: add the two branches.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/helper/setup.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::script_sensors_detect_writes_modules`
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::script_sensors_bad_module_name_skipped` (security regression)
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::script_sensors_none_found`
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::script_sensors_missing_lm_sensors`
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::script_sensors_revert`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: exit 3 for missing lm_sensors; other failures as the command's own output.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: N/A
- Security: module names are checked against a strict pattern before `modprobe`.

## Notes
- Phase P4. `sensors-revert` and `SetupStep::SensorsRevert` (`args()` = `["sensors-revert"]`, as2.29) are settled (R-149 item 2).
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p packaging`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec (`git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`), one commit for this bead.

title: E29-024 tasklens-setup polkit-rule on and off
description:
## Context
P4 branch of `tasklens-setup`: `polkit-rule on|off` writes or removes `/etc/polkit-1/rules.d/49-tasklens.rules`, which lets wheel members in the active local session run tasklens's own polkit actions without a password (APP-049, table (c), R-002). The prefix covers the helper, setup and netmon actions; the systemd and `policykit.exec` actions are not covered. Sources: APP-049, R-002, table (c).

## Deliverable
In `packaging/tasklens-setup` (same root and test-mode rules as E29-022):
- `polkit-rule on`: write to `$ROOT/etc/polkit-1/rules.d/49-tasklens.rules.tmp`, `chmod 0644`, `mv -f` to `49-tasklens.rules`, print `Enabled`. Exact content:
  ```
  polkit.addRule(function(action, subject) {
      if (action.id.indexOf("io.github.oysteinkrog.tasklens.") == 0 &&
          subject.local && subject.active && subject.isInGroup("wheel")) {
          return polkit.Result.YES;
      }
  });
  ```
- `polkit-rule off`: `rm -f "$ROOT/etc/polkit-1/rules.d/49-tasklens.rules"`, print `Reverted`.
- `polkit-rule` with any other second argument: usage, exit 2.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** test mode **When** `polkit-rule on` runs **Then** the file content equals the text above byte for byte, mode 0644, last line `Enabled`.
- **Given** the file exists **When** `polkit-rule off` runs **Then** it is gone and the output is `Reverted`.
- **Given** `polkit-rule maybe` **When** run **Then** exit 2.
- **Given** the rule text **When** checked **Then** it contains the prefix `io.github.oysteinkrog.tasklens.` and no `org.freedesktop.` string (security regression: no third-party action is covered).

## Files
- `packaging/tasklens-setup`: add the branch.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/helper/setup.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::script_polkit_rule_on_exact_text`
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::script_polkit_rule_off`
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::script_polkit_rule_bad_arg`
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::script_polkit_rule_scope` (security regression)

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: as listed.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: N/A
- Security: the rule only covers the tasklens prefix, only for local active wheel sessions.

## Notes
- Phase P4.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p packaging`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E29-025 Additional Setup Enable and Revert flows
description:
## Context
The Enable and Revert flows of the Additional Setup window: a confirm dialog, the pkexec run through the engine, the running state, the success line, the failure block with the script output, and the cancelled-prompt rule (UI-PRF-052, PERF-105, PERF-106, R-029, R-117). Sources: UI-PRF-052, PERF-105, PERF-106, UI-SHL-094, R-117 (pkexec exit 126 and 127), UI-FND-022 (`TlDialog::confirm`, focus on Cancel per R-104).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/window/setup.rs`:
- CPU power draw buttons: "Enable" (primary) when the status is `Not enabled`; "Revert" (primary) when `Enabled` by the tasklens rule; neither for `Enabled (existing rule)` or `Not needed`.
- "Enable" opens `TlDialog::confirm`: title "Enable CPU power draw?", body "Lets every local user read CPU energy counters. This can leak information about other programs (CVE-2020-8694).", buttons "Enable" (primary) and "Cancel". Confirm sends `Command::RunSetup { step: SetupStep::RaplEnable }`.
- "Revert" opens: title "Revert CPU power draw?", body "Removes the tasklens udev rule. A reboot may be needed before the files return to mode 0400.", buttons "Revert" (danger) and "Cancel". Confirm sends `RunSetup { step: RaplRevert }`.
- Running (from `HealthSnapshot.setup.run` with `phase == Running` for this row's step): the card's buttons are disabled and the badge shows a 12 px spinner icon with the text `Running…`. The pkexec prompt is the system's own.
- Outcome (a `run` whose `seq` is newer than the last one this window handled):
  - `Succeeded`: a line under the buttons "Done. No restart needed." in `status.success`; for RAPL steps send `Command::ReprobeSource(SourceId::Cpu)` once, so the Power draw row changes within 2 s; the status badge follows the next `setup.status`.
  - `Failed(output)`: a block under the buttons: "Setup failed" (`t_sm`, weight 500, `status.danger`), the output in a mono read-only scroll area (max height 160), buttons "Copy output" (copies the output text, toast "Copied to clipboard") and "Retry" (sends the same `RunSetup` again).
  - `Cancelled` (pkexec 126 or 127): no block; the card keeps its old status.
- `send` returning `Err(CommandError::Busy)` leaves the card idle with no block.
- Strings appended to `assets/locales/en-US.ftl` with the `setup-` prefix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** status `Not enabled` **When** "Enable" is clicked **Then** the dialog shows the title, body and buttons above, focus is on "Cancel", and no command is sent yet.
- **Given** the dialog **When** "Enable" is pressed **Then** the fake engine records `RunSetup { step: RaplEnable }`.
- **Given** a published `run = Running { step: RaplEnable }` **When** rendered **Then** the CPU card's buttons are disabled and the badge reads `Running…`.
- **Given** a published `Succeeded` **When** rendered **Then** "Done. No restart needed." is shown and `ReprobeSource(SourceId::Cpu)` was sent exactly once.
- **Given** a published `Failed("udevadm: not found\n")` **When** rendered **Then** "Setup failed" and the output show; "Retry" sends `RunSetup { step: RaplEnable }` again.
- **Given** a published `Cancelled` **When** rendered **Then** no failure block shows and the badge still reads `Not enabled`.
- **Given** status `Enabled (existing rule)` **When** rendered **Then** neither Enable nor Revert is shown.
- **Given** status `Enabled` (tasklens rule) **When** "Revert" is confirmed **Then** `RunSetup { step: RaplRevert }` is sent.

description:

title: E29-030 E29: add Shift-at-launch detection to window/main.rs (U-43)
description:
## Context
"Shift held at launch" unlocks privileged actions at start (table (b), APP-003). On Wayland a client gets no modifier state before its window has focus, so the main window counts Shift as held when its first `on_modifiers_changed` event within 500 ms of first focus has `shift` set; this must be verified on KWin (U-43, R-124). If KWin sends no modifiers on first focus, the Shift path is dropped on Wayland and `privilege.unlock_at_launch` remains. The detection code lives in E20's `window/main.rs` (and the X11 `XkbGetState` path in E33's `tl-app/src/main.rs`, which needs an X11 library outside tl-app's ADR-001 row); Section 2 allows this one E29 chain edit in `window/main.rs`, and the same first-focus modifier rule runs on X11 too, so no `XkbGetState` path is needed (R-168 E29-OI-19).

## Deliverable
- Step 1, verify U-43: run tasklens on the owner's KWin Wayland session with a temporary `info!(target: "tasklens::ui", shift = ?, ms_since_focus = ?)` in the first `on_modifiers_changed` handler, start it from KRunner and from a terminal with Shift held, and record whether the event arrives within 500 ms with `shift` set. Record the result (yes or no, with the measured ms) in this bead's close reason. Remove the temporary log.
- Step 2a (U-43 holds): chain edit to `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`: `MainWindow` records `first_focus_at` on its first focus; its `on_modifiers_changed` handler, while `now - first_focus_at <= 500 ms` and not yet decided, sets `shift_at_launch = event.modifiers.shift` and decides once. The step-11 launch hook (E20) dispatches `StartHelperSession` once when `shift_at_launch` or `privilege.unlock_at_launch` is true. The same rule runs on X11 (GPUI delivers modifier events there too); no `XkbGetState`.
- Step 2b (U-43 fails): no code; record "Shift at launch dropped on Wayland (U-43)" in the close reason and tell the leader so table (b) and R-124 can be updated.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a `TestAppContext` main window **When** focus arrives and a modifiers event with `shift = true` follows 100 ms later **Then** exactly one `StartHelperSession` is sent after the first frame.
- **Given** the shift event arrives 600 ms after focus **When** processed **Then** no `StartHelperSession` is sent (unless `unlock_at_launch` is on).
- **Given** two shift events within 500 ms **When** processed **Then** one start at most.
- **Given** `unlock_at_launch = true` and Shift also held **When** launched **Then** one start, not two.

## Files

- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_shield.rs`: add the four tests.

title: E29-022 tasklens-setup script with rapl-enable and rapl-revert
description:
## Context
The packaged setup script `/usr/lib/tasklens/tasklens-setup` (source `packaging/tasklens-setup`, POSIX `sh`, mode 0755, R-138 item 11) with the RAPL subcommands, plus the reference rule file. The Additional Setup window runs it as `pkexec /usr/lib/tasklens/tasklens-setup <subcommand>` under `io.github.oysteinkrog.tasklens.setup`; nothing is ever written to `/tmp` (PERF-105, PERF-106, R-028, R-029, table (c)). This bead writes the script frame and `rapl-enable` / `rapl-revert`; `sensors-detect` (E29-023) and `polkit-rule` (E29-024) add their branches later.

## Deliverable
- `packaging/99-tasklens-powercap.rules`: exactly one line plus a newline:
  `SUBSYSTEM=="powercap", KERNEL=="intel-rapl:*", ACTION=="add", RUN+="/usr/bin/chmod 0444 /sys%p/energy_uj"`
- `packaging/tasklens-setup` (`#!/bin/sh`, `set -eu`, `umask 022`, `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` set at the top):
  - Root and test mode: if `id -u` is 0, the variable `TASKLENS_SETUP_ROOT` is ignored and `ROOT=""`. If not 0 and `TASKLENS_SETUP_ROOT` is set, test mode: `ROOT="$TASKLENS_SETUP_ROOT"` and every external system command (`udevadm`, `modprobe`, `sensors-detect`) is replaced by printing `would run: <command line>`. If not 0 and unset: print `tasklens-setup: must run as root (use pkexec)` to stderr, exit 1. (Test mode accepted, honoured only when not root: R-168 E29-OI-13.)
  - `rapl-enable`: write the rule line above to `$ROOT/etc/udev/rules.d/99-tasklens-powercap.rules.tmp`, `chmod 0644`, `mv -f` it to `99-tasklens-powercap.rules`, then run `udevadm control --reload` and `udevadm trigger --subsystem-match=powercap --action=add`, then print `Enabled`. It never reads, writes or removes `99-powercap.rules`.
  - `rapl-revert`: `rm -f "$ROOT/etc/udev/rules.d/99-tasklens-powercap.rules"`, the same two `udevadm` commands, then print `Reverted. A reboot may be needed before the files return to mode 0400.`
  - Any other first argument, or none: print `usage: tasklens-setup rapl-enable|rapl-revert|sensors-detect|polkit-rule on|off` to stderr, exit 2.
  - Each failing command makes the script exit non-zero with the command's own output (set -e), which the window shows.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** test mode with a temp root containing `etc/udev/rules.d/` **When** `tasklens-setup rapl-enable` runs **Then** the rule file there equals `packaging/99-tasklens-powercap.rules` byte for byte, has mode 0644, stdout lists the two `would run: udevadm ...` lines and ends with `Enabled`, exit 0.
- **Given** a temp root with a file `etc/udev/rules.d/99-powercap.rules` **When** enable then revert run **Then** that file is unchanged (same bytes and mtime).
- **Given** test mode after enable **When** `rapl-revert` runs **Then** the tasklens file is gone and the last line is the reboot sentence.
- **Given** a non-root run without `TASKLENS_SETUP_ROOT` **When** any subcommand runs **Then** exit 1 with the "must run as root" line.
- **Given** `tasklens-setup bogus` **When** run in test mode **Then** exit 2 with the usage line.
- **Given** the script **When** `shellcheck -s sh` runs (skip when absent) **Then** no warnings.

## Files
- `packaging/tasklens-setup`: create (mode 0755 in git).
- `packaging/99-tasklens-powercap.rules`: create.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/helper/setup.rs`: add tests that run the script from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/../../packaging/tasklens-setup` in test mode.

- `helper/setup.rs::tests::script_rapl_revert_removes_rule`

- `helper/setup.rs::tests::script_usage_exit_2`
- `helper/setup.rs::tests::script_shellcheck_clean`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: script output and exit code go to the window's failure block.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: N/A
- Security: runs as root; fixed paths only; `TASKLENS_SETUP_ROOT` is ignored as root (pkexec also clears the environment).

- Depends on E29-019 (the test module lives in `helper/setup.rs`).

It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: tasklens-setup sensors-detect: read the modules sensors-detect really reports, and revert what it writes
description:
Files: packaging/tasklens-setup, crates/tl-engine/src/helper/setup.rs (tests), and the E29-023 text in the spec if it names MODULE_<n>= lines.
Why: qfx.25 read the installed /usr/bin/sensors-detect (lm_sensors 3.6). It never prints MODULE_<n>= lines. With --auto it writes /etc/conf.d/lm_sensors (HWMON_MODULES="...") and may enable and start lm_sensors.service. It prints modprobe lines between "#----cut here----" markers only when it does not write that file. So the current parser finds nothing on a real machine, and sensors-revert leaves the conf.d file and the service behind.
Leader decision:
- Before running, save whether /etc/conf.d/lm_sensors exists (copy it to the tasklens state dir if it does) and whether lm_sensors.service is enabled.
- After sensors-detect --auto, take the module list from HWMON_MODULES in /etc/conf.d/lm_sensors; if that is absent, from the modprobe lines in the cut-here block. Same name check as now.
- sensors-revert: restore the saved conf.d file, or remove it if it did not exist before; disable lm_sensors.service only if it was not enabled before. Then the current unload steps.
AC: test-mode fixtures for both sensors-detect outputs (conf.d written; cut-here block) give the same module list. Given no conf.d before, revert removes it; given one before, revert restores the old content byte for byte. Given the service enabled before, revert leaves it enabled (test mode prints the would-run lines). Never run sensors-detect, systemctl or modprobe for real in tests.
close_reason: tasklens-setup reads modules from /etc/conf.d/lm_sensors (when this run wrote it) or the cut-here modprobe block; saves old conf.d and service state in /var/lib/tasklens; sensors-revert restores or removes conf.d and disables the service only if it was not enabled before. Tests in helper/setup.rs, PERF-108 text updated. b352419

title: Helper: background reads must never start a session or show a polkit prompt
description:
Files: crates/tl-engine/src/helper/mod.rs, crates/tl-engine/src/workers/processes.rs, crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_helper.rs.
Why: qfx.20 (2f49b50) reads restricted process cells through HelperHandle::call after checking the state is Unlocked. call() starts a session when the helper is Locked, so if the helper exits on its own between the check and the call, a background read triggers a polkit password prompt the user did not ask for. Security and UX rule: only a user action may prompt.
Leader decision: add a call option (or a separate method) that never starts a session: when the helper is not Unlocked at call time it returns a NotRunning error at once, atomically with the state check inside the helper task, not in the caller. Background readers (processes sweep reads, and any other worker reads) must use it. User-triggered actions keep the current call.
AC: lab test: the helper exits between the sweep's state check and the read; the read returns NotRunning, no spawn happens and no prompt is requested (fake link records zero starts). Existing lab_helper and lab_actions tests pass. clippy -p tl-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings clean.
close_reason: HelperHandle::read + HelperMsg::Read: helper task refuses with HelperReadError::NotRunning unless Unlocked when it takes the read; HelperReads uses read; 5 lab tests. Commit 5be2bb2

title: E29-002 Helper process operations with own identity check
description:
## Context
The helper's process operations: signals, nice, scheduling policy, affinity and I/O priority on any user's process or thread, as root. They are the same `tl-ops` functions the unprivileged engine uses (ADR-001 consequence, ADR-006), and the helper re-runs `open_verified` itself on every target; it never trusts the engine's check (ADR-006, R-004). Sources: ADR-006 (identity revalidation, PID-based rules, thread targets, deadlines), R-004, R-097, PROC-060 to PROC-068, PROC-076.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-helper/src/ops.rs` (new; add `mod ops;` to `main.rs`):
- `pub fn run_process_op(req: &HelperRequest, boot: BootId) -> HelperReplyBody` handling exactly `Signal`, `SetNice`, `SetSched`, `SetAffinity`, `SetIoPriority`. Any other variant returns `HelperReplyBody::Err(HelperError::NotAllowed)` (rule "not a process operation").
- `boot` is read once at helper start from `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` with `tl_model::time::BootId` parsing and passed in.
- Per target:
  - `HelperTarget::Process(key)`: call `tl_ops::process::open_verified(key, boot)` first; on `IdentityChanged` reply `Err(IdentityChanged)` and do nothing else.
  - `HelperTarget::Thread { process, tid }`: allowed only for `Signal`, `SetNice`, `SetSched`, `SetAffinity`; `SetIoPriority` with a thread target replies `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "thread target"). Verify the process with `open_verified`, then the thread through the same tl-ops thread-target function the engine uses (it checks `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>` and uses `tgkill` for signals).
  - Then call the tl-ops function for the kind (signal through the verified pidfd; nice, sched, affinity, ioprio on every TID with the before and after pidfd poll). Map `OpsError` to `HelperError`: `IdentityChanged`, `NoSuchProcess`, `PermissionDenied` (EPERM, EACCES), `Partial { done, total }`, `Os(errno)`. A pidfd readable after the call (process exited during the change) maps to `Err(Os(libc ESRCH = 3))` so the engine reports `OutcomeUnknown("process exited during the change")`.
  - Success replies `Ok`.
- Value checks before any syscall, each failing with `Err(NotAllowed)` and no syscall (the rule name in parentheses): nice outside `-20..=19` ("nice out of range"); `rt_prio` not in `1..=99` for `Fifo`/`Rr` or not `0` for `Other`/`Batch`/`Idle` ("rt_prio out of range"); `IoPriority` level above 7 ("ioprio level out of range"); `Signal::Other(n)` with `n == 0` or `n > 64` ("signal out of range"); an empty `CpuSet` ("empty cpu set").
- The helper never targets PID 1 with `Signal(Kill)`, `Signal(Term)`, `Signal(Stop)` or any `Signal::Other`: it replies `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "pid 1"). (The engine refuses earlier; this is the helper's own guard.)

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a child `sleep 60` started by the test and its captured `ProcessKey` **When** `run_process_op(Signal { target: Process(key), signal: Term })` runs **Then** the reply is `Ok` and the child exits by SIGTERM.
- **Given** the same key with `start_ticks + 1` **When** any process op runs **Then** the reply is `Err(IdentityChanged)` and the child is still alive.
- **Given** a key whose `boot_id` differs from `boot` **When** any op runs **Then** the reply is `Err(IdentityChanged)`.
- **Given** `SetNice { nice: 25 }` **When** run **Then** the reply is `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "nice out of range") and no syscall is made.
- **Given** `SetIoPriority` with a thread target **When** run **Then** the reply is `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "thread target").
- **Given** a request for PID 1 with `Signal(Kill)` **When** run **Then** the reply is `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "pid 1").
- **Given** a `FreezeGroup` request **When** passed to `run_process_op` **Then** the reply is `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "not a process operation").
- **Given** a child and `SetNice { nice: 5 }` as the same user **When** run **Then** `Ok`, and every TID of the child shows nice 5 in `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/stat` field 19.

## Files
- `crates/tl-helper/src/ops.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/main.rs`: add `mod ops;`.

## Tests
- `ops.rs::tests::signal_verified_child` (spawns `sleep 60` as the current user; no root needed).
- `ops.rs::tests::stale_start_ticks_rejected` (security regression: the helper does its own `open_verified`).
- `ops.rs::tests::boot_id_mismatch_rejected` (security regression).
- `ops.rs::tests::value_ranges_rejected_before_syscall` (nice 25, nice -21, rt_prio 0 with Rr, rt_prio 5 with Other, ioprio level 8, Signal::Other(0), Signal::Other(65), empty CpuSet).
- `ops.rs::tests::pid1_guard` (security regression).
- `ops.rs::tests::thread_target_kinds` (ioprio on a thread is refused; nice on a thread of the child succeeds).
- `ops.rs::tests::set_nice_every_tid`: re-execute the test binary (`std::env::current_exe()`) with env `TL_HELPER_TEST_THREADS=3`; in that mode the test harness entry starts 3 threads and sleeps 60 s. `SetNice { nice: 5 }` gives `Ok` and all 4 TIDs show nice 5.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: only the `HelperError` values above; the engine turns them into `ActionError`.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one syscall loop per TID; no allocation per TID beyond the TID list.
- Privacy: log nothing about the target except pid and the result at `debug` (ADR-015). Never log command lines.
- Security: this runs as root. Every target is re-verified here. No path or free-form argument exists in these requests.

## Notes
- Protocol names are those of `tl-model/src/helper_proto.rs` (E03-070, as2.36, the type owner; R-157). Requests travel as `HelperFrame { seq: u32, request: HelperRequest }` (the engine picks `seq`) and replies as `HelperReply { seq: u32, last: bool, body: HelperReplyBody }` (the helper echoes `seq`; `last: true` marks the final reply of a request). `HelperRequest` has 17 variants: `Hello { proto }`, `Signal { target, signal }`, `SetNice { target, nice }`, `SetSched { target, policy, rt_prio }`, `SetAffinity { target, set }`, `SetIoPriority { key, prio }`, `FreezeGroup(HelperCgroup)`, `ThawGroup(HelperCgroup)`, `KillGroup(HelperCgroup)`, `ReadProcessFiles { key, files: ProcFiles }`, `ScanStrings { key, opts }`, `Dump { key, mode }` (the output fd travels as `SCM_RIGHTS` ancillary data with this frame, R-145 item 3), `ResolveSocketInodes { inodes }`, `SockDestroy { family, proto, four_tuple, cookie }`, `WriteServiceDropIn { unit, keys: Vec<(DropInKey, String)> }`, `NetnsSockDiagDump { netns_ino }`, `CancelScan { seq: u32 }`; `target` is `HelperTarget::{Process(ProcessKey), Thread { process: ProcessKey, tid: u32 }}`. `HelperReplyBody`: `Hello { proto }`, `Ok`, `Err(HelperError)`, `File { file: ProcFiles, data: Vec<u8> }` (one bit per reply, chunked), `Strings(Vec<(u64, StringEncoding, String)>)`, `SocketOwners(Vec<(u64, ProcessKey)>)`, `NetlinkDump(Vec<u8>)`. `HelperError::{IdentityChanged, PermissionDenied, NoSuchProcess, NotAllowed, Partial { done, total }, Os(i32), TooLarge}`. `NotAllowed` carries no text: a quoted rule after `Err(NotAllowed)` in this bead names the check for code comments and test names and is never sent. `HELPER_PROTO_VERSION = 1`; frames are at most 64 KiB; the 4 MiB cap is per reply message for the streamed requests (`ScanStrings`, `NetnsSockDiagDump`) and total for the rest (R-157). Handlers return a `HelperReplyBody`; `dispatch` (E29-A1) wraps each one in a `HelperReply` with the frame's `seq` and the `last` flag.

title: E29-003 Helper cgroup freeze, thaw and kill for any user
description:
## Context
The helper's cgroup operations: `FreezeGroup`, `ThawGroup` and `KillGroup` for any user's cgroup under `/sys/fs/cgroup` (ADR-006 allowlist). ## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-helper/src/ops.rs`, `pub fn run_cgroup_op(req: &HelperRequest) -> HelperReplyBody` for `FreezeGroup(cg)`, `ThawGroup(cg)`, `KillGroup(cg)`:

  1. `cg.rel_path` is non-empty, at most 4096 bytes, relative (no leading `/`), has no NUL, and no component equal to `.` or `..` or empty ("bad cgroup path").
  2. The first component is `user.slice` or `system.slice` ("cgroup outside user.slice and system.slice").
  3. The last component ends in `.scope` or `.service` ("not a scope or service").
  4. Open each component with `openat(dirfd, name, O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC)` starting from a dirfd on `/sys/fs/cgroup`, never by joined path string; `fstat` the final dirfd: `st_ino == cg.cgroup_id`, else `Err(IdentityChanged)`.
  5. The helper's own cgroup (from `/proc/self/cgroup`) and the cgroup of the helper's parent process (tasklens, `getppid()`) are not equal to or inside the target ("would affect tasklens"). `init.scope` is refused ("init.scope").
- Writes through the validated dirfd with the E07-A2 tl-ops write helpers that take a dirfd (R-168 E29-OI-8; `cgroup.freeze` "1" or "0", `cgroup.kill` "1"), and for `FreezeGroup` the same `cgroup.events` wait as the engine (poll `frozen 1` every 50 ms for up to 2 s; not frozen in time replies `Err(Os(EINPROGRESS = 115))`, which the engine maps to `OutcomeUnknown("freeze still in progress")`).
- `run_process_op` from E29-002 still refuses these kinds; `dispatch` (E29-A1) calls `run_cgroup_op` for them.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a `systemd-run --user --scope sleep 60` scope and its captured `HelperCgroup` **When** `FreezeGroup` runs as the same user **Then** the reply is `Ok` and `cgroup.events` shows `frozen 1`; `ThawGroup` then gives `Ok` and `frozen 0`.
- **Given** `rel_path` `user.slice/../system.slice/x.service` **When** run **Then** `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "bad cgroup path").
- **Given** `rel_path` `/user.slice/a.scope` **When** run **Then** `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "bad cgroup path").
- **Given** `rel_path` `machine.slice/x.scope` **When** run **Then** `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "cgroup outside user.slice and system.slice").
- **Given** `rel_path` `user.slice/user-1000.slice` **When** run **Then** `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "not a scope or service").
- **Given** a valid path with a different `cgroup_id` **When** run **Then** `Err(IdentityChanged)` and nothing is written.
- **Given** the cgroup that contains the test process itself **When** `KillGroup` runs **Then** `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "would affect tasklens").
- **Given** a symlink component (test with a tmpfs fake root is not possible for cgroupfs; check through the `O_NOFOLLOW` unit of the open loop on a temp dir tree) **When** the loop meets it **Then** it fails with `bad cgroup path`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-helper/src/ops.rs`: add `run_cgroup_op` and the validator `fn validate_cgroup(cg: &HelperCgroup, root: BorrowedFd) -> Result<OwnedFd, HelperError>`.

## Tests
- `ops.rs::tests::cgroup_path_rules` (pure checks 1 to 3 on 8 strings; security regression).
- `ops.rs::tests::cgroup_open_loop_no_follow` (the per-component open loop against a temp directory tree with a symlink; security regression).
- `ops.rs::tests::cgroup_inode_mismatch` (real cgroupfs, own scope).
- `ops.rs::tests::cgroup_self_refused` (security regression).
- `crates/tl-helper/tests/real_helper_root.rs::freeze_other_users_scope` (`#[ignore]`, root only, written in E29-012).

- Errors: as listed.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: log the cgroup leaf name and result at `debug` only.
- Security: root writes to cgroupfs; path handling is by dirfd only.

## Notes
- The validation rule for other uids is settled (R-168 E29-OI-8).
- E07 exposes the cgroup write helpers that take a validated dirfd (R-168 E29-OI-8); use them and do not copy write code into tl-helper. `HelperCgroup { rel_path, cgroup_id }` is the as2.36 type.
- Protocol names are those of `tl-model/src/helper_proto.rs` (E03-070, as2.36, the type owner; R-157). title: E29-004 Helper ReadProcessFiles
description:
## Context
`ReadProcessFiles { key, files }` lets the engine read root-only `/proc/<pid>` files of other users' processes, so Restricted cells and Properties tabs fill in once the helper runs (PROC-076, R-004, R-098). The set is fixed: `io`, `fd_list`, `fdinfo`, `environ`, `maps`, `smaps`, `smaps_rollup`, `ns`, `cwd`, `exe`, `status`, `root` (`root` added by R-157 for PROC-078 and PROC-096). There is no path argument. Sources: ADR-006, R-004, R-098, PROC-078 to PROC-084, PROC-096, ADR-015 (privacy).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-helper/src/files.rs` (new; add `mod files;` to `main.rs`):
- `pub fn read_process_files(key: ProcessKey, files: ProcFiles, boot: BootId) -> Vec<HelperReplyBody>`: the reply bodies in send order; `dispatch` (E29-A1) sets `last: true` on the final one.
- Steps: `tl_ops::process::open_verified(key, boot)` (keeps the pidfd open for the whole call, so `/proc/<pid>` cannot be reused); open `/proc/<pid>` as a dirfd with `O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC`; read each requested entry relative to that dirfd with `openat`, never by joined path:
  - `io`, `environ`, `maps`, `smaps`, `smaps_rollup`, `status`: file bytes.
  - `cwd`, `exe`, `root`: `readlinkat` bytes.
  - `fd_list`: `readdir` of `fd/`, then `readlinkat` of each entry; the data is the postcard encoding of `Vec<(u32 /* fd */, Vec<u8> /* target */)>` sorted by fd.
  - `fdinfo`: for each fd in `fd/`, the bytes of `fdinfo/<fd>`; the data is the postcard encoding of `Vec<(u32, Vec<u8>)>` sorted by fd.
  - `ns`: `readlinkat` of `ns/{cgroup,ipc,mnt,net,pid,pid_for_children,time,time_for_children,user,uts}`; the data is the postcard encoding of `Vec<(String /* name */, Vec<u8> /* target */)>`, missing names skipped.
- Reply shape (as2.36 `File { file, data }`, R-157): each requested file, in ascending bit order (`IO` first, `ROOT` last), gives either one or more `File { file: <its one bit>, data }` bodies (data split at 60 KiB so each reply fits one 64 KiB frame; an empty file gives one body with empty `data`) or exactly one `Err(Os(errno))` body (EACCES 13, ENOENT 2, ESRCH 3 as read). The engine gives an `Err(Os(_))` body to the next requested file in bit order. One failing file never fails the others.
- Size: the reply's total payload is at most 4 MiB (4_194_304 bytes) per request (ADR-006). Files are read in ascending bit order; once the running total would pass 4_194_304 minus 4096 bytes of headroom, that file and every later one get `Err(Os(27))` (EFBIG). A single read is capped at the remaining budget, never more.
- All bodies are built in memory first (at most 4 MiB). After the reads, check the pidfd once more (poll timeout 0); readable (exited) replaces the whole answer with one `Err(NoSuchProcess)` body, so no data from a different process is ever sent. Whole-request failures are only `Err(IdentityChanged)` and `Err(NoSuchProcess)`, each as the only body; per-file failures are always `Err(Os(_))`.
- The reply is sent through the `tl_model::wire` multi-frame writer (64 KiB frames), done by `dispatch` (E29-A1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a child of the test with a known environment `TL_TEST=1` **When** `read_process_files(key, ENVIRON | CWD | EXE | STATUS)` runs **Then** the `File { file: ENVIRON }` data contains `TL_TEST=1`, the `CWD` data is the child's working directory, the `EXE` data is the child's binary, and the `STATUS` data starts with `Name:`.
- **Given** the child holds a file open on fd 7 **When** `FD_LIST | FDINFO` is requested **Then** the decoded `FD_LIST` list has fd 7 with its target path and the decoded `FDINFO` entry for 7 contains `pos:`.
- **Given** a child of the test **When** `ROOT` is requested **Then** one `File { file: ROOT }` body arrives with data `/` (R-157).
- **Given** a stale `start_ticks` **When** called **Then** the reply is `Err(IdentityChanged)` and no file was opened.
- **Given** a child that exits during the call (test hook: a child that exits after 50 ms and a read of `smaps` of a large mapping) **When** the post-check sees the pidfd readable **Then** the reply is `Err(NoSuchProcess)`.
- **Given** `MAPS | SMAPS` where `smaps` is larger than the remaining budget **When** called **Then** `maps` arrives as `File` bodies, `smaps` is one `Err(Os(27))` body, and the encoded reply is at most 4_194_304 bytes.
- **Given** a request where the target is PID 1 and `ENVIRON` **When** run as an ordinary user (the test) **Then** the `ENVIRON` slot is one `Err(Os(13))` body (EACCES) and the other files still return.

## Files
- `crates/tl-helper/src/files.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/main.rs`: add `mod files;`.

## Tests
- `files.rs::tests::reads_own_child_files`
- `files.rs::tests::fd_list_and_fdinfo`
- `files.rs::tests::reads_root_link` (`ROOT`, R-157)
- `files.rs::tests::bit_order_and_error_slots`: `IO | ENVIRON | ROOT` on PID 1 as an ordinary user gives bodies in bit order with `Err(Os(13))` in the `ENVIRON` slot.
- `files.rs::tests::stale_key_rejected` (security regression)
- `files.rs::tests::exit_during_read_discards_data` (security regression)
- `files.rs::tests::budget_caps_reply_at_4_mib`
- `files.rs::tests::one_file_error_keeps_others`

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: per-file errno; whole-reply `IdentityChanged` or `NoSuchProcess`.
- Validity: the engine maps a per-file `Err(Os(13))` (EACCES) to `Restricted` and `Err(Os(2))` or `Err(Os(3))` (ENOENT, ESRCH) to `Missing`.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one dirfd per call; buffers sized from `fstat` where the file reports a size, else grown up to the budget.
- Privacy: environment, command lines, paths and maps are never logged at any level (ADR-015). Log only `pid`, the requested set and the result code at `debug`.
- Security: no path argument; every open is relative to the verified process's dirfd.

## Notes
- `root` (`ProcFiles::ROOT = 1 << 11`, the `/proc/<pid>/root` link) is in the R-004 set for PROC-078 and PROC-096 (R-157).
- The `File` encoding above (bit order, one `Err(Os(_))` per failed file, postcard lists for `FD_LIST`, `FDINFO` and `NS`) is how this bead fits per-file results into the as2.36 `File { file, data }` body. The engine side reads it the same way (E29-015, E29-016, E29-017).
- Protocol names are those of `tl-model/src/helper_proto.rs` (E03-070, as2.36, the type owner; R-157). Requests travel as `HelperFrame { seq: u32, request: HelperRequest }` (the engine picks `seq`) and replies as `HelperReply { seq: u32, last: bool, body: HelperReplyBody }` (the helper echoes `seq`; `last: true` marks the final reply of a request). `HelperRequest` has 17 variants: `Hello { proto }`, `Signal { target, signal }`, `SetNice { target, nice }`, `SetSched { target, policy, rt_prio }`, `SetAffinity { target, set }`, `SetIoPriority { key, prio }`, `FreezeGroup(HelperCgroup)`, `ThawGroup(HelperCgroup)`, `KillGroup(HelperCgroup)`, `ReadProcessFiles { key, files: ProcFiles }`, `ScanStrings { key, opts }`, `Dump { key, mode }` (the output fd travels as `SCM_RIGHTS` ancillary data with this frame, R-145 item 3), `ResolveSocketInodes { inodes }`, `SockDestroy { family, proto, four_tuple, cookie }`, `WriteServiceDropIn { unit, keys: Vec<(DropInKey, String)> }`, `NetnsSockDiagDump { netns_ino }`, `CancelScan { seq: u32 }`; `target` is `HelperTarget::{Process(ProcessKey), Thread { process: ProcessKey, tid: u32 }}`. `HelperReplyBody`: `Hello { proto }`, `Ok`, `Err(HelperError)`, `File { file: ProcFiles, data: Vec<u8> }` (one bit per reply, chunked), `Strings(Vec<(u64, StringEncoding, String)>)`, `SocketOwners(Vec<(u64, ProcessKey)>)`, `NetlinkDump(Vec<u8>)`. `HelperError::{IdentityChanged, PermissionDenied, NoSuchProcess, NotAllowed, Partial { done, total }, Os(i32), TooLarge}`. `NotAllowed` carries no text: a quoted rule after `Err(NotAllowed)` in this bead names the check for code comments and test names and is never sent. `HELPER_PROTO_VERSION = 1`; frames are at most 64 KiB; the 4 MiB cap is per reply message for the streamed requests (`ScanStrings`, `NetnsSockDiagDump`) and total for the rest (R-157). Handlers return a `HelperReplyBody`; `dispatch` (E29-A1) wraps each one in a `HelperReply` with the frame's `seq` and the `last` flag.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-helper`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E29-005 Helper ScanStrings streaming
description:
## Context
`ScanStrings { key, opts }` runs the Strings tab scan as root and streams result batches (PROC-084, R-004), because with `ptrace_scope = 1` reading another process's memory needs CAP_SYS_PTRACE. The scanner already exists in `tl-collect` (E05-A3, `src/proc/strings.rs`: `StringScanner`, and `ProcMem`, which reads `/proc/<pid>/mem` with `pread`, R-144 item 2). tl-helper may depend on tl-collect and reuses it (R-142 item 14, R-157). PROC-084's 256 MiB result limit fits because the 4 MiB cap applies to each reply message of a streamed request, not to the whole stream (R-157).

## Deliverable
Settled (R-142 item 14, R-157): ADR-001 row `tl-helper: tl-model, tl-ops, tl-collect`; a streamed request's 4 MiB cap applies to each reply message, not the whole stream.
- `crates/tl-helper/Cargo.toml`: add `tl-collect = { workspace = true }`.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/files.rs`: `pub fn scan_strings(key: ProcessKey, opts: &StringScanOpts, boot: BootId, out: &mut dyn FnMut(HelperReplyBody, bool /* last */) -> std::io::Result<()>, cancel: &mut dyn FnMut() -> bool) -> std::io::Result<()>`.
  - `open_verified(key, boot)` first; a stale key sends `Err(IdentityChanged)` as the last reply and stops.
  - Runs tl-collect's `StringScanner` over `ProcMem` (`pread` on `/proc/<pid>/mem` through `rustix::fs::pread`, R-144 item 2) with `opts` (minimum length 4 to 64, default 4; encodings ASCII, UTF-8, UTF-16LE; "Include file-backed mappings" off by default; regions from `maps`: readable, private anonymous plus heap and stack, file-backed only with the option, skipping `[vvar]`, `[vsyscall]` and device mappings; 1 MiB read chunks).
  - Emits `Strings(batch)` with `last: false` (`batch: Vec<(u64 /* address */, StringEncoding, String)>`, as2.36) whenever the batch reaches 2,000 strings or 48 KiB of encoded text, whichever first, so one batch fits one 64 KiB frame. The body has no progress or count field; the engine counts found strings from the batches.
  - Between chunks calls `cancel()`; true ends the scan with a final empty `Strings(vec![])` with `last: true`. A normal end sends the remaining batch (possibly empty) with `last: true`.
  - Stops at 1,000,000 strings or 256 MiB of text with a final `Err(TooLarge)` with `last: true` (the UI shows "String scan stopped: not enough memory."); target exit mid-scan gives a final `Err(NoSuchProcess)`; a read failure gives a final `Err(Os(errno))`.
  - Kernel threads (flag from `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 9 `PF_KTHREAD`): `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "kernel thread").
- `CancelScan` handling (R-157): `pub fn is_cancel_for(frame: &HelperFrame, scan_seq: u32) -> bool` in `files.rs` is true only for `HelperRequest::CancelScan { seq }` with `seq == scan_seq` (the `seq` of the running `ScanStrings` frame). `dispatch` (E29-A1) builds `cancel` from it: between chunks it polls stdin with timeout 0 and reads any waiting frame. A matching `CancelScan` cancels the scan. After the scan's final reply, `dispatch` answers the `CancelScan` frame itself with one `Ok` reply (`last: true`) under that frame's own `seq`; a `CancelScan` that names no running scan gets the same single `Ok`. Any other request read during a scan is a protocol error (exit 3, as in E29-A1), because the engine sends one request at a time (ADR-007).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a child that holds the ASCII string `tasklens-marker-1234` and the UTF-16LE string `wine-marker` in heap memory **When** `scan_strings` runs with defaults **Then** both strings arrive in some batch and the final message has `last: true`.
- **Given** `min_len = 30` **When** the same scan runs **Then** neither marker is reported.
- **Given** a `cancel` that returns true after the first chunk **When** run **Then** the last reply is an empty `Strings` with `last: true` and no further batches follow.
- **Given** a stale key **When** run **Then** the only message is `Err(IdentityChanged)` (security regression).
- **Given** every emitted batch **When** encoded with postcard **Then** it is at most 65_536 bytes.
- **Given** a scan limit lowered to 10 strings (test constructor) and a child with 50 marker strings **When** run **Then** the last reply is `Err(TooLarge)` with `last: true`.
- **Given** a running scan with frame `seq = 7` **When** `is_cancel_for` sees `CancelScan { seq: 7 }`, `CancelScan { seq: 8 }` and `Signal { .. }` **Then** it returns true, false and false (R-157).

## Files
- `crates/tl-helper/Cargo.toml`: add the tl-collect line.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/files.rs`: add `scan_strings`.

## Tests
- `files.rs::tests::scan_finds_ascii_and_utf16`
- `files.rs::tests::scan_min_len_filters`
- `files.rs::tests::scan_cancel_stops`
- `files.rs::tests::scan_stale_key_rejected` (security regression)
- `files.rs::tests::scan_batches_fit_frame`
- `files.rs::tests::scan_limit_too_large`
- `files.rs::tests::cancel_scan_matches_seq` (R-157)

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: "Failed to read process memory." and "Strings unavailable for this process." are the UI's texts for `Err(Os(_))` and for `Err(NotAllowed)` on a kernel thread; "String scan stopped: not enough memory." is the text for `Err(TooLarge)`.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: batch buffers reused; no per-string allocation beyond the string itself.
- Privacy: found strings are never logged at any level.
- Security: memory of other users' processes leaves the helper only to the engine that asked for it.

## Notes
- Settled: R-142 item 14 (tl-collect in the tl-helper row), R-144 item 2 (`pread` on `/proc/<pid>/mem`), R-157 (per-message cap, `CancelScan { seq }`). Field names of `StringScanOpts` and the `Strings` body are as2.36's.
- `cargo xtask check-deps` must pass with the ADR-001 row `tl-helper: tl-model, tl-ops, tl-collect` (R-142 item 14).
- Protocol names are those of `tl-model/src/helper_proto.rs` (E03-070, as2.36, the type owner; R-157). Handlers return a `HelperReplyBody`; `dispatch` (E29-A1) wraps each one in a `HelperReply` with the frame's `seq` and the `last` flag.

title: E29-006 Helper Dump into a passed fd
description:
## Context
`Dump { key, mode }` writes a core file of another user's (or a non-child) process with `/usr/bin/gdb` by fixed path, running `gcore` as a batch command (R-145 item 1), into a file descriptor that tasklens opened, so the core belongs to the user (PROC-075, R-004). An fd cannot travel over a pipe, so the helper's stdin and stdout are one end of a Unix `socketpair` and the engine passes the fd as `SCM_RIGHTS` ancillary data on the `Dump` frame; `Dump` itself has no fd field (R-145 item 3). This bead receives that fd and runs `tl_ops::dump::dump_to_fd` as root (R-145 item 4). Sources: ADR-006, R-004, PROC-075.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-helper/src/ops.rs`: `pub fn run_dump(key: ProcessKey, mode: DumpMode, out_fd: OwnedFd, boot: BootId) -> HelperReplyBody`:
  - `open_verified(key, boot)`; stale gives `Err(IdentityChanged)`.
  - `fstat(out_fd)` must be a regular file (`S_IFREG`) with size 0, and `fcntl(F_GETFL)` must include write access; else `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "bad dump fd").
  - Calls `tl_ops::dump::dump_to_fd(key, boot, mode, out_fd)` (E07-A3, iuz.15; R-145 items 1 and 4): `/usr/bin/gdb` by fixed path with the arguments `--nx --nh --batch -p <pid> -ex "gcore /proc/<helper pid>/fd/<n>"`, environment cleared except `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` and `LC_ALL=C`, stdio on `/dev/null`; Mini uses the process's own `coredump_filter`, Full writes `0x1ff` for the duration and restores the old value afterwards. `<helper pid>` is the helper's own pid, because the received fd is in the helper's fd table. `tl_ops::dump::dump_available()` false (`/usr/bin/gdb` or `/usr/bin/gcore` missing) gives `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "gdb not installed") without running anything.
  - Success `Ok`; a gdb non-zero exit gives `Err(Os(EIO = 5))`; other `OpsError` values map as in E29-002.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/main.rs` (frame reader, owned by this epic): when reading a request frame from fd 0, use `rustix::net::recvmsg` with a `RecvAncillaryBuffer` sized for one fd. A `Dump` request must carry exactly one fd; any other request carrying an fd, or a `Dump` with zero or two fds, is answered `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "unexpected fd") and every received fd is closed. Received fds always get `O_CLOEXEC` (`RecvFlags::CMSG_CLOEXEC`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a child `sleep 60` of the test and an empty temp file opened write-only **When** `run_dump(key, Mini, fd)` runs (as the same user, `ptrace_scope` allowing a child) **Then** the reply is `Ok` and the file starts with the ELF magic `\x7fELF`.
- **Given** `mode = Full` **When** the dump finishes **Then** the child's `coredump_filter` equals its value before the call.
- **Given** an fd opened read-only **When** called **Then** `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "bad dump fd") and gdb is not run.
- **Given** an fd for a directory **When** called **Then** `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "bad dump fd").
- **Given** a `Signal` request frame that carries an fd **When** the frame reader handles it **Then** the reply is `Err(NotAllowed)` (rule "unexpected fd") and the fd is closed (checked by `fcntl` on the sender's duplicate count through `/proc/self/fd` of the helper in-process test).
- **Given** a stale key **When** called **Then** `Err(IdentityChanged)` (security regression).

## Files
- `crates/tl-helper/src/ops.rs`: add `run_dump`.
- `crates/tl-helper/src/main.rs`: ancillary fd receive in the frame reader.

## Tests
- `ops.rs::tests::dump_child_writes_elf` (skips with a message when `tl_ops::dump::dump_available()` is false)
- `ops.rs::tests::dump_restores_coredump_filter`
- `ops.rs::tests::dump_rejects_bad_fd` (security regression)
- `ops.rs::tests::dump_stale_key` (security regression)
- `main.rs::tests::unexpected_fd_closed` (security regression; socketpair in-process)

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: "Creating a dump needs administrator rights" is the UI's text when no helper is available; this bead returns only the codes above.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: the call blocks for the whole dump; the engine's deadline bounds the reply, not the work (ADR-006).
- Privacy: the dump path is never sent to the helper and never logged.
- Security: root writes only into an fd the user opened; gdb is run by fixed path with no shell (R-145 item 1).

## Notes
- Socketpair transport settled (R-145 item 3): R-003's "stdin and stdout" is a socketpair so a file descriptor can travel with the `Dump` request. The engine side (opening the file `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_CLOEXEC` mode 0600 and sending the fd) is E29-013 and E29-014.
- Protocol names are those of `tl-model/src/helper_proto.rs` (E03-070, as2.36, the type owner; R-157). Requests travel as `HelperFrame { seq: u32, request: HelperRequest }` (the engine picks `seq`) and replies as `HelperReply { seq: u32, last: bool, body: HelperReplyBody }` (the helper echoes `seq`; `last: true` marks the final reply of a request). `HelperRequest` has 17 variants: `Hello { proto }`, `Signal { target, signal }`, `SetNice { target, nice }`, `SetSched { target, policy, rt_prio }`, `SetAffinity { target, set }`, `SetIoPriority { key, prio }`, `FreezeGroup(HelperCgroup)`, `ThawGroup(HelperCgroup)`, `KillGroup(HelperCgroup)`, `ReadProcessFiles { key, files: ProcFiles }`, `ScanStrings { key, opts }`, `Dump { key, mode }` (the output fd travels as `SCM_RIGHTS` ancillary data with this frame, R-145 item 3), `ResolveSocketInodes { inodes }`, `SockDestroy { family, proto, four_tuple, cookie }`, `WriteServiceDropIn { unit, keys: Vec<(DropInKey, String)> }`, `NetnsSockDiagDump { netns_ino }`, `CancelScan { seq: u32 }`; `target` is `HelperTarget::{Process(ProcessKey), Thread { process: ProcessKey, tid: u32 }}`. `HelperReplyBody`: `Hello { proto }`, `Ok`, `Err(HelperError)`, `File { file: ProcFiles, data: Vec<u8> }` (one bit per reply, chunked), `Strings(Vec<(u64, StringEncoding, String)>)`, `SocketOwners(Vec<(u64, ProcessKey)>)`, `NetlinkDump(Vec<u8>)`. `HelperError::{IdentityChanged, PermissionDenied, NoSuchProcess, NotAllowed, Partial { done, total }, Os(i32), TooLarge}`. `NotAllowed` carries no text: a quoted rule after `Err(NotAllowed)` in this bead names the check for code comments and test names and is never sent. `HELPER_PROTO_VERSION = 1`; frames are at most 64 KiB; the 4 MiB cap is per reply message for the streamed requests (`ScanStrings`, `NetnsSockDiagDump`) and total for the rest (R-157). Handlers return a `HelperReplyBody`; `dispatch` (E29-A1) wraps each one in a `HelperReply` with the frame's `seq` and the `last` flag.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-helper`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
