title: E18 tl-ui: TlTreeTable, header, selection, cells, text cache, column picker
description: Epic E18 (ui-tree-table). Phases: P1 (P0 anchors). Estimated beads: 30. Scope, sources and file ownership: docs/plan/00-epics.md sections 1 and 2, key E18.

title: E18-A1 Generic tree table
description:
## Context
Anchor E18-A1 "Generic tree table". This bead finishes the A1 group: right-click target capture and the context menu, Shift+F10 and the Menu key, "Copy rows as table", and the integration test suite with the render counter and the text-cache hit rate. When it closes, `table/{tree_table,columns,selection,cells,actions}.rs`, `text_cache.rs` and the one-line header exist and are exported, and other epics (E22, E23, E24, E27, E28, E30, E32) can build tables on `TlTreeTable<D>`. Sources: ADR-009 (right-click selects then opens a menu bound to captured keys; Copy rows as table; verification list), UI-PRC-008 (right-click rows), UI-PRC-009 (Shift+F10 anchor point), UI-FND-022 (menu behaviour), ADR-015 "Exports and copy", UI-FND-026 (glyph copy texts), ADR-013 UI tests.

Closes the group: E18-001 Selection, E18-002 CellTextCache, E18-003 columns, E18-004 cells, E18-005 delegate trait, E18-006 body and one-line header, E18-007 actions and keymap, E18-008 scrolling and demand.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs`:
- `pub enum TreeTableEvent { CopiedRows { rows: usize }, CopyFailed }` and `impl EventEmitter<TreeTableEvent> for TlTreeTable<D>`; the owner page turns them into toasts ("Copied to clipboard" / "Failed to copy to clipboard", APP-044).
- Right-click on a row (`MouseButton::Right` on the row hitbox): if the row is not selected, `selection.right_click(id)` makes it the only selection; a selected row keeps the whole set; a group header changes no selection. Then capture `targets: SmallVec<[D::RowId; 8]>` = the selection in view order (`Selection::in_view_order`; for a group header: just its id) and `clicked_col` = the column under the pointer, call `delegate.context_menu(&targets, clicked_col, TlMenu::new(), window, cx)`, and open the returned menu at the pointer with the kit `PopupMenu` deferred anchored popup. The captured targets travel inside the menu's data actions, so a re-sort or new version before the click does not change them.
- `OpenContextMenu` (Shift+F10, Menu key): same capture for the current selection; the menu opens at the focus row's Name cell text start x and the row's bottom y (UI-PRC-009). No focus row: nothing.
- Opening a menu closes any tooltip; a click outside closes the menu and is consumed (it does not select a row) (UI-FND-022, handled by `TlMenu`).
- One context-menu handler on the table element, never one per row.
- `CopyRowsAsTable`: TSV text, first line the labels of the visible columns in order joined by `\t`, then one line per selected row in view order with each visible column's text joined by `\t`, lines joined by `\n`. Cell text = the cached display text; Name column = `NameCell.primary`; glyph cells copy `…`, `n/a`, `-`, `!`, and the word `Restricted` for Restricted (UI-FND-026, ADR-015). Group header rows are never in the selection, so never copied. Write with `cx.write_to_clipboard(ClipboardItem::new_string(text))`, then emit `CopiedRows { rows }`. No selection: nothing is copied and nothing is emitted.
- `CopyCell { col }` is not handled here (owner page).
- `pub fn scroll_handle(&self) -> UniformListScrollHandle`: returns a clone of the handle the body `uniform_list` tracks (the handle is `Rc`-backed, gpui `UniformListScrollHandle(pub Rc<RefCell<..>>)`), so scrolling through the clone moves this table. E22-A1 exposes it as `ProcessesPage::scroll_handle` for the E01 `table-2000` scene (R-160 OI-8, R-186).

`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_tree_table.rs` gains the integration suite (TestAppContext with the `VecDelegate` from E18-005 and the `FakeEngine` from E16-001 where a snapshot is needed).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** rows A, B, C and selection {A} **When** right-clicking C **Then** the selection is {C} and the menu builder receives targets [C].
- **Given** selection {A, C} **When** right-clicking C **Then** the selection stays {A, C} and targets are [A, C] in view order.
- **Given** a menu opened with targets [C] **When** a new version re-sorts the rows before an item is clicked **Then** the dispatched action still carries C.
- **Given** a group header **When** right-clicked **Then** the selection is unchanged and targets are [group id].
- **Given** focus row B **When** Shift+F10 **Then** the menu opens with its top-left at B's Name text start x and B's bottom edge y.
- **Given** selected rows B and C with columns Name, PID, CPU and C's CPU WarmingUp **When** Ctrl+Shift+C **Then** the clipboard holds `Name\tPID\tCPU\nB\t12\t3.4%\nC\t13\t…` and `CopiedRows { rows: 2 }` is emitted.
- **Given** a Restricted cell in the selection **When** copied as table **Then** the cell text is `Restricted`.
- **Given** 10 identical table versions **When** rendered each time **Then** the `CellTextCache` hit rate is above 95%.
- **Given** a snapshot change that does not touch the delegate's data **When** the owner does not call `on_new_version` **Then** `render_count` does not increase.
- **Given** a 2,000-row table **When** `scroll_handle().scroll_to_item_with_offset(1000, ScrollStrategy::Top, 0)` runs and the table renders **Then** the first visible row index is 1,000.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs`: right-click, `OpenContextMenu`, `CopyRowsAsTable`, `TreeTableEvent`, `scroll_handle`.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_tree_table.rs`: the tests below.

## Tests
- `ui_tree_table::right_click_selects_unselected_and_captures_targets`.
- `ui_tree_table::right_click_keeps_multi_selection`.
- `ui_tree_table::right_click_targets_survive_resort` (ADR-009, ADR-013).
- `ui_tree_table::group_header_right_click_no_selection_change`.
- `ui_tree_table::shift_f10_opens_at_focus_row`.
- `ui_tree_table::copy_rows_as_table_tsv_with_header`.
- `ui_tree_table::copy_rows_glyph_texts`.
- `ui_tree_table::tree_table_text_cache_hit_rate` (UI-PRC-001, ADR-009: above 95% over 10 identical versions).
- `ui_tree_table::selection_survives_resort_in_entity` (ADR-009 verification, through the entity).
- `ui_tree_table::render_counter_unchanged_without_new_version`.
- `ui_tree_table::scroll_handle_clone_scrolls_table`: the `scroll_handle` criterion (R-186).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: clipboard write failure emits `CopyFailed`.
- Validity: glyph copy texts per UI-FND-026.
- Accessibility: Shift+F10 and the Menu key open the same menu as right-click; menu items show key hints because they dispatch the bound Actions (`PopupMenu::action_context(table focus handle)`).
- Performance: the menu is built on open only; nothing per frame while closed.
- Privacy: copy uses the sanitized display text; command lines appear only if the owner shows a command-line column and the user selected the row (ADR-015).

## Notes
- This is the anchor bead; title stays "E18-A1 Generic tree table". Before closing, check that `table/mod.rs` exports `tree_table`, `columns`, `selection`, `cells`, `actions`, `header`, and `lib.rs` exports `table` and `text_cache`.
- `TlMenu` API from E16-009 (`components/menu.rs`); the row and header menus use `TlMenu::min_w(240)` in the process page (R-112), the owner sets it.
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <files>`. New files need `git add` first. Read `CLAUDE.md` first.
- Plan file: `docs/plan/b5-ui-foundation.md` (open items cited by number).
close_reason: 6838a6e, f0911f9. tree_table.rs: TreeTableEvent + EventEmitter; one right-press handler on the body (row and column from the pointer, right_click selection rule, group header target only); OpenContextMenu at focus row Name text start x and row bottom y; menu built via window.defer + TlMenu::build + open_context_menu_at (TlMenu has no public constructor, so the delegate runs in a deferred table update), targets captured as SmallVec in view order; CopyRowsAsTable TSV with copy_text glyph texts; scroll_handle() returns a clone. Chain edit: text_cache.rs CellTextCache::stats() for the hit-rate test. AC evidence (tests/ui_tree_table.rs, all pass with and without test-hooks): AC1 right_click_selects_unselected_and_captures_targets; AC2 right_click_keeps_multi_selection; AC3 right_click_targets_survive_resort (rows reversed with menu open, clicked item carries [3]); AC4 group_header_right_click_no_selection_change; AC5 shift_f10_opens_at_focus_row (origin (70, 84) = pad 20 + gap 6 + chevron 16 + gap 6 + icon 16 + gap 6; header 28 + 2 rows); AC6 copy_rows_as_table_tsv_with_header (exact string, CopiedRows{rows:2}, no selection: nothing); AC7 copy_rows_glyph_texts (Restricted, n/a, -, !, ellipsis, Stale value, group header skipped); AC8 tree_table_text_cache_hit_rate (>95% over 10 versions after the first fill, test-hooks); AC9 render_counter_unchanged_without_new_version (FakeEngine + SnapshotHub publish, hub seq 1, render_count unchanged; on_new_version renders); AC10 scroll_handle_clone_scrolls_table (first visible 1000). Also selection_survives_resort_in_entity. Known gap: CopyFailed is declared but never emitted, because gpui write_to_clipboard returns (). clippy -p tl-ui --all-targets -D warnings clean with and without test-hooks; fmt check clean; cargo test -p tl-ui --features test-hooks all pass.

title: E18-008 Scroll anchoring, keep-visible, jump and visible-range demand
description:
## Context
Scroll behaviour of every tree table: keep the top visible row in place when rows move (re-sort, new rows above, expand above), keep the keyboard focus row visible, centre a jump target, and report the visible identities (plus one viewport of overscan, at most 512) to the delegate for demand, only when the set changes. Sources: UI-PRC-010 (all rules), PROC-013, PROC-071 (jump target centred), ADR-009 "Visible demand", ADR-008 (`detail_keys` max 512), ADR-014 `table-2000` scroll scene.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs`:
- Fields: `visible_range: Range<usize>` (recorded in the `uniform_list` render closure), `anchor: Option<(D::RowId, usize /* rows from top */, Pixels /* sub-row offset */)>`, `last_wheel: Option<Instant>`, `thumb_dragging: bool`, `demand_hash: u64`, `demand_scheduled: bool`.
- `pub fn jump_to(&mut self, id: D::RowId, cx: &mut Context<Self>) -> bool`: if `row_index(id)` is `Some(ix)`: `scroll.scroll_to_item_strict(ix, ScrollStrategy::Center)` (gpui `uniform_list.rs:163`), select it (`selection.click(id)`), notify; returns false when the id is not in the view. Expanding the path is the delegate's job before calling.
- Anchoring: when `on_new_version` installs a new table version, if the previous top-most visible selectable row identity still exists, scroll so it keeps its previous y (`scroll_to_item_with_offset(ix, ScrollStrategy::Top, offset_rows)` keeping the sub-row pixel offset); otherwise keep the scroll top index. Skip anchoring while the scrollbar thumb is being dragged, within 200 ms after the last wheel event, and while `paused` is true (nothing moves during Ctrl-pause).
- Keep visible: after every keyboard focus move (E18-007 handlers), `scroll_to_item_with_offset(ix, ScrollStrategy::Nearest, 1)` so one extra row of margin stays between the focus row and the header or the bottom edge. Mouse selection never scrolls.
- Visible-range demand: the render closure stores `visible_range`; render schedules one `window.on_next_frame` per render (guarded by `demand_scheduled`) that computes the identities of `visible_range` widened by one viewport above and below, capped at 512 ids (centred on the visible range when the cap bites), hashes the sorted ids into a 64-bit FxHash, and calls `delegate.on_visible_range(&ids)` only when the hash differs from `demand_hash`. It runs after every table version even when the range did not change (ADR-009).
- No header shadow when scrolled (the 1 px `divider` under the header is already there).
- Scrollbar drag is not frame-capped by the table (kit `Scrollbar.max_fps` left at default).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** row X at the top of the viewport **When** a new version moves X 40 rows down (re-sort) **Then** after render X is still the top row at the same y.
- **Given** a wheel event 100 ms ago **When** a new version arrives **Then** the scroll position index is unchanged and no anchoring happens.
- **Given** `paused == true` **When** a new version arrives **Then** nothing scrolls.
- **Given** the focus row on the last fully visible line **When** Down is pressed **Then** the list scrolls so one extra row is visible below the focus row.
- **Given** a row 900 rows down **When** `jump_to(id)` **Then** that row is selected and its centre is within half a row of the viewport centre.
- **Given** 2,000 rows, 30 visible **When** the frame after render runs **Then** `on_visible_range` receives 90 ids (30 + 30 above + 30 below).
- **Given** a viewport of 400 rows **When** demand is computed **Then** at most 512 ids are sent.
- **Given** an unchanged id set **When** a new frame or a new version with the same visible ids runs **Then** `on_visible_range` is not called again.
- **Given** a re-sort that changes which ids are visible while the range stays 0..30 **When** the version installs **Then** `on_visible_range` is called with the new ids.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs`: scrolling, anchoring, `jump_to`, demand.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_tree_table.rs`: tests below.

## Tests
- `ui_tree_table::scroll_anchor_keeps_top_row_on_resort` (UI-PRC-010).
- `ui_tree_table::scroll_anchor_skipped_during_wheel`.
- `ui_tree_table::no_scroll_while_paused`.
- `ui_tree_table::focus_move_scrolls_nearest_with_margin`.
- `ui_tree_table::jump_target_centres_row`.
- `ui_tree_table::visible_demand_capped_512_and_sent_on_change_only`.
- `ui_tree_table::tree_table_reports_visible_demand` (UI-PRC-001: range ± one viewport).
- `ui_tree_table::demand_resent_after_resort_with_same_range`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: keyboard moves always keep the focus row visible.
- Performance: anchoring is one hash lookup per version; the demand hash is O(512) per frame (about 10 µs at 1,200 px/s) and the id list is sent only on change; the id buffer is a reused `Vec`.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- The delegate forwards the ids to `DemandAggregator` (E16-004) as its `detail_keys` contribution; the table itself never touches demand.
- Use the test clock (`cx.executor().advance_clock`) for the 200 ms wheel window.
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <files>`. New files need `git add` first. Read `CLAUDE.md` first.
- Plan file: `docs/plan/b5-ui-foundation.md` (open items cited by number).

Commit b8d95f4

title: E18-009 Two-line header: totals, sort arrows, sort click
description:
## Context
The two-line header used by the process, history and system tables: line 1 is the column label with the sort arrow, line 2 the system total (right-aligned, secondary colour). Clicking anywhere on a sortable header cell sorts by that column. Sources: UI-PRC-005 (anatomy, states, sort cycle, tooltips), PROC-038 (totals), PROC-047 (sort gestures), ADR-009 "Header", UI-FND-003 (header name `t_sm`/`t_base` note), UI-FND-051 (numbers never cut), D-004 (Memory tooltip text supplied by the owner).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/table/header.rs` (`TlTreeTableHeader`) gains the two-line mode:
- Height `header_h` 44 when `delegate.header_lines() == Two`, 28 for `One`; background `header`; bottom border 1 px `divider`.
- Line 1 (y 4..22): label `t_base` 13 weight 500 `text_primary`, aligned like the column (Left for Text and Path, Right for Numeric), padding 8, end ellipsis. The active sort column shows Lucide `arrow-up` (ascending) or `arrow-down` (descending), 12 px, `text_primary`, after a 2 px (`sp1`) gap, inside the 12 px reservation of PROC-023. On a right-aligned column the arrow sits at the right edge and the label moves left by 14.
- Line 2 (y 22..40): `delegate.header_total(col, &mut out)`; `false` leaves the line empty. Text `t_base` regular `text_secondary`, always right-aligned (also on the left-aligned Name column there is no line 2 because the owner returns false), formatted through `CellTextCache` with a header row key, validity glyphs as in cells (`…`, `n/a`, lock, `-`, `!`). Never cut: numbers clip at most (UI-FND-051).
- Column boundary lines (1 px `divider`) at all times, at the same x offsets as the body; translated by the shared `x_offset`.
- Hitboxes: one per header cell (`window.insert_hitbox`, gpui `window.rs:5109`). States: hover fills the cell `row_hover`; pressed fills `row_selected` at 50% alpha; unsortable columns (`ColumnSpec.sortable == false`) get no hover fill, no arrow, default cursor, and the tooltip "Only measured for visible rows".
- Tooltip (500 ms) per cell: `ColumnSpec.tooltip` when `Some`; else the picker full name when it differs from the label (for example `Working set private - "Memory"` style, from `full_name`); else none.
- Click on a sortable cell (release without a drag of more than 4 px): dispatch `SortByColumn { id }`. The table handles `SortByColumn` by calling `delegate.on_sort(id)`; the delegate computes the new `SortSpec` with `SortSpec::next_for` (E18-003): first click descending for Numeric, ascending for Text and Path, each further click flips.
- Painting: one `canvas` for fills, boundaries and arrows (`paint_quad`, `paint_svg`) plus one text `div` per line per visible column; at most 2 shaped lines per visible column; texts re-shape only when the cached text changes.
- The header is not focusable; keyboard sorting goes through the header menu and View > Columns.

- **Given** column `cpu` (Numeric) not sorted **When** its header cell is clicked **Then** `on_sort(cpu)` runs and the delegate's next sort is cpu descending; clicking again gives ascending.
- **Given** column `user` (Text) **When** clicked first **Then** the sort is user ascending.

- **Given** a total with validity Unsupported **When** rendered **Then** line 2 shows `n/a`.

title: E18-010 Column resize and fit
description:
## Context
Column resizing by dragging a header boundary, in the two modes of `tables.column_resize` (one key for every table, R-075), double-click to fit one column, and "Resize columns to fit content" for all columns. Widths persist through `delegate.on_columns_changed` on release. Sources: UI-PRC-005 (resize handle, clamp, modes, double-click), UI-PRC-006 (`ResizeColumnsToFit` measurement scope), PROC-025, PROC-023 (minimums), R-075, canonical table (a) `tables.column_resize = "proportional"` (`proportional | last_column`), UI-FND-003 (cursor `col-resize` only over a header edge).

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/columns.rs`:
```rust
/// Drag of the right boundary of `col` to `new_width` (logical px at 100%).
pub fn resize(layout: &mut ColumnLayout, col: ColumnId, new_width: Pixels, mode: ColumnResizeMode,
              viewport: Pixels, mins: &FxHashMap<ColumnId, Pixels>);
```
  - The new width is clamped to the column's minimum (`min_width`, E18-003: template + 16, + 12 on the sort column; text columns 60).
  - `Proportional`: the dragged boundary moves; the visible columns to its right share the remaining width (viewport minus the widths left of and including the dragged column) in proportion to their current widths, each clamped to its minimum; when the minimums do not fit, they sit at their minimums and the table overflows horizontally.
  - `LastColumn`: only the dragged column and the last visible column change; the last column takes the difference, clamped to its minimum.
  - When the dragged column is the last visible column, only it changes in both modes.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/header.rs`:
  - Resize hit band: 8 px wide (4 each side) centred on each column boundary and after the last column, full header height; cursor `CursorStyle::ResizeColumn` over it; the boundary line turns `accent` while dragging (else 1 px `divider`).
  - Drag: live width change each mouse move (layout `rebuild`, table notify); release calls `delegate.on_columns_changed(&layout)` once.
  - Double-click on a boundary: fit that column (rule below) and call `on_columns_changed`.
  - `TlTreeTable::set_resize_mode(&mut self, mode: ColumnResizeMode)`: the owner passes the current `tables.column_resize` value (the table reads no settings itself).
- Fit rule (`ResizeColumnsToFit { table }` for every visible column, double-click for one): width = max(minimum, widest text of the column + 16, header label width + 16 + 12), measured over the currently visible rows plus the texts still in `CellTextCache` from the last 3 table versions (never a full pass over all rows), with the table font at the current scale and `tnum` for numeric columns. The table handles `ResizeColumnsToFit` itself and then calls `on_columns_changed`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a Numeric column with minimum 63 **When** dragged to 20 **Then** its width is 63.
- **Given** a Text column **When** dragged to 30 **Then** its width is 60.
- **Given** columns [name 200, a 100, b 100] in a 400 px viewport, Proportional **When** name is dragged to 240 **Then** a and b become 80 each.
- **Given** the same layout in LastColumn mode **When** name is dragged to 240 **Then** a stays 100 and b becomes 60.
- **Given** a drag over 10 mouse moves **When** released **Then** `on_columns_changed` was called exactly once.
- **Given** a column whose widest visible text is 150 px **When** its boundary is double-clicked **Then** its width is max(minimum, 166, label + 28).
- **Given** `ResizeColumnsToFit` **When** dispatched **Then** every visible column is fitted and no column is below its minimum.
- **Given** the pointer over a boundary band **When** hovering **Then** the cursor is the column-resize cursor; elsewhere the arrow.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/columns.rs`: `resize`, fit helper.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/header.rs`: hit bands, drag, double-click.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs`: `set_resize_mode`, `ResizeColumnsToFit` handler.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_columns.rs`: tests below.

## Tests
- `columns::tests::resize_clamps_to_template_minimum` (UI-PRC-005).
- `columns::tests::resize_proportional_vs_last_column`.
- `columns::tests::resize_last_visible_column_only_changes_itself`.
- `ui_columns::drag_persists_once_on_release`.
- `ui_columns::double_click_boundary_fits_one_column`.
- `ui_columns::fit_columns_never_below_minimum` (UI-PRC-006).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: keyboard users fit columns through the header menu or View > Columns; dragging is mouse only (UI-PRC-005).
- Performance: a drag rebuilds offsets once per mouse move; fitting measures through `TextMetricsCache` and the cached texts only.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- Widths are stored at 100% scale in `ColumnLayout.widths`; convert the dragged pixel width by dividing by `ui_scale`.
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <files>`. New files need `git add` first. Read `CLAUDE.md` first.
- Plan file: `docs/plan/b5-ui-foundation.md` (open items cited by number).

title: E18-011 Column reorder drag
description:
## Context
Column reordering by dragging a header cell. Name is fixed first: it cannot be dragged and nothing can be dropped before it. The new order persists through `on_columns_changed`. Sources: UI-PRC-005 (reorder drag, ghost, insertion line, 4 px threshold, Esc cancels, Name fixed), PROC-025, PROC-022 (Name always first and visible).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/table/header.rs`:
- Pressing on a header cell (not on a resize band) and moving more than 4 px starts a reorder drag; up to 4 px it is a click (sort, E18-009).
- While dragging: a ghost of the cell follows the pointer (fill `header` at 85% opacity, the label, 1 px `divider` border, radius `r_sm` 4 × ui_scale); a 2 px `accent` insertion line spans the header and body height at the nearest column boundary to the pointer. The insertion line never shows before Name.
- Drop: `ColumnLayout::move_column(id, before)` (E18-003), `rebuild`, `delegate.on_columns_changed(&layout)` once.
- Esc during a drag cancels it with no change (handled on the table root while `header_state` is dragging, before the global Esc chain).
- Name (`ColumnSpec.hideable == false`) does not start a drag.
- Drag state lives in `HeaderState` on the table entity (or `with_element_state`), not in the delegate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** order [name, user, pid, cpu] **When** cpu is dragged and dropped between name and user **Then** order is [name, cpu, user, pid] and `on_columns_changed` runs once.
- **Given** a press on pid moving 3 px **When** released **Then** it is a click (sort), not a reorder.
- **Given** a drag of user to the left edge before name **When** dropped **Then** user lands right after name; the insertion line never appeared before name.
- **Given** a press on name **When** moved 50 px **Then** no drag starts.
- **Given** a drag in progress **When** Esc is pressed **Then** the order is unchanged and `on_columns_changed` is not called.
- **Given** a drag in progress **When** rendered **Then** the ghost has `header` fill at 85% opacity and the insertion line is 2 px `accent` over header and body.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/header.rs`: drag state, ghost, insertion line, drop.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs`: Esc handling during a drag; insertion line over the body.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_columns.rs`: tests below.

## Tests
- `ui_columns::reorder_moves_column_and_persists_once`.
- `ui_columns::reorder_cannot_move_name` (UI-PRC-005).
- `ui_columns::reorder_never_before_name`.
- `ui_columns::reorder_threshold_4px`.
- `ui_columns::escape_cancels_reorder`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: reordering is mouse only; the column picker keeps keyboard access to visibility.
- Performance: the ghost and line are painted only during a drag.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- Shares the 4 px threshold logic with the sort click from E18-009.
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <files>`. New files need `git add` first. Read `CLAUDE.md` first.
- Plan file: `docs/plan/b5-ui-foundation.md` (open items cited by number).

title: E18-012 Header context menu
description:
## Context
The header context menu, generic for every table with configurable columns: sort by the clicked column, open the column picker, hide the column, fit columns, choose the resize behaviour and reset columns. Sources: UI-PRC-006 (items, order, disabled rules, tooltips, toasts), PROC-026, PROC-022 (Name cannot be hidden), PROC-025, R-112 (menu min width 240 for process row and header menus), UI-FND-022 (TlMenu), R-075.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/table/header.rs`:
```rust
pub fn header_menu(col: &ColumnSpec, layout: &ColumnLayout, sort: &SortSpec, fixed: bool,
                   resize_mode: ColumnResizeMode, menu: TlMenu) -> TlMenu;
```
Built with `TlMenu` (E16-009), `.min_w(px(240))`, items in this order (labels exact):

| # | Item | Kind | Action | Disabled when | Shown when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Sort by <label>` | check item, checked when `col` is the sort column | `SortByColumn { id }` | column unsortable | always |
| 2 | `Select Columns…` | item | `OpenColumnPicker { table }` | never | `!fixed` |
| 3 | `Hide This Column` | item, tooltip `Hide <label>` | `HideColumn { id }` | id is name (tooltip "Name cannot be hidden"), or only one column visible (tooltip "At least one column must stay visible") | `!fixed` |
| | separator | | | | |
| 4 | `Resize columns to fit content` | item | `ResizeColumnsToFit { table }` | never | always |
| 5 | `Resize Behavior` > | submenu with radio items `Proportional`, `Last Column` (checked = `resize_mode`) | `SetColumnResize { mode }` | never | always |
| 6 | `Reset to default` | item | `ResetColumns { table }` | never | `!fixed` |

- Right-click anywhere on the header opens the menu at the pointer for the column under it (`ColumnLayout::column_at_x`); Shift+F10 over the header does nothing (the header is not focusable).
- `HideColumn { id }` is handled by the table: `ColumnLayout::set_visible(id, false)`; on `Err(LastVisible)` push the Warning toast "At least one column must stay visible" through the window's `ToastQueue` (E16-006); on success `rebuild` and `on_columns_changed`.
- `SetColumnResize` propagates to the owner page, which writes `tables.column_resize` (the table reads no settings; open item 16).
- `ResetColumns { table }` is handled by the table when the owner gave it defaults with `TlTreeTable::set_default_layout(layout: ColumnLayout)` (the owner's default order, visible set and widths, for processes canonical table (a) `[columns.processes]`): the layout is replaced by the defaults, `rebuild`, `on_columns_changed` once, and the Info toast "Columns reset to default" through the window's `ToastQueue`. Without defaults the action propagates to the owner.
- Menu strings go through `i18n::tr` with keys appended to `assets/locales/en-US.ftl` in this bead: `table-header-menu-sort-by = Sort by { $label }`, `table-header-menu-select-columns = Select Columns…`, `table-header-menu-hide = Hide This Column`, `table-header-menu-hide-tooltip = Hide { $label }`, `table-header-menu-fit = Resize columns to fit content`, `table-header-menu-resize-behavior = Resize Behavior`, `table-header-menu-proportional = Proportional`, `table-header-menu-last-column = Last Column`, `table-header-menu-reset = Reset to default`, `table-toast-last-visible = At least one column must stay visible`, `table-tooltip-name-not-hideable = Name cannot be hidden`, `table-toast-columns-reset = Columns reset to default`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a right-click on the Name header **When** the menu opens **Then** "Hide This Column" is disabled with tooltip "Name cannot be hidden".
- **Given** only Name visible **When** the menu opens on Name **Then** item 3 is disabled.
- **Given** a right-click on CPU while sorted by CPU **When** the menu opens **Then** "Sort by CPU" is checked.
- **Given** an unsortable column **When** the menu opens **Then** item 1 is disabled.
- **Given** `fixed = true` **When** the menu opens **Then** items 2, 3 and 6 are absent and 1, 4, 5 remain.
- **Given** `resize_mode = LastColumn` **When** the submenu opens **Then** "Last Column" is the checked radio.
- **Given** "Hide This Column" on User **When** chosen **Then** User disappears, `on_columns_changed` runs once and no toast shows.
- **Given** defaults set with `set_default_layout` and a changed layout **When** "Reset to default" is chosen **Then** the layout equals the defaults, `on_columns_changed` runs once and the toast "Columns reset to default" shows.
- **Given** no defaults set **When** "Reset to default" is chosen **Then** the action propagates to the owner page.
- **Given** the menu at 100% scale **When** rendered **Then** it is at least 240 px wide.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/header.rs`: `header_menu`, right-click on the header.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs`: `HideColumn` and `ResetColumns` handlers, `set_default_layout`, toasts.
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: the keys above (chain edit, E16 file, same batch).
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_columns.rs`: tests below.

## Tests
- `ui_columns::header_menu_hide_disabled_on_name` (UI-PRC-006).
- `ui_columns::header_menu_items_and_order`.
- `ui_columns::header_menu_fixed_columns_hides_items_2_3_6`.
- `ui_columns::hide_column_persists`.
- `ui_columns::resize_behavior_radio_reflects_mode`.
- `ui_columns::reset_columns_restores_defaults_and_toasts`.
- `ui_columns::reset_columns_without_defaults_propagates`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: hiding the last visible column shows the Warning toast above.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: arrows, Enter, Esc as every `TlMenu`; disabled items carry tooltips explaining why.
- Performance: built on open only.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- The process page's own copy of this menu in UI-PRC-006 (`pages/processes/menu.rs::header_menu`) uses this builder; E22 does not re-implement it.
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <files>`. New files need `git add` first. Read `CLAUDE.md` first.
- Plan file: `docs/plan/b5-ui-foundation.md` (open items cited by number).

Commits d4a699b, 003bd42, f3fa67d

title: E18-013 Table render goldens
description:
## Context
Headless screenshot tests for the tree table, compared against golden PNGs. ADR-013 names "30 table rows with each Validity state" as a required render case; UI-FND-052 and UI-FND-053 add a 60 px Name column with an ellipsis and an RTL name in an LTR cell. Sources: ADR-013 "Headless screenshot tests" (pass rule, scales, `TL_UPDATE_GOLDEN`), UI-FND-052 render test, UI-FND-053 `untrusted::tests::rtl_name_in_ltr_cell`, UI-PRC-002 row anatomy.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/tests/render_table.rs` (feature `render-tests`), using the helpers in `crates/tl-ui/src/testing/render.rs` (E16-005), with goldens in `crates/tl-ui/tests/golden/`:
- `table_validity_rows_{100,110}.png`: a 1000 × 900 window with a `TlTreeTable` over a test delegate of 30 rows: a group header, then rows cycling the seven `Validity` states across numeric columns (Valid "11.9%", WarmingUp, Stale, Restricted, Unsupported, Missing, Failed), row 3 selected, row 5 with `NEW`, row 7 with `EXITED`, row 9 `STALE`; Default Dark theme; at scale 1.0 and 1.1 (ADR-013).
- `table_name_60px.png`: a 60 px Name column holding "a-very-long-process-name-for-ellipsis"; the cell shows "…" at its end.
- `table_rtl_name.png`: a Name cell with the Hebrew text "תהליך-בדיקה" followed by a count run "(3)" in a 200 px column; the count and any ellipsis stay at the right of the cell and neighbouring cells do not move (UI-FND-053 rule 3).
- Pass rule: at most 0.1% of pixels differ by more than 2/255 in any channel. `TL_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` rewrites the goldens. If E16-005 recorded that headless capture does not work (U-4), the same cases assert `painted_quads()` and text runs instead, as that bead's fallback provides.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the render-tests feature and lavapipe **When** `cargo test -p tl-ui --features render-tests render_table` runs **Then** all four goldens match within the pass rule.
- **Given** `TL_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` **When** the tests run **Then** the goldens are rewritten and the tests pass.
- **Given** the 60 px case **When** the test asserts the hover tooltip (TestAppContext half of the test) **Then** the tooltip text is the full name.
- **Given** the RTL case **When** rendered **Then** the x of the count run's right edge equals the cell's right padding edge or the text end, never left of the RTL run's start.

Commits b3b7dde, b4418a6, 34e57c5. table_name_60px keeps a 60 px Name column set directly (the 120 px minimum applies to resize only), so the image is unchanged: one dot of the ellipsis. comments.author: oystein
comments.text: Commits b3b7dde, b4418a6. Three goldens pass on lavapipe (validity rows at 1.0 and 1.1, 60 px Name column); clippy is clean with no features, with test-hooks, and with render-tests,test-hooks. What the images show: a group header with Apps (29) and a chevron at x 8, and 29 rows in parents (depth 0) and children (depth 1). Every row and every column has all seven states: 11.9%, the warming-up dots, grey stale text, the lock, n/a, a dash, and an orange !. Row 3 is selected (blue), row 5 has the NEW green tint, row 7 has the EXITED red tint, and row 9's metric cells are drawn at 60% opacity. The 60 px golden shows only the first dot of the ellipsis, because R-190 leaves 4 px for text (48 px indent and chevron, 8 px right padding). title: E18-014 Column separators
description:
## Context
"Show column separators" draws 1 px divider lines between columns in every table body. One setting key, `tables.column_separators = false` by default, applies to all five tables (R-075). Sources: PROC-042 (P4), UI-PRC-002 (1 px `divider` quads at each column boundary when on), R-075, canonical table (a) `[tables] column_separators = false`, UI-SHL settings row "Show column separators" (the setting UI is E21's).

## Deliverable
- `TlTreeTable::set_column_separators(&mut self, on: bool)`; the owner page passes `tables.column_separators` (the table reads no settings).
- When on, each body row paints one 1 px (one physical px, `UiMetrics::hairline`) `divider` vertical quad at every visible column boundary (each x offset after the first, and after the last column), full row height, inside the row's existing `canvas` paint, under the selected fill's text but over zebra, tint and hover fills. Group header rows draw none.
- The header already draws boundary lines at all times (E18-006); nothing changes there.
- Off (default): no quads.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** separators off **When** a row with 5 visible columns renders **Then** no vertical divider quads are painted in the body.
- **Given** separators on **When** the same row renders **Then** 5 one-physical-px `divider` quads are painted at the column boundaries.
- **Given** separators on **When** a group header row renders **Then** no separator quads are painted in it.
- **Given** horizontal scroll of 100 px **When** rendered **Then** the quads move with the cells.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs`: `set_column_separators`, the quads.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/header.rs`: no change unless the boundary positions are shared through a helper; if so, move the boundary-x helper here.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_tree_table.rs`: tests below.

## Tests
- `ui_tree_table::separators_off_by_default` (painted quad count).
- `ui_tree_table::separators_on_one_per_boundary`.
- `ui_tree_table::separators_skip_group_headers`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: at most one quad per visible column per visible row; bit check only when off.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- Phase P4. The Settings switch and the persistence of `tables.column_separators` are E21's; the owner pages pass the value.
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <files>`. New files need `git add` first. Read `CLAUDE.md` first.
- Plan file: `docs/plan/b5-ui-foundation.md` (open items cited by number).
close_reason: set_column_separators + one canvas per non-group body row painting 1 physical px divider quads at each column's right edge (matches header); tests in ui_tree_table (test-hooks). Commit 519bdbf

title: E18-017 Keep the first visible row across a UI scale change
description:
## Context
When the UI scale changes, every table keeps the row that was at the top of its viewport at the top after the new row height is applied (UI-SHL-130 step 5). E20-013 re-applies the metrics; this bead gives `TlTreeTable` the two calls it needs around that re-apply. Sources: UI-SHL-130 step 5 and test `scale_keeps_first_row`, UI-PRC-010 (scroll handle), R-187 (OI-U17). Phase P1.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs`, on `TlTreeTable<D>`:
```rust
/// The row at the top of the viewport: its id and its view index at capture time.
pub fn first_visible_row(&self) -> Option<(D::RowId, usize)>;
/// Scrolls so the captured row is the first visible row again.
pub fn restore_first_visible_row(&mut self, anchor: (D::RowId, usize), cx: &mut Context<Self>);
```
- `first_visible_row`: `None` when the table has no rows. Otherwise `ix = scroll_handle.logical_scroll_top_index()` (gpui-pre 0.3.7 `src/elements/uniform_list.rs:222`), clamped to `row_count() - 1`, and returns `(delegate.row_id(ix), ix)`.
- `restore_first_visible_row`: `ix = delegate.row_index(id)` when the id is still in the view, else the captured index clamped to `row_count() - 1`; then `scroll_handle.scroll_to_item_with_offset(ix, ScrollStrategy::Top, 0)` (`uniform_list.rs:182`) and `cx.notify()`. No rows: does nothing.
- The caller captures before the metrics change and restores after the new metrics are applied (E20-013 does this for the active table only).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a 2,000-row table scrolled so row 300 is first visible **When** `first_visible_row` runs **Then** it returns `(id of row 300, 300)`.
- **Given** that anchor and a row height change from 28 to 42 **When** `restore_first_visible_row(anchor)` runs and the table renders **Then** row 300 is the first visible row.
- **Given** an anchor whose id has left the view and 120 rows remain **When** restored with captured index 300 **Then** the first visible row index is 119.
- **Given** an empty table **When** `first_visible_row` runs **Then** it returns `None`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs`: the two methods.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_tree_table.rs`: the tests below.

## Tests
- `ui_tree_table::scale_keeps_first_row`: criteria 1 and 2 (UI-SHL-130 test name), with the `VecDelegate` from E18-005 and row heights 28 then 42.
- `ui_tree_table::restore_first_row_falls_back_to_index`: criterion 3.
- `ui_tree_table::first_visible_row_empty_table`: criterion 4.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: the focus row and selection do not change; only the scroll position does.
- Performance: two calls per scale change; no allocation.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- E20-013 (tasklens-jqk.15) calls these around its metrics re-apply and depends on this bead (R-187).
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_tree_table`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_tree_table.rs`. Never a bare `git commit`.
- Read `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` in the repo first.
close_reason: first_visible_row and restore_first_visible_row on TlTreeTable, three tests in ui_tree_table; 6068143

title: ColumnLayout: generic over the column id so system tables (SysColumnId) can use it
description:
Files: crates/tl-ui/src/table/columns.rs (and its tests).
Why: rsf.5 (a9a34d8) built ColumnLayout over tl_model::ids::ColumnId, which is the process-column enum only. The system tables use tl_model::table::SysColumnId (Services 19, Startup 7, Connections 17 columns), so ColumnLayout cannot hold them.
Leader decision: make ColumnLayout, ColumnSpec and their helpers generic over a column id trait implemented by ColumnId and SysColumnId (Copy + Eq + Hash + a stable string key for ColumnState persistence). Keep the process-table API unchanged for callers (type alias ProcessColumnLayout = ColumnLayout<ColumnId> is fine).
AC: the 9 existing column tests pass unchanged or with only a type alias. New test: a Services ColumnLayout built from SysColumnId::all(SysTable::Services) round-trips widths and order through ColumnState. clippy -p tl-ui --all-targets -D warnings clean.
close_reason: ColumnLayout/ColumnSpec generic over TableColumn (ColumnId, SysColumnId), default ColumnId; ProcessColumnLayout/SysColumnLayout aliases; next_sys_sort; Services round-trip test. a7ca18f

title: TreeTableDelegate and CellTextCache generic over the column and sort types
description:
Files: crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs, crates/tl-ui/src/table/test_delegate.rs, crates/tl-ui/src/text_cache.rs.
Why: rsf.6 (d1b31eb) fixed the delegate to ColumnId, ColumnLayout<ColumnId> and SortSpec, and CellTextCache keys on ColumnId. Services, Startup and Connections use SysColumnId and SysSortSpec, so they cannot implement the trait. rsf.18 already made ColumnLayout<C: TableColumn = ColumnId> generic.
Leader decision:
- TreeTableDelegate gets two associated types: `type Column: TableColumn;` and `type Sort: Clone + PartialEq + 'static;`. Every method that took ColumnId, ColumnLayout<ColumnId> or SortSpec takes Self::Column, ColumnLayout<Self::Column> or Self::Sort. The process delegate will use ColumnId and SortSpec; system tables use SysColumnId and SysSortSpec.
- CellTextCache<R, C: TableColumn = ColumnId>: key cells and paths on C. Existing callers keep compiling through the default.
- ColumnResizeMode becomes `pub use tl_model::settings::ColumnResize as ColumnResizeMode;` (one enum, the one settings parse). Remove the duplicate enum.
- VecDelegate gets a column type parameter with ColumnId as the default.
AC: tuple_row_id_compiles and the other rsf.6 tests pass. New test: a VecDelegate over SysColumnId with SysSortSpec compiles and reports its sort through the trait. Existing text_cache tests pass unchanged. clippy clean with and without test-hooks.
close_reason: TreeTableDelegate has associated Column and Sort types; CellTextCache<R, C = ColumnId>; ColumnResizeMode re-exports tl_model::settings::ColumnResize; VecDelegate<R, C = ColumnId> with new() for ColumnId and with_columns() for other id sets. Commits 63dbfbd, 6891896.

title: E18-A2 Two-line header, picker and persistence
description:
## Context
Anchor E18-A2 "Two-line header, picker and persistence". This bead adds the column picker window "tasklens Columns" and finishes the A2 group: two-line header with totals and sort (E18-009), resize and fit (E18-010), reorder (E18-011), header menu (E18-012), column state by id (E18-003). The picker is generic: the owning table passes its column registry and its table name, and every table with configurable columns (Processes, History, Services, Startup Apps, Connections) uses the same window. Sources: UI-PRC-007 (window, anatomy, rows, filter, footer, keys), R-106 (tool window, `WindowKey::Columns`, 420 × 560, minimum 320 × 400, one instance bound to the table that opened it, immediate apply), R-065 (groups and aliases), PROC-024, PROC-022, APP-018 (View > Columns acts on every table), UI-FND-021 (`TlSecondaryWindow`), UI-FND-011 (`TlCheckbox`), UI-FND-016 (`TlTextInput`), canonical table (b) ColumnPicker row.

Closes the group: E18-009, E18-010, E18-011, E18-012 (and depends on E18-A1).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/table/columns_window.rs` (open item 3: this path replaces `pages/processes/columns_window.rs`, which would create a cycle with E22-A1; `pub mod columns_window;` in `table/mod.rs`):
```rust
pub trait ColumnHost: 'static {
    fn table_name(&self, cx: &App) -> SharedString;           // first list line, e.g. "Processes table"
    fn specs(&self, cx: &App) -> Arc<[ColumnSpec]>;           // the registry: group, label, full_name (alias), availability; GPU N rows only for present adapters
    fn layout(&self, cx: &App) -> ColumnLayout;
    fn set_visible(&self, id: ColumnId, on: bool, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App) -> Result<(), ColumnError>;
    fn reset(&self, window: &mut Window, cx: &mut App);       // same as ResetColumns on the table
}
impl<D: TreeTableDelegate> ColumnHost for WeakEntity<TlTreeTable<D>> { ... }   // set_visible -> layout change + on_columns_changed
pub struct ColumnPicker { host: Rc<dyn ColumnHost>, filter: Entity<InputState>, ... }   // Entity, window content
pub fn open_column_picker(host: Rc<dyn ColumnHost>, cx: &mut App);
```
- `EnableAllColumns { table: TableId }` (R-180): declare it in `table/actions.rs` next to `ResetColumns` (`#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, gpui::Action)] #[action(namespace = tasklens)] pub struct EnableAllColumns { pub table: TableId }`) and handle it in `TlTreeTable`: when `table` is this table's id, set every column of the owner's column set visible (`ColumnLayout::set_visible(id, true)` for each spec whose availability is not `NotOnThisSystem`, keeping remembered slots and widths) and call `delegate.on_columns_changed`, which persists through the normal `[columns.<table>]` path. Another table's id: ignored. The Debug menu (E21-038) dispatches it with the active tab's `TableId`; this bead does not show a toast (the menu does).
- `OpenColumnPicker { table }` is handled by the table: `open_column_picker(Rc::new(weak_self))`. Through `WindowRegistry` (E16-A2) key `WindowKey::Columns`: an open picker is focused and rebound to the new host instead of opening a second window.
- Window: `TlSecondaryWindow` tool window (Floating, non-modal, pinnable), title "tasklens Columns", default 420 × 560, minimum 320 × 400, resizable, Esc closes (after clearing the filter, below), Ctrl+W closes. Root `key_context("ColumnPicker")`.
- Content top to bottom, outer margin `sp5` 12:
  - Filter: `TlTextInput` md (28 high), prefix Lucide `search` 14, cleanable, placeholder "Filter columns…". Case-insensitive substring match over label, full name (alias) and group name, applied 100 ms after the last change. Non-matching rows and groups left empty are hidden. No match: the centred text "No columns match" in `text_secondary`.
  - List: `uniform_list` with one item height of 28 × ui_scale. Item 0 is the table-name line ("Processes table", `t_sm` `text_secondary`). Group heading items, in the registry's group order (processes: Image, Identity, Security, Scheduling, CPU, Memory, I/O, Disk, Network, GPU, Power, Objects, Linux, R-065), show the group name uppercased, `t_xs` 11 weight 600 `text_secondary`, bottom-aligned in the 28 px item (UI-PRC-007 gives 24 for headings; `uniform_list` needs one height, so the extra 4 px sit above the text). Column rows: `TlCheckbox` 16 px at x 12, label at x 36 `t_base` `text_primary` showing `full_name` with the alias, e.g. `Working set private - "Memory"`; hover fills the row `row_hover`; a click anywhere on the row toggles. Name: checked, disabled checkbox and the note "always on" right-aligned in `text_secondary`. Columns with `Availability::NotOnThisSystem`: enabled, with the note "n/a on this system" right-aligned in `text_secondary`.
  - Footer (padding `sp5`): left the count text `t_sm` `text_secondary` "{shown} of {total} columns shown" (for example "9 of 96 columns shown"); right `TlButton` Ghost "Reset to default" then `TlButton` Primary "Close", gap `sp4` 8.
- Toggling applies at once: `host.set_visible(id, on)`; a re-shown column returns to its remembered slot and width (E18-003). On `Err(LastVisible)` the picker window's own toast queue shows the Warning "At least one column must stay visible".
- Keyboard: Tab order filter, list, Reset, Close. In the list: Up/Down move the list focus (skipping headings), Space toggles, Home/End jump to the first or last column row. Esc: when the filter has text, clear it; else close the window.
- Re-render on the host table's layout changes (observe the table entity).
- Strings through `i18n::tr` with keys appended to `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: `table-picker-title = tasklens Columns`, `table-picker-filter-placeholder = Filter columns…`, `table-picker-always-on = always on`, `table-picker-na = n/a on this system`, `table-picker-no-match = No columns match`, `table-picker-count = { $shown } of { $total } columns shown`, `table-picker-reset = Reset to default`, `table-picker-close = Close`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a test registry with groups Image, Identity, Memory **When** the picker opens **Then** headings appear in that order after the "Processes table" line.
- **Given** the picker **When** looking at Name **Then** its checkbox is checked and disabled with the note "always on".
- **Given** the filter "working set" or "memory" **When** 100 ms pass **Then** the `Working set private - "Memory"` row is visible in both cases.
- **Given** a registry without GPU 1 **When** the picker opens **Then** no "GPU 1" row exists.
- **Given** CPU hidden after being third at width 70 **When** its checkbox is ticked **Then** the table shows CPU third at width 70 and `on_columns_changed` ran.
- **Given** the picker is open **When** `OpenColumnPicker` is dispatched again **Then** there is still one picker window and it is focused.
- **Given** filter text "xyz" **When** Esc **Then** the filter clears and the window stays; a second Esc closes it.
- **Given** 9 of 96 visible **When** rendered **Then** the footer reads "9 of 96 columns shown".
- **Given** a column marked NotOnThisSystem **When** rendered **Then** it is enabled and shows "n/a on this system".
- **Given** a table with 3 of 10 columns visible **When** `EnableAllColumns { table }` with its own id is dispatched **Then** all 10 columns are visible and `on_columns_changed` ran once (R-180).
- **Given** the same table **When** `EnableAllColumns` carries another table's id **Then** nothing changes.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/columns_window.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/mod.rs`: add `pub mod columns_window;`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs`: `OpenColumnPicker` and `EnableAllColumns` handlers, `ColumnHost` impl.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/table/actions.rs`: add `EnableAllColumns { table: TableId }` (R-180).
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: the keys above.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_columns.rs`: tests below.

## Tests
- `ui_columns::picker_lists_groups_in_order` (UI-PRC-007).
- `ui_columns::picker_name_always_on`.
- `ui_columns::picker_alias_filter_matches_both_parts`.
- `ui_columns::picker_gpu_slots_only_for_present_adapters`.
- `ui_columns::picker_toggle_persists_and_restores_width`.
- `ui_columns::picker_single_instance_refocus` (R-106).
- `ui_columns::picker_escape_clears_filter_then_closes`.
- `ui_columns::picker_count_text`.
- `ui_columns::enable_all_columns_shows_every_column`: the two `EnableAllColumns` criteria (R-180).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: the LastVisible Warning toast above.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: every row is a labelled checkbox; headings are plain text; the count line reports each toggle's result; full keyboard path above.
- Performance: at most 96 rows plus headings; trivial.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- This is the anchor bead; title stays as created. Before closing, check that `table/header.rs` has the two-line mode, resize, reorder, sort and header menu, and that column state round-trips by id (E18-003 tests pass).
- `WindowRegistry`, `WindowKey::Columns` and `TlSecondaryWindow` come from E16-A2 and E16-008; `TlCheckbox` and `TlTextInput` from E15-A1.
- The picker lives in `table/columns_window.rs` (R-181, open item 3 settled); it is table-generic.
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <files>`. New files need `git add` first. Read `CLAUDE.md` first.
- Plan file: `docs/plan/b5-ui-foundation.md` (open items cited by number).
close_reason: Column picker window table/columns_window.rs (ColumnHost by column key, ColumnPicker, open_column_picker via WindowKey::Columns), EnableAllColumns and OpenColumnPicker handlers and ColumnHost impl in TlTreeTable, picker strings, ui_columns picker tests. 87a2657, ebebe40, 3e6c685

title: Tree table: cache app icon image sources instead of a new PathBuf per frame
description:
Files: crates/tl-ui/src/table/cells.rs, crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_tree_table.rs.
Why: rsf.8 (e22e48e) builds a new PathBuf for each app row icon every frame because img() takes the path by value. Rendering speed comes first and the row path should not allocate per frame.
Deliverable: keep a per-table cache from icon path to an ImageSource (or Arc<Path>) built once per icon, reused across frames, evicted when the row set's table_version changes and the icon is no longer referenced.
AC: test hook counts icon source constructions; 60 frames over the same 26 visible app rows build each icon source once. Existing ui_tree_table tests pass. clippy clean with and without test-hooks.
close_reason: IconSourceCache in cells.rs, owned by TlTreeTable: one ImageSource per icon path, reused across frames, entries unused by the ending table_version dropped on version change. Test hook icon_sources(); tests in ui_tree_table.rs mod icon_cache. Commit ff2b0e2.

title: Name cell: bidi isolate before the count, Binary icon asset, Name column minimum width
description:
Files: crates/tl-ui/src/table/cells.rs, crates/tl-ui/src/components/icons.rs, crates/tl-ui/src/table/columns.rs, crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_tree_table.rs.
Why: rsf.15 (b3b7dde, b4418a6) found three defects. (1) cosmic-text picks paragraph direction from the first strong character, so a name like the Hebrew "process-check (3)" is laid out RTL and "(3)" draws on the left, breaking UI-FND-053 rule 3. (2) IconName::Binary is in neither the kit default bundle nor TlExtraIcons, so Name cells using it and the missing-file-icon fallback draw nothing. (3) At the 60 px column minimum R-190 geometry leaves 4 px for text.
Leader decisions: (1) In paint_name_cell, shape the name as FSI + name + PDI followed by the count run, so the count always stays on the right in an LTR row; do not allocate per frame (build the isolated string once per cached text). (2) Add TlIcon::Binary to icons.rs (ALL, kit_name, icon_assets! list), like TlIcon::Square in 2b36602. (3) The Name column's minimum width is 120 px times ui_scale (R-190 depth-0 app text start 78 px plus 42 px of text); other columns keep the 60 px minimum.
AC: a Hebrew-first name paints its count to the right of the name (glyph x order test); a row with the Binary icon paints a sprite; resizing Name below 120 px clamps to 120. Existing ui_tree_table and ui_columns tests pass. clippy clean with and without test-hooks.
close_reason: FSI/PDI isolate of the name before the count via name_primary_text, cached in IconSourceCache (456205b, 03180c0); TlIcon::Binary in TlExtraIcons (5265e51); Name min 120 px x ui_scale (5dc681d); tests in ui_tree_table name_cell_fixes (3650424 and follow-ups)

title: Column actions: carry the column key as a string so system tables can sort and hide from the header menu
description:
Files: crates/tl-ui/src/table/actions.rs, crates/tl-ui/src/table/header.rs, crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs, crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_tree_table.rs.
Why: rsf.14 found that SortByColumn and HideColumn carry a ColumnId, so a SysColumnId table (Services, Startup, Connections) cannot name its column. rsf.14 round-trips through ColumnId::from_str(col.key()) and C::parse, and disables Sort and Hide for a system column with no ColumnId.
Leader decision: SortByColumn and HideColumn carry the column key as SharedString (the stable key from TableColumn::key()). The table parses it with C::parse. Remove the ColumnId round trip and the disabled fallback in header_menu.
AC: in a SysColumnId test table, the header menu Sort and Hide items are enabled and act on the right column; process table behaviour is unchanged. clippy clean with and without test-hooks.
close_reason: SortByColumn and HideColumn carry the column key as SharedString; TlTreeTable parses it with C::parse; header_menu round trip and disabled fallback removed; SysColumnId header menu test added. eb67e1c

title: Name cell: end the bidi isolate before the space that precedes the count
description:
Files: crates/tl-ui/src/table/cells.rs, crates/tl-ui/tests/render_table.rs, crates/tl-ui/tests/golden/table_rtl_name.png.
Why: rsf.15 (34e57c5) found that rsf.21's FSI/PDI isolate covers ..count_start, which includes the space before "(". In an RTL isolate that space draws at the name's left edge, so "(3)" touches the Hebrew name and the text starts about 5 px right of "bash (2)".

AC: in the RTL golden there is a gap between the name and "(3)" and the text start matches the LTR rows. Regenerate table_rtl_name.png with TL_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1, view it, commit it. Other goldens unchanged. clippy clean with and without test-hooks and with render-tests,test-hooks.

title: Column picker: Tab order and centring on the table's window
description:
Files: crates/tl-ui/src/components/checkbox.rs, crates/tl-ui/src/table/columns_window.rs, crates/tl-ui/src/table/tree_table.rs, crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_columns.rs, crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_components.rs.
Why: rsf.2 (87a2657, ebebe40, 3e6c685) built the picker, but every row's TlCheckbox is a tab stop, so Tab does not follow filter, list, Reset, Close. open_column_picker(host, cx) takes no parent window, so the picker centres on the screen.
Deliverable: add TlCheckbox::tab_stop(bool) (default true) and use tab_stop(false) for the picker rows; the list keeps focus and its keys. Give open_column_picker the parent window bounds (an Option<Bounds<Pixels>> argument from the table's window) and centre on it, falling back to the screen.
AC: Tab from the filter goes to the list, then Reset, then Close, then back to the filter; a test checks the order. The picker opened from a table window centres on that window. Existing checkbox tests pass. clippy clean with and without test-hooks.

title: Table cells: want_tooltip on the hovered row so Stale and Failed cells get their tooltip
