title: E02-A1 Workspace compiles
description:
## Context
Capstone of the workspace setup. It generates and commits `Cargo.lock`, proves the whole workspace builds on the pinned toolchain with `--locked`, and runs the ADR-002 verification commands. - The outputs of the three ADR-002 verification commands, pasted into the bead close reason (`br close <id> --reason "..."`):

  3. `cargo tree -p tl-app -i gpui-pre --prefix none` shows exactly one version, `0.3.7` (ADR-002 writes `-p tasklens`; use the package name E02-005 settled on).

Record the answer in the close reason. ## Acceptance Criteria

- **Given** the build passed **When** `git status` runs **Then** `Cargo.lock` is tracked and has no uncommitted changes.

title: E02-008 check-deps: allowed rows and closure rules
description:
## Context
Second half of `cargo xtask check-deps`: ADR-001 check 2. It reads `cargo metadata` and enforces the allowed-dependency table on direct dependencies and the asupersync closure rule. Rule 1 and check 2 cover direct dependencies only; transitive dependencies of allowed crates do not count (R-259: `zbus` reaches tl-ui through `gpui-pre-linux` and `gpui-base`, `arc-swap` through `gpui-component`). This bead also switches check 1 (E02-007) to the `cargo tree -i` form (R-259). Sources: ADR-001 (allowed table, checks 1 and 2, rules 1 and 2), R-130, R-131, R-132, R-142, R-245 (serde_json in tl-app), R-259.

## Deliverable
In `xtask/src/check_deps.rs`, add check 2, run by `run()` together with the other three.

Allowed direct normal dependencies (`[dependencies]` and `[build-dependencies]`; `[dev-dependencies]` are not checked by this table), as a constant table `ALLOWED: &[(&str, &[&str])]`:

| Package | Allowed direct deps |
|---|---|
| tl-model | serde, postcard, thiserror, async-channel, bitflags, smallvec, rustix, rustc-hash |
| tl-collect | tl-model, rustix, memchr, thiserror, tracing, smallvec, rustc-hash, netlink-packet-core, netlink-packet-sock-diag, netlink-sys, sha2, md-5 |
| tl-ops | tl-model, rustix, libc, thiserror, tracing |
| tl-engine | tl-model, tl-collect, tl-ops, tl-history, asupersync, arc-swap, async-channel, zbus, futures-lite, rustix, postcard, serde, thiserror, tracing, rustc-hash, smallvec, ureq, serde_json |
| tl-gpu-probe | tl-model, nvml-wrapper, rustix, postcard, serde, ash, khronos-egl |
| tl-ui | tl-model, gpui-kit, tracing, smallvec, rustc-hash, serde, serde_json, fluent-bundle, unic-langid, async-channel, jiff, unicode-segmentation |
| tl-app | tl-model, tl-engine, tl-ui, tl-ops, tl-tray, zbus, toml, serde, serde_json, anyhow, tracing, tracing-subscriber, tracing-appender, rustix, clap, async-channel |
| tl-history | tl-model, zstd, crc32fast, postcard, serde, thiserror |
| tl-tray | tl-model, ksni |
| tl-helper | tl-model, tl-ops, tl-collect, rustix, postcard, serde |
| xtask | serde, serde_json, anyhow |

Row additions settled in R-142: tl-model + `rustc-hash` (item 3), tl-engine + `serde_json` (item 7), tl-ui + `async-channel`, `jiff`, `unicode-segmentation` (items 2, 9, 15), tl-app + `clap`, `async-channel` (items 1, 2), tl-helper + `tl-collect` (item 14). Dev-dependencies (`insta`, `proptest`, `tempfile`, `criterion`, `toml`, `tracing-subscriber`) are outside the rows and not checked (R-142 item 18).

Violations:
1. A workspace member has a direct normal or build dependency not in its row: `<member> depends on <dep>, which is not in its ADR-001 row`.
2. A workspace member not in the table (for example `tl-netmon`, whose row is decided later): `<member> has no ADR-001 row`.
3. `asupersync` is in the normal-dependency closure of any member other than `tl-engine` and `tl-app`: `asupersync in the closure of <member>`.

There is no closure check for `tl-ui` (R-259): its row above is the whole of rule 1, checked on direct dependencies. Direct dependencies are read from `cargo metadata` `packages[].dependencies[]` with `kind` `null` (normal) or `"build"`, for the target or no target; the same set `cargo tree --depth 1 -e normal` prints.

Check 1 change (R-259, replaces the E02-007 form): for each crate `C` in `BANNED_CRATES`, run `cargo tree --workspace -e normal --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -i C` and fail on any output line whose first whitespace-separated word is `C`, message `banned crate <C> in the workspace dependency graph`. No output means absent; ignore the exit status; keep `SHIPPED_BINARIES` only for the P3 and P4 skip note.

Closure: from `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --filter-platform x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, walk `resolve.nodes[].deps[]`, following only edges whose `dep_kinds` include an entry with `kind: null` (normal). Parse with `serde_json::Value`; no new dependencies.

The rustix feature limit on tl-model (feature `time` only) is not checked by this bead; it is reviewed by hand in E03.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the skeleton workspace **When** `cargo xtask check-deps` runs **Then** check 2 reports nothing and the run prints `check-deps: ok`.
- **Given** a scratch copy where tl-ops adds `serde` **When** check-deps runs **Then** it prints `tl-ops depends on serde, which is not in its ADR-001 row` and exits 1.
- **Given** a scratch copy where tl-collect adds `asupersync` **When** check-deps runs **Then** it reports both the row violation and `asupersync in the closure of tl-collect`.
- **Given** a scratch copy where tl-ui adds `tl-engine` **When** check-deps runs **Then** it reports `tl-ui depends on tl-engine, which is not in its ADR-001 row` and `asupersync in the closure of tl-ui`, and exits 1.
- **Given** the real workspace, where `zbus` and `arc-swap` are in tl-ui's closure through gpui-kit **When** check-deps runs **Then** check 2 reports nothing (R-259).
- **Given** a scratch copy where `crates/tl-ui/Cargo.toml` gains `tokio = "1"` **When** check-deps runs **Then** check 1 prints `banned crate tokio in the workspace dependency graph` and exits 1; with `tokio` under `[dev-dependencies]` it passes.
- **Given** a dev-only dependency `tempfile` in tl-ops **When** check-deps runs **Then** no violation.

## Files
- `xtask/src/check_deps.rs`: change, add check 2

## Tests
- `xtask/src/check_deps.rs::tests::closure_follows_normal_edges_only`: a hand-built metadata JSON where A -normal-> B -dev-> C gives closure(A) = {B}.
- `xtask/src/check_deps.rs::tests::row_violation_reported`: metadata JSON with tl-ops -> serde gives exactly the message above.
- `xtask/src/check_deps.rs::tests::transitive_not_checked`: metadata JSON with tl-ui -> gpui-kit -> zbus reports nothing (R-259).
- `xtask/src/check_deps.rs::tests::banned_tree_line_first_word`: the `cargo tree -i` output line `tokio v1.40.0` is a hit; an empty output is not.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: violations as listed; a metadata parse failure is an error naming the missing field.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: N/A
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
R-158 item 4's gpui-kit narrowing is superseded by R-259 (direct dependencies only). Run scratch experiments in a copy under the session scratchpad, never in the shared checkout. Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...`. Never switch branch, reset, rebase or amend in the shared checkout. Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E02-009 scripts/ci.sh running the ADR-013 CI rows
description:
## Context

1. `cargo build -p tl-gpu-probe --features fake --locked` (the fake probe binary that the engine tests spawn; R-166, B3-16 (b))

title: E02-007 check-deps: banned crates and asupersync greps
description:
## Context First half of `cargo xtask check-deps`: the banned-crate check per shipped binary (ADR-001 check 1), the `asupersync::` grep outside tl-engine (check 3), and the banned asupersync API grep in tl-engine production code (ADR-004). description:

title: E01-008 Bench scene table-2000 with synthetic process table
description:
## Context
ADR-014 scene `table-2000` measures the production process table (E22-A1 on E18's `TlTreeTable`) with 2,000 rows that all change every second and re-sort, while it scrolls at 1,200 logical px/s. Gates: UI thread p99 <= 2.0 ms per frame while scrolling, missed frames as in the gate table, RSS <= 150 MB after the run. Sources: ADR-014, UI-PRC-023 (budget split, rules, test name), R-006 (default columns and widths).

## Deliverable
1. In `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/synth.rs`, add `pub struct TableSynth` with `pub fn new(rng: &mut BenchRng) -> Self` and `pub fn tick_1hz(&mut self, rng: &mut BenchRng, t_ns: TimeNs) -> Arc<ProcessTableView>`:
   - 2,000 process rows in 40 groups (grouped mode, `TableMode::Grouped`), sorted by CPU descending with the `ProcessKey` tie-break (so order changes every second).
   - 10 columns (R-160 OI-7): R-006's nine default columns `name, user, pid, cpu, memory, disk, network, gpu, description` plus `power` (101 px), with R-006 widths Name 248, User 92, PID 96, CPU 63, Memory 92, Disk 82, Network 92, GPU 72, Description 342.
   - Every metric value of every row changes on every tick (fresh draws). Names, groups and value ranges (R-160 OI-7): 40 App groups "App 01" to "App 40" of 50 processes each, named `proc-0001` to `proc-2000`; CPU uniform 0..5%, memory 1..500 MiB, disk 0..2 MiB/s, network 0..1 Mbps, GPU 0..10%, all redrawn each second.
   - The view is built directly with `tl-model` table types (E03-A2); group totals are sums of the member rows.
2. In `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/scenes.rs`, implement `BenchScene::Table2000`: the Processes page only (E22-A1 `ProcessesPage`) in the fixture window; `BenchEngine` publishes the `TableSynth` view once per second (component `TABLE` and `PROCESSES` change, nothing else); programmatic scroll at 1,200 logical px/s, bouncing between top and bottom, through the table's `UniformListScrollHandle`, advanced in the `FrameProbe` callback by `1200 px * frame_dt` and clamped to `[0, content_height - viewport_height]`, reversing direction at either end. `rss_mb` is read after the measured window.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** two `TableSynth` from seed 42 **When** each produces its first tick **Then** the row sets (keys in order) are identical (test `bench_table_2000_scene_exists_and_is_deterministic`, UI-PRC-023).
- **Given** a tick **When** inspected **Then** it has 2,000 process rows under 40 group rows and rows are in non-increasing CPU order with ties broken by `ProcessKey`.
- **Given** two consecutive ticks **When** compared **Then** every process row's CPU value differs and the order differs.
- **Given** the scene in a `TestAppContext` **When** 1 s of simulated frames at 144 Hz runs **Then** the scroll offset moved 1,200 +- 20 logical px from the start, and after reaching the bottom it moves upward.
- **Given** `--bench table-2000` **When** run **Then** the report has `"scene": "table-2000"` and a non-zero `rss_mb`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/synth.rs`: change, add `TableSynth`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/scenes.rs`: change, add the `Table2000` scene.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/bench_scenes.rs`: change, add the tests below.

## Tests
- `tests/bench_scenes.rs::bench_table_2000_scene_exists_and_is_deterministic`
- `tests/bench_scenes.rs::table_synth_sorted_grouped_2000`
- `tests/bench_scenes.rs::table_synth_changes_every_tick`
- `tests/bench_scenes.rs::table_scroll_bounces_at_1200_px_per_s`
Run with `cargo test -p tl-ui --features bench --test bench_scenes`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: every synthetic cell `Valid`; no `Restricted` or `Failed` cells (they are covered by E22's own render tests).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: carries the `table-2000` gates. The scene must not add per-frame work in the table path; the scroll update is one `set_offset` call per frame.
- Privacy: N/A (synthetic names).

## Notes
- The scroll needs access to the production table's `UniformListScrollHandle` (R-160 OI-8): E18-A1 (rsf.1) exposes `TlTreeTable::scroll_handle(&self) -> UniformListScrollHandle`, a clone of the `Rc`-backed handle, and E22-A1 (pdu.1) exposes `ProcessesPage::scroll_handle(&self, cx: &App) -> UniformListScrollHandle` (R-186). Call the page method once at scene start. For the pixel scroll, set the offset through the clone's `base_handle` (`handle.0.borrow().base_handle.set_offset(..)`); `scroll_to_item_with_offset` takes its offset in items (`usize`, `src/elements/uniform_list.rs:182`), so it cannot move 1,200 px/s smoothly. Do not edit E18 or E22 files from this bead.
- gpui-pre 0.3.7: `UniformListScrollHandle` wraps `UniformListScrollState { base_handle: ScrollHandle, .. }` (`src/elements/uniform_list.rs:113-145`); `ScrollHandle::offset` and `set_offset` are at `src/elements/div.rs:4258` and `:4394`. Offsets are negative downward; check the sign in source before writing the clamp.
- If the UI-PRC-023 fallback inside GPUI is needed (ADR-014 step 2), it is E22 work in the optimisation pass, not this bead.

title: E01-009 tl-app bench entry: bench_main.rs
description:
## Context
`tasklens --bench <scene> --duration 30 --warmup 5 --json <out>` (ADR-014, table (c), APP-052) runs one scene. `tl-app/src/bench_main.rs` is the binary side: it supplies the clocks `tl-ui` cannot read, starts the real engine for the `bridge` scene, runs GPUI with the scene, and shuts down. Sources: ADR-014, ADR-010 (close and shutdown order), ADR-005 (`Engine::start`, `EngineHandle`), table (c).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-app/src/bench_main.rs`, compiled only with `#[cfg(feature = "bench")]`:

```rust
pub struct BenchArgs { pub scene: String, pub duration_s: u32, pub warmup_s: u32, pub json: Option<PathBuf> }
/// Returns the process exit code: 0 on a finished run, 1 on a scene failure, 2 on an unknown scene.
pub fn run(args: BenchArgs) -> i32;
fn thread_cpu_ns() -> u64;    // rustix::time::clock_gettime(ClockId::ThreadCPUTime), as ns
fn process_cpu_ns() -> u64;   // rustix::time::clock_gettime(ClockId::ProcessCPUTime), as ns
```

Steps of `run`:
1. `BenchScene::from_arg(&args.scene)`; `None` prints `unknown bench scene "<name>"; expected perf-cpu, table-2000, bridge or static` to stderr and returns 2.
2. For `Bridge` only: `Engine::start(EngineConfig::default())` (E09-A1), and set a `Demand` on it with the Performance tab visible, the CPU page shown and fast CPU (10 Hz, `cpu_fast`) on, as the Performance tab would (ADR-008). Wrap the handle as `Arc<dyn EngineClient>`.
3. Build the GPUI `Application` exactly as normal startup does up to fonts, kit init, assets and theme (UI-SHL-110 step 8, through `TasklensUi::init`, E16-A1), but open no main window; call `tl_ui::bench::run(cx, scene, opts, BenchClocks { thread_cpu_ns, process_cpu_ns }, real)`. When the task finishes: on `Ok(report)` keep exit code 0; on `Err(e)` print `bench failed: <e>` to stderr and set exit code 1; then `cx.quit()`.
4. After `Application::run` returns: if an engine was started, `handle.shutdown(Duration::from_millis(1500))` (ADR-010); log the `ShutdownReport` at `info` on target `tasklens::perf`.
5. Return the exit code.

The panic hook, logging and argument parsing are done by `main.rs` (E33-A1) before `run` is called.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `--bench charts` **When** run **Then** stderr has `unknown bench scene "charts"; expected perf-cpu, table-2000, bridge or static` and the exit code is 2, with no window opened.
- **Given** `--bench static --duration 2 --warmup 1 --json /tmp/x.json` on the owner machine **When** run **Then** the process exits 0 within 5 s and the file holds a report with `"scene": "static"`.
- **Given** `--bench bridge --duration 5 --warmup 1` **When** run **Then** the engine is started, the report has a non-null `bridge_latency_ms`, and after exit no `tl-engine` thread is left (process gone within 2 s).
- **Given** two calls of `thread_cpu_ns()` around a 10 ms busy loop **When** compared **Then** the delta is between 5 ms and 50 ms (sanity).

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/src/bench_main.rs`: create.

## Tests
- `bench_main::tests::unknown_scene_exit_2` (calls the scene parsing helper, no GPUI).
- `bench_main::tests::thread_cpu_clock_moves`: the 10 ms busy-loop delta check.
- Manual, recorded by E01-A1: the static and bridge commands above.
Run with `cargo test -p tl-app --features bench bench_main`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: exact texts above; exit codes 0, 1, 2.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: no work between scenes and GPUI beyond startup; the engine is started only for `bridge`.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- `rustix` with feature `time` is in `tl-app`'s allowed row (ADR-001). `ClockId::ThreadCPUTime` and `ClockId::ProcessCPUTime` are rustix 1.x names; check the rustix source in `~/.cargo/registry` before use.
- `ProcessCPUTime` measures the same utime + stime that ADR-014 names from `/proc/self/stat`, with ns resolution. tl-app passes `rustix::time::clock_gettime(ClockId::ProcessCPUTime)` and `ThreadCPUTime` to tl-ui as the `BenchClocks` function pointers (R-144 item 5).
- The `mod bench_main;` line and the `--bench` arm in `main.rs` are E01-010.

title: E01-011 cargo xtask bench: three runs per scene, median and table
description:
## Context
`cargo xtask bench` runs every scene 3 times and writes `target/bench/<date>-<git sha>.json` plus a table (ADR-014, UI-PRF-053). Each later phase re-runs it; a regression above 20% on any gated metric blocks the phase (ADR-014 verification). Sources: ADR-014, UI-PRF-053, ADR-013 layers table (performance gates run on the owner machine, not in CI).

## Deliverable
`xtask/src/bench.rs`:

```rust
pub struct BenchCmd { pub scenes: Vec<String>, pub runs: u32, pub compare: Option<PathBuf> }
pub fn run(cmd: BenchCmd) -> anyhow::Result<()>;
```

- Command line (parsed by hand in this file, xtask has no clap): `cargo xtask bench [--scene <name>]... [--runs <n>] [--compare <old.json>]`. Defaults: scenes `perf-cpu`, `table-2000`, `bridge`, `static` in that order; runs 3.
- Step 1: build once: `cargo build --release -p tl-app --features bench` (through the build rule wrapper when the environment variable `TL_BUILD_WRAP=1` is set; see Notes).
- Step 2: for each scene, `runs` times: `target/release/tasklens --bench <scene> --duration 30 --warmup 5 --json target/bench/tmp/<scene>-<i>.json`. A non-zero exit fails the whole command with `bench: <scene> run <i> failed with exit code <c>`.
- Step 3: for each scene pick the median run by `frame_cpu_ms.p99` (for `static`: by `process_cpu_pct`), and write `target/bench/<date>-<sha>.json` = `{ "date": "<YYYY-MM-DD>", "git_sha": "<sha>", "scenes": { "<scene>": { "median": <report>, "runs": [<report>, ...] } } }`. `<date>` is the UTC date from `SystemTime`, `<sha>` is `git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD`, with `-dirty` appended when `git status --porcelain` is non-empty.
- Step 4: print a Markdown table to stdout, one row per scene: `| Scene | frame CPU p50 ms | p99 ms | missed | process CPU % | RSS MB | stalls | bridge p99 ms |`, values from the median run, two decimals.
- `--compare <old.json>`: for every gated metric (frame CPU p50 and p99, missed frames, process CPU, RSS, bridge p99), print the change in percent and exit 1 with `bench: regression above 20% in <scene> <metric>` if any metric is more than 20% worse.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** three fake report files for one scene with p99 1.0, 1.4, 1.2 ms **When** the median is picked **Then** the 1.2 ms run is the median.
- **Given** an old summary with `perf-cpu` p99 1.0 ms and a new one with 1.25 ms **When** `--compare` runs **Then** the exit code is 1 and the message names `perf-cpu frame_cpu_ms.p99`.
- **Given** a new p99 of 1.15 ms **When** compared **Then** the exit code is 0.
- **Given** a child exit code 1 for `bridge` run 2 **When** the command runs **Then** it stops with `bench: bridge run 2 failed with exit code 1`.
- **Given** `--scene perf-cpu --runs 1` **When** run on the owner machine **Then** `target/bench/<date>-<sha>.json` exists with one scene and one run.

## Files
- `xtask/src/bench.rs`: create.

## Tests
- `bench::tests::median_by_p99`
- `bench::tests::median_static_by_process_cpu`
- `bench::tests::compare_flags_regression_over_20pct`
- `bench::tests::compare_passes_under_20pct`
- `bench::tests::summary_json_shape` (serialize a summary from fixture reports)
Run with `cargo test -p xtask bench`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: exact texts above; `anyhow` is allowed in `xtask` (ADR-015).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: the command itself is not measured; it runs scenes one at a time, never in parallel.

title: E01-015 Bench soak scene for zed#64499: three windows, 10 minutes
description:
## Context
zed#64499 (open) can stop GPUI redraws on KWin until input arrives. ADR-010 step 2 fixes the phase-0 soak: three tasklens windows (the main window plus two detached graph windows of the spike), 1 Hz updates, smooth charts on, 10 minutes with no input; pass is zero stalls longer than 250 ms, counted by the `AnimationDriver` stall detector (`FrameStats.stalls`, E19-A1). The docs name no command for the soak; this bead adds it as a bench scene. Sources: ADR-010 zed#64499 mitigation steps 1 and 2, ADR-014 gate "zed#64499 soak", U-9.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/scenes.rs` and `bench/mod.rs`, a fifth scene (R-160 OI-12; `soak` is in table (c)'s scene list):

- `BenchScene::Soak`, argument name `soak`; default duration 600 s and warm-up 0 s when `--duration` and `--warmup` are not given (the `tl-app` arm passes 30 and 5 by default, so the soak is run with explicit `--duration 600 --warmup 0`).
- Window 1: the `perf-cpu` composition (UI-PRF-053) but with every series fed at 1 Hz (one `BenchEngine` tick per second instead of 10 Hz), smooth graphs on.
- Windows 2 and 3: bench-only windows, 600 x 300 logical px each, each with one `ChartView` (E19-A1) of one synthetic 1 Hz series (window 2: CPU total; window 3: Memory), titles "tasklens Soak Graph 1" and "tasklens Soak Graph 2". These are not the P3 detached graph windows of E26; they only exercise three frame loops.
- The `FrameProbe` is not started (it would force frames and hide the bug). Each window has its own `AnimationDriver`; at the end the scene sums their `FrameStats.stalls` into the report's `stalls` and logs each window's count at `info` on target `tasklens::perf`.
- No input is sent. The scene ends after the duration and quits.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `--bench soak --duration 600 --warmup 0` **When** run on the owner machine with no input **Then** three windows open and the run exits 0 after 600 s with a report whose `"scene"` is `"soak"`.
- **Given** a `TestAppContext` soak with 10 s of simulated time **When** it ends **Then** three windows existed and `FrameStats.requested > 0` in each (charts with smooth graphs request frames).
- **Given** a soak report **When** read **Then** `stalls` equals the sum of the three drivers' stall counts.
- **Given** `BenchScene::from_arg("soak")` **When** called **Then** it returns `Soak`.

title: E01-017 First-frame, minimized-CPU and RSS gate measurements
description:
## Context
Three ADR-014 gates are not covered by the scene JSON: first frame warm (<= 200 ms median of 5 launches, from process start time `/proc/self/stat` field 22 to the first frame callback), first frame cold (<= 500 ms after dropping the page cache, run by the owner), and process CPU with the window minimized and recording off (<= 0.3% of one core over 60 s). ## Deliverable
Fill the section "First frame, minimized CPU and RSS" of `docs/spike/phase0-results.md`:

1. First frame, warm: run the normal release build (`target/release/tasklens`, without `bench`) 5 times in a row; after each first frame, close the main window (ADR-010: closing it quits the app when the tray is off). 3. Minimized CPU: start tasklens normally, minimize the window, wait 10 s, then read `utime + stime` (fields 14 and 15 of `/proc/<pid>/stat`, in clock ticks, `getconf CLK_TCK`) at t = 0 and t = 60 s; CPU % = 100 x delta ticks / CLK_TCK / 60. Recording is off (P0 has no history). PASS if <= 0.3%.

title: E01-021 Phase-0 manual checklist: CSD, monitors, lock, suspend, restore, sharpness, run return
description:
## Context
ADR-014 and ADR-010 fix a manual checklist that headless tests cannot cover. It settles U-36 (CSD on KWin, with the predetermined fallback to server decorations), U-3 (KWin causes a render when a minimized window is restored) and U-2 (`Application::run` returns on Linux after `cx.quit()`). Sources: ADR-014 checklist, ADR-010 decorations, hidden state, multi-monitor, close behaviour, D-006, U-2, U-3, U-36.

## Deliverable
Fill the section "Manual checklist" of `docs/spike/phase0-results.md` with a table `| # | Check | How | Result (PASS or FAIL) | Notes |`, one row per check, run on the owner machine with the normal release build (main window, client-side decorations, the default):

CSD checks (ADR-010; U-36):
1. Drag the window by the title bar.
2. Double-click the title bar maximizes; double-click again restores.
3. Restore from maximized with the caption button.
4. Resize from all four edges and all four corners.
5. Right-click the title bar opens the KWin window menu.
6. Tiling (Meta+Left, Meta+Right, quick tile by dragging to a screen edge).
Multi-monitor and session (ADR-010):
7. Move the window across all three monitors.
8. Straddle two monitors; content renders on both parts.
9. Maximize on each monitor.
10. Unplug one monitor and plug it back while tasklens runs.
11. Lock and unlock the session.
12. One suspend and resume (zed#58382 atlas corruption check: text and icons intact after resume).
13. 10-minute zed#64499 soak: link to the soak section result (E01-018 and E01-020).
14. Minimize and restore re-renders: with the Performance tab showing moving charts, minimize for 30 s, restore; the charts show current data within 1 s without moving the mouse over the window (U-3).
15. Text sharpness at 110%: a screenshot viewed at 2x zoom shows no blur; attach the screenshot path (not committed if it shows personal data).
Run return (U-2):
16. Start tasklens from a terminal with `TASKLENS_LOG=info`, close the main window; record whether the log shows the line `main` writes after `Application::run` returns (the `ShutdownReport` log from E33-A1) or only the `on_app_quit` path ran. Record "U-2 confirmed" or "U-2 failed".

Then add to "Unverified items settled in phase 0":
- U-36: "confirmed, client-side decorations stay the default" if checks 1 to 6 all pass; otherwise "failed on check <n>: `appearance.decorations` default becomes \"server\" (ADR-010, no further discussion)" and tell the leader, who opens the bead that changes the default.
- U-3: "confirmed" if check 14 passes; otherwise "failed: the hidden-state timer calls `window.refresh()` every 1 s while hidden (ADR-010)" and tell the leader (E16's hub timer bead).

title: E01-022 Record the polkit dismissed and denied error names (U-39)
description:
## Context
U-39: on systemd D-Bus calls under `org.freedesktop.systemd1.manage-units`, a dismissed polkit prompt and a denial may come back as the same access-denied error. Phase 0 records both error names. R-117: until verified, systemd D-Bus paths show "<failure text>: not authorized" for both; if phase 0 finds a distinguishing error name, the dismissed case switches to "Authentication cancelled". Sources: U-39, R-117, UI-SYS-007.

## Deliverable
Fill the section "polkit error names (U-39)" of `docs/spike/phase0-results.md`:
1. Pick, with the owner, one system service that is safe to restart on this machine (the owner names it; record its name).
2. Dismissed case: run `busctl --system call --allow-interactive-authorization=yes org.freedesktop.systemd1 /org/freedesktop/systemd1 org.freedesktop.systemd1.Manager RestartUnit ss <unit> replace` as the normal user, and press Cancel (or Esc) on the KDE polkit prompt. Record the full D-Bus error name and message printed by `busctl`.
3. Denied case: run the same command and enter a wrong password until polkit gives up (3 attempts), or, if the owner prefers, use a test user that is not an administrator. Record the error name and message.
4. No-agent case (for completeness, R-117): run the command with `--allow-interactive-authorization=no`; record the error (expected `org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.InteractiveAuthorizationRequired`).
5. In "Unverified items settled in phase 0", write U-39: "confirmed: both cases return <name>" or "failed: dismissed returns <name1>, denied returns <name2>; the dismissed case shows \"Authentication cancelled\" (R-117)". Tell the leader the result, because E11 and E27 beads use it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the three runs **When** recorded **Then** each lists the exact error name and message.
- **Given** the names are equal for dismissed and denied **When** recorded **Then** the U-39 line says "confirmed".
- **Given** the names differ **When** recorded **Then** the U-39 line gives both names and the "Authentication cancelled" rule.

title: E01-024 Collection-cost gates with the real engine (U-10)
description:
## Context
ADR-014 gates: collection cost with the real engine <= 2% of one core with the Performance tab visible, and <= 3.5% with the Processes tab visible with this machine's processes. U-10 asks whether both are reachable. Decision rule step 4: collection-cost gates are engine work and never trigger the UI fallback, so they do not block E01-A2. They need the P1 Processes worker (E10-A1) and system workers (E12-A2). The measurement method is fixed by R-160 OI-15. Sources: ADR-014, ADR-016 verification (15 ms sweep), U-10, open question 1.

## Deliverable
Fill the section "Collection cost" of `docs/spike/phase0-results.md`:
1. Method (R-160 OI-15): run the normal release build; for 60 s sum `utime + stime` of the engine threads, which are the threads in `/proc/<pid>/task/*/comm` whose name starts with `tl-engine` (ADR-004 `thread_name_prefix("tl-engine")`), plus the `tl-gpu-probe` child if running; percent of one core = 100 x delta ticks / CLK_TCK / 60.
2. Run once with the Performance tab visible (CPU page) and once with the Processes tab visible, on this machine's normal process set; record the process count from `ls /proc | grep -c '^[0-9]'`.
3. Record both values with PASS or FAIL against 2% and 3.5%, and the U-10 line: "confirmed" if both pass, else "failed: <which>", with the note that this is engine work (decision rule step 4).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the two 60 s runs **When** recorded **Then** each lists the tick deltas, CLK_TCK, process count, percent and PASS or FAIL.
- **Given** a FAIL **When** recorded **Then** the U-10 line names the failing gate and the leader is told; no UI fallback is triggered.

title: E01-004 Bench synthetic CPU, device and stats sources
description:
## Context
Every phase-0 scene uses deterministic synthetic data from `tl-ui/src/bench/synth.rs`, seeded with 42, so runs are comparable (ADR-014, UI-PRF-053). This bead writes the generators for the `perf-cpu` family: 32 per-core CPU series at 10 Hz, kernel and total series, 9 sidebar device series at 1 Hz, and the 12 live Details values at 1 Hz. The table generator for `table-2000` is added to the same file by E01-008. Sources: UI-PRF-053 (formulas, device list, stats values), UI-PRF-024 (rows 1 to 12), ADR-003 (`Sample`, `SeriesId`, `MetricId`, `DeviceIdx`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/bench/synth.rs`, plus the line `pub mod synth;` in `bench/mod.rs`.

- `pub const SEED: u64 = 42;`
- `pub struct BenchRng` : a deterministic PRNG with `new(seed: u64)`, `next_u64()`, `next_f32_unit()` (uniform in [0, 1)), `uniform(lo: f32, hi: f32) -> f32`, `gaussian(sigma: f32) -> f32`. Algorithm (R-142 item 8): SplitMix64 for `next_u64`, Box-Muller for `gaussian`, written in this file with no new dependency. `tl-ui`'s allowed row in ADR-001 has no PRNG crate. Do not add a crate.
- `pub struct CpuSynth` with `pub fn new(rng: &mut BenchRng) -> Self` and `pub fn sample(&mut self, t_s: f64) -> CpuFrame`:
  - 32 logical CPUs. Per core c, drawn once at construction in core order: `base_c = uniform(5, 60)`, `P_c = uniform(3, 17)` seconds.
  - Per sample: `value_c = clamp(base_c + 25 * sin(2 * PI * t_s / P_c) + gaussian(4), 0, 100)`; `kernel_c = clamp(0.2 * value_c + gaussian(1), 0, 100)`; `total = mean(value_c)`; total kernel = `mean(kernel_c)`.
  - `pub struct CpuFrame { pub per_core: [f32; 32], pub per_core_kernel: [f32; 32], pub total: f32, pub total_kernel: f32 }`.
- `pub struct DeviceSynth` with `sample_1hz(&mut self, rng: &mut BenchRng) -> DeviceFrame` for the 9 sidebar cards, in this order: CPU, Memory, GPU 0, Disk 0, Disk 1, Disk 2, Disk 3, enp38s0, tailscale0. Values (UI-PRF-053): memory 55% with a random walk of +-1 (each second add a uniform step in [-1, 1], clamp to [0, 100]; R-160 OI-2); GPU 10% +- 8 (a fresh uniform draw in [2, 18] each second); disks bursts 0..100% with p = 0.1 per second, else 0; networks bursts 0.01..5 Mbps with p = 0.1 per second, else 0.01 Mbps (R-160 OI-2). The CPU card uses the 10 Hz total from `CpuSynth`, not this generator.
- `pub struct StatsSynth` with `sample_1hz(&mut self, rng, t_s) -> StatsFrame` for Details rows 1 to 12 of UI-PRF-024: Utilization and Kernel time from `CpuSynth`; Processes 295 +- 3; Threads 5 596 +- 20; Handles 253 248 +- 500; Up time counting up from a fixed start; Speed 4631 +- 200 MHz; Temperature 52 +- 2 degrees C; Load average a random walk: each second add a uniform step in [-0.05, 0.05] to each of the three values, clamped at 0, start 1.24 0.98 0.87 (R-160 OI-2). "X +- N" means a fresh uniform draw in [X - N, X + N] each second, rounded for integer counts (R-160 OI-2). Rows 8 (Base speed 4200 MHz), 9 (Sockets 1) and 10 (Power draw, hidden in P0 because it is a P2 row) are static. Rows 13 to 26 are static (`DEVICES`).
- `pub fn prefill(cpu: &mut CpuSynth, ...) -> PrefilledSeries`: produces 600 samples per 10 Hz series (60 s range) and 60 per 1 Hz series, timestamps ending at the scene start time, so decimation and geometry rebuild run from frame 1 (UI-PRF-053).
- Timestamps are `TimeNs` (CLOCK_BOOTTIME ns, ADR-003). Sample values are `f32` in `tl_model::series::Sample`.
- Generators never allocate per sample after construction (fixed arrays).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** two `BenchRng::new(42)` **When** each draws 1,000 `next_u64` **Then** the sequences are identical.
- **Given** two `CpuSynth` built from `BenchRng::new(42)` **When** each produces its first 1,000 samples at 10 Hz **Then** every `per_core`, `per_core_kernel` and `total` value is bit-identical.
- **Given** any sample **When** checked **Then** every per-core and kernel value is in [0, 100] and `total` equals the mean of the 32 per-core values within 1e-4.
- **Given** a `CpuSynth` from seed 42 **When** its 32 `base_c` and `P_c` are read **Then** every `base_c` is in [5, 60) and every `P_c` is in [3, 17).
- **Given** `prefill` at scene start `t0` **When** it returns **Then** each 10 Hz series has exactly 600 samples with the last timestamp `t0` and spacing 100 ms, and each 1 Hz series has 60 samples with spacing 1 s.
- **Given** `StatsSynth` **When** 100 samples are drawn **Then** Processes stays in 292..=298, Threads in 5 576..=5 616, Handles in 252 748..=253 748, Speed in 4431..=4831 MHz, Temperature in 50..=54 C.
- **Given** `DeviceSynth` **When** 10 000 one-second samples are drawn **Then** the fraction of non-zero disk samples per disk is 0.1 +- 0.02.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/synth.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/mod.rs`: change, add `pub mod synth;`.

## Tests
- `bench::synth::tests::synth_is_deterministic`: two runs with seed 42 produce identical first 1,000 samples (UI-PRF-053 test name).
- `bench::synth::tests::cpu_values_in_range`: range and mean checks above.
- `bench::synth::tests::prefill_lengths_and_spacing`: 600 and 60 samples, spacing, last timestamp.
- `bench::synth::tests::stats_ranges`: the StatsSynth ranges above.
- `bench::synth::tests::disk_burst_probability`: 0.1 +- 0.02 over 10 000 samples.
Run with `cargo test -p tl-ui --features bench bench::synth`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A (pure functions).
- Validity: every synthetic sample is a valid measured value (`SampleFlags` empty); no gaps.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: no allocation per sample; the generators run on the bench publisher thread, whose CPU counts toward process CPU, so keep them cheap (32 sines per 100 ms).
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Settled: PRNG is SplitMix64 plus Box-Muller in this file, no PRNG crate (R-142 item 8). Value rules (R-160 OI-2): "X +- N" is a fresh uniform draw in [X - N, X + N] each second (integers rounded for counts); "random walk +- 1" adds a uniform step in [-1, 1] each second and clamps to [0, 100]; the load average walk step is uniform in [-0.05, 0.05], clamped at 0, start 1.24 0.98 0.87; network bursts use the disk rule (p = 0.1 per second, else 0.01 Mbps).
- `std::f64::consts::PI`; `f32::clamp`.
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...`. Bench and gate runs are not builds: run them with nothing else heavy on the machine. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
close_reason: bench/synth.rs: SplitMix64 + Box-Muller BenchRng, CpuSynth, DeviceSynth, StatsSynth, prefill; pub mod synth in bench/mod.rs. 5 tests pass. Commit 48e3e16

title: E01-005 BenchEngine: scripted EngineClient for the bench scenes
description:
## Context
The scenes replace the real `EngineClient` with `BenchEngine`, a fake engine with a scripted publisher (ADR-013 fake engine, UI-PRF-053), except the `bridge` scene, where the total CPU series comes from the real engine. `BenchEngine` builds full `Snapshot`s from the synthetic generators in `synth.rs` and publishes them like the real bridge: replace the latest snapshot, then send one wake token. Sources: ADR-005 (`EngineClient`, one-token wake), ADR-003 (`Snapshot`, `SeriesSet`, `SeriesView`, `DeviceCatalog`, `ComponentHeader`), UI-PRF-053.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/bench/engine.rs`, plus `pub mod engine;` in `bench/mod.rs`.

```rust
pub enum BenchFeed {
    /// Every series synthetic (perf-cpu, static, table-2000).
    Synthetic,
    /// CPU_TOTAL and CPU_KERNEL of the all-CPUs device come from this client; the 32 per-core
    /// series and every other value stay synthetic (bridge scene).
    Bridge(Arc<dyn EngineClient>),
}
pub struct BenchEngine { /* latest: Mutex<Arc<Snapshot>>, wake channel, recorded commands */ }
impl BenchEngine {
    pub fn start(feed: BenchFeed, seed: u64, t0: TimeNs) -> Arc<Self>;
    pub fn stop(&self);                          // joins the publisher thread
    pub fn commands(&self) -> Vec<Command>;      // recorded, for tests
    pub fn published_10hz(&self) -> u64;         // count of 10 Hz publishes
}
impl EngineClient for BenchEngine { ... }
```

- Publisher: one `std::thread` named `tl-bench-pub` with absolute deadlines every 100 ms from `t0` (no drift: next deadline = previous deadline + 100 ms, sleep until it). Each tick appends one `CpuFrame` sample to the 32 per-core, 32 per-core kernel, total and total-kernel series; every 10th tick also appends the 1 Hz device and stats samples. Then it builds a new `Snapshot` (sequence + 1, `published_ns = now_boot_ns()`), stores it, and sends one wake token with `try_send` on an `async_channel::bounded(1)` (a full channel means a wake is already pending; ignore it).
- Series rings: fixed-capacity buffers of 602 samples for 10 Hz series and 62 for 1 Hz series (ADR-003 fast tier), pre-filled with `synth::prefill`. Each publish creates a new `Arc<[Sample]>` only for series that changed; unchanged series reuse their `Arc<SeriesView>` (ADR-003 `SeriesSet` rule) and keep their `version`.
- Device catalog: `DeviceIdx(0)` = `CpuPackage` (display name "CPU"), `DeviceIdx(1..=32)` = `CpuLogical { id: 0..=31 }` (placeholder topology 16 cores x 2 threads, R-160 OI-2), then Memory, GPU 0, Disk 0 to Disk 3, `enp38s0`, `tailscale0` with the identities of ADR-003 (`Gpu`, `Disk`, `Net`) and fixed placeholder fields (major/minor 259:0..3, ifindex 2 and 3, netns inode 1; R-160 OI-2). `present = true`, `generation = 0`.
- Series ids: `MetricId::CPU_TOTAL`, `CPU_KERNEL` on each CPU device; `MEM_USED` on Memory; `GPU_UTIL` on GPU 0; `DISK_ACTIVE` on disks; `NET_RX` and `NET_TX` on networks (ADR-003 constants). `SystemSnapshot` carries the 12 live Details values and a `CpuTopology` of 32 logical CPUs, 16 cores, 2 per core, all `CoreKind::Standard`.
- Bridge feed: on each tick, read `client.latest()`; copy its newest `CPU_TOTAL` and `CPU_KERNEL` samples of the `CpuPackage` device into the bench series (no synthetic total); record for each copied sample `(sample.t_ns, real_snapshot.published_ns)` into a bounded ring of 1,024 entries exposed as `pub fn bridge_origin(&self, t_ns: TimeNs) -> Option<TimeNs>` for the latency measurement in `stats.rs`. Also wake when the real client's wake fires, so a real 10 Hz sample is republished within one tick; count real samples received in `pub fn bridge_samples(&self) -> u64`.
- `set_demand`, `set_settings` store the last value; `send` records the command and returns `Ok(())`; `action_events` returns a receiver that never yields; `journal` returns a handle whose channel is closed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `BenchEngine::start(Synthetic, 42, t0)` **When** 1.0 s of wall time passes **Then** `published_10hz()` is 10 +- 1 and the wake receiver yielded at least one token.
- **Given** two consecutive snapshots **When** compared **Then** `sequence` increased by 1 and the Memory series `Arc` is pointer-equal unless a 1 Hz tick happened between them.
- **Given** a fresh start **When** `latest()` is read before the first tick **Then** every 10 Hz series already has 600 samples (prefill).
- **Given** the catalog **When** read **Then** it has 41 entries: 1 package, 32 logical CPUs, and the 8 non-CPU sidebar devices in the order Memory, GPU 0, Disk 0, Disk 1, Disk 2, Disk 3, enp38s0, tailscale0.
- **Given** `BenchFeed::Bridge(fake)` where `fake` is a `testing::FakeEngine` publishing a CPU_TOTAL sample every 100 ms **When** 1 s passes **Then** the bench total series contains the fake's sample values and `bridge_origin(t)` returns the fake snapshot's `published_ns` for each.
- **Given** `stop()` **When** it returns **Then** the publisher thread has exited and no further wake tokens arrive.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/engine.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/mod.rs`: change, add `pub mod engine;`.

## Tests
- `bench::engine::tests::publishes_at_10hz`: 10 +- 1 publishes per second.
- `bench::engine::tests::unchanged_series_reuse_arc`: pointer equality rule.
- `bench::engine::tests::prefilled_before_first_tick`.
- `bench::engine::tests::catalog_has_41_entries_in_order`.
- `bench::engine::tests::bridge_feed_copies_real_total`: uses `crate::testing::fake_engine::FakeEngine` (E16-A1).
- `bench::engine::tests::stop_joins_thread`.
Run with `cargo test -p tl-ui --features bench bench::engine`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `send` never fails; a panic in the publisher thread is a bench bug and aborts the run (the scene reports it, E01-007).
- Validity: all synthetic components `Validity::Valid`; components the scenes do not draw (connections, services, startup, inventory, windows, details, history) are their `Default` empty values with `Validity::Unsupported` headers.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: per tick, allocate only the changed series' `Arc<[Sample]>` and one `Snapshot`; no per-tick `String` formatting.
- Privacy: N/A (synthetic data).

## Notes
- `tl-ui` may not depend on `tl-engine` or `arc-swap` (ADR-001 allowed rows); use `std::sync::Mutex<Arc<Snapshot>>` for `latest` and take the lock only to clone or replace the `Arc`.
- `async_channel` comes through `tl-model` (allowed there); if `tl-ui` needs it as a direct dependency, that is an allowed-row question: report it, do not add it.
- If any `Snapshot` component type has no `Default` in E03-A2, build an empty value explicitly; do not edit `tl-model`.
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...`. Bench and gate runs are not builds: run them with nothing else heavy on the machine. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
close_reason: BenchEngine in crates/tl-ui/src/bench/engine.rs (c70e34a, 94356cf): 10 Hz publisher thread, prefilled rings with Arc reuse, 41-entry placeholder catalog, bridge feed with bridge_origin; 7 tests pass

title: E01-006 Bench frame statistics and JSON report
description:
## Context
ADR-014 fixes how the bench measures: UI thread CPU per frame from `CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID` read in each `on_next_frame` callback, frame interval from `Instant::now()` in each callback, missed frames above 1.5 x the output period, process CPU over the run, `VmRSS` at the end, PSS reported only, stalls from the `AnimationDriver`. This bead writes the collector and the JSON report. Sources: ADR-014 measurement tools, UI-PRF-053 outputs, ADR-010 stall detection (E19-A1 `FrameStats.stalls`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/bench/stats.rs`, plus `pub mod stats;` in `bench/mod.rs`.

```rust
/// Clocks the UI crate cannot read itself (tl-ui has no rustix or libc, ADR-001).
/// tl-app supplies them (E01-009) as function pointers over rustix::time::clock_gettime (R-144 item 5).
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub struct BenchClocks {
    pub thread_cpu_ns: fn() -> u64,    // ClockId::ThreadCPUTime of the calling thread
    pub process_cpu_ns: fn() -> u64,   // ClockId::ProcessCPUTime (utime + stime of the process)
}
pub const OUTPUT_PERIOD_NS: u64 = 6_944_444;      // 144 Hz fixture output
pub const MISSED_FRAME_NS: u64 = 10_416_667;      // 1.5 x period (10.42 ms)
pub const LONG_MISS_NS: u64 = 20_833_333;         // 3 x period

pub struct FrameProbe { /* intervals_ns: Vec<u64>, cpu_ns: Vec<u64>, last: Option<(Instant, u64)>, active: bool */ }
impl FrameProbe {
    pub fn new(clocks: BenchClocks, capacity: usize) -> Self;   // capacity 144 * 40
    /// Registers window.on_next_frame; the callback records one frame and re-registers while active.
    pub fn start(this: Rc<RefCell<Self>>, window: &mut Window);
    pub fn stop(&mut self);
    pub fn reset(&mut self);   // drops samples taken during warm-up
}
pub struct Percentiles { pub p50: f64, pub p99: f64, pub max: f64 }
pub fn percentiles_ms(ns: &[u64]) -> Percentiles;   // nearest-rank on a sorted copy
pub fn count_missed(intervals_ns: &[u64]) -> (u32 /*> 1.5x*/, u32 /*> 3x*/);

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct BenchReport {
    pub scene: &'static str,
    pub frames: u64,
    pub frame_cpu_ms: Percentiles,
    pub missed_frames: u32,
    pub long_missed_frames: u32,                 // > 3 x period (R-160 OI-3)
    pub process_cpu_pct: f64,
    pub probe_cpu_pct: Option<f64>,
    pub rss_mb: f64,
    pub pss_mb: f64,
    pub stalls: u32,
    pub bridge_latency_ms: Option<LatencyPct>,   // { p50, p99 }
    pub gpu: Option<GpuReport>,                  // { power_w, util_pct }
}
pub fn read_rss_pss_mb() -> (f64, f64);   // VmRSS from /proc/self/status, Pss from /proc/self/smaps_rollup
pub fn write_json(report: &BenchReport, path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<()>;   // serde_json, pretty
```

JSON shape (UI-PRF-053 with R-160 OI-3, field names exact): `{ scene, frames, frame_cpu_ms: { p50, p99, max }, missed_frames, long_missed_frames, process_cpu_pct, probe_cpu_pct, rss_mb, pss_mb, stalls, bridge_latency_ms: { p50, p99 } | null, gpu: { power_w, util_pct } | null }` (UI-PRF-053). Field order as listed. `null` for `probe_cpu_pct`, `bridge_latency_ms` and `gpu` when not measured. Phase-0 reports carry `gpu: null`; E01-023 fills it once the probe exists (R-160 OI-14). MB means 1,000,000 bytes (R-160 OI-4).

Rules:
- The probe records interval and thread-CPU delta between consecutive callbacks only; the first callback after `start` or `reset` records nothing.
- `process_cpu_pct = 100 * delta(process_cpu_ns) / delta(wall ns)` over the measured window (after warm-up).
- `stalls` is copied from the window's `AnimationDriver` `FrameStats.stalls` (E19-A1) at the end, minus its value at the end of warm-up.
- Missed frames: `count_missed` over the measured intervals. `missed_frames` is the count above 1.5 x period; `long_missed_frames` is the count above 3 x period, for the gate "none above 3 x period". `long_missed_frames` goes right after `missed_frames` in the JSON (R-160 OI-3).
- Parsing `/proc/self/status`: the `VmRSS:` line, value in kB (x 1024 bytes). `/proc/self/smaps_rollup`: the `Pss:` line in kB. Missing file or line gives 0.0 and a `warn!(target: "tasklens::perf", ...)`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** intervals `[6.9, 6.9, 11.0, 25.0]` ms **When** `count_missed` runs **Then** it returns `(2, 1)`.
- **Given** 100 values 1..=100 ms **When** `percentiles_ms` runs **Then** p50 = 50.0, p99 = 99.0, max = 100.0 (nearest-rank).
- **Given** an empty slice **When** `percentiles_ms` runs **Then** all three are 0.0 and nothing panics.
- **Given** a `/proc/self/status` fixture string with `VmRSS:\t  123456 kB` **When** parsed **Then** rss is 126.418944 MB.
- **Given** a report with `bridge_latency_ms: None` **When** written **Then** the JSON has `"bridge_latency_ms": null` and the keys appear in the UI-PRF-053 order, with `long_missed_frames` right after `missed_frames` (R-160 OI-3).
- **Given** a running `FrameProbe` in a `TestAppContext` window **When** 10 frames are drawn and `stop` is called **Then** 9 intervals are recorded and no further `on_next_frame` is registered.
- **Given** `reset()` after warm-up **When** called **Then** earlier samples are gone and the next callback records nothing (fresh baseline).

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/stats.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/bench/mod.rs`: change, add `pub mod stats;`.

## Tests
- `bench::stats::tests::count_missed_thresholds`
- `bench::stats::tests::percentiles_nearest_rank`
- `bench::stats::tests::percentiles_empty`
- `bench::stats::tests::parse_vmrss_and_pss` (fixture strings, not the live files)
- `bench::stats::tests::json_shape_and_order` (serialize, compare key order to the UI-PRF-053 list including `long_missed_frames`)
- `bench::stats::tests::frame_probe_stops` (`#[gpui_kit::test]`)
Run with `cargo test -p tl-ui --features bench bench::stats`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: unreadable `/proc` files give 0.0 plus a warning; never a panic.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: the probe callback must not allocate (pre-sized `Vec`s, capacity 144 x 40 = 5 760 frames); it does two clock reads and two pushes.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- `Window::on_next_frame` is at gpui-pre 0.3.7 `src/window.rs:2602`; it calls `schedule_frame()` and wakes the platform, so a running probe keeps frames coming. Use it only in scenes whose content animates every frame anyway (`perf-cpu`, `table-2000`, `bridge`); `static` and `soak` must not start it (E01-007, E01-015).
- `window.frame_duration_snapshot()` (`src/window.rs:3469`, `profiler` feature) gives GPUI's own frame durations; it is not the ADR-014 metric. Do not use it for the gates.
- `serde_json` is in `tl-ui`'s allowed row (ADR-001).
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo ...`. Bench and gate runs are not builds: run them with nothing else heavy on the machine. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
close_reason: bench/stats.rs: FrameProbe, percentiles_ms, count_missed, process_cpu_pct, BenchReport JSON, read_rss_pss_mb, write_json; 8 tests pass. Commit ed5ab44

title: E01-007 Bench scenes perf-cpu, static and bridge with the run loop
description:
## Context
This bead builds the scene runner and the three Performance-tab scenes of ADR-014 and UI-PRF-053. Each scene opens one window with the real production views (the CPU page with chart element, per-core grid, sidebar and Details grid from E24-A1) fed by `BenchEngine`, waits out the warm-up, measures for the duration, writes the JSON report and quits. Sources: ADR-014 (fixture, scenes, gates), UI-PRF-053 (exact composition), ADR-009 (AnimationDriver), ADR-010 (stalls).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/bench/scenes.rs`, `crates/tl-ui/tests/bench_scenes.rs`, and in `bench/mod.rs` the line `pub mod scenes;` plus the public entry point:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum BenchScene { PerfCpu, Table2000, Bridge, Static }
impl BenchScene {
    pub fn from_arg(s: &str) -> Option<Self>;   // "perf-cpu", "table-2000", "bridge", "static"
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str;
}
pub struct BenchOptions { pub duration_s: u32, pub warmup_s: u32, pub json: Option<PathBuf> }  // defaults 30, 5, None
/// Called by tl-app inside Application::run. `real` is Some only for Bridge.
pub fn run(cx: &mut App, scene: BenchScene, opts: BenchOptions, clocks: BenchClocks,
           real: Option<Arc<dyn EngineClient>>) -> Task<Result<BenchReport, BenchError>>;
/// Failure text shown by tl-app; Display prints the inner string.
pub struct BenchError(pub String);
```

Scene composition (UI-PRF-053, exact):
- Common: Phase-0 fixture (ADR-014, UI-PRF-053): window 1600 x 1000 logical px, opened on the 144 Hz output at 110% compositor scale, focused, `motion.smooth_graphs = true`, theme Default Dark, `ui_scale_pct = 100`, `graph_range_s = 60`, synthetic data from `tl-ui/src/bench/` with PRNG seed 42. Window options: `size(px(1600.), px(1000.))`, opaque background, client decorations, `app_id` `io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens`. The Processes tab and all other tabs are not built.
- `perf-cpu`: the Performance page with the CPU page selected, sidebar visible at `nav_width = 252`. The CPU page renders the total CPU chart (width W x 300 px, fill + line + kernel line) above the 32-core grid (8 x 4, kernel overlays on), through the bench-only flag `CpuPage.bench_show_both`, declared behind `#[cfg(feature = "bench")]` in E24's `cpu.rs` by E24-A1 (crw.1, R-160 OI-5). Set it to `true` in this scene; do not edit `cpu.rs` from this bead. Sidebar: 9 cards CPU, Memory, GPU 0, Disk 0, Disk 1, Disk 2, Disk 3, enp38s0, tailscale0. Details grid: rows 1 to 12 live at 1 Hz, rows 13 to 26 static. Per-core percent labels re-format at 10 Hz.
- `static`: `perf-cpu` with `motion.smooth_graphs = false`. The `FrameProbe` is not started. At the end assert `FrameStats.requested == 0` for the window's `AnimationDriver`; a non-zero value fails the run with error text "static scene requested animation frames".
- `bridge`: `perf-cpu` with `BenchFeed::Bridge(real)`. Extra measure: wake-to-render latency, from `Snapshot.published_ns` of the real snapshot that first carried a sample (via `BenchEngine::bridge_origin`) to the first `ChartElement::paint` that includes that sample; use the paint record of E19 (`AnimationDriver::install_paint_log`, `take_paint_log`, `PaintRecord { view, newest_ns, painted_at_ns }`; yrf.7 and yrf.9, exported by E19-A1 yrf.1). The hook sits behind `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-hooks"))`, and tl-ui's feature `bench` enables `test-hooks` (R-160 OI-6). Report p50 and p99 in `bridge_latency_ms`. The run fails with "bridge: only N samples arrived" when fewer than 295 real samples arrive in 30 s.
Run loop: open window, start `BenchEngine`, start `FrameProbe` (not in `static`), wait `warmup_s`, `reset()` the probe and take baselines (process CPU ns, wall ns, stalls), wait `duration_s`, stop, build `BenchReport`, write JSON if requested, print the report as one JSON line on stdout, then `cx.quit()`. title: E31 tl-tray, rasterizer, tray bridge, tray menus and tooltips
description: Epic E31 (tray). Phases: P3. Estimated beads: 15. Scope, sources and file ownership: docs/plan/00-epics.md sections 1 and 2, key E31.

title: E31-A1 Tray crate
description:
## Context
Anchor E31-A1: the `tl-tray` crate works end to end. A dedicated thread receives `TrayModel`s from tl-ui once per second, keeps one ksni item per tray graph plus the optional main icon, rasterizes each graph, and updates an icon only when its bytes changed. It also records U-31 (ksni 0.3.6 with `async-io` and `blocking` brings no Tokio). Sources: ADR-010 Tray, PERF-088 (one StatusNotifierItem per graph; updates at most 1 Hz and only when pixels changed), PERF-091 (main icon not registered while any graph exists), PERF-092 (re-registration within 1 s with the same pixels), UI-PRF-050 (update rule), UI-PRF-051, UI-SHL-113 (main icon contract), R-027, U-31.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-tray/src/lib.rs`:
```rust
pub use tl_model::tray::{TrayServiceEnd, TrayModel, TrayEvent, TrayGraphId};

/// ARGB32 pixels of the app icon for the main tray item, supplied by the caller (b1-infra open item E31-4).
pub struct MainIcon { pub argb_22: Vec<u8>, pub argb_44: Vec<u8> }

/// Starts the thread "tasklens-tray". It runs until the model channel closes, then shuts every item down and returns.
pub fn spawn(end: TrayServiceEnd, main_icon: MainIcon) -> std::io::Result<std::thread::JoinHandle<()>>;

pub fn dropped_events() -> u64; // from item.rs
```
`crates/tl-tray/src/model.rs` (private): `struct ItemState { handle: ksni::blocking::Handle<TrayItem>, icon_22: Vec<u8>, icon_44: Vec<u8>, title: Arc<str>, description: Arc<str>, menu: MenuSource }` and `struct Service { graphs: BTreeMap<TrayGraphId, ItemState>, main: Option<ItemState>, scratch_22: Vec<u8>, scratch_44: Vec<u8> }` with `fn apply(&mut self, model: &TrayModel)`.

`apply` rules, per model:
1. For each `frame` in `model.graphs`: render 22 and 44 px into the scratch buffers with `raster::render(frame.series samples or &[], frame.now_ns, frame.range_ns, frame.max, frame.line_rgb, size, scratch)`. When `frame.state` is `NoMatch` or `Ended`, skip rendering and keep the last pixels (the icon freezes, UI-PRF-050). When `Failed` or `series` is `None`, render with empty samples (baseline only).
2. New id: create a `TrayItem` (E31-005) and start it with `ksni::blocking::TrayMethods::spawn`. On error send `TrayEvent::RegisterFailed(id)` and do not keep it.
3. Existing id: compare the scratch buffers with the stored ones byte for byte; call `handle.update` to swap them in only when either differs. Update the tooltip only when title or description text changed. Update the menu source when the colour, range or `model.menu` changed.
4. Ids in the service but not in the model: `handle.shutdown()` and remove.
5. Main icon: it should exist exactly when `model.show_main_icon && model.graphs.is_empty()` (PERF-091 enforced here too). Create, update tooltip on change, or shut down accordingly. Its pixels are `main_icon`.
6. Re-registration (PERF-092): rely on `watcher_offline` returning `true` (E31-005), so ksni registers each item again with its current icon when `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher` gains a new owner. Nothing else is needed in `apply`.

Thread loop: `while let Ok(model) = end.models.recv_blocking() { service.apply(&model) }`, then shut down every handle.

U-31 record: run `cargo xtask check-deps` with `tl-tray` in the `tasklens` graph (after E31-008 it is a dependency of tl-app; before that, run `cargo tree -p tl-tray -e normal,build --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --prefix none --format "{p}"` and check it for the banned list) and write the result into the `U-31` row of `docs/RECONCILIATION.md`'s unverified list as "Confirmed <date>: ksni 0.3.6 graph has no banned crate" or the failing crate. If a banned crate appears, stop and report (ADR-010 fallback needs the leader).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a model with two graphs **When** `apply` runs **Then** two ksni items are spawned and the main icon is not, even if `show_main_icon` is true.
- **Given** a model with no graphs and `show_main_icon = true` **When** `apply` runs **Then** exactly one item, the main icon, exists.
- **Given** a model with no graphs and `show_main_icon = false` **When** `apply` runs **Then** no item exists.
- **Given** two identical models in a row **When** `apply` runs twice **Then** the second run calls `handle.update` zero times.
- **Given** a graph whose newest sample changed **When** `apply` runs **Then** that graph's icon is updated once and the other graph is not.
- **Given** a graph whose state is `Ended` **When** later models carry new samples **Then** its icon bytes stay the same.
- **Given** a model that drops a graph id **When** `apply` runs **Then** that item is shut down.
- **Given** spawning an item fails **When** `apply` runs **Then** `RegisterFailed(id)` is sent and the graph is not kept.
- **Given** the UI drops its model sender **When** the thread sees the channel closed **Then** it shuts every item down and the join handle returns.
- **Given** a private session bus with a fake `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher` **When** the watcher name loses and regains its owner **Then** every item calls `RegisterStatusNotifierItem` again within 1 s with the same icon bytes.

## Files
- `crates/tl-tray/src/lib.rs`: `MainIcon`, `spawn`, re-exports, `dropped_events`.
- `crates/tl-tray/src/model.rs`: `ItemState`, `Service`, `apply`, with `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`.
- `docs/RECONCILIATION.md`: U-31 row result only.

## Tests
`apply` is tested through a small internal trait `ItemBackend` (spawn, update, shutdown) with a fake implementation that counts calls; the real backend wraps ksni.
- `model.rs::tests::tray_main_icon_hidden_with_graphs`: graphs present means no main item.
- `model.rs::tests::main_icon_follows_flag_without_graphs`.
- `model.rs::tests::identical_model_no_update`: zero `update` calls on a repeated model.
- `model.rs::tests::changed_pixels_update_only_that_item`.
- `model.rs::tests::ended_graph_freezes_pixels`.
- `model.rs::tests::removed_graph_shuts_down`.
- `model.rs::tests::spawn_failure_reports_register_failed`.
- `lib.rs::tests::thread_exits_on_closed_channel`.
- `lib.rs::tests::tray_reregisters_on_watcher_restart` (`#[ignore]`, real-system): starts a private `dbus-daemon --session`, owns `org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher` with a fake object that records `RegisterStatusNotifierItem` calls, spawns one graph item, drops and retakes the name, and asserts a second registration within 1 s. `zbus` is allowed here as a dev-dependency only.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: ksni spawn failure sends `RegisterFailed`; the tl-ui bridge shows "Unable to add tray icon graph" (E31-A2).
- Validity: handled by the frame (`state`, `series`), see E31-003.
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: no work besides one rasterization per graph per model (at most 1 Hz). No allocation per tick: scratch buffers are reused and stored buffers are swapped, not reallocated. Nothing runs on the GPUI thread.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Phase P3. Anchor: other epics depend on this bead for the tray service.
- ksni 0.3.6 blocking API: `ksni::blocking::TrayMethods::spawn(self) -> Result<Handle<T>, Error>`, `Handle::update(|t| ..)`, `Handle::shutdown()`; check the exact names in the ksni 0.3.6 source (`src/blocking.rs`).
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-tray` (and `-- --ignored` for the real-system test on the owner machine). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

MenuSource is { color, range_s, state: TrayMenuState }. ksni 0.3.6 watcher_offline returning true makes ksni re-register on a new StatusNotifierWatcher owner, so no zbus code is needed for PERF-092.

title: E31-008 E31: start the tl-tray thread from tl-app main.rs
description:
## Context
Chain edit to `crates/tl-app` (owner E33): `tl-app` is the only crate allowed to depend on both `tl-ui` and `tl-tray` (ADR-001 row: tl-app -> tl-tray (P3)). It creates the tray channels, starts the `tl-tray` thread and hands the UI end to the tray bridge. Sources: ADR-001 allowed rows, ADR-010 Tray, UI-SHL-110 (startup order; step 8 is `Application::run` with `TasklensUi::init`), UI-SHL-113 Build line.

This bead is the allowed E31 chain edit of `tl-app/src/main.rs` (R-161 item 2, 00-epics section 2). It depends on cr0.1 (E33-A1) and also adds the `tl-tray` dependency line to `tl-app/Cargo.toml`. The main icon pixels come from two pre-rendered files under E15's assets (R-161 item 4), created by E31-013 (tasklens-wox.15, R-251); this bead depends on it.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-app/Cargo.toml`: add `tl-tray = { path = "../tl-tray" }` under `[dependencies]` (same form as the other workspace path dependencies). No other change.
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: inside the `Application::run` closure, directly after `TasklensUi::init(..)` returns (UI-SHL-110 step 8), add:
```rust
let (tray_ui, tray_service) = tl_model::tray::tray_channels();
match tl_tray::spawn(tray_service, main_tray_icon()) {
    Ok(_join) => tl_ui::tray_bridge::install(cx, tray_ui),
    Err(e) => tracing::warn!(target: "tasklens::tray", error = %e, "tray thread did not start"),
}
```
  where `main_tray_icon() -> tl_tray::MainIcon` returns `MainIcon { argb_22: include_bytes!("../../../assets/icons/tray-22.argb").to_vec(), argb_44: include_bytes!("../../../assets/icons/tray-44.argb").to_vec() }` (R-161 item 4). The files are raw ARGB32 pixels pre-rendered from `assets/icons/tasklens.svg`: 22 x 22 x 4 = 1,936 bytes and 44 x 44 x 4 = 7,744 bytes. When the spawn fails, `install` is not called, so `TrayStatus` is never set and every tray entry point treats the tray as unavailable. No other change to `main.rs`.
- `Cargo.lock` regenerated.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a session with a StatusNotifierWatcher and `tray.always_show = true` **When** tasklens starts **Then** the main tasklens tray icon appears within 2 s.
- **Given** `main_tray_icon()` **When** called **Then** `argb_22.len() == 1_936` and `argb_44.len() == 7_744` (R-161 item 4).
- **Given** the `tl-tray` thread cannot be spawned **When** tasklens starts **Then** the app starts normally, a `warn` line with target `tasklens::tray` is logged, and no tray entry point is enabled.
- **Given** the workspace **When** `cargo xtask check-deps` runs **Then** it passes: no banned crate in the `tasklens` binary graph, and `tl-ui`'s closure still lacks `tl-tray`, `ksni` and `zbus` (U-31 confirmed for the shipped binary).
- **Given** tasklens quits **When** `Application::run` returns **Then** the tray UI end is dropped, the tray thread shuts its items down and exits, and shutdown still finishes within the existing 1500 ms engine budget.

## Files
- `crates/tl-app/Cargo.toml`: one dependency line.
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs`: the lines above.
- `Cargo.lock`: regenerated.

## Tests
- `crates/tl-app/src/main.rs::tests::main_tray_icon_sizes`: the two byte lengths above.
- `cargo xtask check-deps` passes (records U-31 for the binary).
- Manual check on the owner machine, written into the commit message: tray icon appears with `tray.always_show = true`; "Exit tasklens" from the tray menu quits.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: spawn failure logs `warn!(target: "tasklens::tray", ..)` and continues without a tray.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: one idle thread blocked on a channel when the tray is not in use.
- Privacy: N/A

title: E31-009 E31: add close-to-tray and minimize-to-tray rows to the close decision
description:
## Context
UI-SHL-113 splits the close decision: E20 builds rows 2, 3 and `Quit` in P1; E31 owns row 1 (close to tray) and minimize to tray in P3. This bead adds those two rules to the close decision E20 wrote, and tells the tray bridge when the main window is hidden so the main tray icon appears. Sources: UI-SHL-113 (close decision table, Minimize, main tray icon visibility, tests), APP-047, ADR-010 Close behaviour, UI-SHL-002 (size saved before the window is removed), shell.md caption buttons (Minimize with `tray.minimize_to_tray`), canonical table (a) `[tray] close_to_tray = false`, `minimize_to_tray = false`.

Allowed chain edit (R-161 item 3): this bead edits E20's `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs` (close decision row 1, the `CloseWindow` handler and `on_window_should_close`) and `window/titlebar.rs` (the Minimize caption handler), and depends on jqk.1 (E20-A1). 00-epics section 2 has the row. Change only the lines described below.

## Deliverable
In the E20 close-decision function (the one both `CloseWindow` and `on_window_should_close` call), insert before row 2:
- Row 1: if `cx.try_global::<TrayStatus>()` is `Some(s)` with `s.running && s.available`, and `settings.tray.close_to_tray` is true: save the window size (UI-SHL-002 path, as the other rows do), remove the main window, call `TrayBridge::set_main_window_hidden(true)`, keep app and engine running, and return `true` from `on_window_should_close`.
In the Minimize caption button handler: if the same tray condition holds and `settings.tray.minimize_to_tray` is true, do exactly what row 1 does instead of `window.minimize_window()`. A compositor-initiated minimize (taskbar, KWin shortcut) is not intercepted.
In the reopen path E20 uses for `ShowMainWindow` and `ToggleMainWindow` (and single-instance `Activate`), call `TrayBridge::set_main_window_hidden(false)` after the window is open again.
`Quit` is unchanged: it always quits.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the tray is running and available and `tray.close_to_tray = true` **When** `CloseWindow` is dispatched **Then** the main window is removed, the app stays alive, and the next tray model has `show_main_icon = true` (no tray graphs).
- **Given** the same state **When** `Quit` is dispatched **Then** the app quits.
- **Given** `tray.close_to_tray = false` and no detached graph windows **When** `CloseWindow` is dispatched **Then** the app quits (row 3).
- **Given** `TrayStatus.available = false` and `tray.close_to_tray = true` **When** `CloseWindow` is dispatched **Then** row 1 does not apply and rows 2 and 3 decide.
- **Given** the tray is running and `tray.minimize_to_tray = true` **When** the Minimize caption button is clicked **Then** the window is removed like row 1.
- **Given** `tray.minimize_to_tray = false` **When** the Minimize caption button is clicked **Then** `window.minimize_window()` runs.
- **Given** the window was removed to the tray **When** `ShowMainWindow` is dispatched **Then** the window reopens on the same tab and the next tray model has `show_main_icon` false unless `tray.always_show` is on.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/main.rs`: row 1 in the close decision; reopen path calls `set_main_window_hidden(false)`.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/window/titlebar.rs`: Minimize handler rule.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_tray_bridge.rs`: the tests below (E31's own test file).

## Tests
- `ui_tray_bridge.rs::close_to_tray_keeps_app`: with tray on and close-to-tray on, `CloseWindow` removes the window and the app stays alive; `Quit` ends it (UI-SHL-113).
- `ui_tray_bridge.rs::close_quits_without_tray_setting`.
- `ui_tray_bridge.rs::close_to_tray_needs_available_tray`.
- `ui_tray_bridge.rs::minimize_to_tray_removes_window`.
- `ui_tray_bridge.rs::reopen_clears_hidden_flag`.

## Cross-cutting

- Accessibility: Ctrl+W and Esc-close (`window.close_with_esc`) follow the same decision because they dispatch `CloseWindow`.
- Performance: while removed, demand drops to tray and detached-graph demand only (ADR-008, handled by the hidden rule and E31-007).

title: E31-010 E31: add the Tray rows to window/settings/startup_window.rs
description:
## Context

Sources: UI-SHL-069 (page table), APP-047, canonical table (a) `[tray]`, shell.md settings model (`ToggleSetting(SettingKey)` flips a bool key; `SettingKey` has one variant per table (a) key), 00-epics section 2 (E31 adds the tray rows in `startup_window.rs`, depends on E21-A2).

title: E31-011 E31: add the tray item to pages/processes/menu.rs
description:
## Context
Chain edit to `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/processes/menu.rs` (owner E22): add row-menu item 18, "Add tray icon graph >" or "Remove tray icon graph". Sources: UI-PRC-013 row menu table (item 18: rows P and A shown, U "same", G hidden; hidden for S, G, M and before P3; disabled state X), UI-PRC-020 submenu (CPU, Memory, Disk, Network, GPU, VRAM; an existing source is checked and disabled with tooltip "Already added"), PROC-094 (modes process, name filter, app; "Remove tray icon graph" appears instead when one exists), PERF-088 ("No system tray available"), R-100 (process source string), 00-epics section 2 (E31 adds the tray item, depends on E22-A2).

PENDING LEADER APPROVAL (b1-infra open item E31-5): processes.md names the actions `AddTrayGraph { column }` / `RemoveTrayGraph` and says items read targets from `MenuTargets`, which needs a handler in `pages/processes/mod.rs` where E31 has no chain-edit rule. This bead instead builds the source string from the captured targets when the menu is built and dispatches the fully specified `AddTrayGraph { source, column }` / `RemoveTrayGraph { source, column }` declared in `tray_bridge.rs` (E31-A2). It also needs the row-kind to source mapping below confirmed.

## Deliverable
In `row_menu(..)` in `menu.rs`, at position 18 (after item 17 "Add App Name Graph >", before the separator that precedes "Properties"):
- Source for the single clicked target (the item is hidden when more than one row is selected, flag M, and on group rows G and system pseudo rows S, as the table says):
  - process row (P): `process:<boot_id 16 hex>:<pid>:<start_ticks>` from the row's `ProcessKey`;
  - app row (A): `app:<app id>`;
