title: E31-A2 Tray bridge
description:
## Context
Anchor E31-A2: the tray bridge is complete. On top of the model building (E31-007) it handles every `TrayEvent` from `tl-tray`, owns the add and remove actions that the menus dispatch, saves `[[tray_graphs]]`, shows the tray toasts, and turns left clicks and menu items into the shell's window actions. Other epics depend on this bead for `TrayStatus` and the add and remove actions. Sources: UI-PRF-051 (menu actions, toasts, left click, events forwarded through `async_channel::bounded(16)` and dispatched on the main window, or on the app when the window is closed), PERF-088 (toasts, persistence, "No system tray available"), PERF-090, PROC-094 (toasts incl. "Unable to remove tray icon graph"), UI-PRC-015 toast table (kinds), UI-SHL-113, R-027, R-128 (one `tasklens` action namespace), canonical table (a) `[[tray_graphs]]`.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/tray_bridge.rs`:

Actions (namespace `tasklens`, `#[derive(Action)]` data form, declared here; b1-infra open item E31-5 records who declares them):
```rust
pub struct PerfAddTrayGraph { pub source: SharedString }                       // column "cpu"
pub struct AddTrayGraph { pub source: SharedString, pub column: SharedString }
pub struct RemoveTrayGraph { pub source: SharedString, pub column: SharedString }
```
`install` (E31-007) also registers app-level handlers with `cx.on_action` for these three, and spawns a foreground task that reads `TrayUiEnd.events` with `recv().await` until the channel closes (then sets `TrayStatus.running = false`).

Add rule (`PerfAddTrayGraph`, `AddTrayGraph`): if a graph with the same `source` and `column` exists, Warning toast "Tray icon graph already exists" and no change. Otherwise append `{ source, column, color = "accent", range_s = 60 }` with the next id, write `[[tray_graphs]]` through `TlSettings::update`, and show the Success toast "Tray icon graph added". The icon appears at the next tick.

Remove rule (`RemoveTrayGraph`): if no graph matches `source` and `column`, Error toast "Unable to remove tray icon graph". Otherwise remove it, write `[[tray_graphs]]`, Success toast "Tray icon graph removed".

Events:
| Event | Effect |
|---|---|
| `WatcherOnline` | `TrayStatus.available = true` |
| `WatcherOffline` | `TrayStatus.available = false` |
| `RegisterFailed(id)` | remove graph `id`, write `[[tray_graphs]]` without it, Error toast "Unable to add tray icon graph" |
| `ToggleMainWindow` | dispatch `ToggleMainWindow` |
| `ShowMainWindow` | dispatch `ShowMainWindow` |
| `ShowMiniWindow` | dispatch `ToggleMiniWindow` |
| `Exit` | dispatch `Quit` (always quits, UI-SHL-113) |
| `SetColor { id, color }` | set the graph's `color`, write `[[tray_graphs]]`; redraw at the next tick (at most 1 s) |
| `SetRange { id, secs }` | set `range_s` to `secs` (one of 30, 60, 300, 600; others ignored), write `[[tray_graphs]]` |
| `Remove { id }` | remove, write, Success toast "Tray icon graph removed" |
| `TogglePageSource { source }` | if a graph with that `source` exists remove it (Success "Tray icon graph removed"), else add it with column `"cpu"` (Success "Tray icon graph added") |

Window actions (`ToggleMainWindow`, `ShowMainWindow`, `ToggleMiniWindow`, `Quit`, shell names per R-128, declared by E20) are dispatched on the main window when it exists (`window.dispatch_action`), else on the app (`cx.dispatch_action`). Toasts go to the main window's `ToastQueue::push(kind, text, None, None)` (E16-A2); its hidden-window rule decides what happens while the window is hidden (b1-infra open item E31-7).

Writes to `[[tray_graphs]]` keep file order equal to id order and write all four keys of each entry.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** no tray graphs **When** `PerfAddTrayGraph { source: "cpu" }` is dispatched **Then** `[[tray_graphs]]` has one entry `source = "cpu"`, `column = "cpu"`, `color = "accent"`, `range_s = 60` and the toast "Tray icon graph added" (Success) is pushed.
- **Given** a cpu tray graph **When** `PerfAddTrayGraph { source: "cpu" }` is dispatched **Then** nothing changes and the Warning toast "Tray icon graph already exists" is pushed.
- **Given** a process graph **When** `RemoveTrayGraph` with its source and column is dispatched **Then** it is gone from `[[tray_graphs]]` and "Tray icon graph removed" (Success) is pushed.
- **Given** no matching graph **When** `RemoveTrayGraph` is dispatched **Then** the Error toast "Unable to remove tray icon graph" is pushed.
- **Given** graph id 2 exists **When** `RegisterFailed(TrayGraphId(2))` arrives **Then** the graph is removed from `[[tray_graphs]]` and the Error toast "Unable to add tray icon graph" is pushed.
- **Given** graph id 1 **When** `SetColor { id: 1, color: "rose" }` arrives **Then** `[[tray_graphs]]` entry 1 has `color = "rose"` and the next model's `line_rgb` is `[0xF4, 0x3F, 0x5E]`.
- **Given** graph id 1 **When** `SetRange { id: 1, secs: 45 }` arrives **Then** nothing changes.
- **Given** a cpu graph **When** `TogglePageSource { source: "cpu" }` arrives **Then** it is removed; **When** it arrives again **Then** a cpu graph is added.
- **Given** the main window is open **When** `ToggleMainWindow` arrives **Then** the `ToggleMainWindow` action reaches the main window.
- **Given** the main window was removed to the tray **When** `ShowMainWindow` arrives **Then** the action is dispatched on the app.
- **Given** any state **When** `Exit` arrives **Then** `Quit` is dispatched.
- **Given** `WatcherOffline` arrives **When** `TrayStatus` is read **Then** `available` is false; after `WatcherOnline` it is true.
- **Given** the event channel closes **When** the task ends **Then** `TrayStatus.running` is false.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/tray_bridge.rs`: actions, handlers, event task.
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_tray_bridge.rs`: add the tests below (the test owns the service end, sends events and reads models).

## Tests
- `ui_tray_bridge.rs::add_page_graph_persists_and_toasts`.
- `ui_tray_bridge.rs::add_existing_graph_warns`.
- `ui_tray_bridge.rs::remove_graph_and_remove_missing`.
- `ui_tray_bridge.rs::register_failed_removes_and_errors`.
- `ui_tray_bridge.rs::set_color_and_range_persist`.
- `ui_tray_bridge.rs::toggle_page_source_adds_and_removes`.
- `ui_tray_bridge.rs::window_events_dispatch_shell_actions`: ToggleMainWindow, ShowMainWindow (window open and removed), ShowMiniWindow, Exit.
- `ui_tray_bridge.rs::watcher_events_set_status`.
- `ui_tray_bridge.rs::closed_channel_marks_not_running`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: "Unable to add tray icon graph" (Error), "Unable to remove tray icon graph" (Error), "Tray icon graph already exists" (Warning); successes "Tray icon graph added" and "Tray icon graph removed" (Success).
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: every tray action is also reachable in the app (page, card and row menus; Settings).
- Performance: event handling does no engine call; settings writes use the 500 ms debounced persist callback (ADR-011).
- Privacy: `[[tray_graphs]] source` for a process stores `process:<boot_id 16 hex>:<pid>:<start_ticks>` only (R-100), never the command line.

## Notes
- Phase P3. Anchor: E31-008 to E31-012 and the E24 tray menu items depend on it.
- The shell action names come from shell.md and R-128: `ToggleMainWindow`, `ShowMainWindow`, `ToggleMiniWindow`, `Quit`.

title: E31-001 Tray contract types in tl-model (TrayModel, TrayEvent, channels)
description:
## Context
`tl-ui` (tray bridge) and `tl-tray` (StatusNotifierItem service) must exchange a model and events, but ADR-001 lets neither crate depend on the other: `tl-tray` may depend only on `tl-model` and `ksni`, and `tl-ui` must never have `zbus` (which `ksni` pulls in) in its closure. So the shared types live in `tl-model`. This bead adds them. Sources: ADR-001 allowed rows and hard rule 1, ADR-010 Tray, UI-SHL-113 Build line ("`tray_bridge.rs` sends `TrayModel { tooltip, menu_state }` to `tl-tray` and receives `TrayEvent::{Activate, ShowMainWindow, Exit, ..}` over channels"), UI-PRF-051 (events forwarded through `async_channel::bounded(16)`), R-027.

Approved as written (R-161 item 1): `crates/tl-model/src/tray.rs` plus one `pub mod tray;` line in `lib.rs`, after E03-A2. E03's frozen module list includes `tray.rs` (00-epics section 2). The model channel `bounded(2)` with `try_send` is accepted (R-161 item 1).

## Deliverable
New file `crates/tl-model/src/tray.rs` and one line `pub mod tray;` in `crates/tl-model/src/lib.rs` (the only change to `lib.rs`). Only `std`, `async-channel` and the existing `tl-model` types `Sample`, `SeriesView`, `TimeNs` are used (all in tl-model's allowed row).

```rust
/// Stable id of one tray graph, assigned at load from the order of `[[tray_graphs]]`
/// (1-based) and then incremented for each new graph. Never reused in one run.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub struct TrayGraphId(pub u32);

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)]
pub enum TrayGraphState { Live, NoMatch, Ended, Failed }

/// Everything `tl-tray` needs to draw and describe one graph icon. Built by tl-ui.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct TrayGraphFrame {
    pub id: TrayGraphId,
    pub series: Option<Arc<SeriesView>>, // None: baseline only (Failed, or no series yet)
    pub now_ns: TimeNs,
    pub range_ns: u64,                   // range_s * 1_000_000_000
    pub max: f32,                        // scale ceiling, computed in tl-ui by the chart scale rules
    pub line_rgb: [u8; 3],               // resolved graph colour (accent or named)
    pub state: TrayGraphState,
    pub tooltip_title: Arc<str>,
    pub tooltip_description: Arc<str>,
    pub color: Arc<str>,                 // stored value: "accent" or a lower-case APP-039 name
    pub range_s: u32,                    // 30 | 60 | 300 | 600
}

/// Check state of the "Tray icon graphs >" submenu.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct TrayMenuState {
    /// In this order: cpu, memory, disk, network, gpu, vram, gpu_temp. true = a tray graph with that source exists.
    pub page_sources: [bool; 7],
    /// Process-source graphs (process:, name:, app:) by id and label, in `[[tray_graphs]]` order.
    pub process_graphs: Arc<[(TrayGraphId, Arc<str>)]>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct TrayModel {
    pub show_main_icon: bool,
    pub main_tooltip_title: Arc<str>,        // "tasklens"
    pub main_tooltip_description: Arc<str>,  // five lines, see E31-007
    pub graphs: Arc<[TrayGraphFrame]>,       // in `[[tray_graphs]]` order
    pub menu: TrayMenuState,
}

/// Page sources in menu order: (stored source string, menu label).
pub const TRAY_PAGE_SOURCES: [(&str, &str); 7] = [
    ("cpu", "CPU"), ("memory", "Memory"), ("disk", "Disk"), ("network", "Network"),
    ("gpu", "GPU"), ("vram", "VRAM"), ("gpu_temp", "GPU temp"),
];

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum TrayEvent {
    WatcherOnline,                 // a StatusNotifierWatcher is on the bus
    WatcherOffline,                // no watcher; "Add tray icon graph" items disable
    RegisterFailed(TrayGraphId),   // ksni spawn failed for this graph
    ToggleMainWindow,              // left click (SNI Activate) on any tasklens item
    ShowMainWindow,
    ShowMiniWindow,
    Exit,
    SetColor { id: TrayGraphId, color: Arc<str> },
    SetRange { id: TrayGraphId, secs: u32 },
    Remove { id: TrayGraphId },
    TogglePageSource { source: &'static str }, // one of TRAY_PAGE_SOURCES .0
}

/// UI end: tl-ui sends models and receives events.
pub struct TrayUiEnd { pub models: async_channel::Sender<TrayModel>, pub events: async_channel::Receiver<TrayEvent> }
/// Service end: tl-tray receives models and sends events.
pub struct TrayServiceEnd { pub models: async_channel::Receiver<TrayModel>, pub events: async_channel::Sender<TrayEvent> }

/// Model channel bounded(2) (the UI uses try_send and drops a model when full, because the next 1 Hz model replaces it);
/// event channel bounded(16) (UI-PRF-051).
pub fn tray_channels() -> (TrayUiEnd, TrayServiceEnd);
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `tray_channels()` **When** the UI end sends a `TrayModel` **Then** the service end receives the same model.
- **Given** a model channel holding 2 models **When** the UI calls `try_send` a third time **Then** it returns `Full` and nothing blocks.
- **Given** the service end sends 16 events without the UI reading **When** it sends a 17th with `try_send` **Then** it returns `Full`.
- **Given** `TRAY_PAGE_SOURCES` **When** read **Then** it holds exactly the seven pairs above in that order.

## Files
- `crates/tl-model/src/tray.rs`: create, the types above with `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`.
- `crates/tl-model/src/lib.rs`: add the line `pub mod tray;`.

## Tests
- `tl-model/src/tray.rs::tests::channel_roundtrip`: a model sent on the UI end arrives on the service end.
- `tl-model/src/tray.rs::tests::model_channel_capacity_is_2`: the third `try_send` is `Full`.
- `tl-model/src/tray.rs::tests::event_channel_capacity_is_16`: the 17th `try_send` is `Full`.
- `tl-model/src/tray.rs::tests::page_sources_order`: the constant matches the seven pairs.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A
- Validity: N/A (the UI turns Validity into text and `max` before building a frame)
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: `TrayGraphFrame` holds `Arc`s only; building one per graph per second allocates no sample copies.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Phase P3. `tl-model` stays free of async runtimes: `async-channel` is only a channel type (allowed in tl-model's row).
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-model`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E31-003 Tray graph icon rasterizer (raster.rs, 22 and 44 px ARGB32)
description:
## Context
The tray graph icon is drawn on the CPU into an ARGB32 buffer at 22 x 22 and 44 x 44 px, because `ksni::Icon { width, height, data }` takes raw pixels. This bead writes the pure rasterizer and its tests. Sources: UI-PRF-050, PERF-088, PERF-091, ADR-010 Tray ("fill columns plus a 1 px line, no anti-aliasing beyond 2x2 supersampling"), R-027, UI-PRF-007 (absolute-time buckets).

The scale ceiling is passed in as `max` instead of the `&mut ScaleState` named in UI-PRF-050, because `tl-tray` cannot depend on `tl-ui` (ADR-001). tl-ui computes `max` with its chart scale rules (E31-007). This follows b1-infra open item E31-1.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-tray/src/raster.rs`:
```rust
/// Draws one tray graph icon. `size` is 22 or 44. `out` is resized to size*size*4 and overwritten.
/// Pure CPU; no allocation after the first call for a given size.
pub fn render(samples: &[tl_model::series::Sample], now_ns: u64, range_ns: u64,
              max: f32, line_rgb: [u8; 3], size: u32, out: &mut Vec<u8>);
```
Layout at 22 px (all values double at 44 px):
- Margin: 1 px fully transparent on all four sides (row 0, row 21, column 0, column 21). At 44 px: 2 px.
- Inner area: columns 1..=20, rows 1..=20 (inner height 20 px; 40 at 44 px).
- History: columns 1..=18 (18 columns; 36 at 44 px). The newest bucket is the right-most history column (18).
- Value bar: columns 19..=20 (2 px wide; 4 at 44 px), directly next to the history with no gap.
- Background: ARGB 0 everywhere nothing is drawn.

Bucketing: `cols` = 18 (36 at 44 px); `bucket_ns = range_ns / cols`; a sample belongs to bucket `t_ns / bucket_ns` (absolute time, so buckets do not shimmer); the newest column is bucket `now_ns / bucket_ns`, the one left of it is that minus 1, and so on. A bucket's value is the maximum of its samples that have `SampleFlags::VALID`. A bucket with no valid sample is a gap and stays transparent.

Column drawing: height `h = round(inner_h * clamp(value / max, 0, 1))` pixels from the bottom inner row upward (`h = 0` draws nothing). The top row of the column is the line colour at alpha 1.0 (the "1 px line"); the rows below it are the fill colour, which is the line colour at alpha 0.55 (alpha byte 140).

Value bar: uses the newest sample in `samples`. If it has `VALID`, the bar is solid line colour at alpha 1.0 from the bottom to `round(inner_h * clamp(value / max, 0, 1))`. If it is not valid or `samples` is empty, the bar is a baseline only: the bottom inner row (1 px; 2 px at 44 px) in line colour at alpha 1.0.

Supersampling: draw the layout at 2x (44 x 44 for the 22 px icon, 88 x 88 for the 44 px icon) into a `thread_local!` buffer, then box-filter each 2 x 2 block down to one pixel (average of the four pixels in premultiplied form, then stored as straight alpha). This is the only anti-aliasing.

Byte order: ARGB32 in network byte order, 4 bytes per pixel as `[A, R, G, B]`, rows top to bottom, as `ksni::Icon.data` expects.

`max <= 0` or not finite: treat every column as height 0 and draw the baseline bar.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** any input at size 22 **When** rendered **Then** every pixel in row 0, row 21, column 0 and column 21 has alpha 0, and `out.len() == 22 * 22 * 4`.
- **Given** a newest valid sample of 50 with `max = 100` at size 22 **When** rendered **Then** the value bar in columns 19 and 20 covers 10 rows from the bottom inner row with alpha 255 in the line colour, and the 10 rows above it are transparent.
- **Given** a newest sample without `VALID` **When** rendered **Then** the value bar shows only the bottom inner row in line colour.
- **Given** a run of samples without `VALID` covering three buckets **When** rendered **Then** those three history columns are fully transparent.
- **Given** the same inputs twice **When** rendered into two buffers **Then** the buffers are byte-for-byte equal.
- **Given** inputs rendered at 22 and at 44 **When** each 44 px pixel block (2x2) is compared with the 22 px layout regions **Then** margins, history columns and bar positions match the 22 px layout doubled (margin 2, history 36 columns, bar 4 px).
- **Given** a column with value equal to `max` **When** rendered **Then** its top inner row carries alpha 255 and the rows below carry fill alpha (140 before downsampling, within 2 of 140 after for interior rows).

## Files
- `crates/tl-tray/src/raster.rs`: the function and private helpers.
- `crates/tl-tray/tests/raster.rs`: the tests below.

## Tests
- `tests/raster.rs::raster_22_has_transparent_margin`: margin alpha 0, buffer length 1936.
- `tests/raster.rs::raster_value_bar_height`: 50 of 100 gives a 10-row bar.
- `tests/raster.rs::raster_invalid_value_draws_baseline`: invalid newest sample gives the 1-row baseline only.
- `tests/raster.rs::raster_identical_input_identical_bytes`: two renders are byte-equal (the update rule depends on it).
- `tests/raster.rs::raster_gap_columns_transparent`: invalid buckets stay alpha 0.
- `tests/raster.rs::raster_44_is_2x_of_22_layout`: margin 2, 36 history columns, 4 px bar.
- `tests/raster.rs::raster_buckets_use_absolute_time`: shifting `now_ns` by less than one bucket does not move a sample to another column.
- `tests/raster.rs::prop_render_never_panics`: proptest over random samples (including NaN values, unsorted times, empty), `max` in [-1, 1e12], sizes 22 and 44: no panic, length always size*size*4.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A (pure function, no error path)
- Validity: invalid or missing samples draw as transparent gaps; an invalid current value draws the baseline.
- Accessibility: N/A (the tooltip carries the value as text, E31-007)
- Performance: 22 px icon works on a 44 x 44 x 4 = 7.7 KiB 2x buffer, 44 px on 31 KiB; under 50 us per icon on the owner machine. No allocation after the first call per size: `out` is reused and the 2x buffer is a `thread_local!`.
- Privacy: N/A

## Notes
- Phase P3. Decided in UI-PRF-050: margin 1 px, 18 history columns, 2 px value bar, fill alpha 0.55, baseline for invalid.
- `Sample` is `{ t_ns: TimeNs, value: f32, flags: SampleFlags }` (16 bytes) with `SampleFlags::VALID = 1 << 0` (ADR-003).
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-tray`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E31-004 Tray dbusmenu contents for graph and main icons (menu.rs)
description:
## Context
Each tasklens tray item exports a dbusmenu on `/MenuBar`. This bead writes the menu contents for the two item kinds (tray graph icon, main icon) as plain data that `item.rs` turns into `ksni::MenuItem`s, so order and labels are testable without D-Bus. Sources: UI-PRF-051 (menu, PERF-090 order), PERF-090, PERF-091 (graph icons carry the main entries), UI-SHL-113 (main icon menu), UI-SHL-085 (tray variant of Graph color: radio items without swatches), APP-039 (colour order), R-027.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-tray/src/menu.rs`:
```rust
use tl_model::tray::{TrayEvent, TrayGraphFrame, TrayGraphId, TrayMenuState, TRAY_PAGE_SOURCES};

pub enum MenuNode {
    Item { label: &'static str, event: TrayEvent },
    Sub { label: &'static str, children: Vec<MenuNode> },
    Radio { options: Vec<(Arc<str>, TrayEvent)>, selected: usize },
    Check { label: Arc<str>, checked: bool, event: TrayEvent },
    Separator,
}

/// (stored value, menu label) in APP-039 order.
pub const GRAPH_COLORS: [(&str, &str); 18];
/// (seconds, label).
pub const RANGES: [(u32, &str); 4] = [(30, "30 seconds"), (60, "1 minute"), (300, "5 minutes"), (600, "10 minutes")];

pub fn graph_icon_menu(frame: &TrayGraphFrame, state: &TrayMenuState) -> Vec<MenuNode>;
pub fn main_icon_menu(state: &TrayMenuState) -> Vec<MenuNode>;
```
`GRAPH_COLORS`, in this order: ("accent", "Accent (theme default)"), ("coral", "Coral"), ("orange", "Orange"), ("amber", "Amber"), ("yellow", "Yellow"), ("lime", "Lime"), ("green", "Green"), ("mint", "Mint"), ("teal", "Teal"), ("cyan", "Cyan"), ("blue", "Blue"), ("indigo", "Indigo"), ("violet", "Violet"), ("lavender", "Lavender"), ("fuchsia", "Fuchsia"), ("pink", "Pink"), ("rose", "Rose"), ("slate", "Slate"). The accent label follows UI-SHL-085 ("the same names"); UI-PRF-051 writes "Accent". This is b1-infra open item E31-6; if the leader picks "Accent", change only that string.

Graph icon menu, in order (PERF-090):
1. Sub "Graph color" with Radio over `GRAPH_COLORS`, selected = index of `frame.color` (unknown value selects 0); each option emits `SetColor { id, color }`.
2. Sub "Time range" with Radio over `RANGES`, selected = index of `frame.range_s` (unknown selects 1, "1 minute"); emits `SetRange { id, secs }`.
3. Item "Close tray icon graph" emits `Remove { id }`.
4. Sub "Tray icon graphs" (see below).
5. Separator.
6. Item "Show Main Window" emits `ShowMainWindow`.
7. Item "Show mini window" emits `ShowMiniWindow`.
8. Item "Exit tasklens" emits `Exit`.

Main icon menu, in order (UI-SHL-113, R-027): Item "Show Main Window" (`ShowMainWindow`), Sub "Tray icon graphs", Separator, Item "Exit tasklens" (`Exit`).

"Tray icon graphs" submenu (shared): one Check per `TRAY_PAGE_SOURCES` entry with its label ("CPU", "Memory", "Disk", "Network", "GPU", "VRAM", "GPU temp"), checked = `state.page_sources[i]`, emitting `TogglePageSource { source }`. If `state.process_graphs` is not empty: a Separator, then one Check per process graph with its label, checked = true, emitting `Remove { id }` (unchecking removes it, UI-PRF-051).

Submenu labels carry no ">" character; the ">" in the specs marks a submenu.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a frame with `color = "teal"`, `range_s = 300` **When** `graph_icon_menu` runs **Then** the top-level labels are, in order, "Graph color", "Time range", "Close tray icon graph", "Tray icon graphs", separator, "Show Main Window", "Show mini window", "Exit tasklens", the colour radio selects index 8 ("Teal") and the range radio selects index 2 ("5 minutes").

- **Given** no process graphs **When** the submenu is built **Then** it has exactly seven entries and no separator.
- **Given** a frame with `color = "unknown"` **When** the menu is built **Then** the colour radio selects index 0.

title: E31-005 ksni Tray item for graph and main icons (item.rs)
description:
## Context
One `ksni::Tray` implementation serves both tray item kinds: a tray graph icon and the main tasklens icon. It exposes the icon pixmaps, the tooltip, the dbusmenu from `menu.rs`, left-click activation, and watcher online and offline callbacks. Sources: ADR-010 Tray (ksni `=0.3.6`, `blocking` API, left click toggles the main window, re-register on watcher owner change), PERF-088 (bus name `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-<n>`, objects `/StatusNotifierItem` and `/MenuBar`), PERF-089 (SNI `ToolTip` `(icon, title, description)`), PERF-090 (`Activate(x, y)` toggles), PERF-092, UI-PRF-051, UI-SHL-113, table (c) row for tray items.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-tray/src/item.rs`:
```rust
pub enum ItemKind { Graph(TrayGraphId), Main }

pub struct TrayItem {
    pub kind: ItemKind,
    pub icon_22: Vec<u8>,          // ARGB32, 22*22*4 bytes
    pub icon_44: Vec<u8>,          // ARGB32, 44*44*4 bytes
    pub tooltip_title: Arc<str>,
    pub tooltip_description: Arc<str>,
    pub menu: MenuSource,          // what menu.rs needs to rebuild the menu on request
    pub events: async_channel::Sender<TrayEvent>,
}

impl ksni::Tray for TrayItem { ... }
```
- `id()`: `"tasklens"` for Main, `"tasklens-graph-<n>"` for `Graph(TrayGraphId(n))`.
- `title()`: `"tasklens"`.
- `category()`: `ksni::Category::SystemServices`.
- `icon_pixmap()`: `vec![Icon { width: 22, height: 22, data: icon_22.clone() }, Icon { width: 44, height: 44, data: icon_44.clone() }]`.
- `tool_tip()`: `ToolTip { icon_name: String::new(), icon_pixmap: vec![], title: tooltip_title, description: tooltip_description }`.
- `activate(x, y)`: `events.try_send(TrayEvent::ToggleMainWindow)` (left click on any tasklens item toggles the main window, PERF-090).
- `menu()`: converts `menu::graph_icon_menu` (Graph) or `menu::main_icon_menu` (Main) into `ksni::menu::MenuItem<Self>`: `MenuNode::Item` to `StandardItem` whose `activate` sends the event, `Sub` to `SubMenu`, `Radio` to `RadioGroup` whose `select` sends the event at that index, `Check` to `CheckmarkItem`, `Separator` to `MenuItem::Separator`.
- `watcher_online()`: sends `TrayEvent::WatcherOnline`.
- `watcher_offline(reason)`: sends `TrayEvent::WatcherOffline` and returns `true`, so the ksni service keeps running and registers again when a `StatusNotifierWatcher` gains an owner (PERF-092). If ksni 0.3.6 has no such callback or does not re-register by itself, stop and report to the leader: `tl-tray` may not use `zbus` directly (ADR-001 row is `ksni` only).
- Events are sent with `try_send`. A full channel drops the event and increments a `static DROPPED_EVENTS: AtomicU64` that `lib.rs` exposes as `pub fn dropped_events() -> u64`. No logging: `tracing` is not in tl-tray's allowed row (ADR-001).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a Graph item for `TrayGraphId(3)` **When** `id()` is read **Then** it is `"tasklens-graph-3"`.
- **Given** a Main item **When** `id()` is read **Then** it is `"tasklens"`.
- **Given** any item **When** `activate(0, 0)` is called **Then** `TrayEvent::ToggleMainWindow` arrives on the event channel.
- **Given** an item **When** `icon_pixmap()` is read **Then** it returns two icons of 22 x 22 and 44 x 44 whose data equals `icon_22` and `icon_44`.
- **Given** an item with title "CPU Usage" and description "18.6%" **When** `tool_tip()` is read **Then** title and description are those strings.
- **Given** a Graph item **When** the "Close tray icon graph" entry of `menu()` is activated **Then** `TrayEvent::Remove { id }` arrives.
- **Given** a Graph item **When** the colour radio selects index 8 **Then** `SetColor { id, color: "teal" }` arrives.
- **Given** a full event channel **When** `activate` is called **Then** nothing blocks and the drop counter increments.
- **Given** `watcher_offline` is called **When** it returns **Then** the value is `true` and `WatcherOffline` was sent.

## Files
- `crates/tl-tray/src/item.rs`: `ItemKind`, `TrayItem`, `MenuSource`, the `ksni::Tray` impl, with `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` that call the trait methods directly (no D-Bus).

## Tests
- `item.rs::tests::item_ids`: Main and Graph ids.
- `item.rs::tests::activate_sends_toggle`: left click event.
- `item.rs::tests::pixmaps_two_sizes`: sizes and data.
- `item.rs::tests::tooltip_fields`: title and description.
- `item.rs::tests::menu_events_reach_channel`: Close, colour radio and Exit entries send the right events.
- `item.rs::tests::full_channel_drops_without_blocking`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: a full event channel drops the event and counts it; no panic.
- Validity: N/A
- Accessibility: tooltip text repeats the graph value (PERF-089).
- Performance: `icon_pixmap` clones two small buffers (1.9 KiB and 7.7 KiB) only when ksni asks for them after an update.
- Privacy: tooltips and labels carry process names, never command lines or environment.

## Notes
- Phase P3. ksni 0.3.6 API to check in its source (`src/lib.rs`, trait `Tray`; `src/menu.rs`): method names `id`, `title`, `category`, `icon_pixmap`, `tool_tip`, `activate`, `menu`, `watcher_online`, `watcher_offline`. If a name differs in 0.3.6, use the 0.3.6 name with the same meaning.
- ksni builds the bus name `org.kde.StatusNotifierItem-<pid>-<n>` and the objects `/StatusNotifierItem` and `/MenuBar` itself; do not set them by hand.
- Build rule: run cargo through `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-tray`. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E31-007 Tray bridge: graph list, 1 Hz model, tooltips, main icon rule, demand
description:
## Context
The tray bridge is the tl-ui half of the tray. This bead builds the `TrayModel` once per second: the tray graph list from `state.toml` `[[tray_graphs]]`, per-graph series, scale, colour and tooltip text, the main icon's visibility and five-line tooltip, the submenu check state, and the demand the tray adds. The next bead (E31-A2) handles events coming back. Sources: UI-PRF-050 (colour, scale, update rule), UI-PRF-051 (tooltip table, "No match" and "Ended"), UI-SHL-113 (main icon visibility, tooltip, hidden-window effects), PERF-088, PERF-089, PERF-091, APP-047, PROC-094, R-027, R-066, R-067, R-085, R-100, ADR-008 (tray icon counts as a visible surface), canonical table (a) `[tray]` and `[[tray_graphs]]`, table (d).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-ui/src/tray_bridge.rs`:
```rust
/// GPUI Global read by menus ("No system tray available") and the close decision.
pub struct TrayStatus { pub available: bool, pub running: bool }
impl gpui::Global for TrayStatus {}

pub struct TrayBridge { /* Entity, one per app */ }

/// Called once by tl-app after TasklensUi::init (E31-008). Stores the UI end, sets TrayStatus
/// { available: true, running: true }, loads the graphs, starts the 1 Hz timer.
pub fn install(cx: &mut App, end: tl_model::tray::TrayUiEnd);

impl TrayBridge {
    /// Called by the close decision (E31-009) when the main window is removed to the tray (true) and when it is reopened (false).
    pub fn set_main_window_hidden(&mut self, hidden: bool, cx: &mut Context<Self>);
}
```
`TrayStatus.available` starts `true` until the first `WatcherOnline` or `WatcherOffline` event (b1-infra open item E31-10).

Graph list: one `TrayGraph { id: TrayGraphId, source: SharedString, column: SharedString, color: SharedString, range_s: u32, scale: ScaleState }` per `[[tray_graphs]]` entry of `TlSettings.state` (keys `source`, `column`, `color`, `range_s`; defaults `"cpu"`, `"cpu"`, `"accent"`, `60`). Ids are 1, 2, 3, ... in file order at load and increase for every graph added later.

Tick (every 1000 ms on the foreground executor, also while the main window is hidden), only while the tray is in use (`!graphs.is_empty() || show_main_icon`):
1. `let snap = client.latest()` from the `EngineClient` global set up by E16-A1.
2. For each graph, resolve `source` and `column` with the minigraph source resolver of `pages/minigraph/sources.rs` (E26-A1; b1-infra open item E31-9) to: the `Arc<SeriesView>` (fast tier when `range_s <= 60`, 1 Hz tier for 300 and 600), the label, the current value text, and the state `Live`, `NoMatch` or `Ended` (a process source whose boot id is not the current boot is `Ended`, R-100). A source whose collector is `Failed` gives `TrayGraphState::Failed`.
3. Scale ceiling `max`: the same `YScale` the matching minigraph card uses (UI-PRF-041 table: `Fixed` 100 for percent sources, `FixedTotal` for memory and VRAM, `AutoRate` with the 10 s fall rule for rates, `StickyTemp` for temperature), from `chart/scale.rs` (E19-A1). Each tray graph keeps its own `ScaleState`.
4. Colour: `color = "accent"` gives the line colour the matching minigraph card uses for a page source (for example `graph.cpu_line` for `cpu`) and `TlTheme.accent` for a process source (UI-PRF-050); a named colour gives its APP-039 hex from the theme palette constants (E17-A1): coral #FF7F50, orange #F28C28, amber #F5B700, yellow #E8D44D, lime #9BCB3C, green #4CAF50, mint #3EB489, teal #14A098, cyan #22B8CF, blue #3B82F6, indigo #6366F1, violet #8B5CF6, lavender #B4A7F5, fuchsia #D946EF, pink #EC4899, rose #F43F5E, slate #64748B.
5. Tooltip (title, description) per UI-PRF-051:

| Source | Title | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cpu` | `CPU Usage` | `18.6%` |
| `memory` | `Memory Usage` | `54.9%` |
| `disk` | `Disk Usage` | busiest disk active time, `1.2%` |
| `network` | `Network Usage` | total rate in the `units.network` unit, `0.3 Mbps` |
| `gpu`, `gpu:<key>` | `GPU Usage` | `3.0%` |
| `process:<boot>:<pid>:<start>` | `<name> (PID <pid>)`; `Process <pid>` until the name is read | `<Col> <value>`, for example `CPU 3.2%` |
| `name:<image>` | `<n> procs` | `<image>`, for example `firefox` |
| `app:<id>` | `<App>` | `<Col> <value>` |

   `<Col>` is the PERF-087 column label: `CPU`, `Memory`, `RSS`, `RSS shared`, `Disk`, `Network`, `GPU`, `VRAM`, `GPU shared`. Numbers use `tl-model::units` (percent `%.1f%%`, network bits SI one decimal or auto-scaled per `units.network_auto_scale`, sizes IEC two decimals). A value that is not valid shows the ADR-003 glyph for its Validity (for example `…` while warming up). For `NoMatch` and `Ended` the description is `No match` or `Ended`, and for a name filter the title is the image name (so it reads `firefox: No match`). `vram` and `gpu_temp` page graphs: see b1-infra open item E31-8; until settled use `VRAM Usage` with the size value and `GPU temp` with `52 °C`.
6. Main icon: `show_main_icon = graphs.is_empty() && (main_window_hidden || settings.tray.always_show)` (UI-SHL-113). Title `tasklens`, description five lines joined by `\n`: `CPU: <cpu %>`, `RAM: <memory used %>`, `GPU: <first GPU in sidebar order, 3D %>`, `Disk: <busiest disk active time %>`, `Network: <total rate in units.network>`, for example `CPU: 11.9%\nRAM: 54.9%\nGPU: 3.0%\nDisk: 1.2%\nNetwork: 0.3 Mbps` (PERF-089). A missing GPU shows the ADR-003 `n/a` glyph text.
7. Menu state: `page_sources[i] = graphs.iter().any(|g| g.source == TRAY_PAGE_SOURCES[i].0)`; `process_graphs` = graphs whose source starts with `process:`, `name:` or `app:`, with their tooltip title as label.
8. Send `TrayModel` with `try_send` (a full channel drops this model; the next tick replaces it). When the tray stops being in use, send one model with no graphs and `show_main_icon = false`, then stop sending until it is in use again.

Demand (ADR-008): while the tray is in use, register a tray contribution with the `DemandAggregator` (E16-A1): the source fields each graph needs (`cpu: Total`, `memory`, `disks`, `nets`, `gpus`, and the process identities the resolver reports), the five main-tooltip sources while the main icon is shown, and the tray as a visible surface (`Demand.tray`, b1-infra open item E31-8). Remove the contribution when the tray is no longer in use.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `state.toml` with `[[tray_graphs]]` cpu and `name:firefox` **When** `install` runs and one tick passes **Then** the model has two frames with ids 1 and 2 in that order.
- **Given** a FakeEngine CPU total of 18.6 **When** a tick runs **Then** the cpu frame has title `CPU Usage` and description `18.6%`.
- **Given** a process graph for pid 1234 named firefox at 3.2% CPU **When** a tick runs **Then** title is `firefox (PID 1234)` and description `CPU 3.2%`.
- **Given** a name graph matching 3 firefox processes **When** a tick runs **Then** title is `3 procs` and description `firefox`.
- **Given** a name graph with no matching process **When** a tick runs **Then** state is `NoMatch`, title `firefox`, description `No match`.
- **Given** a process graph whose boot id differs from the current boot **When** a tick runs **Then** state is `Ended` and description `Ended`.
- **Given** no graphs, `tray.always_show = false` and the main window visible **When** a tick runs **Then** nothing is sent.
- **Given** no graphs and `tray.always_show = true` **When** a tick runs **Then** `show_main_icon` is true and the description is five lines starting `CPU: `.
- **Given** one graph and `tray.always_show = true` **When** a tick runs **Then** `show_main_icon` is false.
- **Given** graphs cpu and network **When** a tick runs **Then** `page_sources` is `[true, false, false, true, false, false, false]`.
- **Given** a graph with `color = "teal"` **When** a tick runs **Then** `line_rgb` is `[0x14, 0xA0, 0x98]`.
- **Given** a cpu graph with `color = "accent"` under Default Dark **When** a tick runs **Then** `line_rgb` is the theme's `graph.cpu_line` (`#0A7096`).
- **Given** the last graph is removed and no main icon is needed **When** the next tick runs **Then** one empty model is sent and the tray demand contribution is removed.

description:
## Context

## Deliverable

- Mouse-down anywhere on a card except the label text starts a GPUI drag (`on_drag` with payload `DraggedMinigraph { id }`) after 4 px of movement. The dragged card renders at opacity 0.85 with its shadow (`drag preview` view); its home slot shows an empty outline (1 px `accent` dashed, `r_md`).

- Drop (`on_drop`) → `MinigraphMoveToSlot { id, slot }`: the entry takes the slot, cards shift to fill; dropping beyond the last card places it at the next free slot (`compact_slots`, no holes); persist. Drop outside the grid but inside the window: cards return to their slots. (Dragging past the window edge is E26-015.)

title: E26: minigraph states "No match", "Ended", Restricted and the boot-ID mismatch rule
description:
## Context
Process cards show what happened to their source. Sources: PERF-086 (states, gap rule, never rebinding), R-100 (boot ID), UI-PRF-041 (state looks).

## Deliverable
In `card.rs`: `CardState::{Live, NoMatch, Ended, Restricted}` with:
- `NoMatch` (name or app card with no live match): value text `No match` in `text_secondary`; the series records a gap (the engine publishes invalid samples; the chart draws the gap). When a process matches again the graph resumes.
- `Ended` (process card whose key is gone from the sweep, or whose `boot_id` differs from `Snapshot.boot_id`): value text `Ended` in `text_secondary`; the chart keeps its last samples and stops (`ChartState::Stale` never applies; the card sets `smooth = false` so it does not slide); the card stays until `Remove graph`; it never rebinds to a new process with the same pid.
- `Restricted` (another user's process, field not readable): the value shows the lock glyph (`TlValidityGlyph`), the graph shows a gap.
- State derived on `PROCESSES` changes (exit detection by the key missing from the snapshot) and once at load for the boot ID.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a name card whose name matches nothing **When** rendered **Then** the value reads `No match` and the chart has a gap after the last sample (`card_no_match_and_ended_states`).
- **Given** a process card whose key disappears from the sweep **When** installed **Then** the value reads `Ended`, the chart stops sliding and the card stays.
- **Given** a new process reusing the pid **When** installed **Then** the card stays `Ended`.
- **Given** a saved card with another boot ID **When** loaded **Then** it starts `Ended` (`card_ended_on_boot_id_mismatch`).
- **Given** a field with `Validity::Restricted` **When** rendered **Then** the lock glyph replaces the value.

description:
## Context
A detached graph window holds one or more cards in a borderless floating window. This bead writes the window entity and its look; detaching, the menu, the bridge and the keep-open rule are the next beads. Sources: PERF-083 (window kind, app id, caption, move), UI-PRF-044 (anatomy, size formula, background, not resizable), R-086, UI-FND-021 (`WindowKey::DetachedGraph`).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/windows/detached_graph.rs` (plus `pub mod detached_graph;` chain edit):

```rust
pub struct DetachedGraphWindow { pub window_id: u32, cards: Vec<(MinigraphId, Entity<MinigraphCard>)>, driver: Entity<AnimationDriver>, focus: FocusHandle, panel: WeakEntity<MinigraphPanel> }
pub fn window_size(n_cards: usize, ui_scale: f32) -> Size<Pixels>;   // (180 + 2 × sp2) × (n × 90 + (n + 1) × sp2), × ui_scale; sp2 = 4
pub fn open_detached(window_id: u32, cards: Vec<MinigraphEntry>, saved: Option<&DetachedWindowState>, cx) -> gpui::Result<WindowHandle<DetachedGraphWindow>>;
```
`open_detached` goes through `WindowRegistry::open_or_focus(WindowKey::DetachedGraph(window_id as u8), ..)` with `WindowOptions { kind: WindowKind::Floating, window_decorations: Some(WindowDecorations::Client), titlebar: None, is_resizable: false, is_movable: true, app_id: Some("io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens"), window_background: Opaque, window_bounds: Some(size from saved or window_size), .. }` and `window.set_window_title("tasklens Graph <n>")` (n = `window_id`). Dragging anywhere on the body (over a card too, no 4 px threshold) calls `window.start_window_move()` on mouse-down. The window owns its `AnimationDriver` (one per window, ADR-009). Esc does nothing (closing is through the menu, E26-016).

title: E26: Detach and Attach: menu items, drag past the window edge, window ids, [[minigraphs]] detached flags and [[detached_windows]] round trip
description:
## Context
Cards move between the panel and detached windows, and the layout survives a restart. Sources: PERF-083, R-084 (state shape), UI-PRF-042 item 6, UI-PRF-043 (edge rule), UI-PRF-044 (data binding).

## Deliverable
In `panel.rs` and `detached_graph.rs`:
- `MinigraphDetach { id }`: allocate `window = next unused id from 1`, set `entry.detached = true, entry.window`, remove the card from the panel (slots compact), open the window with that card; when triggered by a drag released more than 24 px outside the main window's bounds, the new window is placed under the pointer where the compositor allows (KDE through E26-017; else compositor placement). `CardMenuCtx.detach = true` so item 6 shows `Detach` on attached cards and `Attach to main window` on detached ones.

- `MinigraphAddToWindow { window, source }` (E26-016 menu): adds a system card to that window (source not already in it).
- Load: entries with `detached = true` open their windows at startup grouped by `window`, sized by card count, using `[[detached_windows]]` `width`/`height` (and `x`/`y` on KDE, E26-017). Save: `[[detached_windows]]` holds `id`, `width`, `height`, `x`, `y` per open window; debounced 500 ms.

title: E26: KWin bridge for detached graph windows and the mini window: keepAbove, geometry restore, move read-back debounced 500 ms
description:
## Context
On KDE, tasklens's own small windows are kept above and placed through the KWin bridge; the UI finds them in `WindowsSnapshot` by pid and caption. Sources: PERF-083 (KDE behaviour), PERF-093 (mini window), R-086, ADR-004 (KWin worker), ADR-005 (`Command::KWin`), ADR-003 (`WindowsSnapshot` fields).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/minigraph/mod.rs` (or a `bridge.rs` inside the minigraph module, E26-owned): `pub struct OwnWindowBridge` that, on each `WINDOWS` change, matches entries with `pid == std::process::id()` and `caption == "tasklens Graph <n>"` / `"tasklens Mini Window"` to the open windows by caption, then:
- once per window after it is first matched: send `Command::KWin(KWinCommand::KeepAbove { id: internal_id, on: true })` and, for a detached window with saved `x`/`y`, `KWinCommand::SetGeometry { id, x, y, width, height }` (variant names per E03-063; use what E03 declared);
- on every later change of that entry's `frame_geometry`: write `x`/`y` into the window's `[[detached_windows]]` entry, persisted with a 500 ms debounce;
- for the mini window: `KeepAbove { on }` follows its `always_on_top` flag (E26-020).
Without the bridge (`WindowsSnapshot` validity `Unsupported`): nothing is sent, `x`/`y` are neither applied nor written (R-084), and the mini window's "Always on top" item is disabled (E26-020).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a `WindowsSnapshot` with an entry `pid == own, caption == "tasklens Graph 1"` and a saved `x = 100, y = 200` **When** installed **Then** one `KeepAbove { on: true }` and one `SetGeometry { x: 100, y: 200, .. }` are sent for that `internal_id` (`detached_bridge_commands_once`).
- **Given** a later snapshot moving the frame to (300, 400) **When** installed **Then** after 600 ms the state entry has `x = 300, y = 400` and no further command was sent.
- **Given** the bridge `Unsupported` **When** windows open **Then** no `KWin` command is sent and `x`/`y` stay 0.
- **Given** two snapshots with the same geometry **When** installed **Then** nothing is persisted again.

description:

title: E26-021 AddRandomMinigraphs: declare and handle the Debug menu action
description:
## Context
The Debug menu item "Add random process minigraphs" (APP-026, UI-SHL-042) dispatches `AddRandomMinigraphs`. No bead declared or handled it; this bead does (R-238). It fills the free minigraph slots with CPU cards for random processes, a developer aid for testing the panel and the per-process series. Phase P4, like the Debug menu. Sources: APP-026, UI-SHL-042 (item 4, toasts), UI-PRF-040 (12 slots, 3 rows × 4), E26-013 (`add_process`), R-238.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/minigraph/actions.rs`: add `AddRandomMinigraphs` to the unit `actions!(tasklens, [..])` list (namespace `tasklens`, R-128). No key binding.

`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/minigraph/panel.rs`:
- `pub fn add_random(cx: &mut App) -> u32`, registered as the global handler of `AddRandomMinigraphs` (`cx.on_action`, from the minigraph `init`).
- Candidates: the records of the current process snapshot (`GlobalHub`) that are not exited, not kernel threads and not the tasklens process (`std::process::id()`), in snapshot order.
- Shuffle the candidates with a local SplitMix64 (`fn splitmix64(state: &mut u64) -> u64`, the standard constants `0x9E3779B97F4A7C15`, `0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9`, `0x94D049BB133111EB`) seeded from `SystemTime::now()` nanoseconds since the epoch; Fisher-Yates over the vector. No new crate.
- For each candidate in shuffled order: `MinigraphPanel::global(cx).add_process(MinigraphSource::Process { key }, GraphColumn::Cpu)` (E26-013). `Ok(_)` counts one; `Err(Exists)` and `Err(Unavailable)` skip to the next candidate; `Err(Full)` stops. The per-add toasts of E26-013 are not shown on this path (call the inner add that does not toast, or pass a `quiet` flag; keep one code path for the slot and persist logic).
- Result toast in the main window (`push_main_toast`): count ≥ 1: Success "Added { $count } random process minigraphs." (the spec's "%ld" is the count); count 0: Info "No process minigraphs available.".
- String keys appended to `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: `prf-minigraph-random-added` "Added { $count } random process minigraphs.", `prf-minigraph-random-none` "No process minigraphs available.".

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 3 attached system cards and 50 eligible processes **When** `AddRandomMinigraphs` is dispatched **Then** 9 process CPU cards are added (12 slots in total) and the toast reads "Added 9 random process minigraphs.".
- **Given** 12 cards already attached **When** it is dispatched **Then** nothing is added and the toast reads "No process minigraphs available.".
- **Given** a snapshot whose only records are kernel threads, exited rows and the tasklens process **When** it is dispatched **Then** nothing is added and the toast reads "No process minigraphs available.".
- **Given** a candidate that already has a CPU card **When** it comes up **Then** it is skipped and the next candidate is tried.
- **Given** the handler **When** it adds cards **Then** no "Minigraph added" toast shows, only the one result toast.
- **Given** the action **When** `cx.all_action_names()` is read **Then** it contains `tasklens::AddRandomMinigraphs`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/minigraph/actions.rs`: one name in the unit list.
- `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/minigraph/panel.rs`: `add_random`, SplitMix64, handler registration.
- `assets/locales/en-US.ftl`: two keys (chain edit).
- `crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_minigraphs.rs`: tests.

## Tests
`crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_minigraphs.rs` (FakeEngine snapshots):
- `add_random_fills_free_slots`: criterion 1.
- `add_random_full_panel_toast`: criterion 2.
- `add_random_no_candidates_toast`: criterion 3.
- `add_random_skips_existing`: criterion 4.
- `add_random_single_result_toast`: criterion 5.
- `minigraph_actions_in_namespace`: extended with `AddRandomMinigraphs` (criterion 6).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: none beyond the two toasts.
- Validity: cards follow E26-014's states (Ended, Restricted) like any process card.
- Accessibility: reached through the Debug menu (keyboard: Alt+D).
- Performance: at most 12 adds; one shuffle of the record list.
- Privacy: nothing logged beyond the count.

## Notes
- The choice of 12 slots and CPU as the column comes from UI-PRF-040 (slot cap) and APP-026 (no column named; CPU is the first graphable column, PERF-087). The SplitMix64 seed rule is a writer choice; tests must not depend on which processes are picked, only on counts.
- Depends on E26-013 (tasklens-xdh.15, `add_process` and `AddError`), E26-002 (tasklens-xdh.4, the actions file) and E26-011 (tasklens-xdh.13, process cards). E21-038 (tasklens-bj6.42) dispatches the action and depends on this bead.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-ui --test ui_minigraphs`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec: `git commit -m "..." -- crates/tl-ui/src/pages/minigraph/actions.rs crates/tl-ui/src/pages/minigraph/panel.rs assets/locales/en-US.ftl crates/tl-ui/tests/ui_minigraphs.rs`. Never a bare `git commit`.

title: E26: minigraph model: MinigraphId, MinigraphSource parse and format, slot geometry, default layout, state mapping (pages/minigraph/{mod,sources}.rs)
description:
## Context
Minigraph cards are described by `state.toml [[minigraphs]]` entries with a `source` string, a slot and per-card range and colour. This bead writes the pure model every other E26 bead and E31 (tray graph sources) compile against. Sources: PERF-080 (sources, keys, size), PERF-081 (range values), PERF-085 (process sources), R-084, R-085, R-100, UI-PRF-040 (slot numbering, limits, defaults), table (a) `[[minigraphs]]`, `[graphs]`, E03-067 `MinigraphState`.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/minigraph/mod.rs` (`pub mod panel; pub mod card; pub mod menu; pub mod actions; pub mod sources;`, empty modules with `//! filled by <plan key>` until their beads run) plus the line `pub mod minigraph;` in `crates/tl-ui/src/pages/mod.rs` (chain edit, E16-A1), and `sources.rs`:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)] pub struct MinigraphId(pub u32);   // assigned at load, stable while the app runs
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Debug)]
pub enum MinigraphSource {
    Cpu, Memory, Disk, Network,
    Gpu(Option<DeviceKey>), Vram(Option<DeviceKey>), GpuTemp(Option<DeviceKey>),   // None = first GPU in sidebar order (R-085)
    Process { key: ProcessKey /* boot_id, pid, start_ticks */ },
    Name(Arc<str>), App(Arc<str>),
}
#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Debug)] pub enum GraphColumn { Cpu, Memory, Rss, RssShared, Disk, Network, Gpu, Vram, GpuShared }
pub struct MinigraphEntry { pub id: MinigraphId, pub source: MinigraphSource, pub column: GraphColumn, pub range_s: u16, pub color: GraphColor, pub slot: u16, pub detached: bool, pub window: u32 }
impl MinigraphSource {
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<Self>;      // "cpu" | "memory" | "disk" | "network" | "gpu" | "vram" | "gpu_temp" | "gpu:<key>" | "vram:<key>" | "gpu_temp:<key>" | "process:<boot_id 16 hex>:<pid>:<start_ticks>" | "name:<image>" | "app:<id>"
    pub fn to_state_string(&self) -> String;    // inverse of parse
    pub fn is_system(&self) -> bool;
    pub fn system_label(&self) -> Option<&'static str>;   // "CPU", "Memory", "Disk", "Network", "GPU", "VRAM", "GPU temp"
    pub fn settings_key(&self) -> Option<SettingKey>;     // GraphsMinigraphCpu .. GraphsMinigraphGpuTemperature for the seven system kinds
}
impl GraphColumn { pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Option<Self>; pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str /* "cpu", "memory", "rss", "rss_shared", "disk", "network", "gpu", "vram", "gpu_shared" */; pub fn label(self) -> &'static str /* "CPU", "Memory", "RSS", "RSS shared", "Disk", "Network", "GPU", "VRAM", "GPU shared" */; }
pub const MAX_SLOTS: u16 = 12; pub const COLS: u16 = 4; pub const ROWS: u16 = 3;
pub fn slot_cell(slot: u16) -> (u16 /* row from the bottom */, u16 /* column from the right */);   // slot 0 = bottom right; 0..=3 row 0; 4..=7 row 1; 8..=11 row 2
pub fn default_entries() -> Vec<MinigraphEntry>;   // CPU 0, Memory 1, Disk 2, Network 3, GPU 4, VRAM 5 (range 60, Accent, attached); GPU temp is not in the default list (off by default)
pub fn from_state(state: &[MinigraphState], next_id: &mut u32) -> Vec<MinigraphEntry>;   // skips unparsable sources with a warn!; keeps slot order; duplicate slots are compacted in file order
pub fn to_state(entries: &[MinigraphEntry]) -> Vec<MinigraphState>;
pub fn compact_slots(entries: &mut [MinigraphEntry]);   // attached cards only: renumber 0..n keeping relative order (no holes)
```

The seven system kinds are shown when their `graphs.minigraph_*` setting is true (table (a); all true except `minigraph_gpu_temperature`), so `default_entries` lists the six on-by-default cards; the GPU temp card is created at slot 6 (next free) when its setting turns on (E26-004).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** every source form in the list **When** `parse` then `to_state_string` run **Then** the string round-trips (`source_round_trip`, including `process:0123456789abcdef:4242:1234567` and `gpu:gpu:GPU-…`).
- **Given** `"bogus:1"` **When** parsed **Then** `None`.
- **Given** slots 0, 3, 4, 11 **When** `slot_cell` runs **Then** `(0, 0)`, `(0, 3)`, `(1, 0)`, `(2, 3)`.
- **Given** `default_entries()` **When** read **Then** six entries CPU 0, Memory 1, Disk 2, Network 3, GPU 4, VRAM 5 with `range_s == 60`, `color == Accent`, `detached == false`.
- **Given** state entries at slots 0, 2, 2, 5 **When** `from_state` then `compact_slots` run **Then** slots are 0, 1, 2, 3 in file order.
- **Given** `GraphColumn::RssShared` **When** `label()` runs **Then** `RSS shared`; `as_str()` `rss_shared`.

title: E26: MinigraphCard entity: chart per system source, label and value lines, shadow, hover border, CPU tooltip, colour resolution (pages/minigraph/card.rs)
description:
## Context
A minigraph card is a 180 × 90 box with a label at top left, a value at top right and a chart filling the card. This bead writes the card for the seven system sources; process cards are E26-011. Sources: PERF-080 (labels, CPU kernel line, tooltip, size), PERF-024 (colours), UI-PRF-041 (anatomy, shadow, series table, states, colour rule), UI-PRF-008 (palette), R-085.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/minigraph/card.rs`:

```rust
pub const MINI_CARD_W: f32 = 180.; pub const MINI_CARD_H: f32 = 90.;
pub struct MinigraphCard {
    pub id: MinigraphId, pub entry: MinigraphEntry,
    chart: Entity<ChartView>, label: SharedString, value: SharedString, value_bits: u64,
    state: CardState /* Live | NoMatch | Ended | Restricted (E26-012) */,
    hover: bool, dragging: bool, hub, render_count,
}
impl MinigraphCard {
    pub fn new(entry: MinigraphEntry, catalog: &DeviceCatalog, sidebar_gpu_order: &[DeviceKey], hub, cx) -> Self;
    pub fn set_range(&mut self, secs: u16, cx); pub fn set_color(&mut self, color: GraphColor, cx);
    pub fn series_ids(&self) -> SmallVec<[SeriesId; 2]>;
    pub fn demand_part(&self) -> DemandPart;   // which Demand bits this card needs (E26-004 sums them)
}
pub fn resolve_colors(source: &MinigraphSource, color: GraphColor, theme: &TlTheme) -> (Option<Hsla> /* fill */, Hsla /* line */);
pub fn chart_spec_for(source: &MinigraphSource, idx: DeviceIdx, totals: &SystemSnapshot, color: GraphColor, range_s: u16, smooth: bool, theme: &TlTheme) -> ChartSpec;
```

Series and scale per source (UI-PRF-041 table; `MetricId` constants E03-A1, plan open item 1 for the rest):

| source | label | series | scale | value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cpu | `CPU` | `CPU_TOTAL` filled + `CPU_KERNEL` line `kernel_line` (#C1514E) on the all-CPUs device | `Fixed 0..100` | `88.6%` |
| Memory | `Memory` | `MEM_USED` | `FixedTotal(MemTotal)` | `40.5%` (used / total) |
| Disk | `Disk` | `DISK_ACTIVE` of the aggregate disks device (busiest disk) | `Fixed` | the aggregate transfer rate `0.54 MiB/s` (`DISK_READ + DISK_WRITE` of the aggregate device) |
| Network | `Network` | `NET_RX` filled + `NET_TX` dashed of the aggregate nets device (visible physical interfaces) | `AutoRate` or `LinkSpeed` per the net page rule | total rate `0.07 Mbps` |
| Gpu(k) | `GPU` | `GPU_UTIL` of that GPU | `Fixed` | percent |
| Vram(k) | `VRAM` | `GPU_MEM` | `FixedTotal(vram total)` | `2.80 GiB` |
| GpuTemp(k) | `GPU temp` | `GPU_TEMP` | `StickyTemp` | `52 °C` |

`None` GPU key = the first GPU in sidebar order (`sidebar_gpu_order[0]`, R-085). The aggregate disks and nets device indices are plan open item E26-OI-1 (engine-published aggregate devices); if they do not exist when this bead starts, stop and report.

Chart: `ChartSpec { background: List, grid: { lines: true, baseline: true, outline: true, rounded: true }, hover: false (E26-007), .. }`, `ChartLabels { heading: None, value_align: Hidden, legend: [], show_axis_max: false }` (the card draws label and value itself as cached `ShapedLine`s). Colours: `GraphColor::Accent` → the type palette (`cpu_fill`/`cpu_line`, `mem_*`, `disk_*`, `net_*`, `gpu_*`; VRAM and GPU temp use `gpu_*`); a named variant (`GraphColor::Coral` to `Slate`, R-263) → that accent for both line and fill at alpha 0.85 (E26-010 adds the menu; the resolution lives here).

Rendering (× `ui_scale`): `div()` 180 × 90, bg `list_bg`, 1 px `divider` border, radius `r_md`, `BoxShadow { offset: (0, 4), blur: 12, spread: 0, color: black @ 0.35 × appearance.shadow_intensity_pct / 100 }`; the chart fills the whole card; over its top a 20 px row inset `sp3` with the label (`t_sm` 500 `text_primary`, left; middle ellipsis on the name part for process cards, E26-011) and the value (`t_sm` 400 `tnum`, right). Hover: border `accent` at alpha 0.5. Dragging look is E26-008. CPU card tooltip (`TlTooltip`, 500 ms): two lines `── Total 88.6%` and `── Kernel 4.1%` with swatches as UI-PRF-003. Value re-formats only when its bits change; `cx.notify()` only on label, value or state change (the chart notifies itself).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** each of the seven system sources **When** `MinigraphCard::new` runs **Then** the label is the table's word and the chart's scale kind the table's (`card_labels_system`).
- **Given** `GraphColor::Coral` **When** `resolve_colors` runs for Memory **Then** line = Coral and fill = Coral at alpha 0.85; with `Accent`, `mem_fill` / `mem_line` (`card_color_named_overrides`).
- **Given** `Gpu(None)` with two GPUs **When** built **Then** its series device is the first GPU in sidebar order.
- **Given** the CPU card hovered **When** the tooltip shows **Then** it has the two lines with the current total and kernel values.
- **Given** two snapshots with the same newest value **When** installed **Then** the card's `render_count` is unchanged.
- **Given** `shadow_intensity_pct = 50` **When** rendered **Then** the shadow colour alpha is 0.175.

title: E26: MinigraphPanel entity: overlay layout from the bottom right, settings-driven system cards, demand, full-grid toast, reset, state persistence (pages/minigraph/panel.rs)
description:
## Context
The panel owns the cards, places them in the 4 × 3 slot grid over the Processes table, follows the View > Graphs settings, persists `[[minigraphs]]`, and handles reset. Sources: PERF-080, PERF-082 (grid, toasts, reset), APP-021, R-089, UI-PRF-040 (margins, slot order, overlay, visibility, states, demand, build), ADR-011 (debounced persist).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-ui/src/pages/minigraph/panel.rs`:

```rust
pub struct MinigraphPanel {
    cards: Vec<(MinigraphId, Entity<MinigraphCard>)>,   // attached cards, sorted by slot
    entries: Vec<MinigraphEntry>,                         // every entry, attached and detached (E26-015 uses the detached ones)
    next_id: u32, hub, demand, settings_sub, render_count,
}
impl MinigraphPanel {
    pub fn new(hub, demand, cx) -> Self;         // loads UiState.minigraphs through from_state (defaults when empty), creates attached system cards whose graphs.minigraph_* is true
    pub fn attached(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &MinigraphEntry>;
    pub fn add_system(&mut self, source: MinigraphSource, cx) -> Result<MinigraphId, PanelFull>;   // next free slot; Err when 12 attached
    pub fn hide(&mut self, id, cx); pub fn remove(&mut self, id, cx); pub fn reset(&mut self, cx);
    pub fn persist(&self, cx);                   // UiState.minigraphs = to_state(entries), through the state global (500 ms debounce)
}
```

Behaviour:
- Settings: observe `graphs.minigraph_*`; a flag turning true adds that system card at the next free slot (if absent); turning false removes the card (`hide`). `hide` on a system card writes its setting false (so View > Graphs unchecks); on a process card it is `remove`.
- Layout: `div().absolute()` over the Processes table area, `bottom_4 (16) right_4 (16)`; cards 180 × 90 (× `ui_scale`), 8 px apart, placed by `slot_cell`: column `c` from the right, row `r` from the bottom. Only the cards take pointer events (the panel div has `pointer-events: none`; GPUI: the panel is not a hitbox, each card is).
- Full grid: `add_system` on 12 attached cards returns `PanelFull`; the caller shows `ToastQueue::push(Warning, "No space for more minigraphs")`.
- `ResetMinigraphLayout` handler (registered on the panel root and reachable from the shell menu through the window's action dispatch): `entries = default_entries()` (GPU temp follows its setting), detached cards re-attached (E26-015 closes their windows), process cards removed, range and colour reset; toast `Success` `Minigraph layout reset`; persist.
- Demand: the sum of the attached cards' `demand_part()` (`cpu: Total` for the CPU card, `memory`, `disks`, `nets`, `gpus`); never `cpu_fast` (UI-PRF-040). Registered as one surface; updated when the card set changes.
- Ctrl-pause does not pause the cards (they draw live series).
- Empty panel: nothing is drawn.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** empty state and default settings **When** constructed **Then** six cards at slots 0..5 and the CPU card is at bottom right, Memory left of it, GPU at row 1 column 0 (`panel_slots_fill_bottom_right_first`).
- **Given** 12 attached cards **When** `add_system(GpuTemp(None))` runs **Then** `Err(PanelFull)` and the toast `No space for more minigraphs` (`panel_full_toast`).
- **Given** a changed layout (CPU at slot 3, Memory removed) **When** `ResetMinigraphLayout` dispatches **Then** the six defaults are back at slots 0..5 and the toast `Minigraph layout reset` is pushed (`panel_reset_restores_defaults`).
- **Given** `graphs.minigraph_disk` set false **When** observed **Then** the Disk card is gone; set true, it returns at the next free slot.
- **Given** `MinigraphHide` on the CPU card **When** handled **Then** `graphs.minigraph_cpu == false`.
- **Given** the six default cards **When** demand is read **Then** `cpu == Total`, `memory`, `disks`, `nets`, `gpus` all true and `cpu_fast == false`.
- **Given** a card added **When** 600 ms pass **Then** `state.toml` holds the new `[[minigraphs]]` entry.

title: E14-A1 systemd workers and system table rows
description:
## Context
Anchor E14-A1. Fills the body of the reducer's `SysTableQuery` builder for the Services table: the engine sorts, filters and flattens the rows; the UI only shows them (UI-SYS-002, ADR-009). E09-A1 created `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/sys_table.rs` with the full signatures and an empty body (R-138 item 9); this bead writes the Services part and the shared helpers, E14-005 and E14-006 add Startup and Connections. It also closes the systemd worker chain (E14-001 to E14-004), so E11 unit actions and E27 can depend on this anchor. Sources: UI-SYS-002, SYS-001, SYS-002, SYS-004, SYS-016, SYS-017, UI-SYS-011, UI-SYS-013, UI-SYS-014, UI-SYS-016, UI-SYS-022, R-011, APP-028 (filter rules).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/sys_table.rs` (body only; keep E09-A1's signatures unchanged):
- Shared helpers used by all three tables: stable sort by the query's `SortSpec` column id and direction with a final tie-break on the node id; lowercase substring matching against the query's `filter` (`Arc<str>`, already lowercase); output `Arc<[SysRow]>` stamped with the query's `generation` as `query_generation`.
- Services projection from the latest records of both managers plus the process snapshot:
  - Row order: group row `SysNodeId::ServiceGroup(Manager::System)` first, then its units, then `ServiceGroup(Manager::User)` and its units. Group rows have `depth 0`, unit rows `depth 1`, child process rows `depth 2`.
  - `ServiceFilter { states, unit_types, system, user }` (from the query; `None` means defaults: no state filter, unit types service, socket, timer, mount, both managers on):
    - Manager toggle off: that group row and its units are not emitted.
    - Unit type: the id suffix must be in `unit_types` (values `service socket timer mount automount path target swap slice scope`).
    - State class per unit: running = `ActiveState` `active` or `reloading`; failed = `failed`; stopped = not running, not failed, and startup type Enabled or Enabled (runtime); disabled = every other unit. Selected states combine with OR; an empty state set means all states (SYS-004).
    - Text filter: a unit matches when the lowercase filter is a substring of any of its text columns: id, description, status word, startup type word, MainPID as decimal, user, path, manager word, unit type word, sub state, load state, unit file, triggered-by list, active-since text (APP-028: "Services: all visible columns"; see the note). Text filter AND state filter AND unit-type filter.
  - Group rows: `has_children` true when at least one unit of that manager passes the filters; `expanded` from the query's `expanded` list. A `Connected` manager whose filtered unit list is empty: its group row is not emitted (UI-SYS-014 "Empty group: the group row is hidden"). An `Unavailable` manager: its group row is emitted with `has_children = false` and no unit rows.
  - Unit rows: emitted only under an expanded group; `has_children` = the unit's `has_cgroup_procs`; `expanded` from the query; `record` = index of the unit in the published unit array.
  - Child process rows `SysNodeId::UnitProcess(unit, key)`: emitted under an expanded unit for each key in its `cgroup_pids` present in the process snapshot, sorted by PID ascending regardless of the query sort (UI-SYS-013); `record` = index into `Snapshot.processes.records`. Child rows inherit their unit's filter result and are not matched separately.
  - Sort: within each group by the query column; default `name` ascending (R-011). Text columns compare case-insensitively; `pid`, `cpu`, `memory`, `disk`, `tasks` compare numerically with non-`Valid` values last; `active_since` by timestamp; `status` and `startup_type` by the order of their mapping tables in E14-001.
  - `counts { total, running, stopped }` over unit rows after all filters (child rows not counted): running = `ActiveState` `active` or `reloading`; stopped = `inactive` or `failed`; Starting and Stopping count in total only (UI-SYS-022). Counts include units of collapsed groups.
  - `managers: [ManagerState; 2]` copied from the workers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 3 system and 2 user units and both groups expanded **When** projected with no filters **Then** rows are System group, 3 units, User group, 2 units with depths 0,1,1,1,0,1,1.
- **Given** the System group collapsed **When** projected **Then** no system unit rows are emitted and counts still include the system units.
- **Given** states `[failed]` **When** projected **Then** only failed units remain.
- **Given** states `[running, failed]` and filter `"ssh"` **When** projected **Then** only running or failed units whose text contains "ssh" remain.
- **Given** unit types `[timer]` **When** projected **Then** only `.timer` units remain.
- **Given** the user manager `Unavailable` **When** projected **Then** the User group row is present with `has_children = false` and no unit rows.
- **Given** a `Connected` user manager whose units are all filtered out **When** projected **Then** no User group row is emitted.
- **Given** an expanded unit with `cgroup_pids` 300, 100, 200 and sort `name` descending **When** projected **Then** its child rows are in PID order 100, 200, 300.
- **Given** sort `pid` ascending and a unit with MainPID 0 **When** projected **Then** the order is numeric.
- **Given** units with ActiveState active, reloading, activating, inactive, failed **When** counted **Then** total 5, running 2, stopped 2.
- **Given** a query with generation 7 **When** projected **Then** `query_generation` is 7.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/sys_table.rs`: fill the Services body and shared helpers.
- `crates/tl-engine/tests/lab_table.rs` is E09's; do not edit it. Tests go in `sys_table.rs`.

## Tests
In `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `sys_table.rs`, with hand-built unit records and process records:
- `services_rows_order_and_depth`, `services_collapsed_group_counts`, `services_state_filter_or`, `services_state_and_text_filter`, `services_unit_type_filter`, `services_unavailable_group_row`, `services_empty_group_hidden`, `services_child_rows_by_pid`, `services_numeric_sort`, `services_counts_rules`, `sys_query_generation_stamped`.
- `services_projection_10k_units_under_5ms`: 10 000 synthetic units, release-mode timing printed, asserts under 5 ms (skip the assert in debug builds with `cfg!(debug_assertions)`).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A (pure function).
- Validity: non-`Valid` resource values sort last.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: no allocation per unit beyond the output row vector; reuse a scratch `Vec` held by the builder if E09's signature passes one.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- Depends on E09-A1 (the stub file) and E14-004 (the worker chain).
- The query has no visible-column list, so "all visible columns" (APP-028) is matched as "all text columns" here, and the status and startup sort orders follow the SYS-003 mapping tables (R-167 item 10; `SysTableQuery` gets no column list).
- This file is reducer code: never await, never do I/O here.
- Read `/home/oystein/work/tasklens/CLAUDE.md` first.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec (`git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`), one commit for this bead.
- asupersync rules (ADR-004, docs/research/claude-asupersync-apis.md): every zbus call and every signal-stream `next()` is wrapped in `time::timeout` (2 s for reads) followed by `cx.checkpoint()`; blocking work only through `Cx::spawn_blocking` joined with `TaskHandle::join`; never `race!`, `select!`, `asupersync::process`, `asupersync::fs`, `asupersync::signal`, `GenServer`, `ChildSpec::depends_on`. Proxies never outlive their worker generation.

title: E14-006 sys_table.rs: Connections projection
description:
## Context
Adds the Connections projection to the reducer's `SysTableQuery` builder in `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/sys_table.rs`. Sources: UI-SYS-002, SYS-029, SYS-030, SYS-036, UI-SYS-061, UI-SYS-067, R-011.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-engine/src/reducer/sys_table.rs`, the `SysTable::Connections` branch:
- One row per socket record: `SysNodeId::Conn(cookie)`, `depth 0`, no children, `record` = index into `ConnectionsSnapshot.records`.
- Text filter (SYS-036): lowercase substring of Proto ("tcp"/"udp" compared lowercase), the local and foreign address strings with ports as shown (the engine-formatted strings), the State label, the PID text as shown ("812", "812 +2", "?", "-"), the Process name and the User.
- Sort keys (UI-SYS-061): `proto` TCP before UDP; `local` and `foreign` by family (IPv4 before IPv6), address bytes, then port; `state` in the order LISTENING, SYN-SENT, SYN-RECEIVED, ESTABLISHED, FIN-WAIT-1, FIN-WAIT-2, CLOSE-WAIT, CLOSING, LAST-ACK, TIME-WAIT, CLOSED, UNKNOWN, UNCONNECTED, CONNECTED; `pid` numeric with unknown ("?") and none ("-") after all numbers; `local_port`, `foreign_port`, `recv_q`, `send_q`, `inode` numeric; text columns case-insensitive. Default `proto` ascending, then local port ascending (R-011); the final tie-break is the cookie.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Given** `10.0.0.2:80` and `9.0.0.1:80` **When** sorted by `local` **Then** `9.0.0.1:80` comes first (numeric, not text order).
- **Given** PIDs 900, "?", 12, "-" **When** sorted by `pid` ascending **Then** 12, 900, then "?" and "-".
- **Given** filter `":443"` **When** projected **Then** only rows with 443 in an address string remain.
- **Given** 2 TCP ESTABLISHED, 1 TCP LISTEN, 1 UDP **When** counted **Then** total 4, tcp 3, udp 1, established 2, listening 1.

title: E14-009 Journal worker: follow mode and Load older
description:
## Context
Follow mode and Load older for the `Journal` worker (`crates/tl-engine/src/workers/journal.rs`). Follow keeps a `journalctl -f` child and streams new entries in batches at most every 100 ms; `set_follow(false)` kills it and `set_follow(true)` resumes after the last cursor; `load_older()` fetches 200 entries before the oldest loaded one. Sources: ADR-005 (`JournalHandle::load_older`, `set_follow`), R-074, R-118, UI-SYS-037, SYS-015, U-49.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/journal.rs`:
- Follow child, started after the initial fetch when `JournalQuery.follow` is true, and again on `set_follow(true)`:
  `journalctl <unit args> -b -o json --no-pager -f --after-cursor=<last cursor>`; when no entry has been loaded yet: `journalctl <unit args> -b -o json --no-pager -f -n 0`. `<unit args>` is `-u <id>` or `--user-unit <id>`.
- Reader: one `cx.spawn_blocking` job per follow child. It polls stdout with `rustix::event::poll` and a 100 ms timeout, parses complete lines (E14-A4 parser), keeps a pending `Vec<JournalEntry>`, and sends `Batch { entries, older: false, exhausted: false }` on the event channel with `send_blocking` at most once per 100 ms and only when the pending list is not empty. On every poll tick it checks `Sender::is_closed()`; when closed, it kills and waits the child and returns. It updates the shared last cursor after each batch.
- `set_follow(false)`: kill the follow child (SIGKILL through `Child::kill`), `wait()` it, and let the reader job end. No new batches arrive afterwards.
- `set_follow(true)` while not following: start a new follow child with `--after-cursor=<last cursor>`, so no entry is lost or repeated (U-49).
- `load_older()`: one fetch on the blocking pool with the 5 s timeout of E14-A4:
  `journalctl <unit args> -b -o json --no-pager --reverse --cursor=<oldest cursor> -n 201`. Drop the first entry when its cursor equals the oldest cursor, keep at most 200, reverse into chronological order, send `Batch { entries, older: true, exhausted: entries.len() < 200 }`, and update the oldest cursor. With no entries loaded, `load_older()` sends `Batch { entries: [], older: true, exhausted: true }`. A second `load_older()` while one is running is ignored.
- Control messages arrive on the handle's control channel; the session task handles them one at a time in order.
- Follow-child exit with a non-zero code sends `Error(Exit { code, stderr_first_line })`; the task then stays alive so `set_follow(true)` can retry.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fake follow script printing 50 lines within 30 ms **When** read **Then** they arrive in one batch, not 50.
- **Given** a fake script printing one line every 20 ms for 1 s **When** read **Then** at most 11 batches arrive and every line arrives once.
- **Given** following **When** `set_follow(false)` is called **Then** the child is reaped within 200 ms and no further batch arrives.
- **Given** the last cursor `c42` **When** `set_follow(true)` is called **Then** the new child's argv contains `--after-cursor=c42`.
- **Given** the oldest cursor `c10` and a fake reverse fetch returning `c10, c9 .. c0` **When** `load_older()` runs **Then** the batch holds `c0 .. c9` in that order with `older: true` and `exhausted: true`.
- **Given** 201 reverse results starting at the oldest cursor **When** `load_older()` runs **Then** 200 entries with `exhausted: false`.
- **Given** the receiver is dropped while following **When** the next 100 ms tick passes **Then** the child is killed and waited.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/journal.rs`: change.

## Tests
In `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `journal.rs`, with fake `journalctl` scripts that record their argv to a file:
- `follow_batches_at_most_every_100ms`, `follow_every_line_once`, `follow_off_kills_child`, `follow_resume_after_cursor_argv`, `load_older_reverse_and_drop_cursor_entry`, `load_older_exhausted_flag`, `follow_receiver_dropped_kills_child`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: follow-child failures become `Error(Exit ..)` events; the session stays usable.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: at most 10 batches per second per handle (UI-SYS-037); one blocking thread per following handle.
- Privacy: never log message text.

## Notes
- Depends on E14-A4 (same file).
- The `--reverse --cursor=<oldest> -n 201` form for Load older is settled (R-167 item 8). E14-010 verifies it on the owner machine.
- Each following handle holds one blocking-pool thread (pool max 4, ADR-004). The UI opens at most 10 Service Properties windows, but only a visible Logs tab holds a handle.
- Read `/home/oystein/work/tasklens/CLAUDE.md` first.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec (`git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`), one commit for this bead.
- asupersync rules (ADR-004, docs/research/claude-asupersync-apis.md): every zbus call and every signal-stream `next()` is wrapped in `time::timeout` (2 s for reads) followed by `cx.checkpoint()`; blocking work only through `Cx::spawn_blocking` joined with `TaskHandle::join`; never `race!`, `select!`, `asupersync::process`, `asupersync::fs`, `asupersync::signal`, `GenServer`, `ChildSpec::depends_on`. Proxies never outlive their worker generation.
