title: E14-011 Startup worker: scan on open and RefreshNow
description:
## Context
The `Startup` worker (`SourceId::Startup`, `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/startup.rs`, ADR-004). It scans the five startup sources with the tl-collect parsers (E06-A2) when the Startup Apps tab opens and on `RefreshNow(Startup)`, and publishes the entries that feed `StartupSnapshot`. Live rescans (E14-012) and the systemd enrichment with startup impact (E14-013) follow. Sources: SYS-019, SYS-020, ADR-008 row "Startup entries", ADR-016 row "Startup apps", R-082, UI-SYS-049.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/startup.rs` (new):
  - `pub(crate) fn factory(io: WorkerIo) -> impl ManagedChildFactory<WorkerError>`.
  - Loop: wake every `IDLE_RECHECK` (500 ms, from `source.rs`, E08-A1) with a new `sleep_until` each turn, `cx.checkpoint()` after each wake, read `Demand.startup` with `borrow_and_clone()`.
  - Scan when `Demand.startup` changes from false to true (page open, ADR-008) and on `RefreshNow(Startup)` while it is true. No scan while it is false; no scan on repeated wakes with no change.

  - Environment values (`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_DIRS`, `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP`, `HOME`, `PATH`) are read once per scan and passed to the scanner as parameters.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/mod.rs`: add `mod startup;` and one `WorkerSpec` entry for `SourceId::Startup` in `all_workers()` (chain edits on E08-A1, the only changes to that file; R-167 item 2).

title: E14-012 Startup worker: inotify and UnitFilesChanged rescans
description:
## Context
Live rescans for the `Startup` worker while the Startup Apps tab is visible: inotify on the autostart and Plasma script directories and the user manager's `UnitFilesChanged` signal each trigger a rescan; both stop when the tab is hidden. Sources: R-082, SYS-019, ADR-008 row "Startup entries".

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/startup.rs`:
- While `Demand.startup` is true: create inotify watches with the E06-A2 watch helper (`tl-collect/src/startup/watch.rs`) on `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/autostart`, every `$XDG_CONFIG_DIRS` `/autostart` directory, and on KDE `~/.config/plasma-workspace/env` and `~/.config/plasma-workspace/shutdown`. A directory that does not exist is skipped.
- While `Demand.startup` is true: open a session-bus connection with the E08-A2 helper, call the user manager's `Subscribe()`, and add a match for `org.freedesktop.systemd1.Manager.UnitFilesChanged`.
- On each 500 ms wake: drain pending inotify events (non-blocking read on the inotify fd) and pending `UnitFilesChanged` signals (call `futures_lite::future::poll_once(stream.next())` in a loop until it returns `None`, so the worker never waits on the stream). If any arrived, run one rescan (E14-011 scan job). Several events in one wake give one rescan.
- When `Demand.startup` becomes false: drop the watches (close the inotify fd), drop the match and the connection. They are re-created on the next open.
- No session bus: skip the `UnitFilesChanged` part and keep the inotify part.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the tab visible **When** a `.desktop` file is created in the user autostart dir **Then** a rescan happens within 1 s and the new entry is published.
- **Given** three files changed within one 500 ms window **When** the next wake runs **Then** exactly one rescan happens.
- **Given** the tab hidden **When** a file is created **Then** no rescan happens and no inotify fd is open.
- **Given** the tab visible and no session bus **When** the worker runs **Then** inotify rescans still work.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/startup.rs`: change.

## Tests
In `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `startup.rs`:

title: E14-013 Startup worker: generated units, unit state and startup impact
description:
## Context
Adds the systemd side of each startup entry to the `Startup` worker: unit file state of user units, the state of each desktop entry's generated `app-<escaped id>@autostart.service`, and startup impact from systemd activation timestamps. Sources: SYS-019 (generated units linked to their desktop entry), SYS-020 (Status values), SYS-021 (impact), SYS-026 (State code), UI-SYS-043.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/startup.rs`, after each scan (E14-011) and while `Demand.startup` is true, on the user manager over the session bus (2 s timeout per call):
- `ListUnitFilesByPatterns([], ["*"])` and `ListUnitsByPatterns([], ["*"])` once per scan.
- For each desktop entry: the generated unit name `app-<escaped id>@autostart.service`, where `<escaped id>` is the desktop file id escaped with the systemd-escape function from tl-collect `startup/` (E06-A2). If that unit is loaded: link it to the entry (it is not listed again as a separate unit entry, SYS-019) and record its `ActiveState`/`SubState` as the entry's state code (SYS-026); otherwise state code "-".
- For each systemd user unit entry: `UnitFileState` from the file list sets Enabled, Disabled or Masked status (SYS-020).
- Impact (SYS-021), for each entry with a linked or own unit: `GetAll` on the unit for `InactiveExitTimestampMonotonic`, `ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic`, `CPUUsageNSec`, and once per scan the manager property `UserspaceTimestampMonotonic` (on `/org/freedesktop/systemd1`, interface `org.freedesktop.systemd1.Manager`). Activation time = `ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic - InactiveExitTimestampMonotonic` (µs). Start offset = `InactiveExitTimestampMonotonic - UserspaceTimestampMonotonic`. Classify with the E06-A2 impact function using: High at 1000 ms or more, Medium 300 to 999 ms, Low under 300 ms, None when the entry is disabled, Not measured when either timestamp is 0 or the entry has no unit (Plasma scripts, non-systemd boot). Store `impact_detail` with the activation time in ms, the start offset in seconds and the CPU time (`CPUUsageNSec`, `u64::MAX` = not available).
- Impact is read once per scan; `UnitFilesChanged` already triggers a rescan (E14-012), so no other trigger is needed.
- No session bus or no user manager: every entry keeps its scanner values, impact Not measured, state code "-".

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** activation 1200 ms **When** classified **Then** High; 300 ms gives Medium; 299 ms gives Low.
- **Given** a disabled entry with timestamps **When** classified **Then** None.
- **Given** `InactiveExitTimestampMonotonic = 0` **When** classified **Then** Not measured.
- **Given** desktop id `org.kde.foo` with a loaded `app-org.kde.foo@autostart.service` **When** linked **Then** the entry's state code is that unit's `ActiveState/SubState` and the unit is not a separate entry.
- **Given** a user unit with `UnitFileState=masked` **When** merged **Then** its status is Masked.
- **Given** no session bus **When** a scan runs **Then** entries are published with impact Not measured and state code "-".

## Tests
In `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `startup.rs` (pure merge functions over property maps): `impact_thresholds`, `impact_none_when_disabled`, `impact_not_measured_zero_timestamp`, `generated_unit_linked_not_duplicated`, `user_unit_masked_status`, `no_bus_defaults`.

- Performance: one list call pair per scan and one `GetAll` per entry with a unit.

title: E14-014 Connections worker: 2 s dump, socket map, TCP attribution
description:
## Context
The `Connections` worker (`SourceId::Connections`, `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/connections.rs`, ADR-004): every 2 s while the Connections tab or the process Network columns need it, one sock_diag dump plus the socket-inode to pid map, producing the connection records and the per-process TCP attribution. It wraps the tl-collect readers from E06-A1 in a `Source`. Sources: SYS-028, SYS-029, SYS-030, ADR-008 row "Connections and socket attribution", ADR-016 rows "Per-process network", "Socket to pid map", "Connections", PROC-032, U-23.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/connections.rs` (new), a `Source` (E08-A1 trait) run by the standard worker loop:
  - `id()` = `SourceId::Connections`.
  - `period()` = `Some(2 s)` when `Demand.connections` is true, or when `Demand.process_table` is true and `Demand.process_columns` contains any of the column ids `network`, `net_send_rate`, `net_recv_rate`; otherwise `None` (off).
  - `sample()` (on the blocking pool, one job at a time, the whole thing in one job): read `t_ns`; dump TCP over IPv4 and IPv6 with `INET_DIAG_INFO`; dump UDP over IPv4 and IPv6 only when `Demand.connections` is true; rebuild the socket-inode to pid map from `/proc/<pid>/fd`; build the connection records and the per-process attribution (Δ`tcpi_bytes_acked` as send, Δ`tcpi_bytes_received` as receive, per socket inode, over the actual elapsed time; a socket shared by several processes counts for each). All of this uses the E06-A1 functions in `tl-collect/src/net/`.
  - Address strings are formatted once per socket cookie: the source keeps `FxHashMap<u64 cookie, (Arc<str> local, Arc<str> foreign)>` across samples and drops cookies not seen in the latest dump.
  - Rates follow ADR-008 counter rules: first sample of a socket gives no rate (`WarmingUp`); a counter that goes backwards resets the baseline; a boottime-versus-monotonic jump over 250 ms between samples drops all rates for that sample.
  - Publishes one `SourceUpdate` carrying the records (sorted by cookie) and the attribution map `FxHashMap<ProcessKey, (send_bps, recv_bps, shared: bool)>`; owners whose `/proc/<pid>/fd` cannot be read are marked restricted per SYS-030 (the record shows PID "?" and the restricted glyph).
  - Logs the socket-map rebuild time at debug level on every sample, for the phase-0 U-23 check (target under 20 ms).
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/mod.rs`: add `mod connections;` and one `WorkerSpec` entry for `SourceId::Connections` in `all_workers()` (chain edits on E08-A1, the only changes to that file; R-167 item 2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `Demand.connections = false`, `process_table = true` and `process_columns` without network columns **When** `period()` is called **Then** `None`.
- **Given** `process_columns` containing `net_recv_rate` and `process_table = true` **When** `period()` is called **Then** `Some(2 s)`.
- **Given** the Connections tab hidden but the Network column shown **When** a sample runs **Then** no UDP dump is made.
- **Given** two samples 2 s apart where a socket's `tcpi_bytes_acked` grew by 2 000 000 **When** attribution is computed **Then** the owner's send rate is 1 000 000 B/s.
- **Given** a socket seen for the first time **When** attributed **Then** its contribution is `WarmingUp`, not 0.
- **Given** a socket shared by pids 10 and 11 **When** attributed **Then** both get its rate and `shared = true`.
- **Given** the same cookie in two samples **When** records are built **Then** the address strings are the same `Arc`.
- **Given** a boottime jump of 5 s with a monotonic jump of 10 ms **When** sampled **Then** no rates are produced for that sample.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/connections.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/mod.rs`: one `mod` line and one `all_workers()` entry.

## Tests
In `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `connections.rs`, with the E06-A1 fixtures fed through a sampler function parameter:
- `period_off_without_demand`, `period_on_for_network_columns`, `period_on_for_tab`, `no_udp_dump_when_tab_hidden`, `attribution_rate_from_elapsed_time`, `attribution_first_sample_warming_up`, `attribution_shared_socket`, `address_strings_cached_per_cookie`, `suspend_gap_drops_rates`.
- `demand_switches_rate` (LabRuntime): with the E08-A1 loop and a fake sampler, demand off gives zero samples over 60 virtual seconds, demand on gives one sample every 2 s.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: a dump failure (netlink error) is `Validity::Failed` with `SourceHealth.last_error`; `EACCES` on a pid's fd dir is per-owner `Restricted`.
- Validity: `WarmingUp`, `Valid`, `Restricted`, `Failed`.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one blocking job per 2 s; socket map rebuild target under 20 ms (U-23, measured in phase 0).
- Privacy: never log addresses or ports above debug level.

## Notes
- Depends on E06-A1 and E08-A1.
- Close TCP connection (`SockDestroy`, P3) and `destroy_supported` are E11 and E29 work; other namespaces (P4) need the helper (E29).
- Read `/home/oystein/work/tasklens/CLAUDE.md` first.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec (`git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`), one commit for this bead.
- asupersync rules (ADR-004, docs/research/claude-asupersync-apis.md): every zbus call and every signal-stream `next()` is wrapped in `time::timeout` (2 s for reads) followed by `cx.checkpoint()`; blocking work only through `Cx::spawn_blocking` joined with `TaskHandle::join`; never `race!`, `select!`, `asupersync::process`, `asupersync::fs`, `asupersync::signal`, `GenServer`, `ChildSpec::depends_on`. Proxies never outlive their worker generation.

title: E14-015 Connections worker: reverse DNS for Remote host
description:
## Context
P4. The Remote host column: reverse DNS names for the foreign addresses of the visible connection rows, looked up only while the column is shown. Sources: SYS-035, UI-SYS-069, ADR-008 row "Reverse DNS", Demand field `remote_host_cookies`.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/connections.rs`:
- For each cookie in `Demand.remote_host_cookies` whose record has a foreign address (not `*`): look up the address with `tl_ops::sys::reverse_lookup`, the tl-ops wrapper around `getnameinfo` with `NI_NAMEREQD` (R-144 item 3).
- At most 4 lookups run at once, each in its own `cx.spawn_blocking` job; further addresses wait in a FIFO queue. Lookups are started from the worker loop, never block the 2 s sample.
- Cache by address (not by cookie): positive answers 10 minutes, negative answers 1 minute (SYS-035). A cached address is not looked up again before it expires.
- Each record carries `remote_host: Option<Arc<str>>`: `None` while pending (the UI shows the address), `Some(name)` after a positive answer, `None` again after a negative one.
- When `remote_host_cookies` is empty, no lookups start and the queue is cleared; finished jobs still fill the cache.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** 10 demanded cookies with different addresses **When** lookups start **Then** at most 4 run at the same time.
- **Given** a positive answer cached at t=0 **When** the same address is demanded at t=9 min **Then** no new lookup; at t=11 min a new lookup runs.
- **Given** a negative answer at t=0 **When** demanded again at t=61 s **Then** a new lookup runs.
- **Given** `remote_host_cookies` becomes empty **When** the next wake runs **Then** the queue is empty and no new lookup starts.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/connections.rs`: change.

## Tests
In `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `connections.rs`, LabRuntime with a fake resolver (scripted delays and answers): `rdns_max_four_in_flight`, `rdns_positive_ttl_10_min`, `rdns_negative_ttl_1_min`, `rdns_queue_cleared_without_demand`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: resolver errors count as negative answers.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: at most 4 blocking threads for lookups; the pool max is 4 (ADR-004), so while 4 lookups run the 2 s sample waits for a thread. Record this in the commit message if it shows in the phase-4 measurements.
- Privacy: lookups leak queries to the DNS server, which is why the column is off by default (SYS-035). Never log looked-up names.

## Notes
- Depends on E14-014 (same file). The `tl_ops::sys::reverse_lookup` wrapper is written when P4 starts; it has no bead yet, so this bead gets that edge then (R-144 item 3).
- Read `/home/oystein/work/tasklens/CLAUDE.md` first.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec (`git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`), one commit for this bead.
- asupersync rules (ADR-004, docs/research/claude-asupersync-apis.md): every zbus call and every signal-stream `next()` is wrapped in `time::timeout` (2 s for reads) followed by `cx.checkpoint()`; blocking work only through `Cx::spawn_blocking` joined with `TaskHandle::join`; never `race!`, `select!`, `asupersync::process`, `asupersync::fs`, `asupersync::signal`, `GenServer`, `ChildSpec::depends_on`. Proxies never outlive their worker generation.
close_reason: Reverse DNS for Remote host: tl_ops::sys::reverse_lookup (980a5c0, 9c53711), ConnRecord.remote_host (ab4c162), resolver task and cache in connections.rs (a1f13c8, f99b9e5). Negative TTL 1 min per SYS-035. Tests pass; tl-engine test-target clippy blocked by others' errors in actions/mod.rs:1224 and dbus_systemd.rs:4185.

comments.author: oystein
comments.text: Leader decisions (unblock): (a) chain edit in crates/tl-ops/src/sys.rs: `pub fn reverse_lookup(ip: std::net::IpAddr) -> Result<Option<String>, Errno>` using getnameinfo with NI_NAMEREQD; Ok(None) when there is no name (EAI_NONAME); skip IPv6 link-local and any address with a scope id (return Ok(None) without a lookup); loopback and unspecified also Ok(None) without a lookup. (b) chain edit in tl-model snapshot.rs: `ConnRecord.remote_host: Option<Arc<str>>`, None until resolved; update every constructor. (c) Do not change source.rs. connections.rs owns a resolver: the worker factory starts one extra region-owned task next to source::run, fed by a bounded channel (try_send, drop on full); it runs at most 4 lookups at once through spawn_blocking with a 2 s timeout each, and sends results back on a channel the source drains with try_recv in sample(). Cache by IpAddr: hits 10 min, misses 2 min, at most 4096 entries. Tests use a fake resolver function, never real DNS.

title: E14-A2 KWin bridge
description:
## Context
Anchor E14-A2. The KWin bridge worker `SourceId::KWin` in `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_kwin.rs` (R-046, ADR-004): on KDE Plasma it loads the `tasklens-bridge` script into KWin, serves the `WindowBridge` object the script calls, and publishes the window list as `Snapshot.windows` (`WindowsSnapshot`, keyed by pid). Commands (E14-018) and the picker (E14-019) follow. Sources: PROC-052, PROC-053, PROC-056, ADR-003 (`WindowsSnapshot`), ADR-004 (KWin bridge worker), canonical table (c), R-046, R-086, U-13, ADR-015 (untrusted text).

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_kwin.rs` (new):
  - `pub(crate) fn factory(io: WorkerIo) -> impl ManagedChildFactory<WorkerError>`.
  - Availability, checked at generation start: `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` contains `KDE` (colon-separated list, case-sensitive) and the name `org.kde.KWin` has an owner on the session bus (`org.freedesktop.DBus.NameHasOwner`). If not: publish an empty `WindowsSnapshot` with `header.validity = Unsupported`, then idle (wake every 60 s with `cx.checkpoint()`, no further calls). It also sends `Health { state: SourceState::Unsupported, last_error: Some("KWin bridge not available") }` once; `Unsupported` is terminal and the controller never retries it (R-155 item 4). This is not a failure.
  - Session connection from the E08-A2 helper. Serve object `/io/github/oysteinkrog/Tasklens/WindowBridge`, interface `io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.WindowBridge`, method `Update(s json)` with zbus `#[interface]`.
  - Script: write `include_str!("../../../../assets/kwin/kwin-bridge.js")` with `__TL_BUS_NAME__` replaced by the JSON string of this connection's unique name (R-167 item 5) to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/tasklens/kwin-bridge.js` (directory mode 0700, file 0600, `write_atomic` from tl-ops, E07-A3). Then `org.kde.kwin.Scripting.unloadScript("tasklens-bridge")` (clears a stale copy from a crashed run), `loadScript(path, "tasklens-bridge")`, and `start()` on `/Scripting`.
  - `Update` handler, security checks first: reject (log at debug, return an error reply) when the message sender is not the current owner of `org.kde.KWin` (`GetNameOwner`, refreshed on `NameOwnerChanged`) or when the JSON is longer than 1 MiB (R-167 items 5 and 15). Then parse with `serde_json` into window entries: `internal_id`, `pid`, `caption`, `resource_class`, `desktop_file_name`, `minimized`, `maximized`, `keep_above`, `frame_geometry { x, y, width, height }`, `window_type`. `internal_id` must match a braced UUID `{xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx}` (lowercase hex); entries that fail are dropped. `caption`, `resource_class` and `desktop_file_name` pass through the tl-collect `sanitize` rules (ADR-015: C0 and C1 controls to U+FFFD, bidi controls U+202A to U+202E and U+2066 to U+2069 and U+200B to U+200F removed) and are cut at 4 KiB (R-167 item 15).
  - Each accepted `Update` publishes one `SourceUpdate` with the new `WindowsSnapshot` (entries grouped by pid, order within a pid as received, which is topmost first), `header.validity = Valid`.
  - Cancellation (shutdown): call `unloadScript("tasklens-bridge")` with a 500 ms timeout and delete the script file before returning `Outcome::Ok(())` (PROC-052 "On exit tasklens calls unloadScript").
  - KWin restart (`NameOwnerChanged` for `org.kde.KWin` to a new owner): reload the script as above. Owner gone: publish `Unsupported` until it returns.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/mod.rs`: add `mod dbus_kwin;` and one `WorkerSpec` entry for `SourceId::KWin` in `all_workers()` (chain edits on E08-A1, the only changes to that file; R-167 item 2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=GNOME` **When** the worker starts **Then** it publishes `WindowsSnapshot` with validity `Unsupported`, sends health `SourceState::Unsupported` once, and makes no KWin calls.
- **Given** an `Update` whose sender is not the owner of `org.kde.KWin` **When** received **Then** it is rejected and nothing is published.
- **Given** an `Update` of 1 MiB + 1 byte **When** received **Then** rejected.
- **Given** an entry with `internalId` `"x"); evil("` **When** parsed **Then** that entry is dropped and the others are kept.
- **Given** a caption containing U+202E and a newline **When** parsed **Then** the stored caption has no U+202E and the newline is U+FFFD.
- **Given** two windows with pid 42 **When** published **Then** both are under pid 42 in received order.
- **Given** the substituted bridge script **When** checked **Then** no `__TL_` remains and the unique name appears once.
- **Given** the owner machine on Plasma 6.7.5 **When** tasklens runs and a new window opens **Then** it appears in `Snapshot.windows` within 1 s (manual check, record in the commit message, together with any KWin API name that differed).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_kwin.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/mod.rs`: one `mod` line and one `all_workers()` entry.

## Tests
In `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `dbus_kwin.rs`:
- `unsupported_without_kde` (environment value passed as a parameter; asserts validity `Unsupported` and health `SourceState::Unsupported`).
- `update_rejected_wrong_sender`, `update_rejected_oversize` (handler logic as a pure function taking sender, owner and payload).
- `update_drops_bad_internal_id` (security regression: injection-shaped id).
- `update_sanitizes_caption` (security regression: bidi and control characters).
- `update_groups_by_pid`.
- `bridge_script_placeholder_replaced`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: bus failures after a successful start return `Err(WorkerError::Bus)` so the supervisor restarts the generation; KWin absent is `Unsupported`, not an error.
- Validity: `Valid` or `Unsupported` on the component header.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: no polling; one parse and one publish per KWin event.
- Privacy: window captions are never logged.
- Security: only KWin's connection may call `Update`; window text is sanitized; the bus name is inserted as a JSON string.

## Notes
- Depends on E14-016 (script), E07-A3 (`write_atomic`), E08-A1, E08-A2. Uses `serde_json` (in tl-engine's ADR-001 row; E14-A4 adds the `Cargo.toml` line, R-142 item 7) and tl-collect `sanitize` (E05-A1, which is in E14's anchor row, R-167 item 4).
- tl-app owns the well-known name `io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens` on its own blocking connection (ADR-010 single instance), so KWin cannot reach the engine through that name. The engine's unique name in the script and the `org.kde.KWin` owner check are settled (R-167 item 5).
- The WindowsSnapshot field names come from tl-model (E03-A2).
- Read `/home/oystein/work/tasklens/CLAUDE.md` first.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec (`git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`), one commit for this bead.
- asupersync rules (ADR-004, docs/research/claude-asupersync-apis.md): every zbus call and every signal-stream `next()` is wrapped in `time::timeout` (2 s for reads) followed by `cx.checkpoint()`; blocking work only through `Cx::spawn_blocking` joined with `TaskHandle::join`; never `race!`, `select!`, `asupersync::process`, `asupersync::fs`, `asupersync::signal`, `GenServer`, `ChildSpec::depends_on`. Proxies never outlive their worker generation.
close_reason: KWin bridge worker in workers/dbus_kwin.rs plus mod.rs entry (9d04424, b9c0d9b). 9 unit tests pass, clippy clean. Manual Plasma 6.7.5 check not run: loading KWin scripts on the live desktop is not allowed for agents.

title: E14-016 KWin bridge script kwin-bridge.js
description:
## Context
The KWin script that feeds the KWin bridge (PROC-052, R-046): it runs inside KWin as plugin `tasklens-bridge` and calls tasklens's `WindowBridge.Update(s json)` with the full window list. The file is embedded into tl-engine with `include_str!` and written to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/tasklens/kwin-bridge.js` at run time by E14-A2 (R-138 item 12). Sources: PROC-052, ADR-004 (KWin bridge worker), canonical table (c), R-046, R-086, PERF-083, U-13.

## Deliverable

- Placeholder `__TL_BUS_NAME__` (a JSON string literal, quotes included, replaced by E14-A2 with the engine connection's unique bus name, R-167 item 5).
- Constants: path `/io/github/oysteinkrog/Tasklens/WindowBridge`, interface `io.github.oysteinkrog.Tasklens.WindowBridge`, method `Update`.
- `entry(w)` returns an object with exactly these keys: `internalId` (`w.internalId.toString()`, a braced UUID), `pid` (integer), `caption` (string), `resourceClass` (string), `desktopFileName` (string), `minimized` (bool), `maximized` (bool), `keepAbove` (bool), `frameGeometry` (`{ x, y, width, height }` integers), `windowType` (integer, KWin's window type value).

- Sends the full list once at start, then on `workspace.windowAdded` (also hooks the new window), `workspace.windowRemoved`, `workspace.windowActivated` and each window's `captionChanged` (PROC-052). It also sends on each window's `minimizedChanged`, `maximizedChanged` (or the KWin 6.7.5 equivalent), `keepAboveChanged` and `interactiveMoveResizeFinished`, so state and geometry in the snapshot stay current (PERF-083 reads window moves back from the snapshot); see open item 6 of the B4 plan.

- **Given** KWin 6.7.5 on the owner machine **When** the script is loaded by E14-A2 **Then** `Update` is called once at load and again within 1 s of opening a new window (manual check recorded in the E14-A2 commit message).

title: E14-017 KWin one-shot scripts cmd-template.js and pick.js
description:
## Context
The two one-shot KWin script templates used by the KWin bridge worker: `cmd-template.js` for window commands (activate, close, keep above, set geometry) and `pick.js` for the window picker's pid lookup. Commands must be one-shot scripts because KWin scripts cannot receive D-Bus signals (U-13). Sources: PROC-052, PROC-054, PROC-055, PROC-056, APP-009, PERF-083, canonical table (c), R-138 item 12.

## Deliverable
- `assets/kwin/cmd-template.js` (new):
  - Placeholder `__TL_ARGS__`, replaced by E14-018 with a JSON object literal `{ "plugin": "tasklens-cmd-<n>", "id": "<internalId>", "op": "activate" | "close" | "keep_above" | "geometry", "on": <bool>, "x": <int>, "y": <int>, "width": <int>, "height": <int> }`.
  - Finds the window with `workspace.windowList().find(w => w.internalId.toString() === args.id)`.
  - `activate`: `w.minimized = false; workspace.activeWindow = w;` (PROC-054). `close`: `w.closeWindow()`. `keep_above`: `w.keepAbove = args.on`. `geometry`: `w.frameGeometry = { x: args.x, y: args.y, width: args.width, height: args.height }`.
  - Missing window: does nothing.
  - Last statement unloads itself: `callDBus("org.kde.KWin", "/Scripting", "org.kde.kwin.Scripting", "unloadScript", args.plugin)`.
- `assets/kwin/pick.js` (new):
  - Placeholders `__TL_BUS_NAME__` (as in `kwin-bridge.js`) and `__TL_ARGS__` = `{ "plugin": "tasklens-pick", "uuid": "<uuid>" }`.
  - Finds the window by `internalId.toString() === args.uuid` and calls back tasklens through `WindowBridge.Picked(s uuid, s pid)` with the pid as decimal text (`"0"` when not found) (R-149 item 3, R-241), then unloads itself like the command template.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** each template **When** E14-018 and E14-019 substitute their placeholders **Then** no `__TL_` text remains.
- **Given** `op = "activate"` on the owner machine **When** the command runs **Then** a minimized window is restored and focused (manual check recorded in E14-018).

## Files
- `assets/kwin/cmd-template.js`: create.
- `assets/kwin/pick.js`: create.

## Tests
- Text checks in `dbus_kwin.rs` tests of E14-018 and E14-019.
- `node --check` on both files when `node` is installed; otherwise say so in the commit message.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A in the scripts.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one script load per command.
- Privacy: N/A.
- Security: values only ever enter the scripts through the JSON literal built by serde_json in the engine (E14-018); the templates never concatenate strings into code.

## Notes
- Verify `closeWindow`, `frameGeometry` assignment and `workspace.activeWindow` against the KWin 6.7.5 scripting API and record the result.
- The pick callback method is `Picked(s uuid, s pid)` on the `WindowBridge` interface (R-149 item 3; the pid is text because `callDBus` picks the D-Bus type of a JS number itself, R-241).
- No build step.
- Read `/home/oystein/work/tasklens/CLAUDE.md` first.

title: E14-018 KWin worker: window commands as one-shot scripts
description:
## Context
Window commands for the KWin bridge worker: `Command::KWin(KWinCommand)` activate, close, keep above and set geometry, each run as a one-shot KWin script `tasklens-cmd-<n>` built from `assets/kwin/cmd-template.js`. Used by Show Window (PROC-054), the Name-cell window list (PROC-053), the pin on tasklens windows (PROC-056, APP-009) and detached graph and mini window placement (PERF-083, PERF-093). Sources: PROC-052, PROC-053, PROC-054, PROC-056, APP-009, PERF-083, ADR-005 (`Command::KWin`), U-13.

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_kwin.rs`:
- Handle every non-pick `KWinCommand` variant defined in tl-model (E03-A2): activate a window, close a window, set keep-above on or off, set frame geometry. Each names its window by KWin `internalId`. A command whose id is not a braced lowercase UUID, or is not in the current window list, is dropped and logged at debug.
- Per command: `n` = a per-worker `u64` counter starting at 1. Build the args object with `serde_json` (`{ "plugin": "tasklens-cmd-<n>", "id": .., "op": "activate" | "close" | "keep_above" | "geometry", "on": .., "x": .., "y": .., "width": .., "height": .. }`), replace `__TL_ARGS__` in `include_str!` of `assets/kwin/cmd-template.js`, write it to `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/tasklens/tasklens-cmd-<n>.js` (0600), call `loadScript(path, "tasklens-cmd-<n>")` and `start()` with a 2 s timeout each, then delete the file. Geometry values are clamped to `i32` and width and height to at least 1.
- Commands run one at a time in arrival order. While the bridge is `Unsupported`, commands are dropped.
- The UI decides "No window found" and "Process window shown." from `Snapshot.windows` before sending (PROC-054); this worker sends no result events (R-170 item 8).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** activate for a known id **When** handled **Then** the written script contains `"op":"activate"` and that id as a JSON string, and the file is deleted afterwards.
- **Given** an id `{0000…}"); workspace.windowList().forEach(w=>w.closeWindow()); ("` **When** handled **Then** the command is dropped and no script is written (security regression).
- **Given** an id not in the current window list **When** handled **Then** dropped.
- **Given** three commands **When** handled **Then** plugin names `tasklens-cmd-1`, `-2`, `-3` in order.
- **Given** the owner machine **When** activate is sent for a minimized window **Then** it is restored and focused; keep-above on a tasklens window keeps it above others (manual check, recorded in the commit message).

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_kwin.rs`: change.

## Tests
In `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `dbus_kwin.rs` (script building is a pure function): `cmd_script_activate_args`, `cmd_rejects_injection_id`, `cmd_unknown_id_dropped`, `cmd_plugin_counter_increments`, `cmd_geometry_clamped`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: a failed or timed-out `loadScript` or `start` drops that command and logs at `warn` (R-170 item 8).
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one script load per command.
- Privacy: N/A.
- Security: ids are validated and every value enters the script only through serde_json.

## Notes
- Depends on E14-A2 (same file) and E14-017 (template).
- `Command::KWin(c)` reaches this worker as a `QueuedCommand { target: KWin, command: KWin(c) }` in `WorkerIo.control`, sent by the reducer's `forward()` (R-166 B3-1, R-167 item 2). The `KWinCommand` variants are E03-063's, with `seq` on `Pick` and `CancelPick` (R-156 item 1, R-149 item 3).
- Read `/home/oystein/work/tasklens/CLAUDE.md` first.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec (`git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`), one commit for this bead.
- asupersync rules (ADR-004, docs/research/claude-asupersync-apis.md): every zbus call and every signal-stream `next()` is wrapped in `time::timeout` (2 s for reads) followed by `cx.checkpoint()`; blocking work only through `Cx::spawn_blocking` joined with `TaskHandle::join`; never `race!`, `select!`, `asupersync::process`, `asupersync::fs`, `asupersync::signal`, `GenServer`, `ChildSpec::depends_on`. Proxies never outlive their worker generation.

title: E14-019 KWin worker: window picker
description:
## Context
P3. The window picker behind the toolbar "+" button: KWin's interactive pick returns a window, the worker finds its pid and reports it to the UI. Sources: PROC-055, APP-006, UI-SHL-014, U-14, canonical table (c) (`tasklens-pick`).

## Deliverable
In `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_kwin.rs`:
- On `KWinCommand::Pick { seq }` (R-149 item 3): call `org.kde.KWin.queryWindowInfo()` on `/KWin` (interface `org.kde.KWin`) with a 120 s timeout (the user picks interactively). The reply is `a{sv}` with `uuid`.
- If the map has `pid` (U-14): use it. Otherwise load `assets/kwin/pick.js` as plugin `tasklens-pick` with `__TL_BUS_NAME__` and `__TL_ARGS__` (`{ "plugin": "tasklens-pick", "uuid": .. }`) substituted, and wait up to 2 s for the script's callback on the WindowBridge object carrying the pid.
- Callback: add method `Picked(s uuid, s pid)` to the existing `WindowBridge` `#[interface]` (R-149 item 3; `s pid` per R-241). Same sender check as `Update`: only the current owner of `org.kde.KWin` (R-167 item 5). A call whose `uuid` is not the pending pick's uuid is ignored. The pid text is parsed as `u32`; `"0"` or text that does not parse gives `NoWindow` (R-241).
- Shell windows are ignored: when the picked window's `windowType` is desktop, dock, notification, critical notification or on-screen display (KWin window type values verified against KWin 6.7.5), the result is "no window".
- `queryWindowInfo` returning an error because the user pressed Esc: result "cancelled". `KWinCommand::CancelPick { seq }` (UI-SHL-014, R-149 item 3) with the running pick's `seq`: drop the pending result and report "cancelled". A `CancelPick` with another `seq` is ignored.
- Report the result as `WindowsSnapshot.pick = Some(PickResult { seq, outcome })` with `outcome` one of `PickOutcome::Picked { pid }`, `PickOutcome::NoWindow`, `PickOutcome::Cancelled`, published with the current window list through the existing `SourceUpdate::Windows` (R-149 items 3 and 4). Later window-list publishes keep the last `pick`. The UI maps them to the toasts in PROC-055 ("No window found", "No window selected", "Unknown process").
- Record the U-14 outcome (does `queryWindowInfo` return `pid` on KWin 6.7.5) in the commit message.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a reply map with `pid = 1234` **When** handled **Then** the result is `Picked { pid: 1234 }` and no script is loaded.
- **Given** a reply without `pid` and a script callback with 1234 **When** handled **Then** `Picked { pid: 1234 }`.
- **Given** no callback within 2 s **When** handled **Then** `NoWindow`.
- **Given** a picked dock window **When** handled **Then** `NoWindow`.
- **Given** `queryWindowInfo` returns an error **When** handled **Then** `Cancelled`.
- **Given** `CancelPick { seq: 5 }` during pick 5 **When** handled **Then** `Cancelled` and a later reply is ignored.
- **Given** `CancelPick { seq: 4 }` during pick 5 **When** handled **Then** it is ignored and pick 5 continues.
- **Given** `Pick { seq: 5 }` and a reply with `pid = 1234` **When** handled **Then** the next `SourceUpdate::Windows` carries `pick == Some(PickResult { seq: 5, outcome: PickOutcome::Picked { pid: 1234 } })`.
- **Given** a `Picked` callback with pid text `"abc"` or `"0"` **When** handled **Then** `NoWindow`.
- **Given** a `Picked` call from a sender that is not the owner of `org.kde.KWin` **When** received **Then** it is rejected and the pick keeps waiting.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_kwin.rs`: change.

## Tests
In `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `dbus_kwin.rs` with a fake KWin call layer: `pick_uses_reply_pid`, `pick_script_fallback`, `pick_timeout_no_window`, `pick_ignores_shell_windows`, `pick_esc_cancelled`, `pick_cancel_command`, `pick_cancel_wrong_seq_ignored`, `pick_result_in_windows_snapshot`, `pick_callback_bad_pid_text_no_window`, `pick_callback_wrong_sender_rejected` (security regression).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: timeouts give `NoWindow`; bus errors give `Cancelled` and are logged.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A (keyboard handling of the picker is UI work).
- Performance: one pending pick at a time; a second `Pick` while one runs is ignored.
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- Depends on E14-018 and E14-017.
- The result path (`WindowsSnapshot.pick`), `Pick { seq }`, `CancelPick { seq }` and the `Picked(s uuid, s pid)` callback are settled (R-149 items 3 and 4, R-241). `PickResult` and `PickOutcome` are E03-050's types (`snapshot.rs`).
- Read `/home/oystein/work/tasklens/CLAUDE.md` first.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec (`git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`), one commit for this bead.
- asupersync rules (ADR-004, docs/research/claude-asupersync-apis.md): every zbus call and every signal-stream `next()` is wrapped in `time::timeout` (2 s for reads) followed by `cx.checkpoint()`; blocking work only through `Cx::spawn_blocking` joined with `TaskHandle::join`; never `race!`, `select!`, `asupersync::process`, `asupersync::fs`, `asupersync::signal`, `GenServer`, `ChildSpec::depends_on`. Proxies never outlive their worker generation.

title: E14-020 opener.rs: OpenURI portal, FileManager1, xdg-open fallback
description:
## Context
The session-bus opener `crates/tl-engine/src/opener.rs` (R-134): runs `ActionKind::OpenUri` and `ActionKind::ShowInFileManager` for the UI (Open file location, File properties, Open unit file, Open log folder, links). E11 admits the action and calls these functions; this bead writes them. It also writes `activate_action` for `LaunchWhat::DbusActivate` (P3, R-170 item 11) and the portal colour scheme reader that feeds `SystemSnapshot.color_scheme` (R-170 item 4). Sources: R-134, R-148, R-170, UI-FND-042, ADR-005 (action kinds, 2 s deadline), PROC-073, PROC-095 (URL path), SYS-008, SYS-025, UI-SHL-093, PERF-061.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/opener.rs` (new), `pub(crate)` API:
- `async fn open_uri(cx: &Cx, session: Option<Arc<zbus::Connection>>, target: &str) -> Result<(), ActionError>`:
  - `target` is a URI with a scheme (`^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*:`), or an absolute path.
  - URI other than `file:`: portal `org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop`, path `/org/freedesktop/portal/desktop`, `org.freedesktop.portal.OpenURI.OpenURI(s parent_window = "", s uri, a{sv} options = {})`.
  - Absolute path or `file:` URI: open the file `O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC` and call `org.freedesktop.portal.OpenURI.OpenFile(s "", h fd, a{sv} {})`.
  - Fallback when there is no session connection or the portal call fails: spawn `/usr/bin/xdg-open <target>` detached with the tl-ops launch helper (E07-A3: `posix_spawn`, `setsid`, stdio `/dev/null`); a successful spawn is success.
- `async fn show_in_file_manager(cx: &Cx, session: Option<Arc<zbus::Connection>>, path: &str, properties: bool) -> Result<(), ActionError>`:
  - `path` must be absolute; else `ActionError::Internal("not an absolute path")`.
  - If `org.freedesktop.FileManager1` has an owner: `org.freedesktop.FileManager1.ShowItems(as [file_uri(path)], s "")`, or `ShowItemProperties(..)` when `properties` is true, on `/org/freedesktop/FileManager1`.
  - No owner: `properties = false` falls back to `open_uri` on the parent directory (PROC-073); `properties = true` returns `Err(ActionError::Unsupported)` (R-148 item 3; the UI hides File properties in that case).
- `async fn activate_action(cx: &Cx, session: Option<Arc<zbus::Connection>>, bus_name: &str, object_path: &str, action: &str, parameter: Option<&str>) -> Result<(), ActionError>` for `LaunchWhat::DbusActivate` (P3, PERF-061 GNOME network settings, R-170 item 11): calls `org.freedesktop.Application.ActivateAction(s action, av parameter, a{sv} platform_data = {})` on `bus_name` at `object_path`. `parameter` is an empty `av` when `None`, else one string variant. 2 s deadline. No session connection, a D-Bus error or the timeout gives `Err(ActionError::Internal(<reason>))`; nothing is spawned.
- Colour scheme reader (R-170 item 4), portal `org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop`, path `/org/freedesktop/portal/desktop`, interface `org.freedesktop.portal.Settings`:
  - `async fn read_color_scheme(cx: &Cx, session: &zbus::Connection) -> Option<u8>`: `Read("org.freedesktop.appearance", "color-scheme")` with a 2 s timeout. The reply is a variant; unwrap nested variants until a `u32`. Values 0 (no preference), 1 (prefer dark), 2 (prefer light) give `Some(v)`; any other value, a missing key or an error gives `None`.
  - `async fn watch_color_scheme(cx: &Cx, session: &zbus::Connection, tx: &<the EngineMsg sender type of WorkerIo, E08-004>) -> Result<(), WorkerError>`: sends `SourceUpdate::ColorScheme(v)` once with the read value (when `Some`), then subscribes to `SettingChanged(s namespace, s key, v value)` and sends `SourceUpdate::ColorScheme(v)` for each signal with namespace `org.freedesktop.appearance`, key `color-scheme` and a value 0 to 2. Other keys and values are ignored. `SourceUpdate::ColorScheme(u8)` is E08-003's variant (`source_of` gives `None`); the reducer writes `SystemSnapshot.color_scheme` (8q0.9).
- `fn file_uri(path: &str) -> String`: `file://` plus the path with every byte outside `A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~ /` percent-encoded as `%XX` (uppercase hex).
- Every D-Bus call has a 2 s `time::timeout`; the whole call is bounded by the 2 s action deadline E11 applies (ADR-006).
- `crates/tl-engine/src/lib.rs`: add `mod opener;` (chain edit, the only change to that file).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `/home/u/My File#1.txt` **When** `file_uri` runs **Then** `file:///home/u/My%20File%231.txt`.
- **Given** a path with bytes `0xC3 0xA9` **When** encoded **Then** `%C3%A9`.
- **Given** `https://example.org` and a fake portal that errors **When** `open_uri` runs **Then** the xdg-open fallback is spawned with exactly that argument.
- **Given** `relative/path` **When** `show_in_file_manager` runs **Then** an error, and no D-Bus call or spawn.
- **Given** no FileManager1 owner and `properties = false` **When** called with `/usr/bin/foo` **Then** `open_uri("/usr/bin")` runs.
- **Given** no session connection **When** `open_uri("https://x")` runs **Then** xdg-open is spawned.
- **Given** no FileManager1 owner and `properties = true` **When** called with `/usr/bin/foo` **Then** `Err(ActionError::Unsupported)` and no D-Bus call or spawn (R-148 item 3).
- **Given** `activate_action("org.gnome.Settings", "/org/gnome/Settings", "launch-panel", Some("network"))` and a fake bus **When** it runs **Then** one `ActivateAction` call on that bus name and path with action `launch-panel`, `av` holding one string variant `network`, and empty platform data.
- **Given** `parameter = None` **When** `activate_action` runs **Then** the `av` argument is empty.
- **Given** a fake portal whose `Read` reply is a variant holding a variant holding `u32 1` **When** `read_color_scheme` runs **Then** `Some(1)`.
- **Given** a `Read` reply of `u32 7` **When** `read_color_scheme` runs **Then** `None`.
- **Given** a `SettingChanged("org.freedesktop.appearance", "color-scheme", u32 2)` signal **When** watched **Then** `SourceUpdate::ColorScheme(2)` is sent.
- **Given** a `SettingChanged` signal for namespace `org.freedesktop.appearance` and key `accent-color` **When** watched **Then** nothing is sent.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/opener.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/lib.rs`: one `mod` line.

## Tests
In `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `opener.rs`, with the bus calls and the spawn behind small function parameters so fakes record calls: `file_uri_encoding`, `file_uri_utf8`, `open_uri_portal_error_falls_back`, `show_rejects_relative_path` (security regression: no spawn on bad input), `show_without_filemanager_opens_parent`, `open_uri_without_session_spawns_xdg_open`, `show_properties_without_filemanager_unsupported`, `activate_action_args`, `activate_action_no_parameter_empty_av`, `color_scheme_read_nested_variant`, `color_scheme_read_out_of_range_none`, `color_scheme_signal_sends_update`, `color_scheme_other_key_ignored`.
`#[ignore]` real test `real_open_uri_portal`: opens `https://example.org` on the owner machine and expects `Ok`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `Unsupported` for File properties without a `FileManager1` owner (R-148 item 3); `Internal("not an absolute path")` for a relative path; portal failures fall back to xdg-open; `activate_action` failures are `Internal`. The UI shows the toasts named in the specs.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one D-Bus call or one spawn per action.
- Privacy: never log the opened path or URI above debug level.
- Security: arguments go to `xdg-open` as one argv element, never through a shell.

## Notes
- Depends on E07-A3 (spawn helper) and E08-A2 (D-Bus helper). The session connection comes from the `SystemdUser` worker's slot, `SharedHandles.systemd_user` (`ManagerConnSlot`, E08-009, R-166 B3-8); E11 passes it in.
- Colour scheme host, settled (R-244): the `SystemdUser` generation of the systemd worker (E14-001, y6k.5) runs `watch_color_scheme(cx, &conn, &io.tx)` as a child task after its session-bus connect, in `EngineMode::Full` only; a reconnect starts it again. This bead writes the two reader functions and their tests only. It starts no task and adds no worker. Depends on E08-003 (8hz.5) for `SourceUpdate::ColorScheme`.
- `activate_action` serves a P3 feature (PERF-061); it is written here because the launcher (E14-A3) must handle every `LaunchWhat` variant.
- Check that `OpenFile` works for a directory on the owner machine; if the portal rejects directories, use `OpenURI` with the `file:` URI for directories and record it.
- Read `/home/oystein/work/tasklens/CLAUDE.md` first.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

title: E14-021 Real-system tests: launcher scopes and Run now
description:
## Context
Real-system tests for the launcher and opener on the owner machine: a launched command lands in its own transient scope and groups as an app. Sources: SYS-023, PROC-095, canonical table (c) (`app-tasklens-run-<rand>.scope`), ADR-013 (real-system tests).

## Deliverable

- `real_command_lands_in_transient_scope`: launch `Command("sleep 30")`; within 2 s `/proc/<pid>/cgroup` of the spawned shell contains `app-tasklens-run-` and `.scope`; then `systemctl --user stop` that scope.

title: KWin one-shot scripts: delete the script file later, not right after start()
description:
Files: crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_kwin.rs.
Why: y6k.22 deletes tasklens-cmd-<n>.js straight after loadScript and start() return. KWin may read the file on a worker thread after start() returns (unverified), so the delete could win the race and the command would silently do nothing.
Deliverable: keep the file until the next command runs, until the bridge reports the command's effect, or until the worker exits, whichever comes first; then delete it. Never leave more than 2 command files behind. On worker start, delete stale tasklens-cmd-*.js files from earlier runs in the same directory.
AC: Given two commands in a row with the fake script host, when the second runs, then the first file is deleted and the second exists. Given worker shutdown, then no command file remains. Given a stale tasklens-cmd-7.js at start, then it is deleted. Manual: the owner's desktop check (window commands work on Plasma 6.7.5) covers the real race.
close_reason: KWin command script kept until the next command, the next Update or worker exit (CmdFiles); stale tasklens-cmd-<n>.js deleted at start. Commit ffeb285

title: systemd worker: read ControlGroup for slice and scope units
description:
Files: crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_systemd.rs.
Why: y6k.7 found that type_iface reads ControlGroup only for service, socket, mount and timer units (E14-002 code). Slices and scopes therefore never get cgroup pids or stats, but app scopes (app-*.scope) and user slices are exactly the units the Services and process views group by.
Deliverable: read ControlGroup (and the resource properties the record uses) from org.freedesktop.systemd1.Slice and org.freedesktop.systemd1.Scope for those unit types, so cgroup_pids, has_cgroup_procs and the stats fill for them too.
AC: Given a fake bus that lists a scope with ControlGroup /user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/app-foo.scope and a fixture cgroup with 2 pids, when a pid tick runs, then that unit's cgroup_pids has the 2 keys. Same for a slice. Existing dbus_systemd tests pass. Read-only bus access only.
close_reason: type_iface now reads org.freedesktop.systemd1.Slice and .Scope, so ControlGroup and cgroup pids/stats fill for slices and scopes; test slice_and_scope_cgroup_pids. Commit 40e1ee1

title: systemd worker: one cgroup walk per tick, attribute pids to every ancestor unit, skip the root slice
description:
Files: crates/tl-engine/src/workers/dbus_systemd.rs, crates/tl-engine/src/dbus/mod.rs (test constructor only).
Why: y6k.27 made slices and scopes read ControlGroup. -.slice has ControlGroup "/" and the pid walk is recursive per unit, so each listing and each pid tick (while process_table demand is on) now walks every pid on the system once per slice level. Also y6k.27's test could not use a fake bus because DbusConn has no test constructor.
Deliverable:
- Walk the cgroup tree once per tick. For each cgroup with pids, give its pids to the unit that owns that cgroup and to every ancestor slice unit (map ControlGroup path to unit). has_cgroup_procs comes from the same walk.
- -.slice (ControlGroup "/") gets no cgroup_pids and is not walked as a unit of its own.
- Add a #[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-hooks"))] DbusConn constructor over a p2p connection so worker tests can use a fake systemd bus; rewrite slice_and_scope_cgroup_pids to list the units over that fake bus.
AC: Given a fixture tree with system.slice/a.service (2 pids) and user.slice/user-1000.slice/app.slice/app-foo.scope (3 pids), when a pid tick runs, then a.service has 2, app-foo.scope 3, app.slice 3, user.slice 3, system.slice 2, and -.slice none; the walk reads each cgroup.procs file once (count reads through the fixture fs). Existing dbus_systemd tests pass. clippy clean.
close_reason: One cgroup walk per tick and per listing (walk_pids): each cgroup.procs read once, pids go to the owning unit and every ancestor unit, root cgroup / (-.slice) never read and gets no pids; pid stats read once per tick. DbusConn::p2p test constructor; slice_and_scope_cgroup_pids lists units over a fake p2p systemd bus. Commits acd004d, f20c27f

title: E14-A3 Startup and connections workers, launcher, opener
description:
## Context
Anchor E14-A3. The shared launcher `crates/tl-engine/src/launcher.rs` (R-134): runs `ActionKind::Launch(LaunchSpec)` for the Run dialog (PROC-095) and Startup "Run now" (SYS-023). Programs start detached in a new transient user scope so they group as apps. E11 admits the action, applies the deadline and reports events; this bead writes the launch functions. The Startup worker (E14-011 to E14-013) and the Connections worker (E14-014) are separate E14 beads. Sources: R-134, ADR-005 (`LaunchSpec`, `LaunchWhat`), ADR-006 (deadlines, Run as administrator), PROC-095, SYS-023, R-117, canonical table (c) (scope names).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-engine/src/launcher.rs` (new), `pub(crate)`:
- `enum LaunchOutcome { Launched, AlreadyRunning }`. E11 reports `AlreadyRunning` as `ActionState::Rejected(RejectReason::AlreadyRunning)`, not as an error; the UI shows the toast "Already running" (SYS-023, R-148 item 4).
- `async fn launch(cx: &Cx, session: Option<Arc<zbus::Connection>>, spec: &LaunchSpec) -> Result<LaunchOutcome, ActionError>`. Working directory: `spec.cwd`, else `$HOME`.
- `LaunchWhat::Command(text)` (Run dialog, PROC-095):
  1. Text containing NUL or any C0 control character other than tab: `Err(ActionError::Unsupported)` (R-148 item 3; the UI shows "Command contains invalid text.").
  2. Trimmed text matching `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*:` (a URI scheme): `opener::open_uri` (E14-020).
  3. Trimmed text that is an existing path (absolute, or starting with `~/` expanded to `$HOME`) and is a directory or not executable by the current user (`access(X_OK)` fails): `opener::open_uri` with that path.
  4. Text matching `^kcm_[A-Za-z0-9_]+$`: argv `["systemsettings", <text>]`.
  5. Anything else: argv `["/bin/sh", "-c", <text>]`.
  Spawn detached with the tl-ops launch helper (E07-A3: `posix_spawn`, `setsid`, stdio `/dev/null`, the cwd above), then create the scope `app-tasklens-run-<rand>.scope` (below).
- `as_admin = true` with `Command(text)`: argv from the tl-ops administrator form `pkexec env DISPLAY=<$DISPLAY> WAYLAND_DISPLAY=<$WAYLAND_DISPLAY> XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=<$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR> /bin/sh -c <text>` (only variables that are set are passed), under `org.freedesktop.policykit.exec`, never tl-helper (ADR-006). No transient scope. Exit status 126 (dismissed prompt, "Authentication cancelled") gives `Err(ActionError::AuthCancelled)`; 127 (not authorized) gives `Err(ActionError::NotAuthorized)` (R-117, R-148 item 3). The launch counts as `Launched` (E11 reports `Succeeded`) when the `pkexec` child is still running 2 s after the prompt closed (R-148 item 5). Prompt detection (R-253): `pkexec` authenticates in its own process and then `execv`s the program in place, so the pid stays and its comm changes. Poll `/proc/<pid>/stat` every 250 ms on the blocking pool: while the comm (the text between the parentheses) is `pkexec`, the prompt is open or being checked. The prompt counts as closed on the first poll where the comm is not `pkexec`, or when `waitpid(pid, WNOHANG)` reports an exit. Exit while the comm was still `pkexec`: 126 gives `AuthCancelled`, 127 gives `NotAuthorized`, any other status `Err(ActionError::Internal("pkexec exited with status <n>"))`. After the comm changed: still running 2 s later, or exited with status 0 within those 2 s, gives `Launched`; a non-zero exit within the 2 s gives `Err(Internal("exited with status <n>"))`. The child is a direct child (the tl-ops helper spawns with `posix_spawn` and `setsid`, no double fork), so `waitpid` works; the 120 s deadline bounds the whole wait.
- `LaunchWhat::DesktopEntry(id)` (Startup Run now, SYS-023):
  1. Generated unit `app-<escaped id>@autostart.service` (escape with the tl-collect systemd-escape function, E06-A2) on the user manager: if it is loaded or loadable (`LoadUnit` gives `LoadState` not `not-found`): when its `ActiveState` is `active`, return `AlreadyRunning`; else `StartUnit(name, "replace")`, adding the `JobRemoved` match before the call, and wait for `JobRemoved` of the returned job path up to 30 s: `done` gives `Launched`, any other result gives `ActionError::UnitJob { result, error_name: None }` (R-170 item 9).
  2. Otherwise find `<id>.desktop` in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/autostart`, then each `$XDG_CONFIG_DIRS` entry plus `/autostart` (same precedence as SYS-019), parse it with the E06-A2 desktop entry parser, build argv from `Exec` with the tl-ops Exec parser (E07-A3: field codes `%f %F %u %U` removed, `%i %c %k` expanded, quoting rules), cwd from `Path=` if set, spawn as above, then create the scope `app-tasklens-<escaped id>-<rand>.scope` with `Description` = the entry's `Name`.
- `LaunchWhat::DbusActivate { bus_name, object_path, action, parameter }` (P3, PERF-061, GNOME network settings): calls `opener::activate_action` (E14-020) with those fields and returns `Launched` on `Ok`; nothing is spawned and no scope is created (R-170 item 11).
- `LaunchWhat::Unit(unit)`: `StartUnit(name, "replace")` on that unit's manager with the `JobRemoved` wait above (30 s).
- Transient scope (SYS-023, PROC-095): `StartTransientUnit(name, "fail", [("PIDs", au [pid]), ("Description", s <text or Name>), ("CollectMode", s "inactive-or-failed")], [])` on the user manager. Failure (or no session connection) is logged at warning and is not an error; the program still runs.
- `<rand>`: 8 lowercase hex digits from 4 bytes read from `/dev/urandom` (R-167 item 12).
- All `zbus` calls use 2 s timeouts except the 30 s `JobRemoved` wait; `pkexec` waits are bounded by the 120 s deadline E11 applies (R-134).
- `crates/tl-engine/src/lib.rs`: add `mod launcher;` (chain edit, the only change to that file).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** text `"echo\u{0}x"` **When** launched **Then** `Err(ActionError::Unsupported)` and nothing is spawned (security regression).
- **Given** `https://example.org` **When** launched **Then** `open_uri` is called and nothing else is spawned.
- **Given** an existing non-executable file `/tmp/x.txt` **When** launched **Then** `open_uri("/tmp/x.txt")`.
- **Given** `kcm_kwin_effects` **When** launched **Then** argv is `["systemsettings", "kcm_kwin_effects"]`.
- **Given** `firefox --new-window` **When** launched **Then** argv is `["/bin/sh", "-c", "firefox --new-window"]` and a scope named `app-tasklens-run-<8 hex>.scope` is requested with that pid.
- **Given** `as_admin` and `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0` with `DISPLAY` unset **When** launched **Then** argv is `["pkexec", "env", "WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0", "XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=…", "/bin/sh", "-c", <text>]` and no scope is requested.
- **Given** `as_admin` and `pkexec` exits with 126 **When** launched **Then** `Err(ActionError::AuthCancelled)`; with 127 **Then** `Err(ActionError::NotAuthorized)` (R-148 item 3).
- **Given** `as_admin` and the `pkexec` child still running 2 s after the prompt closed **When** launched **Then** `Launched` (R-148 item 5).
- **Given** `as_admin` and a fake `/proc/<pid>/stat` reader whose comm turns from `pkexec` to `env` on the third poll **When** the child is still alive 2 s later **Then** `Launched`; **When** it exits with status 0 within those 2 s **Then** `Launched`; **When** it exits with status 2 within those 2 s **Then** `Err(Internal("exited with status 2"))` (R-253).
- **Given** `as_admin` and the child exits with status 1 while its comm is still `pkexec` **When** launched **Then** `Err(Internal("pkexec exited with status 1"))` (R-253).
- **Given** `DbusActivate { bus_name: "org.gnome.Settings", object_path: "/org/gnome/Settings", action: "launch-panel", parameter: Some("network") }` **When** launched **Then** `opener::activate_action` is called once with those values and nothing is spawned (R-170 item 11).
- **Given** a desktop entry whose generated unit is active **When** launched **Then** `AlreadyRunning` and no `StartUnit`.
- **Given** a desktop entry without a generated unit and `Exec=foo %U --bar` **When** launched **Then** argv `["foo", "--bar"]` and scope `app-tasklens-<escaped id>-<8 hex>.scope` with Description = Name.
- **Given** `StartTransientUnit` fails **When** launching a command **Then** the result is still `Launched`.
- **Given** `JobRemoved` result `failed` **When** launching a unit **Then** `Err(UnitJob { result: "failed", error_name: None })`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/launcher.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/lib.rs`: one `mod` line.

## Tests
In `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `launcher.rs`, with the spawn helper, the opener and the bus calls behind function parameters so fakes record argv and calls:
- `rejects_nul_and_controls` (security), `scheme_goes_to_opener`, `non_executable_path_goes_to_opener`, `kcm_runs_systemsettings`, `shell_command_argv_and_scope_name`, `admin_argv_only_set_vars_no_scope` (security), `admin_exit_126_auth_cancelled`, `admin_exit_127_not_authorized`, `admin_running_after_2s_launched`, `admin_prompt_closed_by_comm_change`, `admin_exit_before_prompt_closed`, `dbus_activate_goes_to_opener`, `desktop_entry_already_running`, `desktop_entry_exec_and_scope`, `scope_failure_not_fatal`, `unit_job_failed_maps_unitjob`.
- `rand_suffix_is_8_lower_hex`.
Real-system coverage is E14-021.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `Unsupported` for invalid command text, `AuthCancelled` for `pkexec` 126, `NotAuthorized` for `pkexec` 127 (R-148 item 3), `UnitJob { result, error_name }` for a failed job (R-170 item 9). "Already running" is `Rejected(AlreadyRunning)`, not an error (R-148 item 4). Scope creation failures never fail the launch.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one spawn and at most three D-Bus calls per launch.
- Privacy: never log command text or Exec lines above debug level (they can hold secrets).
- Security: no shell except the explicit `/bin/sh -c` forms the specs name; argv elements are never re-joined; the administrator path goes only through `pkexec env … /bin/sh -c`.

## Notes
- Depends on E14-020 (opener), E07-A3 (spawn helper, Exec parser, administrator form), E06-A2 (escape function, desktop entry parser), E08-A2 (D-Bus helper). The session connection is the `SystemdUser` worker's slot, `SharedHandles.systemd_user` (`ManagerConnSlot`, E08-009, R-166 B3-8); E11 passes it in.
- Plasma scripts in Startup Run now (SYS-023 "spawned the same way through `/bin/sh <path>`") have no `LaunchWhat` variant; E11 sends them as `LaunchWhat::Command` with the shell-quoted path (R-148 item 5).
- Read `/home/oystein/work/tasklens/CLAUDE.md` first.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-engine`). On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec (`git commit -m "..." -- <your files>`), one commit for this bead.
- asupersync rules (ADR-004, docs/research/claude-asupersync-apis.md): every zbus call and every signal-stream `next()` is wrapped in `time::timeout` (2 s for reads) followed by `cx.checkpoint()`; blocking work only through `Cx::spawn_blocking` joined with `TaskHandle::join`; never `race!`, `select!`, `asupersync::process`, `asupersync::fs`, `asupersync::signal`, `GenServer`, `ChildSpec::depends_on`. Proxies never outlive their worker generation.
close_reason: launcher.rs: Command/DesktopEntry/Unit/DbusActivate launch, pkexec prompt watch (R-253), transient scopes; mod line in lib.rs. Commits 2e6a3d9, fcdb9ad

title: E14-A4 Journal
description:
## Context
Anchor E14-A4. The `Journal` worker: one `journalctl` child per open `JournalHandle`, used by the Service Properties Logs tab. This bead delivers the initial fetch (last 200 entries of the current boot), JSON parsing, the access check, the error events and the hookup of `EngineClient::journal`. Follow mode and Load older are E14-009. Sources: ADR-005 (`EngineClient::journal`, `JournalQuery`, `JournalHandle`, `JournalEvent`, `JournalEntry`, `JournalAccess`, `JournalError`), ADR-016 row "Service logs", SYS-015, R-074, R-118, UI-SYS-036, UI-SYS-038.

## Deliverable
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/journal.rs` (new):
  - `pub(crate) fn open(rt: &RuntimeHandle, query: JournalQuery) -> JournalHandle`: creates the event channel `async_channel::bounded::<JournalEvent>(64)` and the control channel of the tl-model `JournalHandle`, spawns one task with `spawn_checked` that owns the session, and returns the handle.
  - Command line, run with `std::process::Command` inside `cx.spawn_blocking` (never `asupersync::process`):
    - system unit: `journalctl -u <id> -b -n 200 -o json --no-pager`
    - user unit: `journalctl --user-unit <id> -b -n 200 -o json --no-pager`
    The unit id is passed as one argument (no shell). stdin `/dev/null`, stdout and stderr piped.
  - 5 s timeout on this fetch: the blocking closure polls the stdout and stderr fds with `rustix::event::poll` against a deadline of 5 s from spawn; past it, kill the child, `wait()` it and report `JournalError::Timeout`.
  - Parsing, one JSON object per line (`serde_json`): `__REALTIME_TIMESTAMP` (decimal string, µs) to `realtime_us`; `PRIORITY` (decimal string "0" to "7") to `priority`, missing or invalid gives 6; `MESSAGE` as a string, or as an array of bytes decoded with `String::from_utf8_lossy`, missing gives an empty message; `_PID` (decimal string) to `pid`; `__CURSOR` to `cursor`. A line that is not valid JSON or lacks `__CURSOR` is skipped and counted; the count is logged at debug.
  - Events, in order: first `Access(..)`, then one `Batch { entries, older: false, exhausted: entries.len() < 200 }`, or one `Error(..)` instead of the batch.
  - Access (SYS-015): for a system unit, `All` when the effective uid is 0 or the process is a member of group `wheel`, `adm` or `systemd-journal` (gids from `/etc/group`, membership from `getgroups()` plus the primary gid); otherwise `OwnOnly`. For a user unit, always `All` (R-167 item 9).
  - Errors: spawn fails with `NotFound` gives `JournalError::NotFound`; timeout gives `Timeout`; non-zero exit gives `Exit { code, stderr_first_line }` with the first stderr line, at most 200 characters.
  - The task keeps the last cursor and the oldest cursor for E14-009.
  - When the handle's event receiver is dropped (`Sender::is_closed()`), the task kills any running child, waits for it, and ends.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/mod.rs`: add `mod journal;` (chain edit, the only change to that file).
- `crates/tl-engine/src/bridge.rs`: `EngineClient::journal` calls `crate::workers::journal::open(&self.runtime_handle, query)` (one-line chain edit in an E09-owned file, allowed by R-167 item 2).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fixture with 3 valid JSON lines and 1 broken line **When** parsed **Then** 3 entries with the right `realtime_us`, `priority`, `pid`, `message`, `cursor`, and the broken line is skipped.
- **Given** a `MESSAGE` that is a byte array `[104,105]` **When** parsed **Then** the message is "hi".
- **Given** a line without `PRIORITY` **When** parsed **Then** priority is 6.
- **Given** 150 entries returned **When** the fetch ends **Then** the batch has `exhausted: true`; with 200 entries it is `false`.
- **Given** `journalctl` is not on PATH (test sets `PATH` for the child to an empty dir) **When** opened **Then** the events are `Access(..)` then `Error(NotFound)`.
- **Given** a fake `journalctl` script that sleeps 10 s **When** opened **Then** `Error(Timeout)` arrives within 6 s and the child is reaped.
- **Given** a fake script that prints "boom" to stderr and exits 1 **When** opened **Then** `Error(Exit { code: 1, stderr_first_line: "boom" })`.
- **Given** a user not in wheel, adm or systemd-journal **When** a system unit is opened **Then** `Access(OwnOnly)` comes first.
- **Given** the handle is dropped while a child runs **When** the task notices **Then** the child is killed and waited.

## Files
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/journal.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/workers/mod.rs`: one `mod` line.
- `crates/tl-engine/src/bridge.rs`: one line in `EngineClient::journal` (allowed, R-167 item 2).
- `crates/tl-engine/Cargo.toml`: chain edit, add `serde_json = { workspace = true }` (R-142 item 7).

## Tests
In `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `journal.rs`:
- `parse_journal_json_lines`, `parse_message_byte_array`, `parse_missing_priority_default`, `batch_exhausted_flag`.
- `fetch_not_found`, `fetch_timeout_kills_child`, `fetch_exit_error_first_line`: fake `journalctl` shell scripts in a temp dir placed first on the child's PATH; the binary name stays `journalctl`.
- `access_own_only_without_groups`: the group check takes the group file path and gid list as parameters.
- `drop_handle_kills_child`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `JournalError::{NotFound, Timeout, Exit}` as above; never a worker restart.
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one blocking job per fetch; 200 entries parsed once; no per-frame work.
- Privacy: never log journal message text; log only counts, exit codes and durations.

## Notes
- `serde_json` is in tl-engine's ADR-001 row (R-142 item 7). This bead adds the dependency line; E12-028 and E14-009 use it.
- The `JournalHandle` constructor and its control channel type live in tl-model (E03-A2); if a field is missing, stop and report to the leader (R-156 item 4: the leader checks as2.20, as2.21 and as2.27 against the E14 field names before E14-A1 starts).
- Journal message text is passed through unchanged; the UI shows it with its untrusted-text rules.
