title: E05-017 Process flags and the protected set
description:
## Context
`ProcFlags` drive refusals and confirmations: `KERNEL_THREAD` and `PROTECTED` refuse or confirm actions, `IS_SELF` refuses "end tasklens itself", `OTHER_USER` asks for confirmation. The protected set is fixed by ADR-006 and PROC-059. This bead computes the flags for every record each sweep from cheap inputs; the two inputs that need sockets or D-Bus are passed in. Sources: PROC-059 (flag side), ADR-006 "Protected processes", ADR-003 `ProcFlags`, R-036.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-collect/src/apps/classify.rs`:
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)] pub struct ProtectInputs { pub self_pids: SmallVec<[u32; 2]>, pub compositor_pid: Option<u32>, pub session_bus_pid: Option<u32> }`.
  - `self_pids`: tasklens's own pid (`getpid()`) and the `tl-gpu-probe` pid when running; filled by the engine.
  - `compositor_pid`: from `pub fn wayland_compositor_pid(runtime_dir: &Path, display: &OsStr) -> Option<u32>` in this file: connects a `SOCK_STREAM` Unix socket to `<XDG_RUNTIME_DIR>/<WAYLAND_DISPLAY>` (`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` default `wayland-0` when unset; an absolute `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is used as the path), reads `SO_PEERCRED` with `rustix::net::sockopt::socket_peercred`, closes the socket, returns the pid. The engine calls it once at start and again when the stored pid exits.
  - `session_bus_pid`: from `org.freedesktop.DBus.GetConnectionUnixProcessID("org.freedesktop.DBus")`, done by the engine (E10) because `tl-collect` has no D-Bus; `None` until known.
- `pub struct ProtectedSet { pids: FxHashSet<u32> }` and `pub fn protected_set(records: &[(u32 /*pid*/, u32 /*ppid*/, &str /*exe basename or comm*/, Option<&CgroupPath>, u32 /*ruid*/)], self_uid: u32, inp: &ProtectInputs) -> ProtectedSet` that includes:
  1. PID 1;
  2. `compositor_pid` (the session's `kwin_wayland`);
  3. processes of `self_uid` whose exe basename is `plasmashell`, `ksmserver` or `Xwayland`;
  4. `session_bus_pid` (the user's `dbus-broker` or `dbus-daemon`) when it is `Some`;
  5. the user's `systemd --user`: the process whose cgroup is `user.slice/user-<self_uid>.slice/user@<self_uid>.service/init.scope` and whose exe basename is `systemd`;
  6. `sddm`, `login` and `systemd-logind`: walk the ppid chain from `compositor_pid` (or, when `None`, from each `plasmashell`) up to PID 1 and add every ancestor whose exe basename or comm is `sddm` or `login`; add the process in `system.slice/systemd-logind.service`;
  7. every pid in `self_pids`.
- `pub fn flags_for(pid: u32, kernel_thread: bool, ruid: u32, self_uid: u32, set: &ProtectedSet, inp: &ProtectInputs) -> ProcFlags`: `KERNEL_THREAD` when `kernel_thread`; `OTHER_USER` when `ruid != self_uid`; `IS_SELF` when `pid` is in `self_pids`; `PROTECTED` when `pid` is in the set. `NEW` and `EXITED` are the reducer's (E09) and are never set here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** records for PID 1, `kwin_wayland` (pid 900, the compositor pid input), `plasmashell` (901), `ksmserver` (902), `Xwayland` (903), `systemd` in `user@1000.service/init.scope` (800), `dbus-broker` (810, the bus pid input), `sddm` (500, ancestor of 900), `systemd-logind` (450 in `system.slice/systemd-logind.service`), `bash` (2000) and tasklens (3000 in `self_pids`) **When** `protected_set` runs with `self_uid = 1000` **Then** every pid except 2000 is in the set.
- **Given** a `plasmashell` owned by uid 1001 **When** `protected_set` runs with `self_uid = 1000` **Then** it is not in the set (only the current user's session).
- **Given** pid 3000 in `self_pids` **When** `flags_for` runs **Then** the flags contain `IS_SELF` and `PROTECTED`.
- **Given** a kernel thread of uid 0 **When** `flags_for` runs **Then** the flags contain `KERNEL_THREAD` and `OTHER_USER`.
- **Given** a Unix socket server in a temp dir bound by the test process **When** `wayland_compositor_pid(tmp, "sock")` runs **Then** it returns the test process's pid.
- **Given** no socket at the path **When** `wayland_compositor_pid` runs **Then** it returns `None`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/apps/classify.rs`: change, add flags and the protected set.
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixture_apps.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
- `tests/fixture_apps.rs::protected_set_full_session`.
- `tests/fixture_apps.rs::protected_set_other_uid_excluded`.
- `tests/fixture_apps.rs::flags_self_and_protected`: security regression (tasklens must never lose `IS_SELF`).
- `tests/fixture_apps.rs::flags_kernel_thread_other_user`.
- `tests/fixture_apps.rs::compositor_pid_via_peercred`.
- `tests/fixture_apps.rs::compositor_pid_missing_socket`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A (missing inputs give smaller sets, never a panic).
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: the set is rebuilt once per sweep from the records (one pass plus at most one ppid walk of depth under 10).
- Privacy: N/A.

## Notes
- The refusal toasts ("Refusing to end tasklens itself.", "PID 1 (systemd) cannot be ended.", "Kernel threads cannot be signalled.") are UI strings owned by E22; this bead only sets flags.
- The engine (E10) must pass `self_pids` and `session_bus_pid`; until then `IS_SELF` is missing for the probe and the bus daemon is not protected.
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-collect`). Run `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p tl-collect --all-targets -- -D warnings` the same way before committing. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit with a pathspec of only this bead's files: `git commit -m "..." -- <files>` (run `git add` on new files first). Never switch branch, reset, rebase or amend.
- `tl-collect` has no async code and no runtime (ADR-001 rule 3). Allowed dependencies: tl-model, rustix (workspace features fs, process, net, event, system, thread, time, pipe), memchr, thiserror, tracing, smallvec, rustc-hash, sha2, md-5, the netlink crates. No `unsafe`: only `tl-ops/src/sys.rs`, `tl-engine/src/gpu/spawn.rs` and `tl-app/src/main.rs` may hold it. No `procfs` crate (ADR-016). Dev-dependencies (insta 1.48.0, proptest 1.11.0, tempfile 3.27.0, criterion 0.8.2) come from `[workspace.dependencies]`.
- Never log command lines, environment, working directories, open file paths, executable paths of other users' processes or user names other than the current user, at any level (ADR-015). Processes are logged as `pid` plus `comm`, and `comm` only at `debug` or below. No logging above `trace` inside the per-process loop.

title: E05-018 Process display naming and search text
description:
## Context
Every process row needs a display name (`ProcessMeta.name`) and an image name. PROC-007 fixes the rules: app name for app primaries, else exe basename, else the first cmdline token, else `comm`; Wine uses the `.exe` name; kernel threads show `[comm]`; a renamed thread gets a qualifier. Sources: PROC-007, PROC-027 (Name, Image name), ADR-003 `ProcessMeta.name`, ADR-015 (sanitized input).

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/apps/naming.rs`:
- `pub const WINE_LOADERS: &[&str] = &["wine64-preloader", "wine-preloader", "wine64", "wine"];`
- `pub fn exe_basename(exe: &str) -> &str`: the part after the last `/`, with a trailing ` (deleted)` removed.
- `pub fn is_wine(exe_base: Option<&str>, comm: &str) -> bool`: exe basename in `WINE_LOADERS`, or `comm` ends with `.exe` (case-insensitive).
- `pub fn wine_exe_name(argv: &[Arc<str>]) -> Option<&str>`: the first argv token that ends with `.exe` (case-insensitive), cut to its last segment splitting on both `/` and `\` (`C:\Games\game.exe` gives `game.exe`).
- `pub fn image_name<'a>(exe: Option<&'a str>, argv: &'a [Arc<str>], comm: &'a str, wine: bool) -> Option<&'a str>`: Wine → `wine_exe_name`; else `exe_basename(exe)`; `None` when exe is unreadable (the column shows Restricted).
- `pub fn display_name(inp: &NameInput<'_>, out: &mut String)` with `pub struct NameInput<'a> { pub app_name: Option<&'a str>, pub is_app_primary: bool, pub exe: Option<&'a str>, pub argv: &'a [Arc<str>], pub comm: &'a str, pub kernel_thread: bool }`:
  1. `kernel_thread` → `[comm]` (for example `[kworker/0:1]`);
  2. `is_app_primary` and `app_name` → the app name;
  3. Wine (`is_wine`) and `wine_exe_name` is `Some` → that name;
  4. base = exe basename; if exe is `None`, the first argv token with one trailing `:` removed (for example `sshd:` gives `sshd`); if that is empty, `comm`;
  5. if `comm` differs from base and base does not start with `comm` (the kernel cuts `comm` to 15 bytes, so `comm` `Web Content` vs base `firefox` qualifies, while `comm` `chromium-browse` vs base `chromium-browser` does not), the result is `<base> (<comm>)`, for example `firefox (Web Content)`; else base.
- `pub fn search_lower(parts: &[&str], out: &mut String)`: lowercase join with a single space of the non-empty parts, in this order: display name, image name, command line, user, description, app name, unit name (R-043); used for `ProcessMeta.search_lower`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a kernel thread with comm `kworker/0:1` **When** `display_name` runs **Then** the result is `[kworker/0:1]`.
- **Given** an app primary with app name `Firefox` **When** `display_name` runs **Then** the result is `Firefox`.
- **Given** exe `/usr/lib/firefox/firefox`, comm `Web Content`, not an app primary **When** `display_name` runs **Then** the result is `firefox (Web Content)`.
- **Given** exe `/usr/bin/chromium-browser` and comm `chromium-browse` **When** `display_name` runs **Then** the result is `chromium-browser`.
- **Given** exe `/usr/bin/wine64-preloader` and argv `["C:\\Games\\Foo\\game.exe"]` **When** `display_name` and `image_name` run **Then** both give `game.exe`.
- **Given** exe `None` (restricted), argv `["sshd:", "user@pts/0"]` **When** `display_name` runs **Then** the result is `sshd`.
- **Given** exe `None`, empty argv, comm `foo` **When** `display_name` runs **Then** the result is `foo`.
- **Given** exe `/usr/bin/foo (deleted)` **When** `exe_basename` runs **Then** it returns `foo`.
- **Given** parts `["Firefox", "firefox", "/usr/lib/firefox/firefox -P", "alice", "", "Firefox", "app-firefox@1.service"]` **When** `search_lower` runs **Then** the result is `firefox firefox /usr/lib/firefox/firefox -p alice firefox app-firefox@1.service`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/apps/naming.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixture_apps.rs`: add tests.

## Tests

- `tests/fixture_apps.rs::name_app_primary_uses_app_name`.
- `tests/fixture_apps.rs::name_comm_qualifier`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: N/A.
- Validity: `image_name` returns `None` for a restricted exe; the sweep marks Image name and Image path `Restricted`.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: runs when metadata is new or refreshed; writes into caller buffers.
- Privacy: inputs are already sanitized (E05-002); nothing is logged.

## Notes

- Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-collect`). title: E05-019 Icon theme resolution
description:
## Context
App rows draw a 24 px icon and process rows 16 px (times the UI scale). The icon name comes from the desktop entry's `Icon=`; the file comes from the icon theme: the theme in `~/.config/kdeglobals` `[Icons] Theme=`, then `breeze`, then `hicolor`, sizes 16, 22, 24, 32, then `scalable`, preferring SVG. Absolute `Icon=` paths are used directly. Sources: PROC-006, ADR-016 "Icons", ADR-003 `ProcessMeta.icon`.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/apps/icons.rs`:
- `pub const SIZES: [u32; 4] = [16, 22, 24, 32];`
- `pub fn kde_icon_theme(kdeglobals: &[u8]) -> Option<String>`: reads the `[Icons]` group's `Theme=` value (INI, `#` comments, whitespace trimmed).
- `pub fn theme_order(user_theme: Option<&str>) -> SmallVec<[String; 3]>`: `[user_theme, "breeze", "hicolor"]` without duplicates.
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct ThemeDirs { pub theme: String, pub base_dirs: Vec<PathBuf>, pub dirs: Vec<ThemeDir> }` with `pub struct ThemeDir { pub rel: String, pub size: u32, pub scale: u32, pub scalable: bool }`, loaded by `pub fn load_theme(name: &str, icon_bases: &[PathBuf]) -> Option<ThemeDirs>`: finds `<base>/<name>/index.theme` in `icon_bases` (caller passes `~/.local/share/icons`, then each `$XDG_DATA_DIRS/icons`); parses `[Icon Theme] Directories=` (comma list) and each directory group's `Size=`, `Scale=` (default 1) and `Type=` (`Scalable` sets `scalable`). `Inherits=` is not followed (the fixed order above replaces it).
- `pub fn resolve(icon: &str, size: u32, themes: &[ThemeDirs]) -> Option<Arc<str>>`:
  1. `icon` starting with `/`: returned when the file exists;
  2. for each theme in order: for each preferred size, in order `size`, then the other entries of `SIZES` ascending, then `scalable` dirs: look in every directory with that size and `scale == 1` (or `scalable`), in every base, for `<icon>.svg`, then `<icon>.png`; first existing file wins;
  3. `None` when nothing is found.
- `pub fn generic_icon(kind: GenericIcon) -> &'static str` with `pub enum GenericIcon { Executable, KernelThread, Service }`: the theme icon names `application-x-executable`, `cpu`, `preferences-system-services` resolved through `resolve` by the caller (PROC-006 "generic executable icon", "chip icon"; PROC-009 "service icon").

Fixture `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/apps-icons/` with `home/.config/kdeglobals` (`[Icons]` `Theme=breeze-dark`), `usr/share/icons/breeze-dark/index.theme` (directories `apps/16`, `apps/22`, `apps/scalable`), `usr/share/icons/breeze/index.theme`, `usr/share/icons/hicolor/index.theme` (`16x16/apps`, `24x24/apps`, `scalable/apps`) and empty icon files: `breeze-dark/apps/22/firefox.svg`, `hicolor/24x24/apps/konsole.png`, `hicolor/scalable/apps/konsole.svg`, `hicolor/16x16/apps/only16.png`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the fixture kdeglobals **When** `kde_icon_theme` runs **Then** it returns `breeze-dark`.
- **Given** icon `firefox` and size 22 **When** `resolve` runs **Then** it returns the `breeze-dark/apps/22/firefox.svg` path.
- **Given** icon `konsole` and size 24 **When** `resolve` runs **Then** it returns `hicolor/24x24/apps/konsole.png` (size match beats a scalable SVG in a later step).
- **Given** icon `konsole` and size 32 (no 32 dir anywhere) **When** `resolve` runs **Then** it returns `hicolor/24x24/apps/konsole.png` (other sizes ascending come before scalable: 16, 22, 24).
- **Given** icon `only16` and size 24 **When** `resolve` runs **Then** it returns the 16 px file.
- **Given** an absolute `Icon=/opt/app/icon.png` that exists **When** `resolve` runs **Then** it returns that path; when it does not exist, `None`.
- **Given** an unknown icon name **When** `resolve` runs **Then** it returns `None`.

title: E05-020 Icon path cache in icons.toml
description:
## Context
Icon resolution touches many files, so resolved paths are cached in `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/tasklens/icons.toml` (ADR-016, ADR-011 paths table). `tl-collect` has no `toml` or `serde` dependency (ADR-001), so the file is a small hand-written TOML subset. The path itself is resolved by `tl-app/src/paths.rs` (E33) and passed in. Sources: ADR-016 "Icons", ADR-011 "Paths", PROC-006.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-collect/src/apps/icons.rs`:
- File format (a valid TOML subset), written and read only by this module:
  ```toml
  version = 1
  theme = "breeze-dark"
  [paths]
  "firefox@24" = "/usr/share/icons/breeze-dark/apps/22/firefox.svg"
  "konsole@16" = ""
  ```
  Keys are `"<icon name>@<size>"`; an empty value records "not found". Strings escape `\` as `\\` and `"` as `\"`; any other control character in a name or path drops that entry when writing.
- `pub struct IconCache { path: PathBuf, theme: String, map: FxHashMap<(Arc<str>, u32), Option<Arc<str>>>, dirty: bool }` with:
  - `pub fn load(path: PathBuf, theme: &str) -> Self`: reads the file if present; a `version` other than 1, a `theme` different from `theme`, or any parse error discards the contents (start empty, `dirty = true`);
  - `pub fn lookup(&mut self, icon: &str, size: u32, themes: &[ThemeDirs]) -> Option<Arc<str>>`: a cached path that no longer exists, or a miss, calls `resolve` (E05-019) and stores the result (`dirty = true`);
  - `pub fn save(&mut self) -> Result<(), CollectError>`: when `dirty`, creates the parent directory with mode `0700` if missing, writes `icons.toml.tmp-<pid>` with mode `0600` in the same directory, `fsync`s it, `rename`s it over `icons.toml`, `fsync`s the directory (the ADR-011 atomic write steps, written here because `tl-collect` cannot depend on `tl-ops`); clears `dirty`. Entries are written sorted by key so the file is stable.
- The engine calls `save` at most once per 60 s and at shutdown (`pub const ICON_CACHE_SAVE_INTERVAL_S: u64 = 60;`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** an empty temp cache path **When** `lookup("firefox", 24, ..)` and `save` run **Then** the file contains `version = 1`, `theme = "breeze-dark"` and `"firefox@24" = "<path>"`, with mode 0600.
- **Given** that file **When** `load` runs with theme `breeze-dark` and `lookup("firefox", 24, ..)` is called with an empty theme list **Then** it returns the cached path without calling `resolve`.
- **Given** that file **When** `load` runs with theme `breeze` **Then** the map is empty.
- **Given** a cached path whose file was deleted **When** `lookup` runs **Then** it resolves again.
- **Given** a corrupt file (`[paths` without the bracket) **When** `load` runs **Then** the cache starts empty and no error is returned.
- **Given** an icon name containing `"` **When** saved and loaded **Then** the entry round-trips.
- **Given** a cached "not found" (empty value) **When** `lookup` runs **Then** it returns `None` without resolving.
- **Given** no changes since the last save **When** `save` runs **Then** no file is written (mtime unchanged).

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/apps/icons.rs`: change, add the cache.
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixture_apps.rs`, `crates/tl-collect/tests/prop_process.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
- `tests/fixture_apps.rs::icon_cache_write_and_mode`.
- `tests/fixture_apps.rs::icon_cache_hit_skips_resolve`.
- `tests/fixture_apps.rs::icon_cache_theme_change_discards`.
- `tests/fixture_apps.rs::icon_cache_stale_path_reresolved`.
- `tests/fixture_apps.rs::icon_cache_corrupt_starts_empty`.
- `tests/fixture_apps.rs::icon_cache_quote_roundtrip`.
- `tests/fixture_apps.rs::icon_cache_negative_entry`.
- `tests/fixture_apps.rs::icon_cache_no_write_when_clean`.
- `tests/prop_process.rs::icon_cache_parser_arbitrary_bytes_never_panic`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `save` returns `CollectError::ProcRead { file: "icons.toml", errno }` on I/O failure; the engine logs it once at `warn` without the path.
- Validity: N/A.

title: E05-021 PSS and USS from smaps_rollup with the FD cache
description:
## Context
PSS and USS come from `/proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup`, which is expensive, so they are read only for `Demand.detail_keys` (visible rows plus one viewport of overscan, at most 512), at most once per second, and only while a PSS or USS column is shown. The `smaps_rollup` fds are kept in the 128-entry FD cache from E04-A1 (`fdcache.rs`); an entry is dropped when its key leaves demand or the identity check fails. `ProcessSnapshot.coverage` lists which keys have PSS and USS. Sources: PROC-002, PROC-030, ADR-008 schedule row "PSS/USS", ADR-016 "File descriptor policy", ADR-003 `Coverage`.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/proc/smaps.rs` (rollup part):
- `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)] pub struct Rollup { pub pss: u64, pub uss: u64, pub swap: u64 }` in bytes: `pss` from `Pss:`, `uss = Private_Clean + Private_Dirty`, `swap` from `Swap:` (all kB × 1024).
- `pub fn parse_rollup(buf: &[u8], out: &mut Rollup) -> Result<(), CollectError>`; a buffer without `Pss:` gives `ProcParse { pid: 0, file: "smaps_rollup" }`.
- `pub enum RollupRead { Ok(Rollup), Restricted, Gone }`.
- `pub struct PssReader { cache: FdCache }` (the E04-A1 type, capacity 128) with
  `pub fn read(&mut self, root: &SysRoot, keys: &[ProcessKey], buf: &mut Vec<u8>, out: &mut Vec<(ProcessKey, RollupRead)>)`:
  1. for each key (at most 512, the slice is already capped by the demand): take the cached fd for the key, or open `<proc>/<pid>/smaps_rollup` with `O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC` after checking identity with `read_start_ticks` (E05-003) equals `key.start_ticks`; a mismatch gives `Gone` and drops the cache entry;
  2. `pread` at offset 0 into `buf` and parse;
  3. `EACCES` or `EPERM` gives `Restricted` (other users' processes; the helper path is E29's); `ESRCH`, `ENOENT` or a read of 0 bytes gives `Gone` and drops the entry;
  4. drop cache entries whose key is not in `keys` (left demand);
  5. when the cache is full, open without caching (no eviction storm; fds for the first 128 keys stay cached).
- `pub fn apply_rollups(records: &mut [ProcessRecord], results: &[(ProcessKey, RollupRead)], coverage: &mut CoverageBuilder)`: sets `pss_bytes`, `uss_bytes` and validity `Pss`/`Uss` to `Valid`, or `Restricted`, and records the covered keys. `CoverageBuilder` builds the `tl_model::process::Coverage` value as E03-A1 defines it (a sorted key list of the keys that have PSS and USS).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fixture `smaps_rollup` with `Pss: 2048 kB`, `Private_Clean: 512 kB`, `Private_Dirty: 1024 kB`, `Swap: 0 kB` **When** parsed **Then** `pss == 2_097_152`, `uss == 1_572_864`.
- **Given** the test process's own key **When** `PssReader::read` runs twice **Then** the second call reuses the cached fd (cache length 1, no second `open`, checked with the cache's test counter).
- **Given** a key with a wrong `start_ticks` for a live pid **When** read **Then** the result is `Gone` and nothing is cached.
- **Given** PID 1 as uid 1000 (real-system) **When** read **Then** the result is `Restricted`.
- **Given** 130 keys **When** read **Then** 128 fds are cached and the last two are read without caching.
- **Given** a key that left `keys` **When** `read` runs **Then** its cache entry is closed.
- **Given** results for 3 keys **When** `apply_rollups` runs **Then** those 3 records have `Valid` PSS and USS and the coverage lists exactly those keys; every other record keeps `WarmingUp`.

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/proc/smaps.rs`: create (rollup part).
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/process-edge/proc/4201/smaps_rollup`: create.
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixture_process.rs`, `crates/tl-collect/tests/real_restricted.rs`, `crates/tl-collect/tests/prop_process.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::rollup_parse_bytes`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::rollup_fd_cached_and_reused`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::rollup_identity_mismatch_gone` (security regression: a reused pid never yields another process's PSS).
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::rollup_cache_cap_128`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::rollup_drop_left_demand`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::rollup_apply_and_coverage`.
- `tests/real_restricted.rs::rollup_pid1_restricted` (`#[ignore]`).
- `tests/prop_process.rs::rollup_arbitrary_bytes_never_panic`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `ProcParse { file: "smaps_rollup" }` maps to validity `Failed` for that key.
- Validity: `Valid`, `Restricted`, `WarmingUp` (not yet covered), `Failed`.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: at most 512 `pread`s per second while a PSS or USS column is shown; `smaps_rollup` of a large process costs about 1 ms, which is why coverage is limited.
- Privacy: N/A.

title: E05-025 Threads reader in proc/detail.rs
description:
## Context
The Threads tab lists every thread with its name, state, CPU, times, priority, affinity, last CPU, context switches and wait channel, from `/proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/`. This bead creates `proc/detail.rs` with the threads reader; later beads add the other tabs to the same file in sequence. Sources: PROC-079, UI-PWN `ThreadRow` data binding (`docs/ui/process-windows.md` line "ThreadRow { tid, comm, state, cpu_pct, utime_ms, stime_ms, policy, rt_prio, nice, cpus, last_cpu, vol_ctx, invol_ctx, wchan, validity }").

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/proc/detail.rs` (threads part):
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct ThreadInfo { pub tid: u32, pub comm: Arc<str>, pub state: u8, pub cpu_pct: f32, pub utime_ms: u64, pub stime_ms: u64, pub policy: u32, pub rt_prio: u32, pub nice: i8, pub cpus: Arc<str>, pub last_cpu: i32, pub vol_ctx: Option<u64>, pub invol_ctx: Option<u64>, pub wchan: WchanValue, pub cpu_validity: Validity }` with `pub enum WchanValue { Name(Arc<str>), Running /* "0" */, Restricted }`. The engine (E10) maps it to the `tl-model` `ThreadRow`.
- `pub struct ThreadReader { prev: FxHashMap<(ProcessKey, u32), (TimeNs, u64)> }` with
  `pub fn read(&mut self, root: &SysRoot, key: ProcessKey, ticks_per_sec: u64, online_cpus: u32, bufs: &mut ReadBufs, out: &mut Vec<ThreadInfo>) -> Result<DetailRead, CollectError>` where `pub enum DetailRead { Ok, Restricted, Gone }`:
  1. opens `/proc/<pid>` as a dirfd and checks `read_start_ticks == key.start_ticks` (else `Gone`);
  2. lists `task/`; for each tid reads `task/<tid>/stat` (E05-003 parser: comm, state, utime, stime, nice, policy, rt_priority, processor), `task/<tid>/status` (`Cpus_allowed_list`, `voluntary_ctxt_switches`, `nonvoluntary_ctxt_switches`), `task/<tid>/wchan` (EACCES gives `Restricted`; content `0` gives `Running`), sanitizes `comm` with `sanitize_comm`;
  3. `utime_ms = utime × 1000 / ticks_per_sec`, same for `stime_ms`; `cpu_pct = 100 × Δ(utime + stime) / ticks_per_sec / Δt / online_cpus` against `prev` (first read `WarmingUp`, ADR-008 rules);
  4. a tid that disappears mid-list is skipped; `prev` entries of vanished tids are dropped.
- `pub fn thread_exists(pid_dir: BorrowedFd<'_>, tid: u32) -> bool`: `statat(pid_dir, "task/<tid>")` succeeds (used by the thread target check, R-097, in the engine).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fixture `/proc/4201/task/{4201,4211}/{stat,status,wchan}` **When** read twice with 1 s between and 10 ticks of growth on 4211 **Then** 2 rows; 4211 has `cpu_pct` from the formula and `cpu_validity == Valid`; the first read gave `WarmingUp`.
- **Given** a `wchan` of `0` **When** read **Then** `wchan == Running`; a `wchan` of `do_epoll_wait` gives `Name("do_epoll_wait")`.
- **Given** a fixture `wchan` with mode 0000 (non-root run) **When** read **Then** `wchan == Restricted` and the row is still present.
- **Given** a key whose `start_ticks` does not match **When** read **Then** `DetailRead::Gone` and `out` is empty.
- **Given** the test process spawning 2 extra threads **When** read on `/proc` **Then** at least 3 rows and `thread_exists(self, main_tid)` is true; `thread_exists(self, 999_999_999)` is false.

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/proc/detail.rs`: create (threads part).
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/process-edge/proc/4201/task/{4201,4211}/{stat,status,wchan}`: create.
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixture_process.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::threads_rows_and_cpu`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::threads_wchan_values`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::threads_wchan_restricted`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::threads_identity_mismatch_gone` (security regression).
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::threads_live_self`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: per-file failures map to row fields; directory failures to `DetailRead`.
- Validity: `WarmingUp` then `Valid` for CPU; `Restricted` wchan.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: only while a Threads tab is open, at `processes.interval_ms`; buffers reused.

## Notes

- Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-collect`). Run `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p tl-collect --all-targets -- -D warnings` the same way before committing. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

Processes are logged as `pid` plus `comm`, and `comm` only at `debug` or below. No logging above `trace` inside the per-process loop.

title: E05-026 File descriptor and fdinfo reader
description:
## Context
The File descriptors tab lists every fd with its type, target name, access flags and position, plus a details pane with the raw flags, mount id and inode, from `/proc/<pid>/fd/*` and `/proc/<pid>/fdinfo/<fd>`. Socket names need the sock_diag inode map (E06) and pipe peers need a cross-process inode search (E05-031); this reader returns the inodes so the engine can resolve them. Sources: PROC-080, UI-PWN fds data binding and type words (`docs/ui/process-windows.md`).

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-collect/src/proc/detail.rs`:
- `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum FdType { File, Directory, Tcp, Udp, Unix, Netlink, Pipe, Fifo, EventFd, EventPoll, TimerFd, SignalFd, Inotify, Fanotify, MemFd, DmaBuf, Drm, PidFd, IoUring, AnonInode, Device, Socket }` with `pub fn label(self) -> &'static str` giving `file`, `directory`, `TCP`, `UDP`, `unix`, `netlink`, `pipe`, `FIFO`, `eventfd`, `eventpoll`, `timerfd`, `signalfd`, `inotify`, `fanotify`, `memfd`, `dmabuf`, `DRM`, `pidfd`, `io_uring`, `anon_inode`, `device`, and `socket` for a socket not yet resolved to TCP, UDP, unix or netlink (the engine refines it with the E06 map).
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct FdInfo { pub fd: u32, pub kind: FdType, pub target: Arc<str>, pub inode: Option<u64>, pub flags: Option<u32>, pub pos: Option<u64>, pub mnt_id: Option<u32>, pub eventfd_count: Option<u64>, pub drm_client_id: Option<u64>, pub drm_driver: Option<Arc<str>>, pub fdinfo_ok: bool }`.
- Classification of the `readlinkat(fd/<n>)` target (sanitized with `sanitize_link`):
  - `socket:[<ino>]` → `Socket` with `inode`;
  - `pipe:[<ino>]` → `Pipe` with `inode`;
  - `anon_inode:[eventfd]` → `EventFd`; `anon_inode:[eventpoll]` → `EventPoll`; `anon_inode:[timerfd]` → `TimerFd`; `anon_inode:[signalfd]` → `SignalFd`; `anon_inode:inotify` → `Inotify`; `anon_inode:[fanotify]` → `Fanotify`; `anon_inode:[pidfd]` → `PidFd`; `anon_inode:[io_uring]` → `IoUring`; `anon_inode:[dmabuf]` or `/dmabuf:` → `DmaBuf`; other `anon_inode:` → `AnonInode`;
  - `/memfd:` prefix → `MemFd`;
  - `/dev/dri/` prefix → `Drm`;
  - other paths: `statat` with `AT_SYMLINK_FOLLOW` on `fd/<n>`: directory → `Directory`, FIFO → `Fifo`, character or block device → `Device`, else `File`; a failed stat gives `File`.
- fdinfo: `fdinfo/<n>` lines `pos:` (decimal), `flags:` (octal, for example `02104002`), `mnt_id:`, `ino:`, `eventfd-count:` (hex), `drm-client-id:`, `drm-driver:`; `fdinfo_ok = false` when it cannot be read (the pane shows "Handle detail query unavailable.").
- `pub fn read_fds(root: &SysRoot, key: ProcessKey, bufs: &mut ReadBufs, out: &mut Vec<FdInfo>) -> Result<DetailRead, CollectError>`: identity check as E05-025; EACCES on `fd/` gives `Restricted` (the tab shows "Handles unavailable (insufficient privileges)"); entries sorted by fd ascending.
- `pub fn decode_flags(flags: u32) -> FlagWords` with `pub struct FlagWords { pub access: &'static str, pub status: SmallVec<[&'static str; 6]>, pub cloexec: bool }`: access `O_ACCMODE` 0 "Read only", 1 "Write only", 2 "Read/write", and `O_PATH` (0o10000000) "Path only"; status words in this order: `O_APPEND` (0o2000) "Append", `O_NONBLOCK` (0o4000) "Non-blocking", `O_SYNC` (0o4010000) "Sync", `O_DIRECT` (0o40000) "Direct", `O_PATH` "Path", `O_TMPFILE` (0o20200000) "Temp file"; `O_CLOEXEC` (0o2000000) sets `cloexec`; `O_LARGEFILE` (0o100000) is ignored.
- `pub fn access_text(flags: u32, out: &mut String)`: `R`, `W` or `RW`, then ` +A` for append, ` +NB` for non-blocking, ` CLOEXEC` for close-on-exec (for example `RW +NB CLOEXEC`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** flags `0o2104002` **When** `decode_flags` runs **Then** access "Read/write", status `["Non-blocking"]`, `cloexec == true` (the large-file bit is not shown).
- **Given** flags `0o2104002` **When** `access_text` runs **Then** the text is `RW +NB CLOEXEC`.
- **Given** a fixture fd dir with links `socket:[1234]`, `pipe:[99]`, `anon_inode:[eventfd]`, `/memfd:wayland-shm (deleted)`, `/dev/dri/card1`, `/home/user1/file.txt` **When** `read_fds` runs **Then** the kinds are `Socket` (inode 1234), `Pipe` (inode 99), `EventFd`, `MemFd`, `Drm`, `File`.
- **Given** fixture fdinfo with `pos: 42` and `flags: 02100000` **When** read **Then** `pos == Some(42)`, `flags == Some(0o2100000)`, `fdinfo_ok == true`.
- **Given** an fd whose fdinfo file is missing **When** read **Then** the row exists with `fdinfo_ok == false`.
- **Given** PID 1 as uid 1000 (real-system) **When** `read_fds` runs **Then** `DetailRead::Restricted`.
- **Given** the test process with an open `TcpListener` **When** `read_fds` runs on `/proc/self` **Then** one row is `Socket` with an inode.

## Files

title: E05-A3 Detail readers
description:
## Context
Anchor E05-A3 "Detail readers". It delivers `hash.rs` (streamed SHA-256 and MD5 of a process's executable, cached by (dev, inode, mtime)) and closes the detail-reader set (`proc/smaps.rs`, `proc/detail.rs`, `proc/strings.rs`, `proc/handles.rs`), so the engine's `ProcessDetail` and handle-search workers (E10) can depend on one bead. Hashes serve Open in VirusTotal (PROC-074) and the General tab (PROC-078, UI-PWN-008); the two share one computation. Sources: PROC-074, PROC-078, R-096, ADR-001 (`sha2`, `md-5`), UI-PWN `HashState { Pending, Done { sha256: [u8; 32], md5: [u8; 16] }, Failed(HashError) }`.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/hash.rs`:
- `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct Hashes { pub sha256: [u8; 32], pub md5: [u8; 16] }`.
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum HashError { ExeUnavailable, Read { errno: i32 } }` with `pub fn message(&self) -> &'static str`: `ExeUnavailable` → "Executable path unavailable" (General tab) and `Read` → "Failed to compute one or more hashes". The VirusTotal flow maps `ExeUnavailable` to "Process image unavailable" and `Read` to "SHA-256 unavailable" in the UI (PROC-074); this file does not hold those strings.
- `pub const HASH_BUF: usize = 64 * 1024;` (read size per `read` call).
- `pub fn hash_fd(fd: BorrowedFd<'_>, buf: &mut Vec<u8>) -> Result<Hashes, HashError>`: reads the file from offset 0 to EOF in `HASH_BUF` chunks, updating `sha2::Sha256` and `md5::Md5` (crate `md-5`) together; one pass.
- `pub struct HashCache { map: FxHashMap<(u64, u64, i64, u32), Hashes>, order: VecDeque<(u64, u64, i64, u32)> }` keyed by (dev, inode, mtime seconds, mtime nanoseconds), at most 256 entries (oldest inserted is dropped first).
- `pub fn hash_process_exe(root: &SysRoot, key: ProcessKey, argv0: Option<&str>, cache: &mut HashCache, buf: &mut Vec<u8>) -> Result<Hashes, HashError>`:
  1. open `<proc>/<pid>/exe` with `O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC` (works for deleted files) after checking `read_start_ticks == key.start_ticks` (else `ExeUnavailable`);
  2. on EACCES or EPERM, fall back to `argv0` when it is an absolute path and opens for reading; else `ExeUnavailable`;
  3. `fstat` the opened file; a cache hit for (dev, inode, mtime) returns at once; else `hash_fd` and insert.
- Closing the set: this bead also adds `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixture_process.rs::detail_readers_on_self`, which runs every detail reader once on the test process (`/proc/self` through a key built from its own stat): threads, fds, maps with RSS, security, environ, cwd and root, ELF of its exe, a 1-chunk string scan through `VecMem`, a handle walk step, and `hash_process_exe`; each returns `Ok` (or `DetailRead::Ok`) with non-empty output.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a temp file containing `abc` **When** `hash_fd` runs **Then** SHA-256 is `ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad` and MD5 is `900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72`.
- **Given** an empty file **When** hashed **Then** SHA-256 `e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855`, MD5 `d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e`.
- **Given** the test process's own key **When** `hash_process_exe` runs twice **Then** the second call is a cache hit (no file read, checked with a read counter) and both results are equal.
- **Given** a key with a wrong `start_ticks` **When** called **Then** `Err(ExeUnavailable)`.
- **Given** PID 1 as uid 1000 and `argv0 = Some("/usr/lib/systemd/systemd")` (real-system) **When** called **Then** it hashes the argv path (readable) and returns `Ok`.
- **Given** PID 1 as uid 1000 and `argv0 = None` (real-system) **When** called **Then** `Err(ExeUnavailable)`.
- **Given** 257 distinct files hashed **When** the cache is inspected **Then** it holds 256 entries and the first file's entry is gone.
- **Given** the test process **When** `detail_readers_on_self` runs **Then** every reader succeeds.

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/hash.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixture_process.rs`, `crates/tl-collect/tests/real_restricted.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::hash_known_vectors`: `abc` and empty.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::hash_cache_hit`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::hash_identity_mismatch` (security regression: never hash another process's image after pid reuse).
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::hash_cache_cap_256`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::detail_readers_on_self`.

- `tests/real_restricted.rs::hash_pid1_no_argv_unavailable` (`#[ignore]`).

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `HashError` as above.
- Validity: N/A (the General tab shows "Unavailable" with the error tooltip).
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: streamed, 64 KiB buffer reused; a 200 MiB binary hashes in about 1 s on the blocking pool; the cache makes the VirusTotal lookup after Properties instant.
- Privacy: executable paths are not logged; hashes are not secret.

Dev-dependencies (insta 1.48.0, proptest 1.11.0, tempfile 3.27.0, criterion 0.8.2) come from `[workspace.dependencies]`.

title: E05-027 Memory maps reader and node grouping
description:
## Context
The Memory maps tab is a tree with one node per backing file and its regions as children, the main executable first and marked "(Primary)", anonymous regions grouped under "Outside loaded modules", and a "Shared libraries only" filter. This bead adds the `/proc/<pid>/maps` reader and the node grouping. Sources: PROC-081, UI-PWN `MapsDetail { nodes, regions }` data binding.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-collect/src/proc/detail.rs`:
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct MapRegionInfo { pub start: u64, pub end: u64, pub perms: [u8; 4], pub offset: u64, pub inode: u64, pub path: Option<Arc<str>>, pub rss: Option<u64> }`.
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct MapNodeInfo { pub name: Arc<str>, pub path: Option<Arc<str>>, pub primary: bool, pub outside: bool, pub shared_object: bool, pub base: u64, pub size: u64, pub rss: Option<u64>, pub perms: [u8; 4], pub offset: u64, pub regions: std::ops::Range<u32> }`.
- `pub fn parse_maps(buf: &[u8], out: &mut Vec<MapRegionInfo>) -> Result<(), CollectError>`: lines `<start>-<end> <perms> <offset> <dev> <inode> [path]`; the path is the rest of the line after the inode column with leading spaces removed (it may contain spaces); sanitized with `sanitize_link`.
- `pub fn group_maps(regions: &mut Vec<MapRegionInfo>, exe: Option<&str>, rss: Option<&FxHashMap<u64, u64>>, out: &mut Vec<MapNodeInfo>)`:
  - regions with a path that starts with `/` (file-backed) group by path; regions without a path, or with `[heap]`, `[stack]`, `[vdso]`, `[vvar]`, `[vsyscall]`, `[anon:...]` or a `/memfd:` path, group into one node named `Outside loaded modules` with `outside = true`;
  - `primary = true` for the node whose path equals the exe path (without ` (deleted)`), named `<basename> (Primary)`; primary first, then file nodes by lowest start, then the outside node last;
  - `base` = lowest start, `size` = Σ (end − start), `perms` and `offset` of the first region, `rss` = Σ of the region RSS from E05-024's `rss_by_start` when given, else `None`;
  - `shared_object = true` when the basename ends in `.so` or contains `.so.`, or (Wine) ends in `.dll`, `.exe`, `.drv` or `.sys` (case-insensitive) (filter "Shared libraries only", PROC-081);
  - `regions` is the index range of the node's regions after `regions` is reordered to node order.
- `pub fn read_maps(root: &SysRoot, key: ProcessKey, with_rss: bool, bufs: &mut ReadBufs, regions: &mut Vec<MapRegionInfo>, nodes: &mut Vec<MapNodeInfo>) -> Result<DetailRead, CollectError>`: identity check; reads `maps`; when `with_rss`, reads `smaps` (E05-024) for RSS; EACCES on `maps` gives `Restricted` (the tab shows "Needs administrator access.").

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** a fixture `maps` with the exe (2 regions), `libc.so.6` (3 regions), `[heap]`, `[stack]`, an anonymous region and `/memfd:x (deleted)` **When** read with exe `/usr/bin/foo` **Then** 3 nodes in order `foo (Primary)`, `libc.so.6`, `Outside loaded modules`, with sizes the sums of their regions.
- **Given** a path with spaces `/opt/My App/libx.so` **When** parsed **Then** the path is kept whole.

title: E05-028 Security tab reader: credentials, capabilities, namespaces
description:
## Context
The Security tab shows the process's credentials, capabilities, groups, flags, LSM label, session and namespaces. Most fields come from the world-readable `status`; `ns/*` of other users needs ptrace access and shows "Restricted" until the helper reads it. Capability names and descriptions come from a static table of `linux/capability.h`. Sources: PROC-082, PROC-028 (Elevated, Sandbox, Security label, Session columns), UI-PWN `SecurityDetail { caps, groups }` data binding.

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-collect/src/proc/detail.rs`:
- `pub const CAPS: [(&str, &str); 41]` indexed by capability number, names without the `CAP_` prefix in the table and shown with it by the UI:
  0 `CHOWN` "Change file owners", 1 `DAC_OVERRIDE` "Bypass file read, write and execute permission checks", 2 `DAC_READ_SEARCH` "Bypass file read and directory search checks", 3 `FOWNER` "Bypass checks that need the file owner", 4 `FSETID` "Keep set-user-ID and set-group-ID bits on modified files", 5 `KILL` "Send signals to any process", 6 `SETGID` "Change group IDs", 7 `SETUID` "Change user IDs", 8 `SETPCAP` "Change capability sets", 9 `LINUX_IMMUTABLE` "Set immutable and append-only file flags", 10 `NET_BIND_SERVICE` "Bind to ports below 1024", 11 `NET_BROADCAST` "Broadcast and listen to multicast", 12 `NET_ADMIN` "Configure network interfaces, routes and firewall", 13 `NET_RAW` "Use raw and packet sockets", 14 `IPC_LOCK` "Lock memory", 15 `IPC_OWNER` "Bypass IPC permission checks", 16 `SYS_MODULE` "Load and unload kernel modules", 17 `SYS_RAWIO` "Raw I/O port and device access", 18 `SYS_CHROOT` "Use chroot", 19 `SYS_PTRACE` "Trace and inspect any process", 20 `SYS_PACCT` "Configure process accounting", 21 `SYS_ADMIN` "Broad system administration", 22 `SYS_BOOT` "Reboot and load kernels", 23 `SYS_NICE` "Raise priority and set other processes' scheduling", 24 `SYS_RESOURCE` "Override resource limits", 25 `SYS_TIME` "Set the system clock", 26 `SYS_TTY_CONFIG` "Configure terminals", 27 `MKNOD` "Create device files", 28 `LEASE` "Take file leases", 29 `AUDIT_WRITE` "Write audit log records", 30 `AUDIT_CONTROL` "Configure kernel auditing", 31 `SETFCAP` "Set file capabilities", 32 `MAC_OVERRIDE` "Override mandatory access control", 33 `MAC_ADMIN` "Configure mandatory access control", 34 `SYSLOG` "Use privileged syslog operations", 35 `WAKE_ALARM` "Set alarms that wake the system", 36 `BLOCK_SUSPEND` "Block system suspend", 37 `AUDIT_READ` "Read the audit log", 38 `PERFMON` "Use performance monitoring", 39 `BPF` "Use BPF", 40 `CHECKPOINT_RESTORE` "Checkpoint and restore processes".
- `pub const RISKY_CAPS: [u8; 14] = [21, 19, 1, 2, 16, 17, 7, 6, 12, 39, 38, 22, 0, 3];` (SYS_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE, DAC_OVERRIDE, DAC_READ_SEARCH, SYS_MODULE, SYS_RAWIO, SETUID, SETGID, NET_ADMIN, BPF, PERFMON, SYS_BOOT, CHOWN, FOWNER), counted when effective or ambient.
- `pub const ADMIN_GROUPS: [(&str, bool); 8] = [("wheel", false), ("sudo", false), ("root", false), ("adm", false), ("docker", true), ("libvirt", true), ("lxd", true), ("disk", true)];` (the bool is "root-equivalent").
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct SecurityInfo { pub uid: [u32; 4], pub gid: [u32; 4], pub groups: SmallVec<[u32; 16]>, pub cap_inh: u64, pub cap_prm: u64, pub cap_eff: u64, pub cap_bnd: u64, pub cap_amb: u64, pub no_new_privs: Option<bool>, pub seccomp: Option<u8>, pub seccomp_filters: Option<u32>, pub dumpable: Option<bool>, pub lsm_label: LsmLabel, pub loginuid: Option<u32>, pub sessionid: Option<u32>, pub speculation_store_bypass: Arc<str>, pub speculation_indirect_branch: Arc<str>, pub elevated: Elevated, pub namespaces: [NsState; 8] }`:
  - `pub enum LsmLabel { Label(Arc<str>), NotApplicable, Restricted }`: `attr/current` sanitized; `NotApplicable` when `/sys/kernel/security/lsm` lists none of `apparmor`, `selinux`, `smack`, `tomoyo` (PROC-028);
  - `loginuid` and `sessionid`: `4294967295` becomes `None`;
  - `dumpable` (R-163 item 4, PROC-082 edit): `Some(false)` ("not dumpable") when `fstat` of the `/proc/<pid>` dirfd gives owner uid 0 while the real uid (`uid[0]`) is not 0; otherwise `None` (the UI shows "Not reported");
  - `pub enum Elevated { Root, Capabilities, Setuid, No }`, first match: euid 0 → `Root` ("Yes (root)"); `cap_eff != 0` for a non-root process → `Capabilities`; euid ≠ ruid → `Setuid`; else `No`;
  - `pub enum NsState { SharedWithInit, SameAsTasklens, Isolated(u64), Restricted }` for `user`, `pid`, `net`, `mnt`, `ipc`, `uts`, `cgroup`, `time` in that order: the inode from `readlinkat(ns/<name>)` (`<name>:[<ino>]`) compared with PID 1's same link; when PID 1's link is unreadable, compared with `/proc/self/ns/<name>` and equal gives `SameAsTasklens` ("Same as tasklens"); EACCES on the target's link gives `Restricted`.
- `pub fn group_name(gid: u32, group_file: &[u8]) -> Option<Arc<str>>`: looks up `/etc/group` (`name:x:gid:members` lines), sanitized.
- `pub fn read_security(root: &SysRoot, key: ProcessKey, etc_group: &[u8], bufs: &mut ReadBufs, out: &mut SecurityInfo) -> Result<DetailRead, CollectError>`: identity check; `status` through E05-004; `loginuid`, `sessionid`, `attr/current`, `ns/*`; `etc_group` is read by the caller once per window open.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the `4204/status` fixture (setuid, `CapEff` non-zero) **When** `read_security` runs **Then** `elevated == Root` because euid is 0.
- **Given** a fixture with `Uid: 1000 1000 1000 1000` and `CapEff: 0000000000003000` **When** read **Then** `elevated == Capabilities`, and of the two effective caps (bits 12 `NET_ADMIN` and 13 `NET_RAW`) only `NET_ADMIN` counts as risky.
- **Given** `loginuid` content `4294967295` **When** read **Then** `loginuid == None`.
- **Given** fixture `ns/net` link `net:[4026531840]` equal to PID 1's **When** read **Then** `namespaces[2] == SharedWithInit`; a different inode gives `Isolated(ino)`.
- **Given** a fixture without a readable PID 1 `ns` dir **When** read for a process whose `ns/pid` equals `/proc/self`'s fixture link **Then** `SameAsTasklens`.
- **Given** `/sys/kernel/security/lsm` containing `capability,landlock,lockdown,yama,bpf` **When** read **Then** `lsm_label == NotApplicable`.
- **Given** `/etc/group` text with `docker:x:968:user1` **When** `group_name(968, ..)` runs **Then** it returns `docker`.
- **Given** `CAPS[21]` **When** read **Then** it is `("SYS_ADMIN", "Broad system administration")` and `CAPS.len() == 41`.
- **Given** a fixture `/proc/<pid>` directory owned by uid 0 with `Uid: 1000 1000 1000 1000` in `status` **When** read **Then** `dumpable == Some(false)`; the same directory owned by uid 1000 gives `None`. (The real-root variant is `#[ignore]` because a fixture checkout cannot set owner 0 without root.)

- Fixtures under `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/process-edge/proc/{1,4204,4212}/{status,loginuid,sessionid,attr/current,ns/*}` and `process-edge/sys/kernel/security/lsm`, `process-edge/etc/group`: create.

title: E05-029 Environment, cwd and root readers
description:
## Context
The Environment tab shows `/proc/<pid>/environ` (NUL-separated, capped at 1 MiB), read when the tab opens and on Refresh only, and never logged. The General tab and the Working directory column need `readlink` of `cwd` and `root`. All three need ptrace read access, so other users give `Restricted` until the helper reads them. Sources: PROC-083, PROC-078 (Working dir, Root), PROC-036 (`cwd` column), R-099, ADR-015, UI-PWN `EnvDetail { vars, truncated }` data binding.

## Deliverable

- `pub enum EnvRead { Ok, Restricted, Empty, Failed, Gone }`: `Empty` for a zombie or kernel thread (zero bytes; the tab shows "Environment block unavailable"), `Failed` for other read errors ("(read failed)"), `Restricted` for EACCES or EPERM ("Environment unavailable (insufficient privileges)").
- `pub fn read_environ(root: &SysRoot, key: ProcessKey, buf: &mut Vec<u8>, out: &mut EnvInfo) -> Result<EnvRead, CollectError>`: identity check; reads at most `ENVIRON_MAX` bytes (`truncated = true` when the file is longer; the last partial entry is dropped); splits on NUL; each entry splits at the first `=` into name and value (an entry without `=` is a name with an empty value); names and values sanitized with `sanitize_text(.., ENVIRON_MAX, ..)`. Masking (R-099) is done by the UI; this reader returns raw values and nothing else.
- `pub enum LinkRead { Path(Arc<str>), Restricted, Gone }` and `pub fn read_cwd(pid_dir: BorrowedFd<'_>, buf: &mut Vec<u8>) -> LinkRead` and `pub fn read_root(pid_dir: BorrowedFd<'_>, buf: &mut Vec<u8>) -> LinkRead`: `readlinkat` of `cwd` or `root`, at most 4096 bytes, `sanitize_link`.

title: E05-030 General tab static readers: ELF hardening, ASLR, location
description:
## Context
The General tab's static fields need the ELF hardening of the executable (PIE, NX stack, RELRO), its architecture, the shadow-stack state, ASLR, the autogroup, and the location category of the executable path. This bead adds those readers to `proc/detail.rs`. Sources: PROC-078 (column 1), PROC-027 (Architecture), UI-PWN General field list in `docs/ui/process-windows.md` (rows 10 to 19).

## Deliverable
Additions to `crates/tl-collect/src/proc/detail.rs`:
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct ElfInfo { pub class64: bool, pub machine: u16, pub pie: bool, pub nx_stack: bool, pub relro: Relro }` with `pub enum Relro { Full, Partial, None }`.
- `pub fn read_elf(file: BorrowedFd<'_>, buf: &mut Vec<u8>) -> Result<ElfInfo, CollectError>`: reads with `pread` only the ELF header, the program headers and the `PT_DYNAMIC` segment (no full-file read); little-endian 32- and 64-bit; not ELF (`\x7fELF` missing) gives `CollectError::NotElf`.
  - `pie`: `e_type == ET_DYN (3)` and a `PT_INTERP (3)` program header exists;
  - `nx_stack`: a `PT_GNU_STACK (0x6474e551)` header exists and its `p_flags` lacks `PF_X (1)`; no header means executable stack (false);
  - `relro`: `PT_GNU_RELRO (0x6474e552)` present and (`DT_FLAGS (30)` has `DF_BIND_NOW (0x8)` or `DT_FLAGS_1 (0x6ffffffb)` has `DF_1_NOW (0x1)` or `DT_BIND_NOW (24)` exists) → `Full`; `PT_GNU_RELRO` only → `Partial`; else `None`.
- `pub fn arch_label(class64: bool, machine: u16) -> &'static str`: `EM_X86_64 (62)` "x86-64", `EM_386 (3)` "x86 (32-bit)", `EM_AARCH64 (183)` "AArch64", else "Unknown" (General tab wording). `pub fn arch_column_label(class64: bool, machine: u16) -> &'static str` for the Architecture column (PROC-027): "x86-64 (64-bit)", "i386 (32-bit)", "AArch64 (64-bit)", else "Unknown".
- `pub fn pe_machine_label(machine: u16) -> &'static str`: for Wine `.exe` files, `IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_AMD64 (0x8664)` "x64 (64-bit, Wine)", `IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_I386 (0x14c)` "x86 (32-bit, Wine)", else "Unknown"; `pub fn read_pe_machine(file: BorrowedFd<'_>) -> Result<u16, CollectError>` reads `e_lfanew` at offset 0x3c, checks `PE\0\0`, returns the COFF `Machine` field.
- `pub enum ShadowStack { Enabled, Disabled, NotSupported }` from `PidStatus.x86_thread_features`: line absent → `NotSupported`; value contains `shstk` → `Enabled`; else `Disabled`.
- `pub fn aslr_text(randomize_va_space: &[u8], personality: Option<u32>, out: &mut String)`: `2` "Full (2)", `1` "Partial (1)", `0` "Off (0)"; when `personality & ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE (0x0040000)` is set, appends ", disabled for this process"; `personality` is `None` when `/proc/<pid>/personality` is restricted (then nothing is appended).
- `pub fn read_autogroup(pid_dir: BorrowedFd<'_>, buf: &mut Vec<u8>) -> Option<(u32, i8)>`: parses `/proc/<pid>/autogroup` `/autogroup-<n> nice <k>`.
- `pub enum Location { TempDirectory, UserDownloads, UserData, UserProfile, System, OptionalSoftware, Flatpak, AppImage, WinePrefix, Deleted, Other }` with labels "Temp directory", "User Downloads", "User data", "User profile", "System", "Optional software", "Flatpak", "AppImage", "Wine prefix", "Deleted", "Other", and `pub fn location(path: &str, deleted: bool, ctx: &LocationCtx) -> Location` where `pub struct LocationCtx { pub home: String, pub runtime_dir: Option<String>, pub downloads: Option<String> }`. First match: `deleted` → Deleted; `/tmp/.mount_` prefix → AppImage; contains `/drive_c/` → WinePrefix; `/var/lib/flatpak/` or `<home>/.local/share/flatpak/` → Flatpak; `/tmp/`, `/var/tmp/`, or `<runtime_dir>/` → TempDirectory; `<downloads>/` → UserDownloads; `<home>/.local/`, `<home>/.cache/`, `<home>/.config/` → UserData; `<home>/` → UserProfile; `/usr/` → System; `/opt/` → OptionalSoftware; else Other. `downloads` comes from `xdg-user-dir DOWNLOAD`, resolved by the caller from `~/.config/user-dirs.dirs` key `XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR` (`$HOME` expanded).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** `/usr/bin/ls` on the owner machine **When** `read_elf` runs on it **Then** `pie == true`, `nx_stack == true`, `relro == Full`, `arch_label == "x86-64"`.
- **Given** a hand-built ELF fixture with `ET_EXEC`, no `PT_GNU_STACK` and no `PT_GNU_RELRO` **When** read **Then** `pie == false`, `nx_stack == false`, `relro == None`.
- **Given** a text file **When** `read_elf` runs **Then** `Err(NotElf)`.
- **Given** a fixture PE header with machine `0x14c` **When** `read_pe_machine` and `pe_machine_label` run **Then** "x86 (32-bit, Wine)".
- **Given** `randomize_va_space` `2` and personality `0x0040000` **When** `aslr_text` runs **Then** "Full (2), disabled for this process".
- **Given** `x86_Thread_features: shstk wrss` **When** mapped **Then** `Enabled`; no line gives `NotSupported`.
- **Given** autogroup text `/autogroup-123 nice 0` **When** parsed **Then** `Some((123, 0))`.

title: E05-031 Handle walk and pipe peers in proc/handles.rs
description:
## Context
Search File Handles (P3) walks every process's open files, memory-mapped files, working directory, executable and root, like `lsof`, on the blocking pool, cancellable between pids. The File descriptors tab (P2) names a pipe by its peer ("pipe:[ino] ↔ cat (5678)"), which needs the same walk limited to a set of pipe inodes. This bead writes both on one walker in `proc/handles.rs`. It is pulled into P2 because anchor E05-A3, which E10 depends on, delivers `handles.rs`. Sources: PROC-096, PROC-080 (pipe peers), ADR-016, UI-PWN `HandleSearchState { search, phase, progress, chunks, searched, total, skipped }` data binding.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/proc/handles.rs`:
- `pub struct Pattern { ... }` with `pub fn new(text: &str) -> Pattern`: case-insensitive; when the text contains `*` or `?` it is a glob over the whole path (`*` any run, `?` one char), else a substring match. Matching works on the lowercased path; no regex crate.
- `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum HitKind { Fd, Mmap, Cwd, Exe, Root }` with labels `fd`, `mmap`, `cwd`, `exe`, `root`.
- `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct HandleHitInfo { pub key: ProcessKey, pub pid: u32, pub comm: Arc<str>, pub uid: u32, pub kind: HitKind, pub fd: Option<u32>, pub path: Arc<str> }`.
- `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq)] pub struct WalkProgress { pub searched: u32, pub total: u32, pub skipped: u32, pub handles: u64 }`.
- `pub struct HandleWalk { pids: Vec<u32>, next: usize, pattern: Pattern, include_maps: bool, progress: WalkProgress }` with:
  - `pub fn start(root: &SysRoot, pattern: &str, include_maps: bool) -> Self`: lists numeric `<proc>` entries; `total` = their count;
  - `pub fn step(&mut self, root: &SysRoot, ctx_boot: BootId, budget: usize, bufs: &mut ReadBufs, hits: &mut Vec<HandleHitInfo>) -> StepResult` where `pub enum StepResult { More, Done }`: processes up to `budget` pids, then returns, so the caller can check its cancel flag between calls (cancel is "between pids", PROC-096). Per pid: open the dirfd, read `stat` for the key and comm, readlink every `fd/*` (`Fd`, counted in `handles`); when `include_maps`, also the unique file paths of `maps` (`Mmap`), `cwd`, `exe` and `root` links. EACCES on `fd/` counts the pid in `skipped` (other users without the helper); a vanished pid is neither searched nor skipped (decrements `total`). Paths are sanitized with `sanitize_link`; matching paths are pushed as hits.
  - `pub fn progress(&self) -> WalkProgress`.
- `pub fn find_pipe_peers(root: &SysRoot, inodes: &FxHashSet<u64>, skip_pid: u32, bufs: &mut ReadBufs, out: &mut FxHashMap<u64, SmallVec<[(u32, Arc<str>); 2]>>)`: walks all `fd/*` of every other readable pid once and records `pid` and sanitized `comm` for every `pipe:[ino]` link whose inode is in `inodes` (P2, File descriptors tab).

- **Given** pattern `user1` and `include_maps = true` **When** walked **Then** hits include kind `Cwd` for 4201.
- **Given** `include_maps = false` **When** walked **Then** no `Mmap`, `Cwd`, `Exe` or `Root` hits.
- **Given** `budget = 1` **When** `step` is called repeatedly **Then** it returns `More` until every pid is done, and `progress().searched` grows by at most 1 per call.
- **Given** a pid whose `fd` dir has mode 0000 (non-root run) **When** walked **Then** `skipped` is 1 and no error is returned.

title: E05-032 Strings scanner core
description:
## Context
The Strings tab (P3) scans process memory for printable strings in ASCII, UTF-8 and UTF-16LE, with a minimum length of 4 to 64 (default 4), optional file-backed mappings, a cancel, and stop limits of 1,000,000 strings or 256 MiB of text. This bead writes the scanner core: region selection from `/proc/<pid>/maps` and the string finder over byte chunks. How memory is read is behind a trait. The real reader is `pread` on `/proc/<pid>/mem` through `rustix::fs::pread` (R-144 item 2, E05 item 6 accepted); PROC-084's mechanism line changes from `process_vm_readv` to `/proc/<pid>/mem`. It is pulled into P2 because anchor E05-A3 delivers `strings.rs`. Sources: PROC-084, UI-PWN `StringScanState` and `StringHit` data binding.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/proc/strings.rs`:
- `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct ScanOpts { pub min_len: u8, pub ascii: bool, pub utf8: bool, pub utf16le: bool, pub include_file_backed: bool }` with `min_len` clamped to 4..=64; default `{ 4, true, true, true, false }`.
- `pub const CHUNK: usize = 1024 * 1024; pub const MAX_STRINGS: u32 = 1_000_000; pub const MAX_TEXT_BYTES: u64 = 256 * 1024 * 1024;`
- `pub fn select_regions(maps: &[MapRegionInfo], include_file_backed: bool, out: &mut Vec<(u64, u64)>)`: keeps readable (`perms[0] == b'r'`) regions that are private anonymous (no path, `perms[3] == b'p'`), `[heap]` or `[stack]`; plus file-backed regions when `include_file_backed`; always skips `[vvar]`, `[vsyscall]`, `[vdso]` and paths under `/dev/`.
- `pub trait MemSource { fn read(&mut self, addr: u64, buf: &mut [u8]) -> Result<usize, CollectError>; }` (returns bytes read; 0 or an error for an unreadable page range, which the scanner skips).
- `#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum Encoding { Ascii, Utf8, Utf16Le }`; `#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct StringHitInfo { pub address: u64, pub encoding: Encoding, pub length: u32, pub value: Box<str> }` (`length` in characters).
- `pub enum ScanEnd { Finished, Cancelled, Stopped, Failed }`.
- `pub struct StringScanner { opts: ScanOpts, regions: Vec<(u64, u64)>, region: usize, offset: u64, found: u32, text_bytes: u64, carry: Vec<u8> }` with `pub fn new(opts: ScanOpts, regions: Vec<(u64, u64)>) -> Self` and
  `pub fn step(&mut self, mem: &mut dyn MemSource, buf: &mut Vec<u8>, out: &mut Vec<StringHitInfo>) -> Option<ScanEnd>`: reads one `CHUNK` (or the rest of the region), finds strings, returns `None` while more work remains, else the end state. Rules:
  - ASCII: runs of bytes 0x20..=0x7E plus `\t`, length at least `min_len`;
  - UTF-8: runs of valid UTF-8 whose chars are printable (not control, not U+FFFD) and that contain at least one non-ASCII char, at least `min_len` chars (pure-ASCII runs are reported once, as ASCII);
  - UTF-16LE: runs of 2-byte units that decode to printable BMP chars (no surrogates), at least `min_len` chars;
  - a string that crosses a chunk boundary is joined through `carry` so it is reported once;
  - values are sanitized with `sanitize_text(.., 4096, ..)` and longer strings are cut there with `…`;
  - stops with `Stopped` when `found` reaches `MAX_STRINGS` or `text_bytes` reaches `MAX_TEXT_BYTES` (the UI text is "String scan stopped: not enough memory.").
  - `pub fn progress_pct(&self) -> u8`: bytes scanned / total region bytes × 100.
- `pub struct VecMem(pub u64, pub Vec<u8>)` implementing `MemSource` for tests (base address and bytes).
- `pub struct ProcMem { fd: OwnedFd }` with `pub fn open(root: &SysRoot, key: ProcessKey) -> Result<Self, CollectError>` (identity check, then `openat(<pid dirfd>, "mem", O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC)`; `EACCES` or `EPERM` gives a `Restricted` error) implementing `MemSource` with `rustix::fs::pread(fd, buf, addr)`; `EIO` or a short read of 0 returns `Ok(0)` so the scanner skips the range. The same ptrace access rule applies as for `process_vm_readv`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** maps with `[heap]` r/w private, a private anonymous region, `/usr/lib/libc.so.6` r-x, `[vvar]` and `/dev/dri/card1` **When** `select_regions` runs with `include_file_backed = false` **Then** only the heap and anonymous regions are kept; with `true`, libc is added and `[vvar]` and `/dev/` stay out.
- **Given** memory `"\0\0hello world\0ab\0"` at base 0x1000 and `min_len = 4` **When** scanned **Then** one ASCII hit `{address: 0x1002, length: 11, value: "hello world"}`.
- **Given** UTF-16LE bytes for `Wine path` **When** scanned **Then** one `Utf16Le` hit with value `Wine path`.
- **Given** UTF-8 `"grüße\0"` with `min_len = 4` **When** scanned **Then** one `Utf8` hit `grüße`.
- **Given** a 6-byte ASCII string split across a 1 MiB chunk boundary **When** scanned **Then** it is reported once with the right address.
- **Given** a scanner built with `with_limits(10, MAX_TEXT_BYTES)` and 20 strings in memory **When** scanned **Then** the end state is `Stopped` with 10 hits.
- **Given** a scanner and a caller cancel flag set after the first `step` **When** the caller stops calling `step` **Then** the caller reports `Cancelled` (the scanner holds no thread and needs no cleanup).
- **Given** the test process's own key and a static 32-byte buffer holding `tasklens-strings-probe` **When** `ProcMem::open` and `read` at the buffer's address run **Then** the bytes read equal the buffer.

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/proc/strings.rs`: create.
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixture_process.rs`, `crates/tl-collect/tests/prop_process.rs`: add tests.

## Tests
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::strings_region_selection`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::strings_ascii_hit`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::strings_utf16le_hit`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::strings_utf8_hit`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::strings_chunk_boundary_once`.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::strings_stop_limit`.
- `tests/prop_process.rs::strings_arbitrary_memory_never_panics`: arbitrary byte buffers up to 3 MiB and arbitrary options never panic, and every hit's value is at most 4,097 chars.
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::strings_proc_mem_reads_self`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: `MemSource` errors skip the range; `Failed` only when no region could be read at all ("Failed to read process memory.").
- Validity: N/A.
- Accessibility: N/A.
- Performance: one 1 MiB chunk per `step`; the engine sends payloads at most 4 times per second.
- Privacy: memory strings can hold secrets; they are never logged.

## Notes
- Phase P3 feature, written in P2 for the E05-A3 anchor. The real `MemSource` is `ProcMem` (`pread` on `/proc/<pid>/mem`, R-144 item 2). The tl-helper row gains `tl-collect` (R-142 item 14), so the helper's `ScanStrings` (E29) reuses this scanner.
- `#[doc(hidden)] pub fn StringScanner::with_limits(self, max_strings: u32, max_text: u64) -> Self` lowers the limits for tests (integration tests cannot see `#[cfg(test)]` items).
- Build rule: run every cargo command through `heavy-build cargo ...` (for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-collect`). Run `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p tl-collect --all-targets -- -D warnings` the same way before committing. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.

Allowed dependencies: tl-model, rustix (workspace features fs, process, net, event, system, thread, time, pipe, mm, param; R-142 item 5), memchr, thiserror, tracing, smallvec, rustc-hash, sha2, md-5, the netlink crates. No `unsafe`: only `tl-ops/src/sys.rs`, `tl-engine/src/gpu/spawn.rs`, `tl-app/src/main.rs` and `tl-gpu-probe/src/api_versions.rs` may hold it (R-143). No `procfs` crate (ADR-016). Dev-dependencies (insta 1.48.0, proptest 1.11.0, tempfile 3.27.0, criterion 0.8.2) come from `[workspace.dependencies]`.
- Never log command lines, environment, working directories, open file paths, executable paths of other users' processes or user names other than the current user, at any level (ADR-015). title: E05-033 Launcher split: Steam, Lutris and Heroic games
description:
## Context
Scope grouping puts every game under the Steam (or Lutris, Heroic) app. PROC-011 (P4) splits them: each game becomes its own child app row named after the game. Steam games are found by the `reaper` process whose argv contains `AppId=<n>`; Lutris and Heroic games by environment variables. title: E05-035 P2 per-process column readers (proc/extras_p2.rs)
description:
## Context
The P2 per-process columns of PROC-027 to PROC-036 that `ProcessRecord` and `ProcessExtras` do not carry are read only for the rows the user can see (`Demand.detail_keys`, ADR-008 visible-rows rule) and go into a second index-aligned slice `ProcessSnapshot.extras_p2: Arc<[ProcessExtrasP2]>` (R-163 item 2, E05 item 5 second half). This bead writes the readers and fills that slice during the sweep. `ProcessExtrasP2`, `PackageInfo` and `PackageStatus` are tl-model types (E03-072). Sources: R-163, PROC-027 (file and package columns, Architecture), PROC-028 (Session, Security label, Elevated, Sandbox), PROC-029 (Context switches), PROC-036 (Scheduling policy, OOM score, TTY, Working directory), ADR-008, ADR-015.

## Deliverable
`crates/tl-collect/src/proc/extras_p2.rs` plus the `proc/mod.rs` line `pub mod extras_p2;`:

```rust
pub struct ExtrasP2Reader { /* elf: FxHashMap<(u64 dev, u64 ino), (u8, u16)>, prev_ctx: FxHashMap<ProcessKey, u64>, init_userns: Option<u64> */ }
impl ExtrasP2Reader {
    pub fn new() -> Self;
    /// Fills one entry for `key`. `exe` and `stat` come from the sweep (E05-A1); `pkg` is the E05-034 index.
    pub fn read(&mut self, root: &SysRoot, dirfd: BorrowedFd<'_>, key: ProcessKey, stat: &PidStat, exe: &ExeLink,
                cgroup: Option<&CgroupPath>, pkg: &mut PackageIndex, now: Instant, bufs: &mut ReadBufs) -> ProcessExtrasP2;
    /// Drops cached state of dead keys.
    pub fn retain_live(&mut self, live: &FxHashSet<ProcessKey>);
}
```

Field rules (every field is `None` when its read fails; the read never panics):
- `exe_mtime_s`, `exe_size_bytes`: `statx` of the exe link target through `openat(dirfd, "exe", O_PATH)` (PROC-027).
- `elf_class`, `elf_machine`: the first 20 bytes of the exe through the same fd: magic `\x7fELF`, `EI_CLASS` 1 gives 32, 2 gives 64, `e_machine` little-endian u16 at offset 18. Cached by (dev, inode). The UI maps 62 to "x86-64", 3 to "i386", 183 to "AArch64".
- `session_id`: `/proc/<pid>/sessionid`; `4294967295` gives `None` (PROC-028).
- `security_label`: `attr/current`, trailing NUL and newline removed, sanitized; `None` when `/sys/kernel/security/lsm` lists none of `apparmor`, `selinux`, `smack`, `tomoyo`.
- `elevated` (PROC-028, first match): euid 0 gives `Some(true)` ("Full (root)"); euid ≠ ruid, or `CapEff` non-zero for a non-root process, gives `Some(true)`; else `Some(false)`. The UI picks the label from `status` values it already has; this bead stores only the flag.
- `sandbox` (PROC-028, first match): "Flatpak" when the cgroup path contains an `app-flatpak-` scope or `/proc/<pid>/root/.flatpak-info` exists; "Snap" when the cgroup path contains `snap.`; "bwrap" when `readlinkat(dirfd, "ns/user")` differs from PID 1's link; "seccomp + NoNewPrivs" when status `Seccomp` is 2 and `NoNewPrivs` is 1; "seccomp" when `Seccomp` is 2; else "None". `ns/user` and `root` need ptrace access: on `EACCES` the Flatpak and Snap rules use the cgroup only and bwrap gives `None`. Firejail detection is not in this bead.
- `sched_policy_text`: from stat field 41: 0 "Normal", 1 "FIFO", 2 "RR", 3 "Batch", 5 "Idle", 6 "Deadline".
- `oom_score`, `oom_score_adj`: the two files (PROC-036).
- `tty`: stat field 7 `tty_nr` decoded: major 136 to 143 gives `pts/<minor + (major − 136) × 256>`, major 4 with minor below 64 gives `tty<minor>`, 0 gives `None`, anything else `<major>:<minor>`.
- `cwd`: `readlinkat(dirfd, "cwd")`, sanitized, at most 4,096 bytes (PROC-036).
- `ctx_switches_voluntary`, `ctx_switches_involuntary`: sums over `task/*/status` (`voluntary_ctxt_switches`, `nonvoluntary_ctxt_switches`), at most 4,096 tasks; `ctx_switches_delta` is the sum minus the previous sum for the same key, `None` on the first read.
- `package`, `package_status`: `pkg.get(exe_path, exe_mtime_s)`; a miss calls `pkg.request` and leaves both `None`. Status (PROC-027, first match): `DeletedUpgraded` when the exe link ends in " (deleted)"; `Flatpak` or `Snap` from the sandbox rule; `AppImage` when the exe is under `/tmp/.mount_`; `Wine` when the exe basename starts with `wine` and argv[0] ends in `.exe`; `Packaged` when the index has an owner; `NotPackaged` when the index says none. `PackagedModified` is set only by the PROC-078 check result in the detail worker, never here. Flatpak branch, Wine PE version resources and AppImage versions are not read in this bead (the Version cell shows `n/a`).
- `key` is `Some(key)` for a filled entry. `power_w` and `power_trend_w` stay `None`; the reducer fills them (E09-030).

Chain edit to `crates/tl-collect/src/proc/sweep.rs` (E05-A1): `SweepOutput` gains `pub extras_p2: Vec<ProcessExtrasP2>` and `ProcessSampler` gains `p2: ExtrasP2Reader` and `pkg: PackageIndex` (with `pub fn pkg_mut(&mut self) -> &mut PackageIndex` so the engine can run `run_batch` in its own job). In `sweep`, inside the per-pid hook, when `key` is in `inp.detail_keys`, `p2.read(..)` fills the entry; every other record gets `ProcessExtrasP2::default()`; `extras_p2` is sorted with `records`. When `detail_keys` is empty the vector is empty (no per-record cost). The engine copies it into `ProcessSweep.extras_p2` (8hz.5).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Given** the `process-edge` fixture pid `4201` with `sessionid` `3`, `oom_score` `667`, `oom_score_adj` `200`, `tty_nr` `34817` and `cwd` → `/home/user` **When** read **Then** `session_id == Some(3)`, `oom_score == Some(667)`, `oom_score_adj == Some(200)`, `tty == Some("pts/1")`, `cwd == Some("/home/user")`.
- **Given** an exe whose first bytes are `7f 45 4c 46 02 .. ` with `e_machine` 62 **When** read twice for two pids with the same (dev, inode) **Then** `elf_class == Some(64)`, `elf_machine == Some(62)` and the file was read once.
- **Given** `task/1/status` and `task/2/status` with voluntary 10 and 5, nonvoluntary 1 and 2 **When** read, then read again after they grow to 20 and 5, 1 and 2 **Then** the first entry has sums 15 and 3 and `ctx_switches_delta == None`, the second has `ctx_switches_delta == Some(10)`.
- **Given** status `Seccomp: 2` and `NoNewPrivs: 1` and no flatpak or snap cgroup and the same user namespace as PID 1 **When** read **Then** `sandbox == Some("seccomp + NoNewPrivs")`.
- **Given** an exe link `/usr/bin/foo (deleted)` **When** read **Then** `package_status == Some(DeletedUpgraded)`.
- **Given** a package index without an entry for the exe **When** read **Then** `package == None`, `package_status == None` and the path was queued with `request`.
- **Given** `detail_keys = [4201]` and three records **When** the sweep runs **Then** `extras_p2.len() == 3`, only the entry at 4201's index has `key == Some(..)`, and `detail_keys = []` gives an empty vector.
- **Given** arbitrary bytes in `sessionid`, `attr/current`, `oom_score`, `status` and the ELF header (proptest) **When** read **Then** nothing panics (security regression: untrusted input).

## Files
- `crates/tl-collect/src/proc/extras_p2.rs`: create
- `crates/tl-collect/src/proc/mod.rs`: `pub mod extras_p2;` (chain edit, that line only)
- `crates/tl-collect/src/proc/sweep.rs`: chain edit, the `SweepOutput` field, the two `ProcessSampler` fields, `pkg_mut` and the hook call above
- `crates/tl-collect/tests/fixtures/process-edge/proc/4201/{sessionid,oom_score,oom_score_adj,attr/current}` and `task/{1,2}/status`: create

## Tests
- `tests/fixture_process.rs::extras_p2_basic_fields`, `::extras_p2_elf_cached`, `::extras_p2_ctx_switch_delta`, `::extras_p2_sandbox_seccomp`, `::extras_p2_deleted_exe_status`, `::extras_p2_package_miss_queues`, `::extras_p2_only_detail_keys`.
- `tests/prop_process.rs::extras_p2_arbitrary_files_never_panic`.

## Cross-cutting
- Errors: per-field `None`; never an error for the whole entry.
- Validity: `None` shows the WarmingUp glyph for rows outside `detail_keys` and "Not reported" when the read failed (the UI knows which from `key`).
- Accessibility: N/A
- Performance: only `detail_keys` (visible rows, at most a few hundred); ELF headers cached; `task/*/status` capped at 4,096 tasks per process. Part of the E05-023 sweep budget when `detail_keys` is empty (no cost).
- Privacy: `cwd`, the exe path and `security_label` are user data: never logged above `debug`, and `cwd` never logged at all for other users' processes (ADR-015).
- Security: every file is untrusted input; bounded reads, no panics.

## Notes
- Depends on E05-A1 (yms.1) and E05-034 (the package index). Phase P2. E09-030 fills `power_w` and `power_trend_w` in the same slice.
- `tl-collect` has no async code, no runtime and no `unsafe` (ADR-001 rules 3 and 4).
- Read `/home/oystein/work/tasklens/CLAUDE.md` first. Large file: commit `extras_p2.rs` before building or testing.
- Build rule: run every cargo build, test, check, clippy or doc through `heavy-build`, for example `heavy-build cargo test -p tl-collect`. It waits for the machine-wide build lock and runs in a memory-capped scope. On exit 137 (OOM kill) retry once, then report. On exit 75 (low disk) stop and report.
- Commit once with a pathspec: `git add <your files> && git commit -m "E05-035: ..." -- <your files>`. Never a bare `git commit`, never change branch or history.

title: tl-collect sanitize: keep ZWJ, remove U+2028 and U+2029
description:
Files: crates/tl-collect/src/sanitize.rs (and its tests).
Why: ug9.7 found two gaps against UI-FND-053. push_clean removes the whole range U+200B..=U+200F, which includes U+200D (ZWJ); rule 5 says ZWJ is kept, so emoji ZWJ sequences get split. A proptest: for any input, the output passes the same character check as debug_assert_clean in crates/tl-ui/src/text/untrusted.rs (copy the predicate into the test; tl-collect must not depend on tl-ui). Existing tl-collect tests and snapshots pass (update a snapshot only if it contained one of these characters, and say so).

title: E05-001 Add process modules and CollectError variants to tl-collect
description:
## Context
E05 adds the process side of `tl-collect`. This chain-edit bead registers the E05 modules in the E04-owned `lib.rs`, adds the E05 variants to `CollectError` (E04-owned `src/error.rs`, chain-edit rule in `docs/plan/00-epics.md` section 2), and creates the empty `proc/mod.rs` and `apps/mod.rs` that later E05 beads fill.
